docs.text: Regime-cutover U343 (M-24 part 1, shape A of the U342 design note). srt does not nest (M-22), so the Router, the dsh-superagent control host that hcom-seat router runs inside srt, cannot start a worker sandbox of its own. This lever runs outside every sandbox as the operator's user, started by hcom-seat beside the Router (U344), and listens on <seats-root>/.state/<router seat>/broker/sock, the one Unix socket the router row's network.allowUnixSockets opens (U342 measured: that directory's sockets and nothing else). Inside the Router's sandbox dsh-subagent-acp spawns the thin client acp-seat, which connects, sends one header line and relays the ACP stdio stream; this lever starts srt --settings <worker> -- omp acp --profile dsh per connection in a directory of its own and pipes the connection to it. The Router and every worker are separate srt processes started outside both (R-45), the worker never inherits the Router's settings, and the Router cannot name the settings file. The socket and its directory (regime-cutover U343i, the mechanism-change row of 2026-11-10T06:20:28Z, form remove; verdicts U343g-8a049561 P1 :1262 and U343h-eb648bcd P1 acp-relay.py:284, P1 :963, P2 acp-relay.py:232, class record-path). The broker directory <seats-root>/.state/<router seat>/broker/ lies in the Router's own state slot, and until this round the Router's settings granted that slot for write whole, so every path an unsandboxed process named inside the directory followed whatever the Router had planted there (round 5's printf > <id>.tmp, then, once that write sat on a held descriptor, the relay's unlink of the socket and its chmod, and this lever's rm -f of the socket and the records after the Router renamed the directory away and planted a link at its name), however each operation was hardened, because the Router owned the directory entry itself. The premise is gone: hcom-seat's router row renders <state slot>/broker as a denyWrite row of the Router's own settings (tagged slot inside the state-slot grant; srt's later deny wins on macOS and on Linux the path must exist when the settings are written) and makes the directory 0700 before it writes them (hcom-seat's broker_dir_make), so the Router reads it and connects to its socket (the router row's network.allowUnixSockets names this directory and nothing else since regime-cutover U344, so the connect is granted and this sentence holds at this head) and can plant, rename or unlink nothing in it. acp-broker <seats-root> <router seat> <router scratch cwd> makes nothing there: it takes the directory as hcom-seat made it, present (absent refuses naming hcom-seat), no link, a directory of this user, mode 0700 and empty (no entry of any kind: a socket inside is another broker's, one listener per Router launch; anything else is a crashed broker's leftover or a directory that is not hcom-seat's), each refused by name with nothing made, and listens on sock there (mode 0600). The entries are read by a glob (regime-cutover U343j, verdict U343i-76a5c83b P2 :1062: dot names included, no match an empty list), so a name of any bytes counts, one newline alone included, which $(ls -A) had stripped. The listener and the byte relay are the one non-bash part, acp-relay.py beside this file, run as python3 -I -S by its pinned physical argv after its own claude.levers.sha256 pin was checked here; per connection it starts acp-broker --connection <the same three arguments> with the connection as its stdin and stdout and copies bytes both ways until either side closes. The socket is the relay's alone (regime-cutover U343j, verdict U343i-76a5c83b P1 :1061): it binds sock and removes it at its end, a signal to it included; its handlers for HUP, INT and TERM are installed before the bind (regime-cutover U447: the trap below sends it TERM the moment this process's signal arrives, and a TERM between the bind and those handlers ended the relay by the default disposition with the socket bound, which this process read as another broker's and exited 2; the test fixture took the socket's existence for readiness, so it signalled in that window). The take is a check before that bind, so two brokers started together can both pass it, and the bind decides: the relay that loses it refuses (cannot bind the broker socket) and exits 2, and this process, which until this round removed the socket after its relay ended whatever had bound it, removes nothing when the socket stands after the relay's end (another broker's listener, or one the relay could not remove; the records beside it are that broker's) and exits 2 naming it. The records no client read are removed by this process once the listener ended and the socket is gone, and by the trap a hangup, interrupt or termination runs before this process ends by that signal. The trap is armed before the relay's fork, and a signal during the fork, between the & and child=$!, is recorded and handled once the child is known (regime-cutover U447c, verdict U447-669dee44 P1 :1280: bash runs a trap right after the command the signal arrived in and can block no signal, so until this round such a signal ran the trap with child empty, which signalled nothing, read the socket the orphaned relay had bound as another broker's and exited 2; the window is closed by deferral, one flag and one recorded signal, no second cleanup path). Which signals arrive is the launch's: hcom-seat starts this lever as a background job of a non-interactive bash, which inherits SIGINT ignored, and bash refuses to trap a signal ignored at entry, so under hcom-seat the broker is ended by hcom-seat's TERM (and a HUP), and a direct INT reaches it only when it is started in the foreground (the test fixture's form, where the INT cases hold); no caller delivers INT to the broker. The directory is hcom-seat's and stands (no rmdir here): the launch's slot removal takes it with the Router's state slot. The header (regime-cutover U343e, the mechanism-change row of 2026-11-07T09:41:47Z: the Router names no path that becomes a grant). The first line of a connection is ACP-SEAT v1 repo=<path> ref=<rev> name=<name>: the repository a clean absolute path (clean_path) the Router may read, the ref a revision in ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,255}$ without .., the name in the seat-name grammar ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ (never claude or claude-*, the Claude Code login directories' names, never the Router's own seat name, never one beginning acp-, the prefix of the slots below, never broker-logs, the launch logs' directory, U343o), nothing after the fifth field, the whole line within 1024 characters and its newline read. Anything else is refused with one line acp-broker: refused: <reason> on the connection and the connection closed, nothing made. The Router's scratch cwd is the third argument alone: it is neither read nor granted, and no path of the header is a grant. The slot and the clone. Every connection gets a slot of its own, <seats-root>/.state/acp-<name>-<utc stamp>- <pid>/ (0700, made by one mkdir of this connection under a root the Router's sandbox denies for read and no seat may write; the worker's write root cannot lie under .sandbox, whose deny row the worker's settings carry, because srt 0.0.81's macOS profile emits a denyWrite row after the allowWrite roots and the later rule wins), holding settings.json and task, the worker's directory: a repository initialised here with no template, the commit the header's ref names unpacked into it, checked out detached. The repository is read inside the Router's own sandbox: the two reads (rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}, then pack-objects --revs --stdout of that commit) run as srt --settings <the Router's rendered settings> -- git … through the physical git under the isolated library's environment and flags (git-isolated.sh: no config file, no hook, no replacement object, no transport), so a gitfile, an alternates file or a link in the Router's repository reaches only what the Router itself may read, and the pack arrives on the sandboxed git's stdout, a descriptor this process opened in the slot. The pack is indexed into task (index-pack --strict) and the commit checked out by the same isolated git run outside every sandbox, on the slot alone; the pack file is removed. A ref that does not resolve, a pack that does not index or a checkout that fails refuses by name with the slot removed; nothing of the repository is shared with the worker's tree, and the Router may move or relink anything of its own afterwards without changing what the worker reads or writes (test (a) of U343e). The worker's settings. The dsh row's shape, rendered per connection into <slot>/settings.json. The deny table is the Router's own, read from the settings hcom-seat rendered for this launch at <seats-root>/.sandbox/<router seat>/srt-settings.json (the router row is the dsh row with the loopback grant and the state root, U321, so its denyRead and denyWrite lists are the dsh row's deny table for this seats root, checkout, store and host): every row must be a clean path (the macOS worktree patterns, a clean prefix and the fixed worktrees/*/<file> suffix, are the one exception, as in hcom-seat), the rows under the Router's scratch cwd (its project-file denies) are re-rooted under the slot's task, and denyRead gains the Router's credential root <DSH_HOME>/router-credentials (regime-cutover U353, U343l: held from DSH_HOME in this process's environment in hcom-seat's form, cred_root_hold, checked against the Router's own denyWrite row of it so the two levers name one root, and appended last, where the dsh row renders it). The grants are the role's own and the broker's: allowWrite the slot's task, the router login group's Claude Code directory <seats-root>/.state/claude-router (regime-cutover U498b: the workers are the Router's own processes, so they hold the Router's login, the group hcom-seat's login_group_of_role gives the dsh and router roles; the eight configuration rows under it are denied through the Router's own denyWrite table, which this lever requires to carry them, so a worker changes nothing a Router child or the operator's login command there would load), ~/.omp/profiles/dsh (the worker's omp profile, OMP_PROFILE=dsh), ~/.omp/run, and srt 0.0.81's own writable paths (/tmp/claude, /private/tmp/claude on macOS, ~/.npm/_logs), every one physical; allowRead the slot's task, the group's directory, that profile, ~/.agents/skills, the private tool directory ~/.local/state/hcom-seat/tools and the seats' API key file REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE names (U516, the @env row). No row names the Router's scratch cwd, its state slot, the repository or the legacy <seats-root>/.state/claude (U318, one login per seats root; read by nothing since U498b). No DSH_HOME grant and no state slot: the worker is omp, not dsh, and the launch log is this lever's to write. allowLocalBinding false, allowUnixSockets empty, the domain list hcom-seat's. The settings text is the one writer's: both levers source seat-settings-render.sh (regime-cutover U344: the path rule every row obeys, the domain list and the JSON text; the rows are each lever's own and no root is baked in) from a private copy hashed against its pin (renderer_source, U344c), so the worker's file is the dsh row's file with the worker's rows, byte for byte (tests/unit/test_acp_broker.py test_the_worker_settings_are_the_dsh_row_but_the_named_rows and test_one_settings_writer_renders_the_worker_and_the_dsh_row_byte_for_byte). The judgement (regime-cutover U343c; hcom-seat's settings_judge, U272f and U272g). Before anything is made, every grant row is judged against every deny row, by identity for what exists and by the absent components below one shared ancestor otherwise (identity_table, within_ix: one stat for every row); a grant that is, contains or lies inside a deny refuses naming both rows, unless the pair is structural and the grant lies where the role spells it: the slot's task and the router group's Claude Code directory under the seats-root denies (the seats root and ~/.local/state/omp-seats) and over the project-file and configuration denies rendered inside them, and ~/.omp/profiles/dsh under ~/.omp/profiles. A profile that is a link elsewhere is not where the role spells it, so it is judged like any row and refused (the round-1 finding: a dsh profile linked into the orchestrator profile was granted that profile). The canary (R-44). Before omp starts, the four-word probe of the hcom-seat shim runs under the worker's settings by the physical srt argv: a write into the slot, a read of the settings file, a listing of ~/.ssh and a write under the operator's ~/.claude/debug must all fail inside (write-denied read-denied ssh-denied debug-denied); any other answer, a canary that did not run, or a file a probe could make refuses with one line, the slot removed and no omp started. The answer is appended as <utc> acp-broker: canary <four words> to <seats-root>/.state/broker-logs/<name>.log, in a directory this lever makes 0700 under its own .state (regime-cutover U343o, verdict U343n-fd3db1b3 P1 :1264, the record-path premise once more: until round 12 the log was .state/<name>/acp-launch.log, inside the state slot an hcom-seat seat of that name writes, and a hard link a seat planted at that name passed the -L test and redirected this unsandboxed append to its target; .state/broker-logs is granted to no seat, the seats root being denied to every seat but its own slot, and this lever makes and writes nothing under .state/<name> any more), then omp's version is read under the same settings and omp acp start omp <version> cwd <task> repo <path> ref <rev> base <commit> logged, then the launch, then omp acp exit <status> push=<word>, the reaper's line, written only when omp ran; a log line that cannot be appended refuses by name. The three lines of one launch are in that order; between the start and the exit line the reaper appends one session cwd <original> mapped to <task> line per mapped request (the paragraph below). The launch. /usr/bin/env -i HOME PATH OMP_PROFILE=dsh CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/dev/null AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null HCOM_SEAT_SANDBOX=<slot> REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE [USER LANG when this process has them] <srt> --settings <slot>/settings.json -- /usr/bin/env PATH=<seat path> <python3> -I -S <acp-relay.py> --map-session-cwd <task> -- <omp> acp --profile dsh, in the slot's task, its stdin and stdout the connection, its stderr the file <slot>/stderr, in a process group of its own (job control on for the one start), so the reaper ends the mapper, omp and every descendant in that group with one signal; nothing else of this process's environment reaches srt, the mapper or omp, and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is unset before the first child (U312). HCOM_SEAT_SANDBOX makes hcom-seat and this lever refuse inside the worker. The outer PATH is the private tool directory and the system directories; inside, omp gets that list followed by this process's caller's absolute PATH entries (the construction of hcom-seat's seat path). The session cwd (regime-cutover U449b, table row s22; U449's trace /tmp/u449/trace.txt). dsh-subagent-acp names the Router's own task directory as the ACP session/new cwd (its lib/index.js request.cwd into session.new { cwd }), omp makes it the session cwd and claude-bridge spawns Claude Code there; the worker's settings deny the Router's state slot by design (R-45: no worker row names the Router's cwd), so Claude Code died at its spawn (An unknown error occurred (Unexpected), node's uv_cwd EPERM, M-21), while the same settings let it start and reach the API in the slot's task. The Router's cwd is untrusted input at the sandbox boundary, like the header's repository path: nothing is granted for it. The broker's side, which owns the slot's task, maps it: the launch runs the relay helper's second entry point acp-relay.py --map-session-cwd <task> -- <omp> acp --profile dsh inside the worker's sandbox under the pinned python (measured for U449b under the worker's rendered settings: python 3.15.2 runs there with the helper's imports, the helper's own pin check passes, hcom-seat's private copy directory reads), which copies the connection's bytes to omp's stdin line by line and rewrites exactly one shape, a session/new object whose params.cwd is a string, to the slot's task, leaving every other line byte for byte (acp-relay.py map_session_cwd, tested by table). The helper's pin is held here before the launch (relay_helper_check, the listener's check) and by the helper itself at its start. Each mapping is recorded on the mapper's stderr as acp-relay.py: session cwd <original, JSON-quoted> mapped to <task>; an inherited descriptor does not survive srt (measured: fd 6 is closed in the sandboxed child), so the launch's stderr is the file <slot>/stderr, opened by this process in the slot it made, and the reaper reads it once omp's group has ended, before the exit line: a line in the record's shape, anchored at its start, ending in mapped to <task> and free of control characters, becomes the launch-log line session cwd <original> mapped to <task> (the original stays JSON-quoted: the Router's string never reaches the log raw); every other line (omp's own stderr, which the mapper forwards with omp: before any line that begins like the record, srt's) goes to this process's stderr as it did before, at omp's end. The read is a plain redirection into a bounded loop (regime-cutover U449c, standing order 21): the first MiB, the open's status read and a file that cannot be opened named. The record is the mapper's alone: omp's stderr is a pipe the mapper drains, so no worker line is read as it. The push. When omp exits, the worker's HEAD goes back into the repository the header named as refs/acp-seat/<name>/<utc stamp>-<pid>, read and written the way the clone was, across two boundaries: the worker's git (worker_git, inside the worker's sandbox under the slot's settings, U343f) packs the commits above the base (pack-objects --revs --stdout, HEAD ^<base>) into the slot, and inside the Router's own sandbox index-pack --strict --stdin reads that descriptor into the repository and update-ref with the empty old value writes the new ref (an existing ref is never moved). The Router reads content, never a grant (R-45). A HEAD equal to the base pushes nothing (push=none); a step that fails names itself on stderr and the word is push=failed, never silent; a teardown by signal pushes nothing (push=skipped). The exit log line and the record carry the word. The exit report and the teardown (regime-cutover U343g, the mechanism-change row of 2026-11-10T04:18:01Z, form remove; verdict U343f-22a81500). The connection's byte stream carries exactly one broker line, the first, written before omp starts: acp-broker: refused: <reason> or acp-broker: record <id>, <id> the slot name acp-<name>-<stamp>-<pid>; every later byte is the worker's and reaches the client unread, so neither a worker's unterminated tail nor a worker line in any shape can become the broker's report. The report is a record file <seats-root>/.state/<router seat>/broker/<id>, in the broker directory: the Router's settings grant its state slot for read (hcom-seat's router row; the test's rendering holds it in allowRead) and deny the broker directory for write (U343i, the paragraph above), and no worker setting reaches it (the worker's denyRead is the Router's table with the seats root, its grants are the slot's task, the router group's Claude Code directory, the profile and ~/.omp/run, its allowUnixSockets empty; measured on this host for U343g: srt --settings <the Router's settings> -- /bin/cat <record> exits 0 with the content, the same read under a slot's settings fails with Operation not permitted). The group's Claude Code directory is worker-writable and never holds a record. The record is written by the reaper alone, never by the handler: its running form, present before omp starts, is ref=refs/acp-seat/<name>/<stamp>-<pid> and reaper=<pid>; its final form adds one line status=<omp's status when the handler reported it, else 2; 2 when the slot remains> push=<ref|none|failed|skipped>. The record's write (regime-cutover U343h; verdict U343g-8a049561 P1 :1262, class record-path). The broker directory lies in the Router's own state slot, which the Router's settings granted for write until U343i, and the Router learns <id> from the first line, so a path under that directory opened for write by this unsandboxed process followed whatever the Router had planted there: round 5's printf > <id>.tmp and its mv -f did. No bash of this lever redirects into, moves, copies or links a path under the broker directory. Both forms are written by the pinned helper acp-record-place.py beside this file (the form of hcom-seat's profile-config-place.py, U310d and U310f), run by the reaper as <pinned python3> -I -S <private copy> with the record's lines on its stdin: the listener reads the directory's device and inode once, right after its take (broker_dir_id, carried to each connection in ACP_BROKER_DIR_ID), and the helper opens the directory once with O_NOFOLLOW, refuses unless fstat gives that identity, this user and no group or other write bit, then unlinks <id>.tmp, creates it O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW 0600, writes, syncs and renames it onto <id>, every call relative to that descriptor (dir_fd), so a link planted at either name is removed or replaced as an entry and never followed. Before each run the reaper holds the helper (record_place): the path beside this file is no link and this user's regular file with no group or other write bit (record_helper_path_check, run by the handler before the slot is made); it is copied into a directory the reaper makes 0700 under hcom-seat's own state directory ~/.local/state/hcom-seat/, where hcom-seat keeps its tool links and its own helper copies and no seat's settings grant a write (record_helper_copy_make); the copy's sha256 must equal the claude.levers.sha256.acp-record-place.py pin of the manifest the self-check read (record_helper_pin_check); the copy goes after the run. A hold or a helper that fails is one stderr line and the write is not made: before the record line the handler refuses and no omp runs; after it the record keeps its running form and the client exits 2 naming <id>. The teardown is the reaper (connection_reaper): one subshell per connection, forked the moment the slot exists (regime-cutover U343o, verdict U343n-fd3db1b3 P1 :1581: until round 12 it was forked after the settings write, the clone, the canary and the version read, and a signal to the handler in that window, then a process with no trap, stranded the slot), outside omp's process group, with HUP, INT and TERM ignored, holding the connection's stdout and reading one control pipe (a FIFO in the slot, fd 4, closed for the reaper and for every long-lived child the handler starts; a printf, mkdir, mv or rm between the fork and omp's start holds it for its own run time alone) on which the handler writes start <pid> when omp runs, exited <status> when omp has exited and done <status> <word> after the push, or nothing (its death or its refusal closes the pipe). From the fork on the reaper alone removes the slot, in every path of its own: a running form the helper could not place (the slot removed, exit 1, no ready line), EOF or done before any start (no exit line, the slot removed, the record's final line status=2 push=skipped), done or EOF after start (omp's process group ended when one remains: TERM, kill -0 polled for the grace of reaper_grace seconds, then KILL; the exit line; the slot removed; the final line). The handler never removes the slot after the fork: refuse leaves it to the reaper, whose EOF follows the handler's exit. The readiness is a message, never the record's existence (verdict U343n-fd3db1b3 P1 :1657: a helper that renamed the record into place and then failed left a visible record while the reaper exited 1, and omp started with no reaper over a slot nobody removed): once record_place of the running form returned 0 the reaper writes one line ready <its pid> on a second FIFO in the slot (ready, fd 5, opened read-write by the handler before the fork so no open blocks, closed by the reaper after its write and by the handler after its read, so no later child inherits it), and the handler reads one line with a 10 s bound and refuses unless it is ready <the pid it forked>: a reaper that died, failed its placement or stayed silent starts no omp. The reaper's exit closes its stdout: the socket's close is the sign that the record is complete, and the connection's status is the record's. The slot has an owner at every instant (regime-cutover U343p, verdict U343o-c5c2b968 P1 :1648, class handler-window, form remove: a TERM to the handler between the slot's mkdir and the fork, during the two mkfifo and the two exec, still ended a process with no trap and stranded the slot; a window shorter than round 11's is a window). One trap for HUP, INT and TERM (slot_trap), armed right before the slot's mkdir and disarmed right after the ready line is read, for the making of the slot and the reaper's start alone, removes the slot as the state it is in says and exits 2, and touches neither omp nor the record nor the report: before slot_made=1 (a trap runs right after the simple command the signal arrived in, so the mkdir and the flag are two steps; regime-cutover U343q, verdict U343p-901e096a P1 :1669) the slot is at most the empty directory a bare mkdir leaves and /bin/rmdir takes exactly that (nothing non-empty, no file, no link), after the flag slot_remove takes whatever this connection made (idempotent: the reaper's own removal beside it is safe); from the fork to the ready line both it and the reaper may remove the slot, after that line the reaper alone, and no trap on HUP, INT or TERM exists in a connection once the reaper has reported ready: the relay's terminate and kill target the handler pid alone, so no signal that ends the handler reaches omp's end, the removal or the report. What the reaper cannot end, the two residuals of the body's threat table: a worker descendant that made a process group of its own (setsid, a daemonised tool), which stays inside the worker's sandbox and, when it holds stdout, keeps the connection open; and the reaper itself under SIGKILL, which strands the slot and leaves the record in its running form (the client exits 2 naming the record). The client reads the first line, copies the rest to its stdout and, after EOF, reads the record from the socket directory, prints acp-seat: push=<word> on stderr, unlinks the record and exits with status; a missing or incomplete record is exit 2 naming <id>. The broker's own end removes the records no client read and leaves the directory, hcom-seat's, standing (the client's own unlink of the record is refused by the deny row and prints one line until U344 removes it). Tools. srt, omp, python3 and git (and bwrap, socat, rg on Linux, which srt runs by path and which must be binaries) are taken from the private tool directory ~/.local/state/hcom-seat/tools that hcom-seat links on every launch, else from this process's caller's PATH, and run by their physical argv (pin_tool: every link followed, a #! script run by its physical interpreter, an interpreter that is itself a script refused, no mise shim, nothing under the seats root or the Router's scratch cwd); git must be a binary named git, since the isolated library runs it by name from its directory. Every input path (HOME, the seats root, the scratch cwd, the header's repository) and every path written into the settings is clean: absolute, components of [A-Za-z0-9._@+-], no . or .., no trailing /, since srt reads a settings path as a pattern. No caller PATH entry runs anything: the first statement sets PATH to the system directories. Refusals. A launch inside a seat (HCOM_LAUNCHED, HCOM_PROCESS_ID or HCOM_SEAT_SANDBOX set), an unclean or unresolvable path, a Router state slot or settings file that is absent, a link or another user's, a scratch cwd outside the Router's state slot, a template row that is no clean path, a grant that overlaps a deny, a ref that does not resolve in the repository as the Router reads it, a pack that does not index, a tool that cannot be pinned, a broker directory that is absent, a link, not this user's, not 0700 or not empty (U343i), and every failed producer (mkdir, a physical resolution, the template read, the identity, mode and listing reads, the settings write, the clone's reads, the canary, srt's version read, the log append) is exit 2 with the reason on stderr; in a connection the same line goes to the client first. Every producer's status is read (standing order 21); a failed read is never an absence.

<pre><code>#!/bin/bash
# @file acp-broker
# @brief Start omp workers in sibling srt sandboxes for a DSH control host that itself runs inside srt, one per connection on a Unix socket.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U343 (M-24 part 1, shape A of the U342 design note). srt does not nest (M-22), so the Router, the
#   dsh-superagent control host that `hcom-seat router` runs inside srt, cannot start a worker sandbox of its own.
#   This lever runs outside every sandbox as the operator's user, started by `hcom-seat` beside the Router (U344),
#   and listens on `<seats-root>/.state/<router seat>/broker/sock`, the one Unix socket the router row's
#   `network.allowUnixSockets` opens (U342 measured: that directory's sockets and nothing else). Inside the Router's
#   sandbox `dsh-subagent-acp` spawns the thin client `acp-seat`, which connects, sends one header line and relays

# @exitcode 0 The slot is gone, or none was made.
# @exitcode 1 The slot remains, named on stderr.
slot_remove() {
