    [[ ${p} == /* && ${p} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
    while :; do
        while [[ ! -e ${p} && ! -L ${p} ]]; do
            tail=/${p##*/}${tail}
            p=${p%/*}
            [[ -n ${p} ]] || p=/
        done
        [[ -L ${p} ]] || break
        n=$((n + 1))
        ((n <= 40)) || return 1
        link=$(/usr/bin/readlink "${p}" && printf .) || return 1
        link=${link%.}
        link=${link%$'\n'}
        [[ -n ${link} && ${link} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1
        case ${link} in
        /*) p=${link} ;;
        *) p=${p%/*}/${link} ;;
        esac
    done
    if [[ ${p} == / ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the root itself, whose `cd //` form pwd prints as `//`
        printf '%s\n' "${tail:-/}"
    elif [[ -d ${p} ]]; then
        dir=$(cd "${p}/" && pwd -P) || return 1
        printf '%s%s\n' "${dir%/}" "${tail}"
    else
        dir=$(cd "${p%/*}/" && pwd -P) || return 1
        printf '%s/%s%s\n' "${dir%/}" "${p##*/}" "${tail}"
    fi
}

# @description Print the physical, clean form of the path `$1` (physical_path, clean_path); the caller refuses
#   (exit 2) naming the path when this fails, so the refusal is never swallowed by a command substitution.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @stdout The physical path.
# @exitcode 1 The path cannot be resolved, or its physical form is not clean.
physical_clean() {
    local p
    p=$(physical_path "$1") || return 1
    clean_path "${p}" || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${p}"
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) naming `$1` when the path `$2` has no clean physical form (physical_clean).
# @arg $1 string What the path is.
# @arg $2 string The path.
unresolved() {
    refuse "cannot resolve $1 $2 to a clean physical path (absent components, a link that cannot be read, more than 40 links, or a component outside [A-Za-z0-9._@+-])"
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless `$2` is a real directory of this user: present, a directory, no symbolic link.
# @arg $1 string What the directory is.
# @arg $2 string The path.
require_own_dir() {
    [[ ! -L $2 ]] || refuse "$1 $2 is a symbolic link; it must be a real directory"
    [[ -d $2 ]] || refuse "$1 $2 is not a directory"
    [[ -O $2 ]] || refuse "$1 $2 is not this user's directory"
}

# @description Make the directory `$2` 0700 when absent and hold it to a real directory of this user. Two processes
#   at once (the Router's connections) may both find a shared parent absent; the loser of the mkdir race takes the
#   directory the winner made, held by the same check.
# @arg $1 string What the directory is.
# @arg $2 string The path.
ensure_own_dir() {
    if [[ ! -e $2 && ! -L $2 ]]; then
        /bin/mkdir "$2" || [[ -d $2 && ! -L $2 ]] || refuse "cannot create $1 $2"
    fi
    require_own_dir "$1" "$2"
}

# @description Set `ancestors` to the path `$1` and every directory above it, up to `/` (the walk of `hcom-seat`).
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @set ancestors The paths, `$1` first.
ancestors_of() {
    local p=$1 n=0
    [[ ${p} == /* && ${p} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
        refuse "'${p}' is not an absolute path free of control characters"
    ancestors=()
    while :; do
        ancestors+=("${p}")
        [[ ${p} != / ]] || return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow the walk ends at the root, no path compare
        n=$((n + 1))
        ((n <= 4096)) || refuse "the path ${1} has more than 4096 components"
        p=${p%/*}
        [[ -n ${p} ]] || p=/
    done
}

# @description Set the variable named `$2` to `$1` with A-Z made a-z (regime-cutover U95), by builtins only (a case
#   table, no `tr` and no locale; bash 3.2 has no `${x,,}`), so no producer's output is read back.
# @arg $1 string ASCII text.
# @arg $2 string The name of the variable to set.
# @exitcode 1 The variable cannot be set.
ascii_lower() {
    # The locals carry a prefix, so the caller's variable `$2` is never one of them (printf -v sets the nearest).
    local LC_ALL=C al_text=$1 al_out='' al_c al_before al_upper=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
    local al_lower=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
    [[ $2 != al_* && $2 != LC_ALL ]] || return 1
    while [[ -n ${al_text} ]]; do
        al_c=${al_text:0:1}
        al_text=${al_text:1}
        case ${al_c} in
        [ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ])
            al_before=${al_upper%%"${al_c}"*}
            al_c=${al_lower:${#al_before}:1}
            ;;
        esac
        al_out+=${al_c}
    done
    printf -v "$2" '%s' "${al_out}"
}

# @description Set `lines` to the lines of the text `$1`, by builtins alone: bash 3.2 (the `/bin/bash` the relay runs
#   each connection under) backs a here-string with a temporary file, so `read <<<` over a producer's output would
#   fail under a file size limit before the settings write does and name the wrong producer; no file is involved here.
# @arg $1 string Text; a trailing newline ends the last line and opens no empty one.
# @set lines The lines, in order; empty text gives none.
split_lines() {
    local text=$1
    lines=()
    while [[ -n ${text} ]]; do
        case ${text} in
        *$'\n'*) lines+=("${text%%$'\n'*}") text=${text#*$'\n'} ;;
        *) lines+=("${text}") text='' ;;
        esac
    done
}

# @description Fill the identity table for the physical paths `$@` (regime-cutover U95, the table of `hcom-seat`),
#   which every containment decision of the judgement reads: per path, whether it exists, the (device, inode)
#   identities of its deepest existing ancestor (the path itself when it exists) and of every directory above it, and
#   the absent remainder below that ancestor, ASCII case-folded by ascii_lower (builtins only). One `/usr/bin/stat`
#   (through xargs, order kept) serves every path. Fail-closed per record: every input must be a clean path; every
#   identity line must be `<dev>:<ino>`, and their number exactly what the ancestor walks asked for; every folded
#   remainder must have its input's length and the grammar `(/<lower-case component>)*/`; each table must hold one
#   entry per input.
# @set tbl_exists 1 or 0 per path.
# @set tbl_first The identity of the deepest existing ancestor per path.
# @set tbl_chain `\n<id>\n<id>…\n` per path: that ancestor's identity first, then each directory above it.
# @set tbl_rest The absent remainder per path, case-folded, ending in `/` (`/` when the path exists).
identity_table() {
    local p d rest ids line folded chain='' i=0 k=0 all=() counts=()
    tbl_exists=() tbl_first=() tbl_chain=() tbl_rest=()
    for p in "$@"; do
        require_clean_path 'a settings row' "${p}"
        # Absolute, so each step shortens it and the walk ends at `/`, which exists.
        d=${p} rest=''
        while [[ ! -e ${d} && ! -L ${d} ]]; do
            rest=/${d##*/}${rest}
            d=${d%/*}
            [[ -n ${d} ]] || d=/
        done
        if [[ -e ${p} ]]; then tbl_exists+=(1); else tbl_exists+=(0); fi
        ancestors_of "${d}"
        all+=("${ancestors[@]}")
        counts+=("${#ancestors[@]}")
        rest=${rest}/
        ascii_lower "${rest}" folded || refuse "cannot fold the absent part of ${p}"
        [[ ${#folded} == "${#rest}" && ${folded} =~ ^(/[a-z0-9._@+-]+)*/$ ]] ||
            refuse "cannot fold the absent part of ${p} ('${folded}')"
        tbl_rest+=("${folded}")
    done
    (($#)) || return 0
    ids=$(printf '%s\0' "${all[@]}" | /usr/bin/xargs -0 /usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" --) ||
        refuse "cannot read the identity of a settings row or a directory above it"
    split_lines "${ids}"
    for line in ${lines[@]+"${lines[@]}"}; do
        [[ ${line} =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "cannot read the identity of a settings row ('${line}')"
        ((i < ${#counts[@]})) || refuse 'more identities than settings rows were read'
        if ((k == 0)); then tbl_first+=("${line}"); fi
        chain+=${line}$'\n'
        k=$((k + 1))
        if ((k == counts[i])); then
            tbl_chain+=($'\n'"${chain}")
            chain='' k=0 i=$((i + 1))
        fi
    done
    ((i == $# && k == 0)) || refuse "cannot read the identity of every settings row (${i} of $#)"
    ((${#tbl_exists[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_first[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_chain[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_rest[@]} == $#)) ||
        refuse 'the identity table does not hold one entry per settings row'
}

# @description Decide from the identity table whether path `$2` is path `$1` or lies under it (regime-cutover U85,
#   U95), by identity for everything that exists, so a case alias on a case-insensitive volume is the path it aliases.
#   When `$1` exists: yes iff `$1`'s identity is in `$2`'s chain (`$2`'s deepest existing ancestor or a directory
#   above it). When `$1` does not exist, an existing `$2` cannot lie under it (no). When neither exists, `$2` can lie
#   under `$1` only if both have the same deepest existing ancestor; below it nothing exists, so no link or alias can
#   intervene, and the absent remainders decide: yes iff `$1`'s is `$2`'s or a prefix of it on a component boundary
#   (`a/b` is no prefix of `a/bc`), compared ASCII case-folded, since on a case-insensitive volume two spellings that
#   differ by case become one directory once made. No process runs.
# @arg $1 int The table index of the outer path.
# @arg $2 int The table index of the inner path.
# @exitcode 0 `$2` is `$1` or lies under it.
# @exitcode 1 It does not.
within_ix() {
    if ((tbl_exists[$1])); then
        [[ ${tbl_chain[$2]} == *$'\n'"${tbl_first[$1]}"$'\n'* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
        return
    fi
    ((! tbl_exists[$2])) || return 1
    [[ ${tbl_first[$1]} == "${tbl_first[$2]}" ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
    [[ ${tbl_rest[$2]} == "${tbl_rest[$1]}"* ]]              # lint-comparisons: allow absent components below one ancestor of the same identity, compared on component boundaries
}

# @description Set `phys_list` to the physical form of each absolute path `$@`, in order (regime-cutover U95), or
#   refuse (exit 2), in one subshell for all of them, present or absent (physical_path). Fail-closed per record: the
#   subshell writes exactly one record per path, the physical path or `fail`, and fails when a record cannot be
#   written; each record is checked against the clean-path grammar and assigned to its own index. Anything else, a
#   record too many or too few, or an index left without its result refuses.
# @arg $@ string Absolute paths.
# @set phys_list The physical paths, one per input.
physical_each() {
    local out line i=0 args=("$@")
    phys_list=()
    (($#)) || return 0
    out=$(for p in "$@"; do
        physical_path "${p}" || printf 'fail\n' || exit 1
    done) || refuse 'cannot resolve the settings rows (the resolving subshell failed)'
    split_lines "${out}"
    for line in ${lines[@]+"${lines[@]}"}; do
        ((i < $#)) || refuse 'cannot resolve the settings rows (more records than rows)'
        [[ ${line} != fail ]] || refuse "cannot resolve the settings row ${args[i]}"
        clean_path "${line}" || refuse "the settings row ${args[i]} resolves to '${line}', not a clean absolute path"
        phys_list[i]=${line}
        i=$((i + 1))
    done
    ((i == $# && ${#phys_list[@]} == $#)) || refuse "cannot resolve every settings row (${#phys_list[@]} of $#)"
}

# @description Judge the worker's grants against its denies (regime-cutover U343c; the settings_judge of `hcom-seat`,
#   U272f and U272g, whose rows the worker's are): every row of `allow_read` and `allow_write` against every row of
#   `deny_read` and `deny_write` (the macOS write patterns are not rows), and nothing else is the boundary. Every row
#   is resolved to its physical form first (physical_each: a link at the end of a row hides its ancestry from the
#   identity table), the table is filled once (identity_table), and a grant that is, contains or lies inside a deny
#   (within_ix either way) is a hit unless the pair is structural: both rows carry the same tag and the grant lies
#   where the role spells it (its physical path is the path in `allow_read_spelled` or `allow_write_spelled`). The
#   tags are the dsh row's, assigned by construction since this lever reads the deny table instead of rendering it:
#   the grants carry `slot` for the task cwd and the router group's Claude Code directory and `profile` for the omp profile
#   (`allow_read_tags`, `allow_write_tags`); a denyRead row carries `slot` when it has the identity of the seats root
#   or of `~/.local/state/omp-seats` and `profile` when it has the identity of `~/.omp/profiles` (the three
#   references resolved and tabled with the rows); a denyWrite row carries `slot` when it lies strictly inside a
#   slot-tagged grant (the project-file rows under the task cwd, the configuration rows under the group's directory)
#   or when it has the identity of a slot-tagged read grant that is no write grant (the seats' API key file, which
#   hcom-seat grants for read and denies for write under one tag, U512; U516).
#   A profile that is a link elsewhere is spelled `~/.omp/profiles/dsh` and resolves elsewhere, so its tag exempts
#   nothing and it is judged like any row. The read grants go first, so the first hit names the row as the role
#   spells it.
# @set judge_grant The first grant that hits: `<kind> row <spelled path>` and, when it differs, its physical path in
#   parentheses; empty when every grant is clear.
# @set judge_deny The deny it hits: `<path>[ (<physical>)], a row of its <kind> list`; empty when clear.
# @exitcode 0 Every grant keeps clear of every deny it is not structurally paired with.
# @exitcode 1 A pair overlaps; `judge_grant` and `judge_deny` name it.
settings_judge() {
    local i j k n m rows=() kinds=() spelled=() tags=() refs=() ref_tags=(slot slot profile)
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#allow_read[@]}; i++)); do
        rows+=("${allow_read[i]}") kinds+=(allowRead) spelled+=("${allow_read_spelled[i]}") tags+=("${allow_read_tags[i]}")
    done
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#allow_write[@]}; i++)); do
        rows+=("${allow_write[i]}") kinds+=(allowWrite) spelled+=("${allow_write_spelled[i]}") tags+=("${allow_write_tags[i]}")
    done
    n=${#rows[@]}
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#deny_read[@]}; i++)); do
        rows+=("${deny_read[i]}") kinds+=(denyRead) spelled+=("${deny_read[i]}") tags+=('')
    done
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#deny_write[@]}; i++)); do
        [[ ${deny_write[i]} != *\** ]] || continue # lint-comparisons: allow a pattern test on one row, no path compare
        rows+=("${deny_write[i]}") kinds+=(denyWrite) spelled+=("${deny_write[i]}") tags+=('')
    done
    m=$((${#rows[@]} - n))
    judge_grant='' judge_deny=''
    ((n && m)) || return 0
    # The structural references take the table positions after the rows: the seats root, the default seats parent
    # and the profiles directory, each tagged as hcom-seat tags the deny row it renders there.
    refs=("${seats_real}" "${h}/.local/state/omp-seats" "${h}/.omp/profiles")
    physical_each "${rows[@]}" "${refs[@]}"
    identity_table "${phys_list[@]}"
    for ((j = n; j < n + m; j++)); do
        case ${kinds[j]} in
        denyRead)
            for ((k = 0; k < ${#refs[@]}; k++)); do
                i=$((n + m + k))
                if within_ix "${i}" "${j}" && within_ix "${j}" "${i}"; then tags[j]=${ref_tags[k]}; fi
            done
            ;;
        *)
            for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
                [[ ${tags[i]} == slot ]] || continue # lint-comparisons: allow a tag word, no path compare
                if within_ix "${i}" "${j}" && ! within_ix "${j}" "${i}"; then tags[j]=slot; fi
                # The seats' API key file (U516): hcom-seat grants it for read and denies it for write under one tag
                # (U512), so a deny row with the identity of a slot-tagged read grant is that row; the identity of a
                # write grant stays a hit (a write granted and denied is a contradiction, not a pair), the write
                # grants coming after the read grants in the table.
                if within_ix "${i}" "${j}" && within_ix "${j}" "${i}"; then
                    if [[ ${kinds[i]} == allowRead ]]; then tags[j]=slot; else tags[j]=''; fi # lint-comparisons: allow a kind word, no path compare
                fi
            done
            ;;
        esac
    done
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        for ((j = n; j < n + m; j++)); do
            within_ix "${j}" "${i}" || within_ix "${i}" "${j}" || continue
            if [[ -n ${tags[i]} && ${tags[i]} == "${tags[j]}" && ${phys_list[i]} == "${spelled[i]}" ]]; then continue; fi # lint-comparisons: allow two tag words, and one row's spelled and physical forms from the same physical producers; the overlap was decided by identity above
            judge_grant="${kinds[i]} row ${spelled[i]}"
            judge_deny=${rows[j]}
            # The same row in two spellings when the spelled one goes through a link; the reader needs both.
            [[ ${phys_list[i]} == "${spelled[i]}" ]] || judge_grant+=" (${phys_list[i]})" # lint-comparisons: allow one row's spelled and physical forms, both from physical producers, no decision rests on it
            [[ ${phys_list[j]} == "${rows[j]}" ]] || judge_deny+=" (${phys_list[j]})"     # lint-comparisons: allow one row's rendered and physical forms, both from physical producers, no decision rests on it
            judge_deny+=", a row of its ${kinds[j]} list"
            return 1
        done
    done
}

os=$(/usr/bin/uname -s) || refuse 'cannot read the operating system name (uname -s)'
case ${os} in
Darwin) lstat_args=(-f '%d:%i') stat_args=(-L -f '%d:%i') mode_args=(-L -f '%Lp') ;;
Linux)
    lstat_args=(-c '%d:%i') stat_args=(-L -c '%d:%i') mode_args=(-L -c '%a')
    [[ -x /usr/bin/jq ]] || refuse 'the system jq /usr/bin/jq is absent; it reads the Router settings on Linux (apt install jq)'
    ;;
*) refuse "no worker sandbox for ${os}; srt supports macOS and Linux" ;;
esac

# The seats' API key file (regime-cutover U516; handoff/47, U510, U512): REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE as hcom-seat's
# router row set it in the sandbox environment this process runs in (the listener, and every connection through the
# relay), held as data: this lever reads no key, names the path in every worker's environment beside CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
# (where `claude-keyed`, the bridge's Claude Code executable, reads it) and grants its physical path for read. The key
# is a worker's precondition, not the broker's (regime-cutover U516c): the listener starts and listens whatever the
# variable holds, so a launcher that predates U512 (hcom-seat on main sets no such row) still runs the Router, and
# each worker connection is judged here, after its header's shape (a header refusal names the header, as before) and
# before the settings writer is sourced and anything of the worker is made (no state directory, no copy, no slot, no
# task directory, no log line, no socket to omp; verdict U516-a5ea975b P2 :1001). Fail closed, as `claude-keyed`
# refuses: unset or empty, not a clean absolute path, a symbolic link, not a regular file of this user, not mode 0600,
# or a spelling whose physical path is not clean is one line naming the variable and the handout on the stream and on
# stderr, exit 2 of that connection alone; the broker keeps listening. Nothing of the writer's is used before it is
# sourced: early_clean_path spells the path rule, `stat` by the OS table's flag reads the mode, physical_path
# (builtins and readlink) the physical form.
if ((connection)); then
    # One connection: the header line first, from the connection's bytes, at most 1024 characters with its newline (a
    # clean header is shorter); bash reads a pipe one byte at a time, so omp inherits the stream right after the line.
    # `read -n 1025` stops at the newline or after 1025 characters, so a line read whole is at most 1024 long and a
    # longer one, or one whose newline did not arrive, is refused (verdict U343d-136fbe0a P2 :953: nothing after a
    # padded prefix reaches omp).
    # A file size limit must fail a write (EFBIG) and refuse by name, never end this process by SIGXFSZ with the slot
    # behind; the relay restores the signal's default in every handler, so the disposition is set here.
    trap '' XFSZ
    header=''
    IFS= read -r -n 1025 header || refuse 'no header line arrived before the connection closed'
    ((${#header} <= 1024)) || refuse 'the header exceeds 1024 characters, or its newline did not arrive within them'
    f1='' f2='' f3='' f4='' f5='' extra=''
    read -r f1 f2 f3 f4 f5 extra <<< "${header}" || refuse 'cannot split the header line into its fields'
    [[ ${f1} == ACP-SEAT && ${f2} == v1 ]] || refuse "the header '${header}' does not begin 'ACP-SEAT v1'"
    [[ ${f3} == repo=?* ]] || refuse "the header '${header}' has no 'repo=<path>' third field"
    [[ ${f4} == ref=?* ]] || refuse "the header '${header}' has no 'ref=<rev>' fourth field"
    [[ ${f5} == name=?* ]] || refuse "the header '${header}' has no 'name=<name>' fifth field"
    [[ -z ${extra} ]] || refuse "the header '${header}' has more than five fields"
    key_handout="place the seats' API key file by the U510 handout (handouts/anthropic-api-key-u510.md)"
    [[ -n ${REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE:-} ]] ||
        refuse "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE did not reach this connection; the broker runs inside the Router's sandbox, whose environment hcom-seat sets, and no worker starts without the seats' API key; ${key_handout}"
    key_file=${REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE}
    # The one refusal that may carry an unclean path shows it with every line boundary as a space, so the line stays
    # one line whatever the variable holds (verdict U516-a5ea975b P3 :1004: a newline in it printed two lines).
    key_shown=${key_file//[$'\r\n']/ }
    early_clean_path "${key_file}" || refuse "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE '${key_shown}' is not a clean absolute path; no worker starts without the seats' API key; ${key_handout}"
    [[ ! -L ${key_file} ]] || refuse "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE ${key_file} is a symbolic link; the seats' API key file is a regular file of this user; ${key_handout}"
    [[ -f ${key_file} && -O ${key_file} ]] || refuse "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE ${key_file} is not a regular file of this user; ${key_handout}"
    # The mode, read with its status (standing order 21): the handout places the file 0600, and a key file its group
    # or others may read or write is refused by its mode. The producer's own diagnostic is captured (regime-cutover
    # U516d, verdict U516c-23f4f25b P3 :1022): a key removed, or its directory made unsearchable, between the test
    # above and this read made stat's line precede the refusal, and the refusal is the one stderr line.
    key_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat "${mode_args[@]}" -- "${key_file}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE ${key_file}: cannot read its mode; ${key_handout}"
    [[ ${key_mode} == 600 ]] || refuse "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE ${key_file} has mode ${key_mode}, not 0600 (the handout places the seats' API key file 0600); ${key_handout}" # lint-comparisons: allow a mode word from stat, no path compare
    # The physical form, its producer's status read (standing order 21) and its diagnostic captured (U516d: the `cd`
    # inside physical_path names a directory it cannot enter): a resolution that fails leaves no path, and no path
    # is clean, so the one refusal names both (verdict U516-a5ea975b P3 :1007: the shared unresolved() named no
    # handout).
    key_real=$(physical_path "${key_file}" 2> /dev/null) || key_real=''
    early_clean_path "${key_real}" ||
        refuse "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE ${key_file} cannot be resolved to a clean physical path (a link that cannot be read, more than 40 links, or a component outside [A-Za-z0-9._@+-]); no worker starts without the seats' API key; ${key_handout}"
fi

# The one settings writer (regime-cutover U344; U344c), sourced before any row is checked or rendered, from the private
# copy renderer_source makes, hashes and removes: what is hashed is what is sourced, and a rewritten writer stops the
# broker before its first line.
renderer_source

# Every input path is clean before anything is resolved, created or run.
require_clean_path HOME "${HOME}"
require_clean_path 'the seats root' "${seats_root}"
require_clean_path "the Router's scratch cwd" "${scratch}"
[[ ${router} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || refuse "the Router seat name '${router}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$"
case ${router} in
claude | claude-*) refuse "the seat name '${router}' is taken by the Claude Code login directories <seats-root>/.state/claude-<group> (and the legacy <seats-root>/.state/claude), not a Router" ;;
esac

# srt 0.0.81 keeps its own TMPDIR writable whatever the policy says (SANDBOX_OWN_WRITE_PATHS, sandbox-utils.js:499-508
# lists both on every OS); /private exists on macOS alone, and on Linux srt binds only what exists (hcom-seat
# srt_tmp_roots_for), so the second root stays there only when it exists. Each word is spelled once, as the
# portability guard's rows for this file admit it (tests/unit/test_sandbox_portability.py ALLOWED_TMP).
srt_tmp_roots=(/tmp/claude /private/tmp/claude)
if [[ ${os} != Darwin && ! -e ${srt_tmp_roots[1]} ]]; then srt_tmp_roots=("${srt_tmp_roots[0]}"); fi

h=$(physical_clean "${HOME}") || unresolved HOME "${HOME}"
# The Router's credential root (regime-cutover U353; U343l): `<DSH_HOME>/router-credentials`, the directory the agent
# account's gh login lives under, which the Router reads (its allowRead row) and no worker may (srt allows reads by
# default, hcom-seat's U353b comment). Held once, here, in hcom-seat's form (cred_home_hold, cred_root_hold):
# DSH_HOME is the Router's home as hcom-seat set it in the sandbox environment this process runs in (the listener,
# and every connection through the relay), set and non-empty else refused by name; the root is its physical path
# under the physical home, a clean path, a real directory of this user and no link, else refused by name. Nothing
# resolves it again: the worker's denyRead carries `cred_root_real` verbatim, and the Router's own denyWrite must
# carry the same row (checked once the template is read).
[[ -n ${DSH_HOME:-} ]] || refuse "DSH_HOME did not reach this connection; the broker runs inside the Router's sandbox, whose environment hcom-seat sets"
require_clean_path DSH_HOME "${DSH_HOME}"
cred_home_real=$(physical_clean "${DSH_HOME}") || unresolved DSH_HOME "${DSH_HOME}"
cred_root_real=$(physical_clean "${cred_home_real}/router-credentials") || unresolved "the Router's credential root" "${cred_home_real}/router-credentials"
require_clean_path "the Router's credential root" "${cred_root_real}"
[[ -d ${cred_root_real} && ! -L ${cred_root_real} && -O ${cred_root_real} ]] ||
    refuse "the Router's credential root ${cred_root_real} is not a real directory of this user"
seats_real=$(physical_clean "${seats_root}") || unresolved 'the seats root' "${seats_root}"
require_own_dir 'the seats root' "${seats_real}"
state_dir=${seats_real}/.state/${router}
require_own_dir "the Router's state slot" "${state_dir}"
scratch_real=$(physical_clean "${scratch}") || unresolved "the Router's scratch cwd" "${scratch}"
[[ -d ${scratch_real} ]] || refuse "the Router's scratch cwd ${scratch} resolves to ${scratch_real}, which is not a directory"
# The scratch cwd lies inside the Router's own state slot (hcom-seat's directory row for the router role), so every
# task cwd, a directory strictly under it, lies there too; both sides physical, the trailing slash makes the prefix
# a whole component.
[[ ${scratch_real}/ == "${state_dir}"/* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both operands physical (physical_path); the trailing slash makes the prefix a whole component
    refuse "the Router's scratch cwd ${scratch} resolves to ${scratch_real}, outside the Router's state slot ${state_dir}"
# The Router's settings, hcom-seat's rendering of the dsh row with the router cells for this launch: the worker's
# deny table is read from them (template_rows) and nothing is derived from the file's spelling.
template=${seats_real}/.sandbox/${router}/srt-settings.json
[[ ! -L ${template} ]] || refuse "the Router's settings ${template} is a symbolic link"
[[ -f ${template} ]] || refuse "the Router's settings ${template} is absent or not a regular file (hcom-seat renders it on the Router's launch)"
[[ -O ${template} ]] || refuse "the Router's settings ${template} is not this user's file"
# The workers' Claude Code directory (regime-cutover U498b; verdict U498-e08ce84c: until this head the legacy
# `<seats-root>/.state/claude` of U318, which hcom-seat makes no more since U498, so every connection on a fresh seats
# root refused, and the legacy grant carried none of the configuration denies). The Router's subagent workers are the
# Router's own processes, so they belong to the router login group, `<seats-root>/.state/claude-router`: the group
# hcom-seat's `login_group_of_role` (and the preflight's copy of the table) gives the dsh and router roles, one constant
# here since this lever runs for the Router alone. hcom-seat makes the directory on the Router's launch (the connection
# refuses below when it is absent); the eight configuration rows under it come from the Router's own denyWrite table
# (checked once the template is read). The legacy directory is named, read, granted and made by nothing here.
claude_config=${seats_real}/.state/claude-router
[[ ! -L ${claude_config} ]] || refuse "the router group's Claude Code directory ${claude_config} is a symbolic link; it must be a real directory"
claude_real=$(physical_clean "${claude_config}") || unresolved "the router group's Claude Code directory" "${claude_config}"
broker_dir=${state_dir}/broker
sock=${broker_dir}/sock
tools_dir=${h}/.local/state/hcom-seat/tools
tools_real=''
if [[ -e ${tools_dir} || -L ${tools_dir} ]]; then
    require_own_dir 'the private tool directory' "${tools_dir}"
    tools_real=$(physical_clean "${tools_dir}") || unresolved 'the private tool directory' "${tools_dir}"
fi

# @description Set `rows` to the entries of the Router settings' `filesystem.$1` list, read whole by the system's
#   reader (`/usr/bin/plutil … json` on macOS, which escapes `/` as `\/`; `/usr/bin/jq -c` on Linux) and parsed here
#   from the one JSON array text: each element a double-quoted string holding no quote and no backslash once `\/` is
#   undone, each then a clean row (clean_row). Fail-closed: a failed read, a text that is no array of such strings,
#   or a row that is not clean refuses (exit 2) naming the file and the list.
# @arg $1 string The list: denyRead or denyWrite.
# @set rows The entries, in the file's order.
template_rows() {
    local list=$1 text rest item patterns=0 slash_esc='\/'
    [[ ${list} != denyWrite ]] || patterns=1
    case ${os} in
    Darwin) text=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract "filesystem.${list}" json -o - "${template}") || refuse "cannot read filesystem.${list} from the Router's settings ${template}" ;;
    *) text=$(/usr/bin/jq -c ".filesystem.${list}" "${template}") || refuse "cannot read filesystem.${list} from the Router's settings ${template}" ;;
    esac
    text=${text%$'\n'}
    [[ ${text} == \[*\] ]] || refuse "filesystem.${list} in the Router's settings ${template} is not a JSON array ('${text}')"
    rest=${text#\[}
    rest=${rest%\]}
    rows=()
    while [[ -n ${rest} ]]; do
        [[ ${rest} == \"* ]] || refuse "filesystem.${list} in the Router's settings ${template} holds an element that is no string ('${rest}')"
        rest=${rest#\"}
        [[ ${rest} == *\"* ]] || refuse "filesystem.${list} in the Router's settings ${template} holds an unterminated string"
        item=${rest%%\"*}
        rest=${rest#*\"}
        item=${item//"${slash_esc}"/\/}
        clean_row "${item}" "${patterns}" || refuse "filesystem.${list} in the Router's settings ${template} holds '${item}', not a clean absolute path"
        rows+=("${item}")
        case ${rest} in
        '') ;;
        ,\"*) rest=${rest#,} ;;
        *) refuse "filesystem.${list} in the Router's settings ${template} is malformed after '${item}'" ;;
        esac
    done
}

# @description Print the first executable `$1` in the private tool directory (hcom-seat's links), else on the caller's
#   PATH; the private directory first, so the tool hcom-seat checked on the Router's launch is the one a worker runs.
# @arg $1 string The command name.
# @stdout The path, symlinks not yet followed.
# @exitcode 1 None found.
# @exitcode 2 The caller's PATH could not be split into directories (the `read` failed; standing order 21).
find_tool() {
    local path_dir path_dirs=()
    if [[ -n ${tools_real} && -x ${tools_real}/$1 && ! -d ${tools_real}/$1 ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${tools_real}/$1"
        return 0
    fi
    IFS=: read -r -a path_dirs <<< "${caller_path}" || return 2
    for path_dir in ${path_dirs[@]+"${path_dirs[@]}"}; do
        [[ ${path_dir} == /* && ${path_dir} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || continue # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
        [[ -x ${path_dir}/$1 && ! -d ${path_dir}/$1 ]] || continue
        printf '%s\n' "${path_dir}/$1"
        return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) a tool file that a seat could rewrite: one that is or lies under the seats root or
#   the Router's scratch cwd (both physical, prefix on a whole component), or a mise shim (named mise, or found in or
#   resolving to a `shims` directory, as scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh decides it), which reads the cwd's config.
# @arg $1 string A label for the refusal.
# @arg $2 string The path the tool was found at.
# @arg $3 string Its physical file.
tool_place_check() {
    local d
    [[ ${3}/ != "${seats_real}"/* && ${3}/ != "${scratch_real}"/* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both operands physical (physical_path); the trailing slash makes the prefix a whole component
        refuse "$1 $3 lies under the seats root or the Router's scratch cwd, where a seat could rewrite it"
    [[ ${3##*/} != [Mm][Ii][Ss][Ee] ]] || refuse "$1 $3 is mise itself" # lint-comparisons: allow a file-name test, not a comparison of two paths
    for d in "${2%/*}" "${3%/*}"; do
        d=$(physical_path "${d:-/}") || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of $1 $2"
        [[ ${d}/ != */[Ss][Hh][Ii][Mm][Ss]/* ]] || refuse "no $1 from a shims directory ('$2'): a mise shim picks its version from the cwd" # lint-comparisons: allow a directory-name test, not a comparison of two paths
    done
}

# @description Resolve the tool `$1` to the argv that runs it with no lookup left (hcom-seat pin_exec): its physical
#   file (find_tool, physical_path), preceded by the physical interpreter when it is a `#!` script (`#!/abs/interp`
#   or `#!/usr/bin/env <name>`, no arguments; the name found as a tool is; an interpreter that is itself a script is
#   refused). Each file passes tool_place_check. A failure exits 2 naming `$1`.
# @arg $1 string The tool's name.
# @set pinned The argv.
pin_tool() {
    local label=$1 found file first magic interp name extra interp_path status=0
    # The lookup's status is read (standing order 21): 2 is a failed split of the caller's PATH, 1 is none found.
    found=$(find_tool "$1") || status=$?
    ((status != 2)) || refuse "cannot split the caller's PATH into directories while resolving ${label}"
    ((status == 0)) || refuse "${label} not found in the private tool directory ${tools_dir} or on the caller's PATH; run hcom-seat once (make update)"
    file=$(physical_path "${found}") || refuse "cannot resolve ${label} to a physical file: ${found}"
    [[ -f ${file} && -x ${file} && -r ${file} ]] || refuse "${label} ${found} resolves to ${file}, not a readable executable file"
    tool_place_check "${label}" "${found}" "${file}"
    # Each read's status is checked (pipefail covers head; /usr/bin/od only formats): a failed read is refused, never
    # taken for a file without an interpreter line.
    magic=$(/usr/bin/head -c 2 -- "${file}" | /usr/bin/od -An -tx1) || refuse "cannot read ${label}: ${file}"
    first=''
    if [[ ${magic//[[:space:]]/} == 2321 ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the hex bytes of `#!`, no path compare
        first=$(/usr/bin/head -n 1 -- "${file}") || refuse "cannot read the interpreter line of ${label}: ${file}"
    fi
    pinned=("${file}")
    case ${first} in
    '#!'*)
        extra=''
        read -r interp name extra <<< "${first#??}" || refuse "cannot split the interpreter line of ${label}: ${file}"
        if [[ ${interp} == /usr/bin/env ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the literal interpreter line, no path compare
            [[ -n ${name} && -z ${extra} && ${name} != -* ]] ||
                refuse "${label}: unsupported interpreter line '${first}' in ${file}"
            status=0
            interp_path=$(find_tool "${name}") || status=$?
            ((status != 2)) || refuse "cannot split the caller's PATH into directories while resolving the interpreter ${name} of ${label}"
            ((status == 0)) || refuse "${label}: interpreter ${name} not found in the private tool directory or on the caller's PATH"
        else
            [[ -z ${name} ]] || refuse "${label}: unsupported interpreter line '${first}' in ${file}"
            [[ ${interp} == /* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path test
                refuse "${label}: interpreter line '${first}' in ${file} names no absolute path"
            interp_path=${interp}
        fi
        interp=$(physical_path "${interp_path}") || refuse "cannot resolve the interpreter of ${label}: ${interp_path}"
        [[ -f ${interp} && -x ${interp} && -r ${interp} ]] || refuse "the interpreter of ${label}, ${interp_path}, resolves to ${interp}, not a readable executable file"
        tool_place_check "the interpreter of ${label}" "${interp_path}" "${interp}"
        magic=$(/usr/bin/head -c 2 -- "${interp}" | /usr/bin/od -An -tx1) || refuse "cannot read the interpreter of ${label}: ${interp}"
        [[ ${magic//[[:space:]]/} != 2321 ]] || refuse "${label}: its interpreter ${interp} is itself a script" # lint-comparisons: allow the hex bytes of `#!`, no path compare
        pinned=("${interp}" "${file}")
        ;;
    esac
}

# The tools, by their physical argv, before anything is made: the deny table is read once here too, so a Router
# settings file that does not read refuses the broker before it listens and a connection before its slot exists.
pin_tool srt
srt_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
pin_tool omp
omp_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
pin_tool python3
python_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
# git, for the clone and the push: a binary named `git`, so the isolated library's `exec git` from its directory runs
# this file and no other (find_tool: the private tool directory hcom-seat links first, then the caller's PATH).
pin_tool git
((${#pinned[@]} == 1)) || refuse "git ${pinned[1]} is a script; the broker runs git by its binary alone"
git_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
[[ ${git_cmd[0]##*/} == git ]] || refuse "git resolves to ${git_cmd[0]}, whose name is not git; the isolated library runs git by name from its directory" # lint-comparisons: allow a file-name test, not a comparison of two paths
git_dir=${git_cmd[0]%/*}
require_clean_path "git's directory" "${git_dir}"
linux_tools=''
if [[ ${os} == Linux ]]; then
    # srt runs bwrap, socat and rg by the paths the settings name, so each must be a binary (no interpreter lookup).
    bwrap_real='' socat_real='' rg_real=''
    for tool in bwrap socat rg; do
        pin_tool "${tool}"
        ((${#pinned[@]} == 1)) || refuse "${tool} ${pinned[1]} is a script; srt runs it by path, so it must be a binary"
        case ${tool} in
        bwrap) bwrap_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        socat) socat_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        rg) rg_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        esac
    done
    require_clean_path bwrap "${bwrap_real}"
    require_clean_path socat "${socat_real}"
    require_clean_path rg "${rg_real}"
    linux_tools=",\"bwrapPath\":\"${bwrap_real}\",\"socatPath\":\"${socat_real}\",\"ripgrep\":{\"command\":\"${rg_real}\"}"
else
    [[ -x /usr/bin/sandbox-exec ]] || refuse 'sandbox-exec absent: /usr/bin/sandbox-exec'
fi
template_rows denyRead
template_deny_read=("${rows[@]}")
template_rows denyWrite
template_deny_write=(${rows[@]+"${rows[@]}"})
# The two levers name one root (regime-cutover U343l): hcom-seat's router row denies writing the credential root it
# held (U353), so the Router's denyWrite carries the root this process held, or the two disagree (another DSH_HOME
# reached this process than the Router's launch, or another hcom-seat rendered the settings) and the connection
# refuses before anything is made.
cred_root_denied=0
for row in ${template_deny_write[@]+"${template_deny_write[@]}"}; do
    if [[ ${row} == "${cred_root_real}" ]]; then cred_root_denied=1; fi # lint-comparisons: allow both operands physical (hcom-seat renders its rows physical, cred_root_real is physical_clean); an identity test of one row
done
((cred_root_denied)) || refuse "the Router's settings deny no write of its credential root ${cred_root_real}; hcom-seat and this lever disagree on the root"
# The two levers name one login directory (regime-cutover U498b): hcom-seat's router row denies writing the eight
# configuration rows (SEAT_SETTINGS_CLAUDE_ROWS, the one writer's table: the settings files, rules, hooks, plugins,
# skills, commands and agents) under the router group's directory it derived, so the Router's denyWrite carries each of
# them under the directory this process derived, or the two disagree (another hcom-seat rendered the settings, or one
# that still spelled the legacy directory) and the connection refuses before anything is made. The worker's denyWrite
# is the Router's table (deny_write below), so the eight rows reach the worker's settings under its grant of the
# directory through it, and the grant carries what hcom-seat's router row carries (verdict U498-e08ce84c P1
# hcom-seat:2062).
for path in "${SEAT_SETTINGS_CLAUDE_ROWS[@]}"; do
    claude_row_denied=0
    for row in ${template_deny_write[@]+"${template_deny_write[@]}"}; do
        if [[ ${row} == "${claude_real}/${path}" ]]; then claude_row_denied=1; fi # lint-comparisons: allow both operands physical (hcom-seat renders its rows physical, claude_real is physical_clean); an identity test of one row
    done
    ((claude_row_denied)) || refuse "the Router's settings deny no write of ${claude_real}/${path}; hcom-seat and this lever disagree on the router group's Claude Code directory"
done

# The worker's PATH inside the sandbox: the private tool directory and the system directories, then the caller's
# absolute entries (hcom-seat's seat path); outside, srt itself runs with the first two alone.
outer_path=${tools_real:+${tools_real}:}${system_path}
seat_path=${outer_path}
IFS=: read -r -a caller_dirs <<< "${caller_path}" || refuse "cannot split the caller's PATH into directories for the worker's seat path"
for caller_dir in ${caller_dirs[@]+"${caller_dirs[@]}"}; do
    if [[ ${caller_dir} == /* && ${caller_dir} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]]; then seat_path+=:${caller_dir}; fi # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
done

# @description Remove the leftover records after the listener ended (the normal end and the trap), once the socket is
#   gone: every record left by a connection whose client never read it (a reaper's temporary file included;
#   regime-cutover U343g), each failure named. The socket is the relay's alone (regime-cutover U343j, verdict
#   U343i-76a5c83b P1 :1061): it binds `sock` and removes it at its end, so a socket that stands here, after the
#   relay's end, is another broker's listener (the relay lost the bind: two brokers passed the take, a check before
#   the bind, and the loser's relay refused) or one the relay could not remove (it said so), and the records beside
#   it are that broker's; then nothing is removed, the socket is named and the function fails. The directory is
#   hcom-seat's and stands (regime-cutover U343i: no `rmdir`; the Router's settings deny it for write, so no link and
#   no rename of it can stand at these names, and the launch's slot removal takes it with the Router's state slot).
# @exitcode 0 The socket is gone and every record is removed.
# @exitcode 1 The socket stands, named on stderr; nothing was removed.
# @exitcode 2 The socket is gone and a record could not be removed (regime-cutover U344b, verdicts U343j-62c10228 P3
#   :1000 and U343l-426188c6 P3 :1028: until this head the failure was named and the function returned 0), each named
#   on stderr as `cannot remove the exit record <path>` and the remaining records named once more at the end.
broker_cleanup() {
    local entry remaining=()
    path_presence "${sock}"
    ((! slot_present)) || {
        echo "acp-broker: the socket ${sock} stands after the relay's end (another broker's listener, or one the relay could not remove); this broker removes nothing in ${broker_dir}" >&2
        return 1
    }
    for entry in "${broker_dir}"/acp-*; do
        [[ -e ${entry} || -L ${entry} ]] || continue
        /bin/rm -f -- "${entry}" || {
            echo "acp-broker: cannot remove the exit record ${entry}" >&2
            remaining+=("${entry}")
        }
    done
    ((${#remaining[@]} == 0)) || {
        echo "acp-broker: ${#remaining[@]} exit record(s) remain in ${broker_dir} after the removal (${remaining[*]}); remove them by hand" >&2
        return 2
    }
}

# @description The listener's signal trap: a hangup, interrupt or termination ends the relay (and, through it, every
#   worker it started; the relay removes its socket), removes the records once the socket is gone and then ends this
#   process by the same signal, its disposition restored; a socket that stands, or a record that could not be
#   removed, is exit 2 whatever the signal, each named by broker_cleanup and told apart by its status. Two states
#   (regime-cutover U447c, verdict U447-669dee44 P1 :1280): while `forking` is set (from right before the relay's `&`
#   to right after `child=$!`) the signal is recorded in `deferred_signal` and the handler returns, since bash runs a
#   trap right after the command the signal arrived in and `child` may be empty there; once the flag is cleared the
#   recorded signal is handled by this same function with the child known. One handler, one flag, one recorded
#   signal; the body below is the one cleanup path. Which signals the launch can deliver is the header's: under
#   hcom-seat a TERM (and a HUP); a direct INT only when started in the foreground, the test fixture's form.
# @arg $1 string The signal name.
# shellcheck disable=SC2329 # invoked by the trap installed below
broker_signal() {
    local removed=0
    if ((forking)); then
        deferred_signal=$1
        return 0
    fi
    trap - HUP INT TERM
    if [[ -n ${child} ]]; then
        if kill -TERM "${child}" 2> /dev/null; then :; fi
        if wait "${child}"; then :; fi
    fi
    broker_cleanup || removed=$?
    ((removed != 1)) || {
        echo "acp-broker: ended by SIG$1; the broker exits 2 because the socket stands and nothing was removed" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    ((removed == 0)) || {
        echo "acp-broker: ended by SIG$1; the broker exits 2 because an exit record remains (named above)" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    kill -s "$1" $$
    exit 2
}

# @description Wait for the child `$1` and set `child_status` to its status, reading `wait` again when a trapped
#   signal interrupted it (bash returns from `wait` with the signal's status and runs the trap first).
# @arg $1 int The pid.
# @set child_status The exit status.
wait_child() {
    child_status=0
    while :; do
        # The status is read in the else branch, where `$?` is still `wait`'s own.
        if wait "$1"; then
            child_status=0
        else
            child_status=$?
        fi
        if kill -0 "$1" 2> /dev/null; then continue; fi
        return 0
    done
}

# @description Hold the relay helper beside this file to its `claude.levers.sha256` pin (the sourced-helper rule of
#   regime-env): the listener before the relay runs, a connection before the slot exists (the launch runs the helper's
#   mapper inside the worker's sandbox, U449b); the helper checks the same pin itself when it starts.
# @set helper The helper's path.
relay_helper_check() {
    local helper_pin helper_digest
    helper=${LEVER_DIR}/acp-relay.py
    [[ -r ${helper} && ! -L ${helper} ]] || refuse "the relay helper is unreadable or a link beside this script: ${helper}"
    helper_pin=$(sed -n -E 's/^      acp-relay\.py: ([0-9a-f]{64})$/\1/p' "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || refuse "cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    [[ ${helper_pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || refuse "no single sha256 pin for acp-relay.py in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        helper_digest=$(sha256sum < "${helper}") || helper_digest=''
    else
        helper_digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${helper}") || helper_digest=''
    fi
    helper_digest=${helper_digest%% *}
    [[ ${helper_digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || refuse "cannot hash ${helper}"
    [[ ${helper_digest} == "${helper_pin}" ]] || refuse "sha256 ${helper_digest} of ${helper} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
}

if ((! connection)); then
    relay_helper_check
    self_file=${LEVER_DIR}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    [[ -r ${self_file} ]] || refuse "cannot read ${self_file}"
    # The broker directory is hcom-seat's (regime-cutover U343i; the header's first paragraph): the router launch made
    # `<state slot>/broker` 0700 before the Router's settings were written, and those settings deny the Router every
    # write under it, so this process makes nothing there and takes the directory as made: present, no link, a directory
    # of this user (require_own_dir), mode 0700 and empty, every read status-checked (standing order 21). Anything else
    # refuses by name and makes nothing: absent (no router launch of hcom-seat made it); a socket inside (another broker
    # listens: one listener per Router launch, and the loser never removes the winner's socket, verdict U343d-136fbe0a
    # P2 :854); any other entry (a crashed broker's leftovers, or a directory that is not hcom-seat's, left in place).
    # The take is a check before the relay's bind, so two brokers started together can both pass it (verdict
    # U343i-76a5c83b P1 :1061); the bind decides, and the loser removes nothing at its end (broker_cleanup).
    [[ -e ${broker_dir} || -L ${broker_dir} ]] ||
        refuse "the broker directory ${broker_dir} is absent; hcom-seat's router launch makes it (0700) before the Router's settings are written, and this lever makes nothing there"
    require_own_dir 'the broker directory' "${broker_dir}"
    broker_dir_mode=$(/usr/bin/stat "${mode_args[@]}" -- "${broker_dir}") || refuse "cannot read the mode of the broker directory ${broker_dir}"
    [[ ${broker_dir_mode} == 700 ]] || refuse "the broker directory ${broker_dir} has mode ${broker_dir_mode}, not 0700 (hcom-seat makes it 0700)" # lint-comparisons: allow a mode word from stat, no path compare
    [[ ! -e ${sock} && ! -L ${sock} ]] || refuse "a broker already listens for the Router ${router} (${sock} exists); one listener per Router launch"
    # Empty: the entries by a glob, dot names included (`dotglob`) and no match an empty list (`nullglob`), so a name
    # of any bytes counts, one newline alone included (regime-cutover U343j, verdict U343i-76a5c83b P2 :1062:
    # `$(ls -A)` strips trailing newlines, so such an entry read as an empty directory); the names are shown
    # `%q`-quoted. A glob reports no failure, so the directory is read once for its status first (standing order 21).
    /bin/ls -A -- "${broker_dir}" > /dev/null || refuse "cannot list the broker directory ${broker_dir}"
    shopt -s nullglob dotglob
    broker_dir_entries=("${broker_dir}"/*)
    shopt -u nullglob dotglob
    if ((${#broker_dir_entries[@]} > 0)); then
        broker_dir_names=''
        for broker_dir_entry in "${broker_dir_entries[@]}"; do
            printf -v broker_dir_name '%q' "${broker_dir_entry##*/}"
            broker_dir_names+=${broker_dir_names:+, }${broker_dir_name}
        done
        refuse "the broker directory ${broker_dir} is not empty (${broker_dir_names}); hcom-seat makes it empty, and a broker's end leaves it so; remove the leftovers by hand when no broker runs"
    fi
    # The directory's identity, read once after the take (regime-cutover U343h): the device and inode the record helper
    # holds every record write to; no connection reads it again, and a directory of another identity at the name is
    # refused there.
    broker_dir_id=$(/usr/bin/stat "${lstat_args[@]}" -- "${broker_dir}") || refuse "cannot read the identity of the broker directory ${broker_dir}"
    [[ ${broker_dir_id} =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "the identity of the broker directory ${broker_dir} read as '${broker_dir_id}', not <device>:<inode>"
    # The start-up is a sequence of states: this process started, the relay forked, the socket bound, the readiness
    # line printed, serving. The trap is armed before the fork, so from the first state a HUP, INT or TERM ends this
    # process by that signal with the relay ended (its own handlers precede its bind, U447), the socket and the
    # records gone and the directory standing; before the trap nothing exists to remove, and the signal's default
    # disposition ends this process the same way. Bash runs a trap right after the simple command the signal arrived
    # in and can block no signal, so between the relay's `&` and `child=$!` the trap would run with `child` empty
    # (regime-cutover U447c, verdict U447-669dee44 P1 :1280: the relay orphaned with the socket bound, the broker
    # exit 2); the window is closed by deferral: `forking` is set right before the `&` and cleared right after
    # `child=$!`, broker_signal records a signal that arrives meanwhile and returns, and the recorded signal is
    # handled right after the flag is cleared, with the child known. Under hcom-seat the signals are its TERM (and a
    # HUP): the broker is a background job of a non-interactive bash there, which inherits SIGINT ignored, and bash
    # refuses to trap a signal ignored at entry; a direct INT reaches the broker only when it is started in the
    # foreground (the test fixture's form). No caller delivers INT to the broker.
    # shellcheck disable=SC2064 # expanded now on purpose: the handler needs the signal's name
    for sig in HUP INT TERM; do trap "broker_signal ${sig}" "${sig}"; done
    # The relay runs as a child: it removes its socket at its end, and the records go here once it has; every
    # connection it accepts
    # re-enters this lever by its physical path under /bin/bash (the interpreter line), with the same three arguments
    # and the caller's PATH, from which each connection resolves the tools as this process did; the broker directory's
    # identity travels in its environment (regime-cutover U343h).
    forking=1
    ACP_BROKER_DIR_ID=${broker_dir_id} PATH=${caller_path} "${python_cmd[@]}" -I -S "${helper}" "${sock}" -- /bin/bash "${self_file}" --connection "${seats_root}" "${router}" "${scratch}" &
    child=$!
    forking=0
    if [[ -n ${deferred_signal} ]]; then broker_signal "${deferred_signal}"; fi
    wait_child "${child}"
    status=${child_status}
    trap - HUP INT TERM
    removed=0
    broker_cleanup || removed=$?
    ((removed != 1)) || {
        echo "acp-broker: the relay exited ${status}; the broker exits 2 because the socket stands and nothing was removed" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    ((removed == 0)) || {
        echo "acp-broker: the relay exited ${status}; the broker exits 2 because an exit record remains (named above)" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    exit "${status}"
fi

repo=${f3#repo=}
ref=${f4#ref=}
name=${f5#name=}
require_clean_path "the header repo" "${repo}"
[[ ${ref} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,255}$ && ${ref} != *..* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow a grammar test on one revision word, no path compare
    refuse "the header ref '${ref}' is outside ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,255}\$ without '..'"
[[ ${name} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || refuse "the header name '${name}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$"
case ${name} in
claude | claude-*) refuse "the seat name '${name}' is taken by the Claude Code login directories <seats-root>/.state/claude-<group> (and the legacy <seats-root>/.state/claude); choose another name" ;;
esac
[[ ${name} != "${router}" ]] || refuse "the header name '${name}' is the Router's own seat name; a worker is never the Router"                                   # lint-comparisons: allow two seat names, no path compare
[[ ${name} != acp-* ]] || refuse "the header name '${name}' begins with 'acp-', the prefix of the broker's slots under <seats-root>/.state; choose another name" # lint-comparisons: allow a prefix test on one seat name, no path compare
[[ ${name} != broker-logs ]] || refuse "the header name 'broker-logs' is the broker's log directory <seats-root>/.state/broker-logs (regime-cutover U343o); choose another name"
stamp=$(utc_stamp slot) || refuse 'cannot read the time (/bin/date failed or answered outside the shape)'
# The slot name is its three validated parts (verdict U343d-136fbe0a P2 :980: the seat-name length applied to the
# whole refused a name of 64 characters); the name's own grammar was checked above.
slot_name=acp-${name}-${stamp}-$$
[[ ${slot_name} =~ ^acp-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{6}-[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "the per-connection slot name '${slot_name}' is outside its shape"
slot=${seats_real}/.state/${slot_name}
task=${slot}/task
pushed_ref=refs/acp-seat/${name}/${stamp}-$$
# The exit record, the reaper's alone (regime-cutover U343g): in the Router's socket directory, named as the slot.
record=${broker_dir}/${slot_name}
# The broker directory's identity, read once by the listener and carried to every connection by the relay's
# environment (regime-cutover U343h): the record helper holds each write to it. A connection run without it refuses
# before anything is made; the record helper beside this file is held before the slot (record_helper_path_check).
broker_dir_id=${ACP_BROKER_DIR_ID:-}
[[ ${broker_dir_id} =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "the broker directory's identity did not reach this connection (ACP_BROKER_DIR_ID is '${broker_dir_id}', not <device>:<inode>); a connection runs under the listener's relay alone"
# The launch log (regime-cutover U343o, verdict U343n-fd3db1b3 P1 :1264): under a directory of this lever's own,
# never inside `.state/<name>`, the state slot an hcom-seat seat of that name writes (where a planted hard link named
# `acp-launch.log` redirected the append until round 12). No seat's settings grant `.state/broker-logs`.
log_dir=${seats_real}/.state/broker-logs
log=${log_dir}/${name}.log

# The worker's settings: the deny table from the Router's settings, the project-file rows re-rooted under the slot's
# task and the held credential root appended last (where the dsh row renders it, U343l); the grants the role's own
# and the broker's (the file header), each with the
# path the role spells and its structural tag for the judgement (settings_judge). Every row physical, every list
# rendered and judged before anything is made. The task does not exist yet; its ancestors under the seats root do,
# and the identity table reads an absent path by its deepest existing ancestor.
deny_read=("${template_deny_read[@]}")
deny_read+=("${cred_root_real}")
deny_write=()
for row in ${template_deny_write[@]+"${template_deny_write[@]}"}; do
    if [[ ${row}/ == "${scratch_real}"/?* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both operands physical (hcom-seat renders its rows physical, scratch_real is physical_path); the trailing slash makes the prefix a whole component
        row=${task}/${row#"${scratch_real}"/}
    fi
    deny_write+=("${row}")
done
profile_spelled=${h}/.omp/profiles/dsh
profile_real=$(physical_clean "${profile_spelled}") || unresolved "the worker's omp profile" "${profile_spelled}"
run_real=$(physical_clean "${h}/.omp/run") || unresolved "omp's run directory" "${h}/.omp/run"
skills_real=$(physical_clean "${h}/.agents/skills") || unresolved 'the skills directory' "${h}/.agents/skills"
tools_row=$(physical_clean "${tools_dir}") || unresolved 'the private tool directory' "${tools_dir}"
allow_read=("${task}" "${claude_real}" "${profile_real}" "${skills_real}" "${tools_row}" "${key_real}")
allow_read_spelled=("${task}" "${claude_real}" "${profile_spelled}" "${h}/.agents/skills" "${tools_dir}" "${key_real}")
allow_read_tags=(slot slot profile '' '' slot)
allow_write=("${task}" "${claude_real}" "${profile_real}" "${run_real}")
allow_write_spelled=("${task}" "${claude_real}" "${profile_spelled}" "${h}/.omp/run")
allow_write_tags=(slot slot profile '')
for row in "${srt_tmp_roots[@]}" "${h}/.npm/_logs"; do
    row_real=$(physical_clean "${row}") || unresolved "srt's own write path" "${row}"
    allow_write+=("${row_real}")
    allow_write_spelled+=("${row}")
    allow_write_tags+=('')
done
check_rows 'a worker read deny' 0 "${deny_read[@]}"
check_rows 'a worker write deny' 1 ${deny_write[@]+"${deny_write[@]}"}
check_rows 'a worker read root' 0 "${allow_read[@]}"
check_rows 'a worker write root' 0 "${allow_write[@]}"
# The judgement (hcom-seat's refusal row, U272e): every grant against every deny, before the slot, the settings file
# or anything else of this connection exists.
settings_judge ||
    refuse "the worker's ${judge_grant} is, contains or lies inside ${judge_deny}; the launch is refused before anything is made"
# The four lists and the file's text through the one writer (seat-settings-render.sh, U344), each producer's status
# read (verdict U343d-136fbe0a P2 :1023; verdict U343b-cae04852 P2 `:750`): a writer that fails refuses by name with no
# slot made. The rows were held to clean_row by check_rows above; the writer holds them again and escapes nothing.
deny_read_json=$(seat_settings_rows_json 0 "${deny_read[@]}") || refuse "cannot render the worker's denyRead list (seat_settings_rows_json failed)"
deny_write_json=$(seat_settings_rows_json 1 ${deny_write[@]+"${deny_write[@]}"}) || refuse "cannot render the worker's denyWrite list (seat_settings_rows_json failed)"
allow_read_json=$(seat_settings_rows_json 0 "${allow_read[@]}") || refuse "cannot render the worker's allowRead list (seat_settings_rows_json failed)"
allow_write_json=$(seat_settings_rows_json 0 "${allow_write[@]}") || refuse "cannot render the worker's allowWrite list (seat_settings_rows_json failed)"
seat_settings_json false '[]' "${deny_read_json}" "${allow_read_json}" "${allow_write_json}" "${deny_write_json}" "${linux_tools}" ||
    refuse 'cannot render the worker settings text (seat_settings_json failed)'
json=${settings_json}

# The worker's environment, built and never inherited (hcom-seat's dsh launch): HOME, the outer PATH, the profile,
# the router group's Claude Code directory, the AWS file names omp's Bedrock discovery stats (an EPERM there ends omp), the
# seat marker, and USER and LANG when this process's caller exported them. The Router-side git runs get HOME and the
# outer PATH alone.
worker_env=("HOME=${HOME}" "PATH=${outer_path}" OMP_PROFILE=dsh "CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=${claude_real}"
    AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE=/dev/null AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null "HCOM_SEAT_SANDBOX=${slot}" "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE=${key_file}")
router_env=("HOME=${HOME}" "PATH=${outer_path}")
inherited=$(compgen -e) || refuse 'cannot list the environment'
for var in USER LANG; do
    if [[ $'\n'${inherited}$'\n' == *$'\n'"${var}"$'\n'* && -n ${!var:-} ]]; then worker_env+=("${var}=${!var}"); fi
done

# @description Append one log line `<utc> acp-broker: $*` to the launch log in the broker's own log directory, made
#   0700 when absent and held to a real directory of this user; a line that cannot be appended refuses by name.
# @arg $@ string The event.
log_line() {
    local when
    when=$(utc_stamp log) || refuse 'cannot read the time (/bin/date failed or answered outside the shape)'
    ensure_own_dir "the broker's log directory" "${log_dir}"
    [[ ! -L ${log} ]] || refuse "the launch log ${log} is a symbolic link"
    printf '%s acp-broker: %s\n' "${when}" "$*" >> "${log}" || refuse "cannot append to the launch log ${log}"
}

# @description Append the exit line `omp acp exit <status> push=<word>` to the launch log without refusing (verdict
#   U343e-fd94feae P2 :1284: the append's failure after a written ref refused, so the client read no report and
#   learned no ref). A log that cannot be appended (or is a link) is one stderr line naming the line and the log;
#   the slot's removal and the record follow in the caller, the reaper, the one writer of the exit line, which
#   writes it only when omp ran (regime-cutover U343o: a connection that never started omp leaves no line).
# @arg $1 string omp's exit status.
# @arg $2 string The push word.
exit_line() {
    local when line
    when=$(utc_stamp log) || when=unknown-time
    line="omp acp exit $1 push=$2"
    if [[ -L ${log} ]] || ! printf '%s acp-broker: %s\n' "${when}" "${line}" 2> /dev/null >> "${log}"; then
        echo "acp-broker: cannot append the exit line '${line}' to the launch log ${log}; the slot's removal and the record follow" >&2
    fi
    return 0
}

# @description Append one `session cwd <original> mapped to <task>` line to the launch log without refusing (the
#   reaper's form, exit_line); a log that cannot be appended (or is a link) is one stderr line naming the record.
# @arg $1 string The record, `session cwd <original, JSON-quoted> mapped to <task>`.
mapping_line() {
    local when
    when=$(utc_stamp log) || when=unknown-time
    if [[ -L ${log} ]] || ! printf '%s acp-broker: %s\n' "${when}" "$1" 2> /dev/null >> "${log}"; then
        echo "acp-broker: cannot append the session cwd record '$1' to the launch log ${log}" >&2
    fi
    return 0
}

# @description Read the launch's stderr file `<slot>/stderr` once omp's group has ended (regime-cutover U449b): the
#   mapper's records, `acp-relay.py: session cwd <original, JSON-quoted> mapped to <task>`, anchored at the line's
#   start, ending in this slot's task and free of control characters, go to the launch log through mapping_line;
#   every other line (omp's and srt's stderr; a worker line that began like a record carries the mapper's `omp: `)
#   goes to this process's stderr as it did before the file. The file is opened by a plain redirection on
#   launch_stderr_read and the redirection's status is read (regime-cutover U449c, verdict U449-6017f53f P2 :1509,
#   standing order 21: a process substitution's status was never read, so a `head` that failed read as an empty
#   file, and shellcheck SC2312 held CI red): a file that cannot be opened is named; a file that is absent is nothing
#   to read; a link or a non-regular file is named and not opened. Never refuses: the exit line follows in the caller.
launch_stderr_lines() {
    local file=${slot}/stderr status=0
    [[ -e ${file} || -L ${file} ]] || return 0
    if [[ -L ${file} || ! -f ${file} ]]; then
        echo "acp-broker: the launch's stderr file ${file} is not a regular file; its lines are not read" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    launch_stderr_read "${slot}" < "${file}" || status=$?
    if ((status != 0)); then
        echo "acp-broker: cannot open the launch's stderr file ${file} for reading; its lines are not read" >&2
    fi
    return 0
}

# @description The loop of launch_stderr_lines over its stdin, the launch's stderr file: one line per `read` (at most
#   `launch_stderr_cap` bytes and one, so a line without end holds no more than that), a byte counter against the
#   cap (LC_ALL=C: a character is a byte), the mapper's records to the launch log and every other line to this
#   process's stderr. `read` ends the loop with 1 at the file's end and at a read error alike (bash names the error
#   itself); the open is the caller's to judge.
# @arg $1 string The slot, for the cap's line (the file is `<slot>/stderr`).
# @exitcode 0 Always: the loop ends at the file's end or at the cap (named).
launch_stderr_read() {
    local LC_ALL=C line rest bytes=0
    while IFS= read -r -n "$((launch_stderr_cap + 1))" line || [[ -n ${line} ]]; do
        bytes=$((bytes + ${#line} + 1))
        if ((bytes > launch_stderr_cap)); then
            echo "acp-broker: the launch's stderr file $1/stderr holds more than ${launch_stderr_cap} bytes; the rest is not read" >&2
            return 0
        fi
        case ${line} in
        'acp-relay.py: session cwd '*)
            rest=${line#acp-relay.py: }
            if [[ ${rest} == *" mapped to ${task}" && ${rest} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a suffix test against this connection's own task string, no path compare
                mapping_line "${rest}"
                continue
            fi
            ;;
        esac
        printf '%s\n' "${line}" >&2
    done
    return 0
}

# @description Run git on the repository the header named, inside the Router's own sandbox: `srt --settings <the
#   Router's rendered settings>` around `/usr/bin/env` with the isolated library's environment, the pinned physical
#   git and the library's flag arrays before the arguments (regime-cutover U343e). The sandboxed git reads and writes
#   what the Router may and nothing else, so a gitfile, an alternates file or a link in the repository cannot reach
#   the operator's files; its stdout and stdin are this process's descriptors (a pack written into the slot, a pack
#   read from it), which the sandbox does not revoke; the reaper's control pipe (fd 4, open during the push) is
#   closed for it. The status is srt's, git's own through it.
# @arg $@ string git's arguments.
router_git() {
    /usr/bin/env -i "${router_env[@]}" "${srt_cmd[@]}" --settings "${template}" -- /usr/bin/env "${GIT_ISOLATED_ENV[@]}" "${git_cmd[@]}" "${GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS[@]}" "$@" 4>&- # git-isolated: allow srt runs the pinned git under the library's own arrays; a shell function cannot cross the sandbox
}

# @description Run git on the worker's clone after omp has started, inside the worker's own sandbox: `srt --settings
#   <the slot's settings.json>` around `/usr/bin/env` with the isolated library's environment, the pinned physical
#   git and the library's flag arrays, under the environment omp itself had (regime-cutover U343f, verdict
#   U343e-fd94feae P1 :1146). The worker may write everything under `task`, `.git` included, so a git that read it
#   outside every sandbox reached whatever this process may read: an alternates file, a gitfile or a HEAD naming an
#   object store under a denied path made the push read that store and import it into the Router's repository.
#   Inside the worker's settings such a plant reaches only what the worker may read, and the step fails. The
#   worker's repository is read here and nowhere else once omp runs; its stdout is this process's descriptor in the
#   slot (the pack), which the sandbox does not revoke; the reaper's control pipe (fd 4) is closed for it. The
#   status is srt's, git's own through it.
# @arg $@ string git's arguments.
worker_git() {
    /usr/bin/env -i "${worker_env[@]}" "${srt_cmd[@]}" --settings "${settings}" -- /usr/bin/env "${GIT_ISOLATED_ENV[@]}" "${git_cmd[@]}" "${GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS[@]}" "$@" 4>&- # git-isolated: allow srt runs the pinned git under the library's own arrays inside the worker's settings; a shell function cannot cross the sandbox
}

# @description Run the isolated git outside every sandbox on the slot's own repository (`git_isolated` of the
#   library, which runs `git` by name: the pinned git's directory leads PATH for the call, the system directories
#   after it), before omp starts, when the worker has written nothing. Never on the Router's repository; never on
#   the worker's once omp runs (worker_git). The reaper's control pipe (fd 4, open since the slot was made) is
#   closed for it.
# @arg $@ string git's arguments.
slot_git() {
    PATH=${git_dir}:${system_path} git_isolated "$@" 4>&-
}

# @description Push the worker's HEAD back into the repository as `pushed_ref` (regime-cutover U343e) and set
#   `push_word`: the ref when it was written; `none` when HEAD is the base the worker started from; `failed` when a
#   step failed, the step named on stderr (never silent). Two git boundaries, one per repository, and the pack
#   between them on descriptors this process opened in the slot: the worker's clone is read inside the worker's own
#   sandbox (worker_git, verdict U343e-fd94feae P1 :1146: `rev-parse --verify 'HEAD^{commit}'`, then the commits
#   above the base packed onto `${slot}/out.pack` by `pack-objects --revs --stdout`, `HEAD ^<base>`), and the
#   Router's repository is written inside the Router's own sandbox (router_git: `index-pack --strict --stdin` from
#   the pack's descriptor, `update-ref` with the empty old value, so an existing ref is never moved). Every status
#   is read; this function itself never fails, so the `done` line to the reaper always follows.
# @set push_word The word of the exit line and the record.
push_back() {
    local head
    push_word=failed
    if ! head=$(worker_git -C "${task}" rev-parse --verify 'HEAD^{commit}'); then
        echo "acp-broker: the push of the worker's HEAD to ${pushed_ref} in ${repo} failed at rev-parse on ${task} inside the worker's settings ${settings}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    head=${head%%$'\n'*}
    if [[ ! ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40,64}$ ]]; then
        echo "acp-broker: the push of the worker's HEAD to ${pushed_ref} in ${repo} failed: HEAD of ${task} read as '${head}', not a commit id" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ ${head} == "${base}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow two commit ids, not paths
        push_word=none
        return 0
    fi
    if ! printf '%s\n^%s\n' "${head}" "${base}" > "${slot}/revs"; then
        echo "acp-broker: the push of ${head} to ${pushed_ref} in ${repo} failed: cannot write ${slot}/revs" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    if ! worker_git -C "${task}" pack-objects --revs --stdout -q < "${slot}/revs" > "${slot}/out.pack"; then
        echo "acp-broker: the push of ${head} to ${pushed_ref} in ${repo} failed at pack-objects on ${task} inside the worker's settings ${settings}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    if ! router_git -C "${repo}" index-pack --strict --stdin < "${slot}/out.pack" > /dev/null; then
        echo "acp-broker: the push of ${head} to ${pushed_ref} in ${repo} failed at index-pack inside the Router's settings ${template}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    if ! router_git -C "${repo}" update-ref "${pushed_ref}" "${head}" '' < /dev/null; then
        echo "acp-broker: the push of ${head} to ${pushed_ref} in ${repo} failed at update-ref inside the Router's settings ${template}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    push_word=${pushed_ref}
}

# @description Hold the record helper `acp-record-place.py` beside this file to the rules lever_self_check applies to
#   this file, before anything of the connection is made (regime-cutover U343h; hcom-seat's helper_path_check,
#   U310f): it sits in LEVER_DIR, the physical directory of this file, and is itself no link (`-L` refused first), a
#   regular file of this user whose mode grants no group or other write (`stat`, read with its status). Nothing here
#   reads the file's bytes: the one read is the reaper's copy (record_helper_copy_make), made right before each run.
# @set record_helper The helper's path beside this file, named in refusals.
record_helper_path_check() {

printf 'done %s %s\n' "${status}" "${push_word}" >&4 || echo "acp-broker: cannot tell the reaper that the push ended (${push_word})" >&2
exec 4>&-
if wait "${reaper}"; then
    reaper_status=0
else
    reaper_status=$?
fi
((reaper_status == 0)) || {
    echo "acp-broker: omp ended ${status}; the connection exits 2 because the reaper (pid ${reaper}) ended ${reaper_status} (a per-connection slot or the record remains)" >&2
    exit 2
}
exit "${status}"
</code></pre>
