<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -I
"""Refuse a brief that judges an open-ended input without naming its closing form and its trust boundary (regime-cutover
U104, U121).

`~/.local/bin/common/brief-check.py .orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/briefs/U<n>-<slug>.md`, run from the
checkout, reads one brief. Exit 0, printing nothing: the brief's GOAL, CHANGE and CONTEXT hold no trigger term, or
its CLOSURE section names exactly one form and its TRUST section names what the unit trusts. Exit 1, one reason per
line on stdout: a trigger term fired and there is no CLOSURE section, or CLOSURE names zero, two or more forms or a
word outside `ast`, `parser-module`, `allowlist` and `remove`; a trigger term fired and there is no TRUST section, or
it is under 40 characters, or it holds neither `trusted` nor `trusts`; CLOSURE names `allowlist` or `ast` while CHANGE
holds `denylist`, `forbidden words` or `list of commands` (a denylist dressed as a form); or no GOAL, CHANGE or
CONTEXT section was found at all. Exit 2, nothing on stdout: usage, a file that cannot be read or decoded, or a
section heading that appears twice; a brief the check cannot read is never read as clean.

A brief whose SCOPE names more than two levers is refused too (regime-cutover U130; plan P-41 measured the four units
whose one brief rewrote several levers at 6.5 audits each, the single-surface units of the same period at 2). The
lever set is the manifest's `claude.levers.sha256` names, read from the same block as the pin (the self pin is that
list's `brief-check.py` entry) and spelled nowhere else; a manifest without the block is exit 2. A backticked path in
SCOPE is a lever when its basename is a pinned name, or `executable_<name>` under `home/dot_local/bin/common/` (the
generated copy counts once with its source); a path under a `tests` directory or named `README.md`,
`generated-agent-outputs.json` or `agent-config.yaml` never counts. More than two distinct levers is exit 1 with the
one line `SCOPE names <n> levers (<names>); split into sequenced units of at most two levers each (plan P-41: ...)`;
the count and the threshold are the whole rule.

A brief whose SCOPE names a repository path and whose ACCEPTANCE names no CI gate is refused too (regime-cutover U249,
standing order 44: the heads of U244 and U240 passed every ACCEPTANCE line their briefs named and failed CI minutes
later, at the prettier check and at the shebang table of `scripts/ci/run-on-lint-files.sh`, because the briefs named
their own lines and not the gates CI runs). The gates are one table of (class, name, term) rows, `GATES`: the `lint`
class is the Makefile's `format` target, the three `scripts/ci/run-on-lint-files.sh` checks CI's test job runs before
the unit tests; the `test` class is `python -m unittest`, `make unit-test`, `node --test`, or a records brief's own
check, `python3 -I <path>/check-<name>.py` (U280: a brief that changes no repository file proves itself by its check
script, and the unit-test line U274 had to add proved nothing of its work). When SCOPE names at least
one repository path (a relative backticked span of two or more names, or one name with an extension; `~/...` or a path under the system temporary directory
and `../...` are outside the repository and a bare word names no file), the ACCEPTANCE section must exist and match one
term of each class: `no ACCEPTANCE section`, `ACCEPTANCE names no lint gate (...)` and `ACCEPTANCE names no test gate
(...)` are the exit-1 lines. A sweep brief, whose SCOPE writes under `~/.local/state/` alone, is exempt by that shape,
not by a name list. Whether a gate was run is the body's pasted lines, read by the coordinator, never by this check.

The script is a pinned lever (regime-cutover U31, round 3 of U104): `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` writes the
same bytes to `home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_brief-check.py`, which chezmoi installs as
`~/.local/bin/common/brief-check.py`, and pins their sha256 under `claude.levers.sha256`; the orchestrator seat's
policy allows that path alone. Before anything else the file hashes itself and refuses to run (exit 2, nothing on
stdout) when the digest differs from its pin, so a repository without `scripts/orchestrator/` runs the same checked
copy and a rewritten copy judges no brief.

The data shape: a brief is a sequence of upper-case section headings, each a line that is exactly its name (plus the
`WORKER RULES (...)` line, whose body names shells, paths and hooks as rules, not as the thing judged), each followed
by its text; `sections` parses it into one `dict[str, str]` and refuses a heading that appears twice (a merge would
read `CLOSURE\nast\nCLOSURE\n` as `ast`). The trigger terms are one tuple of (term, reason) rows: the words the
thirteen treadmill rows of the program's `handoff/02-audit-treadmill-analysis.md` and U109 and U112 held in GOAL,
CHANGE and CONTEXT before three or more rounds found the form. The forms are one tuple of four. A later unit adds a
term by adding a row. Only SCOPE, FORBIDDEN and the other sections name paths and limits, so a term there fires
nothing.

A brief whose unit id another row of the store's `units.tsv` holds is refused too (regime-cutover U436: on 2026-11-11
the coordinator numbered a new unit U345 while `units.tsv` held U345 as a done sweep unit of 2026-11-07; this check
passed the brief, the unit ran for an hour, and pr-audit.sh refused at the pull request because two files matched
`briefs/U345-*.md`). The brief's path as given is `<store>/briefs/<file>` and the store is the parent of `briefs/`; a
path whose directory is not named `briefs`, or whose file name does not start with a unit id (`U`, digits, an optional
lowercase letter run, then `-`), has no register and is judged without this check. The register `<store>/units.tsv`
is read once by one grammar: the header line is exactly `id track state branch pr head_sha brief note`, tab-separated,
and every row has eight cells; a missing file is no register (a scratch brief beside no store passes as before), and
a file that cannot be read or decoded, a wrong header or a row of another width is exit 2 naming the file and the
line, never a pass (standing order 21). The decision over every row whose id is this file's: no such row passes; a
row whose brief cell equals `briefs/<file>` passes; a row whose brief cell is empty or another path is the exit-1 line
`unit id U<n> is taken: line <k> of <store>/units.tsv holds it with brief cell "<cell>", not briefs/<file>` (`an empty
brief cell` for an empty one), printed before the other reasons. Equality is the whole rule: a row written before the
store move (`orchestrate/<program>/briefs/<file>`) refuses the brief it names, a finding for the coordinator's records,
not a reason to widen the rule.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import re
import sys

LEVER = "brief-check.py"
# The levers block of the manifest, read as text by indentation alone, never parsed as YAML: the top-level `claude:`
# mapping, its `levers:` key, its `sha256:` key, then one pin line per lever, `<name>: <sha256>`, which names the
# lever by its file name under scripts/orchestrator/ (U136). A mapping key is a line that is a bare `<key>:`; a pin
# is its indented `<name>: <64 hex>`, every pin at the one indentation the first fixes, and this lever's own pin is
# the block's `brief-check.py` entry read by the same rule (round 2: a separate six-space read of it refused a
# manifest whose pins all sat at eight spaces). Nothing else of YAML is read: no anchors, no flow style, no quoted
# keys.
MAPPING_KEY = re.compile(r"^(\S+):$")
LEVER_PIN = re.compile(r"^(\S+): ([0-9a-f]{64})$")
LEVERS_KEYS = ("claude", "levers", "sha256")


def refuse(reason):
    """Print the refusal in the shell levers' words on stderr and exit 2; no brief was judged."""
    print(f"{LEVER}: refused: {reason}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def lever_self_check():
    """Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31).

    Returns the lever names pinned under the manifest's `claude.levers.sha256` block (U130, read by `manifest_levers`
    since U136), the one list of levers the SCOPE count reads; a manifest without the block, or with an empty one,
    is refused like an unreadable one, and before the pin is looked for. The pin is the block's `brief-check.py`
    entry: one entry is the pin, none or two is a refusal.

    The physical directory of this file decides the manifest: the deployed `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` when the
    directory is the physical `~/.local/bin/common`, else the checkout's `home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` two
    levels up; an unset or unresolvable HOME means the checkout manifest. The whole install path is resolved, not
    HOME alone, since an install reached through a symlinked `.local`, `bin` or `common` compared unequal and read
    the checkout manifest two levels up (round 5). The cwd decides nothing: the shebang runs
    `python3 -I` from PATH as the shell levers' `bash` comes from PATH, since `uv run` honoured a `.python-version`
    in the checkout the lever ran from and a planted interpreter answered before this check (round 4), and `-I`
    ignores `PYTHON*` variables, the user site and the script directory. Every read is checked and a failed one is
    a refusal, never a pass (preferences.md standing order 21).
    """
    directory = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    self_path = os.path.join(directory, os.path.basename(__file__))
    home = os.environ.get("HOME", "")
    if home and os.path.isdir(home) and directory == os.path.realpath(os.path.join(home, ".local/bin/common")):
        manifest = os.path.join(home, ".agents/agent-config.yaml")
    else:
        manifest = os.path.join(directory, "../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml")
    if not os.access(manifest, os.R_OK):
        refuse(f"manifest unreadable: {manifest}")
    try:
        with open(manifest, "rb") as handle:
            lines = handle.read().decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()
    except OSError:
        refuse(f"cannot read {manifest}")
    pinned = manifest_levers(lines, manifest)
    pins = [digest for name, digest in pinned if name == LEVER]
    if len(pins) != 1:
        refuse(f"no single sha256 pin for {LEVER} in {manifest}")
    try:
        with open(self_path, "rb") as handle:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(handle.read()).hexdigest()
    except OSError:
        refuse(f"cannot hash {self_path}")
    if digest != pins[0]:
        refuse(f"sha256 {digest} of {self_path} differs from the pin in {manifest}")
    return tuple(name for name, _ in pinned)


def manifest_levers(lines, manifest):
    """The `(name, sha256)` pins under the manifest's `claude.levers.sha256` mapping, in file order (U136).

    The one reader walks the mapping keys by indentation: a bare `<key>:` line opens a mapping, and a line indented
    no deeper than an open key closes it, so `levers:` counts only under the top-level `claude:` and `sha256:` only
    under that `levers:`. Inside the block, blank lines and lines whose first non-space character is `#` are
    skipped, the entries share the indentation of the first pin (any indentation deeper than the `sha256:` key),
    and the list ends at the first line indented less than its entries. An entry that is not `<name>: <64 hex>` is
    a refusal naming the line; no entry at all is the missing-block refusal, checked before the self pin, so a
    manifest lacking both names the block.
    """
    pins = []
    keys = []  # the open mapping keys as (indentation, key), outermost first
    block = None  # the indentation of the `sha256:` key once the path is open
    entries = None  # the indentation of the pin lines, fixed by the first
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        text = line.lstrip(" ")
        if not text or text.startswith("#"):
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(text)
        if block is not None:
            if indent <= block or (entries is not None and indent < entries):
                break
            match = LEVER_PIN.match(text)
            if match is None or (entries is not None and indent != entries):
                refuse(f"line {number} of {manifest} is not a `<name>: <sha256>` pin under claude.levers.sha256")
            entries = indent
            pins.append((match.group(1), match.group(2)))
            continue
        while keys and indent <= keys[-1][0]:
            keys.pop()
        match = MAPPING_KEY.match(text)
        if match and (keys or indent == 0):
            keys.append((indent, match.group(1)))
            if tuple(key for _, key in keys) == LEVERS_KEYS:
                block = indent
    if not pins:
        refuse(f"no claude.levers.sha256 block in {manifest}")
    return tuple(pins)


LEVERS = lever_self_check()

SECTIONS = (
    "GOAL",
    "SCOPE",
    "CHANGE",
    "CONTEXT",
    "ACCEPTANCE",
    "VERIFY",
    "TIMEBOX",
    "FORBIDDEN",
    "CLOSURE",
    "TRUST",
    "REPORT",
    "STANDING",
)
# The one heading that carries a parenthesised note: `WORKER RULES (standing orders ...)`.
WORKER_RULES = "WORKER RULES"
# The sections whose text says what the unit judges; SCOPE and FORBIDDEN name paths and limits, not the form.
JUDGED = ("GOAL", "CHANGE", "CONTEXT")
# One row per term, (term, why a brief holding it must name its closing form and its trust boundary). A term is
# matched as a whole word, any case; a space in a term also matches a hyphen (`fail-closed`); a term ending in `*`
# matches every word that begins with it (`tokenize`, `tokenizer`, `tokenization`). A later unit adds a row.
TRIGGERS = (
    ("shell", "shell text has quoting, expansion and word-splitting forms no hand-written reader lists"),
    ("tokeniz*", "a hand-written tokenizer leaks on the next token form its author did not list"),
    ("parse", "hand parsing of an open-ended input is the shape of every treadmill row"),
    ("parser", "a hand-written parser is replaced by an AST walk or one strict parser module in the end"),
    ("regex", "a regular expression over an open-ended input matches forms its author did not list"),
    ("hook", "a hook runs on text its author does not control"),
    ("worktree", "worktree records and paths have forms git keeps adding (U95: ten rounds, then refusal)"),
    ("config", "a configuration file holds keys, includes and values its reader did not list"),
    ("path", "a path has symlink, case, encoding and quoting forms no string check closes"),
    ("process", "a process tree read as text changes under the reader"),
    ("signal", "signal delivery and handling have an open set of orderings"),
    ("supervisor", "a supervisor judges a live process's state from open-ended evidence"),
    ("curl", "fetched content is open-ended input"),
    ("wget", "fetched content is open-ended input"),
    ("heredoc", "here-document bodies carry every quoting and substitution form"),
    ("quote", "quoting rules differ by shell, by context and by the word's position"),
    ("bound", "a bound over an open-ended input is a check whose cases its author listed (U109: 24 rounds)"),
    ("refuse", "a refusal decides on evidence read from an open-ended input"),
    ("fail closed", "a fail-closed read decides on a producer's output, an open-ended input (U112: 18 rounds)"),
    ("untrusted", "untrusted input is open-ended by definition"),
    ("sandbox", "a sandbox boundary is judged from paths, mounts and probes the reader did not list"),
    ("lint", "a lint over text is a hand-written reader unless it walks the language's own tree"),
    ("rule", "a rule over text has cases its author did not list"),
    ("allowlist", "an allowlist closes only as an exact-form table; written as prose it is a denylist"),
    ("denylist", "a denylist over an open-ended input never closes (research/04 entries 14 and 15)"),
    ("walk", "a walk over a tree or a directory meets node kinds its author did not list"),
    ("census", "a census of a scope is complete only against a closed set"),
)
# The four closing forms; a CLOSURE names exactly one.
FORMS = ("ast", "parser-module", "allowlist", "remove")
# A CLOSURE naming one of these forms while CHANGE holds one of the phrases below is a denylist dressed as a form.
DRESSED_FORMS = ("ast", "allowlist")
DRESSED_PHRASES = ("denylist", "forbidden words", "list of commands")
# The TRUST section names what the unit trusts and does not read: at least this many characters, one of these words.
TRUST_WORDS = ("trusted", "trusts")
TRUST_MINIMUM = 40
# The SCOPE section declares what the unit writes as backticked paths; a span holding whitespace is a command or a
# phrase, not a path, and names nothing. A path is a lever when its basename is a pinned name, or `executable_<name>`
# under INSTALLED_DIR (the generated copy counts once with its source). A path under a `tests` directory or with one
# of the NEVER_LEVERS basenames never counts: tests, READMEs, the generated outputs and the manifest name levers
# without rewriting one. More than LEVER_LIMIT distinct levers is refused (plan P-41, U130).
BACKTICKED = re.compile(r"`([^`\n]+)`")
INSTALLED_DIR = "home/dot_local/bin/common"
INSTALLED_PREFIX = "executable_"
TESTS_DIR = "tests"
NEVER_LEVERS = ("README.md", "generated-agent-outputs.json", "agent-config.yaml")
LEVER_LIMIT = 2
LEVER_REASON = (
    "SCOPE names {count} levers ({names}); split into sequenced units of at most two levers each "
    "(plan P-41: multi-lever briefs took 6.5 audits, single-surface ones 2)"
)
# The CI gates a brief's ACCEPTANCE may paste, (class, name, term) rows; a term is matched as a trigger term is (a whole
# word, any case, a space also a hyphen), or as written when it is a compiled pattern, and the name is what the reason
# line prints. The `lint` class is the Makefile's `format` target: the three `scripts/ci/run-on-lint-files.sh` checks
# (shfmt, ruff format, prettier) that CI's test job runs before the unit tests. The `test` class is the unit tests, a
# `node --test` run, or a records brief's own check script run under `python3 -I` (U280: U274 wrote tables under the
# store's `tests/` and changed no repository file, and the gate that proves such a unit is its `check-*.py`; the flag
# is matched case-sensitively since `-i` is the interactive interpreter; after `.py` the text ends or a whitespace or
# closing backtick follows, never another path character, so `check-tables.py.bak` and `check-tables.py/run.py` are
# no gate, U280b). The ACCEPTANCE of a brief whose SCOPE names a repository path must match one term of each class in
# GATE_CLASSES (standing order 44, U249); the `check` rows are gate forms a brief may paste that no class requires.
# `bats` is no gate: AGENTS.md Test Policy forbids a local run.
RECORDS_CHECK = re.compile(r"(?-i:\bpython3 -I (?:\S*/)?check-[^\s/]*\.py(?:$|\s|`))")
GATES = (
    ("lint", "run-on-lint-files.sh", "run-on-lint-files.sh"),
    ("lint", "make format", "make format"),
    ("test", "python -m unittest", "unittest"),
    ("test", "make unit-test", "make unit-test"),
    ("test", "node --test", "node --test"),
    ("test", "records-check", RECORDS_CHECK),
    ("check", "make shellcheck", "make shellcheck"),
    ("check", "make render-check", "make render-check"),
    ("check", "make validate-agent-assets", "make validate-agent-assets"),
)
GATE_CLASSES = ("lint", "test")
# A SCOPE span (no whitespace, a `./` prefix dropped) is a repository path when it is relative, its first name not
# empty (`/tmp/...`), `~` or `..`, nor a `$VAR`, and it names more than a bare word: two or more names joined by `/`,
# or one name with an extension (`AGENTS.md`). `scratch/` and `Makefile` are bare words; a branch ref (`origin/main`)
# reads as a path, which holds every brief that names a branch to the gate rule, and a sweep brief names no branch.
OUTSIDE_FIRST_NAMES = ("", "~", "..")
VARIABLE_PREFIX = "$"


def word_pattern(terms):
    """One regex over the terms, each a whole word, any case, with one named group per row (`t<index>`).

    One group per row, so the row whose reason is printed is the row the regex matched: `re.IGNORECASE` folds
    `ſhell` and a Kelvin-sign `hooK` onto their terms, and neither spelling has a `.lower()` form the table holds.
    A term that is a compiled pattern is taken as written, its own bounds and case inside it (U280).
    """
    alternatives = []
    for index, term in enumerate(terms):
        if isinstance(term, re.Pattern):
            body = term.pattern
        else:
            stem = term.endswith("*")
            body = "[ -]".join(re.escape(part) for part in term.rstrip("*").split(" "))
            body = rf"\b{body}" + ("" if stem else r"\b")
        alternatives.append(rf"(?P<t{index}>{body})")
    return re.compile("|".join(alternatives), re.IGNORECASE)


TRIGGER_WORD = word_pattern([term for term, _ in TRIGGERS])
# The reason by the term as a reason line names it, without a stem's `*`.
REASONS = {term.rstrip("*"): reason for term, reason in TRIGGERS}
DRESSED_WORD = word_pattern(DRESSED_PHRASES)
TRUST_WORD = word_pattern(TRUST_WORDS)
# One pattern per gate class over its rows' terms; a class whose pattern finds nothing in ACCEPTANCE is one reason.
GATE_WORDS = {cls: word_pattern([term for row, _, term in GATES if row == cls]) for cls in GATE_CLASSES}
# The store's id register (U436): the brief's path as given is `<store>/briefs/<file>` and `units.tsv` sits beside
# `briefs/`, its header exactly these names, tab-separated, every row that many cells; the brief cell is the path
# relative to the store. A unit id is `U`, digits, an optional lowercase letter run, then the `-` of the file name.
BRIEFS_DIR = "briefs"
UNITS_FILE = "units.tsv"
UNITS_HEADER = ("id", "track", "state", "branch", "pr", "head_sha", "brief", "note")
UNIT_ID = re.compile(r"(U[0-9]+[a-z]*)-")


def matched_term(pattern, terms, text):
    """The row of `terms` the first match in `text` belongs to, stripped of a stem `*`, or None."""
    match = pattern.search(text)
    if match is None:
        return None
    return terms[int(match.lastgroup[1:])].rstrip("*")


class BriefError(Exception):
    """The text is not a brief in the grammar, so nothing is judged (exit 2)."""


class StoreError(BriefError):
    """The store's `units.tsv` cannot be read by the one grammar, so nothing is judged (exit 2); `file` names it."""

    def __init__(self, file, message):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.file = file


def heading(line):
    """The section name when `line` is a heading, else None."""
    name = line.rstrip()
    if name in SECTIONS:
        return name
    if name.startswith(WORKER_RULES + " (") and name.endswith(")"):
        return WORKER_RULES
    return None


def sections(text):
    """The brief as name to body text; a heading that appears twice raises BriefError naming both lines."""
    found = {}
    heading_line = {}
    current = None
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        name = heading(line)
        if name is not None:
            if name in found:
                raise BriefError(
                    f"{name} appears twice (lines {heading_line[name]} and {number}); a brief has one of each"
                )
            current = name
            found[current] = []
            heading_line[name] = number
        elif current is not None:
            found[current].append(line)
    return {name: "\n".join(body) for name, body in found.items()}


def first_trigger(found):
    """(section, term) of the first trigger term in a judged section, or None."""
    for name in JUDGED:
        term = matched_term(TRIGGER_WORD, [term for term, _ in TRIGGERS], found.get(name, ""))
        if term is not None:
            return name, term
    return None


def closure(body):
    """(form, []) when the CLOSURE body is exactly one form line, else (None, every fault of the body).

    Every fault is collected, not the first: a line naming no form and a wrong count of forms are two faults of one
    body, and a check that returned on the first hid the second until the next run (round 2 of U121).
    """
    lines = [line.strip() for line in body.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if not lines:
        return None, ["CLOSURE is empty"]
    faults = []
    named = []
    for line in lines:
        name = line.split(":", 1)[0].rstrip()
        if name in FORMS:
            named.append(name)
        else:
            faults.append(f'CLOSURE line "{line}" names no form ({", ".join(FORMS)})')
    if len(named) != 1:
        listed = f" ({', '.join(named)})" if named else ""
        faults.append(f"CLOSURE names {len(named)} forms{listed}, not one")
    return (named[0], []) if not faults else (None, faults)


def trust(body):
    """Every fault of the TRUST body; empty when it names what the unit trusts.

    A body both under the minimum and without a trust word has two faults, and both are printed in one run.
    """
    text = " ".join(body.split())
    faults = []
    if len(text) < TRUST_MINIMUM:
        faults.append(f"TRUST is {len(text)} characters, under {TRUST_MINIMUM}")
    if matched_term(TRUST_WORD, TRUST_WORDS, text) is None:
        faults.append("TRUST names nothing as trusted (no word `trusted` or `trusts`)")
    return faults


def scope_paths(body):
    """Each backticked span of the SCOPE body that names one path, split at `/`, a `./` prefix dropped.

    A span holding whitespace is a command or a phrase, not a path, and names nothing.
    """
    for span in BACKTICKED.findall(body):
        if any(character.isspace() for character in span):
            continue
        path = span[2:] if span.startswith("./") else span  # lint-comparisons: allow the brief's spelled text
        yield path.split("/")


def scope_levers(body, levers):
    """The distinct pinned lever names the SCOPE body names in backticked paths, sorted."""
    named = set()
    for parts in scope_paths(body):
        name = parts[-1]
        if TESTS_DIR in parts[:-1] or name in NEVER_LEVERS:  # lint-comparisons: allow spelled names
            continue
        installed = "/".join(parts[:-1]) == INSTALLED_DIR  # lint-comparisons: allow the spelled install directory
        if installed and name.startswith(INSTALLED_PREFIX):  # lint-comparisons: allow the generated copy's prefix
            name = name[len(INSTALLED_PREFIX) :]
        if name in levers:
            named.add(name)
    return sorted(named)


def in_repository(parts):
    """Whether a split SCOPE span is a repository path: relative, and more than a bare word (see OUTSIDE_FIRST_NAMES)."""
    first = parts[0]
    if first in OUTSIDE_FIRST_NAMES or first.startswith(VARIABLE_PREFIX):  # lint-comparisons: allow spelled prefixes
        return False
    names = [name for name in parts if name]
    return len(names) > 1 or "." in names[0][1:]


def gates(body):
    """One reason per gate class the ACCEPTANCE body names no gate of; `no ACCEPTANCE section` when there is none."""
    if body is None:
        return ["no ACCEPTANCE section"]
    faults = []
    for cls in GATE_CLASSES:
        if GATE_WORDS[cls].search(body) is None:
            names = ", ".join(name for row, name, _ in GATES if row == cls)
            faults.append(f"ACCEPTANCE names no {cls} gate ({names})")
    return faults


def judge(found):
    """The reasons the parsed brief is refused, one per line; empty when it passes."""
    if not any(name in found for name in JUDGED):
        return ["no GOAL, CHANGE or CONTEXT section"]
    reasons = []
    trigger = first_trigger(found)
    form, faults = closure(found["CLOSURE"]) if "CLOSURE" in found else (None, ["no CLOSURE section"])
    if trigger is None:
        if "CLOSURE" in found:
            reasons.extend(faults)  # a CLOSURE the check cannot read is never read as clean
    else:
        section, term = trigger
        # The term's reason is printed once, on the first CLOSURE fault; every further line names the term alone.
        why = f" ({REASONS[term]})"
        for fault in faults:
            reasons.append(f'{section} holds "{term}"{why}; {fault}')
            why = ""
        trust_faults = trust(found["TRUST"]) if "TRUST" in found else ["no TRUST section"]
        reasons.extend(f'{section} holds "{term}"; {fault}' for fault in trust_faults)
    if form in DRESSED_FORMS:
        phrase = matched_term(DRESSED_WORD, DRESSED_PHRASES, found.get("CHANGE", ""))
        if phrase is not None:
            reasons.append(f'CLOSURE names {form} and CHANGE holds "{phrase}": a denylist dressed as a form')
    levers = scope_levers(found.get("SCOPE", ""), LEVERS)
    if len(levers) > LEVER_LIMIT:
        reasons.append(LEVER_REASON.format(count=len(levers), names=", ".join(levers)))
    if any(in_repository(parts) for parts in scope_paths(found.get("SCOPE", ""))):
        reasons.extend(gates(found.get("ACCEPTANCE")))
    return reasons


def taken_unit_id(path):
    """The refusal line when another row of the store's `units.tsv` holds this brief's unit id, else None (U436).

    The path is read as given, unresolved: its directory must be named `briefs` and its file name must start with a
    unit id, else there is no store and no id to look up. The register is `units.tsv` beside `briefs/`; a missing one
    is no register (a scratch brief passes as before), and one that cannot be read or decoded, whose first line is
    not the header, or holding a row of another width raises StoreError naming the file and the line, so a failed
    store read is never a pass (standing order 21). Every row is read, not the first with the id: a duplicated id
    whose second row names another file refuses too. The decision is equality of the row's brief cell with this
    file's store-relative path, `briefs/<file>`, and nothing looser: a row written before the store move
    (`orchestrate/<program>/briefs/<file>`) refuses the brief it names, a finding for the coordinator's records.
    """
    directory, name = os.path.split(path)
    if os.path.basename(directory) != BRIEFS_DIR:  # lint-comparisons: allow the brief's spelled directory name
        return None
    match = UNIT_ID.match(name)
    if match is None:
        return None
    unit_id = match.group(1)
    units = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(directory), UNITS_FILE)
    try:
        with open(units, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            lines = handle.read().splitlines()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
        raise StoreError(units, str(error))
    if not lines or lines[0] != "\t".join(UNITS_HEADER):
        raise StoreError(units, f"line 1 is not the header ({', '.join(UNITS_HEADER)})")
    rows = []
    for number, line in enumerate(lines[1:], 2):
        cells = line.split("\t")
        if len(cells) != len(UNITS_HEADER):
            raise StoreError(units, f"line {number} has {len(cells)} columns, not {len(UNITS_HEADER)}")
        rows.append((number, cells[UNITS_HEADER.index("id")], cells[UNITS_HEADER.index("brief")]))
    relative = f"{BRIEFS_DIR}/{name}"
    for number, row_id, cell in rows:
        if row_id != unit_id or cell == relative:  # lint-comparisons: allow the register's spelled brief cell
            continue
        held = f'brief cell "{cell}"' if cell else "an empty brief cell"
        return f"unit id {unit_id} is taken: line {number} of {units} holds it with {held}, not {relative}"
    return None


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("brief", help="the brief file, .orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/briefs/U<n>-<slug>.md")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        with open(args.brief, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            text = handle.read()
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
        print(f"brief-check: cannot read {args.brief}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        found = sections(text)
    except BriefError as error:
        print(f"brief-check: cannot read {args.brief}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    try:
        taken = taken_unit_id(args.brief)
    except StoreError as error:
        print(f"brief-check: cannot read {error.file}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    reasons = ([taken] if taken is not None else []) + judge(found)
    for reason in reasons:
        print(f"brief-check: {args.brief}: {reason}")
    return 1 if reasons else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file bus-history.sh
# @brief Print a team's hcom bus history as TSV rows the records can paste.
# @description
#   Plan 025 W2b (C-1). Reads `hcom events --type message --thread <team> --full
#   --last <limit> [--after <since>]` (`hcom events --help`; hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31,
#   measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; at v0.7.30 src/commands/events.rs:33 last,
#   :39 full; `--last` is `ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT n`, events.rs:185, so the newest
#   rows) and prints one row per message,
#   ascending by id: `id<TAB>at<TAB>from<TAB>to<TAB>kind<TAB>body`. `at` is hcom's
#   `ts` as printed, `to` the delivered_to names joined with commas (`-` when
#   none), `kind` the first word of the text, and `body` the text with backslash,
#   tab, CR and LF escaped as `\\`, `\t`, `\r` and `\n`, so every row is one line
#   of five tabs. `--kind` keeps only the rows whose kind equals it. Never writes:
#   the store `$HCOM_DIR/hcom.db` must already exist, because `hcom events`
#   creates one on first use (observed with 0.7.30 and 0.7.31).
# @arg $1 string Team, the hcom thread (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`).
# @option --limit <n> Newest rows to read (default 200, a positive integer).
# @option --since <ts> Only rows after this time, hcom's `--after` (`YYYY-MM-DD[THH:MM:SS[Z]]`).
# @option --kind <kind> Only rows of this kind, the first word of the line (e.g. RESULT).
# @env HCOM_DIR The private hcom store directory; default: the store derived from the checkout (regime-env).
# @stdout TSV rows `id<TAB>at<TAB>from<TAB>to<TAB>kind<TAB>body`, possibly none.
# @exitcode 0 Printed.
# @exitcode 1 Usage error, store absent, or hcom failed (its error on stderr).
# @example
#   HCOM_DIR=/path/to/.hcom scripts/orchestrator/bus-history.sh dotfiles --limit 50 --kind RESULT
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.

shift

        exit 1

  def kind_of: [splits("[ \t]+") | select(. != "")][0] // "-";

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_cdgwq
# @brief Change into a repository path selected from `gwq`.
# @description
#   Uses `gwq list --json` and `fzf` to select a known repository path, then
#   changes the current shell into that directory.
# @example
#   cdgwq

# @description Fuzzy-select a `gwq` workspace path and `cd` into it.
function cdgwq() {
    # Require a Git worktree before reading `gwq` workspaces.
    if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Not inside a git repository."
        return 1
    fi
    local workspaces paths moveto
    if ! workspaces=$(gwq list --json); then
        echo "gwq list failed." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! paths=$(jq -r '.[].path' <<< "$workspaces"); then
        echo "Cannot read the gwq workspace list." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    moveto=$(fzf <<< "$paths") || return 1
    cd -- "$moveto" || return 1
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    cdgwq
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_cdw
# @brief Change into the most recent `gwq` workspace.
# @description
#   Selects the newest path returned by `gwq list --json` and changes the
#   current shell into that repository.
# @example
#   cdw

# @description Jump to the newest `gwq` workspace path.
function cdw() {
    # Require a Git worktree before reading `gwq` workspaces.
    if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Not inside a git repository."
        return 1
    fi

    local workspaces moveto
    if ! workspaces=$(gwq list --json); then
        echo "gwq list failed." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! moveto=$(jq -r 'max_by(.created_at) | .path' <<< "$workspaces"); then
        echo "Cannot read the gwq workspace list." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [ -z "$moveto" ]; then
        echo "No recent gwq found."
        return 1
    fi
    cd -- "$moveto" || return 1
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    cdw
fi

    ancestor and 1 for none; any other status is a failed read and refuses."""
    for candidate in candidates:
        status, _, err = git("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, candidate)
        if status == 0:
            return True
        if status != 1:
            refuse(
                "git merge-base --is-ancestor %s %s exited %d: %s" % (commit.decode(), candidate.decode(), status, err)
            )
    return False

    """The commit REF names now, or None when there is no such ref: `rev-parse --verify -q` exits 0 with the object
    name and 1 for no such ref; any other status is a failed read and refuses."""
    status, out, err = git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", ref)

        return out.strip()
    if status == 1:
        return None

#   `shasum -a 256` (the self-check's pair; on stdin, so no file name is escaped into the output), its status read: a

# @arg $1 string The path.
# @set digest 64 lowercase hex.
# @exitcode 1 The tool failed or printed no digest; `digest` is empty.
file_digest() {
    local out
    digest=''
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        out=$(sha256sum < "$1") || return 1
    else
        out=$(shasum -a 256 < "$1") || return 1
    fi
    digest=${out%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]
}

#   holding exactly this lever's bytes), `older` (the hook alone: a regular file whose sha256 is in EARLIER_HOOKS, an
#   earlier hook text this lever wrote, U219b), `differs` (a regular file of any other content) or, for a file that is not
#   judged, its kind: `a symlink` (whatever it points at: nothing is written through one), `a directory`, `a fifo`,
#   `a socket`, `a device` or `not a regular file`; `executable` is 1 when a regular file has its owner's execute
#   bit. The comparison is `cmp -s` against the scratch copy, and for `pre-commit` against both of its forms: 0 equal,
#   1 different, anything else a failed read and a refusal, never an absence (standing order 21).
# @arg $1 string The path.
# @arg $2 string The hook name.
# @set state `absent`, `own`, `older` (the hook alone), `differs` or the kind of a file that is not judged.
# @set executable 0 or 1.
hook_state() {
    local target=$1 name=$2 same form earlier
    executable=0
    if [[ -L ${target} ]]; then
        state='a symlink'
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ ! -e ${target} ]]; then
        state=absent
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ ! -f ${target} ]]; then
        if [[ -d ${target} ]]; then
            state='a directory'
        elif [[ -p ${target} ]]; then
            state='a fifo'
        elif [[ -S ${target} ]]; then
            state='a socket'
        elif [[ -b ${target} || -c ${target} ]]; then
            state='a device'

esac

        missing=1
        ;;

        printf 'checkout-guard: absent\t%s\n' "${target}"
        missing=1
        ;;
    older:*)
        printf 'checkout-guard: older\t%s\n' "${target}"
        missing=1
        ;;
    *)
        printf 'checkout-guard: differs\t%s\n' "${target}"
        missing=1
        ;;

    own) printf 'checkout-guard: installed\t%s\n' "${hooks}/${marker}" ;;
    absent)
        printf 'checkout-guard: absent\t%s\n' "${hooks}/${marker}"
        missing=1
        ;;
    *)
        printf 'checkout-guard: differs\t%s\n' "${hooks}/${marker}"
        missing=1
        ;;
    esac
    for name in "${stale[@]+"${stale[@]}"}"; do
        printf 'checkout-guard: stale\t%s\n' "${hooks}/${name}"
        missing=1
    done
    exit "${missing}"
fi

[[ ${hook_own} != differs ]] || refuse "${hooks}/${hook} exists and is not this lever's hook; it is never overwritten (move it away by hand, then rerun)"
[[ ${marker_own} != differs ]] || refuse "${hooks}/${marker} exists and is not this lever's marker; it is never overwritten (move it away by hand, then rerun)"
if [[ ! -d ${hooks} ]]; then
    mkdir "${hooks}" || refuse "cannot make ${hooks}"
    made_hooks=${hooks}
fi

# The hook path and the marker path are each written by one rename, the hook's first. Unless the hook is already this
# lever's own and executable (an `older` hook, an earlier text of this lever's, is replaced the same way and its row
# is `upgraded`, U219b), its bytes go to a temporary file in the hooks directory (`mktemp` there, so the rename
# stays on one filesystem; a dotfile git runs as no hook), its mode is set, and it is read back (`cmp -s` against the
# scratch copy, the execute bit); unless the marker is already this lever's own, its bytes go to a second temporary
# file the same way (mode 0644, read back; U219). Only then does one `mv` put the hook at its path and one the marker
# at its. A failure at any step before the hook's rename refuses with both paths exactly as found (absent stays
# absent, this lever's own hook that lacked its execute bit keeps its bytes; the trap removes the temporary files):
# writing the hook path in place left an empty, a non-executable or an unverified hook behind a refusal (audit round
# 5 P2). A failed rename of the marker after the hook's leaves the hook in place and is named.

    write_hook "${hook}" "${staged}"
    chmod 755 "${staged}" || refuse "cannot make ${staged} executable"
    hook_state "${staged}" "${hook}"

    hook_row=installed

fi

    staged_marker=$(mktemp "${hooks}/.${marker}.XXXXXX") || refuse "cannot make a temporary file in ${hooks} for the marker"
    write_hook "${marker}" "${staged_marker}"
    chmod 644 "${staged_marker}" || refuse "cannot make ${staged_marker} mode 0644"
    hook_state "${staged_marker}" "${marker}"
    [[ ${state} == own ]] || refuse "${staged_marker} reads back as ${state} after the write; ${marker_target} is as it was"
    marker_row=installed
fi

    mv -f -- "${staged}" "${target}" || refuse "cannot move ${staged} onto ${target}"
    staged=''
fi

if [[ -n ${staged_marker} ]]; then
    mv -f -- "${staged_marker}" "${marker_target}" || refuse "cannot move ${staged_marker} onto ${marker_target}"

fi

# The round-1 hooks go only after the new hook and its marker are in place, so no run leaves the checkout unguarded.
for name in "${stale[@]+"${stale[@]}"}"; do
    rm -- "${hooks}/${name}" || refuse "cannot remove the round-1 ${hooks}/${name}"
    [[ ! -e ${hooks}/${name} ]] || refuse "${hooks}/${name} is still there after its removal"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_chezmoi-cd
# @brief Change into the active chezmoi source directory.
# @description
#   Resolves `chezmoi source-path` and changes the current shell into that
#   repository checkout.
# @example
#   chezmoi-cd

# @description Change into the current chezmoi source path.
chezmoi-cd() {
    local source_path
    source_path=$(chezmoi source-path) || return
    cd -- "$source_path" || return
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    chezmoi-cd
fi

docs.text: Regime-cutover U510 (handoff/47-api-key-route-design.md). A seat's model turn ran on the seats' shared claude.ai login, whose refresh-token rotation revoked every seat five times since 2026-11-10 (handoff/43, handoff/46). This lever stands as the pi-claude-bridge's provider.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable (~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/ claude-bridge.json, placed by the generated modify_claude-bridge.json of every role on the claude-bridge route), so the SDK spawns it where it spawned Claude Code: it execs the one Claude Code binary of the bridge's SDK package with its own arguments unchanged (the SDK passes --output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json ...), stdin and stdout untouched, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exported from the key file and the login names CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL unset (the bridge README: an exported gateway variable redirects the child); nothing else of the environment changes, and the key reaches the child's environment alone, never an argument, a file, a log or a message. What shares the sandbox and the uid (the seat's bash tool) can read that environment as it can read the key file (ps eww, /proc/<pid>/environ, a core dump of the child): the residual U514's key-holding proxy outside the sandbox closes. The key file is the one path REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE names (hcom-seat sets it to <seats-root>/.state/ anthropic/api-key, regime-cutover U512; the operator places the key there by the U510 handout): an absolute path to a regular file of this user, mode 0600, no symbolic link in its last component (-L false on the spelled path and on its physical directory's form), holding one line in the closed class ^sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}$ ending in one line feed or none; a second line, a carriage return, a trailing space, a NUL or any other byte refuses naming the file, never the content. The directory that holds it is held too (U510d): its spelled last component no link, this user's, mode 0700, so no other writer can swap a link in between the checks on the file and its read, each of which opens the path anew. The mode and the owner of the directory and of the file come from one stat call each, whose status and shape are read (standing order 21), the owner compared with this shell's EUID; the bytes come from cat with its status read, counted by wc -c against what the shell holds, so a NUL the shell drops is seen. Every producer this lever runs (uname, stat, cat, wc, awk, cd and pwd, the hash tool and sed of the self-check) runs with its stderr dropped, so a failure that prints a diagnostic still yields exactly one refusal line; and uname, stat, cat, wc and awk run on the system directories alone (PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin, hcom-seat's form, U510d): bash -p keeps PATH, and inside a seat PATH holds the seat's tool directory and the caller's, where a planted tool would decide the file admitted and the binary the key reaches; the caller's PATH is the child's again on the exec line. The executable is the one path <bridge>/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-<platform>/claude, where <bridge> is the directory omp.extension_providers.claude-bridge names in the manifest the self-check read (a ~/ spelled through the installed copy's own root, else HOME), required to be a row of claude.levers.extensions, the seats' extension allow-list, and <platform> comes from a closed table over uname -s and uname -m: Darwin arm64 is darwin-arm64, Darwin x86_64 darwin-x64, Linux x86_64 linux-x64, Linux aarch64 linux-arm64; any other pair refuses naming both words (U510c; a glob count chose wrong when the SDK installed both Linux packages of an architecture). On Linux the suffix -musl is appended when and only when a file matches the musl loader glob /lib/ld-musl-*.so* (a glibc host has none; CLAUDE_KEYED_MUSL_MARKER_GLOB renames the glob for the tests). The path must be an executable regular file and no link, else one refusal naming it. The manifest is read as text by indentation (awk, status read), as seat-login-preflight reads its overlays. Every refusal is one stderr line claude-keyed: refused: <reason> and exit 2 with nothing started (a line boundary in a path the environment named is folded to a space first, U510e); a refusal never falls back to the login (fail closed). Every name the lever assigns is unset before anything is assigned, so a variable of one of those names exported into its environment carries neither the key nor another value into a producer's or the child's environment under a second name (U510e; an export attribute survives an assignment); those names leave the child's environment, nothing else of it changes. --check runs every check and prints one stdout line key file ok: <path>; executable: <path> (exit 0) or refuses; the seat-login preflight and the doctor call it (U512, U513). --dry-run [<argument>...] prints the command it would exec with the key replaced by <redacted> and the names it unsets, and runs nothing. #!/bin/bash -p (pr-audit.sh and router-gh's form, U465f): bash ignores the functions, BASH_ENV, ENV, SHELLOPTS and CDPATH an environment could carry, so a poisoned environment replaces no builtin this lever runs; the self pin check runs before anything else is read.

<pre><code>#!/bin/bash -p
# @file claude-keyed
# @brief The bridge's Claude Code executable: run the Agent SDK's bundled Claude Code binary with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` read from one file, never on the seats' shared login.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U510 (handoff/47-api-key-route-design.md). A seat's model turn ran on the seats' shared claude.ai
#   login, whose refresh-token rotation revoked every seat five times since 2026-11-10 (handoff/43, handoff/46). This
#   lever stands as the pi-claude-bridge's `provider.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` (`~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/
#   claude-bridge.json`, placed by the generated `modify_claude-bridge.json` of every role on the claude-bridge route),
#   so the SDK spawns it where it spawned Claude Code: it `exec`s the one Claude Code binary of the bridge's SDK
#   package with its own arguments unchanged (the SDK passes `--output-format stream-json --input-format stream-json
#   ...`), stdin and stdout untouched, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` exported from the key file and the login names
#   `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` unset (the bridge README: an exported
#   gateway variable redirects the child); nothing else of the environment changes, and the key reaches the child's
#   environment alone, never an argument, a file, a log or a message. What shares the sandbox and the uid (the seat's
#   bash tool) can read that environment as it can read the key file (`ps eww`, `/proc/<pid>/environ`, a core dump
#   of the child): the residual U514's key-holding proxy outside the sandbox closes.
#   The key file is the one path `REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE` names (hcom-seat sets it to `<seats-root>/.state/
#   anthropic/api-key`, regime-cutover U512; the operator places the key there by the U510 handout): an absolute path
#   to a regular file of this user, mode 0600, no symbolic link in its last component (`-L` false on the spelled path
#   and on its physical directory's form), holding one line in the closed class `^sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}$` ending
#   in one line feed or none; a second line, a carriage return, a trailing space, a NUL or any other byte refuses
#   naming the file, never the content. The directory that holds it is held too (U510d): its spelled last component
#   no link, this user's, mode 0700, so no other writer can swap a link in between the checks on the file and its
#   read, each of which opens the path anew. The mode and the owner of the directory and of the file come from one
#   `stat` call each, whose status and shape are read (standing order 21), the owner compared with this shell's EUID;
#   the bytes come from `cat` with its status read, counted by `wc -c` against what the shell holds, so a NUL the shell
#   drops is seen. Every producer this lever runs (`uname`, `stat`, `cat`, `wc`, `awk`, `cd` and `pwd`, the hash tool
#   and `sed` of the self-check) runs with its stderr dropped, so a failure that prints a diagnostic still yields
#   exactly one refusal line; and `uname`, `stat`, `cat`, `wc` and `awk` run on the system directories alone
#   (`PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, hcom-seat's form, U510d): `bash -p` keeps PATH, and inside a seat PATH
#   holds the seat's tool directory and the caller's, where a planted tool would decide the file admitted and the
#   binary the key reaches; the caller's PATH is the child's again on the exec line. The executable is the one path
#   `<bridge>/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-<platform>/claude`, where `<bridge>` is the directory
#   `omp.extension_providers.claude-bridge` names in the manifest the self-check read (a `~/` spelled through the
#   installed copy's own root, else HOME), required to be a row of `claude.levers.extensions`, the seats' extension
#   allow-list, and `<platform>` comes from a closed table over `uname -s` and `uname -m`: Darwin arm64 is
#   darwin-arm64, Darwin x86_64 darwin-x64, Linux x86_64 linux-x64, Linux aarch64 linux-arm64; any other pair refuses
#   naming both words (U510c; a glob count chose wrong when the SDK installed both Linux packages of an architecture).
#   On Linux the suffix `-musl` is appended when and only when a file matches the musl loader glob `/lib/ld-musl-*.so*`
#   (a glibc host has none; `CLAUDE_KEYED_MUSL_MARKER_GLOB` renames the glob for the tests). The path must be an
#   executable regular file and no link, else one refusal naming it. The manifest is read as text by indentation
#   (awk, status read), as seat-login-preflight reads its overlays. Every refusal is one stderr line
#   `claude-keyed: refused: <reason>` and exit 2 with nothing started (a line boundary in a path the environment named
#   is folded to a space first, U510e); a refusal never falls back to the login (fail closed). Every name the lever
#   assigns is unset before anything is assigned, so a variable of one of those names exported into its environment
#   carries neither the key nor another value into a producer's or the child's environment under a second name
#   (U510e; an export attribute survives an assignment); those names leave the child's environment, nothing else of
#   it changes.
#   `--check` runs every check and prints one stdout line `key file ok: <path>; executable: <path>` (exit 0) or
#   refuses; the seat-login preflight and the doctor call it (U512, U513). `--dry-run [<argument>...]` prints the
#   command it would exec with the key replaced by `<redacted>` and the names it unsets, and runs nothing.
#   `#!/bin/bash -p` (pr-audit.sh and router-gh's form, U465f): bash ignores the functions, `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`,
#   `SHELLOPTS` and `CDPATH` an environment could carry, so a poisoned environment replaces no builtin this lever
#   runs; the self pin check runs before anything else is read.
# @arg $1 string `--check`, `--dry-run`, or the first of Claude Code's own arguments.
# @arg $@ string Claude Code's arguments, verbatim.
# @env REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE The key file, an absolute path.
# @env HOME The checkout copy expands the manifest's `~/` spellings through it; the installed copy reads the manifest
#   of its own root, `<root>/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for `<root>/.local/bin/common/claude-keyed`, and expands `~/`
#   through that root, so HOME steers neither the pin nor the bridge directory.
# @env PATH The caller's; the child gets it back on the exec line. The lever's own producers run on the system
#   directories alone.
# @env CLAUDE_KEYED_MUSL_MARKER_GLOB The musl loader glob, `/lib/ld-musl-*.so*` unless set; it chooses between the
#   SDK's glibc and musl package of one Linux architecture and nothing outside the bridge's node_modules.
# @stdout With `--check`, the one ok line; with `--dry-run`, the command and the unset names; else Claude Code's own.
# @stderr The refusal line; else Claude Code's own.
# @exitcode 0 `--check` passed, or `--dry-run` printed.
# @exitcode 2 A refusal: the self-check, the usage, the key file or its directory, the manifest, the platform or the executable.
# @exitcode * Claude Code's own status after the exec.
# @example
#   REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE=~/.local/state/omp-seats/dotfiles/.state/anthropic/api-key claude-keyed --check
set -euo pipefail

# Every name this lever assigns is unset before anything is assigned (U510e, verdict U510-88ae09c6 P2 :228): a variable
# of one of these names exported into this environment keeps its export attribute through the assignment (and a
# `local` of the same name inherits it), so the key, the mode or a path would otherwise reach the producers' and the
# child's environment under a second name. The names leave the child's environment; nothing else of it changes, and
# PATH stays (the caller's is saved below and handed back on the exec line). `tests/unit/test_claude_keyed.py` holds
# this list equal to the names the text assigns.
unset LEVER_MANIFEST LEVER_ROOT src dir self name pin digest caller_path caller_path_set system_path usage mode \
    key_file key_parent parent_rule key_dir key_phys os arch platform owner_mode_re parent_what parent_owner_mode \
    parent_mode parent_owner owner_mode key_mode key_owner read_status key_text key_bytes key_chars key key_class \
    bridge allowed listed row tilde_slash tilde_root musl_glob musl marker exe arg

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing has started when it runs. The reason is folded onto one
#   line first: a line feed, a carriage return, a vertical tab or a form feed in a path the environment named (U510e,
#   P3 :150) becomes a space, pr-audit.sh's one_line form, so every refusal is one stderr line whatever the path holds.
# @arg $1 string The reason, which never holds the key.
refuse() {
    echo "claude-keyed: refused: ${1//[$'\n\r\v\f']/ }" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31),
#   chosen by this file's own physical directory and nothing else (U510d: a HOME of the caller's choosing steered the
#   old form to the checkout layout's path): `<root>/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under
#   `<root>/.local/bin/common`, which a sandboxed session cannot write, the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
#   for the copy under scripts/orchestrator, and a copy in neither layout refuses. Every read is checked; a failure
#   exits 2 naming the file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py`
#   refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_ROOT The installed copy's root (the home its manifest sits in); empty for the checkout copy.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P 2> /dev/null) || refuse "cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}"
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    case ${dir} in # lint-comparisons: allow the layout is read from the pwd -P form's last components, no path compared with another
    */.local/bin/common)
        LEVER_ROOT=${dir%/.local/bin/common}
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${LEVER_ROOT}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
        ;;
    */scripts/orchestrator)
        LEVER_ROOT=''
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
        ;;
    *)
        refuse "${self} is neither an installed copy under <home>/.local/bin/common nor a checkout copy under scripts/orchestrator, so no manifest holds its pin"
        ;;
    esac
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || refuse "manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}" 2> /dev/null) ||
        refuse "cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || refuse "no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}" 2> /dev/null) || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}" 2> /dev/null) || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || refuse "cannot hash ${self}"
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || refuse "sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
}
lever_self_check

# The lever's own producers (uname, stat, cat, wc, awk) run on the system directories alone (hcom-seat's form, U85;
# U510d): `bash -p` drops the imported functions and BASH_ENV, not PATH, and inside a seat PATH holds the seat's tool
# directory and the caller's, where a planted tool would decide the file admitted and the binary the key reaches. The
# caller's PATH is the child's again on the exec line (Claude Code finds its own tools by it); the self-check above
# reads sed and the hash tool as every shell lever does (tests/unit/test_lever_self_check.py).
caller_path=${PATH-}
caller_path_set=${PATH+1}
system_path=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
PATH=${system_path}

# The producers' stderr below is dropped per call (`2> /dev/null`), and where bash itself opens the file (a redirection
# inside a command substitution) the whole block's is, so a diagnostic of either never joins the refusal line.

usage='usage: claude-keyed --check | claude-keyed --dry-run [<argument>...] | claude-keyed [<argument>...]'
mode='exec'
if (($# > 0)); then
    case $1 in
    --check)
        (($# == 1)) || refuse "${usage}"
        mode=check
        shift
        ;;
    --dry-run)
        mode=dry-run
        shift
        ;;
    esac
fi

# The key file: the one path the environment names, held to the form described in the header before a byte is read.
key_file=${REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE:-}
[[ -n ${key_file} ]] ||
    refuse 'REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE is not set; hcom-seat sets it to <seats-root>/.state/anthropic/api-key (regime-cutover U512) and the operator places the key there (the U510 handout)'
[[ ${key_file} == /* ]] || refuse "REGIME_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE '${key_file}' is not an absolute path" # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path shape test on one path, no path compare
[[ ! -L ${key_file} ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} is a symbolic link; the key file must be a regular file of this user"
[[ -e ${key_file} ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} is absent; place the API key there (the U510 handout)"
[[ -f ${key_file} ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} is not a regular file"
# The directory that holds the key file (U510d): its spelled last component is no link (a link earlier in the path is
# allowed, as for the file), and below it is this user's alone; the physical directory's form of the file's name is
# read from it too, so a link in the file's last component is refused under either spelling.
key_parent=${key_file%/*}
[[ -n ${key_parent} ]] || key_parent=/
parent_rule="the directory must be this user's alone (0700)"
[[ ! -L ${key_parent} ]] || refuse "the directory ${key_parent} of the key file ${key_file} is a symbolic link; ${parent_rule}"
key_dir=$(cd "${key_parent}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P 2> /dev/null) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of the key file ${key_file}"
key_phys=${key_dir%/}/${key_file##*/}
[[ ! -L ${key_phys} ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} is a symbolic link; the key file must be a regular file of this user"
# The platform, from a closed table over the two uname words (each producer's status read, its stderr dropped): it
# chooses the stat dialect here and the SDK's platform package below; a pair outside the table refuses by name.
os=$(uname -s 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'cannot read the operating system name (uname -s)'
arch=$(uname -m 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'cannot read the machine name (uname -m)'
case "${os} ${arch}" in
'Darwin arm64') platform=darwin-arm64 ;;
'Darwin x86_64') platform=darwin-x64 ;;
'Linux x86_64') platform=linux-x64 ;;
'Linux aarch64') platform=linux-arm64 ;;
*) refuse "no Claude Code platform package for the pair '${os}' '${arch}' (uname -s, uname -m); the table is Darwin arm64, Darwin x86_64, Linux x86_64 and Linux aarch64" ;;
esac
# One stat call each for the directory's and the file's mode and owner, the status and the shape read; an injected or
# failing stat refuses. The directory first: it is what holds the file still between the checks and the read.
owner_mode_re='^([0-7]{3,4}) ([0-9]+)$'
parent_what="the directory ${key_parent} of the key file ${key_file}"
case ${os} in
Darwin) parent_owner_mode=$(stat -f '%Lp %u' "${key_parent}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "cannot read the mode and owner of ${parent_what} (stat failed)" ;;
*) parent_owner_mode=$(stat -c '%a %u' "${key_parent}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "cannot read the mode and owner of ${parent_what} (stat failed)" ;;
esac
[[ ${parent_owner_mode} =~ ${owner_mode_re} ]] ||
    refuse "cannot read the mode and owner of ${parent_what} (stat printed '${parent_owner_mode}')"
parent_mode=${BASH_REMATCH[1]} parent_owner=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
[[ ${parent_owner} == "${EUID}" ]] || refuse "${parent_what} is owned by uid ${parent_owner}, not this user (uid ${EUID})"
[[ -O ${key_parent} ]] || refuse "${parent_what} is owned by uid ${parent_owner}, not this user (uid ${EUID})"
[[ ${parent_mode} =~ ^0?700$ ]] || refuse "${parent_what} has mode ${parent_mode}; ${parent_rule}"
case ${os} in
Darwin) owner_mode=$(stat -f '%Lp %u' "${key_file}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "cannot read the mode and owner of the key file ${key_file} (stat failed)" ;;
*) owner_mode=$(stat -c '%a %u' "${key_file}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "cannot read the mode and owner of the key file ${key_file} (stat failed)" ;;
esac
[[ ${owner_mode} =~ ${owner_mode_re} ]] ||
    refuse "cannot read the mode and owner of the key file ${key_file} (stat printed '${owner_mode}')"
key_mode=${BASH_REMATCH[1]} key_owner=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
[[ ${key_owner} == "${EUID}" ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} is owned by uid ${key_owner}, not this user (uid ${EUID})"
[[ -O ${key_file} ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} is owned by uid ${key_owner}, not this user (uid ${EUID})"
[[ ${key_mode} =~ ^0?600$ ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} has mode ${key_mode}; the key must be readable by this user alone (0600)"
# The bytes, read by cat with its status read (bash 5.2 runs `$(< file)` without a fork, so a failed redirection there
# would end the script under errexit before a handler ran, U310e), with a sentinel so a trailing line feed survives
# the substitution; the block's stderr is dropped so bash's own note about a dropped NUL never joins a refusal line,
# and the byte count, taken in a subshell under LC_ALL=C (the child's environment stays as it was), sees that NUL.
read_status=0
{ key_text=$(cat -- "${key_file}" && printf x) || read_status=$?; } 2> /dev/null
((read_status == 0)) || refuse "cannot read the key file ${key_file}"
key_text=${key_text%x}
# The wc read: the `<` redirection is bash's own open, so its failure note (the file gone between cat and wc) would
# print before wc ran; the block's stderr is dropped before the redirection is opened (U510e, P3 :231).
read_status=0
{ key_bytes=$(wc -c < "${key_file}") || read_status=$?; } 2> /dev/null
((read_status == 0)) || refuse "cannot count the bytes of the key file ${key_file} (wc -c failed)"
key_bytes=${key_bytes//[[:space:]]/}
[[ ${key_bytes} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "cannot count the bytes of the key file ${key_file} (wc -c printed '${key_bytes}')"
key_chars=$(LC_ALL=C && printf '%s' "${#key_text}") || refuse "cannot count the bytes of the key file ${key_file}"
((key_bytes > 0)) || refuse "the key file ${key_file} is empty; the key must be one line of the form sk-ant-... (the U510 handout)"
((key_bytes == key_chars)) || refuse "the key file ${key_file} holds a byte the shell cannot read (a NUL); the key must be one line"
[[ ${key_text} != *$'\r'* ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} holds a carriage return; the key must be one line ending in a line feed alone"
key=${key_text%$'\n'}
[[ ${key} != *$'\n'* ]] || refuse "the key file ${key_file} holds more than one line; the key must be one line"
key_class='^sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}$'
[[ ${key} =~ ${key_class} ]] ||
    refuse "the key file ${key_file} does not hold a key of the form sk-ant-<20 or more of [A-Za-z0-9_-]> (the content is never printed)"

# The bridge directory: `omp.extension_providers.claude-bridge` of the manifest the self-check read, by indentation,
# required among the `claude.levers.extensions` rows (the seats' only -e directories); `~/` spelled through the
# installed copy's root, else HOME.
bridge=$(awk '
/^omp:$/ { in_omp = 1; next }
/^[^ #]/ { in_omp = 0; in_ext = 0 }
in_omp && /^  extension_providers:$/ { in_ext = 1; next }
in_omp && /^  [^ ]/ { in_ext = 0 }
in_omp && in_ext && $1 == "claude-bridge:" { print $2; exit }
' "${LEVER_MANIFEST}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "cannot read the omp.extension_providers rows of the manifest ${LEVER_MANIFEST} (awk failed)"
[[ -n ${bridge} ]] || refuse "the manifest ${LEVER_MANIFEST} names no omp.extension_providers.claude-bridge directory"
allowed=$(awk '
/^claude:$/ { in_claude = 1; next }
/^[^ #]/ { in_claude = 0; in_levers = 0; in_ext = 0 }
in_claude && /^  levers:$/ { in_levers = 1; next }
in_claude && /^  [^ ]/ { in_levers = 0; in_ext = 0 }
in_levers && /^    extensions:$/ { in_ext = 1; next }
in_levers && /^    [^ ]/ { in_ext = 0 }
in_ext && $1 == "-" { print $2 }
' "${LEVER_MANIFEST}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "cannot read the claude.levers.extensions rows of the manifest ${LEVER_MANIFEST} (awk failed)"
listed=0
while IFS= read -r row; do
    if [[ ${row} == "${bridge}" ]]; then listed=1; fi # lint-comparisons: allow two manifest spellings of the same row, compared as the manifest writes them
done <<< "${allowed}"
# The manifest spells the directory through `~/`: the home the installed copy's manifest sits in (LEVER_ROOT), else
# this user's HOME for the checkout copy (hcom-seat holds the entry the same way).
# shellcheck disable=SC2088 # the manifest's own spelling, matched as text; the root replaces it on the line below
tilde_slash='~/'
case ${bridge} in
"${tilde_slash}"*)
    tilde_root=${LEVER_ROOT:-${HOME:-}}
    [[ -n ${tilde_root} ]] || refuse "HOME is not set, so the manifest's spelling ${bridge} of the claude-bridge directory cannot be expanded"
    bridge=${tilde_root}/${bridge#"${tilde_slash}"}
    ;;
esac
((listed)) || refuse "the claude-bridge directory ${bridge} is not a row of claude.levers.extensions in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
[[ -d ${bridge} ]] || refuse "the claude-bridge directory ${bridge} is not a directory"
# The SDK's platform package of the table above (bun.lock names eight; the SDK installs the glibc and the musl one
# of a Linux architecture side by side, so a count over the glob cannot choose). On Linux the musl package is the
# one when and only when the musl loader is present: a file matching the marker glob, read by the shell's own glob
# (compgen, a builtin, no producer); a glibc host has no such file.
if [[ ${platform} == linux-* ]]; then
    musl_glob=${CLAUDE_KEYED_MUSL_MARKER_GLOB:-/lib/ld-musl-*.so*}
    musl=0
    while IFS= read -r marker; do
        if [[ -n ${marker} && -f ${marker} ]]; then musl=1; fi
    done < <(compgen -G "${musl_glob}" || true)
    ((musl == 0)) || platform=${platform}-musl
fi
exe=${bridge}/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-${platform}/claude
[[ -e ${exe} || -L ${exe} ]] || refuse "no Claude Code executable at ${exe}; the SDK's ${platform} package is not installed under ${bridge}"
[[ ! -L ${exe} && -f ${exe} && -x ${exe} ]] || refuse "the Claude Code executable ${exe} is not an executable regular file"

case ${mode} in
check)
    printf 'key file ok: %s; executable: %s\n' "${key_file}" "${exe}"
    exit 0
    ;;
dry-run)
    printf 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<redacted> %s' "${exe}"
    for arg in "$@"; do
        printf ' %q' "${arg}"
    done
    printf '\nunset: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL\n'
    exit 0
    ;;
esac
# The login names leave; the key rides as the exec'd process's environment alone, never an argument; the caller's PATH
# is the child's again (a caller without one hands none on: the binary is run by its absolute path).
unset CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
if [[ -z ${caller_path_set} ]]; then
    unset PATH
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=${key} exec "${exe}" "$@"
fi
PATH=${caller_path} ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=${key} exec "${exe}" "$@"
</code></pre>

Python runs isolated (-I), so a module committed in the session's working directory (for example a json.py in an untrusted repository) cannot shadow the standard library. Lookup walks from the session cwd to the nearest Git root (a .git directory or worktree gitfile), selecting the nearest opted-in project. Outside Git, only cwd is checked. The receiver's walk and vendor no-follow directory construction close pre-construction races; a same-user process swapping a storage path after construction remains outside this protection because later I/O, including SQLite, reopens paths by name.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_contextdb-codex-notify
# @brief Ingest a Codex notification or hook event into an opted-in project's CompactionDB.
# @description
#   Codex `notify` passes the JSON payload as the first argument; Codex command
#   hooks (PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionEnd) deliver it on stdin. Either way
#   the payload is ingested with `--no-maintenance`, which skips the SessionEnd
#   retention pass, and the CLI gets 2 seconds, so the SessionEnd hook returns
#   within Codex's 3-second limit; retention stays on the explicit `prune`
#   command and on Claude Code's own SessionEnd hook. Failures print one stderr
#   line and exit 0 so Codex is never blocked. Python runs isolated (`-I`), so a
#   module committed in the session's working directory (for example a
#   `json.py` in an untrusted repository) cannot shadow the standard library.
#   Lookup walks from the session cwd to the nearest Git root (a .git directory
#   or worktree gitfile), selecting the nearest opted-in project. Outside Git,
#   only cwd is checked. The receiver's walk and vendor no-follow directory
#   construction close pre-construction races; a same-user process swapping a
#   storage path after construction remains outside this protection because
#   later I/O, including SQLite, reopens paths by name.
# @arg $1 string Optional JSON payload; read from stdin when absent.

if ! command -v python3 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '%s\n' 'contextdb-codex-notify: ingest failed' >&2
    exit 0
fi

payload="${1:-$(cat)}"

if ! python3 -I - "${payload}" 2> /dev/null << 'PY'
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

try:
    payload = sys.argv[1]
    event = json.loads(payload)
    if not isinstance(event, dict):
        raise ValueError("notify payload must be an object")
    cwd = event.get("cwd")
    if cwd is not None and not isinstance(cwd, str):
        raise ValueError("notify cwd must be a string")
    project_dir = (Path(cwd) if cwd else Path.cwd()).resolve()
    ancestors = (project_dir, *project_dir.parents)
    boundary = next((p for p in ancestors if os.path.lexists(p / ".git")), project_dir)
    for candidate in ancestors:
        if (candidate / ".claude" / "contextdb").is_dir():
            project_dir = candidate
            break
        if candidate == boundary:
            break
    opt_in = project_dir / ".claude" / "contextdb"
    cli = Path.home() / ".agents" / "compactiondb" / ".claude" / "hooks" / "contextdb_cli.py"
    # Only a real directory inside the project opts in: a repository could point
    # .claude or .claude/contextdb elsewhere with a symlink, and the CLI would
    # then create its state there.
    if not opt_in.is_dir() or opt_in.resolve() != opt_in or not cli.is_file():
        raise SystemExit(0)
    # The CLI creates, chmods and writes under this tree, so a symlink at any
    # depth would send its writes outside the project: refuse every symlink,
    # and require each storage directory to be a real directory or absent.
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(opt_in, followlinks=False):
        for name in dirs + files:
            if os.path.islink(os.path.join(root, name)):
                raise ValueError(f"{os.path.join(root, name)} must not be a symlink")
    for child in ("state", "spool", "spool/incoming", "spool/quarantine", "health"):
        storage = opt_in / child
        if storage.exists() and not storage.is_dir():
            raise ValueError(f"{storage} must be a directory")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            str(cli),
            "--project-root",
            str(project_dir),
            "ingest",
            "--ingested-from",
            "codex",
            "--no-maintenance",
        ],
        input=payload,
        text=True,
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        timeout=2,
        check=True,
        cwd=project_dir,
    )
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit(1)
PY
then
    printf '%s\n' 'contextdb-codex-notify: ingest failed' >&2
fi

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_dev
# @brief Change into a repository selected from `ghq`.
# @description
#   Lets the user choose a repository path from `ghq` and changes into it.
# @example
#   dev

# @description Fuzzy-select a repository path from `ghq`.
function ghq-path() {
    local repositories selected_path
    if ! repositories=$(ghq list --full-path); then
        echo "ghq list failed." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    selected_path=$(fzf <<< "$repositories") || return 1
    [[ -n $selected_path ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$selected_path"
}

# @description Change into a selected `ghq` repository.
function dev() {
    local moveto
    moveto=$(ghq-path) || return 0
    cd -- "$moveto" || exit 1
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    dev
fi
