#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_disk-gc
# @brief Reclaim disk from Docker leftovers and merged git worktrees.
# @description
#   Prunes dangling Docker images, unused images created more than DISK_GC_IMAGE_AGE ago, anonymous
#   volumes no container references that are older than DISK_GC_VOLUME_DAYS, trims the build cache to
#   DISK_GC_BUILD_CACHE_MAX, drops uv and npm cache entries no environment references,
#   then removes linked git worktrees of each repo in DISK_GC_REPOS (default: every repo under
#   DISK_GC_WORKSPACE that has one) that are merged into the default branch (origin/HEAD, origin/main,
#   origin/master, main or master, the first that exists), carry no tracked edits, were not touched within
#   DISK_GC_WORKTREE_DAYS, and are not locked by a live process. A worktree is removed only through
#   `git worktree remove`; one git refuses is logged and kept for the operator. Untracked files of
#   a removed worktree are archived under ~/.local/share/disk-gc/scratch first, and
#   archives older than DISK_GC_ARCHIVE_DAYS are purged. Without --apply it reports.
# @example
#   disk-gc                      # report only
#   disk-gc --apply              # reclaim
#   DISK_GC_REPOS="$HOME/Workspace/a:$HOME/Workspace/b" disk-gc --apply
#   DISK_GC_WORKSPACE="$HOME/src" disk-gc

set -Eeuo pipefail

apply=0
case "${1:-}" in
--apply) apply=1 ;;
"") ;;
*)
    echo "usage: disk-gc [--apply]" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

repos="${DISK_GC_REPOS:-}"
workspace="${DISK_GC_WORKSPACE:-${HOME}/Workspace}"
worktree_days="${DISK_GC_WORKTREE_DAYS:-3}"
archive_days="${DISK_GC_ARCHIVE_DAYS:-30}"
cache_max="${DISK_GC_BUILD_CACHE_MAX:-80GB}"
image_age="${DISK_GC_IMAGE_AGE:-720h}"
volume_days="${DISK_GC_VOLUME_DAYS:-7}"
scratch="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/share}/disk-gc/scratch"
mkdir -p "${scratch}"

# @description Print one log line.
function log() {
    printf 'disk-gc: %s\n' "$*"
}

# @description Run a mutating command under --apply; print it otherwise.
function run() {
    if [ "${apply}" -eq 1 ]; then
        "$@"
    else
        log "would run: $*"
    fi
}

# @description Print the root filesystem's used and available space with a label.
function report_df() {
    df -h / | awk -v label="$1" 'NR == 2 { print "disk-gc: " label " used=" $3 " avail=" $4 }'
}

# @description Prune dangling images, unused images created more than image_age ago (a stopped container
#   still counts as a use; a pruned base image is pulled again on the next build), anonymous unreferenced
#   volumes older than volume_days, and trim the build cache to cache_max (least recently used first).
function docker_gc() {
    if ! command -v docker > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        log "docker not installed; skipping"
        return 0
    fi
    if ! docker info > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        log "docker daemon unreachable; skipping"
        return 0
    fi
    run docker image prune -f || log "image prune failed; continuing"
    run docker image prune -a -f --filter "until=${image_age}" || log "unused image prune failed; continuing"
    volume_gc
    run docker builder prune -f --max-used-space "${cache_max}" || log "builder prune failed; continuing"
}

# @description Remove anonymous volumes no container references that are older than volume_days. `docker volume
#   prune` has no age filter, and `dangling=true` also lists named volumes, so each candidate is checked by name
#   shape (64 hex digits) and creation time. A volume a stack recreated minutes ago is left alone.
function volume_gc() {
    local volumes v created created_ts cutoff
    volumes=$(docker volume ls -q -f dangling=true)
    cutoff=$(date -d "${volume_days} days ago" +%s)
    while read -r v; do
        [[ ${v} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || continue
        created=$(docker volume inspect "${v}" --format '{{.CreatedAt}}') || continue
        created_ts=$(date -d "${created}" +%s) || continue
        [ "${created_ts}" -lt "${cutoff}" ] || continue
        log "remove volume ${v:0:12}: anonymous, unreferenced, created ${created:0:10}"
        run docker volume rm "${v}" || log "volume rm failed for ${v:0:12}; continuing"
    done <<< "${volumes}"
}

# @description Drop uv and npm cache entries that no installed environment references. Both commands keep
#   everything still in use, so a later install pays only for what was already unreferenced. uv holds a cache
#   lock while another uv runs, so the wait is bounded and a busy cache is skipped until the next run.
function package_cache_gc() {
    if command -v uv > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        run env UV_LOCK_TIMEOUT=30 uv cache prune || log "uv cache prune skipped: cache busy or failed"
    fi
    if command -v npm > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        run npm cache verify || log "npm cache verify failed; continuing"
    fi
}

# @description Whether a worktree lock names a process that is still alive.
#   Claude Code writes "claude agent <name> (pid N start S)"; a lock without a
#   pid is treated as live, since nothing proves it stale.
# @exitcode 1 When there is no lock, or its pid is gone (process died or host rebooted).
function lock_is_live() {
    local lock="$1" pid
    [ -f "${lock}" ] || return 1
    pid=$(awk 'match($0, /pid [0-9]+/) { print substr($0, RSTART + 4, RLENGTH - 4); exit }' "${lock}")
    [ -n "${pid}" ] || return 0
    kill -0 "${pid}" 2> /dev/null
}

# @description List the files of a worktree that git does not track, NUL-separated: untracked files, plus
#   ignored files under 1 MiB outside .venv/ and node_modules/, so an .env survives and dependency trees do not.
function scratch_files() {
    local wt="$1"
    git -C "${wt}" ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z
    # shellcheck disable=SC2185 # -files0-from supplies find's starting points; a '.' would add the whole tree
    git -C "${wt}" ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z ':(exclude).venv' ':(exclude)node_modules' |
        (cd "${wt}" && find -files0-from - -maxdepth 0 -type f -size -1024k -print0)
}

# @description Archive a worktree's scratch files as a tarball.
function archive_scratch() {
    local wt="$1" archive="$2"
    scratch_files "${wt}" | tar --null -C "${wt}" -T - -czf "${archive}"
    log "archived the scratch files of $(basename "${wt}") to ${archive}"
}

# @description Print the repos under the workspace that have at least one linked worktree, colon-separated.
#   A repo whose listing cannot be read is left out, so a broken repo is never swept by accident.
function discover_repos() {
    local d count found=""
    for d in "${workspace}"/*/; do
        [ -d "${d}/.git" ] || continue
        count=$(git -C "${d}" worktree list --porcelain 2> /dev/null | grep -c '^worktree ') || continue
        [ "${count}" -gt 1 ] || continue
        found="${found:+${found}:}${d%/}"
    done
    printf '%s' "${found}"
}

# @description Print the first ref that exists of origin/HEAD, origin/main, origin/master, main, master.
# @exitcode 1 None exists.
function default_branch() {
    local repo="$1" ref
    ref=$(git -C "${repo}" symbolic-ref -q --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2> /dev/null) && {
        printf '%s' "${ref}"
        return 0
    }
    for ref in origin/main origin/master main master; do
        if git -C "${repo}" rev-parse --verify -q "${ref}^{commit}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            printf '%s' "${ref}"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

# @description Read the worktrees of a repo from `git worktree list --porcelain -z` into wt_paths and wt_locked,
#   two parallel arrays with the main worktree first. The listing goes to a file, never a pipe, so its exit status
#   is read; each NUL-terminated line is read whole, so a space or a newline in a path stays in the path.
# @arg $1 path The repo.
# @set wt_paths array The worktree paths in git's order.
# @set wt_locked array 1 where the record carries `locked`, else 0.
# @exitcode 1 The listing could not be read; both arrays are empty.
function read_worktrees() {
    local repo="$1" listing line status=0
    wt_paths=() wt_locked=()
    listing=$(mktemp) || return 1
    git -C "${repo}" worktree list --porcelain -z > "${listing}" || status=$?
    if [ "${status}" -eq 0 ]; then
        while IFS= read -r -d '' line; do
            case ${line} in
            'worktree '*) wt_paths+=("${line#worktree }") wt_locked+=(0) ;;
            locked | 'locked '*) [ "${#wt_locked[@]}" -eq 0 ] || wt_locked[${#wt_locked[@]} - 1]=1 ;;
            esac
        done < "${listing}"
    fi
    rm -f "${listing}"
    return "${status}"
}

# @description Prove that a listed path is the root of a linked worktree of the repo before anything removes it: a
#   directory that is not a symlink, is not the main worktree, is its own toplevel (`rev-parse --show-prefix` prints
#   nothing there), and whose `--git-common-dir` is the repo's. Paths are compared by identity (`-ef`: same device
#   and inode), never as text, so nothing is resolved or stripped and a name ending in a newline is compared whole.
#   The common directory git prints is read behind a sentinel, so a name whose last character is a newline (one git
#   would quote in a listing) is seen as such and refused before the comparison: stripped, it would name its
#   neighbour, and a foreign repository at `<repo>/.git<newline>` would pass as the repo's own.
#   Every read's status is checked and a failed read fails the proof, so a directory that replaced a worktree, a
#   subdirectory of one, or a tree of another repo is kept.
# @arg $1 path The worktree path as listed.
# @arg $2 path The main worktree's path, the listing's first record.
# @arg $3 path The repo's common git directory.
# @set reason string The check that failed, for the log line.
# @exitcode 1 The path is not such a root.
function worktree_root() {
    local wt="$1" main_wt="$2" gitdir="$3" prefix common
    reason=''
    if [ -L "${wt}" ]; then
        reason="a symlink"
        return 1
    fi
    if [ "${wt}" -ef "${main_wt}" ]; then
        reason="the main worktree"
        return 1
    fi
    if ! prefix=$(git -C "${wt}" rev-parse --show-prefix 2> /dev/null); then
        reason="no toplevel"
        return 1
    fi
    if [ -n "${prefix}" ]; then
        reason="inside the tree at ${prefix}"
        return 1
    fi
    if ! common=$(git -C "${wt}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2> /dev/null && printf x); then
        reason="no common git dir"
        return 1
    fi
    common=${common%x}
    common=${common%$'\n'}
    case ${common} in
    *$'\n')
        reason="a git directory name git had to quote"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    if ! [ "${common}" -ef "${gitdir}" ]; then
        reason="of another repo, ${common}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# @description Remove the merged, idle, unlocked linked worktrees of one repo. The listing comes from read_worktrees
#   (every path whole), each lock from the tree's own admin directory, and `git worktree remove` runs only on a path
#   worktree_root proved; the lever runs no `rm -rf` on a worktree path, so a removal git refuses is logged and the
#   tree kept for the operator; a failed read keeps the tree, a failed listing keeps the repo.
function worktree_gc() {
    local repo="$1" base gitdir i wt locked name admin head porcelain edits recent untracked size archive reason
    local -a wt_paths=() wt_locked=()
    if ! git -C "${repo}" rev-parse --git-dir > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        log "not a git repo: ${repo}; skipping"
        return 0
    fi
    git -C "${repo}" fetch -q origin 2> /dev/null || log "fetch failed for ${repo}; using the last-known refs"
    base=$(default_branch "${repo}") || {
        log "no default branch in ${repo}; skipping its worktrees"
        return 0
    }
    log "repo ${repo}: base ${base}"
    run git -C "${repo}" worktree prune --expire "${worktree_days}.days.ago"
    if ! gitdir=$(git -C "${repo}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir); then
        log "cannot read the git dir of ${repo}; skipping its worktrees"
        return 0
    fi
    if ! read_worktrees "${repo}"; then
        log "cannot list the worktrees of ${repo}; skipping its worktrees"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${#wt_paths[@]}" -eq 0 ] || [ ! -d "${wt_paths[0]}" ]; then
        log "cannot read the main worktree of ${repo}; skipping its worktrees"
        return 0
    fi
    for i in "${!wt_paths[@]}"; do
        [ "${i}" -gt 0 ] || continue
        wt=${wt_paths[i]} locked=${wt_locked[i]}
        [ -d "${wt}" ] || continue
        name=$(basename "${wt}")
        if ! worktree_root "${wt}" "${wt_paths[0]}" "${gitdir}"; then
            log "keep ${name}: not a worktree root of ${repo} (${reason})"
            continue
        fi
        head=$(git -C "${wt}" rev-parse HEAD 2> /dev/null) || {
            log "keep ${name}: cannot read HEAD"
            continue
        }
        if ! git -C "${repo}" merge-base --is-ancestor "${head}" "${base}"; then
            log "keep ${name}: not merged into ${base}"
            continue
        fi
        porcelain=$(git -C "${wt}" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no 2> /dev/null) || {
            log "keep ${name}: cannot read its status"
            continue
        }
        if [ -n "${porcelain}" ]; then
            edits=$(printf '%s\n' "${porcelain}" | wc -l)
            log "keep ${name}: ${edits} tracked edits"
            continue
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC2185 # -files0-from supplies find's starting points; a '.' would add the whole tree
        recent=$(git -C "${wt}" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard |
            (cd "${wt}" && find -files0-from - -maxdepth 0 -type f -newermt "${worktree_days} days ago" -print) |
            awk 'NR == 1')
        if [ -n "${recent}" ]; then
            log "keep ${name}: touched within ${worktree_days} days (${recent#"${wt}"/})"
            continue
        fi
        # The lock lives in the tree's own admin directory, which git names `worktrees/<basename><n>` when two
        # trees share a basename, so it is asked for, never built from the name.
        admin=$(git -C "${wt}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir 2> /dev/null) || {
            log "keep ${name}: cannot read its admin directory"
            continue
        }
        if [ "${locked}" -eq 1 ] && [ ! -f "${admin}/locked" ]; then
            log "keep ${name}: listed as locked, no lock file in ${admin}"
            continue
        fi
        if lock_is_live "${admin}/locked"; then
            log "keep ${name}: locked by a live process"
            continue
        fi
        untracked=$(scratch_files "${wt}" | tr -cd '\0' | wc -c)
        if [ "${untracked}" -gt 0 ]; then
            archive="${scratch}/$(basename "${repo}")-${name}-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S).tar.gz"
            run archive_scratch "${wt}" "${archive}" || {
                log "keep ${name}: scratch archive failed"
                continue
            }
        fi
        size=$(du -sh "${wt}" 2> /dev/null | awk '{ print $1 }')
        log "remove ${name}: merged into ${base}, ${size}, ${untracked} scratch files"
        run git -C "${repo}" worktree remove --force --force "${wt}" || {
            log "keep ${name}: git worktree remove failed; the tree is left for the operator"
            continue
        }
    done
    run git -C "${repo}" worktree prune --expire "${worktree_days}.days.ago" || log "worktree prune failed for ${repo}"
}

report_df before
docker_gc

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_fgc
# @brief Fuzzy-pick and checkout a local Git branch.
# @description
#   Lists local branches, selects one with `fzf`, and checks it out.
# @example
#   fgc

# @description Checkout a branch selected from the local branch list.
function fgc() {
    local branches branch
    if ! branches=$(git for-each-ref refs/heads/ --format='%(refname:short)'); then
        echo "Cannot list the local branches." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    branch=$(fzf <<< "$branches") || return 1
    git checkout "$branch"
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    fgc
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_git-delete-merged-branches
# @brief Delete local branches already merged through squash-and-merge.
# @description
#   Detects the repository default branch, compares local branches against it,
#   and removes branches whose tree has already been integrated upstream.
# @example
#   git-delete-merged-branches

# @description Check whether the current directory is inside a Git repository.
function is_inside_git_repository() {
    git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree > /dev/null 2>&1
}

# @description Detect the default branch name from the `origin` remote.
# @exitcode 1 When `git remote show origin` fails or names no HEAD branch.
function get_default_branch() {
    local remote_info default_branch

    remote_info=$(LC_ALL=C git remote show origin) || return 1
    default_branch=$(sed -n '/HEAD branch/s/.*: //p' <<< "${remote_info}") || return 1
    [[ -n ${default_branch} ]] || return 1
    echo -n "${default_branch}"
}

# @description Delete local branches whose content is already on the default branch.
# @exitcode 1 When the default branch, the branch list or a branch's squash check cannot be read; nothing more is deleted.
function git-delete-merged-branches() {
    # delete all git branches which have been "squash and merge" via GitHub
    # ref. https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43489303/how-can-i-delete-all-git-branches-which-have-been-squash-and-merge-via-github

    if ! is_inside_git_repository; then
        return 0
    fi

    local default_branch branches branch merge_base tree squashed cherry
    if ! default_branch=$(get_default_branch); then
        echo "git-delete-merged-branches: cannot read the HEAD branch of origin; nothing deleted" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    git checkout -q "${default_branch}" || return 1
    if ! branches=$(git for-each-ref refs/heads/ "--format=%(refname:short)"); then
        echo "git-delete-merged-branches: cannot list the local branches; nothing deleted" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    while read -r branch; do
        [[ -n ${branch} ]] || continue
        # No common ancestor: the branch was never forked from the default branch.
        merge_base=$(git merge-base "${default_branch}" "${branch}") || continue
        if ! tree=$(git rev-parse "${branch}^{tree}") ||
            ! squashed=$(git commit-tree "${tree}" -p "${merge_base}" -m _) ||
            ! cherry=$(git cherry "${default_branch}" "${squashed}"); then
            echo "git-delete-merged-branches: cannot check whether ${branch} was squash-merged; stopping" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        if [[ ${cherry} == "-"* ]]; then
            git branch -D "${branch}"
        fi
    done <<< "${branches}"
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    git-delete-merged-branches
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file git-isolated.sh
# @brief One isolated git for every lever: the flag set as data, the function that runs git under it, the environment scrub.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U113 (plan P-22, research 01 section 1). Git documents no single switch that removes all
#   configuration from a command: `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` and `GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM` are
#   per-level switches, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` override every file from the environment, and
#   the repository level has no off switch. Until this file each lever carried a flag set of its own (`git_plain`,
#   `git_scratch`, `git_safe`, `git_tree`), none complete. Here the set is written once, as data: GIT_ISOLATED_ENV and
#   GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS, read by `git_isolated`, by the one `bounded` fetch of pr-audit.sh (a perl exec cannot run a
#   shell function) and by scripts/lint-comparisons.py (from this file's syntax tree, never by sourcing it).
#   Sourced by the levers from the directory they run from (`LEVER_DIR`), never run on its own; it checks its own
#   sha256 against its `claude.levers.sha256.git-isolated.sh` pin first, like every lever, so a rewritten copy under
#   ~/.local/bin/common stops the lever that sources it. scripts/ci/git-invocation-check.sh refuses any `git` word in
#   the levers outside `git_isolated` and outside a line carrying `# git-isolated: allow <reason>`.
#   bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash): plain arrays, no here-string, no case-modifying expansion.
#   The three arrays are the library's own and never exported: each is unset before it is assigned (a readonly one is
#   a refusal), git_env_scrub refuses one that is exported, and git_isolated refuses to run with one unset or empty.
# @set GIT_ISOLATED_ENV The environment of every isolated git, a plain array that is never exported (so a scrub leaves it).
# @set GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS The arguments before the caller's; a caller's later `-c` or `--git-dir` wins by git's last-wins rule.
# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, beside the lever that sourced it.
set -euo pipefail

lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''             # producer-status: allow the if below takes an empty home as the checkout layout
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

# The library's own three names are never exported, and a caller's environment may already export one (a stray
# `export`, or a planted one): an array assigned over an exported variable keeps the export attribute, git_env_scrub
# would then remove the library's own data as one more `GIT_*` name, and git_isolated would run git with nothing
# (audit round 2 P1). So each is unset before it is assigned, and one that cannot be (readonly) is a refusal.
for git_isolated_name in GIT_ISOLATED_ENV GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS GIT_ISOLATED_SCRUB_NAMES; do
    unset -v "${git_isolated_name}" 2> /dev/null || {
        echo "git-isolated.sh: refused: ${git_isolated_name} is readonly in the sourcing shell; the library cannot assign it" >&2
        exit 2
    }
done
unset -v git_isolated_name
declare +x -a GIT_ISOLATED_ENV GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS GIT_ISOLATED_SCRUB_NAMES

# The environment of every isolated git: one entry per line, each with the channel it closes and where that channel
# was found. The level switches close the files; the command scope (`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`) is
# closed by git_env_scrub below, and the repository level by the choice of command alone (research 01 section 1.5).
GIT_ISOLATED_ENV=(
    # No global config file: no `url.*.insteadOf`, credential helper, hook path, identity or include of ~/.gitconfig
    # or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config (research 01 section 1.1; records-sync.sh U101, the redirected push).
    GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
    # No system config file $(prefix)/etc/gitconfig (research 01 section 1.1).
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
    # No system attributes file $(prefix)/etc/gitattributes, so it names no filter driver (research 01 section 1.4
    # item 3; pr-audit.sh U71b audit round 1, a filter driver run on the audited tree).
    GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM=1
    # No credential or passphrase prompt on the terminal: a transport that needs one fails instead of waiting
    # (pr-audit.sh U71b, the bounded fetch).
    GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
)
GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS=(
    # No replacement refs: a `refs/replace/*` of the repository cannot stand in for an object (pr-audit.sh U71b audit
    # round 7, with GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS).
    --no-replace-objects
    # No hook of any repository runs: git's documented off switch (research 01 section 1.1; records-sync.sh U101 round
    # 6, a post-checkout hook that planted files in the sync).
    -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null
    # No fsmonitor program: a hook path in core.fsmonitor ran inside `git ls-files` (measured, research 01 section 1.1;
    # records-sync.sh U101 round 12).
    -c core.fsmonitor=false
    # No user attributes file ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/attributes), so no filter, diff or merge driver comes from it
    # (research 01 section 1.4 item 3; pr-audit.sh git_tree).
    -c core.attributesFile=/dev/null
    # No commit-graph file of the repository: an ancestry read (merge-base) must not trust a file the checkout wrote
    # (pr-audit.sh git_safe and git_tree).
    -c core.commitGraph=false
    # No ssh program: the ssh transport fails, whatever `core.sshCommand` any config names (research 01 section 1.1;
    # scripts/lint-comparisons.py GIT_C).
    -c core.sshCommand=false
    # Every transport off by default (file, git, ext, and any `insteadOf` rewrite to one); a caller re-opens one per
    # command, as the tests do with `-c protocol.file.allow=always` (research 01 section 1.1; hcom-seat U85).
    -c protocol.allow=never
    # https is the one transport left on: the levers fetch and push over https only (scripts/lint-comparisons.py GIT_C).
    -c protocol.https.allow=always
    # The empty helper resets the helper list, so no helper of any config answers; a caller adds its own after it
    # (records-sync.sh: `!gh auth git-credential`, standing order 19; research 01 section 1.1).
    -c credential.helper=
    # No credential prompt (research 01 section 1.1).
    -c credential.interactive=false
    # No automatic gc in a scratch repository that is removed on exit (records-sync.sh git_scratch; tests U100).
    -c gc.auto=0
    # No detached maintenance process left behind a command (records-sync.sh git_scratch; tests U100).
    -c maintenance.auto=false
)
# The non-`GIT_` names git_env_scrub removes: they steer libcurl and OpenSSL under a fetch or push (research 01
# section 1.4 item 2).
GIT_ISOLATED_SCRUB_NAMES=(http_proxy HTTPS_PROXY https_proxy HTTP_PROXY NO_PROXY no_proxy SSL_CERT_FILE SSL_CERT_DIR CURL_CA_BUNDLE)

# @description Run git under GIT_ISOLATED_ENV with GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS before the caller's arguments. A later `-c` of
#   the caller wins for its key by git's last-wins rule (measured, research 01 section 1.1): records-sync.sh adds its
#   credential helper after the empty one, and a test re-opens the local transport with `-c protocol.file.allow=always`.
#   The environment is exported in a subshell that execs git, so nothing is exported into the caller and no `env` from
#   PATH runs. This function body is the one place in the levers where a bare `git` word is accepted
#   (scripts/ci/git-invocation-check.sh).
# @arg $@ string git's arguments.
# @exitcode 2 An array of the library is unset or empty.
# @exitcode * git's own status.
git_isolated() {
    local who
    who=${BASH_SOURCE[1]:-${BASH_SOURCE[0]}}
    who=${who##*/}
    # An array unset or emptied after the sourcing would run git with fewer flags than documented: a refusal instead.
    # `${name[*]:-}` reads an unset array as empty under `set -u` on bash 3.2, where `${#name[@]}` is unbound.
    [[ -n ${GIT_ISOLATED_ENV[*]:-} ]] || {
        echo "${who}: refused: GIT_ISOLATED_ENV is empty; the library's flag set is gone" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ -n ${GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS[*]:-} ]] || {
        echo "${who}: refused: GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS is empty; the library's flag set is gone" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ -n ${GIT_ISOLATED_SCRUB_NAMES[*]:-} ]] || {
        echo "${who}: refused: GIT_ISOLATED_SCRUB_NAMES is empty; the library's flag set is gone" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    (
        export "${GIT_ISOLATED_ENV[@]}" && exec git "${GIT_ISOLATED_ARGS[@]}" "$@"
    )
}

# @description Refuse if $2 is one of the library's own names (`GIT_ISOLATED_*`): they are never exported, and a scrub
#   that removed one as a stray `GIT_*` name would leave git_isolated with no flags (audit round 2 P1).
# @arg $1 string The prefix of the refusal.
# @arg $2 string An exported name.
# @exitcode 2 The name is the library's own.
git_isolated_own_name() {
    case $2 in
    GIT_ISOLATED_*)
        echo "$1: refused: $2 is exported; the library's own names are never exported" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Whether $1 is a name git_env_scrub removes: an exported `GIT_*` name or one of GIT_ISOLATED_SCRUB_NAMES,
#   unless it is among the names to keep ($2...).
# @arg $1 string The name.
# @arg $@ string The names to keep.
# @exitcode 0 Remove it. 1 Leave it.
git_env_scrubbed() {
    local name=$1 listed keep
    shift
    listed=0
    case ${name} in
    GIT_*) listed=1 ;;
    *)
        for keep in "${GIT_ISOLATED_SCRUB_NAMES[@]}"; do
            [[ ${name} != "${keep}" ]] || listed=1
        done
        ;;
    esac
    ((listed)) || return 1
    for keep in "$@"; do
        [[ ${name} != "${keep}" ]] || return 1
    done
    return 0
}

# @description Remove every exported `GIT_*` name and the transport names of GIT_ISOLATED_SCRUB_NAMES from the
#   environment, except the names given as arguments, then list again and refuse if any is left. `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`
#   and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` override every config file and only this closes them (research 01 section 1.3), an exported
#   GIT_AUTHOR_NAME would name a commit's author, and GIT_DIR would point every command at another repository. The names
#   come from the builtin `compgen -e` through a command substitution and are split on the default IFS, which bash never
#   imports (an exported name has no blank or glob character), so bash 3.2 with an unwritable TMPDIR, which cannot make
#   a here-string file, cannot skip the loop (records-sync.sh U101 round 6). The library's own `GIT_ISOLATED_*` names
#   are never exported: one found exported is a refusal, kept or not, never removed. The refusal is prefixed with the
#   sourcing script's name, or with this file's when a harness sourced it from a command string (no `BASH_SOURCE[1]`,
#   which `set -u` would otherwise report as unbound).
# @arg $@ string Names to keep.
# @exitcode 2 The environment cannot be listed, an `unset` fails (a readonly name), a name of the library is exported,
#   or a name is still there afterwards.
git_env_scrub() {
    local who names name
    who=${BASH_SOURCE[1]:-${BASH_SOURCE[0]}}
    who=${who##*/}
    names=$(compgen -e) || {
        echo "${who}: refused: cannot list the environment" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    for name in ${names}; do
        git_isolated_own_name "${who}" "${name}"
        git_env_scrubbed "${name}" "$@" || continue
        unset -v "${name}" 2> /dev/null || {
            echo "${who}: refused: cannot remove ${name} from the environment" >&2
            exit 2
        }
    done
    names=$(compgen -e) || {
        echo "${who}: refused: cannot list the environment" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    for name in ${names}; do
        git_isolated_own_name "${who}" "${name}"
        git_env_scrubbed "${name}" "$@" || continue
        echo "${who}: refused: ${name} is still in the environment after the scrub" >&2
        exit 2
    done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file hcom-dispatch
# @brief Send one protocol line from one seat to another over hcom and print a durable receipt.
# @description
#   Plan 025 W2b (C-1). The words after the recipient are joined with spaces into one
#   line, which reaches hcom as one argument after `--` (`hcom send --help`:
#   "Everything after -- is the message"). The line's first word is its kind
#   (`^[A-Z]+$`, e.g. TASK or PING); any other first word, such as the `-` or pane
#   label of the retired agmsg-dispatch form, is refused before any hcom call. The send is
#   `hcom send @<to> --thread <team> --from <from> --json -- <line>` (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31,
#   measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; the send.rs and events.rs lines are at v0.7.30):
#   `@<to>` is the seat's exact hcom name (send --help "Target matching"; a name
#   hcom does not know fails with its "No active agent" error), `--thread <team>`
#   seeds the team thread the seat answers in with `hcom send --thread <team> --
#   <line>` and no target (src/commands/send.rs:300 refuses a thread without
#   members, so the TASK carries the mention), `--from <from>` is the external
#   sender identity (send.rs:96; the row's `from`, send.rs:403) and `--json` prints
#   `{"delivered_to": [...], "event_id": N}` on stdout (send.rs:1135). hcom's own
#   error stays on stderr and its exit status is passed through. The event id is
#   then read back with `hcom events --type message --thread <team> --sql "id = N"
#   --full` (src/commands/events.rs:45 sql, :39 full), so the receipt names a row
#   the bus holds, the one bus-history.sh prints:
#   `id=<N> at=<hcom ts> to=<to> kind=<first word of the line>`.
#   hcom delivers to a bound seat itself (`hcom list --help`: "[OMP] hcom-launched,
#   automatic delivery"), so there is no wake. The store is `$HCOM_DIR/hcom.db` (`hcom start --help`: "Prefix all hcom
#   commands with: HCOM_DIR=..."); an unset HCOM_DIR or an absent store is refused
#   before any hcom call, because hcom creates a store on first use and the seats'
#   launch owns that.
# @arg $1 string Team, the hcom thread (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`).
# @arg $2 string Sender seat, same grammar.
# @arg $3 string Recipient seat, its exact hcom name, same grammar.
# @arg $@ string Message words, joined with spaces into one line whose first word is the kind.
# @env HCOM_DIR The private hcom store directory; default: the store derived from the checkout (regime-env).
# @stdout One receipt line `id=<event id> at=<ts> to=<to> kind=<kind>`.
# @exitcode 0 Sent and found in the bus.
# @exitcode 1 Usage, grammar, empty line, a first word that is not a kind, store absent, or the sent id was not found.
# @exitcode * hcom's own status when the send fails (its error on stderr).
# @example
#   HCOM_DIR=/path/to/.hcom hcom-dispatch dotfiles orch u5team-nemo 'TASK v1 task_id=T1 ...'
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

(($# >= 4)) || {
    echo 'usage: hcom-dispatch <team> <from> <to> <line...>' >&2
    exit 1
}
team=$1 from=$2 to=$3
shift 3
line=$*
[[ ${1%%[[:space:]]*} =~ ^[A-Z]+$ ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: the line's first word '${1%%[[:space:]]*}' is not a kind (^[A-Z]+\$)" >&2
    echo 'usage: hcom-dispatch <team> <from> <to> <line...>' >&2
    exit 1
}
for identifier in "${team}" "${from}" "${to}"; do
    [[ ${identifier} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || {
        echo "hcom-dispatch: identifier '${identifier}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$" >&2
        exit 1
    }
done
[[ -n ${line} ]] || {
    echo 'hcom-dispatch: empty line' >&2
    exit 1
}
# The store is HCOM_DIR when set, else the one derived from this checkout (regime-env, regime-cutover U33); a
# derived store that does not exist yet is refused like an explicit one, because `hcom events` would create it.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: refused: regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env" >&2
    exit 1
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
regime_env hcom-dispatch || exit 1
[[ -n ${HCOM_DIR:-} && -f ${HCOM_DIR:-}/hcom.db ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: store absent: \${HCOM_DIR}/hcom.db (HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR:-unset})" >&2
    exit 1
}

receipt=$(hcom send "@${to}" --thread "${team}" --from "${from}" --json -- "${line}")
id=$(jq -r '.event_id' <<< "${receipt}" 2> /dev/null) || id=
[[ ${id} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: no event_id in the hcom receipt: ${receipt}" >&2
    exit 1
}
row=$(hcom events --type message --thread "${team}" --sql "id = ${id}" --full)
[[ -n ${row} ]] || {
    echo "hcom-dispatch: sent event ${id} was not found in thread ${team}" >&2
    exit 1
}
jq -r --arg to "${to}" '
  def kind_of: [splits("[ \t]+") | select(. != "")][0] // "-";
  "id=\(.id) at=\(.ts) to=\($to) kind=\(.data.text | kind_of)"' <<< "${row}"

docs.title: home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_hcom-seat
docs.text: Plan 025 W5b (U7), the minimal form before X. A seat is one omp process that hcom omp starts in a herdr pane (hcom omp --help: hcom [N] omp [args...], --tag <name>, --dir <path>, --terminal <preset>; hcom gives the seat HCOM_LAUNCHED=1, HCOM_TAG and HCOM_DIR). For <role> the launch line is hcom omp --tag <name> --dir <dir> --terminal herdr --go -- --profile <role> --config ~/.agents/omp/policies/<role>.yml --config ~/.agents/omp/profiles/<role>.yml --append-system-prompt ~/.agents/omp/rules/<role>.md -e <ext>...; hcom drops the -- and forwards what follows to omp verbatim (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31, measured 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; extract_launch_flags, src/commands/launch.rs:572-581 at v0.7.30). --go is hcom's launch gate: inside an AI tool, hcom without it prints == LAUNCH PREVIEW == / Add --go to proceed. and starts nothing (launch.rs:48,388-389, measured on the real host 2026-10-23), and extract_launch_flags consumes it only before the -- (launch.rs:650-652). The profile equals the role. A named profile reads its own ~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml (pi-utils src/dirs.ts:312-315, U10), so the manifest's modelRoles.default and skills.customDirectories reach the seat only through the second overlay, rendered per role (U14); the first overlay owns the approval mode (U6). Both are required. The seat's standing rules, rendered per role from the manifest's standing_rules (U75), ride --append-system-prompt: the overlays disable the native provider (U66), so no profile context file loads, and the explicit flag also wins over any project APPEND_SYSTEM.md. The rules file is required and must be non-empty, since omp reads a missing path as literal text. The extensions default to the pi-claude-bridge, which the role's model route needs, plus the openai-siwc when it is present; --ext replaces that list. The roles are orchestrator and worker; every audit is one fresh ~/.local/bin/common/pr-audit.sh <n> --records <store> run, never a seat (regime-cutover U57, U58; the omp audit route was retired by U119 round 3). The stop gate's directory ~/.agents/omp/hooks is loaded on every launch, whatever --ext says, and the launch line ends with --hcom-team <HCOM_TEAM>: hcom passes HCOM_DIR into the pane but not HCOM_TEAM, so the flag, which the gate registers, carries exactly the team this launch was given, an explicit one included (regime-cutover U33c; omp refuses the flag when no loaded extension registers it, so a launch without the gate fails instead of running unguarded). Every directory, a default, --ext or the gate's, must resolve to an entry of claude.levers.extensions in the manifest the self-check reads (regime-cutover U31), else the launch is refused. The orchestrator sits in the repository this command runs in; every other role gets the worktree <seats-root>/<name>, which is created detached from origin/main (HEAD in a repository without it) when absent and reused when it is a worktree of this repository (any other directory at that path is refused). HCOM_DIR, HCOM_TEAM and the seats root come from the environment or --seats-root when set, else from the checkout through the sourced regime-env helper (regime-cutover U33: ~/.local/state/hcom/<slug>, <slug>, ~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>), and are exported to the seat. The program store's root REGIME_STORE_ROOT (<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>, regime-env's fixed derivation, U215c; regime-cutover U219, store move 3 of 5, handoff/07-store-move-design.md) is held once (store_root_hold: clean, each component a 0700 directory of this user or absent, resolved physically once into store_root_phys) and, since U219c (verdict U219-985b7c04), four things hold of it: it is made by every role's launch that finds it absent, before its settings file is written (store_root_make, after the judgement, as the credential root is made, because srt's Linux backend skips an absent path); it is printed verbatim into the orchestrator's write roots (row 7, seat_write_roots, never resolved again) and granted for read to both omp roles; it is denied for write to every other row (the worker's, the dsh's and the router's denyWrite, tagged store); and every rendered write grant of every role is judged against it (store_root_judge: a row that is, contains or lies inside the root refuses the launch by name, the orchestrator's own row excepted by position and byte equality). An hcom store HCOM_DIR that is, lies inside or contains it refuses the launch by name before anything is made (store_root_overlap_check, by identity: the hcom store is every seat's write grant, so the records would lie inside it; verdict U215-15c6be1e P1); the dsh and router rows carry no grant of it. The seat's omp runs under OS containment (regime-cutover U85): Anthropic's sandbox-runtime srt (sandbox-exec on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux) with per-seat settings, through an omp shim at <seats-root>/.sandbox/<name>/bin/omp that is put first on PATH, so hcom pins it as the pane's tool; the shim runs a canary under the settings and refuses to start omp unless a write into the sandbox directory and reads of the settings and ~/.ssh fail inside (seat_sandbox_write below). srt and omp run by their physical argv (pin_exec), and so do hcom (exec'd by it) and herdr (through wrappers in the shim directory); none of their files may be or lie under a write root of any seat. Every input path (HOME, --seats-root, HCOM_DIR, REGIME_SEATS_ROOT, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) and every path written into the srt settings must be clean: absolute, components of [A-Za-z0-9._@+-] only, no '.' or '..' component and no trailing '/', since srt reads a settings path as a pattern. The settings are written by the shell (no JSON tool) and read back by /usr/bin/plutil on macOS, /usr/bin/jq on Linux. No caller PATH entry runs anything: the first statement sets PATH to the system directories, the complete protected set is built by (device, inode) identity before mise or any other tool runs, and the tools beyond them (git, hcom, herdr, omp, srt, node, bun, claude, jq; bwrap, socat and rg on Linux) are resolved through mise which under env -i from /, else command -v on the caller's PATH, checked (absolute, no control character, an executable regular file, no shim, neither it nor a directory above it with the identity of a seat write root) and linked into ~/.local/state/hcom-seat/tools; PATH is then that directory and the system directories, for hcom-seat, hcom, the shim and srt (whose Linux settings name bwrap, socat and rg). Inside the sandbox omp gets that PATH followed by the caller's absolute entries. Every executable is checked with its interpreter chain, and hcom-seat, the shim and the wrappers run under #!/bin/bash. The git state host git reads for this repository's worktrees (config, config.worktree, info, hooks, commondir, gitdir, the worktree's .git file) is denied to every seat, and a launch over such state holding a key host git would act on is refused (git_state_check) before the first git command; every git command hcom-seat runs has hooks, fsmonitor and worktree config off. Every program's seats root is read-denied but the seat's own paths. No seat launches a seat: the orchestrator's sandbox, like the worker's, has no herdr socket and no write to the seats root, and a launch from inside a seat is refused; seats are started from a terminal outside every seat (the operator or the coordinator, as gate G7 was). Every input is checked before anything is created or started: an unknown role, a launch inside a seat, a name or team outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$, a store regime-env refuses, an absent policy or profile overlay or extension directory, a cwd outside a git checkout, a required tool that is missing, a shim or a file that is or lies under a seat write root, or no sandbox-exec (macOS) or bubblewrap, socat and ripgrep (Linux) is exit 2 with the reason. A seat directory that holds .omp is refused too, after the worktree exists and before hcom starts (U66: omp applies the cwd's .omp/config.yml at start, which no setting turns off). --dry-run prints the launch line, and the derived environment and sandbox on stderr, and creates and starts nothing but the private tool links. Otherwise hcom's own exit status is returned (hcom omp --help: 0 ready, 1 launch failed, 2 still launching or blocked on user attention). The seat login (regime-cutover U318, U314 alternative A; per login group since U498): every seat's bridge child and the dsh role's gateway child run with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>, one directory per login group under the seats root, holding one interactive claude.ai login that Claude Code itself stores and refreshes (the Keychain item keyed to that directory on macOS, .credentials.json 0600 there otherwise). The group is a function of the role, the one table login_group_of_role (worker, orchestrator and audit each their own; the dsh and router roles the router group, since the gateway child is the Router's), copied as text into seat-login-preflight: a role's seats share their group's login, and two groups rotate no refresh token together (U318's one directory per seats root let the Router's long-lived children and the sweep seat rotate one token, and the login was invalidated five times, handoff/40). The directory is the role table's claude_config row: this lever makes it 0700 when absent, the shim exports it, seat-login-preflight judges claude auth status under it, and the settings grant it for write and deny its settings.json, settings.local.json, rules, hooks, plugins, skills, commands and agents to every seat, so no seat changes what another seat's child, or the operator's login command, would load from it. Every other group's directory and the legacy shared .state/claude are denied for read, by name, to every seat (U498c: srt reopens a root's subtree under an allow but for a more specific deny, so the orchestrator's read grant of the seats root reached the worker group's login until then; the rows come from the table's range, LOGIN_GROUPS, minus the own group), and every group's directory of that range is made, 0700 and empty, by every launch before its settings file is written (U498d, login_dirs_make: srt 0.0.81's Linux backend mounts nothing for a denyRead entry that is not there, so a deny of another group's directory bound nothing until that group's first launch or login made it; a link, a file or another user's directory at any group's path refuses the launch by name, own_slots_check and login_dirs_make), and the own group's directory is the one login a seat reads or writes. The legacy shared directory .state/claude is read, granted, copied, made and removed by no launch (standing order 54). No token file and no CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: the shim clears the name, and no seat reads the operator's ~/.claude. The dsh role (regime-cutover U272, after the four audits of the standalone launcher of PR 687): the DeepSeek harness control host is contained the same way, by this lever, as a role whose differences from the worker are rows of the role table (the case ${role} after the options, seat_write_roots, the read grants in seat_sandbox_write, the command the shim execs, the launch at the end) and nothing else. Its rows: no pane and no hcom bus (the launch runs the shim <sandbox>/bin/dsh in the foreground, waits and returns dsh's status); a per-launch seat name <name>-<utc stamp>-<pid>, so the sandbox, its settings file and the state slot are per launch and two launches at once share no file (the Claude Code directory is the shared one, as for every role); the cwd <seats-root>/.state/<name>/cwd, a scratch directory this lever makes (no worktree); the write roots DSH_HOME, that slot, the role's own omp profile ~/.omp/profiles/dsh (the login child omp auth-gateway stdio lives there, selected by OMP_PROFILE, and writes its agent.db at start) and ~/.omp/run, with no git common directory and no hcom store; the read grants the cwd, that slot, DSH_HOME, that profile, ~/.agents/skills and the pinned tool directory, with no git common directory, no hcom store and no record of the main checkout (U272c); a deny row (U272d: srt reads everything an explicit deny does not name, so a grant the role lacks denies nothing) naming the physical paths of the checkout's git directory and common directory, the .git entry of every linked worktree git lists, the hcom store and every existing ~/.local/state/hcom-* sibling, the records <checkout>/.orchestration and every other seat's directory, denied for read and for write; every row of the final allowRead and allowWrite lists judged against every row of the final denyRead and denyWrite lists (U272f: the rendered settings are the refusal's only source; every path physical and by identity; U272g: the own slots and the own profile exempt from their structural denies by a tag that names each one row by its position in its list, never a spelling, so a DSH_HOME at or inside an exempted row's path is judged like any row), a hit refused before anything is made; DSH_HOME in the protected set before any tool is resolved; the command <DSH_HOME>/bin/dsh, a physical executable file that runs inside srt only; and the environment reduced by /usr/bin/env -i to HOME, USER, LANG, TERM, PATH, DSH_HOME, OMP_PROFILE and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR before the shim adds its own exports (regime-cutover U312: a caller's CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is no input for any role). No rules file, --config overlay, -e list or login preflight is read for it. Its profile config row (regime-cutover U310): the rendered overlay ~/.agents/omp/profiles/dsh.yml (the generator's, like the seat overlays) is placed as the profile's own ~/.omp/profiles/dsh/agent/config.yml, the file the gateway child omp auth-gateway stdio reads for its model providers, every extensions entry rewritten to its canonical claude.levers.extensions path as the omp roles' -e list is; a config already equal is left alone, a different one replaced and the launch says so, and a linked agent/ or config.yml is refused before anything is made (profile_config_check, a reading that creates nothing; a canonical path holding a control character, a leading - or a # after white space is refused by name before it is rendered, rendered_path_check, U310f). The write is one run of the pinned helper profile-config-place.py on one held descriptor of agent/ (profile_config_place, regime-cutover U310d: the compare, the exclusive create at a random name, the write, the rename and the read-back all through dir_fd; this lever checks no path in agent/ and then acts on it), after the per-launch slots; the helper runs from the lever's own copy, made once this launch in a directory of its own and hashed there against the manifest pin, so the path beside this file is read once (helper_copy_make, U310f); a dry run runs it with --dry-run after settings_judge and writes nothing. The per-launch sandbox and state slot are removed when dsh exits, by a refusal after they were made (refuse), and by the trap a hangup, interrupt or termination runs before this process ends by that signal. The router role (regime-cutover U321, U343i): the dsh row with four cells of its own and nothing else. U317b measured (2026-11-07T00:12Z, the prototype at pin 8c32a9dc) that dsh-superagent's Runtime does not start without the dsh-host-webserver plugin, so the Router needs a loopback listener, which the dsh row forbids. The cells: the DSH profile router, the only one the role accepts (--profile router or none; a --profile, --profile=<name>, -p or -p<name> among the verbatim dsh arguments is refused by name too, U321b, so dsh never reads a second selector after the fixed one); allowLocalBinding: true in the srt settings (srt 0.0.81 has no loopback-only form, so the grant is bind and inbound on every interface; the upstream Management API bounds it: it accepts the hosts 127.0.0.1:<port> and localhost:<port> alone and only with the x-orchestrator-request header, upstream docs/006-deployment.md; the port is the profile's, this role grants binding and no port); the Router's state root <DSH_HOME>/router-state, where U317b renders stateDir, as a write root of its own (seat_write_roots), derived from the one physical DSH_HOME the launch holds (dsh_home_hold: the DSH_HOME grant, the environment line and the state root all read it, U321d) and held exactly once, by state_root_hold, before anything of the launch is made (U321b, U321c: no link, present a directory of this user, its physical path inside the held home; the rendering carries the held value and nothing resolves the path again); absent, it is made 0700 after the home has passed the deny judgement, in a real launch alone (a dry run makes nothing and says what a launch would make, U321d); and the broker directory <state slot>/broker (regime-cutover U343i, the mechanism-change row of 2026-11-10T06:20:28Z, form remove; verdicts U343g-8a049561 and U343h-eb648bcd, class record-path), where acp-broker listens and writes its exit records, denied to the Router for write as one tagged denyWrite row inside the state-slot grant and made 0700 by the launch before the settings are written (broker_dir_make; a dry run says what a launch would make), so the Router reads it and connects to its socket and can plant, rename or unlink nothing in it. The Router's credential root <DSH_HOME>/router-credentials (regime-cutover U353, M-26 stage B; U353b; U353d): the one directory the role reads beyond the dsh row's grants, allowRead row 7, where the operator places the agent account's gh login (router-gh reads the token from its gh/hosts.yml); held like the state root by every role (cred_home_hold, cred_root_hold: under the held physical DSH_HOME for the foreground rows and under the caller's DSH_HOME else ~/.dsh for the omp roles, which hold no DSH_HOME; no link, a directory of this user, inside the home), made 0700 by every role's real launch before its settings file is written (cred_root_make; the foreground rows after the judgement), because srt 0.0.81's Linux backend mounts nothing for a denyRead entry that is not there (U353d), and denied for read and for write by every row but the router's (the role table's cred_root_grant cell: read for the router row, deny for the dsh row; the omp rows in seat_settings_render) and for write by the router row too, so no role writes it and only the Router reads it. The omp profile, OMP_PROFILE and every other row are the dsh role's, so the role's rendered settings differ from the dsh role's in exactly the binding value, that one write root, that one deny row and the credential root's grant. The router row's broker (regime-cutover U344, M-24 part 2; U344c): the row's broker cell starts acp-broker from a private per-launch copy of the lever set beside this file (<state>/acp-broker.<name>/, each file held as helper_path_check holds a helper and its copy hashed against its claude.levers.sha256.<name> pin before the broker's first byte runs, broker_copy_make; the copy run under /bin/bash with the held physical DSH_HOME in its environment) after the settings are written and before the shim, reads the broker's own line acp-broker: listening on <sock> from a pipe it holds as the readiness sign (never the socket path's existence, which precedes listen; broker_start), and renders network.allowUnixSockets naming the socket's directory <seats-root>/.state/<name>/broker, the fourth cell's, for this role alone (U342 measured: srt opens the sockets under it and nothing else); when dsh exits, and in the trap, the broker is stopped by SIGTERM, its exit status read and the copy directory removed (broker_stop): a status other than a clean end is named and the launch exits 2, never silent (standing order 21). Every role's settings text comes from the one writer both levers source, seat-settings-render.sh (sourced from a private copy hashed against its pin, renderer_source, U344c; every root an argument of this lever), so the worker's settings the broker renders and the dsh row's cannot drift (tests/unit/test_acp_broker.py holds them byte for byte).
