# @arg $@ string The rows after them.
json_paths() {
    local what=$1 patterns=$2 row
    shift 2
    for row in "$@"; do
        clean_row "${row}" "${patterns}" ||
            refuse "${what} '${row}' is not a clean absolute path: every component must be [A-Za-z0-9._@+-] and neither '.' nor '..', with no trailing '/'"
    done
    seat_settings_rows_json "${patterns}" "$@" || refuse "the ${what} list could not be rendered (seat_settings_rows_json failed)"
}

# @description Print the `filesystem.allowWrite` entries of the seat settings file `$2`, one per line: by
#   `/usr/bin/plutil` on macOS (`-extract … raw -expect array` prints the count, `-expect string` each entry; macOS
#   12 and later, plutil(1)), by `/usr/bin/jq` on Linux (from install/ubuntu/common/dependencies.sh). Each entry must
#   be a clean path.
# @arg $1 string The system name (`uname -s`).
# @arg $2 string The settings file.
# @exitcode 1 The file cannot be read, has no such array, or holds an entry that is not a clean path.
allow_write_list() {
    local n i entry line
    case $1 in
    Darwin)
        n=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract filesystem.allowWrite raw -expect array -o - "$2") || return 1
        [[ ${n} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
        for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
            # -n prints no newline of plutil's own, and the 'x' keeps an entry's trailing newlines from the command
            # substitution, so "/tmp/root\n" reaches clean_path whole and is refused.
            entry=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract "filesystem.allowWrite.${i}" raw -expect string -n -o - "$2" && printf x) ||
                return 1
            entry=${entry%x}
            clean_path "${entry}" || return 1
            printf '%s\n' "${entry}"
        done
        ;;
    *)
        [[ -x /usr/bin/jq ]] || return 1
        # Every entry must be a string without a newline, or the line-per-entry output below would drop or split it.
        /usr/bin/jq -e '.filesystem.allowWrite | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string" and (test("\n") | not))' \
            "$2" > /dev/null || return 1
        n=$(/usr/bin/jq -e '.filesystem.allowWrite | length' "$2") || return 1
        # No -e here: an empty array prints nothing, which -e would report as a failure; so jq's status is checked
        # unconditionally, and an empty read with a nonzero n fails the count check below.
        entry=$(/usr/bin/jq -r '.filesystem.allowWrite[]' "$2") || return 1
        i=0
        while IFS= read -r line; do
            [[ -n ${line} ]] || continue
            clean_path "${line}" || return 1
            printf '%s\n' "${line}"
            i=$((i + 1))
        done <<< "${entry}"
        ((i == n)) || return 1
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Set `ancestors` to the absolute path `$1` and every directory above it, up to `/` (regime-cutover
#   U85). Every ancestor walk of hcom-seat goes through this: a relative path (a `#!sh` interpreter line) would never
#   reach `/`, so it is refused before the walk, and the walk itself stops at `/` and refuses after 4096 steps.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @set ancestors The paths, `$1` first.
ancestors_of() {
    local p=$1 n=0
    [[ ${p} == /* && ${p} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
        refuse "'${p}' is not an absolute path free of control characters"
    ancestors=()
    while :; do
        ancestors+=("${p}")
        [[ ${p} != / ]] || return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow the walk ends at the root, no path compare
        n=$((n + 1))
        ((n <= 4096)) || refuse "the path ${1} has more than 4096 components"
        p=${p%/*}
        [[ -n ${p} ]] || p=/
    done
}

# @description Set `dir_list` to every entry of directory `$1`, dot names included, `.` and `..` excluded, in glob
#   order (regime-cutover U95): `dotglob` and `nullglob` for this one glob, then restored. Every directory whose
#   entries matter (the worktree git directories, a seats root, a `.sandbox`) is listed this way, so no consumer sees
#   a dot-named entry that another misses. Fail-closed, so `nullglob` cannot pass a failed read off as an empty
#   directory: an absent `$1` lists nothing; one that exists must be a real directory, no link, readable and
#   searchable, and `/bin/ls -A` (its status checked) must count exactly the entries the glob saw. Anything else, an
#   unreadable directory or one whose read fails, refuses (exit 2).
# @arg $1 string A directory.
# @set dir_list The entries, as `$1/<name>`.
dir_entries() {
    local de_dot=0 de_null=0 de_p de_listing de_line de_n=0
    dir_list=()
    if [[ ! -e $1 && ! -L $1 ]]; then return 0; fi
    [[ -d $1 && ! -L $1 ]] || refuse "cannot list $1: it is not a real directory (a symbolic link or another file)"
    [[ -r $1 && -x $1 ]] || refuse "cannot list $1: it is not readable"
    if shopt -q dotglob; then de_dot=1; fi
    if shopt -q nullglob; then de_null=1; fi
    shopt -s dotglob nullglob
    for de_p in "$1"/*; do
        case ${de_p##*/} in
        . | ..) ;;
        *) dir_list+=("${de_p}") ;;
        esac
    done
    if ((! de_dot)); then shopt -u dotglob; fi
    if ((! de_null)); then shopt -u nullglob; fi
    de_listing=$(/bin/ls -A -- "$1" && printf .) || refuse "cannot list $1: reading it failed"
    de_listing=${de_listing%.}
    if [[ -n ${de_listing} ]]; then
        while IFS= read -r de_line; do
            [[ -n ${de_line} ]] || refuse "cannot list $1: reading it gave an empty name"
            de_n=$((de_n + 1))
        done <<< "${de_listing%$'\n'}"
    fi
    ((de_n == ${#dir_list[@]})) ||
        refuse "cannot list $1: reading it gave ${de_n} entries, the glob ${#dir_list[@]} (a failed or changing read)"
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) when `$1`, a seats root's `.sandbox`, exists and cannot be listed (regime-cutover
#   U85): every seat's sandbox denies reads of it, so this process runs inside a seat that unset the environment
#   markers. Checked before the directory is enumerated (dir_entries), which would refuse with a generic message.
# @arg $1 string A `.sandbox` directory.
refuse_inside_a_seat() {
    if [[ -e $1 ]] && ! /bin/ls "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        refuse "refused inside a seat sandbox ($1 is unreadable): launch seats from a terminal outside every seat"
    fi
}

# @description Set `settings_files` to the srt settings file of every seat under each seats root `$@`, dot-named
#   sandbox entries included (dir_entries), whether or not the file exists (the caller skips absent ones).
# @arg $@ string Seats roots.
# @set settings_files The paths.
seat_settings_files() {
    local root seat
    settings_files=()
    for root in "$@"; do
        refuse_inside_a_seat "${root%/}/.sandbox"
        dir_entries "${root%/}/.sandbox"
        for seat in ${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"}; do settings_files+=("${seat}/srt-settings.json"); done
    done
}

# @description Succeed when `$1`, a path read from a git pointer file (a `.git` file's `gitdir:`, a `commondir`, a
#   `gitdir` back-pointer), is in git's own form (regime-cutover U95): non-empty, no control character, no empty
#   component (`//`), no trailing `/`, no `.` component, and `..` only as the leading components of a relative path
#   (git's relative form, `../..` or `../../.git/worktrees/x`). git writes its pointers so. Anything else refuses at
#   the caller before any type test, since a trailing `/` or `/.` makes `[[ -L … ]]` follow a link and a `..` after
#   a link resolves differently from the text. Builtins only.
# @arg $1 string The path as read.
# @exitcode 1 It is not in git's form.
git_form_path() {
    local rest c lead=1
    [[ -n $1 && $1 != */ && $1 != *//* && $1 != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow a form test on one path, no compare
    rest=$1
    if [[ ${rest} == /* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path test
        rest=${rest#/}
        lead=0
    fi
    while [[ -n ${rest} ]]; do
        c=${rest%%/*}
        if [[ ${rest} == */* ]]; then rest=${rest#*/}; else rest=''; fi # lint-comparisons: allow splitting one path into components
        case ${c} in
        .) return 1 ;;
        ..) ((lead)) || return 1 ;;
        *) lead=0 ;;
        esac
    done
}

# @description Print the physical form of the absolute path `$1`: every symlink followed (at most 40 hops in all,
#   one budget for the whole resolution) and the directory in its `pwd -P` form. A path that does not exist yet is
#   its nearest existing ancestor's physical form with the rest appended, so a write root a launch has not created
#   yet still compares with what it will be. Iterative (regime-cutover U85): a dangling link that names a path
#   under itself (`.state/<name> -> <name>/child`) spends the one budget and fails instead of recursing. Only shell
#   builtins and `/usr/bin/readlink` run.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @stdout The physical path.
# @exitcode 1 Not absolute, a control character in it or in a link, more than 40 links, or a directory that cannot
#   be resolved.
physical_path() {
    local p=$1 tail='' link dir n=0
    [[ ${p} == /* && ${p} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
    while :; do
        # p is absolute, so each step shortens it and the walk ends at `/`, which exists.
        while [[ ! -e ${p} && ! -L ${p} ]]; do
            tail=/${p##*/}${tail}
            p=${p%/*}
            [[ -n ${p} ]] || p=/
        done
        [[ -L ${p} ]] || break
        n=$((n + 1))
        ((n <= 40)) || return 1
        # The '.' keeps a target's own trailing newlines from the command substitution.
        link=$(/usr/bin/readlink "${p}" && printf .) || return 1
        link=${link%.}
        link=${link%$'\n'}
        [[ -n ${link} && ${link} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1
        case ${link} in
        /*) p=${link} ;;
        *) p=${p%/*}/${link} ;;
        esac
    done
    if [[ ${p} == / ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the root itself, whose `cd //` form pwd prints as `//`
        printf '%s\n' "${tail:-/}"
    elif [[ -d ${p} ]]; then
        dir=$(cd "${p}/" && pwd -P) || return 1
        printf '%s%s\n' "${dir%/}" "${tail}"
    else
        dir=$(cd "${p%/*}/" && pwd -P) || return 1
        printf '%s/%s%s\n' "${dir%/}" "${p##*/}" "${tail}"
    fi
}

# @description Print the physical file `$1` names (physical_path); it must be a regular executable file.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @stdout The physical path.
# @exitcode 1 physical_path failed, or the result is not a regular executable file.
physical_file() {
    local p
    p=$(physical_path "$1") || return 1
    [[ -f ${p} && -x ${p} ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${p}"
}

# @description Hold the dsh and router rows' DSH_HOME in its one physical form (regime-cutover U321d, verdict
#   U321c-b80a4794 P1 `:630` and P2 `:635`, class containment-boundary, form remove): `dsh_home` is a path the seat's
#   user can retarget (a link at the seat-writable physical home), and rounds 2 and 3 resolved it in three places (the
#   state root's hold, the write-root rendering and the deny row), so a retarget between two of them rendered the
#   DSH_HOME grant at the real home and the state root under another directory. Now the home is resolved exactly once,
#   here, into `dsh_home_phys`, right after the one resolver (physical_path) is defined and before the private tool
#   directory or anything else of the launch; the protected set, the state root (state_root_hold), the DSH_HOME grant
#   and read grant (seat_write_roots, seat_settings_render), the judged rows, the dsh command and the environment line
#   all read that variable and nothing resolves or re-reads `dsh_home` after this. The physical form is held to the same
#   clean-path rule as the spelled one (srt renders it), and it is a directory.
# @set dsh_home_phys The physical DSH_HOME; empty for the omp roles.
dsh_home_hold() {
    dsh_home_phys=$(physical_path "${dsh_home}") || refuse "cannot resolve DSH_HOME ${dsh_home}"
    require_clean_path DSH_HOME "${dsh_home_phys}"
    [[ -d ${dsh_home_phys} ]] || refuse "DSH_HOME ${dsh_home} resolves to ${dsh_home_phys}, which is not a directory"
}

# @description Hold the role table's `state_root` cell (regime-cutover U321b, verdict U321-fec87e14 P1 `:1551`; U321c,
#   verdict U321b-7dfaa839 P1 `:1567` and P3, the mechanism-change row of 2026-11-07T02:25:00Z, form remove; U321d,
#   verdict U321c-b80a4794 P1 `:630` and P2 `:635`): `<DSH_HOME>/<state_root>` is the one write root of the router row
#   that is neither a slot this lever makes nor DSH_HOME itself. Round 1 rendered it as spelled, so a link at
#   `router-state` escaped DSH_HOME; round 2 held it physical here and resolved it a second time where the roots are
#   rendered, so a swap between the two reads rendered an outside grant; round 3 resolved the path once but derived it
#   from `dsh_home`, which it resolved on its own, and made the directory here, before the home's deny judgement, so a
#   retargeted DSH_HOME link put the state root outside the home the grant named, and `--home ~/.ssh --dry-run` made
#   `~/.ssh/router-state` before refusing. Now the path is `${dsh_home_phys}/<state_root>`, opened relative to the held
#   physical home (dsh_home_hold) and never through the spelled DSH_HOME, resolved exactly once, here, into
#   `state_root_phys`, which seat_write_roots prints verbatim and nothing else resolves again. The hold is one of the
#   pre-launch checks, before the private tool directory, any link, tool copy or host git call of the launch, in a dry
#   run too, and it writes nothing: the path is no symbolic link; present, it is a directory and this user's (each
#   refused by name); its physical form (physical_path, its status read) lies inside the held home by the prefix of
#   the two trailing-slash forms. Absent, it is noted (`state_root_absent`) and made 0700 by state_root_make, after
#   the home has passed the deny judgement (settings_judge) and only in a real launch; a dry run makes nothing and
#   prints what a launch would make. srt enforces the held physical directory; a later swap of the spelled path grants
#   nothing (seat_sandbox_write refuses by name when the held directory is gone, and derives nothing from the path).
# @set state_root_phys The physical path of the held state root; empty for a row without one.
# @set state_root_absent 1 when the held state root does not exist yet (state_root_make makes it).
state_root_hold() {
    local spelled=${dsh_home_phys}/${state_root}
    [[ ! -L ${spelled} ]] ||
        refuse "the ${role} role's state root ${spelled} is a symbolic link; it must be a real directory inside DSH_HOME, or absent"
    if [[ -e ${spelled} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${spelled} ]] || refuse "the ${role} role's state root ${spelled} exists and is not a directory"
        [[ -O ${spelled} ]] || refuse "the ${role} role's state root ${spelled} is not this user's directory"
        state_root_absent=0
    else
        state_root_absent=1
    fi
    state_root_phys=$(physical_path "${spelled}") || refuse "cannot resolve the ${role} role's state root ${spelled}"
    [[ ${state_root_phys}/ == "${dsh_home_phys}"/* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both operands physical (physical_path); the trailing slash makes the prefix a whole component
        refuse "the ${role} role's state root ${spelled} resolves to ${state_root_phys}, outside DSH_HOME ${dsh_home_phys}"
}

# @description Make the held state root (state_root_hold) when it was absent, 0700, after the home's deny judgement
#   passed and only in a real launch (regime-cutover U321d, verdict U321c-b80a4794 P2 `:635`): the one write before
#   the launch's own, inside the held physical DSH_HOME, which the dsh row owns. A dry run makes nothing and says what
#   a launch would make. Present or made, the held path is a real directory of this user, else refused by name.
# @arg $1 int 1 for a dry run.
state_root_make() {
    if ((state_root_absent)); then
        if (($1)); then
            echo "hcom-seat: the ${role} role's state root ${state_root_phys} does not exist; a launch creates it (0700)" >&2
            return 0
        fi
        # mkdir takes no existing entry, so a link planted since the hold fails it.
        (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${state_root_phys}") || refuse "cannot create the ${role} role's state root ${state_root_phys}"
    fi
    [[ -d ${state_root_phys} && ! -L ${state_root_phys} && -O ${state_root_phys} ]] ||
        refuse "the ${role} role's state root ${state_root_phys} is not a real directory of this user"
}

# @description The router row's broker directory `<state slot>/broker` (regime-cutover U343i; the mechanism-change row
#   of 2026-11-10T06:20:28Z, form remove; verdicts U343g-8a049561 P1 `acp-broker:1262` and U343h-eb648bcd P1
#   `acp-relay.py:284`, `acp-broker:963`, class record-path: an unsandboxed process naming a path inside a directory the
#   Router may write follows whatever the Router planted there, however each operation is hardened, because the Router
#   owns the directory entry; the Router's write grant on the directory ceases to exist). The row's denyWrite entry
#   (seat_settings_render) must exist when the settings are written (srt 0.0.81's Linux backend mounts nothing for a
#   deny entry that does not exist, U353d), so a launch makes it here, 0700, by one `mkdir` that takes no existing entry:
#   called by seat_sandbox_write once the per-launch state slot exists (proved absent before anything was made, so an
#   entry at the name is planted since and refuses) and before the settings file is written, with the slot trap armed,
#   so a refusal removes the slot and the directory with it. A dry run (`$1` is 1) makes nothing and says what a launch
#   would make, the form of state_root_make. acp-broker takes the directory as made (this user's, 0700, no link, empty,
#   else it refuses by name and makes nothing there) and leaves it standing at its end; slots_remove takes it with the
#   slot. A row without a broker directory (`broker_dir` empty) makes and says nothing.
# @arg $1 int 1 for a dry run.
broker_dir_make() {
    [[ -n ${broker_dir} ]] || return 0
    if (($1)); then
        echo "hcom-seat: the ${role} role's broker directory ${broker_dir_phys} does not exist; a launch creates it (0700)" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${broker_dir_phys}") ||
        refuse "cannot create the ${role} role's broker directory ${broker_dir_phys} (an entry stands at the name; the per-launch slot is never reused)"
    [[ -d ${broker_dir_phys} && ! -L ${broker_dir_phys} && -O ${broker_dir_phys} ]] ||
        refuse "the ${role} role's broker directory ${broker_dir_phys} is not a real directory of this user"
}

# @description Hold the home the Router's credential root lies in (regime-cutover U353d, verdict U353-318f268d P1
#   `:2383`): every role makes and denies `<home>/router-credentials`, so every role resolves the home exactly once,
#   here, before anything of the launch is made. The foreground rows take the held physical DSH_HOME (dsh_home_hold).
#   The omp roles hold no DSH_HOME; their home is the one router-gh resolves, the caller's `DSH_HOME` else `~/.dsh`,
#   held to a clean path, resolved once (physical_path; a linked home through its target) into a clean physical path
#   and, present, a directory, each else refused by name. Absent (an omp seat host without the dsh kit), it is noted
#   (`cred_home_absent`) and made 0700 by cred_root_make with the root, so the omp rows' deny names a directory that
#   exists.
# @set cred_home_phys The physical home the credential root lies in.
# @set cred_home_absent 1 when that home does not exist yet.
cred_home_hold() {
    local spelled
    if [[ ${role_launch} == foreground ]]; then
        cred_home_phys=${dsh_home_phys}
        return 0
    fi
    spelled=${DSH_HOME:-${HOME}/.dsh}
    require_clean_path DSH_HOME "${spelled}"
    cred_home_phys=$(physical_path "${spelled}") || refuse "cannot resolve DSH_HOME ${spelled}, the home of the Router's credential root"
    require_clean_path DSH_HOME "${cred_home_phys}"
    if [[ -e ${spelled} || -L ${spelled} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${cred_home_phys} ]] || refuse "DSH_HOME ${spelled} resolves to ${cred_home_phys}, which is not a directory"
    else
        cred_home_absent=1
    fi
}

# @description Hold the Router's credential root (regime-cutover U353, U353d): `<home>/router-credentials` (`cred_root`
#   under the held home of cred_home_hold), the directory the agent account's gh login lives under (`router-gh` sets
#   `GH_CONFIG_DIR` to its `gh/`): the one read grant of the router row beyond the dsh row's (`cred_root_grant` read)
#   and a read-and-write deny of every other row (the dsh row's `deny` cell; the omp rows, U353b and U353d). The same
#   hold as the state root (state_root_hold): the path is opened relative to the held physical home and resolved
#   exactly once, here, into `cred_root_phys`, which seat_settings_render renders verbatim and nothing resolves again;
#   one of the pre-launch checks of every role, before the private tool directory, any link, tool copy or host git
#   call, in a dry run too, and it writes nothing: no symbolic link (a link into the operator's own `~/.config/gh`
#   would hand the Router another account's login, or an omp seat a deny of another directory); present, a directory
#   of this user; its physical form inside the held home. Absent, it is noted (`cred_root_absent`) and made 0700 by
#   cred_root_make for every role: srt 0.0.81's Linux backend mounts nothing for a denyRead entry that is not there
#   (dist/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.js:1810-1812: "a tmpfs (directory) or a /dev/null mask on the entry itself;
#   nothing when it is not there"), so a deny of an absent root held nothing once the Router had made it (verdict
#   U353-318f268d P1 `:2383`); now the root exists before any role's settings file is written.
# @set cred_root_phys The physical path of the held credential root.
# @set cred_root_absent 1 when the held credential root does not exist yet.
cred_root_hold() {
    local spelled=${cred_home_phys}/${cred_root}
    [[ ! -L ${spelled} ]] ||
        refuse "the ${role} role's credential root ${spelled} is a symbolic link; it must be a real directory inside DSH_HOME, or absent"
    if [[ -e ${spelled} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${spelled} ]] || refuse "the ${role} role's credential root ${spelled} exists and is not a directory"
        [[ -O ${spelled} ]] || refuse "the ${role} role's credential root ${spelled} is not this user's directory"
        cred_root_absent=0
    else
        cred_root_absent=1
    fi
    cred_root_phys=$(physical_path "${spelled}") || refuse "cannot resolve the ${role} role's credential root ${spelled}"
    [[ ${cred_root_phys}/ == "${cred_home_phys}"/* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both operands physical (physical_path); the trailing slash makes the prefix a whole component
        refuse "the ${role} role's credential root ${spelled} resolves to ${cred_root_phys}, outside DSH_HOME ${cred_home_phys}"
}

# @description Make the held credential root (cred_root_hold) when it was absent, 0700, for every role (regime-cutover
#   U353; U353d: the dsh and omp rows too, since the deny they render must name a directory that exists when srt reads
#   it), the home first when it was absent (cred_home_hold, the omp roles alone), in a real launch alone and, for the
#   foreground rows, after their home has passed the deny judgement (the form of state_root_make). A dry run makes
#   nothing and says what a launch would make. Two launches at once (the dsh role's normal case; an orchestrator and a
#   worker started together) may both find the root absent: the loser of the mkdir race takes the directory the winner
#   made, held to a real directory of this user, while a link planted since the hold fails mkdir and that hold alike.
#   Present or made, the held path is a real directory of this user, else refused by name. The login inside it is
#   never made here: it is the operator's step.
# @arg $1 int 1 for a dry run.
cred_root_make() {
    local path
    if ((cred_root_absent)); then
        if (($1)); then
            echo "hcom-seat: the ${role} role's credential root ${cred_root_phys} does not exist; a launch creates it (0700)" >&2
            return 0
        fi
        if ((cred_home_absent)); then
            path=${cred_home_phys}
            (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${path}") || [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
                refuse "cannot create DSH_HOME ${path}, the home of the ${role} role's credential root"
        fi
        path=${cred_root_phys}
        (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${path}") || [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
            refuse "cannot create the ${role} role's credential root ${path}"
    fi
    [[ -d ${cred_root_phys} && ! -L ${cred_root_phys} && -O ${cred_root_phys} ]] ||
        refuse "the ${role} role's credential root ${cred_root_phys} is not a real directory of this user"
}
dsh_home_phys='' state_root_phys='' state_root_absent=0 broker_dir_phys='' cred_home_phys='' cred_home_absent=0 cred_root_phys='' cred_root_absent=0
if [[ ${role_launch} == foreground ]]; then dsh_home_hold; fi
if [[ -n ${state_root} ]]; then state_root_hold; fi
cred_home_hold
cred_root_hold

# @description Refuse (exit 2) when the physical path `$2`, or any directory above it, has the identity of a
#   protected write root (`root_ids`).
# @arg $1 string A label for the refusal.
# @arg $2 string A physical path.
refuse_if_seat_writable() {
    local ids id i named probe=()
    # The physical file and every directory above it, up to /, each compared by (device, inode): a case alias on a
    # case-insensitive file system or a hardlink of a writable file has the identity of what it aliases.
    ancestors_of "$2"
    probe=("${ancestors[@]}")
    ids=$(/usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" -- "${probe[@]}") || refuse "cannot read the identity of $1 $2 or a directory above it"
    i=0
    while IFS= read -r id; do
        if [[ ${root_ids} == *$'\n'"${id}"$'\n'* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
            named=$(root_named "${id}") || named=${id}
            refuse "$1 $2 is or lies under the seat write root ${named} (${probe[i]} has its identity ${id})"
        fi
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "${ids}"
}

# @description Print the write root whose identity is `$1`.
# @arg $1 string A `<device>:<inode>` identity.
root_named() {
    local i
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#root_id_list[@]}; i++)); do
        [[ ${root_id_list[i]} != "$1" ]] || { # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
            printf '%s\n' "${root_path_list[i]}"
            return 0
        }
    done
}

# @description Add the (device, inode) identity of every argument that exists, file or directory, every link
#   followed, to the protected set (`root_ids`, `root_id_list`, `root_path_list`). A path that does not exist holds
#   no executable; one that exists and cannot be read is a refusal.
# @arg $@ string Absolute paths.
add_roots() {
    local present=() path ids id i=0 named
    for path in "$@"; do
        [[ ${path} == /* && ${path} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || refuse "the seat write root '${path}' is not an absolute path" # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
        [[ -e ${path} || -L ${path} ]] || continue
        present+=("${path}")
    done
    ((${#present[@]})) || return 0
    ids=$(/usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" -- "${present[@]}") || refuse "cannot read the identity of a seat write root among: ${present[*]}"
    while IFS= read -r id; do
        [[ ${id} =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "unexpected identity '${id}' of ${present[i]}"
        root_ids+=${id}$'\n'
        root_id_list+=("${id}")
        named=$(physical_path "${present[i]}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seat write root ${present[i]}"
        root_path_list+=("${named}")
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "${ids}"
}

# @description Succeed when a tool is a shim, as scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh decides it (U61): its physical file
#   is named mise in any letter case or is the mise binary, or the directory it was found in or resolves to is named
#   shims in any letter case. A mise shim picks its version from the cwd's config files, which a seat writes.
# @arg $1 string The path the tool was found at.
# @arg $2 string Its physical path.
is_shim() {
    local d
    [[ ${2##*/} == [Mm][Ii][Ss][Ee] ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow a file-name test, not a comparison of two paths
    [[ -n ${mise_real} && $2 -ef ${mise_real} ]] && return 0
    for d in "${1%/*}" "${2%/*}"; do
        d=$(physical_path "${d:-/}") || return 0
        [[ ${d}/ == */[Ss][Hh][Ii][Mm][Ss]/* ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow a directory-name test, not a comparison of two paths
    done
    return 1
}

# @description Print the first executable `$1` on PATH, which hcom-seat has set: the system directories, then the
#   private tool directory before them once it is filled.
# @arg $1 string The command name.
# @stdout The path, symlinks not yet followed.
# @exitcode 1 None found.
find_on_path() {
    local path_dir path_dirs=()
    IFS=: read -r -a path_dirs <<< "${PATH}"
    for path_dir in "${path_dirs[@]}"; do
        [[ -n ${path_dir} && -x ${path_dir}/$1 && ! -d ${path_dir}/$1 ]] || continue
        printf '%s\n' "${path_dir}/$1"
        return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# @description Print the value of the git pointer file `$1` (a `.git` file, `commondir`, `gitdir`) read whole
#   (regime-cutover U85). git consumes the complete content less its trailing newlines, so only a single line is a
#   value: content that cannot be read, is empty, or holds any control character once one final newline is dropped (a
#   second line, a carriage return) fails, and the caller refuses. Pointer files are read this way only where git
#   cannot be asked yet (before the git state is checked); everywhere after, git answers (git_paths_of). A NUL
#   byte, or a byte count other than the file's size, fails too.
# @arg $1 string The file.
# @stdout The value.
# @exitcode 1 It cannot be read, is empty, or is not a single line free of control characters.
pointer_value() {
    local LC_ALL=C content size
    # Bash drops NUL bytes from a command substitution, so they are made \001 (a control character, refused) in the
    # same pass, and the bytes read must number the file's size: what is checked is what git reads.
    content=$({ /bin/cat -- "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\000' '\001'; } && printf .) || return 1
    content=${content%.}
    size=$(/usr/bin/wc -c < "$1") || return 1
    size=${size//[[:space:]]/}
    [[ ${size} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && ((${#content} == size)) || return 1
    content=${content%$'\n'}
    [[ -n ${content} && ${content} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${content}"
}

# @description Set `size_list` to the byte size of each file `$@`, links followed, in order, from one
#   `/usr/bin/stat` run (regime-cutover U95). Fail-closed: the run's status (xargs passes a failed stat on), every
#   line a bare number, and exactly one line per file; anything else refuses (exit 2) before a size is used.
# @arg $@ string Files.
# @set size_list The sizes.
sizes_of() {
    local out line
    size_list=()
    (($#)) || return 0
    out=$(printf '%s\0' "$@" | /usr/bin/xargs -0 /usr/bin/stat "${size_args[@]}" --) || refuse 'cannot read the size of the git state files'
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ ${line} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "cannot read the size of a git state file ('${line}')"
        size_list+=("${line}")
    done <<< "${out}"
    ((${#size_list[@]} == $#)) || refuse "cannot read the size of every git state file (${#size_list[@]} of $#)"
}

# @description Set `pointer_list` to the value of each git pointer file `$@`, with the rule of pointer_value
#   (regime-cutover U95): all are read in one pass (`cat | tr`, NUL bytes made \001 there) and cut at the sizes one
#   `stat` gave (sizes_of). The pass counts only when its pipeline succeeded (the `.` sentinel follows its status)
#   and the bytes read number the sizes' sum, checked before any value is cut, so a failed or short read is never
#   used. A file that is empty, or not a single line free of control characters once one final newline is dropped,
#   refuses (exit 2).
# @arg $@ string Pointer files.
# @set pointer_list The values.
pointer_values() {
    local LC_ALL=C all value off=0 total=0 i=0 files=("$@")
    pointer_list=()
    (($#)) || return 0
    sizes_of "$@"
    all=$({ printf '%s\0' "$@" | /usr/bin/xargs -0 /bin/cat -- | /usr/bin/tr '\000' '\001'; } && printf .) ||
        refuse 'cannot read the git pointer files'
    all=${all%.}
    for ((i = 0; i < $#; i++)); do total=$((total + size_list[i])); done
    ((total == ${#all})) || refuse "cannot read the git pointer files whole (${#all} of ${total} bytes)"
    for ((i = 0; i < $#; i++)); do
        value=${all:off:size_list[i]}
        off=$((off + size_list[i]))
        value=${value%$'\n'}
        [[ -n ${value} && ${value} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] ||
            refuse "cannot read ${files[i]} as one line free of control characters${pointer_hint:-}"
        pointer_list+=("${value}")
    done
}

# @description Resolve `$2` to the argv that runs it with no lookup left: its physical file, preceded by the physical
#   interpreter when it is a `#!` script (`#!/abs/interp` or `#!/usr/bin/env <name>`, no arguments; an interpreter
#   that is itself a script is refused). No part may be, or lie under, a write root of any seat (`root_ids`), since
#   a seat that could rewrite a file the launch runs would run uncontained on the next launch. A failure exits 2
#   naming `$1`.
# @arg $1 string A label for the refusal.
# @arg $2 string The executable's path.
# @set pinned The argv.
# @set pinned_spelled The interpreter as the `#!` line spells it (what the kernel follows), or empty.
pin_exec() {
    local label=$1 file first magic interp name extra interp_path
    pinned_spelled=''
    # The spelling the kernel will follow, every link hop, is held to the identity check too: a link in a write root
    # that points outside it passes the physical check today and can be retargeted before the next exec.
    refuse_if_link_chain_writable "${label}" "$2"
    file=$(physical_file "$2") || refuse "cannot resolve ${label} to a physical executable file: $2"
    refuse_if_seat_writable "${label}" "${file}"
    [[ -r ${file} ]] || refuse "cannot read ${label}: ${file}"
    # Each read's status is checked (pipefail covers head; /usr/bin/od on macOS exits 0 on a read error, so it only
    # formats): a failed read is refused, never taken for a file without an interpreter line.
    magic=$(/usr/bin/head -c 2 -- "${file}" | /usr/bin/od -An -tx1) || refuse "cannot read ${label}: ${file}"
    first=''
    if [[ ${magic//[[:space:]]/} == 2321 ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the hex bytes of `#!`, no path compare
        first=$(/usr/bin/head -n 1 -- "${file}") || refuse "cannot read the interpreter line of ${label}: ${file}"
    fi
    pinned=("${file}")
    case ${first} in
    '#!'*)
        extra=''
        read -r interp name extra <<< "${first#??}"
        pinned_spelled=${interp}
        if [[ ${interp} == /usr/bin/env ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the literal interpreter line, no path compare
            [[ -n ${name} && -z ${extra} && ${name} != -* ]] ||
                refuse "${label}: unsupported interpreter line '${first}' in ${file}"
            interp_path=$(find_on_path "${name}") || refuse "${label}: interpreter ${name} not found on PATH"
        else
            [[ -z ${name} ]] || refuse "${label}: unsupported interpreter line '${first}' in ${file}"
            # The kernel would not run a relative interpreter as written; it is refused before any walk over it.
            [[ ${interp} == /* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path test
                refuse "${label}: interpreter line '${first}' in ${file} names no absolute path"
            interp_path=${interp}
        fi
        refuse_if_link_chain_writable "the interpreter of ${label}" "${interp_path}"
        interp=$(physical_file "${interp_path}") || refuse "cannot resolve the interpreter of ${label}: ${interp_path}"
        refuse_if_seat_writable "${label}" "${interp}"
        [[ -r ${interp} ]] || refuse "cannot read the interpreter of ${label}: ${interp}"
        magic=$(/usr/bin/head -c 2 -- "${interp}" | /usr/bin/od -An -tx1) || refuse "cannot read the interpreter of ${label}: ${interp}"
        [[ ${magic//[[:space:]]/} != 2321 ]] || refuse "${label}: its interpreter ${interp} is itself a script" # lint-comparisons: allow the hex bytes of `#!`, no path compare
        pinned=("${interp}" "${file}")
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) an optional tool whose `#!` line spells its interpreter outside the trusted system
#   directories (regime-cutover U85, a best-effort reduction of the G17 residual, README "Boundary"): the directory
#   the line names, followed physically, must be or lie under `/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/sbin`, `/usr/sbin` or
#   `~/.local/share/mise/installs`, by (device, inode) identity (`trusted_ids`), however the spelling reaches it, so
#   a directory alias into a seat write root (`alias -> $HCOM_DIR/subdir`) is refused. A binary passes.
# @arg $1 string The tool's name, for the refusal.
trusted_interpreter_check() {
    local dir ids id
    [[ -n ${pinned_spelled} ]] || return 0
    dir=${pinned_spelled%/*}
    dir=$(physical_path "${dir:-/}") || refuse "cannot resolve the interpreter directory of $1: ${pinned_spelled}"
    ancestors_of "${dir}"
    ids=$(/usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" -- "${ancestors[@]}") || refuse "cannot read the identity of ${dir}"
    while IFS= read -r id; do
        [[ ${trusted_ids} != *$'\n'"${id}"$'\n'* ]] || return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
    done <<< "${ids}"
    refuse "$1: its interpreter ${pinned_spelled} lies outside /bin, /usr/bin, /sbin, /usr/sbin and ~/.local/share/mise/installs (${dir})"
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) when any hop of the symlink chain `$2` (the spelling itself, then each link target in
#   turn) is, or lies under, a protected write root (refuse_if_seat_writable on each hop as spelled, which compares
#   the hop's target and every directory above the spelling), so the path the kernel follows at exec time cannot be retargeted by a seat.
# @arg $1 string A label for the refusal.
# @arg $2 string An absolute path.
refuse_if_link_chain_writable() {
    local p=$2 link n=0
    [[ ${p} == /* ]] || refuse "$1 ${p} is not an absolute path" # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path test
    while :; do
        # The hop as spelled: stat follows it to its target, and every directory above the spelling is compared too.
        refuse_if_seat_writable "$1" "${p}"
        [[ -L ${p} ]] || return 0
        n=$((n + 1))
        ((n <= 40)) || refuse "$1 ${2}: too many symbolic links"
        link=$(/usr/bin/readlink "${p}") || refuse "cannot read the link $1 ${p}"
        case ${link} in
        /*) p=${link} ;;
        *) p=${p%/*}/${link} ;;
        esac
    done
}

# The tools (regime-cutover U85, the pattern of scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh, U61). First the complete protected
# set, by identity: the (device, inode) of every write root any seat may have that exists, files and directories,
# computed with builtins, /usr/bin/stat, /usr/bin/readlink and the system's settings reader only, before any tool outside the
# system directories runs. It holds the seats roots and the hcom stores of every program, ~/Workspace, the checkout
# this runs in and its git directories, the omp profiles and leases, the Claude Code state, srt's implicit write paths,
# and every `allowWrite` entry of every existing seat settings file (another program's checkout outside ~/Workspace
# included). Then mise's own physical file is held to it before mise runs. Every tool beyond the system directories
# is what `mise which` answers under `env -i` from `/` (no project config, no caller environment), else what
# `command -v` finds on the caller's PATH; an answer is only a name until it passes: absolute, no control character,
# a regular executable file once every link is followed, no shim, and neither its physical file nor any directory
# above it has the identity of a protected root. A passing tool is linked into the private directory
# ~/.local/state/hcom-seat/tools (0700, this user's, outside every seat write root), and PATH becomes that directory
# followed by the system directories; no caller entry is inherited.
os=$(/usr/bin/uname -s) || refuse 'cannot read the operating system name (uname -s)'
if [[ ${os} == Linux && ! -x /usr/bin/jq ]]; then
    refuse 'the system jq /usr/bin/jq is absent; it reads the seat sandbox settings on Linux (apt install jq)'
fi
case ${os} in
Darwin) stat_args=(-L -f '%d:%i') lstat_args=(-f '%d:%i') size_args=(-L -f '%z') mode_args=(-L -f '%Lp') ;;
Linux) stat_args=(-L -c '%d:%i') lstat_args=(-c '%d:%i') size_args=(-L -c '%s') mode_args=(-L -c '%a') ;;
*) refuse "no seat sandbox for ${os}; srt supports macOS and Linux" ;;
esac
# srt 0.0.81 keeps its own TMPDIR writable whatever the policy says (SANDBOX_OWN_WRITE_PATHS in
# dist/sandbox/sandbox-utils.js:499-508 lists /tmp/claude and /private/tmp/claude on every OS). /private exists on
# macOS only; on Linux srt can bind only what exists, so /private/tmp/claude is a write root there only if it exists
# (a nonexistent /private would resolve to no path a seat can write).
# @description Set `srt_tmp_roots` to srt's own writable TMPDIR paths on the operating system `$1` (`uname -s`).
# @arg $1 string Darwin or Linux.
# @set srt_tmp_roots The paths.
srt_tmp_roots_for() {
    srt_tmp_roots=(/tmp/claude /private/tmp/claude)
    if [[ $1 != Darwin && ! -e ${srt_tmp_roots[1]} ]]; then srt_tmp_roots=("${srt_tmp_roots[0]}"); fi
}
srt_tmp_roots_for "${os}"
root_ids=$'\n' root_id_list=() root_path_list=()
# The program stores' root parent `~/.local/state/regime-store` is in the set whole, before the slug is known (regime-cutover
# U219b, verdict U219-ce7e875e P1): the orchestrator writes `<root>/<slug>` (seat_write_roots), so a tool a seat
# plants under it must be refused here, before anything runs it, like one under `~/.local/state/hcom` or the seats roots.
roots=("${HOME}/.local/state/omp-seats" "${HOME}/.local/state/hcom" "${HOME}/.local/state/regime-store" "${HOME}/Workspace"
    "${HOME}/.omp/profiles" "${HOME}/.omp/run" "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-${HOME}/.claude}" "${HOME}/.claude"
    "${HOME}/.claude.json" "${HOME}/.npm/_logs" "${srt_tmp_roots[@]}")
# The dsh role's DSH_HOME, the held physical home (dsh_home_hold), is protected from here on (U272): a tool `mise which`
# or the caller's PATH answers under it is refused before anything runs it, as a tool under a seats root is.
for root in ${HCOM_DIR:+"${HCOM_DIR}"} ${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:+"${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT}"} ${seats_root:+"${seats_root}"} ${dsh_home_phys:+"${dsh_home_phys}"}; do
    roots+=("${root}")
done
# The checkout this runs in, found with builtins: the nearest ancestor with a `.git`, and for a worktree the git
# directory its `.git` file names and that directory's common directory and main checkout. Type before content, as in
# git_state_check (regime-cutover U95): `.git` is a regular file or a real directory, never a link; the git directory
# a `.git` file names is a real directory; its `commondir` is absent or a regular file, no link. A FIFO there would
# leave the guess at the admin directory, so the scan below would miss it and the first git command would block on
# it. A linked worktree's admin directory (git writes a `gitdir` file only there) must hold its `commondir`: without
# it git takes the admin directory for the common directory. All before any git command runs.
cwd_real=$(pwd -P) || refuse 'cannot resolve the working directory'
top=${cwd_real}
while [[ ! -e ${top}/.git && -n ${top} ]]; do top=${top%/*}; done
if [[ -n ${top} || -e /.git ]]; then
    top=${top:-/}
    gitdir=${top}/.git
    [[ ! -L ${gitdir} && (-f ${gitdir} || -d ${gitdir}) ]] ||
        refuse "${gitdir} is not a regular file or a real directory (a symbolic link, FIFO, device or socket), which git would follow or block on; launch from a checkout git made"
    if [[ -f ${gitdir} ]]; then
        line=$(pointer_value "${gitdir}") || refuse "cannot read ${gitdir} as one line free of control characters"
        [[ ${line} == 'gitdir: '* ]] || refuse "${gitdir} holds no 'gitdir: ' line" # lint-comparisons: allow the literal prefix git writes, no path compare
        gitdir=${line#gitdir: }
        git_form_path "${gitdir}" ||
            refuse "${top}/.git names '${gitdir}', not a path in git's own form (no trailing /, no . component, .. only leading a relative path); repair the worktree (\`git worktree repair\`)"
        case ${gitdir} in # lint-comparisons: allow a relative operand is made absolute, no path compare
        /*) ;;
        *) gitdir=${top}/${gitdir} ;;
        esac
        [[ -d ${gitdir} && ! -L ${gitdir} ]] ||
            refuse "the git directory ${gitdir} that ${top}/.git names is not a real directory (absent, a symbolic link or another file); repair the worktree (\`git worktree repair\`) or launch elsewhere"
    fi
    common_guess=${gitdir}
    if [[ -e ${gitdir}/commondir || -L ${gitdir}/commondir ]]; then
        [[ -f ${gitdir}/commondir && ! -L ${gitdir}/commondir ]] ||
            refuse "the git state ${gitdir}/commondir is not a regular file (a symbolic link, FIFO, device, socket or directory), which git would follow or block on; replace it with a regular file holding ../.., or delete the worktree and run \`git worktree prune\` from the main checkout"
        line=$(pointer_value "${gitdir}/commondir") ||
            refuse "cannot read ${gitdir}/commondir as one line free of control characters"
        git_form_path "${line}" ||
            refuse "${gitdir}/commondir holds '${line}', not a path in git's own form (no trailing /, no . component, .. only leading a relative path); replace it with ../.."
        case ${line} in # lint-comparisons: allow a relative operand is made absolute, no path compare
        /*) common_guess=${line} ;;
        *) common_guess=${gitdir}/${line} ;;
        esac
    elif [[ -e ${gitdir}/gitdir || -L ${gitdir}/gitdir ]]; then
        refuse "the worktree git directory ${gitdir} has no commondir, so git would take it for its own common directory; delete the worktree and run \`git worktree prune\` from the main checkout"
    fi
    roots+=("${top}" "${gitdir}" "${common_guess}")
    # The main checkout is the common directory's parent only when that parent's `.git` is the common directory, by
    # identity (a `.GIT` spelling on a case-insensitive volume included); a separate git directory
    # (`git init --separate-git-dir`) has no checkout above it, and its checkout is `top`.
    common_parent=$(physical_path "${common_guess}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common_guess}"
    common_parent=${common_parent%/*}
    common_parent=${common_parent:-/}
    if [[ -d ${common_parent}/.git && ! -L ${common_parent}/.git && ${common_parent}/.git -ef ${common_guess} ]]; then
        roots+=("${common_parent}")
    fi
fi
# Every existing seat settings file, read by the system's reader (allow_write_list); an entry that cannot be read, or
# that is not a clean path, is a refusal.
dir_entries "${HOME}/.local/state/omp-seats"
seat_settings_files ${seats_root:+"${seats_root}"} ${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:+"${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT}"} ${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"}
for settings_file in ${settings_files[@]+"${settings_files[@]}"}; do
    [[ -e ${settings_file} ]] || continue
    listed=$(allow_write_list "${os}" "${settings_file}") ||
        refuse "cannot read a clean allowWrite list from ${settings_file}"
    while IFS= read -r root; do
        if [[ -n ${root} ]]; then roots+=("${root}"); fi
    done <<< "${listed}"
done
add_roots "${roots[@]}"
# @description Resolve every extension directory `$@` to its canonical entry of the extension allow-list
#   (regime-cutover U31): `claude.levers.extensions` in the manifest the self-check read, so the installed copy reads
#   it from ~/.agents, outside every sandbox write root. A read failure is a refusal, not an empty list. The caller
#   gets the canonical allow-list entry (`pwd -P` of the listed path), never the caller's spelling: a symlink the
#   caller controls could be swapped between this check and omp resolving the path.
# @arg $@ string Extension directories.
# @set checked The canonical allow-list entries, in the order given.
extensions_canonical() {
    local allowed ext real listed entry entry_real
    allowed=$(awk '
    /^  levers:$/ { levers = 1; next }
    levers && /^  [^ ]/ { levers = 0 }
    levers && /^    extensions:$/ { list = 1; next }
    list && /^      - / { sub(/^      - /, ""); print; next }
    list { list = 0 }
' "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || refuse "cannot read the extension allow-list in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    [[ -n ${allowed} ]] || refuse "no extension allow-list (claude.levers.extensions) in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    checked=()
    for ext in "$@"; do
        [[ -d ${ext} ]] || refuse "extension directory absent: ${ext}"
        real=$(cd "${ext}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve extension directory: ${ext}"
        listed=''
        while IFS= read -r entry; do
            entry=${entry/#\~/${HOME}}
            # An entry that is absent or cannot be resolved lists nothing, so the extension stays refused.
            [[ -d ${entry} ]] || continue
            entry_real=$(cd "${entry}" && pwd -P) || continue
            if [[ ${entry_real} -ef ${real} ]]; then listed=${entry_real}; fi
        done <<< "${allowed}"
        [[ -n ${listed} ]] || refuse "extension directory is not in the allow-list (claude.levers.extensions): ${ext}"
        checked+=("${listed}")
    done
}
# @description Read whether the path `$1` below HOME exists, every directory above it tested for searchability first
#   (standing order 21, regime-cutover U310b): `[ -e ]` below a directory this user cannot search is false for a
#   present file as for an absent one, so an existing directory that cannot be searched refuses naming it, and
#   `path_present` is read only below searchable directories. A symbolic link counts as present and is not followed; the
#   caller judges it.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path below HOME.
# @set path_present 1 when the path exists, 0 when it is absent.
present_under_home() {
    local above=${HOME} rest=${1#"${HOME}"/} part
    path_present=0
    while :; do
        [[ -d ${above} && -x ${above} ]] || refuse "cannot search ${above}; the dsh profile config below it cannot be read"
        part=${rest%%/*}
        [[ -e ${above}/${part} || -L ${above}/${part} ]] || return 0
        [[ ${rest} != "${part}" ]] || break
        above=${above}/${part} rest=${rest#*/}
    done
    path_present=1
}
# @description Run the profile config helper `profile-config-place.py` (the lever's own copy, helper_copy_make) once
#   over the dsh profile's
#   `agent/` directory `$1` and read its status (regime-cutover U310d): the one writer of the row. Three audit rounds
#   of U310 found one class, symlink-write, in this lever's own write: each round checked a path in `agent/` (a
#   directory the role's own sandboxed process writes too) and then acted on it, and the entry was swapped between
#   the two (round 1 a link planted at the temporary's predictable name, round 2 the temporary swapped after its
#   open, round 3 `config.yml` swapped to a directory link before `mv`). Nothing of that shape remains here: the
#   helper opens `agent/` once (`O_NOFOLLOW`) and runs every step on that descriptor (`dir_fd`): the identity read,
#   the compare, the exclusive create at a random name, the write, the rename and the read-back, and the removal on
#   a refusal; this lever makes no check over a path in `agent/` that a later act depends on. The rendering goes to
#   the helper's stdin; its status decides (standing order 21): 0 and one decision word, 2 a refusal whose line (the
#   step, the path, the errno) becomes this lever's refusal, any other status a helper that could not run, refused
#   naming the status. With `$2` set to `--dry-run` the helper stops after the compare and writes nothing.
# @arg $1 string The `agent/` directory of the role's own profile, its physical path.
# @arg $2 string `--dry-run`, or empty.
# @set profile_config_decision The helper's word: placed, replaced, kept, absent or differs.
profile_config_place() {
    local agent=$1 mode=$2 target=$1/config.yml output status=0
    output=$("${profile_config_cmd[@]}" ${mode:+"${mode}"} "${agent}" "${UID}" <<< "${profile_config_text}" 2>&1) || status=$?
    # The one run is over: the copy's directory goes now, whatever the status says below.
    helper_copy_remove
    case ${status} in
    0)
        case ${output} in
        placed | replaced | kept | absent | differs) profile_config_decision=${output} ;;
        *) refuse "the profile config helper ${profile_config_helper##*/} printed no decision for ${target}: '${output}'" ;;
        esac
        ;;
    2) refuse "the dsh profile config ${target} was not placed: ${output}" ;;
    *) refuse "the profile config helper ${profile_config_helper##*/} exited ${status} for ${target}: ${output:-no output}" ;;
    esac
}
# @description Print what the helper decided about the config `$1`, in the words the earlier rounds printed; a config
#   the check already announced as absent (profile_config_action `place`) gets no second line.
# @arg $1 string The config path.
profile_config_report() {
    case ${profile_config_decision} in
    kept) echo "hcom-seat: the dsh profile config $1 equals ${profile_config}; the launch leaves it" >&2 ;;
    replaced | differs) echo "hcom-seat: the dsh profile config $1 differs from ${profile_config}; the launch replaces it" >&2 ;;
    placed | absent)
        [[ ${profile_config_action} == place ]] ||
            echo "hcom-seat: the dsh profile config $1 went absent after the check; the launch places it from ${profile_config}" >&2
        ;;
    esac
}
# @description Read the placement target: every existence read goes through present_under_home, and an `agent/` or
#   `config.yml` that is a symbolic link or not a plain directory or file refuses, since a write would follow it out
#   of the profile (the profile root itself is judged by settings_judge). A reading that decides the early refusal,
#   before anything is made, and the printed decision only: the write's own judgement of what stands at `agent/` and
#   `config.yml` is the helper's, on its held descriptor (profile_config_place, regime-cutover U310d).
# @arg $1 string The `agent/` directory.
# @arg $2 string The config path inside it.
# @set path_present 1 when the config exists, 0 when it or `agent/` is absent.
profile_config_target_check() {
    present_under_home "$1"
    ((path_present)) || return 0
    [[ ! -L $1 ]] || refuse "$1 is a symbolic link; the dsh role writes its profile config inside its profile only"
    [[ -d $1 ]] || refuse "$1 is not a directory"
    present_under_home "$2"
    ((path_present)) || return 0
    [[ ! -L $2 ]] || refuse "$2 is a symbolic link; the dsh role writes its profile config inside its profile only"
    [[ -f $2 ]] || refuse "$2 is not a regular file"
}
# @description The dsh role's profile config row (regime-cutover U310, round 2 U310b): render what the role's own omp
#   profile must hold and decide what the launch does about it, before anything is made (the private tool directory
#   included) and in a dry run too. The gateway child `omp auth-gateway stdio` the harness starts in that profile
#   resolves a request's model among the providers the profile's own `agent/config.yml` loads (omp 18.12.6
#   src/cli/auth-gateway-stdio.ts:60-64: `Settings.init`, then `loadCliExtensionProviders`), with no `--config`
#   overlay and no `-e` list, so the kit's bridge route reaches it through that file alone (item g6,
#   2026-11-06T19:22Z: without it, `HTTP 404: No available model matches "claude-bridge/claude-opus-5-5"`). The file
#   is the rendered overlay `profile_config` (the generator's, like the seat overlays), each `extensions` entry
#   replaced by its canonical allow-list path (extensions_canonical, the rule the omp roles' `-e` list follows),
#   written as a single-quoted YAML scalar with a `'` doubled, so a path holding ` # `, a quote or a trailing space
#   is read whole by the child (regime-cutover U310e); an overlay naming no extension refuses, as does a failed read
#   (the read is `/bin/cat` with its status read: bash 5.2 runs `$(< file)` without a fork, so its failed redirection
#   ended the launch by errexit on Linux before the handler ran, exit 1 with no refusal; U310e). The target
#   `~/.omp/profiles/<role>/agent/config.yml`

#   entry refused); an absent one is placed. A present one is compared by the helper on its held descriptor: in a
#   dry run after settings_judge has accepted the profile boundary (profile_config_compare, nothing written), in a
#   launch at the write itself (profile_config_write), so the compare and the act are one program on one descriptor
#   (regime-cutover U310d). The decision is printed, in a dry run too.
# @set profile_config_text The config to place, without its final newline.
# @set profile_config_action `place` (the target is absent), or `compare` (present: the helper decides at the write).
profile_config_check() {
    local text line list=0 i=0 agent target q="'"
    local -a listed_exts=()
    [[ -f ${profile_config} && ! -L ${profile_config} ]] ||
        refuse "profile config overlay absent or a symbolic link: ${profile_config}"
    text=$(/bin/cat -- "${profile_config}") || refuse "cannot read the profile config overlay ${profile_config}"
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if ((list)) && [[ ${line} == '  - '* ]]; then
            listed_exts+=("${line#  - }")
        elif [[ ${line} == 'extensions:' ]]; then
            list=1
        else
            list=0
        fi
    done <<< "${text}"
    ((${#listed_exts[@]})) ||
        refuse "the profile config overlay ${profile_config} names no extension; the gateway child needs the bridge route"
    extensions_canonical "${listed_exts[@]}"
    rendered_path_check 'the canonical extension path' "${checked[@]}"
    profile_config_text='' list=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if ((list)) && [[ ${line} == '  - '* ]]; then
            line="  - '${checked[i]//${q}/${q}${q}}'"
            i=$((i + 1))
        elif [[ ${line} == 'extensions:' ]]; then
            list=1
        else
            list=0
        fi
        profile_config_text+=${line}$'\n'
    done <<< "${text}"
    profile_config_text=${profile_config_text%$'\n'}
    agent=${HOME}/.omp/profiles/${omp_profile}/agent
    target=${agent}/config.yml
    profile_config_target_check "${agent}" "${target}"
    if ((! path_present)); then
        profile_config_action=place
        echo "hcom-seat: the dsh profile config ${target} is absent; the launch places it from ${profile_config}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    profile_config_action=compare
}
# @description Refuse (exit 2) a path this lever would render into the profile config when it holds a control
#   character (a newline among them: inside a single-quoted YAML scalar a line break folds into a space, so the child
#   would read another path; regime-cutover U310f, the round-5 verdict's P2 at :1121), begins with `-`, or holds a
#   `#` after white space, each named before anything is rendered. The scalars stay single-quoted with a `'` doubled
#   (U310e); this check refuses the shapes the quoting is not asked to carry. Every path value the lever renders is
#   a canonical extension path (`pwd -P` of an allow-list entry); the other values come from the overlay unchanged.
# @arg $1 string What the paths are, for the refusal.
# @arg $@ string The paths.
rendered_path_check() {
    local what=$1 path
    shift
    for path in "$@"; do
        [[ ${path} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || refuse "${what} holds a control character and is not rendered into the profile config: '${path}'"        # lint-comparisons: allow a content test
        [[ ${path} != -* ]] || refuse "${what} begins with '-' and is not rendered into the profile config: '${path}'"                             # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test
        [[ ${path} != *[[:space:]]'#'* ]] || refuse "${what} holds a '#' after white space and is not rendered into the profile config: '${path}'" # lint-comparisons: allow a content test
    done
}
# @description The dry run's reading of a present profile config (regime-cutover U310d): the helper runs with
#   `--dry-run` after settings_judge has accepted the profile boundary and prints the decision a launch would take,
#   writing nothing (round 2 wrote a temporary file here, so a linked profile root took it into another profile:
#   verdict U310-8f393491 P2; nothing is written here any more). A launch reads nothing here: its one helper run is
#   the write (profile_config_write), after the per-launch slots, so no decision is carried across the launch's own
#   mkdirs.
# @set profile_config_decision The helper's word.
profile_config_compare() {
    local profile agent

    profile_config_hold

        profile_config_report "${agent}/config.yml"

# @description Place the dsh role's profile config (regime-cutover U310, rounds U310b to U310d), after

#   one helper run does the rest on its held descriptor: whether `agent/` is a real directory of this user, whether
#   `config.yml` equals the rendering (nothing written then), the exclusive create, the write, the rename and the
#   read-back. This function tests nothing about `agent/` or `config.yml` by path: a failed mkdir is read by its

    profile_config_report "${agent}/config.yml"

# @description Collect the git state host git reads for the worktrees of this repository into `git_state`, make sure
#   each file exists, and refuse (exit 2) a launch over state a seat may have written. The set: the common `config`,
#   `config.worktree`, `info/` and `hooks/`; for every linked worktree `worktrees/<n>/config.worktree`, `info/`,
#   `commondir` and `gitdir`; and the seat worktree's own `.git` file. None may be a symbolic link. Every

#   `core.sparseCheckoutCone`): anything else (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`, `filter.*`, `diff.*.textconv`,

#   empty, which git reads as no setting.
#   It runs before the first host git command (with the seat directory empty) and again before each git command in
#   the seat directory and when the settings are written.
# @arg $1 string The physical git common directory.
# @arg $2 string The physical seat directory, or empty.
# @set git_state The paths, for the seat's write denies.
# The repair a refusal over a worktree's git files names (regime-cutover U95).
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # literal backquotes in a message
git_fix_hint='; repair or drop the worktree first (`git worktree move`, `git worktree remove` or `git worktree prune`)'
git_state_check() {

    # files"): `worktrees` is a real directory; each admin directory is a real directory holding `commondir`, or git
    # would take the admin directory for its own common directory (setup.c get_common_dir_noenv) and read its
    # `config` and `hooks`, which a seat can write; and it holds none of the names path.c's common_list sends to the
    # common directory (git never writes them into an admin directory; `refs`, `logs` and `info` it does).
    [[ ! -L ${common_real}/worktrees ]] ||
        refuse "the worktree git directories ${common_real}/worktrees are a symbolic link, which host git would follow${git_fix_hint}"
    # One enumeration, dot names included, as git's own readdir_skip_dot_and_dotdot (worktree.c:203): every entry

    admin_dirs=(${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"})

        [[ -d ${wt} && ! -L ${wt} ]] ||
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${wt} is not a real directory (a symbolic link, file or other entry), which host git would follow or no worktree owns${git_fix_hint}"
        [[ -e ${wt}/commondir || -L ${wt}/commondir ]] ||
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${wt} has no commondir, so git would take it for its own common directory and read its config and hooks${git_fix_hint}"
        for f in branches common hooks lost-found objects remotes worktrees rr-cache svn config gc.pid packed-refs shallow; do
            [[ ! -e ${wt}/${f} && ! -L ${wt}/${f} ]] ||
                refuse "the worktree git directory ${wt} holds ${f}, which git keeps in the common directory and never writes there${git_fix_hint}"
        done

    # a read or a write, and a device or socket is no file git means. Each entry is absent, or a real directory
    # (`info`, `hooks`), or a regular file, never a symbolic link.

        [[ -e ${f} ]] || continue

        info | hooks) [[ -d ${f} ]] || refuse "the git state ${f} is not a directory${git_fix_hint}" ;;
        *) [[ -f ${f} ]] || refuse "the git state ${f} is not a regular file (a FIFO, device, socket or directory)${git_fix_hint}" ;;
        esac

        /*) target=${line} ;;

    # A dry run validates and creates nothing: an absent file holds no setting, and the real launch creates it. The
    # absent `info/` and `hooks/` directories are made in one `mkdir` (U95), without -p: each parent is a real
    # directory checked above, so an entry that appeared since the check fails the run, which refuses. Each is then
    # checked to be a real directory, no link. An empty `config.worktree` is made by a builtin.
    if ((! dry_run)); then
        for f in "${git_state[@]}"; do
            case ${f##*/} in
            info | hooks) [[ -d ${f} ]] || missing+=("${f}") ;;
            config.worktree) [[ -f ${f} ]] || : >> "${f}" || refuse "cannot create ${f}" ;;
            esac
        done
        if ((${#missing[@]})); then
            /bin/mkdir -- "${missing[@]}" || refuse "cannot create the git state directories (${missing[*]})"
            for f in "${missing[@]}"; do
                [[ -d ${f} && ! -L ${f} ]] || refuse "the git state ${f} is not a real directory after it was created"
            done
        fi
    fi
    for f in "${git_state[@]}"; do
        if [[ ${f##*/} == config.worktree && -e ${f} ]]; then configs+=("${f}"); fi
    done
    # An empty config.worktree (what a launch creates) holds no key, so git reads only the others (U95): one size read.
    # The rest cost one git each: git config validates one --file per run, and joining files would let one file's
    # section run into the next. A sparse checkout's file is the only non-empty one git writes (none on this host).
    sizes_of ${configs[@]+"${configs[@]}"}
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#configs[@]}; i++)); do
        ((size_list[i] > 0)) || continue
        f=${configs[i]}
        # From /, so no repository around the cwd is discovered or read; git() adds the overrides.
        names=$(cd / && git config --file "${f}" --no-includes --name-only --list) ||
            refuse "cannot read the git config ${f}"
        while IFS= read -r name; do
            case ${name} in
            '' | core.sparsecheckout | core.sparsecheckoutcone) ;;
            *) refuse "the git config ${f} sets ${name}, which host git would act on; a seat may have written it" ;;
            esac
        done <<< "${names}"
    done
    # The seat worktree's `.git` file is git's to read (relative forms, `--relative-paths`, included): once the
    # state it reads has passed, git names the git directory and common directory it resolves there.
    if [[ -n ${dir_real} && -f ${dir_real}/.git ]]; then
        git_paths_of 2 -C "${dir_real}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
        [[ ${git_paths[0]%/*} -ef ${common_real}/worktrees && ${git_paths[1]} -ef ${common_real} ]] ||
            refuse "${dir_real}/.git leads to ${git_paths[0]}, outside ${common_real}/worktrees"
    fi
}

# @description Run host git (git, the checked argv) with `$2...` and read its whole answer into `git_paths`
#   (regime-cutover U85): exactly `$1` newline-terminated lines, each an absolute path free of control characters. A
#   failing git, an unterminated line, another count (a path holding a newline splits into more), a relative path or
#   a control character refuses (exit 2).
# @arg $1 int The number of paths.
# @arg $@ string git's arguments after it.
# @set git_paths The paths.
git_paths_of() {
    local count=$1 out line
    shift
    out=$(git "$@" && printf .) || refuse "git $* failed"
    out=${out%.}
    git_paths=()
    while [[ -n ${out} ]]; do
        [[ ${out} == *$'\n'* ]] || refuse "git $* printed an unterminated line"
        line=${out%%$'\n'*}
        out=${out#*$'\n'}
        [[ ${line} == /* && ${line} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
            refuse "git $* printed '${line}', not an absolute path free of control characters"
        git_paths+=("${line}")
    done
    ((${#git_paths[@]} == count)) || refuse "git $* printed ${#git_paths[@]} paths, not ${count}"
}

# @description Run git with nothing a repository's config or hooks name: no hooks (`core.hooksPath=/dev/null`), no
#   fsmonitor program, no per-worktree config, no transport, and no system config (regime-cutover U85). Every host git
#   command of hcom-seat and the sourced regime-env goes through this function, before and after the git state is
#   checked.
# @arg $@ string git's arguments.
git() {
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 "${git_cmd[@]}" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false \
        -c extensions.worktreeConfig=false -c protocol.allow=never "$@"
}

if [[ -n ${top} || -e /.git ]]; then

    [[ -d ${early_common} ]] || refuse "the git common directory ${early_common} is not a directory"
    # The checkout and its git directories reach the srt settings: clean before anything (metadata included) is made.
    for root in "${top}" "${gitdir}" "${early_common}"; do
        root=$(physical_path "${root}") || refuse "cannot resolve ${root}"
        require_clean_path 'the checkout or its git directory' "${root}"
    done
    git_state_check "${early_common}" ''
fi

# @description Hold the program store's root (regime-cutover U219, U219c): regime-env derived `REGIME_STORE_ROOT`
#   (U215c: from the physical HOME and the slug, never from the environment; empty only outside a checkout, which the
#   toplevel check below refuses for every role) and held its components to plain directories of this user or absent,
#   a link or a file refused by name. Here each component (`regime-store`, `<slug>`), when present, is held to mode
#   0700 as well (store_root_mode_check, regime-init's rule: a pre-made 0755 root is a refusal, never kept), the root
#   is resolved physically once into `store_root_phys` (the clean-path rule holds both forms), and an absent root is
#   noted (`store_root_absent`) for store_root_make. Nothing resolves the root again: seat_write_roots prints the held
#   value verbatim as the orchestrator's row 7, seat_settings_render renders it into the read grants and the deny rows,
#   and store_root_judge and store_root_overlap_check judge against it.
# @set store_root_phys The physical store root; empty when regime-env derived none.
# @set store_root_absent 1 when the root does not exist yet (store_root_make makes it).
store_root_hold() {
    local path
    store_root_absent=0
    require_clean_path REGIME_STORE_ROOT "${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}"

            [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] || refuse "the store root component ${path} is not a real directory of this user"
            store_root_mode_check "${path}"
        else
            store_root_absent=1
        fi
    done
    store_root_phys=$(physical_path "${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}") || refuse "cannot resolve the store root ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}"
    require_clean_path 'the store root' "${store_root_phys}"
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless the store root component `$1` has mode 0700, read by `/usr/bin/stat` (mode_args)
#   with its status (standing order 21): regime-init makes each component 0700 and refuses any other mode, and so does
#   every launch, so a component another process widened is never granted or denied as if it were the root's.
# @arg $1 string A store root component.
store_root_mode_check() {
    local mode
    mode=$(/usr/bin/stat "${mode_args[@]}" -- "$1") || refuse "cannot read the mode of the store root component $1"
    [[ ${mode} == 700 ]] || refuse "the store root component $1 has mode ${mode}, not 0700 (regime-init makes it 0700; chmod 700 it, or move it aside)"
}

# @description Make the held store root (store_root_hold) when it was absent, `regime-store` then `<slug>`, each by its
#   own `mkdir` under `umask 077` (no `-p`, so none is made through an entry planted above it), for every role, in a
#   real launch alone and after the judgement (the shape of cred_root_make, regime-cutover U353d: the foreground rows
#   after settings_judge, the omp roles beside their credential root, before their settings are rendered): srt
#   0.0.81's Linux backend skips an absent write path (dist/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.js:1990-1992) and binds nothing
#   for an absent deny (:2413-2416), so a root nothing had made left the orchestrator's first regime-init unable to
#   write it and the worker's deny of it void (verdict U219-985b7c04 P2 `:1815`). A dry run makes nothing and says what
#   a launch would make. Two launches at once may both find a component absent: the loser of the mkdir race takes the
#   directory the winner made, while a link planted since the hold fails mkdir and the check alike. Present or made,
#   each component is a real directory of this user with mode 0700, else refused by name. The program store under the
#   root is regime-init's to make.
# @arg $1 int 1 for a dry run.
store_root_make() {
    local path
    [[ -n ${store_root_phys} ]] || return 0
    if ((store_root_absent)); then
        if (($1)); then
            echo "hcom-seat: the program store's root ${store_root_phys} does not exist; a launch creates it (0700)" >&2
            return 0
        fi
        for path in "${store_root_phys%/*}" "${store_root_phys}"; do
            if [[ ! -e ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]]; then
                (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${path}") || [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
                    refuse "cannot create the store root component ${path}"
            fi
        done
    fi
    for path in "${store_root_phys%/*}" "${store_root_phys}"; do
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] || refuse "the store root component ${path} is not a real directory of this user"
        store_root_mode_check "${path}"
    done
}

# @set rules The standing rules file.

omp_inputs_check() {

if [[ ${role_launch} == hcom ]]; then omp_inputs_check; fi

[[ -n ${top} ]] || refuse 'run hcom-seat inside the repository checkout'
git_paths_of 3 rev-parse --path-format=absolute --show-toplevel --git-dir --git-common-dir
repo=${git_paths[0]}
launch_gitdir=${git_paths[1]}
common=${git_paths[2]}

claude_config=${seats_root%/}/.state/claude-${login_group}

case ${role} in

# @description Fill the identity table for the physical paths `$@` (regime-cutover U95), which every containment
#   decision of the overlap check reads: per path, whether it exists, the (device, inode) identities of its deepest
#   existing ancestor (the path itself when it exists) and of every directory above it, and the absent remainder below
#   that ancestor, ASCII case-folded by ascii_lower (builtins only). One `/usr/bin/stat` (through xargs, order kept)
#   serves every path, instead of several processes per pair. Fail-closed per record: every input must be a clean path; every identity line must be `<dev>:<ino>`, and
#   their number exactly what the ancestor walks asked for; every folded remainder must have its input's length and
#   the grammar `(/<lower-case component>)*/`; each table must hold one entry per input.
# @set tbl_exists 1 or 0 per path.
# @set tbl_first The identity of the deepest existing ancestor per path.
# @set tbl_chain `\n<id>\n<id>…\n` per path: that ancestor's identity first, then each directory above it.
# @set tbl_rest The absent remainder per path, case-folded, ending in `/` (`/` when the path exists).
identity_table() {
    local p d rest ids line folded chain='' i=0 k=0 all=() counts=()
    tbl_exists=() tbl_first=() tbl_chain=() tbl_rest=()
    for p in "$@"; do
        require_clean_path 'a seat path' "${p}"
        # Absolute, so each step shortens it and the walk ends at `/`, which exists.
        d=${p} rest=''
        while [[ ! -e ${d} && ! -L ${d} ]]; do
            rest=/${d##*/}${rest}
            d=${d%/*}
            [[ -n ${d} ]] || d=/
        done
        if [[ -e ${p} ]]; then tbl_exists+=(1); else tbl_exists+=(0); fi
        ancestors_of "${d}"
        all+=("${ancestors[@]}")
        counts+=("${#ancestors[@]}")
        rest=${rest}/
        ascii_lower "${rest}" folded || refuse "cannot fold the absent part of ${p}"
        [[ ${#folded} == "${#rest}" && ${folded} =~ ^(/[a-z0-9._@+-]+)*/$ ]] ||
            refuse "cannot fold the absent part of ${p} ('${folded}')"
        tbl_rest+=("${folded}")
    done
    (($#)) || return 0
    ids=$(printf '%s\0' "${all[@]}" | /usr/bin/xargs -0 /usr/bin/stat "${stat_args[@]}" --) ||
        refuse "cannot read the identity of a seat path or a directory above it"
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ ${line} =~ ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ ]] || refuse "cannot read the identity of a seat path ('${line}')"
        ((i < ${#counts[@]})) || refuse 'more identities than seat paths were read'
        if ((k == 0)); then tbl_first+=("${line}"); fi
        chain+=${line}$'\n'
        k=$((k + 1))
        if ((k == counts[i])); then
            tbl_chain+=($'\n'"${chain}")
            chain='' k=0 i=$((i + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "${ids}"
    ((i == $# && k == 0)) || refuse "cannot read the identity of every seat path (${i} of $#)"
    ((${#tbl_exists[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_first[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_chain[@]} == $# && ${#tbl_rest[@]} == $#)) ||
        refuse 'the identity table does not hold one entry per seat path'
}

# @description Set the variable named `$2` to `$1` with A-Z made a-z (regime-cutover U95), by builtins only (a case
#   table, no `tr` and no locale; bash 3.2 has no `${x,,}`), so no producer's output is read back.
# @arg $1 string ASCII text.
# @arg $2 string The name of the variable to set.
# @exitcode 1 The variable cannot be set.
ascii_lower() {
    # The locals carry a prefix, so the caller's variable `$2` is never one of them (printf -v sets the nearest).
    local LC_ALL=C al_text=$1 al_out='' al_c al_before al_upper=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
    local al_lower=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
    [[ $2 != al_* && $2 != LC_ALL ]] || return 1
    while [[ -n ${al_text} ]]; do
        al_c=${al_text:0:1}
        al_text=${al_text:1}
        case ${al_c} in
        [ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ])
            al_before=${al_upper%%"${al_c}"*}
            al_c=${al_lower:${#al_before}:1}
            ;;
        esac
        al_out+=${al_c}
    done
    printf -v "$2" '%s' "${al_out}"
}

# @description Decide from the identity table whether path `$2` is path `$1` or lies under it (regime-cutover U85,
#   U95), by identity for everything that exists, so a case alias on a case-insensitive volume is the path it aliases.
#   When `$1` exists: yes iff `$1`'s identity is in `$2`'s chain (`$2`'s deepest existing ancestor or a directory
