#   above it). When `$1` does not exist, an existing `$2` cannot lie under it (no). When neither exists, `$2` can lie
#   under `$1` only if both have the same deepest existing ancestor; below it nothing exists, so no link or alias can
#   intervene, and the absent remainders decide: yes iff `$1`'s is `$2`'s or a prefix of it on a component boundary
#   (`a/b` is no prefix of `a/bc`), compared ASCII case-folded, since on a case-insensitive volume two spellings that
#   differ by case become one directory once made. No process runs.
# @arg $1 int The table index of the outer path.
# @arg $2 int The table index of the inner path.
# @exitcode 0 `$2` is `$1` or lies under it.
# @exitcode 1 It does not.
within_ix() {
    if ((tbl_exists[$1])); then
        [[ ${tbl_chain[$2]} == *$'\n'"${tbl_first[$1]}"$'\n'* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
        return
    fi
    ((! tbl_exists[$2])) || return 1
    [[ ${tbl_first[$1]} == "${tbl_first[$2]}" ]] || return 1 # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
    [[ ${tbl_rest[$2]} == "${tbl_rest[$1]}"* ]]              # lint-comparisons: allow absent components below one ancestor of the same identity, compared on component boundaries
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) when the hcom store `HCOM_DIR` is, lies inside or contains the program store's root
#   (regime-cutover U219; verdict U215-15c6be1e P1 `:127`, held residual on this unit): the hcom store is a write root
#   of every seat (seat_write_roots) and no rendered deny covers a directory under it, so a root at or under it would
#   put the records inside a worker's write grant, and a store under the root would put the bus inside the records.
#   Both paths in their physical form (store_root_hold, physical_path), the decision by identity for what exists and
#   by the absent components below one shared ancestor otherwise (identity_table, within_ix), before the seats root, a
#   slot or a settings file is made, in a dry run too. The refusal names both paths and which contains which. Nothing
#   to judge without a root (outside a checkout, with an explicit HCOM_DIR, where no slug exists).
store_root_overlap_check() {
    local hcom_phys spelled why
    [[ -n ${store_root_phys} ]] || return 0
    hcom_phys=$(physical_path "${HCOM_DIR}") || refuse "cannot resolve the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR}"
    spelled=${HCOM_DIR}
    [[ ${hcom_phys} == "${HCOM_DIR}" ]] || spelled="${HCOM_DIR} (${hcom_phys})" # lint-comparisons: allow one path's spelled and physical forms, for the message alone; the decision is by identity below
    identity_table "${store_root_phys}" "${hcom_phys}"
    if within_ix 0 1 && within_ix 1 0; then
        why=is
    elif within_ix 0 1; then
        why='lies inside'
    elif within_ix 1 0; then
        why=contains
    else
        return 0
    fi
    refuse "the hcom store HCOM_DIR ${spelled} ${why} the store root REGIME_STORE_ROOT ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}; the hcom store is every seat's write grant, so the records would lie inside it (set HCOM_DIR to a directory outside the store root)"
}
store_root_overlap_check

# @description Set `phys_list` to the physical form of each absolute path `$@`, in order (regime-cutover U95), or
#   refuse (exit 2), in one subshell for all of them, present or absent. In that subshell a path's deepest existing entry is found with builtins (physical_path's
#   walk); it must be a directory, which `cd -P` resolves, and the absent rest is appended, as physical_path does.
#   The inputs are worktree records (git's list and the admin directories' `gitdir`) and seat directories: a path
#   that is, or lies below, a regular file or a dangling link is no directory-backed worktree but a corrupt record,
#   and refuses, naming `git worktree prune` and `git worktree repair` (no per-record fallback). Fail-closed per record: the subshell writes exactly one record per path,
#   `ok<TAB><physical path>` after a `cd -P` whose status was 0, `notdir` for a path not backed by a directory, or
#   `fail` after a failed `cd`, and fails when a record cannot be written. Each record is checked against its
#   grammar and its result assigned to its own index (nothing is printed and read back): only `ok` with a clean
#   path passes. Anything else, a record too many or too few, or an index left without its result refuses.
# @arg $@ string Absolute paths free of control characters.
# @set phys_list The physical paths, one per input.
physical_paths() {
    local out line resolved i=0 args=("$@")
    phys_list=()
    (($#)) || return 0
    out=$(for p in "$@"; do
        rest=''
        while [[ ! -e ${p} && ! -L ${p} ]]; do
            rest=/${p##*/}${rest}
            p=${p%/*}
            [[ -n ${p} ]] || p=/
        done
        if [[ ! -d ${p} ]]; then
            printf 'notdir\n' || exit 1
        elif [[ ${p} == / ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the root itself, whose `cd //` form pwd prints as `//`
            printf 'ok\t%s\n' "${rest:-/}" || exit 1
        elif cd -P -- "${p}/" 2> /dev/null; then
            printf 'ok\t%s%s\n' "${PWD%/}" "${rest}" || exit 1
        else
            printf 'fail\n' || exit 1
        fi
    done) || refuse 'cannot resolve the paths (the resolving subshell failed)'
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        ((i < $#)) || refuse 'cannot resolve the paths (more records than paths)'
        case ${line} in
        notdir) refuse "the worktree record ${args[i]} is not backed by a directory: it, or its deepest existing ancestor, is a regular file or a dangling symbolic link, so the record is corrupt; run \`git worktree prune\` if the worktree is gone, or \`git worktree repair\` if it moved" ;;
        ok$'\t'*) resolved=${line#ok$'\t'} ;;
        *) refuse "cannot resolve the path ${args[i]} ('${line}')" ;;
        esac
        clean_path "${resolved}" || refuse "the path ${args[i]} resolves to '${resolved}', not a clean absolute path"
        phys_list[i]=${resolved}
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "${out}"
    ((i == $# && ${#phys_list[@]} == $#)) || refuse "cannot resolve every path (${#phys_list[@]} of $#)"
}

# @description Set `phys_list` to the physical form of each absolute path `$@` (physical_path: every link followed,
#   a file or an absent tail kept by name), in order, in one subshell for all of them (regime-cutover U272e). The
#   inputs are rendered settings rows (settings_judge), directories and files alike, so physical_paths' directory rule does not
#   apply. Fail-closed per record: one line per path, the physical path or `fail`; anything else, a record too many
#   or too few, or a result that is not a clean path refuses (exit 2).
# @arg $@ string Absolute paths.
# @set phys_list The physical paths, one per input.
physical_each() {
    local out line i=0 args=("$@")
    phys_list=()
    (($#)) || return 0
    out=$(for p in "$@"; do
        physical_path "${p}" || printf 'fail\n' || exit 1
    done) || refuse 'cannot resolve the settings paths (the resolving subshell failed)'
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        ((i < $#)) || refuse 'cannot resolve the settings paths (more records than paths)'
        [[ ${line} != fail ]] || refuse "cannot resolve the settings path ${args[i]}"
        clean_path "${line}" || refuse "the settings path ${args[i]} resolves to '${line}', not a clean absolute path"
        phys_list[i]=${line}
        i=$((i + 1))
    done <<< "${out}"
    ((i == $# && ${#phys_list[@]} == $#)) || refuse "cannot resolve every settings path (${#phys_list[@]} of $#)"
}

# @description Set `worktree_paths` to the worktrees git records for this repository, main worktree first, and
#   `main_bare` to 1 when that record is a bare repository (regime-cutover U85). `git worktree list --porcelain -z`
#   is read whole: NUL-terminated fields, each turned into one line (a newline inside a field becomes \001, a control
#   character, refused in a path); every path must be absolute and free of control characters.
# @set worktree_paths The worktree paths, as git prints them.
# @set main_bare 1 for a bare main record, else 0.
worktree_records() {
    local listing line record=0
    listing=$({ git -C "${repo}" worktree list --porcelain -z | /usr/bin/tr '\0\n' '\n\001'; } && printf .) ||
        refuse "git cannot list the worktrees of ${repo}"
    listing=${listing%.}
    worktree_paths=()
    main_bare=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case ${line} in
        '') record=$((record + 1)) ;;
        'worktree '*)
            line=${line#worktree }
            [[ ${line} == /* && ${line} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path and content test
                refuse "git names the worktree '${line}', not an absolute path free of control characters"
            worktree_paths+=("${line}")
            ;;
        bare) if ((record == 0)); then main_bare=1; fi ;;
        esac
    done <<< "${listing}"
    ((${#worktree_paths[@]} > 0)) || refuse "git lists no worktree of ${repo}"
}

# The main checkout, by identity, never by the common directory's spelling (a `.GIT` on a case-insensitive volume is
# `.git`): the common directory's parent when that parent's `.git` is the common directory; else the main worktree
# git records. A bare repository has none, and the launch checkout stands in. For a separate git directory git
# records the git directory itself as the main worktree, so its checkout is known only when the launch runs in it
# (its git directory is the common directory); from another worktree of it the launch is refused.
worktree_records
common_parent=$(physical_path "${common}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common}"
common_parent=${common_parent%/*}
common_parent=${common_parent:-/}
if [[ -d ${common_parent}/.git && ! -L ${common_parent}/.git && ${common_parent}/.git -ef ${common} ]]; then
    checkout=${common_parent}
elif ((main_bare)); then
    checkout=$(physical_path "${repo}") || refuse "cannot resolve the checkout ${repo}"
elif [[ ${worktree_paths[0]} -ef ${common} ]]; then
    [[ ${launch_gitdir} -ef ${common} ]] ||
        refuse "git records no main checkout for the separate git directory ${common}; launch from that checkout"
    checkout=$(physical_path "${repo}") || refuse "cannot resolve the checkout ${repo}"
else
    checkout=$(physical_path "${worktree_paths[0]}") || refuse "cannot resolve the main checkout ${worktree_paths[0]}"
fi

# OS containment (regime-cutover U85): the seat's omp runs under Anthropic's sandbox-runtime (`srt`, sandbox-exec on
# macOS, bubblewrap on Linux). hcom pins the `omp` it finds first on this process's PATH as the runner's
# --hcom-tool-path, so a per-seat shim placed first on PATH is what the pane runs; the shim never falls back to an
# uncontained omp. Every prerequisite is checked here, before anything is created or started.
sandbox=${seats_root%/}/.sandbox/${name}
# Every seat's sandbox denies reads of <seats-root>/.sandbox (refuse_inside_a_seat).
refuse_inside_a_seat "${seats_root%/}/.sandbox"
# The dsh role's slots are per launch and never reused (U272): a sandbox or state slot of this name is a refusal.
if [[ ${role_launch} == foreground ]]; then
    for path in "${sandbox}" "${seats_root%/}/.state/${name}"; do
        [[ ! -e ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "the per-launch slot ${path} exists; a dsh launch never reuses one"
    done
fi

# @description Print the srt write roots of one seat, one per line in physical form: the list the seat's settings
#   carry as `allowWrite` (seat_sandbox_write writes exactly this list), followed by the paths srt 0.0.81 makes
#   writable without a listing (`srt_tmp_roots`: `/tmp/claude`, and `/private/tmp/claude` on macOS; `~/.npm/_logs`).
#   The role table's write-root row (U272): the omp roles write the repository's git common directory, the program's
#   hcom store and their own omp profile, and the orchestrator the program store's root as well (regime-cutover U219,
#   U219c: the held physical `store_root_phys`, printed verbatim as row 7, the held slot after `~/.omp/run`, never
#   resolved here; where the records live once U221 has moved them); the
#   dsh role writes DSH_HOME and its own omp profile, where its login child
#   lives, and no git or hcom path. Row 2 of every role is its login group's Claude Code directory
#   `<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>` (the `claude_config` row, regime-cutover U318, U498), which the shim exports
#   as the seat's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: the child's login, `.claude.json`, state and sessions live there, and
#   seat_settings_render denies its settings, rules, hooks, plugins, skills, commands and agents under this grant (srt
#   keeps a deeper deny under an allow). The operator's Claude Code state (a caller's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `~/.claude`,
#   `~/.claude.json`) is no root of any seat (regime-cutover U190). Being no root is not enough: srt 0.0.81 grants
#   `~/.claude/debug` of the real HOME on its own, so seat_sandbox_write denies that state explicitly
#   (operator_claude_paths, regime-cutover U190b).
# @arg $1 string The role.
# @arg $2 string The seat name.
# @arg $3 string The seat directory (the worktree, the checkout for the orchestrator, the scratch cwd for dsh).
# @stdout The roots.
# @exitcode 1 A path could not be resolved.
seat_write_roots() {
    local path extra=() held='' home=''
    case $1 in
    dsh | router)
        # Row 3 is the held physical DSH_HOME (dsh_home_hold, regime-cutover U321d), printed verbatim below, never
        # resolved here; rows 4 and 5 are the omp profile and `~/.omp/run`, resolved as every row is.
        home=${dsh_home_phys}
        extra=("${HOME}/.omp/profiles/${omp_profile}" "${HOME}/.omp/run")
        # The row's state root (regime-cutover U321): `<DSH_HOME>/router-state` for the router row, where U317b renders
        # the Router's `stateDir`, after the dsh row's roots, so every tagged position (rows 0 to 2 and 4) stays the
        # dsh role's. It is the value state_root_hold holds (U321c): printed verbatim below, never resolved here.
        held=${state_root_phys}
        ;;
    orchestrator)
        extra=("${common}" "${HCOM_DIR}" "${HOME}/.omp/profiles/$1" "${HOME}/.omp/run")
        # The program store's root (regime-cutover U219, U219c): the value store_root_hold holds, printed verbatim
        # below as row 7, the held slot after `~/.omp/run` that the router row's state root takes, never resolved
        # here (verdict U219-985b7c04 P1 `:2161`: round 2 put it in `extra`, so a directory-to-link swap of the root
        # during this render granted the link's target). seat_settings_render tags that position `store`.
        held=${store_root_phys}
        ;;
    *) extra=("${common}" "${HCOM_DIR}" "${HOME}/.omp/profiles/$1" "${HOME}/.omp/run") ;;
    esac
    # The seat's own slots come first, then its login group's Claude Code directory (seat_overlap_check and the dsh
    # judge's tags rely on the positions): its directory, its state directory, the group's directory.
    for path in "$3" "${seats_root%/}/.state/$2" "${claude_config}"; do
        physical_path "${path}" || return 1
    done
    if [[ -n ${home} ]]; then printf '%s\n' "${home}"; fi
    for path in "${extra[@]}"; do
        physical_path "${path}" || return 1
    done
    if [[ -n ${held} ]]; then printf '%s\n' "${held}"; fi
    for path in "${srt_tmp_roots[@]}" "${HOME}/.npm/_logs"; do
        physical_path "${path}" || return 1
    done
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless a seat's own slots under the seats root are what the overlap check's exemption
#   takes them for (regime-cutover U85): `<seats-root>/.state`, `<seats-root>/.state/<name>` and, for a worker,
#   `<seats-root>/<name>`, and every login group's Claude Code directory `<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>` (U318;
#   U498: the own group's, which the settings grant; U498d: every group of the table's range `LOGIN_GROUPS`, which
#   the settings deny by name and login_dirs_make makes before the settings file is written), are each no symbolic
#   link, a directory when they exist, and, when they exist, their physical parent has the identity of the physical
#   seats root (resp. `.state`) and their physical basename is the name they are spelled with. A `.state/<name> -> ..`
#   or `<name> -> /` would otherwise resolve the slot to a wider root that the exemption skips, and a
#   `.state/claude-worker -> <elsewhere>` would make the deny or the grant name a directory outside the seats root.
#   It runs before anything resolves those paths (lstat first, then physical_path), so a slot that is a link is
#   refused before any link is followed. Missing slots are created later, one component at a time
#   (seat_sandbox_write, login_dirs_make).
# @arg $1 string The role.
# @arg $2 string The seat name.
own_slots_check() {
    local slot parent real seats_phys group what own i slots=("${seats_root}/.state" "${seats_root}/.state/$2")
    [[ $1 == orchestrator ]] || slots+=("${seats_root}/$2")
    own=${#slots[@]}
    for group in "${LOGIN_GROUPS[@]}"; do slots+=("${seats_root}/.state/claude-${group}"); done
    seats_phys=$(physical_path "${seats_root}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${seats_root}"
    for i in "${!slots[@]}"; do
        slot=${slots[i]}
        if ((i < own)); then what='the seat slot'; else what='the login group directory'; fi
        [[ ! -L ${slot} ]] || refuse "${what} ${slot} is a symbolic link; a seat's own slots and the login group directories must be real directories"
        [[ -e ${slot} ]] || continue
        [[ -d ${slot} ]] || refuse "${what} ${slot} is not a directory"
        real=$(physical_path "${slot}") || refuse "cannot resolve ${what} ${slot}"
        parent=${slot%/*}
        [[ ${real%/*} -ef ${parent} && ${parent} -ef ${seats_phys}${parent#"${seats_root}"} ]] ||
            refuse "${what} ${slot} does not sit in ${parent}"
        [[ ${real##*/} == "${slot##*/}" ]] || refuse "${what} ${slot} resolves to ${real}" # lint-comparisons: allow a basename test, the parent by identity
    done
}
own_slots_check "${role}" "${name}"
own_slots_check orchestrator orchestrator
# The group's directory in physical form, for the shim's export, the dsh role's environment and the deny rows under it
# (own_slots_check has just proved it is no link and sits in `.state`); seat_write_roots renders the same path.
claude_config_real=$(physical_path "${claude_config}") || refuse "cannot resolve the login group's Claude Code directory ${claude_config}"
# The physical seats root goes to the preflight, so the login it judges and the directory the shim exports are one
# spelling (the macOS Keychain item is keyed to the directory's path).
seats_root_real=$(physical_path "${seats_root}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${seats_root}"

# The exact roots (regime-cutover U85): this seat's `allowWrite` list, from the same function that writes the
# settings, so the check and the sandbox cannot drift, and the other role's; the derived seats root and hcom store;
# and every settings file under the derived seats root. Their identities join the set computed before any tool ran
# (which already covers them by their parents); every link, mise included, is then checked again.
seat_write=()
seat_roots_out=$(seat_write_roots "${role}" "${name}" "${dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the write roots of ${name}"
while IFS= read -r root; do seat_write+=("${root}"); done <<< "${seat_roots_out}"
other_roots=$(seat_write_roots orchestrator orchestrator "${repo}") || refuse 'cannot resolve the orchestrator write roots'

# Every linked worktree git records, resolved once for both overlap checks (the first record is the main worktree).
worktree_phys=()
if ((${#worktree_paths[@]} > 1)); then
    physical_paths "${worktree_paths[@]:1}"
    worktree_phys=("${phys_list[@]}")
fi

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless the admin directories in `<common>/worktrees` (dir_entries, dot names included)
#   are, one to one, the git directories of the linked worktrees git lists (regime-cutover U95): each admin directory's
#   `gitdir` names, the way git reads it (worktree.c get_linked_worktree: trailing `/.git` stripped, a relative path
#   resolved against the admin directory), a worktree git lists, no two name the same one, and their number is the
#   number git lists. So every consumer (the git-state denies, the shape check, the overlap check) sees the same set:
#   an admin directory no listed worktree owns, or one the scan missed, refuses. Sameness is identity, never text:
#   `cd -P` keeps a spelling's case, so on a case-insensitive volume `trees/a` and `TREES/A` are one directory under
#   two texts. Each path's key is its identity_table entry, the (device, inode) of its deepest existing ancestor
#   followed by the case-folded absent rest (`/` for an existing path), the same rule within_ix decides by. One read,
#   one resolving batch and one identity table.
# @arg $1 string The physical git common directory.
admin_dirs_match() {
    local a v key listed=$'\n' seen=$'\n' i n derived=() gitdirs=()
    dir_entries "$1/worktrees"
    ((${#dir_list[@]} == ${#admin_dirs[@]})) ||
        refuse "the worktree git directories of $1 changed while hcom-seat ran (${#dir_list[@]} now, ${#admin_dirs[@]} checked)"
    ((${#admin_dirs[@]} == ${#worktree_phys[@]})) ||
        refuse "$1/worktrees holds ${#admin_dirs[@]} worktree git directories but git lists ${#worktree_phys[@]} linked worktrees; an entry no listed worktree owns cannot be checked${git_fix_hint}"
    n=${#worktree_phys[@]}
    ((n)) || return 0
    for a in "${admin_dirs[@]}"; do
        [[ -f ${a}/gitdir && ! -L ${a}/gitdir ]] ||
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${a} has no regular gitdir file, so git lists no worktree for it${git_fix_hint}"
        gitdirs+=("${a}/gitdir")
    done
    pointer_values "${gitdirs[@]}"
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        git_form_path "${pointer_list[i]}" ||
            refuse "${gitdirs[i]} holds '${pointer_list[i]}', not a path in git's own form (no trailing /, no . component, .. only leading a relative path)${git_fix_hint}"
        v=${pointer_list[i]%/.git}
        case ${v} in # lint-comparisons: allow a relative operand is made absolute, no path compare
        /*) derived+=("${v}") ;;
        *) derived+=("${admin_dirs[i]}/${v}") ;;
        esac
    done
    physical_paths "${derived[@]}"
    ((${#phys_list[@]} == n)) || refuse "the worktrees the git directories of $1 record were not all resolved"
    # Listed worktrees at indices 0..n-1, recorded ones at n..2n-1.
    identity_table "${worktree_phys[@]}" "${phys_list[@]}"
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do listed+=${tbl_first[i]}${tbl_rest[i]}$'\n'; done
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        v=${phys_list[i]}
        key=${tbl_first[n + i]}${tbl_rest[n + i]}
        [[ ${listed} == *$'\n'"${key}"$'\n'* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities with case-folded absent rests, not paths
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${admin_dirs[i]} records ${v}, which git does not list as a worktree${git_fix_hint}"
        [[ ${seen} != *$'\n'"${key}"$'\n'* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities with case-folded absent rests, not paths
            refuse "the worktree git directory ${admin_dirs[i]} records ${v}, which another worktree git directory records too (the same directory by identity)${git_fix_hint}"
        seen+=${key}$'\n'
    done
}
if ((${#worktree_paths[@]} > 1 || ${#admin_dirs[@]} > 0)); then admin_dirs_match "${early_common}"; fi

# @description Set `operator_claude` to the operator's Claude Code state in physical form, and `operator_claude_labels`
#   to one label per entry (regime-cutover U190b): `<HOME>/.claude`, `<HOME>/.claude.json` and, when the caller set it
#   and it is another directory, the physical `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. The overlap check protects these paths (no root may
#   be, contain or lie under one) and seat_sandbox_write denies them for write and for read, from this one list.
# @set operator_claude The paths.
# @set operator_claude_labels Their labels.
operator_claude_paths() {
    local h config
    h=$(physical_path "${HOME}") || refuse "cannot resolve HOME ${HOME}"
    operator_claude=("${h}/.claude" "${h}/.claude.json")
    operator_claude_labels=("the operator's Claude Code directory" "the operator's Claude Code settings file")
    if [[ -n ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-} ]]; then
        config=$(physical_path "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR}") || refuse "cannot resolve CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR}"
        if [[ ${config} != "${h}/.claude" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both operands are physical (physical_path), one spelling per path
            operator_claude+=("${config}")
            operator_claude_labels+=("the caller's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR")
        fi
    fi
}

# @description Set `dsh_deny` and `dsh_deny_labels` to the paths the dsh role denies for read and for write, physical,
#   with one label each (regime-cutover U272d, the role table's deny row). srt's read policy is deny-then-allow over
#   an explicit list, and everything the list does not name is readable, so a grant the role does not carry denies
#   nothing: each path is named. The list is what this lever already computes for the omp roles' grants: the
#   checkout's git directory and the git common directory, the `.git` entry of every linked worktree git lists, the
#   hcom store `HCOM_DIR` and every existing `~/.local/state/hcom-*` sibling store (regime-env's convention; the
#   lever's own `~/.local/state/hcom-seat` excepted, by identity), the orchestration records
#   `<checkout>/.orchestration` and every other seat's directory under the seats root (their state slots are under
#   the seats-root deny, which only the own slot re-opens; `.state` is not listed because a concurrent dsh launch
#   makes its slot there while this one lists). Git directories elsewhere on the host are not known here and stay a
#   named residual of the PR body. Every path must be clean (it reaches the settings and the identity table).
# @set dsh_deny The paths.
# @set dsh_deny_labels Their labels.
dsh_deny_paths() {
    local h p i stores=() seats_phys seat_dirs=()
    dsh_deny=() dsh_deny_labels=()
    p=$(physical_path "${launch_gitdir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git directory ${launch_gitdir}"
    if [[ ! ${p} -ef ${common} ]]; then
        dsh_deny+=("${p}") dsh_deny_labels+=("the checkout's git directory")
    fi
    p=$(physical_path "${common}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common}"
    dsh_deny+=("${p}") dsh_deny_labels+=("the git common directory")
    for p in ${worktree_phys[@]+"${worktree_phys[@]}"}; do
        dsh_deny+=("${p}/.git") dsh_deny_labels+=("the linked worktree's git entry")
    done
    p=$(physical_path "${HCOM_DIR}") || refuse "cannot resolve the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR}"
    dsh_deny+=("${p}") dsh_deny_labels+=("the hcom store")
    h=$(physical_path "${HOME}") || refuse "cannot resolve HOME ${HOME}"
    dir_entries "${h}/.local/state"
    for p in ${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"}; do
        case ${p##*/} in # lint-comparisons: allow a basename shape (regime-env's store convention), no path compare
        hcom-*) ;;
        *) continue ;;
        esac
        [[ -d ${p} ]] || continue
        # The lever's own state directory is no store; the store HCOM_DIR names is listed once, above.
        if [[ ${p} -ef ${tools_dir%/*} || ${p} -ef ${HCOM_DIR} ]]; then continue; fi
        stores+=("${p}")
    done
    physical_paths ${stores[@]+"${stores[@]}"}
    for p in ${phys_list[@]+"${phys_list[@]}"}; do
        dsh_deny+=("${p}") dsh_deny_labels+=("an hcom store")
    done
    # Physical, as every row is: a `.orchestration` that is a link into DSH_HOME would otherwise hide its physical
    # ancestry from the identity table, whose chains follow the spelled parents (U272d's finding).
    p=$(physical_path "${checkout}/.orchestration") || refuse "cannot resolve the orchestration records ${checkout}/.orchestration"
    dsh_deny+=("${p}") dsh_deny_labels+=("the orchestration records")
    seats_phys=$(physical_path "${seats_root}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${seats_root}"
    dir_entries "${seats_phys}"
    for p in ${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"}; do
        case ${p##*/} in .state | .sandbox) continue ;; esac
        [[ -d ${p} ]] || continue
        seat_dirs+=("${p}")
    done
    physical_paths ${seat_dirs[@]+"${seat_dirs[@]}"}
    for p in ${phys_list[@]+"${phys_list[@]}"}; do
        dsh_deny+=("${p}") dsh_deny_labels+=("another seat's directory")
    done
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#dsh_deny[@]}; i++)); do
        require_clean_path "a path the dsh role denies (${dsh_deny_labels[i]})" "${dsh_deny[i]}"
    done
}

# The one settings writer (regime-cutover U344; U344c): the path rule every settings row obeys (clean_row, and
# clean_path again, byte for byte), the fixed deny rows, the structural tags of the grant positions, the domain list
# and the JSON text every role's settings are written in, sourced here, after the manifest's own checks and before any
# row is rendered, from a private copy this launch makes, hashes against the writer's pin and removes at once
# (renderer_source): what is hashed is what is sourced, and a rewritten writer stops this launch before its first line.
renderer_source

# @description Render the seat's settings lists (regime-cutover U272e): `write` (the allowWrite roots, exactly
#   seat_write_roots' list, so the protected set and the sandbox cannot drift), `deny_write` with the macOS
#   `deny_write_patterns`, `deny_read` and `allow_read`, with the structural rows tagged where they are rendered
#   (tag_rows). The lists are the one statement of the seat's boundary: seat_sandbox_write writes them into the
#   settings file, and the dsh role judges every grant of them against every deny of them before anything is made
#   (settings_judge, regime-cutover U272f), so a refusal reads what the settings will say and no hand-kept list of
#   inputs or of denied places can lack a member. Every directory is resolved by physical_path, present or
#   absent, so the lists are the same before and after the slots are made. The settings name what the seat may
#   write (its directory, the repository's git common directory, the program's hcom store, its own omp profile and
#   the omp session leases, its own state slot (a per-seat cache root) and its login group's Claude Code directory
#   `<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>` (the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` the shim exports, regime-cutover U318, U498: one
#   login per group, stored and refreshed by Claude Code itself); the same for both omp roles,
#   so no seat writes the seats root or reaches the herdr socket, and none can start a seat), what it may not change
#   inside those roots (git config and hooks, the hcom store's launch scripts and configuration, agent configuration
#   that runs outside the seat and the package the checkout's Claude Code hooks import), what it may not write or
#   read of the operator's Claude Code state (`~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json`, a caller's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`;
#   regime-cutover U190b: srt 0.0.81 grants `~/.claude/debug` of the real HOME on its own, whatever
#   `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` says, so leaving that state out of the roots denies nothing, and the deny is explicit; srt keeps
#   a deeper deny under an allow, measured at U85), and what else it may not read (SSH, GPG, cloud and codex
#   credentials, the chezmoi sources, `~/Workspace` but its own repository, other omp profiles, other hcom stores,
#   every seat's sandbox directory, and for a worker the other seats).
# @set write The allowWrite roots.
# @set deny_write The denyWrite paths; `deny_write_patterns` the macOS pattern rows rendered after them.
# @set unix_sockets The allowUnixSockets directories: the broker's for the router row, none otherwise (U344).
# @set deny_read The denyRead paths.
# @set allow_read The allowRead paths.
# @set row_tags The structural tags, each naming one row by list and position (tag_row): `slot` for the seat's own
#   slots (its directory and state slot) and the shared Claude Code directory, the seats-root denies they re-open, the
#   project-file denies under its directory and the configuration denies under the shared directory; `profile` for
#   its own omp profile and the profiles deny it re-opens; `store` for the program store's root (U219c): the
#   orchestrator's held write row 7, the one grant store_root_judge exempts, and the deny row of every other role. The
#   grant tags are the dsh role's and the orchestrator's store row, read by their judges; the deny tags are rendered
#   for every role and change no list.
seat_settings_render() {
    local root path kind i group project_files=() spelled=()
    h=$(physical_path "${HOME}") || refuse "cannot resolve HOME ${HOME}"
    dir_real=$(physical_path "${dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seat directory ${dir}"
    common_real=$(physical_path "${common}") || refuse "cannot resolve the git common directory ${common}"
    hcom_real=$(physical_path "${HCOM_DIR}") || refuse "cannot resolve the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR}"
    seats_real=$(physical_path "${seats_root}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${seats_root}"
    sandbox_state=${seats_real}/.state/${name}
    # The router row's socket directory (regime-cutover U344): `allowUnixSockets` names `<state slot>/broker`, where
    # acp-broker listens for this launch, for the row whose `broker` cell is 1, and nothing for every other role (U342
    # measured: srt opens the sockets under that one directory and no other socket).
    unix_sockets=()
    if ((broker)); then unix_sockets=("${sandbox_state}/${broker_dir}"); fi
    write=("${seat_write[@]}")
    row_tags=() row_tag_kinds=() row_tag_ixs=() row_tag_paths=()
    deny_write=("${seats_real}/.sandbox")
    # The hook shims under .claude/hooks import their code from .claude/contextdb, run by sessions outside the seat.
    project_files=("${SEAT_SETTINGS_PROJECT_FILES[@]}")
    # The project-file rows under the seat's own directory are refinements inside its write root (srt keeps the
    # deeper deny), so the slot and the cwd contain them by construction: each is tagged at its position.
    for path in "${project_files[@]}"; do
        tag_row slot denyWrite ${#deny_write[@]} "${dir_real}/${path}"
        deny_write+=("${dir_real}/${path}")
    done
    # The login group's Claude Code directory is a write root of every seat (the child's login, `.claude.json`, state
    # and sessions live there, regime-cutover U318, U498), and these rows under it are what a seat must not change:
    # the settings, rules, hooks, plugins, skills, commands and agents that another seat's child, or the operator's
    # login command under that directory, would load (the U190 hole, closed among seats). The bridge child loads none of
    # them (`settingSources: []`, `--strict-mcp-config`); the rows hold whatever a child loads. Tagged like the
    # project-file rows: the grant at write row 2 contains them by construction.
    for path in "${SEAT_SETTINGS_CLAUDE_ROWS[@]}"; do
        tag_row slot denyWrite ${#deny_write[@]} "${claude_config_real}/${path}"
        deny_write+=("${claude_config_real}/${path}")
    done
    for path in "${project_files[@]}"; do deny_write+=("${checkout}/${path}"); done
    # The git state host git reads for any worktree of this repository (regime-cutover U85): a seat that could write
    # it could make a later host git command run a program of its choosing (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`,
    # filter and textconv drivers, includes). git_state_check refuses a launch over such state and creates the files
    # that are absent, so each deny below names an existing path (srt on Linux binds only existing paths).
    git_state_check "${common_real}" "${dir_real}"
    deny_write+=("${git_state[@]}")
    # A worktree created after this launch gets its files denied on macOS by pattern; on Linux srt takes literal
    # write denies only, and the next launch's git_state_check covers it.
    # The patterns are the one place a settings entry is not a clean path: a clean prefix and a fixed suffix, rendered
    # after the deny rows as rows of their own (clean_row admits the form for denyWrite alone).
    deny_write_patterns=()
    if [[ ${os} == Darwin ]]; then
        require_clean_path 'the git common directory' "${common_real}"
        for path in config.worktree info commondir gitdir; do
            # srt reads `*` as `[^/]*` (glob-pattern.js:179-180, globToRegex :208-209), so dot-named ids match too.
            deny_write_patterns+=("${common_real}/worktrees/*/${path}")
        done
    fi
    for path in config.toml env config.env .tmp/launch scripts integrations shell_env.json; do
        deny_write+=("${hcom_real}/${path}")
    done
    deny_read=()
    for path in "${SEAT_SETTINGS_CREDENTIAL_DENIES[@]}"; do deny_read+=("${h}/${path}"); done
    # The profiles deny: the seat's own omp profile is the one row re-opened under it (the dsh case below tags that
    # row; settings_judge pairs the two tags).
    tag_row profile denyRead ${#deny_read[@]} "${h}/.omp/profiles"
    deny_read+=("${h}/.omp/profiles" "${h}/.hcom" "${h}/.local/state/hcom"
        "${h}/.local/share/chezmoi" "${h}/.local/share/chezmoi-private" "${h}/.config/chezmoi"
        "${h}/.config/chezmoi-private" "${h}/Workspace" "${seats_real}/.sandbox")
    # Every program's seats root is unreadable but this seat's own paths: the whole ~/.local/state/omp-seats tree
    # and every configured seats root. srt keeps a deeper deny under an allow (measured, 0.0.81), so each
    # `.sandbox` stays unreadable inside an allowed root. These rows exist to be re-opened by the own slot alone.
    for path in "${h}/.local/state/omp-seats" "${seats_real}"; do
        tag_row slot denyRead ${#deny_read[@]} "${path}"
        deny_read+=("${path}")
    done
    if [[ -n ${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:-} ]]; then
        root=$(physical_path "${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT}"
        tag_row slot denyRead ${#deny_read[@]} "${root}"
        deny_read+=("${root}")
    fi
    # The other login groups' Claude Code directories and the legacy shared one (regime-cutover U498c; verdict
    # U498-4d18d6dd P1 `:2062`): srt reopens a root's subtree under an allow but for a more specific deny, so the
    # orchestrator's read grant of the seats root (its allowRead row 7) reached `.state/claude-worker`, the worker
    # group's login (`.credentials.json` there on Linux). Every role denies, by name, each directory of the table's
    # range (LOGIN_GROUPS) but its own group's, and `.state/claude` (U318's shared directory, which no launch makes,
    # reads or grants, standing order 54), under the physical seats root, as the own directory is rendered. Each
    # group's directory exists when srt reads the file (U498d, login_dirs_make, before the settings file is written;
    # verdict U498-8f2cca8c P1 `:2713`: srt 0.0.81's Linux backend mounts nothing for a denyRead entry that is not
    # there, so the orchestrator's deny of the worker group's directory bound nothing until the worker's first launch
    # or login made it, and the seats-root grant reached the credentials made later); the legacy directory binds when
    # it exists and is made by nothing. The rows stand here, before the role's own deny row, so the router row's
    # denyRead stays a prefix of the dsh row's (acp-broker copies the Router's table to its workers and appends the
    # credential root, U343l); they carry no tag, since no grant of any role lies at or under them. The own group's
    # directory is the one login a seat reads or writes (allowRead and allowWrite row 2 of the foreground roles, the
    # omp roles' `claude_config_real` rows).
    for group in "${LOGIN_GROUPS[@]}"; do
        [[ ${group} != "${login_group}" ]] || continue # lint-comparisons: allow two group words of the login table, not a path
        deny_read+=("${seats_real}/.state/claude-${group}")
    done
    deny_read+=("${seats_real}/.state/claude")
    operator_claude_paths
    deny_write+=("${operator_claude[@]}")
    deny_read+=("${operator_claude[@]}")
    # The role table's read-grant row (U272c): denyRead is broad and every allowRead entry re-opens a path under it,
    # so the list is the role's own. The omp roles re-open their directory, the repository's git directory (the
    # worktree's objects and refs), the hcom store, their omp profile, their state slot, the shared Claude Code
    # directory (U318), the coordinator's records under the main checkout (briefs, verdict files), read by absolute
    # path, and the program store's root (regime-cutover U219: the held physical `store_root_phys`, last; where the
    # records live once U221 has moved them; made by this launch when absent, U219c); the main checkout itself is unreadable
    # to a worker wherever it lives, and the orchestrator also reads the worker clones of its own program, which it
    # reviews. The dsh role has no worktree, no bus and no store: it re-opens its scratch cwd and state slot, the
    # shared Claude Code directory, DSH_HOME, its own omp profile, the skills it loads and the pinned tool directory
    # on its PATH, and no git, hcom, record or store-root path.
    # The omp roles' rows of the Router's credential root (regime-cutover U353b, verdict U353-8791100f P1 `:430`; U353d,
    # verdict U353-318f268d P1 `:2383` and P2 `:2393`): srt allows reads by default, and the U353 head denied the root
    # to the dsh row alone, so a worker or orchestrator seat read `router-credentials/gh/hosts.yml` once the login was
    # there; U353b's row named the kit's root whether or not it existed, which srt's Linux backend mounts nothing for,
    # and denied it for read alone, so a worker under `DSH_HOME=HCOM_DIR` held the root under a write root. The rows
    # are the held physical root (cred_root_hold, under the home router-gh resolves; made by cred_root_make before this
    # render): one denyRead row before the read grants, one denyWrite row after the operator's Claude Code paths.
    case ${role} in
    orchestrator)
        deny_read+=("${cred_root_phys}")
        deny_write+=("${cred_root_phys}")
        allow_read=("${dir_real}" "${common_real}" "${hcom_real}" "${h}/.omp/profiles/${role}" "${sandbox_state}"
            "${claude_config_real}" "${checkout}/.orchestration/orchestrate" "${seats_real}" ${store_root_phys:+"${store_root_phys}"})
        # The held store root is write row 7 (seat_write_roots), the one grant store_root_judge exempts, by this tag.
        if [[ -n ${store_root_phys} ]]; then tag_row store allowWrite 7 "${store_root_phys}"; fi
        ;;
    worker)
        deny_read+=("${checkout}" "${cred_root_phys}")
        deny_write+=("${cred_root_phys}")
        # The program store's root (regime-cutover U219c, verdict U219-985b7c04 P1 `:1981`): the orchestrator's write
        # root is the worker's deny, in the credential root's shape (the held physical path, tagged; made by
        # store_root_make before this launch's settings are written, so srt's Linux backend binds it), so a worker
        # grant a link folds onto the root (`~/.omp/run -> <root>`) is denied by srt as well as refused by
        # store_root_judge.
        if [[ -n ${store_root_phys} ]]; then
            tag_row store denyWrite ${#deny_write[@]} "${store_root_phys}"
            deny_write+=("${store_root_phys}")
        fi
        allow_read=("${dir_real}" "${common_real}" "${hcom_real}" "${h}/.omp/profiles/${role}" "${sandbox_state}"
            "${claude_config_real}" "${checkout}/.orchestration/orchestrate" ${store_root_phys:+"${store_root_phys}"})
        ;;
    dsh | router)
        # The deny row (U272d): the role's own denies for read and for write, after the worker's. The credential root
        # (U353, `cred_root_grant`): the dsh row denies it for read, both rows for write, and each of its rows carries
        # the `credential` tag that pairs it with the DSH_HOME grant it lies inside by construction. The read deny
        # stands last, after the dsh denies, so the router row's denyRead is a prefix of the dsh row's and the row
        # acp-broker appends to its workers' copy of the Router's table makes the same list (regime-cutover U343l);
        # the write deny keeps its place, before the dsh denies.
        deny_read+=("${checkout}")
        deny_read+=(${dsh_deny[@]+"${dsh_deny[@]}"})
        if [[ ${cred_root_grant} == deny ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a cell word of the role table (read, deny), not a path
            tag_row credential denyRead ${#deny_read[@]} "${cred_root_phys}"
            deny_read+=("${cred_root_phys}")
        fi
        # The program store's root (U219c): denied for write by the dsh and router rows as by the worker, right before
        # the credential root's row; the rows carry no grant of it, for read or for write.
        if [[ -n ${store_root_phys} ]]; then
            tag_row store denyWrite ${#deny_write[@]} "${store_root_phys}"
            deny_write+=("${store_root_phys}")
        fi
        tag_row credential denyWrite ${#deny_write[@]} "${cred_root_phys}"
        deny_write+=("${cred_root_phys}" ${dsh_deny[@]+"${dsh_deny[@]}"})
        # The router row's broker directory (regime-cutover U343i, broker_dir_make): `<state slot>/broker`, where
        # acp-broker listens and writes its exit records, is denied to the Router for write, one row inside allowWrite
        # row 1 (the state slot) as the project-file denies lie inside row 0, and tagged `slot` like them so the judge
        # pairs it with that grant (and with allowRead row 1) and with nothing else. srt keeps the deeper deny (on macOS
        # the later rule wins, acp-broker's header; on Linux the path must exist, so the launch makes it before the
        # settings are written). The Router keeps the read (allowRead row 1) and the socket (U344's allowUnixSockets
        # row) and can plant, rename or unlink nothing in it. After every deny the dsh row renders (the store root's
        # and the credential root's rows among them, U219c and U353), so every existing position, tagged or not,
        # stays; the dsh row renders no such row.
        if [[ -n ${broker_dir} ]]; then
            broker_dir_phys=${sandbox_state}/${broker_dir}
            tag_row slot denyWrite ${#deny_write[@]} "${broker_dir_phys}"
            deny_write+=("${broker_dir_phys}")
        fi
        allow_read=("${dir_real}" "${sandbox_state}" "${claude_config_real}" "${dsh_home_phys}" "${h}/.omp/profiles/${omp_profile}"
            "${h}/.agents/skills" "${tools_dir}")
        # The router row's credential root (U353): allowRead row 7, after the tool directory, so every position the dsh
        # row tags stays; tagged `credential` like its denyWrite row, which it is by construction.
        if [[ ${cred_root_grant} == read ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a cell word of the role table (read, deny), not a path
            tag_row credential allowRead ${#allow_read[@]} "${cred_root_phys}"
            allow_read+=("${cred_root_phys}")
        fi
        # The judge's exempted grants, each one row by its position (tag_row, regime-cutover U272g): the own cwd and
        # state slot, rows 0 and 1 of both grant lists, the login group's Claude Code directory, row 2 of both
        # (seat_write_roots puts the three first; the directory sits under the seats-root denies and over its
        # configuration denies, U318, U498), and the own omp profile, row 4 of both. DSH_HOME (row 3 of both) carries
        # the `credential` tag (U353), which
        # pairs it with the credential-root rows alone (the denies it contains by construction, and the router row's
        # read grant against its own write deny); against every other deny it is judged like any row, as are
        # `~/.omp/run` (write row 5) and the router role's state root (write row 6), which carry no tag whatever they
        # are spelled, so a DSH_HOME at or inside the profiles directory, or a `~/.omp/run` linked there, is a hit.
        for kind in allowRead allowWrite; do
            tag_row slot "${kind}" 0 "${dir_real}"
            tag_row slot "${kind}" 1 "${sandbox_state}"
            tag_row slot "${kind}" 2 "${claude_config_real}"
            tag_row credential "${kind}" 3 "${dsh_home_phys}"
            tag_row profile "${kind}" 4 "${h}/.omp/profiles/${omp_profile}"
        done
        ;;
    esac
}

# @description Tag one rendered row, the one at position `$3` of the list `$2`, with the structural tag `$1`
#   (regime-cutover U272g): a tag names why that row may overlap another by construction, and settings_judge exempts a
#   (grant, deny) pair only when both rows carry the same tag. A tag is a reference to one row by its position, never
#   a pattern over spellings: round 5 keyed the tags by rendered spelling, so a `DSH_HOME` equal to the profiles
#   directory, or a `~/.omp/run` linked there, was rendered in that spelling and inherited the profile tag (verdict
#   U272f P1). `$4` is the path the lever rendered at that position; row_tag applies the tag only to a row byte-equal
#   to it, so a list that drifted from its tags exempts nothing.
# @arg $1 string The tag.
# @arg $2 string The list: allowRead, allowWrite, denyRead or denyWrite.
# @arg $3 string The row's position in that list.
# @arg $4 string The path rendered at that position.
# @set row_tags The tags so far; `row_tag_kinds` their lists, `row_tag_ixs` their positions and `row_tag_paths` their
#   paths, one entry per tagged row.
tag_row() {
    row_tags+=("$1") row_tag_kinds+=("$2") row_tag_ixs+=("$3") row_tag_paths+=("$4")
}

# @description Set `tag_of` to the structural tag of the row `$3` at position `$2` of the list `$1` (tag_row), or to
#   the empty string when no tag names that position or the row there is not byte-equal to the path the tag was
#   rendered with.
# @arg $1 string The list.
# @arg $2 string The position.
# @arg $3 string The row at it, as rendered.
# @set tag_of The tag or empty.
row_tag() {
    local i
    tag_of=''
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#row_tags[@]}; i++)); do
        [[ ${row_tag_kinds[i]} == "$1" && ${row_tag_ixs[i]} == "$2" && ${row_tag_paths[i]} == "$3" ]] || continue # lint-comparisons: allow a list name, a position, and one rendered row against the path rendered at that position, both from seat_settings_render
        tag_of=${row_tags[i]}
    done
}

# @description Judge the rendered `allowWrite` rows against the program store's root (regime-cutover U219c, verdict
#   U219-985b7c04 P1 `:1981`: round 2 judged `HCOM_DIR` alone, so a worker whose `~/.omp/run` was a link to the root
#   launched with the records in its write grants). The root is the held `store_root_phys`, taken as held and never
#   resolved again (the overlap check's form); the rows are the `write` list seat_settings_render set, resolved in
#   one subshell (physical_each); both are judged by identity for what exists and by the absent components below
#   one shared ancestor otherwise (identity_table, within_ix). A row
#   that is, contains or lies inside the root is a hit, whatever role renders it, unless it is the orchestrator's own
#   store-root row: the row at the position tag_row tagged `store` (row 7, seat_write_roots), byte-equal to the held
#   path and lying where it is rendered (its physical path is its rendered path), so a profile directory or a
#   `~/.omp/run` linked to the root, a seats root inside it, or the held row itself once a link has moved it, is a hit.
#   The first step of settings_judge for the dsh and router rows; the omp roles run it alone after their render, since
#   their grants contain their denies by design (the common directory over its `config` and `hooks`). Nothing to judge
#   without a root.
# @set judge_grant The first hit: `allowWrite row <path>` and, when it differs, its physical path in parentheses;
#   empty when every row is clear.
# @set judge_deny `the store root REGIME_STORE_ROOT <root>`; empty when clear.
# @exitcode 0 Every write row keeps clear of the root, the orchestrator's own row aside.
# @exitcode 1 A row hits; `judge_grant` and `judge_deny` name it.
store_root_judge() {
    local i n
    judge_grant='' judge_deny=''
    [[ -n ${store_root_phys} ]] || return 0
    n=${#write[@]}
    ((n)) || return 0
    physical_each "${write[@]}"
    phys_list+=("${store_root_phys}")
    identity_table "${phys_list[@]}"
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        within_ix "${n}" "${i}" || within_ix "${i}" "${n}" || continue
        row_tag allowWrite "${i}" "${write[i]}"
        if [[ ${tag_of} == store && ${phys_list[i]} == "${write[i]}" ]]; then continue; fi # lint-comparisons: allow a tag word, and one row's rendered and physical spellings from the same physical producers; the overlap was decided by identity above
        judge_grant="allowWrite row ${write[i]}"
        [[ ${phys_list[i]} == "${write[i]}" ]] || judge_grant+=" (${phys_list[i]})" # lint-comparisons: allow one row's rendered and physical spellings, both from physical producers, no decision rests on it
        judge_deny="the store root REGIME_STORE_ROOT ${store_root_phys}"
        return 1
    done
}

# @description Judge the rendered grants against the rendered denies (regime-cutover U272f): every row of the final
#   `allowRead` and `allowWrite` lists against every row of the final `denyRead` and `denyWrite` lists, and nothing
#   else is the boundary. Rounds 3 and 4 each judged a list of inputs (`DSH_HOME`, then the slot and the cwd too)
#   and each time a rendered grant was missing from that list (round 4: the profile root `~/.omp/profiles/dsh`,
#   linked to `~/.aws`, was granted write); the input list is gone and the lists seat_sandbox_write will write are
#   the judge's only source. Every row is resolved to its physical form first (physical_each, one subshell): a link
#   at the end of a rendered path hides its ancestry from the identity table, whose chains follow the spelled
#   parents. The decision is by identity for everything that exists, and by the absent components below one shared
#   deepest existing ancestor otherwise (identity_table, within_ix; one table, one stat). A grant that is, contains
#   or lies inside a deny is a hit unless the pair is structural: both rows carry the same tag, each tag naming its
#   one row by list and position (tag_row, regime-cutover U272g: the own cwd and state slot under the seats-root
#   denies and over the project-file denies, the own profile under the profiles deny), and the grant lies where it
#   is rendered (its physical path is its rendered path), so a tagged grant that a link moves elsewhere
#   (`~/.omp/profiles/dsh -> ~/.omp/profiles/orchestrator`) is judged like any row, and so is an untagged row of
#   an exempted row's spelling (`DSH_HOME=~/.omp/profiles/dsh`, `~/.omp/run -> ~/.omp/profiles`). The read grants
#   go first: they are spelled as rendered (the profile by its name), so the first hit names the row as the caller
#   knows it. The macOS write patterns are not rows (no grant of the role lies under the common directory).
#   The program store's root is judged first (store_root_judge, regime-cutover U219c): every allowWrite row against
#   the held root, the orchestrator's own tagged row excepted; the omp roles run that step alone after their render.
# @set judge_grant The first grant that hits: `<kind> row <path>` and, when it differs, its physical path in
#   parentheses; empty when every grant is clear.
# @set judge_deny The deny it hits: `<path>[ (<physical>)], a row of its <kind> list`; empty when clear.
# @exitcode 0 Every grant keeps clear of every deny it is not structurally paired with.
# @exitcode 1 A pair overlaps; `judge_grant` and `judge_deny` name it.
settings_judge() {
    local i j n m rows=() kinds=() ixs=() tags=()
    store_root_judge || return 1
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#allow_read[@]}; i++)); do rows+=("${allow_read[i]}") kinds+=(allowRead) ixs+=("${i}"); done
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#write[@]}; i++)); do rows+=("${write[i]}") kinds+=(allowWrite) ixs+=("${i}"); done
    n=${#rows[@]}
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#deny_read[@]}; i++)); do rows+=("${deny_read[i]}") kinds+=(denyRead) ixs+=("${i}"); done
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#deny_write[@]}; i++)); do rows+=("${deny_write[i]}") kinds+=(denyWrite) ixs+=("${i}"); done
    m=$((${#rows[@]} - n))
    judge_grant='' judge_deny=''
    ((n && m)) || return 0
    for ((i = 0; i < n + m; i++)); do
        row_tag "${kinds[i]}" "${ixs[i]}" "${rows[i]}"
        tags+=("${tag_of}")
    done
    physical_each "${rows[@]}"
    identity_table "${phys_list[@]}"
    for ((i = 0; i < n; i++)); do
        for ((j = n; j < n + m; j++)); do
            within_ix "${j}" "${i}" || within_ix "${i}" "${j}" || continue
            if [[ -n ${tags[i]} && ${tags[i]} == "${tags[j]}" && ${phys_list[i]} == "${rows[i]}" ]]; then continue; fi # lint-comparisons: allow two tag words, and one row's rendered and physical spellings from the same physical producers; the overlap was decided by identity above
            judge_grant="${kinds[i]} row ${rows[i]}"
            judge_deny=${rows[j]}
            # The same row in two spellings when the rendered one goes through a link; the reader needs both.
            [[ ${phys_list[i]} == "${rows[i]}" ]] || judge_grant+=" (${phys_list[i]})" # lint-comparisons: allow one row's rendered and physical spellings, both from physical producers, no decision rests on it
            [[ ${phys_list[j]} == "${rows[j]}" ]] || judge_deny+=" (${phys_list[j]})"  # lint-comparisons: allow one row's rendered and physical spellings, both from physical producers, no decision rests on it
            judge_deny+=", a row of its ${kinds[j]} list"
            return 1
        done
    done
}

# @description Refuse (exit 2) unless the final `allowWrite` list of one seat keeps clear of every protected path
#   (regime-cutover U85), one invariant instead of a list of cases: for every granted root R and every protected
#   path P, R must not be or contain P, and R must not lie inside P. The protected paths are defined once: the main
#   checkout, the seats root, its `.sandbox`, every other seat directory under the seats root, every other
#   worktree of this repository and the operator's Claude Code state (operator_claude_paths, regime-cutover U190b: a
#   `HCOM_DIR=~/.claude` or `--seats-root ~/.claude/seats` would grant that state whole); the seat's own directory
#   (same identity) is not protected for it. Exempt by
#   construction, not by comparing text: the seat's own slots under the seats root (the first two roots: a worker's
#   `<seats-root>/<name>`, and `<seats-root>/.state/<name>`) against the seats root and its `.sandbox`, and the git
#   common directory named `.git` whose parent is the main checkout (identity). A linked worktree inside R (Claude
#   Code keeps its worktrees under `<checkout>/.claude/worktrees`) refuses, present or absent, naming the worktree
#   and `git worktree move`, `remove` or `prune` (regime-cutover U95, operator decision U95-nested-refuse-decided:
#   a seat could rewrite its `.git` file and tracked files, which host git and host tools read). Containment is
#   decided by identity for everything that exists, and below one shared deepest existing ancestor by the absent
#   components (identity_table, within_ix), one table for every pair. Every path must be clean (clean_path) before
#   anything is created, so this runs in a dry run too.
# @arg $1 string The role.
# @arg $2 string The seat directory, physical.
# @arg $@ string The seat's allowWrite roots after them, physical, its own slots first (seat_write_roots).
seat_overlap_check() {
    local own_role=$1 own_dir=$2 r p i j k nroots seats_phys labels=() protected=() own=() roots=() seat_dirs=()
    shift 2
    roots=("$@")
    nroots=$#
    seats_phys=$(physical_path "${seats_root}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seats root ${seats_root}"
    labels+=("the main checkout" "the seats root" "the seats' sandbox directory")
    protected+=("${checkout}" "${seats_phys}" "${seats_phys}/.sandbox")
    # Every directory in the seats root, dot names included (dir_entries); `.state` and `.sandbox` are protected or
    # exempt by their own rules above. All resolved in one batch (physical_paths), so more seats start no process.
    dir_entries "${seats_phys}"
    seat_dirs=()
    for p in ${dir_list[@]+"${dir_list[@]}"}; do
        [[ -d ${p} ]] || continue
        case ${p##*/} in .state | .sandbox) continue ;; esac
        seat_dirs+=("${p}")
    done
    physical_paths ${seat_dirs[@]+"${seat_dirs[@]}"}
    ((${#phys_list[@]} == ${#seat_dirs[@]})) ||
        refuse "the seat directories in ${seats_phys} were not all resolved (${#phys_list[@]} of ${#seat_dirs[@]})"
    for p in ${phys_list[@]+"${phys_list[@]}"}; do
        labels+=("the seat directory")
        protected+=("${p}")
    done
    # One resolved path per linked worktree git records (physical_paths), or the check below could miss one.
    ((${#worktree_phys[@]} == ${#worktree_paths[@]} - 1)) ||
        refuse "the worktrees of ${repo} were not all resolved (${#worktree_phys[@]} of $((${#worktree_paths[@]} - 1)))"
    for p in ${worktree_phys[@]+"${worktree_phys[@]}"}; do
        labels+=("the worktree")
        protected+=("${p}")
    done
    operator_claude_paths
    for ((i = 0; i < ${#operator_claude[@]}; i++)); do
        labels+=("${operator_claude_labels[i]}")
        protected+=("${operator_claude[i]}")
    done
    for p in "${protected[@]}"; do
        require_clean_path 'a protected seat path' "${p}"
        # The seat's own directory is its to write.
        if [[ -e ${p} && ${p} -ef ${own_dir} ]]; then own+=(1); else own+=(0); fi
    done
    ((${#own[@]} == ${#protected[@]})) || refuse "the overlap table of the ${own_role} seat does not hold one entry per protected path"
    for r in "${roots[@]}"; do
        require_clean_path "a write root of the ${own_role} seat" "${r}"
    done
    identity_table "${roots[@]}" "${protected[@]}"
    for ((k = 0; k < nroots; k++)); do
        r=${roots[k]}
        for ((i = 0; i < ${#protected[@]}; i++)); do
            ((! own[i])) || continue
            # Its own slots under the seats root sit there by construction, as siblings of `.sandbox`: the state
            # directory of every seat, and a worker's directory (the orchestrator's is the launch checkout, checked);
            # so does the shared Claude Code directory, root 2 of every role, inside `.state` (U318).
            # own_slots_check has proved, before this runs, that they are what they claim (no link, right parent).
            if [[ (${k} == 1 || (${k} == 0 && ${own_role} != orchestrator)) && (${i} == 1 || ${i} == 2) ]]; then continue; fi
            if [[ ${k} == 2 && ${i} == 1 ]]; then continue; fi
            p=${protected[i]}
            j=$((nroots + i))
            if within_ix "${k}" "${j}"; then
                if [[ ${labels[i]} == 'the worktree' ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a fixed label, no path compare
                    refuse "the worktree ${p} lies inside the ${own_role} seat's write root ${r}, where the seat could rewrite its .git file and tracked files; move it out (\`git worktree move ${p} <a path outside>\`), remove it (\`git worktree remove ${p}\`), or prune it if its directory is gone (\`git worktree prune\`)"
                fi
                refuse "the ${own_role} seat's write root ${r} contains ${labels[i]} ${p}; seat write roots must not overlap (choose another --seats-root, HCOM_DIR or git directory)"
            fi
            if within_ix "${j}" "${k}"; then
                # The main checkout's own `.git`, by identity of the common directory and its parent.
                if ((i == 0)) && [[ -e ${r} && ${r} -ef ${common} && -d ${checkout}/.git && ! -L ${checkout}/.git && ${checkout}/.git -ef ${r} ]]; then continue; fi
                refuse "the ${own_role} seat's write root ${r} lies inside ${labels[i]} ${p}; seat write roots must not overlap (choose another --seats-root, HCOM_DIR or git directory)"
            fi
        done
    done
}

dir_phys=$(physical_path "${dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the seat directory ${dir}"
# The role table's deny row (U272d): in a dry run too, and before anything is made. DSH_HOME is the held physical home
# (dsh_home_hold, U321d); nothing resolves it again here.
dsh_deny=() dsh_deny_labels=()
if [[ ${role_launch} == foreground ]]; then dsh_deny_paths; fi
seat_overlap_check "${role}" "${dir_phys}" "${seat_write[@]}"
orchestrator_write=()
while IFS= read -r root; do orchestrator_write+=("${root}"); done <<< "${other_roots}"
# The orchestrator's own directory is the launch checkout (`${repo}`, a linked worktree or the main checkout), the
# directory its write list holds; the main checkout stays protected for it only when it is not that checkout.
repo_phys=$(physical_path "${repo}") || refuse "cannot resolve the launch checkout ${repo}"
seat_overlap_check orchestrator "${repo_phys}" "${orchestrator_write[@]}"
# The role table's refusal row (U272e, U272f): the dsh role's settings are rendered now and every grant of them is
# judged against every deny of them, after the overlap invariant (whose refusals name the protected place) and
# before anything is made, in a dry run too. The omp roles render theirs once their worktree exists (its `.git` file
# is one of the denies).
if [[ ${role_launch} == foreground ]]; then
    seat_settings_render
    settings_judge ||
        refuse "the dsh role's ${judge_grant} is, contains or lies inside ${judge_deny}; the launch is refused before anything is made"
    # The router row's state root and both foreground rows' credential root are made now, after the home they lie in
    # has passed the judgement, in a real launch alone (state_root_make, regime-cutover U321d; cred_root_make, U353,
    # the dsh row too since U353d); a dry run says what a launch would make and makes nothing. The router row's broker
    # directory (regime-cutover U343i): a dry run says here what a launch would make; a launch makes it in
    # seat_sandbox_write, once the state slot it lies in exists and the slot trap is armed (broker_dir_make).
    if [[ -n ${state_root} ]]; then state_root_make "${dry_run}"; fi
    cred_root_make "${dry_run}"
    # The program store's root (U219c): made now, for the deny row the dsh and router rows render of it.
    store_root_make "${dry_run}"
    if ((dry_run)); then broker_dir_make 1; fi
    # The dry run's compare of a present profile config runs the helper after the judge's acceptance of the profile
    # boundary and writes nothing (regime-cutover U310c, U310d); a launch compares at the write.
    profile_config_compare
fi
roots=("${seat_write[@]}" "${seats_root}" "${HCOM_DIR}" "${common}")
while IFS= read -r root; do roots+=("${root}"); done <<< "${other_roots}"
seat_settings_files "${seats_root}"
for settings_file in ${settings_files[@]+"${settings_files[@]}"}; do
    [[ -e ${settings_file} ]] || continue
    listed=$(allow_write_list "${os}" "${settings_file}") ||
        refuse "cannot read a clean allowWrite list from ${settings_file}"
    while IFS= read -r root; do
        if [[ -n ${root} ]]; then roots+=("${root}"); fi
    done <<< "${listed}"
done
add_roots "${roots[@]}"
if [[ -n ${mise_real} ]]; then PATH=${system_path} pin_exec mise "${mise_real}"; fi

# Every link in the private tool directory, with its interpreter chain, is re-checked against the exact set, and PATH
# is that directory and the system directories, so hcom's own lookups (`herdr`, `node`) and srt's (`env`, the shell)
# find nothing a seat writes.
for link in "${tools_dir}"/*; do
    [[ -e ${link} || -L ${link} ]] || continue
    pin_exec "${link##*/}" "${link}"
    for tool in "${optional_tools[@]}"; do
        if [[ ${tool} == "${link##*/}" ]]; then trusted_interpreter_check "${tool}"; fi
    done
done
pin_exec git "${git_path}"
git_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
IFS=: read -r -a path_dirs <<< "${PATH}"
for path_dir in "${path_dirs[@]}"; do
    path_real=$(physical_path "${path_dir}") || refuse "cannot resolve the PATH entry ${path_dir}"
    refuse_if_seat_writable 'the PATH entry' "${path_real}"
done
pinned=()
omp_path=$(find_on_path omp) || refuse 'omp not found in the private tool directory'
pin_exec omp "${omp_path}"
omp_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
# The role table's command row: what the shim execs under srt. The omp roles run omp with --no-extensions first (U66);
# the dsh and router roles run `<DSH_HOME>/bin/dsh`, a physical executable file that runs inside srt alone: it lies in
# its own write root, so no identity rule can pin it, and nothing probes it outside containment (the U251 finding).
case ${role_launch} in
hcom) seat_cmd=("${omp_cmd[@]}" --no-extensions) shim_tool=omp ;;
foreground)
    dsh_exec=$(physical_file "${dsh_home_phys}/bin/dsh") ||
        refuse "cannot resolve the dsh command to a physical executable file: ${dsh_home_phys}/bin/dsh"
    seat_cmd=("${dsh_exec}") shim_tool=dsh
    ;;
esac
srt_path=$(find_on_path srt) || refuse 'srt (@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime) not found in the private tool directory'
pin_exec srt "${srt_path}"
srt_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
# The installed srt is of the line this script encodes (SRT_LINE): its `--version` is read by the checked argv, status
# first, so a failed or empty read is a refusal, never a pass; no seats root, store or process exists yet.
srt_version=$("${srt_cmd[@]}" --version 2> /dev/null) ||
    refuse "cannot read the srt version (${srt_cmd[*]} --version failed); hcom-seat encodes the srt ${SRT_LINE} line"
srt_version=${srt_version%%$'\n'*}
srt_version=${srt_version%% *}
[[ ${srt_version} =~ ^([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)(\.[0-9A-Za-z.+-]+)?$ ]] ||
    refuse "cannot read the srt version from '${srt_version}' (${srt_cmd[*]} --version); hcom-seat encodes the srt ${SRT_LINE} line"
[[ ${BASH_REMATCH[1]} == "${SRT_LINE}" ]] ||
    refuse "srt ${srt_version} is not of the ${SRT_LINE} line hcom-seat encodes; home/dot_mise/config.toml pins the release, and a bump is a reviewed edit of the pin and SRT_LINE together"
# hcom and the herdr it drives run outside every sandbox: the launch execs hcom by its physical argv, and hcom finds
# `hcom` and `herdr` through the shim directory first on PATH, as wrappers around their physical argv.
hcom_path=$(find_on_path hcom) || refuse 'hcom not found on PATH'
pin_exec hcom "${hcom_path}"
hcom_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
herdr_path=$(find_on_path herdr) || refuse 'herdr not found on PATH'
pin_exec herdr "${herdr_path}"
herdr_cmd=("${pinned[@]}")
os=$(uname -s) || refuse 'cannot read the operating system name (uname -s)'
linux_tools=''
case ${os} in
Darwin) [[ -x /usr/bin/sandbox-exec ]] || refuse 'sandbox-exec absent: /usr/bin/sandbox-exec' ;;
Linux)
    # srt looks bwrap, socat and rg up on PATH unless its settings name them; they name the checked physical files.
    # srt runs them by these paths, so a script among them (whose interpreter the kernel would look up) is refused.
    bwrap_real='' socat_real='' rg_real=''
    for tool in bwrap socat rg; do
        pin_exec "${tool}" "${tools_dir}/${tool}"
        ((${#pinned[@]} == 1)) || refuse "${tool} ${pinned[1]} is a script; srt runs it by path, so it must be a binary"
        case ${tool} in
        bwrap) bwrap_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        socat) socat_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        rg) rg_real=${pinned[0]} ;;
        esac
    done
    require_clean_path bwrap "${bwrap_real}"
    require_clean_path socat "${socat_real}"
    require_clean_path rg "${rg_real}"
    linux_tools=",\"bwrapPath\":\"${bwrap_real}\",\"socatPath\":\"${socat_real}\",\"ripgrep\":{\"command\":\"${rg_real}\"}"
    ;;
*) refuse "no seat sandbox for ${os}; srt supports macOS and Linux" ;;
esac
# @description Make every login group's Claude Code directory `<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>`, one per group of
#   the table's range `LOGIN_GROUPS` (the own group's, which the settings grant, among them), 0700 and empty, when
#   absent (regime-cutover U498d; verdict U498-8f2cca8c P1 `:2713`): srt 0.0.81's Linux backend mounts nothing for a
#   denyRead entry that is not there (dist/sandbox/linux-sandbox-utils.js:1810-1812, the U353d class), so the
#   orchestrator's deny of `.state/claude-worker` bound nothing until the worker group's first launch or the operator's
#   login made that directory, and its read grant of the seats root reached the credentials made later. Called by
#   seat_sandbox_write once `.state` exists and before the settings file is written, so every deny row of every role
#   names a directory that exists when srt reads the file, on both backends. The shape of the own directory's make
#   step (U318): own_slots_check proved each path no link and, when present, a directory sitting in `.state`; one
#   `mkdir` under `umask 077` that takes no existing entry (two launches at once may both find a directory absent, and
#   the loser of the race takes the directory the winner made); present or made, each is a real directory of this
#   user, else the launch refuses naming the group and the path. No login is made, read or copied: the directory is
#   empty until the operator's `claude auth login` under it (seat-login-preflight prints the command); the legacy
#   `.state/claude` is not in the range and is made by nothing (standing order 54).
# @noargs
login_dirs_make() {
    local group path
    for group in "${LOGIN_GROUPS[@]}"; do
        path=${seats_root}/.state/claude-${group}
        if [[ ! -e ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]]; then
            (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${path}") || [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] ||
                refuse "cannot create the ${group} login group's Claude Code directory ${path}"
        fi
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
            refuse "the ${group} login group's Claude Code directory ${path} is not a real directory of this user"
    done
}
# @description Write the seat's srt settings (the lists seat_settings_render rendered) and its shim under
#   `<seats-root>/.sandbox/<name>` (regime-cutover U85), afresh on every launch, after the seat directory exists.
#   The shim runs a canary under those settings first, a write into the sandbox directory, reads of the settings
#   file and `~/.ssh`, and a write under the operator's `~/.claude/debug`, and refuses (exit 2) unless all four fail
#   inside; only then does it run the seat's command under srt, both by the physical argv `pin_exec` checked.
# @noargs
seat_sandbox_write() {
    local sandbox_real path settings shim json origin_url push_url srt_q cmd_q
    local write_json deny_write_json deny_read_json allow_read_json unix_sockets_json
    # srt on Linux grants writes only to paths that exist, so omp's own state directories are made first. The seat's
    # slots under the seats root were proved free of links (own_slots_check); they are made one component at a time,
    # and each is checked again to be a real directory. The login group directories, the own group's grant and the
    # other groups' denies, are made right after `.state` (login_dirs_make, U498d).
    (umask 077 && mkdir -p "${seats_root}" "${HOME}/.omp/profiles/${omp_profile}" "${HOME}/.omp/run") ||
        refuse "cannot create the seats root ${seats_root} or omp's state directories"
    # The row's state root (U321b, U321c, U321d): held by state_root_hold from the held physical DSH_HOME and made by
    # state_root_make after the home's deny judgement, it is the held physical path the settings carry, whatever stands
    # at the spelled path now. Gone since, or no longer a real directory of this user, the launch refuses by name
    # before the settings are written; nothing is derived from the path.
    if [[ -n ${state_root_phys} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${state_root_phys} && ! -L ${state_root_phys} && -O ${state_root_phys} ]] ||
            refuse "the ${role} role's state root ${state_root_phys} is not a real directory of this user"
    fi
    # The credential root (U353, U353d): every role's must be the real directory of this user cred_root_make left, so
    # the deny or the grant that names it names a directory that exists when srt reads the settings.
    [[ -d ${cred_root_phys} && ! -L ${cred_root_phys} && -O ${cred_root_phys} ]] ||
        refuse "the ${role} role's credential root ${cred_root_phys} is not a real directory of this user"
    # `.state` first, then every login group's directory under it (login_dirs_make), then the per-launch slots. Two
    # launches at once (the dsh role's normal case) may both find a shared parent absent; the loser of the mkdir race
    # takes the directory the winner made, held to a real directory by the check after it.
    path=${seats_root}/.state
    if [[ ! -e ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]]; then
        (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${path}") || [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "cannot create ${path}"
    fi
    [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "${path} is not a real directory"
    login_dirs_make
    for path in "${seats_root}/.state/${name}" ${scratch_dir:+"${scratch_dir}"} "${seats_root}/.sandbox" "${sandbox}" "${sandbox}/bin"; do
        if [[ ! -e ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]]; then
            (umask 077 && /bin/mkdir "${path}") || [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "cannot create ${path}"
        fi
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "${path} is not a real directory"
    done
    # The router row's broker directory, inside the state slot made above and before the settings file names it as a
    # denyWrite row (regime-cutover U343i, broker_dir_make): the one directory of the slot the Router cannot write.
    broker_dir_make 0
    sandbox_real=$(cd "${sandbox}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the seat sandbox directory ${sandbox}"
    settings=${sandbox_real}/srt-settings.json
    write_json=$(json_paths 'a seat write root' 0 "${write[@]}") || exit 2
    deny_write_json=$(json_paths 'a seat write deny' 1 "${deny_write[@]}" ${deny_write_patterns[@]+"${deny_write_patterns[@]}"}) || exit 2
    deny_read_json=$(json_paths 'a seat read deny' 0 "${deny_read[@]}") || exit 2
    allow_read_json=$(json_paths 'a seat read root' 0 "${allow_read[@]}") || exit 2
    unix_sockets_json=$(json_paths 'a seat socket directory' 0 ${unix_sockets[@]+"${unix_sockets[@]}"}) || exit 2
    # No unix socket for any seat but the router row's broker directory (`unix_sockets`, seat_settings_render, U344):
    # the herdr socket would let a seat open a pane outside every sandbox. Local binding is the role table's
    # `allow_local_binding` cell: false for every role but the router, whose Runtime needs its loopback listener
    # (U321); srt 0.0.81 grants it as bind and inbound on `*:*` (every interface), and the upstream host check bounds
    # what that listener answers. The one listener an omp seat runs, the hcom plugin's notify server, falls back to
    # polling every 5 s when its bind fails (hcom.ts `startNotifyServer`, `FALLBACK_PENDING_POLL_MS`). The text is
    # the one writer's (seat_settings_json, seat-settings-render.sh), built by the shell from clean rows only
    # (json_paths), so no JSON tool runs and none is needed on macOS.
    seat_settings_json "${allow_local_binding}" "${unix_sockets_json}" "${deny_read_json}" "${allow_read_json}" \
        "${write_json}" "${deny_write_json}" "${linux_tools}" ||
        refuse "cannot render the settings text (allowLocalBinding '${allow_local_binding}' is neither true nor false)"
    json=${settings_json}
    if ! printf '%s\n' "${json}" > "${settings}.tmp" || ! mv -f "${settings}.tmp" "${settings}"; then
        refuse "cannot write ${settings}"
    fi
