        allowed = " or ".join(kinds)
        detail = ": it holds a lone surrogate" if "string" in kinds and isinstance(value, str) else ""
        refuse(path, f"{where} is not of type {allowed}{detail}")
    if is_number(value):
        for keyword, side, outside in BOUNDS:
            if keyword in schema and outside(value, schema[keyword]):
                refuse(path, f"{where} is {value}, {side} the {keyword} {schema[keyword]}")
    if "enum" in schema and value not in schema["enum"]:
        allowed = ", ".join(schema["enum"])
        refuse(path, f"{where} is {shown(value)}, not one of {allowed}")
    if isinstance(value, str):
        shortest, pattern = schema.get("minLength"), schema.get("pattern")
        if shortest is not None and len(value) < shortest:
            refuse(path, f"{where} is {shown(value)}, shorter than the minLength {shortest}")
        if pattern is not None and re.search(ecma(pattern), value) is None:
            refuse(path, f"{where} is {shown(value)}, which does not match the pattern {pattern}")
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key in schema.get("required", []):
            if key not in value:
                refuse(path, f"{where} lacks the required key {key}")
        properties = schema.get("properties", {})
        if schema.get("additionalProperties") is False:
            for key in value:
                if key not in properties:
                    refuse(path, f"{where} has the unknown key {key}")
        for key, subschema in properties.items():
            if key in value:
                check(value[key], subschema, f"{where}.{key}", path)
    if isinstance(value, list) and "items" in schema:
        for index, item in enumerate(value):
            check(item, schema["items"], f"{where}[{index}]", path)


def one_line(text):
    return " ".join(str(text).split())


def write_whole(text_path, text):
    """verdict.md appears whole or not at all: written under a partial name beside it and renamed over the final name.
    A write that fails leaves no verdict.md (U106 audit round 4: a failed write left an empty file at the path the
    lever prints)."""
    partial = f"{text_path}.partial"
    try:
        with open(partial, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(text)
        os.replace(partial, text_path)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        try:
            os.unlink(partial)
        except OSError:
            pass
        refuse(text_path, f"cannot write the verdict text: {error}")


def main():
    schema_path, verdict_path, text_path = sys.argv[1:4]
    try:
        with open(schema_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            schema = json.load(handle)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        refuse(schema_path, f"cannot read the verdict schema: {error}")
    check_schema(schema, "the schema", schema_path)
    try:
        with open(verdict_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            document = json.load(
                handle, parse_float=number, parse_int=number, parse_constant=constant, object_pairs_hook=pairs
            )
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(verdict_path, f"cannot read the verdict file: {error}")
    except ValueError as error:
        refuse(verdict_path, f"not valid JSON: {error}")
    except Departure as error:
        refuse(verdict_path, f"not JSON: {error}")
    check(document, schema, "the verdict", verdict_path)
    verdict = document["verdict"]
    findings = document["findings"]
    blocking = [f for f in findings if f["priority"] in BLOCKING and f["frequency"] * f["severity"] >= WEIGHT_THRESHOLD]
    filed = [f for f in findings if f["frequency"] * f["severity"] < WEIGHT_THRESHOLD]
    derived = "incorrect" if blocking else "correct"
    if ACCEPTED_WITH[verdict] != derived:
        refuse(
            verdict_path,
            f"the verdict.verdict {verdict} contradicts the verdict.findings: {len(blocking)} of priority P0 or P1 "
            f"with weight {WEIGHT_THRESHOLD} or more (weight is frequency times severity; any one means incorrect, "
            "none means correct or blocked; a finding under the threshold is filed and a P2 or P3 changes no verdict)",
        )
    lines = ["## Findings", ""]
    for finding in findings:
        priority, confidence, path, line = (finding[key] for key in ("priority", "confidence", "path", "line"))
        frequency, severity = int(finding["frequency"]), int(finding["severity"])
        # The path passed the pattern of the schema (no colon, no whitespace), so `<path>:<line>` is the location the
        # two readers will read: the first colon-free token. The rationale is free text and is folded to one line.
        rationale = one_line(finding["rationale"])
        lines.append(f"- {priority} ({confidence}) [f{frequency} s{severity}] {path}:{int(line)}: {rationale}")
    if not findings:
        lines.append("- none")
    lines += ["", "## Reproduced", ""]
    lines += [f"- {one_line(entry)}" for entry in document["reproduced"]] or ["- nothing"]
    if document["notes"]:
        lines += ["", "## Notes", "", document["notes"].rstrip()]
    lines += ["", f"Blocking: {len(blocking)}", f"Filed: {len(filed)}", f"Verdict: {verdict}", ""]
    write_whole(text_path, "\n".join(lines))
    print(verdict)


main()
'

schema=${run}/verdict.schema.json
printf '%s\n' "${verdict_schema}" > "${schema}" || fail "cannot write the verdict schema ${schema}"
verdict_json=${run}/verdict.json
verdict=${run}/verdict.md
codex_started=1
status=0
codex_scratch "${audit_timeout}" "${prompt}" "${run}/codex.log" exec --strict-config --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral \
    --ignore-rules "${cyber_program_args[@]}" -C "${work}/cwd" --output-schema "${schema}" -o "${verdict_json}" - ||
    status=$?
((status == 0)) || fail "codex exec exited ${status}; its log is ${run}/codex.log"
[[ -s ${verdict_json} ]] || fail "codex exec wrote no final message to ${verdict_json}; its log is ${run}/codex.log"
# The reader's status decides (standing order 21): a reader that failed or refused yields no verdict, never a default.
value=$("${python}" -I -S -c "${verdict_reader}" "${schema}" "${verdict_json}" "${verdict}") ||
    fail "no verdict was taken from ${verdict_json}; its log is ${run}/codex.log"
[[ ${value} =~ ^(correct|incorrect|blocked)$ ]] || fail "the verdict reader named no verdict for ${verdict_json}: ${value}"
printf '%s\n%s\n' "${verdict}" "Verdict: ${value}"
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-body-edit.sh
# @brief Replace the body of the open pull request of the current branch, the worker seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, the worker seat's lever, allowed only in the form
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-body-edit.sh --body-file *` by `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/worker.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"); the orchestrator's policy denies it. It
#   edits only the pull request of the branch the seat has checked out: `git branch --show-current` must name a
#   branch other than `main`, and `gh pr view --json number,headRefName,state` (the pull request of that branch)
#   must report it as `headRefName` and `OPEN`. The body file is a regular file (not a symlink) of 1 to 65536
#   bytes whose real path is inside `$TMPDIR` or the checkout. The new body must hold exactly one line starting
#   `Program-Unit:`, and it must be `Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>`, the line `regime-ci.py` reads: `<program>` in
#   `regime-init`'s grammar (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) naming a store the checkout holds,
#   `.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/units.tsv` (U71), and a plain unit id (a fix round writes its parent id,
#   `preferences.md` standing order 24); when the current body already carries one such line, the program and the
#   unit must stay the same, so an edit fixes the line or the text but never moves a pull request to another
#   program or unit. Every `## ` heading line and the `Generated with [Claude Code]` footer line of
#   the current body must still be in the new body, so sections are added or rewritten, never dropped. The one
#   write is `gh pr edit <n> --body-file <file>`. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl
#   `alarm`).
# @option --body-file <file> The new body.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `edited pr=<n> branch=<b> program=<program> unit=U<n> sha256=<body sha256>`.
# @exitcode 0 The body was replaced.
# @exitcode 1 A `git` or `gh` read, or the edit, failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the branch, the pull request's state, the body file, or the body's content.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-body-edit.sh --body-file "$TMPDIR/body.md"
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''             # producer-status: allow the if below takes an empty home as the checkout layout
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}

# The isolated git and the environment scrub come from the library beside this script (U113): the toplevel and the
# current branch are read by a git no caller variable or configuration steers.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh ]] || {
    echo "pr-body-edit.sh: refused: git-isolated.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh"
# shellcheck disable=SC2119 # no name is kept: every GIT_* and transport variable goes
git_env_scrub

[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh ]] || {
    echo "pr-body-edit.sh: refused: read-lib.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/read-lib.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh"

lever='pr-body-edit.sh'
usage='usage: pr-body-edit.sh --body-file <file>'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
unit_line='^Program-Unit: [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}/U[0-9]+$'
footer_re='Generated with \[Claude Code\]\(https://claude\.com/claude-code\)'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Refuse unless $1 is a regular file of 1 to 65536 bytes inside $TMPDIR or the checkout.
# @arg $1 path The body file.
# @set body_path Its real path.
body_file_check() {
    local file=$1 dir root size
    [[ -f ${file} && ! -L ${file} ]] || refuse "the body file is not a regular file: ${file}"
    case ${file} in # lint-comparisons: allow splits the argument at its last slash; the real path is compared below
    */*) dir=${file%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${file}"
    body_path=${dir}/${file##*/}
    size=$(wc -c < "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
    size=${size//[[:space:]]/}
    if ! [[ ${size} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ((size == 0 || size > 65536)); then
        refuse "the body file must hold 1 to 65536 bytes: ${body_path}"
    fi
    for root in "${TMPDIR:-}" "${toplevel}"; do
        [[ -n ${root} && -d ${root} ]] || continue
        root=$(cd "${root}" && pwd -P) || continue    # producer-status: allow a root that cannot be entered holds no body file; the refusal after the loop stands
        [[ ${body_path} == "${root}"/* ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    done
    refuse "the body file is outside \$TMPDIR and the checkout: ${body_path}"
}

# @description Print the lines of file $2 (CR stripped) that match the ERE $1, one per line. The ERE reaches awk
#   through the environment, since `awk -v` would read its backslashes as escapes.
# @arg $1 string The ERE.
# @arg $2 path The file.
lines_matching() {
    LINES_RE=$1 awk '{ sub(/\r$/, "") } $0 ~ ENVIRON["LINES_RE"]' "$2"
}

[[ $# -eq 2 && $1 == --body-file ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
toplevel=$(git_isolated rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
branch=$(git_isolated branch --show-current) || fail 'git branch --show-current failed'
[[ -n ${branch} ]] || refuse 'HEAD is detached; switch to the branch of your pull request'
[[ ${branch} != main ]] || refuse 'the current branch is main'
body_file_check "$2"
markers=$(lines_matching '^Program-Unit:' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
[[ -n ${markers} && ${markers} != *$'\n'* && ${markers} =~ ${unit_line} ]] ||
    refuse "the body must hold exactly one line 'Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>' (a plain unit id); it holds: ${markers:-none}"
marker=${markers#Program-Unit: }
program=${marker%/*}
unit=${marker##*/}
[[ -f ${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/units.tsv ]] ||
    refuse "the Program-Unit line names ${program}, but the checkout holds no .orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/units.tsv"

view=$(gh_bounded pr view --json number,headRefName,state --jq '[(.number | tostring), .headRefName, .state] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read the pull request of ${branch}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r number head state <<< "${view}"
[[ ${number} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || fail "gh pr view printed no pull request number: ${number}"
[[ ${head} == "${branch}" ]] || refuse "pull request ${number} is the pull request of ${head}, not of the current branch ${branch}"
[[ ${state} == OPEN ]] || refuse "pull request ${number} is ${state}, not OPEN"

current=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pr-body-edit.XXXXXX") || fail 'mktemp failed'
trap 'rm -f "${current}"' EXIT
gh_bounded pr view "${number}" --json body --jq .body > "${current}" || fail "cannot read the body of pull request ${number}"
old_markers=$(lines_matching "${unit_line}" "${current}") || fail "cannot read ${current}"
if [[ -n ${old_markers} && ${old_markers} != *$'\n'* && ${old_markers#Program-Unit: } != "${marker}" ]]; then
    refuse "the current body names ${old_markers#Program-Unit: }; an edit keeps the program and the unit (the new body names ${marker})"
fi
kept=$(lines_matching "^## |${footer_re}" "${current}") || fail "cannot read ${current}"
new_lines=$(lines_matching '' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ -n ${line} ]] || continue
    grep -Fxq -- "${line}" <<< "${new_lines}" || refuse "the new body drops the line of the current body: ${line}"
done <<< "${kept}"

gh_bounded pr edit "${number}" --body-file "${body_path}" >&2 || fail "gh pr edit ${number} failed"
if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
    digest=$(sha256sum < "${body_path}") || fail "the body was pushed; cannot hash ${body_path} for the report"
else
    digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${body_path}") || fail "the body was pushed; cannot hash ${body_path} for the report"
fi
echo "edited pr=${number} branch=${branch} program=${program} unit=${unit} sha256=${digest%% *}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-close.sh
# @brief Close the pull requests a clean-up table marks `close:`, with the row's text as the comment.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed only in the form
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table *` by `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). The table is a table the orchestrator
#   wrote: a regular file (not a symlink) whose real path is `<store>/handouts/<file>` of one program store, the
#   store chosen by one rule with two forms (regime-cutover U216, store move 2 of 5, handoff/07-store-move-design.md):
#   the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` when that directory exists, the root being the fixed derivation
#   `<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>` the sourced `regime-env` exports (U215); else, until U221 moves
#   the live store of this program there and removes the form, the checkout's own store
#   `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>` of the main checkout, where the orchestrator seat runs (the
#   pre-move form; `store_resolve`, which prints the form chosen on stderr; a table in the other form is refused
#   naming both). A linked worktree, a worker's clone, is refused. The lever reads its `## Open pull requests` section,
#   whose header row must be `| PR | branch | opened | files | title | default |`; every row must carry a `#<n>`
#   PR cell and a backticked branch cell, else the whole table is refused before any `gh` call. The selected rows
#   are those whose `default` cell starts with `close:`; `--only <pr>` narrows them to that one row and is refused
#   when the table has no such `close:` row. Then, per row, read-only: `gh pr view <n>` must report `OPEN` and the
#   table's branch as `headRefName`, and `gh pr list --state open --head <branch>` must list no other pull
#   request (#396 and #412 share `tools/anthropic-auth-route-structured`); a row failing that is refused with its
#   own line. A failed `gh` read aborts the run before any close. Only then does each remaining row get
#   `gh pr close <n> --comment <default cell>`. The lever never passes `--delete-branch` (closing one of two pull
#   requests on a shared branch that way would close the other) and never deletes a branch. Each `gh` call is
#   bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @option --from-table <file> The clean-up table.
# @option --only <pr> Close only this row.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One line per selected row, `closed pr=<n> branch=<b>` or `refused pr=<n> reason=<why>`, then
#   `summary closed=<n> refused=<n>`.
# @exitcode 0 Every selected row was closed.
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` read failed (nothing was closed) or a close failed (the lines say which were closed).
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the table's path or shape, no selected row, or at least one row refused (its line
#   says why; the other rows were closed).
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover/handouts/cleanup-table.md
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover/handouts/cleanup-table.md --only 378
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table ~/.local/state/regime-store/dotfiles/regime-cutover/handouts/cleanup-table.md
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33, U216).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

# The store root (regime-cutover U216): the program stores lie under `REGIME_STORE_ROOT`, the root the sourced
# regime-env derives from the physical HOME and this checkout's slug (U215) and holds component by component; the
# helper is sourced from the directory this lever runs from and self-checked like a lever (U33), so a rewritten copy
# stops this lever. The call that derives the root comes after this lever's own checkout checks, below.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || {
    echo "pr-close.sh: refused: regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"

lever='pr-close.sh'
usage='usage: pr-close.sh --from-table <table.md> [--only <pr>]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
header='| PR | branch | opened | files | title | default |'
# The `## Open pull requests` rows as `<pr>\t<branch>\t<default>`; exit 3 for a missing section or header, 4 for a
# row without a `#<n>` PR cell or a backticked branch cell. `\|` inside a cell is text, not a separator.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # awk source, not shell
table_awk='
function trim(s) { sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", s); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
/^## / { if (in_section) { done = 1 } in_section = ($0 == "## Open pull requests"); next }
!in_section || done { next }
/^[ \t]*$/ { if (rows) { done = 1 } next }
!seen_header { if ($0 != header) { exit 3 } seen_header = 1; next }
/^\|( *:?-+:? *\|)+ *$/ { next }
{
    line = $0
    gsub(/\\\|/, "\001", line)
    n = split(line, cell, "|")
    if (n != 8 || trim(cell[1]) != "" || trim(cell[8]) != "") { exit 4 }
    pr = trim(cell[2]); branch = trim(cell[3]); text = trim(cell[7])
    gsub(/\001/, "|", text); gsub(/\t/, " ", text)
    if (pr !~ /^#[1-9][0-9]*$/ || branch !~ /^`[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]+`$/) { exit 4 }
    rows++
    print substr(pr, 2) "\t" substr(branch, 2, length(branch) - 2) "\t" text
}
END { if (!seen_header) { exit 3 } }
'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Choose the program store this lever reads (regime-cutover U216, store move 2 of 5,
#   handoff/07-store-move-design.md; U215 gave regime-env the root): the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>`
#   when that directory exists, the root being the fixed derivation `<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>`
#   the sourced regime-env exports after holding every component of it; else the pre-move form
#   `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`, this main checkout's own store, which stands until U221 moves the
#   live store of this program to the root and removes this form. One rule, two forms: while the derived store exists
#   the checkout form is refused (the caller refuses a path naming it, naming both forms), and while it does not the
#   checkout form is read as before U216. The per-component holds of the chain walk (U71) stay and apply to the form
#   chosen: a symbolic link at `<root>/<program>` is refused by name before anything is read through it, an entry
#   there that is not a directory of this user is refused by name, and only an absent one falls through to the
#   checkout chain, whose three components are each a directory of this user and no symlink. The root's own
#   components are held by regime-env (`regime_store_root`). Nothing is written. The form chosen is printed once on
#   stderr (`store: derived <dir>`, or `store: checkout <dir> (pre-move form, removed by U221)`), the line the
#   coordinator reads after the deploy. The same text stands in pr-merge.sh (two levers, standing order 36: no helper
#   file).
# @arg $1 string The program name.
# @set store The chosen store, `pwd -P` form (the root and the toplevel are both physical).
# @set store_form `derived` or `checkout`.
# @set store_derived The derived candidate `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>`.
# @set store_checkout The checkout candidate `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`.
store_resolve() {
    local program=$1 path part
    [[ -n ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT:-} ]] ||
        refuse "regime-env derived no store root for ${toplevel}; the program store is judged under it (U216)"
    store_derived=${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/${program}
    store_checkout=${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
    [[ ! -L ${store_derived} ]] ||
        refuse "${store_derived} is a symlink; the derived program store is a plain directory of this user under the store root ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}, and nothing is read through a link"
    if [[ -e ${store_derived} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${store_derived} && -O ${store_derived} ]] ||
            refuse "${store_derived} exists but is not a directory of this user; the derived program store under ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT} is read only as one"
        store=${store_derived}
        store_form=derived
        echo "${lever}: store: derived ${store}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    path=${toplevel}
    for part in .orchestration orchestrate "${program}"; do
        path=${path}/${part}
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
            refuse "${path} is not a directory of this user (a symlink or a missing store); no derived store ${store_derived} exists, so ${lever} reads only the checkout's own store (the pre-move form, until U221)"
    done
    store=${store_checkout}
    store_form=checkout
    echo "${lever}: store: checkout ${store} (pre-move form, removed by U221)" >&2
}

table=''
only=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --from-table)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        table=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    --only)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        only=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
done
[[ -n ${table} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ -z ${only} || ${only} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "--only is not a decimal number: ${only}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
git_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"

# bound form would stop every run on this host); the collision refusal (an `origin` naming another checkout) and
# every store-root hold stay. The helper's refusal (return 1) is this lever's refusal status, exit 2.
regime_env pr-close.sh --unbound-ok || exit 2

case ${table} in
*/*) table_dir=${table%/*} ;;
*) table_dir=. ;;
esac
[[ -n ${table_dir} ]] || table_dir=/
table_dir=$(cd "${table_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${table}"
# U216: the table lies in `<store>/handouts/` of one program store, the store store_resolve chooses for the program

"${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}"/*/handouts) store_parent=${REGIME_STORE_ROOT} ;;
"${toplevel}"/.orchestration/orchestrate/*/handouts) store_parent=${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate ;;
*) refuse "the table is not under ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>/handouts/ (the derived store, U216) or ${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/handouts/ (the pre-move form, until U221): ${table_dir}" ;;
esac
program=${table_dir#"${store_parent}"/}
program=${program%/handouts}
[[ ${program} =~ ${program_re} ]] || refuse "the program component of ${table_dir} is outside ${program_re}"
store_resolve "${program}"
[[ ${store_parent}/${program} == "${store}" ]] || { # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms (the physical root and toplevel)
    case ${store_form} in
    derived) refuse "the table ${table} lies in the checkout store ${store_checkout}/handouts/, the pre-move form, but the derived store ${store} exists and is the program's store (U216); the checkout form is refused while it exists, until U221 removes it" ;;
    *) refuse "the table ${table} lies in ${store_parent}/${program}/handouts/, which is not the program's store ${store} (no derived store ${store_derived} exists, so the pre-move checkout form stands until U221)" ;;

status=0
rows=$(awk -v header="${header}" "${table_awk}" "${table_dir}/${table##*/}") || status=$?
case ${status} in
0) ;;
3) refuse "no '## Open pull requests' section with the header ${header} in ${table}" ;;
4) refuse "a row of '## Open pull requests' in ${table} has no #<n> PR cell or backticked branch cell" ;;
*) refuse "cannot read ${table} (awk exited ${status})" ;;
esac

selected=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text; do
    [[ -n ${pr} && ${text} == close:* ]] || continue
    [[ -z ${only} || ${pr} == "${only}" ]] || continue
    selected+=("${pr}"$'\t'"${branch}"$'\t'"${text}")
done <<< "${rows}"
if ((${#selected[@]} == 0)); then
    [[ -n ${only} ]] && refuse "the table has no close: row for pull request ${only}"
    refuse "the table has no row whose default starts with close:"
fi

closable=()
refused=0
for row in "${selected[@]}"; do
    IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text <<< "${row}"
    view=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,headRefName --jq '[.state, .headRefName] | @tsv') ||
        fail "cannot read pull request ${pr}; nothing was closed"
    IFS=$'\t' read -r state head <<< "${view}"
    if [[ ${state} != OPEN ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=state ${state:-unreadable}, not OPEN"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    if [[ ${head} != "${branch}" ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=head branch ${head} is not the table's ${branch}"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    sharing=$(gh_bounded pr list --state open --head "${branch}" --json number --jq '[.[].number | tostring] | join(",")') ||
        fail "cannot list the open pull requests of ${branch}; nothing was closed"
    if [[ ${sharing} != "${pr}" ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=branch ${branch} is the head of open pull requests ${sharing:-none}"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    closable+=("${row}")
done

closed=0
for row in ${closable[@]+"${closable[@]}"}; do
    IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text <<< "${row}"
    gh_bounded pr close "${pr}" --comment "${text}" >&2 || {
        echo "summary closed=${closed} refused=${refused}"
        fail "gh pr close ${pr} failed after ${closed} closed"
    }
    echo "closed pr=${pr} branch=${branch}"
    closed=$((closed + 1))
done
echo "summary closed=${closed} refused=${refused}"
((refused == 0)) || exit 2

#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the

# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {

    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.

    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;

        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2

    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}

    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2

    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2

        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }

    rest=${row#*$'\t'}
    audited_unit=${rest%%$'\t'*}
    rest=${rest#*$'\t'}
    verdict=${rest%%$'\t'*}
    evidence=${rest#*$'\t'}

    rest=${rest#*$'\t'}

            next
        }
        NF != width { printf "line %d has %d columns, not %d: %s\n", NR, NF, width, $0; exit 4 }
        {
            for (i = 1; i <= required; i++) {
                if ($(column[i]) == "") { printf "line %d: column %d (%s) is empty: %s\n", NR, column[i], name[column[i]], $0; exit 4 }
            }
            print
        }
        END { if (NR == 0) exit 3 }
    ' "$1") || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0) printf '%s' "${out}" ;;
    3) refuse "$1 does not start with the header (${2//$'\t'/ }); line 1: ${out##*$'\n'}" ;;
    4) refuse "$1 ${out##*$'\n'}" ;;
    *) fail "cannot read $1" ;;
    esac
}

# @description Succeed when the store's `units.tsv` has a row whose `id` is $1. The table is read once per run and
#   checked as every table is (its header, each row's column count, a non-empty `id`); a symlink or a missing file is
#   a refusal naming it and a failed read exits 1 (standing order 21), never "no row". The cache and its flag are
#   locals of require_dispositions, assigned empty there before this function runs (U119 round 6, audit of 4f9f958a):
#   a `units_rows` the caller exported was taken as the table already read, so a row it held passed the lookup
#   without being in `units.tsv`. Nothing this function reads comes from outside this run.
# @arg $1 string The unit id.
# @set units_rows The table's data rows, read once; the caller's local.
# @set units_read Non-empty once `units_rows` holds the table; the caller's local.
# @exitcode 0 Found. 1 Not found.
unit_row_exists() {
    local row
    if [[ -z ${units_read} ]]; then
        [[ ! -L ${units_file} && -f ${units_file} && -O ${units_file} ]] ||
            refuse "${units_file} is not a regular file of this user (a symlink or missing); a residual's unit is judged against it"
        units_rows=$(table_rows "${units_file}" "${units_header}" '1') || exit $?
        units_read=1
    fi
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        [[ ${row%%$'\t'*} == "$1" ]] && return 0
    done <<< "${units_rows}"
    return 1
}

# @description Set `priority`, `path` and `lineno` from a pending entry of require_dispositions (U119 round 5),
#   `<priority>\t<path>\t<lineno>`, by parameter expansion and no `IFS` write: the fields are the lever's own matched
#   text (finding_re), so none is empty and the path holds no tab.
# @arg $1 string The entry.
# @set priority path lineno The three fields.
pending_fields() {
    priority=${1%%$'\t'*}
    lineno=${1##*$'\t'}
    path=${1#*$'\t'}
    path=${path%$'\t'*}
}

# @description Refuse unless every P2 and P3 finding of the head's verdict file in the store has a holding `residual`
#   row in `dispositions.tsv` (U119 round 2): the ledger row says `correct`, and since standing order 35 `correct` no
#   longer means "no finding". Every read is checked; a failed read exits 1 (standing order 21). Every name the gate
#   reads is a local assigned here before its first read, the `units.tsv` cache of unit_row_exists included, so a
#   caller's environment holds nothing the gate takes for its own data (U119 round 6).
# @arg $1 string The 40-hex head the ledger row named (the audited head).
# @arg $2 string The unit of that ledger row, which names the verdict file and the disposition rows (round 2).
# @arg $3 string The 40-hex head being merged: $1 itself under a `correct` row, the carried head under a `carried` row
#   (U180: a `fixed` row whose reference starts with this sha holds when it differs from $1).
require_dispositions() {
    local head=$1 row_unit=$2 merge_head=$3 verdicts_dir verdict_file dispositions text line section=0 seen=0 last='' n=1 satisfied status
    local findings=() pending=() rows=() cols=() entry priority frequency severity weight path lineno why residual_unit none_seen='' listed=''
    local units_rows='' units_read=''
    # The reference of a `fixed` row as the coordinator writes it: a 40-hex sha first, then prose (U180). The sha is the
    # whole first token (the end or a character outside hex after it), so a 41-hex prefix of another sha never matches.
    local fixed_reference_re='^([0-9a-f]{40})($|[^0-9a-f])'
    verdicts_dir=${store}/verdicts
    [[ ! -L ${verdicts_dir} && -d ${verdicts_dir} && -O ${verdicts_dir} ]] ||
        refuse "${verdicts_dir} is not a directory of this user (a symlink or missing); the verdict file is read from the checkout's own store"
    verdict_file=${verdicts_dir}/${row_unit}-${head:0:8}.md
    [[ ! -L ${verdict_file} && -f ${verdict_file} && -O ${verdict_file} && -r ${verdict_file} ]] ||
        refuse "${verdict_file} is not a readable regular file of this user; a merge needs the verdict file of the head, not only its ledger row"
    text=$(cat -- "${verdict_file}") || fail "cannot read ${verdict_file}"
    # Only the leading `## Findings` section is read (U119 round 4, audit of dc08660f): from the first `## Findings`
    # line to the next `## ` heading. A later `## Findings` line, in the Notes the reader copies from the model or in
    # a rationale, is text, never a second list.
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line=${line%$'\r'}
        [[ -n ${line} ]] || continue
        last=${line}
        if ((seen == 0)); then
            [[ ${line} != '## Findings' ]] || seen=1 section=1
            continue
        fi
        ((section == 1)) || continue
        if [[ ${line} == '## '* ]]; then
            section=0
            continue
        fi
        findings+=("${line}")
    done <<< "${text}"
    ((seen == 1)) ||
        refuse "${verdict_file} has no '## Findings' section; the gate reads the verdict.md pr-audit.sh writes (a '## Findings' list of '- P<n> (<confidence>) [f<n> s<n>] <path>:<line>: <rationale>' or '- none', then 'Blocking: <n>', 'Filed: <n>' and the last line 'Verdict: <value>'); a verdict of the retired omp-run.sh audit route has no such section and no merge head has one"
    [[ ${last} == 'Verdict: correct' ]] ||
        refuse "the last line of ${verdict_file} is not 'Verdict: correct' although the ledger row for ${head} is: ${last}"
    ((${#findings[@]} > 0)) || refuse "${verdict_file}: the Findings section lists nothing; ${findings_grammar}"
    for entry in ${findings[@]+"${findings[@]}"}; do
        if [[ ${entry} == '- none' ]]; then
            [[ -z ${none_seen} ]] || refuse "${verdict_file}: the Findings section lists '- none' more than once; ${findings_grammar}"
            none_seen=1
            continue
        fi
        listed=1
        [[ ${entry} =~ ${finding_re} ]] ||
            refuse "${verdict_file}: a Findings line is not '- P<n> (<confidence>) [f<n> s<n>] <path>:<line>: <rationale>' with a path free of colons and whitespace, the first such token (the reader writes the frequency and severity scores since U125; a line without them is the unscored reader's, whose verdicts belong to merged units, never to a merge head): ${entry}"
        priority=${BASH_REMATCH[1]} frequency=${BASH_REMATCH[3]} severity=${BASH_REMATCH[4]} path=${BASH_REMATCH[5]} lineno=${BASH_REMATCH[6]}
        [[ ${frequency} =~ ${score_re} ]] ||
            refuse "${verdict_file}: a Findings line's frequency score 'f${frequency}' is not one of 1 to 10, so its weight cannot be read: ${entry}"
        [[ ${severity} =~ ${score_re} ]] ||
            refuse "${verdict_file}: a Findings line's severity score 's${severity}' is not one of 1 to 10, so its weight cannot be read: ${entry}"
        # Both scores matched score_re, so the product is arithmetic on two small decimals the gate itself read.
        weight=$((frequency * severity))
        case ${priority} in
        P0 | P1)
            ((weight < WEIGHT_THRESHOLD)) ||
                refuse "${verdict_file} lists ${priority} at ${path}:${lineno} under a correct ledger row with weight ${weight} (f${frequency} s${severity}); a P0 or P1 of weight ${WEIGHT_THRESHOLD} or more blocks (standing order 35, the AGENTS.md Audit rule), so the row or the file is wrong"
            ;;
        esac
        # Under the threshold the finding is filed (U125): reported, the code left as it is, no disposition row asked.
        ((weight >= WEIGHT_THRESHOLD)) || continue
        pending+=("${priority}"$'\t'"${path}"$'\t'"${lineno}")
    done
    [[ -z ${none_seen} || -z ${listed} ]] || refuse "${verdict_file}: the Findings section lists '- none' beside a finding line; ${findings_grammar}"
    ((${#pending[@]} > 0)) || return 0
    dispositions=${store}/dispositions.tsv
    pending_fields "${pending[0]}"
    [[ ! -L ${dispositions} && -f ${dispositions} && -O ${dispositions} && -r ${dispositions} ]] ||
        refuse "${verdict_file} lists ${priority} at ${path}:${lineno} and ${dispositions} is not a readable regular file of this user; every P2 and P3 finding of a correct verdict needs its residual row before the merge"
    # Every column of a disposition row is required, so a validated row holds no adjacent tabs and `read` splits it
    # into its eight fields; the column count and the empty-field check are awk's (table_rows), never bash's.
    text=$(table_rows "${dispositions}" "${dispositions_header}" '1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8') || exit $?
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -n ${line} ]] || continue
        n=$((n + 1))
        IFS=$'\t' read -ra cols <<< "${line}"
        case ${cols[6]} in
        residual | fixed) ;;
        *) refuse "${dispositions} line ${n}: disposition '${cols[6]}' is neither residual nor fixed" ;;
        esac
        rows+=("${line}")
    done <<< "${text}"
    for entry in ${pending[@]+"${pending[@]}"}; do
        pending_fields "${entry}"
        why="no ${dispositions} row for unit ${row_unit}, head ${head}, ${priority} at ${path}:${lineno}"
        satisfied=0
        for line in ${rows[@]+"${rows[@]}"}; do
            IFS=$'\t' read -ra cols <<< "${line}"
            [[ ${cols[1]} == "${row_unit}" && ${cols[2]} == "${head}" && ${cols[3]} == "${priority}" && ${cols[4]} == "${path}" && ${cols[5]} == "${lineno}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow the path column is matched as the text the reader wrote, never resolved
                continue
            if [[ ${cols[6]} == fixed ]]; then
                # U180: under a carried row the head being merged differs from the audited head, and a fix at a
                # carried head can only be a body fix (a code change would have changed the digest), so a `fixed`
                # row whose reference names the head being merged holds for the audited head it judges.
                if [[ ${head} != "${merge_head}" && ${cols[7]} =~ ${fixed_reference_re} ]] &&
                    [[ ${BASH_REMATCH[1]} == "${merge_head}" ]]; then
                    satisfied=1
                    break
                fi
                why="the row at ${cols[0]} says fixed in ${cols[7]}, which is not this head; merge the head that fixed it"
                continue
            fi
            [[ ${cols[7]} =~ ${residual_re} ]] || {
                why="the row at ${cols[0]} is residual but its reference is not 'unit=U<n> gate=<clause>': ${cols[7]}"
                continue
            }
            residual_unit=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
            status=0
            unit_row_exists "${residual_unit}" || status=$?
            if ((status == 0)); then
                satisfied=1
                break
            fi
            why="the row at ${cols[0]} is residual for ${residual_unit}, which is not a row of ${units_file}"
        done
        ((satisfied == 1)) ||
            refuse "${verdict_file} lists ${priority} at ${path}:${lineno} without a holding disposition: ${why}; write the residual row (unit=U<n> gate=<clause>, U<n> a units.tsv row) or fix it in a new head"
    done
}

# @description Refuse unless the ledger holds the unit's sweep row at `audited_head` (regime-cutover U147, every unit
#   since U244; the AGENTS.md Audit sweep rule: every unit and every program milestone gets one sweep of the
#   `security-audit` skill before its pull request merges). The row is asked of the checkout's ledger.py (`sweep <unit>
#   <head>`, the one reader, its status read as ledger_verdict reads it and its exit-0 answer read by its shape, `none`
#   or one row of four tab-separated fields with a ts, as require_verdict_row reads a row) at `audited_head`: the head
#   itself, or for a `carried` row the earlier head whose verdict file the merge reads, so a head moved under a
#   carried row needs no second sweep. `none` is a refusal naming the unit, the head and the rule. The row must be the
#   exact row of the rule (Codex thread 4457544811: a row written by hand with verifier `coordinator` admitted the
#   merge): the reader already refuses a `sweep` row whose pr is not `-`, whose verifier is not `security-audit-skill
#   <pin>` or whose evidence is not `sweeps/<path>.json` as a malformed store, and the lever reads the answer by its
#   shape all the same, then requires the pin word to be a prefix of the manifest's `assets.security-audit-skill.pin`
#   (sweep_pin_probe over LEVER_MANIFEST: exit 0 the pin, 2 a refusal carrying its line, anything else a failure) and
#   the findings file to be a regular file of this user under `<store>/sweeps/` (`sweeps/` a directory of this user
#   and no symlink, the file `-f`, `-O`, `! -L`, as the verdict file), never opened; a pin that is no prefix or a file
#   that is missing, a symlink or another user's is a refusal naming it. The lever reads neither the findings file the
#   row names nor the sweep's content.
require_sweep_row() {
    local status=0 row rest verifier evidence pin_word manifest_pin findings_path sweeps_dir findings_file
    row=$("${python}" -I -S "${ledger_reader}" "${store}" sweep "${unit}" "${audited_head}" 2>&1) || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0) ;;
    2) refuse "${row#ledger: }" ;;
    *) fail "${ledger_reader} exited ${status} reading ${ledger} for the sweep row of ${unit}: ${row:-no output}" ;;
    esac
    [[ ${row} != none ]] ||
        refuse "${ledger} has no sweep row for ${unit} (or a fix unit of it) at the audited head ${audited_head}; the AGENTS.md Audit sweep rule says every unit and every program milestone gets one sweep of the security-audit skill before its pull request merges (a row with verdict sweep, pr -, head ${audited_head}); run the sweep and write its row, or wait for it"
    # The answer is read by its shape, as require_verdict_row reads a row (round 2, finding 3): one line of four
    # tab-separated fields, `<ts> <unit> <verifier> <evidence>`, with a ts. The tab count is the row with every other
    # byte removed, read as a word; the ts is the text before the first tab.
    case ${row//[!$'\t']/} in
    $'\t\t\t') ;;
    *) refuse "${ledger_reader} answered the sweep question for ${unit} at ${audited_head} with neither none nor one row of four tab-separated fields (ts, unit, verifier, evidence): ${row:-nothing}" ;;
    esac
    [[ ${row} != *$'\n'* && -n ${row%%$'\t'*} ]] ||
        refuse "${ledger_reader} answered the sweep question for ${unit} at ${audited_head} with text beside the row or an empty ts, not one row of four tab-separated fields: ${row}"
    # The row's columns as the reader prints them (ts, unit, verifier, evidence), each the text up to the next tab.
    rest=${row#*$'\t'}
    rest=${rest#*$'\t'}
    verifier=${rest%%$'\t'*}
    evidence=${rest#*$'\t'}
    # The verifier's two words are the skill's name and the pin word the sweep ran at (round 4): the reader refuses any
    # other sweep row, and the lever reads the answer by its shape all the same before it compares the pin.
    case ${verifier} in
    'security-audit-skill '*) ;;
    *) refuse "the sweep row of ${unit} at ${audited_head} names '${verifier}' as its verifier, not the pinned skill and its pin (security-audit-skill <pin>); the gate admits the row the AGENTS.md Audit sweep rule defines alone" ;;
    esac
    pin_word=${verifier#security-audit-skill }
    pin_word=${pin_word%%[[:space:]]*}
    [[ ${pin_word} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{8,}$ ]] ||
        refuse "the sweep row of ${unit} at ${audited_head} names '${pin_word}' as the skill's pin, not 8 or more lowercase hex characters of it"
    status=0
    manifest_pin=$("${python}" -I -S -c "${sweep_pin_probe}" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}" 2>&1) || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0) ;;
    2) refuse "${manifest_pin#manifest: }; the sweep row's pin is compared with that pin, so a manifest without it admits no sweep" ;;
    *) fail "the pin probe over ${LEVER_MANIFEST} exited ${status}, neither the pin (0) nor a refusal (2): ${manifest_pin:-no output}" ;;
    esac
    [[ ${manifest_pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] ||
        refuse "the pin probe over ${LEVER_MANIFEST} answered with no 40-hex pin: ${manifest_pin:-nothing}"
    [[ ${manifest_pin} == "${pin_word}"* ]] ||
        refuse "the sweep row of ${unit} at ${audited_head} names pin ${pin_word}, which is not a prefix of the manifest's assets.security-audit-skill.pin ${manifest_pin} (${LEVER_MANIFEST}); the sweep ran at another pin than the one the manifest pins, or the row was written by hand"
    # The findings file is the evidence's first `;`-separated field stripped of whitespace, a relative path under
    # `sweeps/` ending in `.json` with no `..`, `.` or empty component, checked as the verdict file is (the directory,
    # then the file: regular, this user's, no symlink) and never opened.
    findings_path=${evidence%%;*}
    findings_path=${findings_path#"${findings_path%%[![:space:]]*}"}
    findings_path=${findings_path%"${findings_path##*[![:space:]]}"}
    case ${findings_path} in # lint-comparisons: allow the row's store-relative path is judged as the text it is, then the file is stat'ed under the store
    sweeps/*.json) ;;
    *) refuse "the sweep row of ${unit} at ${audited_head} names '${evidence}' as its evidence, not a findings file sweeps/<path>.json under the store" ;;
    esac
    case /${findings_path}/ in # lint-comparisons: allow the same text, its components fenced by slashes
    */../* | */./* | *//*) refuse "the findings file ${findings_path} of the sweep row of ${unit} at ${audited_head} has a '..', '.' or empty path component; the file is read under the store alone" ;;
    esac
    sweeps_dir=${store}/sweeps
    [[ ! -L ${sweeps_dir} && -d ${sweeps_dir} && -O ${sweeps_dir} ]] ||
        refuse "${sweeps_dir} is not a directory of this user (a symlink or missing); the findings file a sweep row names must be in the checkout's own store"
    findings_file=${store}/${findings_path}
    [[ ! -L ${findings_file} && -f ${findings_file} && -O ${findings_file} ]] ||
        refuse "${findings_file}, the findings file the sweep row of ${unit} at ${audited_head} names, is not a regular file of this user (a symlink or missing); a sweep whose findings file is not in the store admits no merge"
}

# @description Choose the program store this lever reads (regime-cutover U216, store move 2 of 5,
#   handoff/07-store-move-design.md; U215 gave regime-env the root): the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>`
#   when that directory exists, the root being the fixed derivation `<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>`
#   the sourced regime-env exports after holding every component of it; else the pre-move form
#   `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`, this main checkout's own store, which stands until U221 moves the
#   live store of this program to the root and removes this form. One rule, two forms: while the derived store exists
#   the checkout form is refused (the caller refuses a path naming it, naming both forms), and while it does not the
#   checkout form is read as before U216. The per-component holds of the chain walk (U71) stay and apply to the form
#   chosen: a symbolic link at `<root>/<program>` is refused by name before anything is read through it, an entry
#   there that is not a directory of this user is refused by name, and only an absent one falls through to the
#   checkout chain, whose three components are each a directory of this user and no symlink. The root's own
#   components are held by regime-env (`regime_store_root`). Nothing is written. The form chosen is printed once on
#   stderr (`store: derived <dir>`, or `store: checkout <dir> (pre-move form, removed by U221)`), the line the
#   coordinator reads after the deploy. The same text stands in pr-close.sh (two levers, standing order 36: no helper
#   file).
# @arg $1 string The program name.
# @set store The chosen store, `pwd -P` form (the root and the toplevel are both physical).
# @set store_form `derived` or `checkout`.
# @set store_derived The derived candidate `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>`.
# @set store_checkout The checkout candidate `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`.
store_resolve() {
    local program=$1 path part
    [[ -n ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT:-} ]] ||
        refuse "regime-env derived no store root for ${toplevel}; the program store is judged under it (U216)"
    store_derived=${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/${program}
    store_checkout=${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
    [[ ! -L ${store_derived} ]] ||
        refuse "${store_derived} is a symlink; the derived program store is a plain directory of this user under the store root ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}, and nothing is read through a link"
    if [[ -e ${store_derived} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${store_derived} && -O ${store_derived} ]] ||
            refuse "${store_derived} exists but is not a directory of this user; the derived program store under ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT} is read only as one"
        store=${store_derived}
        store_form=derived
        echo "${lever}: store: derived ${store}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    path=${toplevel}
    for part in .orchestration orchestrate "${program}"; do
        path=${path}/${part}
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
            refuse "${path} is not a directory of this user (a symlink or a missing store); no derived store ${store_derived} exists, so ${lever} reads only the checkout's own store (the pre-move form, until U221)"
    done
    store=${store_checkout}
    store_form=checkout
    echo "${lever}: store: checkout ${store} (pre-move form, removed by U221)" >&2
}

# @description Set `ledger`, `store`, `units_file` and `unit` to the one store the merge may read (U71, bot P1
#   4370212009: a caller-chosen ledger.tsv could hold a fabricated row): the store `store_resolve` chooses for
#   `<program>` (U216: the derived store under `REGIME_STORE_ROOT` when it exists, else this main checkout's own
#   store, the pre-move form), `<program>` and `U<n>` taken from the pull request body's one
#   `Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>` line. No directory of the chosen chain and not the ledger is a symlink, each is
#   owned by this user, and `--records` must resolve (`pwd -P`) to exactly that directory: one that names the other
#   form is refused naming both forms, one outside the checkout while the checkout form stands is named as such, and
#   anything else is refused as not the program's store.
# @set ledger The canonical ledger path.
# @set store The canonical store directory.
# @set units_file The store's `units.tsv`, read by unit_row_exists.
# @set unit The body's unit id; a ledger row for the pull request must be it or a `U<n>[a-z]` fix unit of it, and the row's unit names the verdict file (require_verdict_row).
resolve_store() {
    local body markers line program given
    body=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json body --jq .body) || fail "cannot read the body of pull request ${pr}"
    markers=''
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line=${line%$'\r'}
        [[ ${line} == Program-Unit:* ]] && markers+="${line}"$'\n'
    done <<< "${body}"
    markers=${markers%$'\n'}
    [[ -n ${markers} && ${markers} != *$'\n'* && ${markers} =~ ${program_unit_re} ]] ||
        refuse "the body of pull request ${pr} must hold exactly one line 'Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>'; it holds: ${markers:-none}"
    program=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
    unit=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
    store_resolve "${program}"
    given=$(cd "${records}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || refuse "--records ${records} is no directory"
    if [[ ${given} != "${store}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms (the root and the toplevel are physical)
        case ${store_form} in
        derived)
            [[ ${given} != "${store_checkout}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
                refuse "--records ${records} resolves to the checkout store ${given}, the pre-move form, but the derived store ${store} exists and is the program's store (U216); the checkout form is refused while it exists, until U221 removes it"
            ;;
        *)
            [[ ${given} == "${toplevel}/"* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
                refuse "--records ${records} resolves to ${given}, outside the checkout ${toplevel}; no derived store ${store_derived} exists, so the merge reads only the checkout's own store (the pre-move form, until U221)"
            ;;
        esac
        refuse "--records ${records} is not the program's store ${store} (named by the body's Program-Unit line; the ${store_form} form)"
    fi
    ledger=${store}/ledger.tsv
    units_file=${store}/units.tsv
    [[ -f ${ledger} && ! -L ${ledger} && -O ${ledger} && -r ${ledger} ]] ||
        refuse "${ledger} is not a readable regular file of this user"
}

[[ $# -ge 1 ]] || refuse "${usage}"
pr=$1
shift
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"
[[ $# -eq 2 && $1 == --records && -n $2 ]] || refuse "${usage}"
records=$2
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
python=$(command -v python3) || refuse 'no python3 found (it runs the ledger reader, scripts/orchestrator/ledger.py)'
# The checkout the lever runs in, by its physical path, and it must be the main checkout: a linked worktree (a
# worker's clone) holds a copy of the store that is not the orchestrator's record (U71, bot P1 4370212009).
toplevel=$(git_isolated rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'run from the repository checkout that holds the program store'
[[ -n ${toplevel} && -d ${toplevel} ]] || refuse 'run from the repository checkout that holds the program store'
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
git_dir=$(git_isolated -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git_isolated -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) ||
    refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree; run from the main checkout, where the orchestrator keeps its store"
# U216: regime-env derives `REGIME_STORE_ROOT` for this checkout (its own refusals name this lever). This lever reads
# nothing in the hcom store, so the store's `origin` binding is not asked of it (`--unbound-ok`; the dotfiles program
# runs on the pre-U33 store pair and its derived hcom store `~/.local/state/hcom/dotfiles` carries no `origin`, so the
# bound form would stop every merge on this host); the collision refusal (an `origin` naming another checkout) and
# every store-root hold stay. The helper's refusal (return 1) is this lever's refusal status, exit 2.
regime_env pr-merge.sh --unbound-ok || exit 2
# The one reader of the ledger (U122 round 6), run from the checkout the store is in, as pr-audit.sh runs the
# checkout's rounds-check.py and audit-carry.py; the lever's awk reader is gone with it.
ledger_reader=${toplevel}/scripts/orchestrator/ledger.py
[[ -f ${ledger_reader} ]] || refuse "no ${ledger_reader} in the checkout; the ledger is read through it alone"

view=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid,isDraft \
    --jq '[.state, .baseRefName, .headRefOid, (.isDraft | tostring)] | @tsv') || fail "cannot read pull request ${pr}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r state base head draft <<< "${view}"
[[ ${state} == OPEN ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} is ${state:-unreadable}, not OPEN"
[[ ${base} == main ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} targets ${base:-nothing}, not main"
[[ ${draft} == false ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} is a draft (isDraft=${draft:-unreadable})"

require_dispositions "${audited_head}" "${audited_unit}" "${head}"

checks=$(gh_bounded pr checks "${pr}" --json bucket,name --jq '.[] | [.bucket, .name] | @tsv') || status=$?

# and a pull request retargeted from main with the same head would otherwise merge into the new base.
again=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json headRefOid,baseRefName --jq '[.headRefOid, .baseRefName] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read the head and base of ${pr} again"
IFS=$'\t' read -r again again_base <<< "${again}"
[[ ${again} == "${head}" ]] || refuse "the head of pull request ${pr} moved from ${head} to ${again:-unreadable} during the checks"
[[ ${again_base} == main ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} was retargeted from main to ${again_base:-unreadable} during the checks"
[[ -n ${checks} ]] || {
    ((status == 0)) && refuse "no check is reported on the head ${head}"
    fail "gh pr checks ${pr} failed (exit ${status}) and printed nothing"
}
red=''
while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket name; do
    case ${bucket} in
    pass | skipping) ;;
    *) red+="${red:+, }${name}=${bucket}" ;;
    esac
done <<< "${checks}"
[[ -z ${red} ]] || refuse "CI is not green on the head ${head}: ${red}"
# The named checks (U330): every REQUIRED_CHECKS name must be listed with bucket `pass`. The listing is scanned once
# per required name and the name compared whole (a check whose name only starts with a required one is no result for
# it); a name listed twice is `pass` only when every line of it is, so `skipping` beside `pass` is no result either.
# An absent required name is named bare, one listed with another bucket with that bucket, so the refusal tells a
# workflow that never ran from a job that skipped. Every listed check is `pass` or `skipping` here (the red check
# above), so a required check that is not `pass` is `skipping`.
missing=''
for required in "${REQUIRED_CHECKS[@]}"; do
    found=''
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket name; do
        [[ ${name} == "${required}" ]] || continue
        case ${bucket} in
        pass) [[ -n ${found} ]] || found=pass ;;
        *) found=${bucket} ;;
        esac
    done <<< "${checks}"
    [[ ${found} == pass ]] || missing+="${missing:+, }${required}${found:+=${found}}"
done
[[ -z ${missing} ]] ||
    refuse "CI has no result for: ${missing}; every check of REQUIRED_CHECKS (the main ruleset's required contexts) must pass on the head ${head}, and a pull request whose pull_request workflows never ran (a conflict with main) lists none of them"
((status == 0)) || fail "gh pr checks ${pr} exited ${status} although every listed check passed"

merge_status=0
gh_bounded pr merge "${pr}" --squash --match-head-commit "${head}" >&2 || merge_status=$?
after=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,mergeCommit,baseRefName,headRefOid \
    --jq '[.state, (.mergeCommit.oid // ""), .baseRefName, .headRefOid] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read pull request ${pr} after the merge command (exit ${merge_status}); read it before anything else"
IFS=$'\t' read -r state commit merged_base merged_head <<< "${after}"
[[ ${state} == MERGED && ${commit} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] ||
    fail "pull request ${pr} is ${state:-unreadable} after the merge command (exit ${merge_status})"
# A merge this lever did not make (U71 audit round 9): when the pinned merge failed and someone else merged a later
# head, MERGED alone would credit the audited head with that merge, so the merged head must be the audited one.
[[ ${merged_head} == "${head}" ]] ||
    fail "pull request ${pr} merged at head ${merged_head:-unreadable} as ${commit}, not at the audited head ${head} (merge command exit ${merge_status}); that merge is not this verdict's; tell the operator"
# gh pr merge takes no base (`gh pr merge --help`), so a retarget between the second read and the merge call is
# reported here, loudly, with the base it landed on; it cannot be undone by the lever.
[[ ${merged_base} == main ]] ||
    fail "pull request ${pr} merged into ${merged_base:-an unreadable base}, not main: it was retargeted after the last read; tell the operator"
((merge_status == 0)) || echo "${lever}: the merge command exited ${merge_status}, but the pull request is MERGED" >&2
echo "merged pr=${pr} head=${head} commit=${commit} verdict=${verdict_ts}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-thread-reply.sh
# @brief Reply to one review thread of a pull request with a disposition, the orchestrator seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed by the row
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-thread-reply.sh *` of `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). Every argument is checked before the
#   first `gh` call, and the one write is
#   `gh api -X POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<pr>/comments/<comment-id>/replies -F body=@<file>`.
#   `<pr>` and `<comment-id>` are decimal. The body file is a regular file (not a symlink) of 1 to 65536 bytes
#   whose real path is inside `$TMPDIR` or the checkout's `.orchestration/` (the program's store), so no other
#   file of the account can be posted. Its first line is a disposition of `preferences.md` standing order 22:
#   `fixed: <40-hex sha>`, `refuted: <text citing a URL or a file:line>`, `residual: unit=U<n> gate=<clause>`,
#   `residual: operator=<decisions.tsv ts>` or `filed: f=<n> s=<n> <reason>` (two decimal scores and a reason,
#   regime-cutover U124); `pr-threads-check.sh` reads the same grammar and judges the values. `<owner>/<repo>`
#   comes from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`, never from an argument. The comment must be a review comment
#   of that pull request (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/comments/<comment-id>`, its `pull_request_url`
#   ends in `/pulls/<pr>`) and the first comment of its thread (no `in_reply_to_id`), since GitHub takes a reply
#   only to that one. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @arg $2 int The id of the thread's first review comment (`databaseId`, the `#discussion_r<id>` anchor).
# @option --body-file <file> The reply text.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `replied pr=<pr> comment=<id> reply=<new id> url=<html url>`.
# @exitcode 0 The reply was posted.
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` read or the write failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the body file, the disposition, or a comment that is not the thread's first on <pr>.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-thread-reply.sh 480 4365170609 --body-file "$TMPDIR/reply.md"
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='pr-thread-reply.sh'
usage='usage: pr-thread-reply.sh <pr> <comment-id> --body-file <file>'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Succeed when $1, a reply's first line, is a disposition (`preferences.md` standing order 22).
# @arg $1 string The line.
disposition_line() {
    local fixed='^fixed: [0-9a-f]{40}( |$)'
    local refuted='^refuted: .*(https://[^[:space:]]+|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*:[0-9]+)'
    local unit='^residual: unit=U[0-9]+[a-z]? gate=[^[:space:]]'
    local operator='^residual: operator=[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$'
    local filed='^filed: f=[0-9]+ s=[0-9]+ [^[:space:]]'
    [[ $1 =~ ${fixed} || $1 =~ ${refuted} || $1 =~ ${unit} || $1 =~ ${operator} || $1 =~ ${filed} ]]
}

# @description Refuse unless $1 is a regular file of 1 to 65536 bytes inside $TMPDIR or <toplevel>/.orchestration.
# @arg $1 path The body file.
# @set body_path Its real path.
body_file_check() {
    local file=$1 dir root size
    [[ -f ${file} && ! -L ${file} ]] || refuse "the body file is not a regular file: ${file}"
    case ${file} in # lint-comparisons: allow splits the argument at its last slash; the real path is compared below
    */*) dir=${file%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${file}"
    body_path=${dir}/${file##*/}
    size=$(wc -c < "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
    size=${size//[[:space:]]/}
    if ! [[ ${size} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ((size == 0 || size > 65536)); then
        refuse "the body file must hold 1 to 65536 bytes: ${body_path}"
    fi
    for root in "${TMPDIR:-}" "${toplevel}/.orchestration"; do
        [[ -n ${root} && -d ${root} ]] || continue
        root=$(cd "${root}" && pwd -P) || continue
        [[ ${body_path} == "${root}"/* ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    done
    refuse "the body file is outside \$TMPDIR and the checkout's .orchestration/: ${body_path}"
}

[[ $# -eq 4 && $3 == --body-file ]] || refuse "${usage}"
pr=$1
comment=$2
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"
[[ ${comment} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}$ ]] || refuse "the comment id is not a decimal number: ${comment}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
body_file_check "$4"
first=$(sed -n '1{s/\r$//;p;}' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
disposition_line "${first}" ||
    refuse "the first line is not a disposition (fixed: <sha> | refuted: <doc or file:line> | residual: unit=U<n> gate=<clause> | residual: operator=<ts> | filed: f=<1..10> s=<1..10> <reason>): ${first}"

repo=$(gh_bounded repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner) || fail 'gh repo view failed'
[[ ${repo} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || fail "gh repo view printed no owner/repo: ${repo}"
owner_pr=$(gh_bounded api "repos/${repo}/pulls/comments/${comment}" \
    --jq '[(.pull_request_url | capture("/pulls/(?<n>[0-9]+)$").n), (.in_reply_to_id // 0 | tostring)] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read review comment ${comment} of ${repo}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r comment_pr reply_to <<< "${owner_pr}"
[[ ${comment_pr} == "${pr}" ]] || refuse "review comment ${comment} belongs to pull request ${comment_pr:-none}, not ${pr}"
[[ ${reply_to} == 0 ]] || refuse "review comment ${comment} is a reply (to ${reply_to}); name the thread's first comment"

posted=$(gh_bounded api -X POST "repos/${repo}/pulls/${pr}/comments/${comment}/replies" -F "body=@${body_path}" \
    --jq '[(.id | tostring), .html_url] | @tsv') || fail "the reply to ${comment} on pull request ${pr} failed"
IFS=$'\t' read -r reply url <<< "${posted}"
echo "replied pr=${pr} comment=${comment} reply=${reply} url=${url}"
