set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

# The isolated git and the environment scrub come from the library beside this script (U113): `disposition` is one
# text with pr-threads-check.sh's (U28b F1), so its ancestry and commit-date reads go through the same git.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh ]] || {
    echo "pr-thread-resolve.sh: refused: git-isolated.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh"
# shellcheck disable=SC2119 # no name is kept: every GIT_* and transport variable goes
git_env_scrub

lever='pr-thread-resolve.sh'
usage='usage: pr-thread-resolve.sh <pr> <comment-id> [--records <dir>]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
# The weighted finding rule (AGENTS.md "Audit", regime-cutover U124): a `filed:` reply holds when frequency times
# severity is under this number, the one pr-threads-check.sh names.
WEIGHT_THRESHOLD=10
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # GraphQL variables, not shell
threads_query='query($owner: String!, $name: String!, $pr: Int!) {
  repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
    pullRequest(number: $pr) {
      headRefOid
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        pageInfo { hasNextPage }
        nodes { id isResolved comments(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { databaseId createdAt body authorAssociation author { login } } } }
      }
    }
  }
}'
# `head <sha> <hasNextPage>`, then per thread `<node id> <resolved> <first id> <created epoch> <P0-P3 or -> <count>
# <newest reply's authorAssociation or -> <its author's login or -> <newest reply's first non-blank line>` (TSV; the
# reply is last because it may be empty, and `@tsv` writes a tab in it as `\t`, which `disposition` decodes; a line
# is blank when it holds no character outside whitespace, so a reply opened by an empty line is read at its text).
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq source, not shell
threads_jq='.data.repository.pullRequest
  | (["head", .headRefOid, (.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage | tostring)] | @tsv),
    (.reviewThreads.nodes[] | .comments as $c | [.id, (.isResolved | tostring),
      ($c.nodes[0].databaseId | tostring), ($c.nodes[0].createdAt | fromdateiso8601 | tostring),
      ([($c.nodes[0].body // "") | capture("!\\[P(?<p>[0-3]) Badge\\]") | "P" + .p] | first // "-"),
      ($c.totalCount | tostring),
      (($c.nodes[1:] | last) as $reply | ($reply.authorAssociation // "-"), ($reply.author.login // "-"),
        (($reply.body // "") | split("\n") | map(rtrimstr("\r")) | map(select(test("\\S"))) | (.[0] // "")))] | @tsv)'
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # GraphQL variables, not shell
resolve_mutation='mutation($thread: ID!) { resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: $thread}) { thread { id isResolved } } }'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Succeed when the TSV file $1 has a row whose first field is $2.
# @arg $1 path The file.
# @arg $2 string The key.
# @exitcode 0 Found. 1 Not found. 2 Unreadable.
has_row() {
    [[ -r $1 ]] || return 2
    ROW_KEY=$2 awk -F '\t' '$1 == ENVIRON["ROW_KEY"] { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$1" || return 1
}

# @description Print the disposition a thread's newest reply carries, or `open (<why>)`.
# @arg $1 int The created epoch of the thread's first comment.
# @arg $2 string Its severity, P0-P3 or `-`.
# @arg $3 string The `authorAssociation` of the newest reply's author (GitHub's enum), or `-` without a reply.
# @arg $4 string The newest reply's author login, or `-`.
# @arg $5 string The first non-blank line of the newest reply as the listing's `@tsv` escaped it; decoded here before
#   any read.
disposition() {
    local created=$1 severity=$2 association=$3 login=$4 line='' fix fix_time status frequency severity_score weight why
    # The associations GitHub gives a maintainer's comment (U124 round 3); a reply by anyone else closes nothing.
    local maintainer_associations='^(OWNER|MEMBER|COLLABORATOR)$'
    local fixed='^fixed: ([0-9a-f]{40})( |$)'
    local refuted='^refuted: .*(https://[^[:space:]]+|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*:[0-9]+)'
    local unit='^residual: unit=(U[0-9]+[a-z]?) gate=[^[:space:]]'
    local operator='^residual: operator=([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z)$'
    local filed='^filed: f=([^[:space:]]+) s=([^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]'
    local filed_scores='^filed: f=[^[:space:]]+ s=[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]*$'
    local score_re='^(10|[1-9])$'
    # `@tsv` wrote a tab as `\t`, a carriage return as `\r` and a backslash as `\\`, and nothing else starts with a
    # backslash in its output; `%b` reads those three back, so the regexes below see the reply's own characters and
    # a tab-only reason is whitespace, not the two characters `\t` (U124 round 3). An empty reply is left as the
    # empty string above: `printf -v` with nothing to print leaves its variable unset.
    [[ -z $5 ]] || printf -v line '%b' "$5"
    # A reply exists when the listing names its author's association (`-` without one), and its author must be a
    # maintainer whatever the reply says, a reply of blank lines alone included (U125 round d).
    if [[ ${association} != - && ! ${association} =~ ${maintainer_associations} ]]; then
        echo "open (newest reply by ${login}, association ${association}: not a maintainer)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ ${line} =~ ${fixed} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        git_isolated cat-file -e "${fix}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} is not a commit here)"
            return
        }
        status=0
        git_isolated merge-base --is-ancestor "${fix}" "${head}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) ;;
        1)
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} is not in the head)"
            return
            ;;
        *) fail "git merge-base --is-ancestor ${fix} ${head} failed" ;;
        esac
        fix_time=$(git_isolated show -s --format=%ct "${fix}") || fail "git show ${fix} failed"
        if ((fix_time < created)); then
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} predates the finding)"
            return
        fi
        echo "fixed ${fix}"
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${refuted} ]]; then
        echo refuted
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${unit} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ ${severity} == P2 || ${severity} == P3 ]] || {
            echo "open (residual: unit= is for P2 and P3; this is ${severity/-/P1 (no badge)})"
            return
        }
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check units.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/units.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual ${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no units.tsv row ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/units.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${operator} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check decisions.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/decisions.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual operator=${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no decisions.tsv row at ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/decisions.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ ${line} == filed:* ]]; then
        # The shape, then each score by its decimal string (score_re) before any arithmetic: bash evaluates a name or
        # a subscript inside `(( ))` and wraps a decimal past its range (U124 round 2: f=18446744073709551617 read as
        # 1), and the reply is text anyone with a GitHub account wrote. A refusal names the fault and quotes the line.
        why=''
        if [[ ${line} =~ ${filed} ]]; then
            frequency=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
            severity_score=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
            if ! [[ ${frequency} =~ ${score_re} ]]; then
                why="f=${frequency} is not a whole number from 1 to 10"
            elif ! [[ ${severity_score} =~ ${score_re} ]]; then
                why="s=${severity_score} is not a whole number from 1 to 10"
            fi
        elif [[ ${line} =~ ${filed_scores} ]]; then
            why='the reason is missing'
        else
            why='a score is missing'
        fi
        if [[ -n ${why} ]]; then
            echo "open (filed: reply needs f=<1..10> s=<1..10> <reason>; ${why}; got: ${line})"
            return
        fi
        weight=$((frequency * severity_score))
        ((weight < WEIGHT_THRESHOLD)) || {
            echo "open (filed: f=${frequency} s=${severity_score} weighs ${weight}, not under ${WEIGHT_THRESHOLD}; fix it, or answer refuted: or residual:)"
            return
        }
        echo "filed f=${frequency} s=${severity_score} weight=${weight}"
    elif [[ -z ${line} && ${association} == - ]]; then
        echo 'open (no reply)'
    elif [[ -z ${line} ]]; then
        echo "open (the newest reply by ${login}, association ${association}, holds no text)"
    else
        echo 'open (the newest reply is not a disposition)'
    fi
}

pr=''
comment=''
records=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --records)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        records=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    -*) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    *)
        if [[ -z ${pr} ]]; then
            pr=$1
        elif [[ -z ${comment} ]]; then
            comment=$1
        else
            refuse "${usage}"
        fi
        shift
        ;;
    esac
done
[[ -n ${pr} && -n ${comment} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"
[[ ${comment} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,19}$ ]] || refuse "the comment id is not a decimal number: ${comment}"
[[ -z ${records} || (-f ${records}/units.tsv && -f ${records}/decisions.tsv) ]] ||
    refuse "--records holds no units.tsv and decisions.tsv: ${records}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

repo=$(gh_bounded repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner) || fail 'gh repo view failed'
[[ ${repo} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || fail "gh repo view printed no owner/repo: ${repo}"
listing=$(gh_bounded api graphql -f "query=${threads_query}" -f "owner=${repo%%/*}" -f "name=${repo#*/}" \
    -F "pr=${pr}" --jq "${threads_jq}") || fail "cannot list the review threads of pull request ${pr}"

head=''
page=''
thread=''
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id resolved first created severity count association login reply; do
    if [[ ${id} == head ]]; then
        head=${resolved}
        page=${first}
    elif [[ ${first} == "${comment}" ]]; then
        thread=${id}
        thread_resolved=${resolved}
        thread_created=${created}
        thread_severity=${severity}
        thread_count=${count}
        thread_association=${association}
        thread_login=${login}
        thread_reply=${reply}
    fi
done <<< "${listing}"
[[ ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} has no readable head"
[[ ${page} == false ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} has more than 100 review threads; resolve it by hand"
[[ -n ${thread} ]] || refuse "no review thread of pull request ${pr} starts with comment ${comment}"
[[ ${thread_resolved} == false ]] || refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} is already resolved"
if ! [[ ${thread_count} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ((thread_count > 100)); then
    refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} has more than 100 comments; resolve it by hand"
fi
[[ ${thread_created} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fail "unreadable creation time for the thread of comment ${comment}"
git_isolated cat-file -e "${head}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || refuse "the head ${head} of pull request ${pr} is not a commit here; git fetch first"
state=$(disposition "${thread_created}" "${thread_severity}" "${thread_association}" "${thread_login}" "${thread_reply}") || exit $?
[[ ${state} != open* ]] ||
    refuse "the thread of comment ${comment} has no valid disposition, ${state#open }; reply with pr-thread-reply.sh first"

done_id=$(gh_bounded api graphql -f "query=${resolve_mutation}" -f "thread=${thread}" \
    --jq '.data.resolveReviewThread.thread | select(.isResolved) | .id') || fail "resolveReviewThread failed for ${thread}"
[[ ${done_id} == "${thread}" ]] || fail "resolveReviewThread did not report ${thread} resolved"
echo "resolved pr=${pr} comment=${comment} thread=${thread} disposition=${state}"

# @file pr-threads-check.sh
# @brief Refuse a merge while a review thread of the pull request has no disposition, read-only.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28 (ADDENDUM 2), the orchestrator seat's pre-merge check, allowed by the row
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-threads-check.sh *` of `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`; the
#   `hcom-orchestration` SKILL runs it before the merge command (step 6). It lists every review thread of the
#   pull request (GraphQL `reviewThreads`, read-only; more than 100 threads, or more than 100 comments in one,
#   is a refusal, never a partial read) and requires `--head` to be the pull request's current `headRefOid` and
#   a commit in this checkout (`git fetch` first). Every thread, resolved or not (GitHub's `isResolved` alone
#   proves nothing, U28b F1), passes only when the first non-blank line of its newest reply is a disposition of
#   `preferences.md` standing order 22 and that reply's author is a maintainer of the repository: GitHub's
#   `authorAssociation` of the comment is `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR` (`maintainer_associations` below, named
#   once; U124 round 3). A newest reply by anyone else leaves the thread `open (newest reply by <login>, association
#   <value>: not a maintainer)` whatever its text, since the forms are public and the reply is text anyone with a
#   GitHub account wrote. The forms, checked here:
#   `fixed: <sha>` when `<sha>` is `--head` or an ancestor of it and was committed after the thread's first
#   comment (so a thread opened after the head cannot be `fixed`); `refuted: <text>` citing a URL or a
#   `file:line`; `residual: unit=U<n> gate=<clause>` when the finding is P2 or P3 (the `![P<n> Badge]` of its
#   first comment; no badge counts as P1) and `units.tsv` in `--records` has the row `U<n>`; or
#   `residual: operator=<ts>` when `decisions.tsv` in `--records` has a row at `<ts>`, the only residual for a P1;
#   or `filed: f=<n> s=<n> <reason>` (regime-cutover U124, the weighted finding rule of AGENTS.md "Audit") for a
#   thread of any priority when both scores are whole numbers from 1 to 10 and their product, the finding's weight,
#   is under WEIGHT_THRESHOLD below, the one place this file names that number; a weight at or above it is refused
#   naming the product. Each score is accepted by its decimal string (`^(10|[1-9])$`) before any arithmetic, so a
#   decimal past bash's range cannot wrap into one (U124 round 2); a `filed:` of any other shape (a score outside
#   that grammar, a missing score, no reason) is a malformed reply, refused naming what is wrong and quoting the line.
#   The reason is the text after `s=<n>` with the whitespace around it trimmed and must hold a character that is not
#   whitespace (`filed: f=1 s=1  reason`, two spaces, holds; U125 round d), judged on the reply's own text: the
#   listing's `@tsv` writes a tab as the two characters `\t`, and `disposition` decodes the line before it reads it,
#   so a tab-only reason is a missing reason, not a reason of two characters (U124 round 3). A reply whose first line
#   is blank is judged by its first non-blank line, and a reply of blank lines alone is `open` naming its author's
#   login and association as any reply is (U125 round d).
#   A residual without `--records` is a refusal. Any other newest reply, or none, is a refusal: the remedy is a
#   `U<n>b` TASK or a `pr-thread-reply.sh` disposition, never a merge. `<owner>/<repo>` comes from
#   `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @option --head <sha> The head the orchestrator is about to merge (40 hex).
# @option --records <dir> The program's records directory, holding `units.tsv` and `decisions.tsv`.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One line per thread, `thread comment=<id> severity=<P0-P3> state=<disposition>`, then
#   `summary threads=<n> open=<n>`.
# @exitcode 0 Every thread carries a valid disposition.
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` or `git` read failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, a moved or unknown head, an unread page, or at least one thread without a valid
#   disposition (its line says `state=open`).
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-threads-check.sh 480 --head 907240ec0f2b1f8b0a6a8b1f1c0b3f0d0e2a4b6c --records .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''             # producer-status: allow the if below takes an empty home as the checkout layout
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi

usage='usage: pr-threads-check.sh <pr> --head <sha> [--records <dir>]'

# severity is under this number. AGENTS.md names the same number once in its verdict bullet, and
# tests/unit/test_review_rules.py keeps the two equal.

# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # GraphQL variables, not shell

  repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
    pullRequest(number: $pr) {
      headRefOid
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        pageInfo { hasNextPage }
        nodes { isResolved comments(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { databaseId createdAt body authorAssociation author { login } } } }

# `head <sha> <hasNextPage>`, then per thread `<first id> <resolved> <created epoch> <P0-P3 or -> <count> <newest
# reply's authorAssociation or -> <its author's login or -> <newest reply's first non-blank line>` (TSV; the reply is
# last because it may be empty, and `@tsv` writes a tab in it as `\t`, which `disposition` decodes; a line is blank
# when it holds no character outside whitespace, so a reply opened by an empty line is read at its text).
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq source, not shell

# @description Succeed when the TSV file $1 has a row whose first field is $2.

# @description Print the disposition a thread's newest reply carries, or `open (<why>)`.
# @arg $1 int The created epoch of the thread's first comment.
# @arg $2 string Its severity, P0-P3 or `-`.
# @arg $3 string The `authorAssociation` of the newest reply's author (GitHub's enum), or `-` without a reply.
# @arg $4 string The newest reply's author login, or `-`.
# @arg $5 string The first non-blank line of the newest reply as the listing's `@tsv` escaped it; decoded here before
#   any read.
disposition() {
    local created=$1 severity=$2 association=$3 login=$4 line='' fix fix_time status frequency severity_score weight why

    local maintainer_associations='^(OWNER|MEMBER|COLLABORATOR)$'

    local unit='^residual: unit=(U[0-9]+[a-z]?) gate=[^[:space:]]'
    local operator='^residual: operator=([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z)$'
    local filed='^filed: f=([^[:space:]]+) s=([^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]'
    local filed_scores='^filed: f=[^[:space:]]+ s=[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]*$'
    local score_re='^(10|[1-9])$'
    # `@tsv` wrote a tab as `\t`, a carriage return as `\r` and a backslash as `\\`, and nothing else starts with a
    # backslash in its output; `%b` reads those three back, so the regexes below see the reply's own characters and
    # a tab-only reason is whitespace, not the two characters `\t` (U124 round 3). An empty reply is left as the
    # empty string above: `printf -v` with nothing to print leaves its variable unset.
    [[ -z $5 ]] || printf -v line '%b' "$5"

    # maintainer whatever the reply says, a reply of blank lines alone included (U125 round d).
    if [[ ${association} != - && ! ${association} =~ ${maintainer_associations} ]]; then
        echo "open (newest reply by ${login}, association ${association}: not a maintainer)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ ${line} =~ ${fixed} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        git_isolated cat-file -e "${fix}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} is not a commit here)"
            return
        }
        status=0
        git_isolated merge-base --is-ancestor "${fix}" "${head}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) ;;
        1)
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} is not in the head)"
            return
            ;;
        *) fail "git merge-base --is-ancestor ${fix} ${head} failed" ;;
        esac
        fix_time=$(git_isolated show -s --format=%ct "${fix}") || fail "git show ${fix} failed"
        if ((fix_time < created)); then
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} predates the finding)"
            return
        fi
        echo "fixed ${fix}"
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${refuted} ]]; then
        echo refuted
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${unit} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ ${severity} == P2 || ${severity} == P3 ]] || {
            echo "open (residual: unit= is for P2 and P3; this is ${severity/-/P1 (no badge)})"
            return
        }
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check units.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/units.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual ${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no units.tsv row ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/units.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${operator} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check decisions.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/decisions.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual operator=${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no decisions.tsv row at ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/decisions.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ ${line} == filed:* ]]; then
        # The shape, then each score by its decimal string (score_re) before any arithmetic: bash evaluates a name or
        # a subscript inside `(( ))` and wraps a decimal past its range (U124 round 2: f=18446744073709551617 read as
        # 1), and the reply is text anyone with a GitHub account wrote. A refusal names the fault and quotes the line.
        why=''
        if [[ ${line} =~ ${filed} ]]; then
            frequency=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
            severity_score=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
            if ! [[ ${frequency} =~ ${score_re} ]]; then
                why="f=${frequency} is not a whole number from 1 to 10"
            elif ! [[ ${severity_score} =~ ${score_re} ]]; then
                why="s=${severity_score} is not a whole number from 1 to 10"
            fi
        elif [[ ${line} =~ ${filed_scores} ]]; then
            why='the reason is missing'
        else
            why='a score is missing'
        fi
        if [[ -n ${why} ]]; then
            echo "open (filed: reply needs f=<1..10> s=<1..10> <reason>; ${why}; got: ${line})"
            return
        fi
        weight=$((frequency * severity_score))
        ((weight < WEIGHT_THRESHOLD)) || {
            echo "open (filed: f=${frequency} s=${severity_score} weighs ${weight}, not under ${WEIGHT_THRESHOLD}; fix it, or answer refuted: or residual:)"
            return
        }
        echo "filed f=${frequency} s=${severity_score} weight=${weight}"
    elif [[ -z ${line} && ${association} == - ]]; then
        echo 'open (no reply)'
    elif [[ -z ${line} ]]; then
        echo "open (the newest reply by ${login}, association ${association}, holds no text)"
    else
        echo 'open (the newest reply is not a disposition)'
    fi
}

pr=''
head=''
records=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --head | --records)

[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
git_isolated cat-file -e "${head}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || refuse "${head} is not a commit in this checkout; git fetch first"

repo=$(gh_bounded repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner) || fail 'gh repo view failed'
[[ ${repo} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || fail "gh repo view printed no owner/repo: ${repo}"
listing=$(gh_bounded api graphql -f "query=${threads_query}" -f "owner=${repo%%/*}" -f "name=${repo#*/}" \
    -F "pr=${pr}" --jq "${threads_jq}") || fail "cannot list the review threads of pull request ${pr}"

threads=0
open=0
seen_head=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r first resolved created severity count association login reply; do
    if [[ ${first} == head ]]; then
        [[ ${resolved} == "${head}" ]] || refuse "the head of pull request ${pr} is ${resolved}, not ${head}"

        continue
    fi
    ((seen_head)) || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} does not start with its head"
    [[ ${first} =~ ^[0-9]+$ && ${created} =~ ^[0-9]+$ && ${count} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] ||
        fail "unreadable thread row: ${first}"
    ((count <= 100)) || refuse "the thread of comment ${first} has more than 100 comments; check it by hand"
    threads=$((threads + 1))
    # A resolved thread is judged like an open one (U28b F1): GitHub's isResolved says someone clicked, not why.
    state=$(disposition "${created}" "${severity}" "${association}" "${login}" "${reply}") || exit $?
    if [[ ${resolved} == true ]]; then
        case ${state} in
        open*) state="open (resolved without a valid disposition: ${state#open (}" ;;
        *) state="resolved ${state}" ;;
        esac
    fi
    [[ ${state} != open* ]] || open=$((open + 1))
    echo "thread comment=${first} severity=${severity/-/none} state=${state}"
done <<< "${listing}"
((seen_head)) || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} has no head"
echo "summary threads=${threads} open=${open}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-update-branch.sh
# @brief Merge main into an open pull request's branch (`gh pr update-branch`), the orchestrator seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed by the row
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-update-branch.sh *` of `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). `<pr>` is decimal and checked before the
#   first `gh` call. `gh pr view <pr> --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid` must report `OPEN` and base `main`,
#   else the lever refuses; the one write is `gh pr update-branch <pr>`, GitHub's merge form (never `--rebase`,
#   which rewrites the worker's branch), and the head is read again afterwards. The new head needs its own audit
#   and `correct` ledger row before `pr-merge.sh` merges it (U71: no verdict carries over from the old head). Each
#   `gh` call is bounded
#   by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `updated pr=<pr> old=<head before> new=<head after>`.
# @exitcode 0 The branch was updated (`old` equals `new` when it was already up to date).
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` read or the update failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, a pull request that is not open, or a base other than main.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-update-branch.sh 480
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='pr-update-branch.sh'
usage='usage: pr-update-branch.sh <pr>'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

[[ $# -eq 1 ]] || refuse "${usage}"
pr=$1
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

view=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid --jq '[.state, .baseRefName, .headRefOid] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read pull request ${pr}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r state base old <<< "${view}"
[[ ${state} == OPEN ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} is ${state:-unreadable}, not OPEN"
[[ ${base} == main ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} targets ${base:-nothing}, not main"
[[ ${old} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || fail "pull request ${pr} has no readable head: ${old}"

gh_bounded pr update-branch "${pr}" >&2 || fail "gh pr update-branch ${pr} failed"
new=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid) || fail "cannot read the new head of ${pr}"
[[ ${new} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || fail "pull request ${pr} has no readable head after the update: ${new}"
echo "updated pr=${pr} old=${old} new=${new}"

#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -I
"""Place a dsh profile's `agent/config.yml` through one held directory descriptor, or refuse (regime-cutover U310d).

`profile-config-place.py [--dry-run] <agent-dir> <uid>`, the rendered config on stdin, is the one writer of the dsh
role's profile config: `scripts/orchestrator/hcom-seat` resolves the profile's `agent/` directory (the dsh row's own
containment judgement, U272 and U306) and runs this file beside it as `python3 -I -S`, reading its status. Three audit
rounds of U310 found one class, symlink-write, in the launcher's bash: each round checked a path and then acted on it,
and a process that owns `agent/` (the role's own sandboxed dsh) swapped the entry between the two. Here no path is
checked and then acted on: every operation on `agent/` runs on one descriptor of the directory itself, opened once
with `O_NOFOLLOW`, and every entry inside it is named relative to that descriptor (`dir_fd`), so no component can be
swapped between a reading and the act that follows it. The steps, in order:

- `open-agent`: `agent-dir` is opened `O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW` (a link at `agent` is ELOOP on Linux and
  ENOTDIR on macOS, either a refusal naming a link); `fstat-agent`: it is a directory of `uid` whose mode grants no
  group or other write.
- `open-config`: `config.yml` is opened through the descriptor with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` (ENOENT is absence; a link
  is ELOOP and refuses); `fstat-config`: a regular file of `uid` (a directory or a FIFO refuses); `read-config`: its
  bytes. Equal to the rendering: `verify-kept`, then `kept`, nothing written. With `--dry-run` the run stops here:
  `absent` or `differs`.
- `create-temporary`: `.config.yml.<16 hex>` (`secrets.token_hex`) is created through the descriptor with
  `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` (read-write, so the read-back below runs on this same descriptor), mode 0600, so a
  regular file, a link (dangling too), a FIFO or a directory planted at the name is EEXIST and refuses without the name
  being opened and without blocking; `fstat-temporary`: the new descriptor is a regular file of `uid` with one link, and
  its identity (device, inode) is kept; `fchmod-temporary` 0600; `write-temporary`; `fsync-temporary`.
- `rename`: `os.rename(tmp, "config.yml", src_dir_fd, dst_dir_fd)`: one atomic step; a link at the destination is
  replaced as an entry (its target untouched), a directory there is EISDIR and refuses.
- `verify-placed`: the written descriptor is read back from its start and must hold the rendering; then `config.yml`
  is opened again through the held directory descriptor (`O_NOFOLLOW`) and the identity of that open must be the
  written descriptor's. Another inode at the name (round-4 verdict P2 at :225: a writer that replaced `config.yml`
  during the read-back was reported as `placed`) is read once through the directory descriptor: it must be a regular
  file of `uid` holding the rendering (two launches at once that land the same bytes, the role's normal case) and must
  still be the inode at the name on one more open; anything else refuses, so the launch never reports `placed` while
  the name holds another inode's bytes. `verify-kept` is the same identity check after a compare that found the
  rendering, so a replacement of the entry during that read is never reported as `kept`. What no read-back closes
  (round-5 verdict P2 at :197): a process of the directory's owner, the role's own user (`fstat-agent` admits no
  other writer), may rewrite `config.yml` in place, during a read or at any moment after placement; the kit treats
  that writer as the role itself, and the U310 body carries it as a residual row, not as a guarantee.
- On any refusal after the create and before the rename, `unlink-temporary` removes the temporary through the
  descriptor; its own failure is reported in the same line, naming the path that remains.

Exit 0 with one word on stdout: `placed`, `replaced` or `kept` (`absent`, `differs` or `kept` with `--dry-run`). Exit 2
refused, one line on stderr naming the step, the path and the errno. Exit 1 a usage error. The file imports `errno`,
`os`, `secrets`, `stat` and `sys` only, reads no environment variable and runs under `-I -S`. It is shipped and pinned
like the levers (`scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` writes the byte-identical
`home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_profile-config-place.py` and the `claude.levers.sha256` pin, which hcom-seat
checks before running it); `tests/unit/test_profile_config_place.py` holds every step and every injected failure.
"""

import errno
import os
import secrets
import stat
import sys

NAME = "profile-config-place"
USAGE = f"usage: {NAME}.py [--dry-run] <agent-dir> <uid>  (the rendered config on stdin)"
CONFIG = "config.yml"
TEMPORARY_PREFIX = ".config.yml."
INSIDE = "the dsh role writes its profile config inside its profile only"
# The read-only opens: no link followed at the last component, and no blocking on a FIFO planted at the name.
READ_FLAGS = os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK | os.O_CLOEXEC
DIRECTORY_FLAGS = os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_CLOEXEC
# The exclusive create: an entry of any kind at the name is EEXIST before anything is opened. Read-write, so the
# read-back after the rename runs on this descriptor, the one that wrote the bytes.
CREATE_FLAGS = os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK | os.O_CLOEXEC
CHUNK = 65536


class Refusal(Exception):
    """A refused placement: the step, the path it concerned and the reason, printed as one stderr line (exit 2)."""

    def __init__(self, step: str, path: str, reason: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"refused at {step}: {path}: {reason}")
        self.step = step
        self.path = path
        self.reason = reason


def errno_text(error: OSError) -> str:
    """`<strerror> (<ERRNO NAME>)`, the kernel's own words for a failed step."""
    code = errno.errorcode.get(error.errno, str(error.errno)) if error.errno is not None else "no errno"
    return f"{error.strerror or 'failed'} ({code})"


def read_all(fd: int, step: str, path: str) -> bytes:
    parts = []
    while True:
        try:
            chunk = os.read(fd, CHUNK)
        except OSError as error:
            raise Refusal(step, path, f"cannot read it: {errno_text(error)}") from None
        if not chunk:
            return b"".join(parts)
        parts.append(chunk)


def write_all(fd: int, data: bytes, step: str, path: str) -> None:
    view = memoryview(data)
    while view:
        try:
            written = os.write(fd, view)
        except OSError as error:
            raise Refusal(step, path, f"cannot write it: {errno_text(error)}") from None
        view = view[written:]


def close_quietly(fd: int) -> None:
    try:
        os.close(fd)
    except OSError:
        pass


def open_agent(agent_dir: str, uid: int) -> int:
    """The one descriptor every later step runs on: `agent/` itself, a directory of `uid` nobody else can write."""
    try:
        dfd = os.open(agent_dir, DIRECTORY_FLAGS)
    except OSError as error:
        if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
            raise Refusal("open-agent", agent_dir, f"is a symbolic link or not a directory; {INSIDE}") from None
        raise Refusal("open-agent", agent_dir, f"cannot open it: {errno_text(error)}") from None
    try:
        info = os.fstat(dfd)
    except OSError as error:
        close_quietly(dfd)
        raise Refusal("fstat-agent", agent_dir, f"cannot read its identity: {errno_text(error)}") from None
    if not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
        close_quietly(dfd)
        raise Refusal("fstat-agent", agent_dir, "is not a directory")
    if info.st_uid != uid:
        close_quietly(dfd)
        raise Refusal("fstat-agent", agent_dir, f"is owned by uid {info.st_uid}, not {uid}")
    if info.st_mode & (stat.S_IWGRP | stat.S_IWOTH):
        close_quietly(dfd)
        mode = oct(stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode))
        raise Refusal("fstat-agent", agent_dir, f"is writable by its group or by others (mode {mode}); {INSIDE}")
    return dfd


def open_config(dfd: int, agent_dir: str, uid: int) -> "tuple[int, tuple[int, int]] | None":
    """`config.yml` opened through the held descriptor with its identity (device, inode), None when the entry is
    absent (ENOENT alone); a link, an irregular entry or another uid's file refuses."""
    path = f"{agent_dir}/{CONFIG}"
    try:
        cfd = os.open(CONFIG, READ_FLAGS, dir_fd=dfd)
    except OSError as error:
        if error.errno == errno.ENOENT:
            return None
        if error.errno == errno.ELOOP:
            raise Refusal("open-config", path, f"is a symbolic link; {INSIDE}") from None
        raise Refusal("open-config", path, f"cannot open it: {errno_text(error)}") from None
    try:
        try:
            info = os.fstat(cfd)
        except OSError as error:
            raise Refusal("fstat-config", path, f"cannot read its identity: {errno_text(error)}") from None
        if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
            raise Refusal("fstat-config", path, f"is not a regular file; {INSIDE}")
        if info.st_uid != uid:
            raise Refusal("fstat-config", path, f"is owned by uid {info.st_uid}, not {uid}")
    except Refusal:
        close_quietly(cfd)
        raise
    return cfd, (info.st_dev, info.st_ino)


def read_config(dfd: int, agent_dir: str, uid: int) -> "tuple[bytes | None, tuple[int, int] | None]":
    """The bytes of `config.yml` read through the held descriptor and the identity of the file they were read from,
    (None, None) when the entry is absent."""
    opened = open_config(dfd, agent_dir, uid)
    if opened is None:
        return None, None
    cfd, identity = opened
    try:
        return read_all(cfd, "read-config", f"{agent_dir}/{CONFIG}"), identity
    finally:
        close_quietly(cfd)


def identity_at(dfd: int, agent_dir: str, step: str, uid: int) -> "tuple[int, int]":
    """The identity of the entry `config.yml` names now, through one more open on the held descriptor; an absent
    entry refuses, since the name held the config a moment ago."""
    opened = open_config(dfd, agent_dir, uid)
    if opened is None:
        raise Refusal(
            step, f"{agent_dir}/{CONFIG}", "is absent after it held the rendered config (replaced during placement)"
        )
    cfd, identity = opened
    close_quietly(cfd)
    return identity


def settled(dfd: int, agent_dir: str, uid: int, rendered: bytes, identity: "tuple[int, int]", step: str) -> None:
    """The name `config.yml` holds the inode `identity` (the written temporary's after the rename, or the compared
    config's), read through the held directory descriptor; another inode there is read once and must hold the
    rendering and still stand at the name after that read (a concurrent launch of the same bytes); anything else
    refuses, so no replacement of the entry during a read is reported as placed or kept (an owner's rewrite in place
    is the residual the module docstring names)."""
    target = f"{agent_dir}/{CONFIG}"
    for attempt in (0, 1):
        if identity_at(dfd, agent_dir, step, uid) == identity:
            return
        if attempt:
            break
        current, identity = read_config(dfd, agent_dir, uid)
        if current != rendered:
            raise Refusal(
                step,
                target,
                "does not hold the rendered config after the rename (a writer inside the directory replaced it)",
            )
    raise Refusal(step, target, "config.yml replaced during placement (another inode at the name on every read)")


def create_temporary(dfd: int, agent_dir: str, uid: int) -> "tuple[str, int, tuple[int, int]]":
    """A fresh 0600 regular file of `uid` at a random name inside the held directory, created exclusively, with the
    identity (device, inode) of the descriptor."""
    name = TEMPORARY_PREFIX + secrets.token_hex(8)
    path = f"{agent_dir}/{name}"
    try:
        tfd = os.open(name, CREATE_FLAGS, 0o600, dir_fd=dfd)
    except OSError as error:
        if error.errno == errno.EEXIST:
            raise Refusal(
                "create-temporary", path, "an entry already stands at the temporary name; nothing was opened"
            ) from None
        raise Refusal(
            "create-temporary", path, f"cannot create a temporary file in {agent_dir}: {errno_text(error)}"
        ) from None
    try:
        try:
            info = os.fstat(tfd)
        except OSError as error:
            raise Refusal("fstat-temporary", path, f"cannot read its identity: {errno_text(error)}") from None
        if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != uid or info.st_nlink != 1:
            raise Refusal("fstat-temporary", path, "is not a fresh regular file of this user with one link")
        try:
            os.fchmod(tfd, 0o600)
        except OSError as error:
            raise Refusal("fchmod-temporary", path, f"cannot set its mode: {errno_text(error)}") from None
    except Refusal as refusal:
        close_quietly(tfd)
        raise unlink_temporary(dfd, name, path, refusal) from None
    return name, tfd, (info.st_dev, info.st_ino)


def unlink_temporary(dfd: int, name: str, path: str, refusal: Refusal) -> Refusal:
    """Remove the temporary through the held descriptor after a refusal; a removal that fails is named in the line."""
    try:
        os.unlink(name, dir_fd=dfd)
    except OSError as error:
        return Refusal(
            refusal.step, refusal.path, f"{refusal.reason}; the temporary {path} remains (unlink: {errno_text(error)})"
        )
    return refusal


def place(agent_dir: str, uid: int, rendered: bytes, dry_run: bool) -> str:
    """Place `rendered` as `config.yml` inside `agent_dir`, or raise Refusal; the decision word for stdout."""
    dfd = open_agent(agent_dir, uid)
    try:
        current, identity = read_config(dfd, agent_dir, uid)
        if current == rendered and identity is not None:
            settled(dfd, agent_dir, uid, rendered, identity, "verify-kept")
            return "kept"
        if dry_run:
            return "absent" if current is None else "differs"
        name, tfd, written = create_temporary(dfd, agent_dir, uid)
        path = f"{agent_dir}/{name}"
        target = f"{agent_dir}/{CONFIG}"
        try:
            write_all(tfd, rendered, "write-temporary", path)
            try:
                os.fsync(tfd)
            except OSError as error:
                raise Refusal("fsync-temporary", path, f"cannot flush it: {errno_text(error)}") from None
            try:
                os.rename(name, CONFIG, src_dir_fd=dfd, dst_dir_fd=dfd)
            except OSError as error:
                if error.errno in (errno.EISDIR, errno.ENOTEMPTY, errno.EEXIST, errno.ENOTDIR):
                    raise Refusal("rename", target, f"a directory stands at the destination; {INSIDE}") from None
                raise Refusal("rename", target, f"cannot install it: {errno_text(error)}") from None
        except Refusal as refusal:
            close_quietly(tfd)
            raise unlink_temporary(dfd, name, path, refusal) from None
        try:
            try:
                os.lseek(tfd, 0, os.SEEK_SET)
            except OSError as error:
                raise Refusal("verify-placed", target, f"cannot rewind the written file: {errno_text(error)}") from None
            if read_all(tfd, "verify-placed", target) != rendered:
                raise Refusal(
                    "verify-placed",
                    target,
                    "does not hold the rendered config after the rename (a writer inside the directory replaced it)",
                )
        finally:
            close_quietly(tfd)
        settled(dfd, agent_dir, uid, rendered, written, "verify-placed")
        return "placed" if current is None else "replaced"
    finally:
        close_quietly(dfd)


def main(argv: "list[str]", stdin) -> int:
    dry_run = False
    args = list(argv)
    if args and args[0] == "--dry-run":
        dry_run = True
        args = args[1:]
    absolute = len(args) == 2 and args[0].startswith("/")  # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test, no two paths compared
    if len(args) != 2 or args[0].startswith("-") or not absolute or not args[1].isdigit():
        print(USAGE, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    agent_dir, uid = args[0].rstrip("/") or "/", int(args[1])
    try:
        rendered = stdin.read()
    except OSError as error:
        print(f"{NAME}: cannot read the rendered config from stdin: {errno_text(error)}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    try:
        decision = place(agent_dir, uid, rendered, dry_run)
    except Refusal as refusal:
        print(f"{NAME}: {refusal}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(decision)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:], sys.stdin.buffer))

<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -I
"""Print the operator's state report of a program store in standing order 56's shape (regime-cutover U497).

The operator asked (2026-11-12 JST, order 57) whether the program is moving or stopped and could not tell from the
coordinator's prose. This lever answers from the store's tables alone: `program-status.py <store> [--ja]
[--now <ts>] [--progress-root <dir>]` prints one word of state and its reason, one signal line per goal element, the
operator's acts, the decisions only the operator can make, and what the agent runs; the coordinator's reply quotes
this output instead of composing it. Plain text, five headings, at most one line per item, no table, no colour, no
chronology, no commit hash, and no unit id outside the running-work section (order 56). Every input is a store file
with a fixed header, read by one reader each and refused on any other shape (order 21); nothing is written.

The report, line by line:
- `state: <word>: <reason>, last record <age> min ago`. The word is `done` when every tests table is green;
  `stopped` when no unit is in flight and an open decision or a pending operator act exists, or when a stall check
  beside this lever reports every in-flight unit `stalled` or `no-file`; otherwise `moving`. The reason is the first
  matching condition in words (`every table green`; `nothing in flight, waiting on <n> operator acts and <m>
  decisions`; `every in-flight worker silent`; `<n> units in flight`); the age is `--now` (else the clock, UTC) minus
  the last row's `ts` of `decisions.tsv` (header `ts phase decision why evidence result`), in whole minutes, a ts
  after now reading 0. A decisions table with no row is a refusal: the last recorded step is read from it.
- `elements`, then one line per `tests/<element>.tsv` in name order (header `id use_case source kind host command
  expected observed verdict ts`; a file under `tests/` not ending in `.tsv` is ignored; an element name outside
  `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, so one holding a tab, a newline, a control character or a space, is a refusal naming the file):
  `<element>: <signal> <ok>/<rows> OK, <ng> NG, <pending> pending`, the signal `green` when every verdict is `OK`,
  `red` when any is `NG`, `yellow` when none is `NG` and one is `pending`, else `grey` (no row, or every verdict
  another word).
- `operator acts`, then every tests row whose `kind` is `operator` and whose verdict is `pending`, tables in name
  order and rows in file order: `<element> <id>: <command>` (the command cell holds the step as the handouts write
  it).
- `operator decisions`, then every `gates.md` row whose `result` cell is empty: `<id>: <gate> (<moment>; default
  <default>)`. The table is the one whose header is the file's first table row (a line starting with `|`), read as a
  row: split on `|`, each cell stripped, the six names `id gate moment options default result` in that order, any
  padding (the kit's template `home/dot_agents/regime/gates.md` pads them, the live store does not; U497c); the next
  table row is the separator, six cells of dashes judged the same way; lines that are no table row are skipped; the
  result is the text after the fifth cell, so a `||` typed into a row lands there; a header of other names or another
  count, a missing separator and a row with fewer than six cells are refusals naming `<file>:<line>`.
- `agent running`, then every `units.tsv` row (header `id track state branch pr head_sha brief note`) whose state is
  `in-flight`, in file order: `<id> <track> pr <pr or -> progress: <column>`. When `stall-check.py` (U496) is a
  regular file beside this lever it is run once as `python3 -I <dir>/stall-check.py <store> [--progress-root <dir>]
  [--now <ts>]` with this lever's interpreter, its stdout and stderr read as bytes and decoded as strict UTF-8, and
  its rows, `unit<TAB>state<TAB>age_minutes<TAB>last_line` (an optional first row of those names is skipped), fill
  the column as `<state>, <age_minutes> min, <last_line>`, the state one of moving, stalled, done, no-file,
  unreadable and the age `-` or 1 to 10 decimal digits; an in-flight unit it names no row for reads `progress: no
  row`; its exit 0 or 1 is a report, its exit 2 is a refusal of this report quoting its first stderr line, any other
  exit, output that is not UTF-8, a row of another width, a carriage return, a state or an age of another shape, a
  unit named twice, a time limit of 120 seconds or a start that fails is a refusal too, the row ones naming the line.
  Without the file beside this one the column reads `progress: unknown`. Rows of units not in flight print nothing.
A section with no item prints `none`. `--ja` prints the five headings and the state word in the operator's forms
(状態 / 要素 / 操作者の作業 / 操作者の判断 / agent が動かしているもの; 進んでいる / 止まっている / 完了) and translates nothing else.

Exit 0 when the report printed. Exit 2 with one stderr line, `program-status.py: refused: <reason>`, and nothing on
stdout for every refusal: the self pin (below), a store that is no directory, `--now` not exactly
`<YYYY-MM-DD>T<HH:MM:SS>Z` (the shape is checked before strptime, which would take `2026-1-2T3:4:5Z`), a file that is
missing, unreadable or not UTF-8, a tests table, `units.tsv` or `decisions.tsv` whose first line is not its header
(named `<file>:1`) or whose row has another number of cells or a carriage return, a `gates.md` whose first table row
is not the six header names or whose next is not the separator, with a short row or with a carriage return, a
`decisions.tsv` with no row or whose last ts is not a timestamp of that exact shape, a `tests` directory that is
missing, and the stall-check outcomes above. Every file is read byte-exact (`newline=""`, split on `\n` alone), so a
CRLF row reaches the carriage-return refusal instead of being normalised into a report (U497c). One sanitiser serves
the refusal and every printed line: each line boundary `str.splitlines` knows (newline, carriage return, VT, FF, FS,
GS, RS, NEL, U+2028, U+2029) inside a path, a quoted value or a printed cell becomes a space, so one refusal is one
stderr line and one report item is one line whatever the store holds. No file is written and no mode is changed.

Installed as `~/.local/bin/common/program-status.py` in `brief-check.py`'s form: `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py`
writes the same bytes to `home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_program-status.py` and pins their sha256 under
`claude.levers.sha256`; before anything else the file hashes itself against that pin, the deployed manifest
`~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` when its physical directory is the physical `~/.local/bin/common`, else the checkout's
`home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` two levels up, and refuses to run on a difference, so a rewritten copy prints no
report. The orchestrator seat's policy allows that installed path alone.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import re
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone

LEVER = "program-status.py"
STALL_CHECK = "stall-check.py"
# The levers block of the manifest, read as text by indentation alone, never parsed as YAML (brief-check.py, U136).
MAPPING_KEY = re.compile(r"^(\S+):$")
LEVER_PIN = re.compile(r"^(\S+): ([0-9a-f]{64})$")
LEVERS_KEYS = ("claude", "levers", "sha256")

# A timestamp's exact shape, checked before strptime (which would take `2026-1-2T3:4:5Z`); ASCII digits only.
TS_SHAPE = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z")
TS_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
TESTS_HEADER = ("id", "use_case", "source", "kind", "host", "command", "expected", "observed", "verdict", "ts")
UNITS_HEADER = ("id", "track", "state", "branch", "pr", "head_sha", "brief", "note")
DECISIONS_HEADER = ("ts", "phase", "decision", "why", "evidence", "result")
# The element name a tests table's file name carries before `.tsv`: one report item is one line, so no tab, newline,
# control character or space (U497b).
ELEMENT_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+")
# The gates header's six cell names, read as a table row with any padding (U497c); the separator row's cells.
GATES_HEADER = ("id", "gate", "moment", "options", "default", "result")
GATES_WIDTH = len(GATES_HEADER)
SEPARATOR_CELL = re.compile(r":?-+:?")
STALL_HEADER = ("unit", "state", "age_minutes", "last_line")
# The stall check's row contract (U496, U496b): the five states, the age `-` or 1 to 10 decimal digits.
STALL_STATES = ("moving", "stalled", "done", "no-file", "unreadable")
STALL_AGE = re.compile(r"-|[0-9]{1,10}")
STALL_TIMEOUT = 120
# The stall check's states that mean the worker is silent (U496).
SILENT = frozenset({"stalled", "no-file"})
# The line boundaries `str.splitlines` knows; `one_line` replaces each with a space in every refusal and every printed
# line.
LINE_BREAK = re.compile(r"[\n\r\x0b\x0c\x1c\x1d\x1e\x85\u2028\u2029]")

HEADINGS = {
    "en": ("state", "elements", "operator acts", "operator decisions", "agent running"),
    "ja": ("状態", "要素", "操作者の作業", "操作者の判断", "agent が動かしているもの"),
}
WORDS = {
    "en": {"moving": "moving", "stopped": "stopped", "done": "done"},
    "ja": {"moving": "進んでいる", "stopped": "止まっている", "done": "完了"},
}


def one_line(text):
    """`text` with every line boundary `str.splitlines` knows (newline, carriage return, VT, FF, FS, GS, RS, NEL,
    U+2028, U+2029) a space: the one sanitiser of every refusal and every printed report line, so an id, a gate text, a
    command or a stall-check cell that holds one cannot add a line (U497b, U497c)."""
    return LINE_BREAK.sub(" ", text)


def refuse(reason):
    """One stderr line in the levers' words, exit 2; nothing was printed. A line boundary inside the reason (a newline
    or a carriage return in a path or a quoted value) becomes a space, so every refusal is one line (U497b)."""
    print(f"{LEVER}: refused: {one_line(reason)}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def lever_self_check():
    """Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31).

    The physical directory of this file decides the manifest: the deployed `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` when the
    directory is the physical `~/.local/bin/common`, else the checkout's `home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` two
    levels up; an unset or unresolvable HOME means the checkout manifest. The pin is the block's `program-status.py`
    entry: one entry is the pin, none or two is a refusal. Every read is checked and a failed one is a refusal, never
    a pass (preferences.md standing order 21); the reader is brief-check.py's, spelled the same.
    """
    directory = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    self_path = os.path.join(directory, os.path.basename(__file__))
    home = os.environ.get("HOME", "")
    if home and os.path.isdir(home) and directory == os.path.realpath(os.path.join(home, ".local/bin/common")):
        manifest = os.path.join(home, ".agents/agent-config.yaml")
    else:
        manifest = os.path.join(directory, "../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml")
    if not os.access(manifest, os.R_OK):
        refuse(f"manifest unreadable: {manifest}")
    try:
        with open(manifest, "rb") as handle:
            lines = handle.read().decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()
    except OSError:
        refuse(f"cannot read {manifest}")
    pins = [digest for name, digest in manifest_levers(lines, manifest) if name == LEVER]
    if len(pins) != 1:
        refuse(f"no single sha256 pin for {LEVER} in {manifest}")
    try:
        with open(self_path, "rb") as handle:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(handle.read()).hexdigest()
    except OSError:
        refuse(f"cannot hash {self_path}")
    if digest != pins[0]:
        refuse(f"sha256 {digest} of {self_path} differs from the pin in {manifest}")


def manifest_levers(lines, manifest):
    """The `(name, sha256)` pins under the manifest's `claude.levers.sha256` mapping, in file order (brief-check.py,
    U136): the mapping keys are walked by indentation, so `levers:` counts only under the top-level `claude:` and
    `sha256:` only under that `levers:`; inside the block, blank and comment lines are skipped, the entries share the
    indentation of the first pin, and the list ends at the first line indented less. An entry that is not
    `<name>: <64 hex>` is a refusal naming the line; no entry at all is the missing-block refusal."""
    pins = []
    keys = []  # the open mapping keys as (indentation, key), outermost first
    block = None  # the indentation of the `sha256:` key once the path is open
    entries = None  # the indentation of the pin lines, fixed by the first
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        text = line.lstrip(" ")
        if not text or text.startswith("#"):
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(text)
        if block is not None:
            if indent <= block or (entries is not None and indent < entries):
                break
            match = LEVER_PIN.match(text)
            if match is None or (entries is not None and indent != entries):
                refuse(f"line {number} of {manifest} is not a `<name>: <sha256>` pin under claude.levers.sha256")
            entries = indent
            pins.append((match.group(1), match.group(2)))
            continue
        while keys and indent <= keys[-1][0]:
            keys.pop()
        match = MAPPING_KEY.match(text)
        if match and (keys or indent == 0):
            keys.append((indent, match.group(1)))
            if tuple(key for _, key in keys) == LEVERS_KEYS:
                block = indent
    if not pins:
        refuse(f"no claude.levers.sha256 block in {manifest}")
    return tuple(pins)


lever_self_check()


def read_text(path):
    """The whole file as strict UTF-8, byte-exact (`newline=""`: no CRLF or CR is turned into a newline, so a carriage
    return reaches the row checks; U497c); a file that is missing, unreadable or not UTF-8 is a refusal naming it."""
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
            return handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        refuse(f"{path} is missing; the report is read from the store's tables")
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot read {path}: {error.strerror}")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
        refuse(f"{path} is not UTF-8: {error.reason}")


def read_tsv(path, header):
    """The rows of a tab-separated table whose first line is exactly `header`, each line without a carriage return and
    each row with the header's number of cells; any other shape is a refusal naming the file and the line (the
    header's, `:1`). The text is split on `\\n` alone, so a CRLF table is refused at its first line."""
    lines = read_text(path).split("\n")
    if lines and lines[-1] == "":
        lines.pop()
    if lines and "\r" in lines[0]:
        refuse(f"line 1 of {path} holds a carriage return")
    if not lines or lines[0] != "\t".join(header):
        refuse(f"{path}:1 is not the header `{' '.join(header)}`")
    rows = []
    for number, line in enumerate(lines[1:], 2):
        if "\r" in line:
            refuse(f"line {number} of {path} holds a carriage return")
        cells = line.split("\t")
        if len(cells) != len(header):
            refuse(f"line {number} of {path} has {len(cells)} cells, not the header's {len(header)}")
        rows.append(cells)
    return rows


def elements(store):
    """One (element, signal, ok, ng, pending, rows) per `tests/*.tsv` in name order, and the operator's pending acts
    as (element, id, command) in table then file order; a table whose element name is outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` is a
    refusal naming the file, so every element line is one line."""
    tests = os.path.join(store, "tests")
    try:
        names = sorted(os.listdir(tests))
    except FileNotFoundError:
        refuse(f"{tests} is missing; one goal element per table is read from it")
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot list {tests}: {error.strerror}")
    signals = []
    acts = []
    for name in names:
        if not name.endswith(".tsv"):
            continue
        element = name[: -len(".tsv")]
        if ELEMENT_NAME.fullmatch(element) is None:
            refuse(
                f"the tests table {os.path.join(tests, name)} is not `<element>.tsv` with the element in [A-Za-z0-9._-]"
            )
        rows = read_tsv(os.path.join(tests, name), TESTS_HEADER)
        verdicts = [row[8] for row in rows]
        ok = verdicts.count("OK")
        ng = verdicts.count("NG")
        pending = verdicts.count("pending")
        if rows and ok == len(rows):
            signal = "green"
        elif ng:
            signal = "red"
        elif pending:
            signal = "yellow"
        else:
            signal = "grey"
        signals.append((element, signal, ok, ng, pending, len(rows)))
        acts.extend((element, row[0], row[5]) for row in rows if row[3] == "operator" and row[8] == "pending")
    return signals, acts


def table_rows(path):
    """The `(line number, stripped cells)` of every table row of a markdown file, in file order: a table row is a line
    that starts with `|` once stripped and ends with one, its cells the text between the bars, each stripped; a line
    holding a carriage return or a row that starts and does not end is a refusal naming the line; every other line is
    skipped."""
    rows = []
    for number, line in enumerate(read_text(path).split("\n"), 1):
        if "\r" in line:
            refuse(f"line {number} of {path} holds a carriage return")
        text = line.strip()
        if not text.startswith("|"):
            continue
        if not text.endswith("|"):
            refuse(f"line {number} of {path} starts a table row and does not end one")
        rows.append((number, [cell.strip() for cell in text[1:-1].split("|")]))
    return rows


def open_gates(store):
    """The (id, gate, moment, default) of every gates row whose result cell is empty. The header is the file's first
    table row read by cell names (`id gate moment options default result`, any padding: the kit's template pads them,
    the live store does not), the separator the next table row (six cells of `:?-+:?`); other names, another count, a
    missing separator and a short row are refusals naming `<file>:<line>` (U497c)."""
    path = os.path.join(store, "gates.md")
    rows = table_rows(path)
    if not rows:
        refuse(f"{path} holds no table row; the header `{' '.join(GATES_HEADER)}` is read as its first")
    number, cells = rows[0]
    if tuple(cells) != GATES_HEADER:
        refuse(f"{path}:{number} is not the header `{' '.join(GATES_HEADER)}` read as cells")
    if len(rows) < 2:
        refuse(f"{path}:{number} is the header and no separator row follows it")
    number, cells = rows[1]
    if len(cells) != GATES_WIDTH or not all(SEPARATOR_CELL.fullmatch(cell) for cell in cells):
        refuse(f"{path}:{number} is not the separator row of {GATES_WIDTH} dash cells under the header")
    opened = []
    for number, cells in rows[2:]:
        if len(cells) < GATES_WIDTH:
            refuse(f"line {number} of {path} has {len(cells)} cells, fewer than the header's {GATES_WIDTH}")
        result = "|".join(cells[GATES_WIDTH - 1 :]).strip("| ")
        if not result:
            opened.append((cells[0], cells[1], cells[2], cells[4]))
    return opened


def in_flight(store):
    """The (id, track, pr or -) of every `in-flight` row of units.tsv, in file order."""
    rows = read_tsv(os.path.join(store, "units.tsv"), UNITS_HEADER)
    return [(row[0], row[1], row[4] or "-") for row in rows if row[2] == "in-flight"]


def timestamp(text, what):
    """`text` as an aware UTC datetime; a value that is not exactly `<YYYY-MM-DD>T<HH:MM:SS>Z` (checked as a shape
    before strptime, which would take `2026-1-2T3:4:5Z`) or that names no calendar moment is a refusal naming `what`."""
    if TS_SHAPE.fullmatch(text) is None:
        refuse(f"{what} {text!r} is not <YYYY-MM-DD>T<HH:MM:SS>Z")
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(text, TS_FORMAT).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    except ValueError:
        refuse(f"{what} {text!r} is not <YYYY-MM-DD>T<HH:MM:SS>Z")


def last_record_age(store, now):
    """Whole minutes from the last decisions row's ts to now; a table with no row is a refusal."""
    path = os.path.join(store, "decisions.tsv")
    rows = read_tsv(path, DECISIONS_HEADER)
    if not rows:
        refuse(f"{path} holds no row; the last recorded step is read from it")
    last = timestamp(rows[-1][0], f"the last row's ts of {path}")
    return max(0, int((now - last).total_seconds() // 60))


def decoded(data, what):
    """`data` as strict UTF-8; anything else is a refusal naming the stream."""
    try:
        return data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
        refuse(f"{what} is not UTF-8: {error.reason} at byte {error.start}")


def stall_rows(here, store, args):
    """The stall check's rows by unit as (state, age_minutes, last_line), or None when no `stall-check.py` is beside
    this lever; its exit 2 and every other failure of the run, of its encoding or of a row's shape (width, carriage
    return, state, age) is a refusal, the row ones naming the line."""
    path = os.path.join(here, STALL_CHECK)
    try:
        status = os.lstat(path)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot stat {path}: {error.strerror}")
    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"{path} is not a regular file")
    command = [sys.executable, "-I", path, store]
    if args.progress_root is not None:
        command += ["--progress-root", args.progress_root]
    if args.now is not None:
        command += ["--now", args.now]
    try:
        run = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, timeout=STALL_TIMEOUT, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        refuse(f"{STALL_CHECK} gave no answer within {STALL_TIMEOUT} seconds")
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot run {path}: {error.strerror}")
    stdout = decoded(run.stdout, f"{STALL_CHECK}'s stdout")
    stderr = decoded(run.stderr, f"{STALL_CHECK}'s stderr")
    first = stderr.strip().split("\n", 1)[0] if stderr.strip() else "no reason given"
    if run.returncode == 2:
        refuse(f"{STALL_CHECK} refused this report: {first}")
    if run.returncode not in (0, 1):
        refuse(f"{STALL_CHECK} exited {run.returncode}: {first}")
    rows = {}
    for number, line in enumerate(stdout.split("\n"), 1):
        if not line:
            continue
        if "\r" in line:
            refuse(f"line {number} of {STALL_CHECK}'s output holds a carriage return")
        cells = line.split("\t")
        if tuple(cells) == STALL_HEADER:
            continue
        if len(cells) != len(STALL_HEADER):
            refuse(f"line {number} of {STALL_CHECK}'s output has {len(cells)} cells, not {' '.join(STALL_HEADER)}")
        if cells[1] not in STALL_STATES:
            refuse(
                f"line {number} of {STALL_CHECK}'s output has the state {cells[1]!r}, not one of {' '.join(STALL_STATES)}"
            )
        if STALL_AGE.fullmatch(cells[2]) is None:
            refuse(
                f"line {number} of {STALL_CHECK}'s output has the age_minutes {cells[2]!r}, not `-` or 1 to 10 digits"
            )
        if cells[0] in rows:
            refuse(f"{STALL_CHECK} names the unit {cells[0]} twice")
        rows[cells[0]] = (cells[1], cells[2], cells[3])
    return rows


def progress_column(unit, rows):
    if rows is None:
        return "unknown"
    if unit not in rows:
        return "no row"
    state, age, last_line = rows[unit]
    return f"{state}, {age} min, {last_line}"


def state_word(signals, acts, opened, running, rows):
    """The word and its reason, the first matching condition in order: done, stopped (nothing in flight), stopped
    (every worker silent), moving."""
    if signals and all(signal == "green" for _, signal, *_ in signals):
        return "done", "every table green"
    if not running and (acts or opened):
        return "stopped", f"nothing in flight, waiting on {len(acts)} operator acts and {len(opened)} decisions"
    if running and rows is not None and all(unit in rows and rows[unit][0] in SILENT for unit, _, _ in running):
        return "stopped", "every in-flight worker silent"
    return "moving", f"{len(running)} units in flight"


def section(lines, heading, items):
    """The heading, then the items or `none`."""
    lines.append(heading)
    lines.extend(items or ["none"])


def report(store, here, args):
    language = "ja" if args.ja else "en"
    now = timestamp(args.now, "--now") if args.now is not None else datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    signals, acts = elements(store)
    opened = open_gates(store)
    running = in_flight(store)
    age = last_record_age(store, now)
    rows = stall_rows(here, store, args)
    word, reason = state_word(signals, acts, opened, running, rows)
    headings = HEADINGS[language]
    lines = [f"{headings[0]}: {WORDS[language][word]}: {reason}, last record {age} min ago"]
    section(
        lines,
        headings[1],
        [
            f"{element}: {signal} {ok}/{count} OK, {ng} NG, {pending} pending"
            for element, signal, ok, ng, pending, count in signals
        ],
    )
    section(lines, headings[2], [f"{element} {row_id}: {command}" for element, row_id, command in acts])
    section(
        lines,
        headings[3],
        [f"{gate_id}: {gate} ({moment}; default {default})" for gate_id, gate, moment, default in opened],
    )
    section(
        lines,
        headings[4],
        [f"{unit} {track} pr {pr} progress: {progress_column(unit, rows)}" for unit, track, pr in running],
    )
    return "\n".join(one_line(line) for line in lines) + "\n"


def parser():
    top = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=LEVER, description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    top.add_argument("store", help="the program store directory (tests/, gates.md, units.tsv, decisions.tsv)")
    top.add_argument("--ja", action="store_true", help="the five headings and the state word in the operator's forms")
    top.add_argument("--now", help="the clock as <YYYY-MM-DD>T<HH:MM:SS>Z, for the ages and the stall check")
    top.add_argument("--progress-root", help="passed through to stall-check.py")
    return top


def main(argv=None):
    args = parser().parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv))
    if args.now is not None:
        timestamp(args.now, "--now")
    store = os.path.realpath(args.store)
    try:
        status = os.lstat(store)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"the store {store} cannot be read: {error.strerror}")
    if not stat.S_ISDIR(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"the store {store} is not a directory")
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    sys.stdout.write(report(store, here, args))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
