<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file regime-start
# @brief Start a program's orchestrator seat, or, as the supervisor's pass, relaunch every registered one that died.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U36: the operator starts the orchestrator seat and talks to it; an operator or coordinator command
#   from a terminal outside every seat starts and relaunches the worker seats (the hcom-orchestration skill's step 0);
#   only the orchestrator is supervised. Run `regime-start [<program>]` in the repository checkout. The store and
#   team are an explicit HCOM_DIR and HCOM_TEAM when set; else, for the dotfiles program before its one-time store
#   move (slug `dotfiles`, no `~/.local/state/hcom/dotfiles/origin`, and `~/.local/state/hcom-regime/hcom.db`
#   present), the pre-move pair `~/.local/state/hcom-regime` and `regime`, because a seat's environment carries
#   no HCOM_TEAM and the slug would name another thread (decisions 2026-10-24T10:19:06Z); else the sourced
#   regime-env derives both (U33). An explicit store must already exist. A program's store is chosen by the two-form
#   rule the levers read by (regime-cutover U221, store move 5 of 5, handoff/07-store-move-design.md; U216's
#   `store_resolve`): the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` when that directory exists, the root being
#   the fixed derivation `<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>` the sourced regime-env exports (U215),
#   else the checkout's own `.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`, the pre-move form that stands until
#   `regime-store-move` moves the live store; the form chosen is printed once on stderr, and with neither the
#   refusal names both. When a seat tagged `orchestrator` is
#   alive in the store (hcom status active, listening or blocked) it is reported, not duplicated; otherwise
#   `hcom-seat orchestrator` (the copy beside this file) launches it from the checkout, and the command waits up
#   to 120 s for it to be alive. Either way the checkout is registered for the supervisor (toplevel, store, team,
#   program, last seat name), and the command prints the seat's name and where to type. A checkout already
#   registered on another store or team is refused until regime-stop, and a store whose `origin` names another
#   checkout is refused, an explicit one included.
#
#   `--supervise` is one supervisor pass, run every 60 s by the launchd agent
#   `com.mryfmo.dotfiles.regime-supervisor` (macOS) or the `regime-supervisor.timer` user unit (Linux) once the
#   operator enables them; both ship disabled. For each registration with no orchestrator alive in its store it reads
#   hcom's newest stop record of the last seat (the `(latest)` event of `hcom list --stopped <base name>`):
#   `killed by:cli`, an operator's `hcom kill`, ends the supervision (the registration is removed); a record that
#   cannot be read launches nothing; anything else (a crash, a herdr restart) is relaunched like the interactive
#   form, at most once per backoff window (60 s doubling, saturated at 30 minutes, reset by a seat seen alive). Every
#   decision is a line in `<store>/supervisor.log`.
#
#   `--stop [--all]` is regime-stop (the lever beside this file runs it). Start, stop and the supervisor pass take
#   one host lock, the kernel's flock on `~/.local/state/regime-supervisor/supervisor.lock` (take_lock), so a stop
#   never interleaves with a relaunch: start and stop wait for it, a pass that finds it held skips. A registration is
#   `~/.local/state/regime-supervisor/<slug>-<first 12 hex of sha256(toplevel)>.conf`, one per checkout, with every
#   key exactly once (toplevel, hcom_dir, hcom_team, program, seat, base, fails, next); a registration that breaks
#   that, names another toplevel, or whose store's `origin` names another checkout is never launched, replaced or
#   stopped from.
# @arg $1 string Program name (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) whose store is `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` when that directory exists, else the checkout's `.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/` (the pre-move form), one of which must exist; optional.
# @option --supervise One supervisor pass over every registration; no other argument.
# @option --stop [--all] regime-stop.
# @env HCOM_DIR The hcom store (default: as described above).
# @env HCOM_TEAM The team (default: as described above).
# @stdout The seat's name and where to type (interactive form).
# @exitcode 0 The orchestrator is alive, or the pass ran.
# @exitcode 1 The launch failed or the seat did not come alive within 120 s.
# @exitcode 2 A refusal, before anything is started.
# @example
#   regime-start regime-cutover
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced regime-env helper sits (U33).
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

usage='usage: regime-start [<program>] | regime-start --supervise | regime-start --stop [--all]'
me=regime-start
registry=${HOME}/.local/state/regime-supervisor
lock=${registry}/supervisor.lock
lock_holder=''
name_grammar='^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$'
wait_seconds=${REGIME_START_WAIT_SECONDS:-120}
[[ ${wait_seconds} =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] || wait_seconds=120
lock_wait=${REGIME_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS:-300}
[[ ${lock_wait} =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] || lock_wait=300

refuse() {
    echo "${me}: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Take the host's one regime lock, which regime-start, its supervisor pass and regime-stop share, so a
#   stop never interleaves with a launch (U36 F2). The lock is the kernel's flock(2) on the file `lock`, held through
#   descriptor 9 of this process: perl (on both hosts; macOS ships no flock command) takes it on that inherited
#   descriptor and exits, and the lock stays with the open file, which this process keeps, and the subshell that runs
#   a launch keeps until the launch returns. Every hcom call and hcom-seat get the descriptor closed, so no seat or
#   hcom process ever holds it. The kernel releases it when the last holder exits or dies, so nothing is ever
#   recovered by age or pid, no other process can release it, and the file itself is never removed. The holder
#   writes its pid into the file, for messages only. A lock file replaced after it was opened (another inode at the
#   path) is opened again, at most three times.
# @arg $1 string `wait` (up to REGIME_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS, default 300) or `try` (once).
# @set lock_holder The pid the current holder wrote, when the lock is held.
# @exitcode 1 The lock is held by another process.
take_lock() {
    local seconds=0 status attempt=0
    [[ $1 == wait ]] && seconds=${lock_wait}
    mkdir -p "${registry}" || refuse "cannot create ${registry}"
    while ((attempt < 3)); do
        attempt=$((attempt + 1))
        [[ ! -L ${lock} ]] || refuse "${lock} is a symlink; nothing changed"
        exec 9>> "${lock}" || refuse "cannot open ${lock}; nothing changed"
        status=0
        perl -MFcntl=:flock -e '
            my ($wait, $owner, $path) = @ARGV;
            open(my $fh, ">>&=", 9) or exit 3;
            for my $try (0 .. $wait) {
                if (flock($fh, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)) {
                    my @held = stat($fh);
                    my @named = stat($path);
                    exit 4 unless @named && $named[0] == $held[0] && $named[1] == $held[1];
                    truncate($fh, 0) or exit 3;
                    syswrite($fh, "$owner\n") or exit 3;
                    exit 0;
                }
                sleep 1 if $try < $wait;
            }
            exit 1;' "${seconds}" "$$" "${lock}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) return 0 ;;
        1)
            lock_holder=$(cat "${lock}" 2> /dev/null) || lock_holder=''
            [[ ${lock_holder} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || lock_holder=unknown
            exec 9>&-
            return 1
            ;;
        4) exec 9>&- ;;
        *) refuse "cannot take the flock on ${lock} (perl exited ${status}); nothing changed" ;;
        esac
    done
    refuse "${lock} was replaced while it was being locked, three times; nothing changed"
}

# @description Print the registration file of a checkout: `<slug>-<first 12 hex of sha256(toplevel)>.conf`, so two
#   checkouts with one basename never share a registration (U36 F3).
# @arg $1 path The physical toplevel.
# @arg $2 string Its slug.
# @exitcode 1 The digest could not be computed.
registration_path() {
    local digest
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(printf '%s' "$1" | sha256sum) || return 1
    else
        digest=$(printf '%s' "$1" | shasum -a 256) || return 1
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s/%s-%s.conf\n' "${registry}" "$2" "${digest:0:12}"
}

# @description Read a registration into reg_top, reg_store, reg_team, reg_program, reg_seat, reg_base, reg_fails and
#   reg_next. Every key must appear exactly once and nothing else may (U36 F4); the seat is `orchestrator-<base>`;
#   the counters have bounded lengths (U36 F5); and the file must be the one registration_path names for its own
#   toplevel, so a registration copied to another checkout's name is refused, and a store with an `origin` file
#   (a derived one, written by regime-init) must name that toplevel (U36 F3).
# @arg $1 path The registration file.
# @stdout Nothing.
# @stderr Nothing.
# @set reg_error Why the registration is unusable, empty when it is usable.
read_registration() {
    local conf=$1 line key value expected slug recorded
    # Bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash) has no associative arrays, so the keys seen are one space-separated string.
    local seen=' '
    reg_error='' reg_top='' reg_store='' reg_team='' reg_program='' reg_seat='' reg_base='' reg_fails='' reg_next=''
    if ! [[ -f ${conf} && -r ${conf} ]]; then
        reg_error='unreadable'
        return 0
    fi
    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n ${line} ]]; do
        key=${line%%=*}
        value=${line#*=}
        if [[ ${line} != *=* ]]; then
            reg_error="a line without a key: '${line}'"
            return 0
        fi
        case ${key} in
        toplevel | hcom_dir | hcom_team | program | seat | base | fails | next) ;;
        *)
            reg_error="unknown key '${key}'"
            return 0
            ;;
        esac
        if [[ ${seen} == *" ${key} "* ]]; then
            reg_error="key '${key}' appears twice"
            return 0
        fi
        seen+="${key} "
        printf -v "reg_${key/toplevel/top}" '%s' "${value}"
    done < "${conf}" || {
        reg_error='unreadable'
        return 0
    }
    reg_store=${reg_hcom_dir:-} reg_team=${reg_hcom_team:-}
    for key in toplevel hcom_dir hcom_team program seat base fails next; do
        if [[ ${seen} != *" ${key} "* ]]; then
            reg_error="key '${key}' is missing"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    if [[ ${reg_top} != /* || ! -d ${reg_top} || ${reg_store} != /* || ! -d ${reg_store} ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path prefix test, not a comparison of two paths
        reg_error='the toplevel or the store is not an existing absolute directory'
    elif [[ ! ${reg_team} =~ ${name_grammar} || ! ${reg_base} =~ ${name_grammar} ]]; then
        reg_error='the team or the base name is outside the grammar'
    elif [[ -n ${reg_program} && ! ${reg_program} =~ ${name_grammar} ]]; then
        reg_error='the program is outside the grammar'
    elif [[ ${reg_seat} != "orchestrator-${reg_base}" ]]; then
        reg_error="the seat '${reg_seat}' is not orchestrator-<base>"
    elif [[ ! ${reg_fails} =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ || ! ${reg_next} =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ ]]; then
        reg_error='the counters are not bounded numbers'
    elif ! slug=$(regime_slug "${reg_top}" 2> /dev/null) || ! expected=$(registration_path "${reg_top}" "${slug}"); then
        reg_error="cannot derive the registration name of ${reg_top}"
    elif [[ ${conf##*/} != "${expected##*/}" ]]; then
        reg_error="the file name does not belong to the toplevel ${reg_top}"
    elif [[ -e ${reg_store}/origin ]]; then
        if ! recorded=$(cat "${reg_store}/origin" 2> /dev/null); then
            reg_error="cannot read ${reg_store}/origin"
        elif [[ ${recorded} != "${reg_top}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are pwd -P forms (regime-init, regime_toplevel)
            reg_error="the store ${reg_store} belongs to ${recorded}, not ${reg_top}"
        fi
    fi
    return 0
}

# @description Append one timestamped line to the store's supervisor log; a log that cannot be written is said on stderr.
# @arg $1 path The hcom store.
# @arg $@ string The line.
log_line() {
    local store=$1 stamp
    shift
    stamp=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) || stamp=unknown-time
    printf '%s %s\n' "${stamp}" "$*" >> "${store}/supervisor.log" 2> /dev/null ||
        echo "regime-start: cannot write ${store}/supervisor.log: $*" >&2
}

# @description Print `<name> <base name>` of every alive seat tagged orchestrator in the store HCOM_DIR names.
# @exitcode 1 hcom could not be read (a failed read is never "no seat").
alive_orchestrators() {
    local listing name base tag status
    listing=$(hcom list --format '{name} {base_name} {tag} {status}' 9>&-) || return 1
    while read -r name base tag status; do
        [[ ${tag} == orchestrator ]] || continue
        case ${status} in
        active | listening | blocked) printf '%s %s\n' "${name}" "${base}" ;;
        esac
    done <<< "${listing}"
}

# @description Launch the orchestrator seat from the checkout and wait for it to be alive.
# @arg $1 path The checkout's toplevel.
# @stdout `<name> <base name>` of the seat that came alive.
# @exitcode 1 hcom-seat failed, or no seat was alive within the wait.
launch_orchestrator() {
    local top=$1 status=0 waited=0 alive=''
    # Killing regime-start cannot release the lock while a launch runs (U36 F2): both callers run this function in a
    # command-substitution subshell, which keeps descriptor 9 until the launch and its wait return, and the subshell
    # below keeps it until hcom-seat returns, so the hold does not depend on the caller (the command after hcom-seat
    # keeps bash from exec-ing it in place of that subshell). hcom-seat, and the hcom and seat processes it starts,
    # get the descriptor closed, so a detached seat never holds the lock after the launch.
    (
        cd "${top}" || exit 1
        "${LEVER_DIR}/hcom-seat" orchestrator 9>&-
        launched=$?
        exit "${launched}"
    ) >&2 || status=$?
    # hcom's status 2 is "still launching": wait for the seat like a ready one.
    if ((status != 0 && status != 2)); then
        echo "regime-start: hcom-seat orchestrator exited ${status}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    while ((waited <= wait_seconds)); do
        if alive=$(alive_orchestrators) && [[ -n ${alive} ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${alive%%$'\n'*}"
            return 0
        fi
        sleep 2
        waited=$((waited + 2))
    done
    echo "regime-start: no orchestrator seat alive in ${HCOM_DIR} after ${wait_seconds} s" >&2
    return 1
}

# @description Write a registration atomically (a temporary file, then a rename).
# @arg $1 path The registration file.
# @arg $@ string `key=value` lines.
write_registration() {
    local file=$1 temp
    shift
    mkdir -p "${registry}"
    temp=$(mktemp "${file}.XXXXXX")
    printf '%s\n' "$@" > "${temp}"
    mv -f "${temp}" "${file}"
}

# @description Print the backoff after the given number of failed launches: 60 s doubling, saturated at 1800 s
#   before it can overflow (U36 F5).
# @arg $1 int Failed launches in a row, at least 1.
backoff_seconds() {
    local delay=60 step=1
    while ((step < $1 && delay < 1800)); do
        delay=$((delay * 2))
        step=$((step + 1))
    done
    ((delay <= 1800)) || delay=1800
    printf '%s\n' "${delay}"
}

mode=start all=0
case ${1:-} in
--supervise)
    (($# == 1)) || refuse "${usage}"
    mode=supervise
    ;;
--stop)
    me=regime-stop
    case ${#}:${2:-} in
    1:) ;;
    2:--all) all=1 ;;
    *) refuse 'usage: regime-stop [--all]' ;;
    esac
    mode=stop
    ;;
*) (($# <= 1)) || refuse "${usage}" ;;
esac
command -v hcom > /dev/null || refuse 'hcom not found on PATH'
[[ -x ${LEVER_DIR}/hcom-seat ]] || refuse "hcom-seat is not beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/hcom-seat"
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || refuse "regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"

if [[ ${mode} == supervise ]]; then
    # A pass that finds the lock held skips: the next one comes in 60 s.
    if ! take_lock try; then
        echo "regime-start: pid ${lock_holder} holds ${lock}; this pass skips" >&2
        exit 0
    fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    for conf in "${registry}"/*.conf; do
        [[ -f ${conf} ]] || continue
        newest=''
        read_registration "${conf}"
        if [[ -n ${reg_error} ]]; then
            echo "regime-start: skipped ${conf}: ${reg_error}" >&2
            if [[ ${reg_store} == /* && -d ${reg_store} ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path prefix test
                log_line "${reg_store}" "skipped ${conf}: ${reg_error}; nothing launched"
            fi
            continue
        fi
        top=${reg_top} store=${reg_store} team=${reg_team} program=${reg_program}
        seat=${reg_seat} base=${reg_base} fails=$((10#${reg_fails})) next=$((10#${reg_next}))
        export HCOM_DIR=${store} HCOM_TEAM=${team}
        if ! alive=$(alive_orchestrators); then
            log_line "${store}" "hcom list failed; nothing launched"
            continue
        fi
        if [[ -n ${alive} ]]; then
            read -r seat base <<< "${alive%%$'\n'*}"
            if ((fails != 0)) || [[ ${seat} != "${reg_seat}" ]]; then
                write_registration "${conf}" "toplevel=${top}" "hcom_dir=${store}" "hcom_team=${team}" "program=${program}" "seat=${seat}" "base=${base}" fails=0 next=0
            fi
            continue
        fi
        if ! stopped=$(hcom list --stopped "${base}" 9>&-); then
            log_line "${store}" "hcom list --stopped ${base} failed; nothing launched"
            continue
        fi
        # The named form ends with `Stop history (<n> events):` and one `<age>  [<reason> by:<who>]` line per event,
        # the newest marked `(latest)` (hcom 0.7.30 and 0.7.31, measured; 0.7.31 on 2026-10-24, U22b). A stop record
        # that cannot be read is no license.
        newest=$(grep -m1 -E '\[[^]]+\] \(latest\)$' <<< "${stopped}" || true)
        newest=${newest#"${newest%%[![:space:]]*}"}
        if [[ -z ${newest} ]]; then
            log_line "${store}" "cannot read the stop record of ${seat}; nothing launched"
            continue
        fi
        if [[ ${newest} == *"[killed by:cli] (latest)" ]]; then
            log_line "${store}" "${seat} was stopped with hcom kill; supervision of ${top} ends (registration removed)"
            rm -f "${conf}"
            continue
        fi
        if ((now < next)); then
            continue
        fi
        log_line "${store}" "no orchestrator alive (last seat ${seat}: ${newest}); relaunching from ${top}"
        if alive=$(launch_orchestrator "${top}" 2>> "${store}/supervisor.log"); then
            read -r seat base <<< "${alive}"
            log_line "${store}" "relaunched ${seat}"
            write_registration "${conf}" "toplevel=${top}" "hcom_dir=${store}" "hcom_team=${team}" "program=${program}" "seat=${seat}" "base=${base}" fails=0 next=0
        else
            ((fails >= 9999)) || fails=$((fails + 1))
            delay=$(backoff_seconds "${fails}")
            log_line "${store}" "relaunch failed (${fails} in a row); next attempt in ${delay} s"
            write_registration "${conf}" "toplevel=${top}" "hcom_dir=${store}" "hcom_team=${team}" "program=${program}" "seat=${seat}" "base=${base}" "fails=${fails}" "next=$((now + delay))"
        fi
    done
    exit 0
fi

# @description Choose the store and team of this checkout when it has no registration: an explicit pair, else the
#   dotfiles pre-move pair, else regime-env's derivation. A store whose `origin` names another checkout is refused,
#   an explicit one included (U36 F3).
choose_store() {
    local legacy=${HOME}/.local/state/hcom-regime recorded
    if [[ -z ${HCOM_DIR:-} && -z ${HCOM_TEAM:-} && ${slug} == dotfiles && ! -e ${HOME}/.local/state/hcom/dotfiles/origin && -f ${legacy}/hcom.db ]]; then
        # The dotfiles program before its one-time store move (README "Run a program in another repository").
        export HCOM_DIR=${legacy} HCOM_TEAM=regime
        echo "${me}: the dotfiles program has not moved its store yet; using HCOM_DIR=${HCOM_DIR} HCOM_TEAM=${HCOM_TEAM}" >&2
    fi
    regime_env regime-start || exit 2
    [[ -d ${HCOM_DIR} ]] || refuse "the hcom store ${HCOM_DIR} does not exist; run regime-init <program> first or set an existing store"
    [[ ${HCOM_TEAM} =~ ${name_grammar} ]] || refuse "team '${HCOM_TEAM}' is outside ${name_grammar}"
    if [[ -e ${HCOM_DIR}/origin ]]; then
        recorded=$(cat "${HCOM_DIR}/origin") || refuse "cannot read ${HCOM_DIR}/origin"
        if [[ ${recorded} != "${top}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are pwd -P forms (regime-init, regime_toplevel)
            refuse "the store ${HCOM_DIR} belongs to ${recorded}, not ${top}"
        fi
    fi
}

# @description Choose the program store (regime-cutover U221, store move 5 of 5, handoff/07-store-move-design.md;
#   the `store_resolve` shape of U216's pr-merge.sh and pr-close.sh, in this lever's own body: no helper file,
#   standing order 36): the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` when that path exists, which must then be
#   a directory of this user and no symlink (a link is refused by name before anything is read through it; a file or
#   another user's directory is refused by name too), the root being the fixed derivation regime-env exported from the
#   physical HOME and the slug when choose_store ran it (U215); else the checkout's own
#   `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`, the pre-move form that stands until `regime-store-move` moves
#   the live store, which must exist as a directory; with neither the refusal names both. Nothing is written. The form
#   chosen is printed once on stderr (`store: derived <dir>`, or `store: checkout <dir> (pre-move form, removed by
#   U221)`), the line the coordinator reads after the deploy.
# @arg $1 string The program name.
# @set store_dir The chosen store.
store_resolve() {
    local program=$1 store_derived store_checkout
    [[ -n ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT:-} ]] ||
        refuse "regime-env derived no store root for ${top}; the program store is judged under it (U216, U221)"
    store_derived=${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/${program}
    store_checkout=${top}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
    [[ ! -L ${store_derived} ]] ||
        refuse "${store_derived} is a symlink; the derived program store is a plain directory of this user under the store root ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}, and nothing is read through a link"
    if [[ -e ${store_derived} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${store_derived} && -O ${store_derived} ]] ||
            refuse "${store_derived} exists but is not a directory of this user; the derived program store under ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT} is read only as one"
        store_dir=${store_derived}
        echo "${me}: store: derived ${store_dir}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    [[ -d ${store_checkout} ]] ||
        refuse "no program store at ${store_derived} (the derived store, U216) or ${store_checkout} (the checkout's own, the pre-move form); run regime-init ${program} first"
    store_dir=${store_checkout}
    echo "${me}: store: checkout ${store_dir} (pre-move form, removed by U221)" >&2
}

top=$(regime_toplevel) || refuse "run ${me} inside the repository checkout"
slug=$(regime_slug "${top}") || refuse "cannot derive a repository slug from ${top}"
conf=$(registration_path "${top}" "${slug}") || refuse "cannot hash the toplevel ${top}"

if [[ ${mode} == stop ]]; then
    take_lock wait || refuse "pid ${lock_holder} still holds ${lock} after ${lock_wait} s; nothing changed"
    if [[ -e ${conf} ]]; then
        # The registered store wins: it is the one the supervisor would relaunch into.
        read_registration "${conf}"
        [[ -z ${reg_error} ]] || refuse "the registration ${conf} is unusable (${reg_error}); check it and remove it by hand; nothing changed"
        if [[ ${reg_top} != "${top}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are pwd -P forms
            refuse "the registration ${conf} names ${reg_top}, not ${top}; nothing changed"
        fi
        export HCOM_DIR=${reg_store} HCOM_TEAM=${reg_team}
    else
        choose_store
    fi
    listing=$(hcom list --format '{name} {tag} {status}' 9>&-) || refuse "cannot read the seats of ${HCOM_DIR} (hcom list failed); nothing changed"
    rm -f "${conf}"
    log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-stop: supervision of ${top} ended"
    failed=0 stopped=0
    while read -r name tag status; do
        [[ -n ${name} ]] || continue
        case ${status} in active | listening | blocked) ;; *) continue ;; esac
        ((all)) || [[ ${tag} == orchestrator ]] || continue
        if hcom kill "${name}" --go > /dev/null 9>&-; then
            echo "regime-stop: stopped ${name}"
            log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-stop: stopped ${name}"
            stopped=$((stopped + 1))
        else
            echo "regime-stop: hcom kill ${name} failed" >&2
            failed=1
        fi
    done <<< "${listing}"
    ((stopped || failed)) || echo "regime-stop: no seat to stop in ${HCOM_DIR}; supervision ended"
    exit "${failed}"
fi

program=${1:-}
[[ -z ${program} || ${program} =~ ${name_grammar} ]] || refuse "program '${program}' is outside ${name_grammar}"
choose_store
store_dir=''
if [[ -n ${program} ]]; then
    store_resolve "${program}"
fi
take_lock wait || refuse "pid ${lock_holder} still holds ${lock} after ${lock_wait} s; nothing changed"
# This checkout's own registration is replaced only for the same store and team (U36 F3).
if [[ -e ${conf} ]]; then
    read_registration "${conf}"
    [[ -z ${reg_error} ]] || refuse "the registration ${conf} is unusable (${reg_error}); check it, remove it, then run regime-start again"
    if [[ ${reg_store} != "${HCOM_DIR}" || ${reg_team} != "${HCOM_TEAM}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both are the absolute store paths regime-start wrote
        refuse "this checkout is registered on the store ${reg_store} and team ${reg_team}; run regime-stop first to move it to ${HCOM_DIR} and ${HCOM_TEAM}"
    fi
fi
alive=$(alive_orchestrators) || refuse "cannot read the seats of ${HCOM_DIR} (hcom list failed)"
if [[ -n ${alive} ]]; then
    read -r seat base <<< "${alive%%$'\n'*}"
    state="is already alive"
    log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-start found ${seat} alive; registered for the supervisor"
else
    alive=$(launch_orchestrator "${top}") || {
        log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-start could not launch the orchestrator from ${top}"
        exit 1
    }
    read -r seat base <<< "${alive}"
    state="is listening"
    log_line "${HCOM_DIR}" "regime-start launched ${seat} from ${top}"
fi
write_registration "${conf}" "toplevel=${top}" "hcom_dir=${HCOM_DIR}" "hcom_team=${HCOM_TEAM}" "program=${program}" "seat=${seat}" "base=${base}" fails=0 next=0
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the backticks are text: the pane's name, set off for the reader
printf '%s %s on team %s. Type your instruction in the pane `orchestrator`; the store is %s.\n' \
    "${seat}" "${state}" "${HCOM_TEAM}" "${store_dir:-${HCOM_DIR}}"
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file regime-stop
# @brief Stop a program's orchestrator seat on purpose and end its supervision.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U36. Run in the repository checkout. It is `regime-start --stop` (the regime-start beside this
#   file), so it takes the same host lock as regime-start and its supervisor pass and never interleaves with a
#   relaunch. Under that lock it reads this checkout's own registration (`~/.local/state/regime-supervisor/
#   <slug>-<hash of the toplevel>.conf`, which must name this toplevel), removes it, then runs
#   `hcom kill <name> --go` for every alive seat tagged `orchestrator` in the registered store (with `--all`, for
#   every alive seat in that store), and logs each step in `<store>/supervisor.log`. Without a registration it uses
#   the store regime-start would choose (an explicit HCOM_DIR and HCOM_TEAM, the dotfiles pre-move pair, else
#   regime-env), and a store whose `origin` names another checkout is refused. A seat's worktree and branch stay; a
#   later `regime-start` starts the program again.
# @option --all Also stop the worker seats of the store.
# @stdout One line per seat stopped, or that none was alive.
# @exitcode 0 Stopped, or nothing was alive.
# @exitcode 1 An hcom kill failed (the registration is already removed).
# @exitcode 2 A refusal, before anything is changed.
# @example
#   regime-stop
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.

lever_self_check() {

    }

Each round's audit found a same-user writer the control did not see: a record written between two observations, a descriptor opened before the mode change, a pathname replaced between an identity read and its removal, two movers overlapping. A same-user writer defeats every observation, mode and identity control. The one actor who can make the host quiescent is the operator, by stopping every seat and ending every coordinator process, and the write to the checkout was the operator's already; so the copy phase left the lever. It reads, judges and prints the operator's procedure as commands to run from a terminal on a quiescent host. Why it no longer compares the live store with origin's main (U393). Until U393 the pre-move run refused while the live store, redacted, differed from main at the published prefix. <pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file regime-store-move
# @brief Judge whether a program's live store may move out of the main checkout to the derived store root, and print the operator's whole procedure, the copy included; this lever moves nothing.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U221, store move 5 of 5 (handoff/07-store-move-design.md; U215 gave regime-env the root, U216 and
#   U220 gave the levers the two-form rule, U219 the seats' grants), reshaped by U221b, U221c and U221d (verdicts
#   U221-e82581f3, U221-738e89ca and U221-595a116a, class move-race; the mechanism-change rows of decisions
#   2026-11-08T05:44:20Z and 2026-11-08T10:26:46Z, form remove), hardened in its reads by U221e (verdict

#   while `main` holds its redacted copies, so the checkout is never clean once main has published them and nothing

#   gate could never pass. It guarded nothing the procedure does not already check: line 3 (`diff -r` and the count)

#   publication, listed from the derived store (U220), carries whatever the live store held beyond main. So the
#   pre-move run reads no origin and runs no git but the checkout's `rev-parse`.
#   What it reads. The main checkout (a linked worktree is refused), `regime_env` for the root, the live store's walk
#   (U220's derived walk, `find ! -type d` through `read_listing`: every entry a regular file below the store with no
#   symlink component, no control character, no `..`, no name beginning with `.`, no name beginning or ending with a
#   space; `redact-words.txt` included, since the new root is the live store), and whether the derived store
#   `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` exists (a link or a file there, or a component whose mode is not 0700, is
#   refused by name).
#   Before the move (the derived store absent; the store root `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}` must exist, as hcom-seat makes it
#   when a seat starts, U219) it counts the live store's files and prints the verdict `ready: <n> live files; the
#   derived store is absent` and the procedure, seven numbered lines, each a complete command or one sentence: (1)
#   stop every seat and end every coordinator process (`regime-stop --all`, the kit's stop); (2) the copy of the
#   checkout store to `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` with its modes and times kept (`cp -a`), then the group and
#   other bits removed below it (`go-rwx`, recursive, in the same line: `cp -a` keeps the checkout store's 0755, and
#   the post-move check of line 7 holds the program store to 0700, the mode the kit gives every store it makes;
#   U221e); (3) the recursive comparison of the two and the count of the copy's files (`<n>`); (4) the checkout's own
#   `checkout -- <prefix>`; (5) its `clean -fd -- <prefix>`; (6) its `pull --ff-only`; (7) this lever again. The

#   its stdout goes to a scratch file and its stderr to another, and a non-zero status or anything on stderr is a
#   failed read that refuses naming the producer (a `wc` that warns while printing a valid count is no count; round 4
#   read the status alone). Every listing is NUL-delimited and read with `IFS= read -r -d ''`, so every byte of a

# @stdout Before the move: `ready: <n> live files; the derived store is absent`, then the procedure, seven numbered lines. After it: `moved: the derived store holds <m> files; the checkout store is clean against HEAD`.

# @exitcode 1 A write under the scratch directory failed (the file list; nothing is printed on stdout), or the scratch directory could not be removed after a `ready` or `moved` verdict (the verdict line stands).

# @example
#   regime-store-move regime-cutover
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes. The
#   HOME read and the hash read are each tested where they stand (an `if`, a `||` with the refusal), so no read
#   carries a producer-status allow comment (U221).
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced libraries sit.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    # The checkout layout unless this file sits in the installed directory under the physical HOME; a HOME that cannot
    # be entered is the checkout layout too, decided here, not by an empty value read later.
    LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    if home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P); then
        if [[ ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
            LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
        fi
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || {
            echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
            exit 2
        }
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || {
            echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
            exit 2
        }
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }

# The isolated git and the environment scrub come from the library beside this script (U113). The scrub runs here,
# before the first git: GIT_CONFIG_* would add config, includes and URL rewrites to every git command, and GIT_DIR
# would point every command at another repository.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh ]] || {
    echo "regime-store-move: refused: git-isolated.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh"
# shellcheck disable=SC2119 # no name is kept: every GIT_* and transport variable goes
git_env_scrub

[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh ]] || {
    echo "regime-store-move: refused: read-lib.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/read-lib.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh"

# The store root (U215, U216): the program stores lie under `REGIME_STORE_ROOT`, the root the sourced regime-env
# derives from the physical HOME and this checkout's slug and holds component by component; the helper is sourced
# from the directory this lever runs from and self-checked like a lever (U33), so a rewritten copy stops this lever.
# The call that derives the root comes after this lever's own checkout checks, below.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || {
    echo "regime-store-move: refused: regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"

lever=regime-store-move
usage='usage: regime-store-move <program>'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1 (the EXIT trap removes the scratch directory).
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

scratch=''
# @description The EXIT trap: the scratch directory goes, and nothing else; this lever makes nothing anywhere else.
#   The removal's status is read (U221e): the directory holds the producers' outputs and the live store's file list,
#   so a removal that fails names the directory on stderr and ends a run that would have exited 0 with exit 1 (the
#   verdict line already printed stands; the status says the run did not end clean). A refusal's or a failure's own
#   status is kept: it already says the run did not end clean, and the line names the directory either way.
cleanup() {
    local cl_status=$?
    if [[ -n ${scratch} && -d ${scratch} ]]; then
        if ! rm -r "${scratch}"; then
            echo "${lever}: could not remove ${scratch}; remove it by hand (it holds the run's read files and the live store's file list)" >&2
            [[ ${cl_status} != 0 ]] || exit 1
        fi
    fi
}

# @description Set the variable $2 to the one line a producer prints (a path, an object id, a mode), the producer run
#   through `read_listing` (its status read, its stderr captured to `<prefix>.err`: a non-zero status or anything on
#   stderr is a failed read naming the producer) and its output read back whole through `read_file`, the one final
#   newline removed; a producer that prints nothing is a failed read here (no path, no id and no mode is an absence).
# @arg $1 path The scratch prefix for the output file and the stderr file.
# @arg $2 string The variable that receives the line.
# @arg $@ string The producer and its arguments: a command or a function, run as written.
# @exitcode 0 The variable holds the line.
# @exitcode 2 The producer failed, warned or printed nothing, or a scratch file could not be written or read.
read_line() {
    local ln_prefix=$1 ln_name=$2 ln_value=''
    shift 2
    read_listing "${ln_prefix}.out" "${ln_prefix}.err" "$@" || return 2
    read_file "${ln_prefix}.out" ln_value || return 2
    ln_value=${ln_value%$'\n'}
    printf -v "${ln_name}" '%s' "${ln_value}"
}

# @description Print the number `wc` reports for a file: `wc <flag>` through `read_listing` (a `wc` that warns while
#   printing a valid count is a failed read, not a count; U221e), the count read back through `read_file`, its blanks
#   removed and held to digits.
# @arg $1 path The file to count.
# @arg $2 path The scratch prefix for wc's output file and stderr file.
# @arg $3 string wc's flag (`-c`, `-l`).
# @exitcode 0 The count was printed.
# @exitcode 2 wc failed or warned, or printed no number.
count_with_wc() {
    local cw_file=$1 cw_prefix=$2 cw_flag=$3 cw_out=''
    read_listing "${cw_prefix}.count" "${cw_prefix}.wc.err" wc "${cw_flag}" < "${cw_file}" || return 2
    read_file "${cw_prefix}.count" cw_out || return 2
    cw_out=${cw_out//[[:space:]]/}
    [[ ${cw_out} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 2
    printf '%s\n' "${cw_out}"
}

# @description Print the number of entries of a NUL-separated listing: `tr -cd '\000'` keeps the NULs alone, through
#   `read_listing` (its status read, its stderr captured; an empty result is zero entries, not a failure), and
#   `count_with_wc` counts the bytes left.
# @arg $1 path The listing.
# @arg $2 path The scratch prefix for the two outputs and the two stderr files.
# @exitcode 0 The count was printed.
# @exitcode 2 tr or wc failed or warned, or wc printed no number.
count_entries() {
    local ce_listing=$1 ce_prefix=$2 ce_status=0
    read_listing "${ce_prefix}.nuls" "${ce_prefix}.tr.err" tr -cd '\000' < "${ce_listing}" || ce_status=$?
    [[ ${ce_status} != 2 ]] || return 2
    count_with_wc "${ce_prefix}.nuls" "${ce_prefix}" -c || return 2
}

# @description Print the operator's procedure, seven numbered lines, each a complete command or one sentence, the
#   paths quoted for the shell: the stop of every seat and every coordinator process (`regime-stop --all`, the kit's
#   stop, which is `regime-start --stop --all`), the copy of the checkout store to the derived store with its modes
#   and times kept and then the group and other bits removed below it in the same line (`cp -a` keeps the checkout
#   store's 0755; the post-move check of line 7 holds the program store to 0700, the kit's mode for every store;
#   U221e, verdict U221-af547232 P1), the recursive comparison and the count of the copy's files, the checkout's own
#   `checkout -- <prefix>`, `clean -fd -- <prefix>` and `pull --ff-only`, and this lever again, which then reports
#   the moved state. The procedure is printed, never run: the host is quiescent only under the operator's hand, and
#   the live checkout is written by the operator's hand alone, once (the struck order 40's successor rule).
# @arg $1 int The number of files of the live store, the count the copy must show (the note of line 3).
print_procedure() {
    local pp_total=$1
    printf '1. Stop every seat and end every coordinator process: run regime-stop --all in %q (the stop of the kit, regime-start --stop --all), confirm with hcom list -v that no seat of this checkout is alive, and close every session that runs a lever of the kit against it.\n' "${top_real}"
    printf '2. cp -a %q %q && chmod -R go-rwx %q\n' "${live}" "${dest}" "${dest}"
    printf '3. diff -r %q %q && find %q -type f | wc -l   # expect no line from diff and the count %s\n' "${live}" "${dest}" "${dest}" "${pp_total}"
    printf '4. git -C %q checkout -- %q\n' "${top_real}" "${records}"
    printf '5. git -C %q clean -fd -- %q\n' "${top_real}" "${records}"
    printf '6. git -C %q pull --ff-only\n' "${top_real}"
    printf '7. regime-store-move %q\n' "${program}"
}

case ${OSTYPE} in
darwin*) stat_mode=(-f %Lp) ;;
*) stat_mode=(-c %a) ;;
esac

# @description Hold one component of the destination (`regime-store`, the store root `<slug>`, the program directory)
#   as regime-init holds them (U215b, U215c): a symbolic link refuses by name; present, it must be a real directory of
#   this user whose mode is 0700, read by `/usr/bin/stat` (the system's, so a coreutils `stat` first on PATH, whose
#   flags differ, never steers the read) through `read_line` (its status and its stderr both read; a failed or
#   warning read refuses, standing order 21); absent, nothing. Nothing is written.
# @arg $1 path The directory.
# @arg $2 string What it is, for the refusal.
store_dir_hold() {
    local path=$1 what=$2 mode=''
    [[ ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "${what} ${path} is a symlink"
    [[ -e ${path} ]] || return 0
    [[ -d ${path} && -O ${path} ]] || refuse "${what} ${path} is not a real directory of this user"
    read_line "${scratch}/mode" mode /usr/bin/stat "${stat_mode[@]}" "${path}" ||
        refuse "cannot read the mode of ${what} ${path} (/usr/bin/stat failed or warned)"
    [[ ${mode} == 700 ]] || refuse "${what} ${path} has mode ${mode}, not 0700"
}

# @description Hold one entry of the live store's walk to the derived walk's shape (U220, U28b F2): below the store,
#   no control character (a newline would hide a component), no `..`, no component beginning with `.` (no record
#   carries such a name, and the derived form's walk refuses it, so the move does too), no component beginning or
#   ending with a space (no record carries such a name either; `units.tsv ` beside `units.tsv` is a second file the
#   sync never published, and round 4's `read` trimmed the space off before this check saw it; U221e), no symbolic
#   link at any component, a regular file whose directory resolves (`pwd -P`) inside the store; then append its
#   relative path to the file list. A refusal names the entry's relative path, never its text.
# @arg $1 path The entry as find prints it, every byte kept (the caller reads the listing with `IFS= read -r -d ''`).
# @arg $2 path The NUL-separated file list the relative path is appended to.
check_entry() {
    local ce_entry=$1 ce_out=$2 rel prefix part rest entry_dir
    case ${ce_entry} in # lint-comparisons: allow a path as find prints it, refused unless below the live store
    "${live}"/?*) ;;
    *) refuse "the walk of ${live} names a path outside the live store; the procedure is not printed" ;;
    esac
    rel=${ce_entry#"${live}/"}
    [[ ${rel} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || refuse "a path of the live store holds a control character; the procedure is not printed" # lint-comparisons: allow a character test on the raw path
    [[ ${rel} != *..* ]] || refuse "a path of the live store holds '..': ${rel}; the procedure is not printed"                 # lint-comparisons: allow refuses a raw path that holds ..
    prefix=${live}
    rest=${rel}
    # Split on `/` by parameter expansion (no here-string, so no temporary file can go missing, U101).
    while [[ -n ${rest} ]]; do
        part=${rest%%/*}
        if [[ ${rest} == */* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow splits the path into its components
            rest=${rest#*/}
        else
            rest=''
        fi
        [[ ${part} != .* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow a name test on one component of the walk
            refuse "a name of the live store begins with '.', which no record carries and the derived walk refuses (U220): ${rel}; remove it by hand, the procedure is not printed"
        [[ ${part} != ' '* && ${part} != *' ' ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow a name test on one component of the walk
            refuse "a name of the live store begins or ends with a space: '${rel}'; no record carries such a name; remove it by hand, the procedure is not printed"
        prefix=${prefix}/${part}
        [[ ! -L ${prefix} ]] || refuse "a component of a path of the live store is a symlink: ${prefix}; the derived walk refuses it (U220); remove it by hand, the procedure is not printed"
    done
    [[ -f ${prefix} ]] || refuse "a path of the live store is not a regular file: ${rel}; the procedure is not printed"
    entry_dir=$(cd "${prefix%/*}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${rel}"
    [[ ${entry_dir} == "${live}" || ${entry_dir} == "${live}"/* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        refuse "a path of the live store resolves outside ${live}: ${rel}; the procedure is not printed"
    printf '%s\0' "${rel}" >> "${ce_out}" || fail 'cannot write the file list'
}

# @description Walk the live store as U220's derived walk does: the directories first, each readable and searchable
#   (find exits non-zero for a directory it cannot read, and any warning of either producer refuses the run,
#   read_listing); then every entry below it that is not a directory (`-type f` would skip a symbolic link instead of
#   refusing it), each held by check_entry, its relative path appended to the file list. Both listings are
#   NUL-delimited and read with `IFS= read -r -d ''`, every byte of a name kept (U221e). Neither find output is shown
#   (a store path may hold a redact word).
# @arg $1 path The NUL-separated file list this writes, under the scratch directory.
walk_store() {
    local ws_out=$1 ws_status=0 entry=''
    read_listing "${ws_out}.dirs" "${ws_out}.dirs.err" find "${live}" -type d -print0 ||
        refuse "the directory walk of the live store ${live} failed or warned (find; its output is withheld); the procedure is not printed"
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
        [[ -r ${entry} && -x ${entry} ]] || refuse "a directory under ${live} cannot be read or entered; the procedure is not printed"
    done < "${ws_out}.dirs"
    [[ -z ${entry} ]] || refuse "the directory walk of ${live} ends mid-entry; the procedure is not printed"
    read_listing "${ws_out}.listing" "${ws_out}.listing.err" find "${live}" ! -type d -print0 || ws_status=$?
    case ${ws_status} in
    0) ;;
    1) refuse "the live store ${live} holds no file; nothing to move" ;;
    *) refuse "the walk of the live store ${live} failed or warned (find; its output is withheld); the procedure is not printed" ;;
    esac
    : > "${ws_out}" || fail "cannot write the file list ${ws_out}"
    entry=''
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
        check_entry "${entry}" "${ws_out}"
    done < "${ws_out}.listing"
    [[ -z ${entry} ]] || refuse "the walk of ${live} ends mid-entry; the procedure is not printed"
}

program=''
for arg in "$@"; do
    case ${arg} in
    -*) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    *)
        [[ -z ${program} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
        program=${arg}
        ;;
    esac
done
[[ -n ${program} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ ${program} =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]] || refuse "program '${program}' is outside ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\$"

# The scratch directory comes first: every read below captures its producer's stderr to a file in it (U221e), and it
# is the one place this lever writes.
scratch=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/regime-store-move.XXXXXX") || fail 'mktemp failed'
trap cleanup EXIT

toplevel=''
read_line "${scratch}/toplevel" toplevel git_isolated rev-parse --show-toplevel ||
    refuse 'not in a git checkout (git rev-parse --show-toplevel failed, warned or printed nothing)'
git_dir=''
read_line "${scratch}/git-dir" git_dir git_isolated rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir ||
    refuse 'cannot read the git directory (git rev-parse --git-dir failed or warned)'
common_dir=''
read_line "${scratch}/common-dir" common_dir git_isolated rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir ||
    refuse 'cannot read the git common directory (git rev-parse --git-common-dir failed or warned)'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree; run from the main checkout, where the live store lies"
cd "${toplevel}" || refuse "cannot enter ${toplevel}"
# The toplevel is physical, so every path below is measured against the real checkout (U28b F2).
top_real=$(pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
# regime-env derives `REGIME_STORE_ROOT` for this checkout (its own refusals name this lever). This lever reads nothing
# in the hcom store, so the store's `origin` binding is not asked of it (`--unbound-ok`, as pr-merge.sh and
# records-sync.sh ask: the dotfiles program runs on the pre-U33 store pair and its derived hcom store carries no
# `origin`); the collision refusal and every store-root hold stay. The helper's return 1 is this lever's exit 2.
regime_env regime-store-move --unbound-ok || exit 2
[[ -n ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT:-} ]] || refuse "regime-env derived no store root for ${top_real}; the derived store lies under it (U215, U216)"

# The live store: the checkout's own `.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`, the pre-move form, each of its three
# components a directory of this user and no symlink (the pr-merge.sh hold of U216).
records=.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
live=${top_real}/${records}
path=${top_real}
for part in .orchestration orchestrate "${program}"; do
    path=${path}/${part}
    [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
        refuse "${path} is not a directory of this user (a symlink or a missing store); the live store this lever judges is the checkout's ${records}/"
done
# The destination and its components, outermost first: `regime-store`, the store root `<slug>`, the program store.
store_root=${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}
store_parent=${store_root%/*}
dest=${store_root}/${program}

# The destination before anything is read from the store: every component held, nothing written. The program store's
# existence is the state: absent, the move is still to come and the procedure is judged; present, the move ran and
# the operator's step is judged.
store_dir_hold "${store_parent}" 'the store parent'
store_dir_hold "${store_root}" 'the store root'
store_dir_hold "${dest}" 'the program store'

if [[ -e ${dest} ]]; then
    # After the move. The derived store's files are counted (a report, not a decision: no shape hold, since the
    # levers write there now), and the checkout's store subtree is read through `git status --porcelain`, under
    # `--no-optional-locks` so the read refreshes no index: an empty status is the operator's step finished; anything
    # else is the step still to finish, refused naming the count of entries; a status that fails or warns refuses.
    derived_status=0
    read_listing "${scratch}/derived" "${scratch}/derived.err" find "${dest}" ! -type d -print0 || derived_status=$?
    case ${derived_status} in
    0) ;;
    1) refuse "the derived store ${dest} exists and holds no file: regime-init's empty directory, not the moved store; remove it by hand before the move, nothing printed" ;;
    *) refuse "the walk of the derived store ${dest} failed or warned (find; its output is withheld); nothing printed" ;;
    esac
    moved=$(count_entries "${scratch}/derived" "${scratch}/derived-count") || refuse "cannot count the files of the derived store ${dest} (tr or wc failed or warned); nothing printed"
    status_state=0
    read_listing "${scratch}/status" "${scratch}/status.err" git_isolated --no-optional-locks status --porcelain -- "${records}" || status_state=$?
    case ${status_state} in
    0)
        dirty=$(count_with_wc "${scratch}/status" "${scratch}/dirty" -l) || refuse 'cannot count the entries of git status (wc failed or warned); nothing printed'
        refuse "the checkout store is not clean (${dirty} entries); finish the step"
        ;;
    1) ;;
    *) refuse "cannot read git status of ${records} (git status failed or warned; its output is withheld); nothing printed" ;;
    esac
    echo "${lever}: derived store ${dest} (${moved} files); checkout store ${live} clean against HEAD" >&2
    echo "moved: the derived store holds ${moved} files; the checkout store is clean against HEAD"
    exit 0
fi

# Before the move. The store root must exist: hcom-seat makes it when a seat of this checkout starts (U219), and the
# procedure's copy lands under it; this lever makes nothing.
[[ -d ${store_root} ]] ||
    refuse "the store root ${store_root} does not exist (hcom-seat makes it when the orchestrator seat starts, U219; this lever makes nothing); the procedure is not printed"

# The live store's walk, every entry held to the derived walk's shape; its count is the count the copy must show.
walk_store "${scratch}/rels"
total=$(count_entries "${scratch}/rels" "${scratch}/rels-count") || refuse 'cannot count the live store (tr or wc failed or warned; the read_listing line above names it); the procedure is not printed'

# The verdict and the procedure (U393: no comparison with origin's main; the live store is ahead of it after every
# records publication, and line 3's `diff -r` and count, line 7's post-move check and the next publication from the
# derived store are the controls that remain).
echo "${lever}: live store ${live} (${total} files); derived store ${dest} absent" >&2
echo "ready: ${total} live files; the derived store is absent"
print_procedure "${total}"
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""regime-url-opener: open a seat host's sign-in URL in this laptop's default browser (regime-cutover U37).

A seat on a remote host (Ubuntu, reached through `herdr --remote` over SSH) cannot open a browser, and the
vendors' sign-in flows end in a browser consent. The SSH host entry tagged `seat-host` carries
`RemoteForward 127.0.0.1:1456 127.0.0.1:1456`, so the remote `regime-open-url <url>` reaches this
loopback listener (docs/remote-host-logins.md). launchd starts it
(`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.mryfmo.dotfiles.url-opener.plist`).

It accepts exactly one request shape, `POST /open` with the header `X-Regime-Open: 1` and the URL as the
body, and opens the URL only when it is `https` on an allow-listed sign-in host with no user info and no
port but 443. The header keeps a web page in this browser from posting here, since a cross-origin request
with a custom header needs a CORS preflight this server never answers. Every request is logged to
`~/.local/state/hcom/url-opener.log` with the decision and the URL's scheme, host and path only, never
its query. It binds 127.0.0.1 only and never runs a shell.

launchd sends its stdout and stderr to /dev/null, because launchd opens those files before Python starts
and a fresh home has no log directory yet. The start, a failed bind and every request therefore go to the
log file, whose parent this script creates before it binds.

Usage: regime-url-opener [--port 1456] [--log PATH]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime
import http.server
import os
import shutil
import socketserver
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.parse
from pathlib import Path

# The sign-in hosts of the two seat routes: SIWC (`auth.openai.com`) and Claude Code's `claude auth login`
# (`claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize`, measured 2026-10-24 with Claude Code 2.1.309) and its Console flow.
ALLOWED_HOSTS = frozenset(
    {"auth.openai.com", "claude.ai", "claude.com", "console.anthropic.com", "platform.claude.com"}
)
MAX_BODY = 8192
HEADER = "X-Regime-Open"


def utc_now() -> str:
    # datetime.UTC is Python 3.11+; launchd runs /usr/bin/python3, which is 3.9 on this macOS.
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")  # noqa: UP017


def check_url(text: str) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """Return (reason it is refused or None, the scheme://host/path to log)."""
    if not text or any(ch.isspace() or ord(ch) < 32 or ord(ch) == 127 for ch in text):
        return "not one URL", ""
    try:
        parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(text)
        port = parts.port
    except ValueError:
        return "not a URL", ""
    host = (parts.hostname or "").lower()
    shown = f"{parts.scheme}://{host}{parts.path}"
    if parts.scheme != "https":
        return "not https", shown
    if parts.username is not None or parts.password is not None:
        return "user info in the URL", shown
    if port not in (None, 443):
        return f"port {port}", shown
    if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
        return "host not on the allow-list", shown
    return None, shown


def opener() -> str | None:
    return shutil.which("open" if sys.platform == "darwin" else "xdg-open")


def append_log(path: Path, entry: str) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
    with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
        log.write(f"{utc_now()} {entry}\n")


class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = "regime-url-opener"
    log_path: Path

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: object) -> None:
        return None  # the decision log below is the only record

    def record(self, decision: str, shown: str = "") -> None:
        append_log(self.log_path, f"{decision}{' ' + shown if shown else ''}")

    def reply(self, status: int, text: str) -> None:
        body = (text + "\n").encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def do_GET(self) -> None:
        self.record("refused method GET")
        self.reply(405, "POST /open only")

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        if self.path != "/open":  # lint-comparisons: allow an HTTP request target, not a filesystem path
            self.record(f"refused path {self.path[:80]!r}")
            self.reply(404, "POST /open only")
            return
        if self.headers.get(HEADER) != "1":
            self.record(f"refused missing {HEADER} header")
            self.reply(403, f"the {HEADER}: 1 header is required")
            return
        try:
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", ""))
        except ValueError:
            length = -1
        if length < 0 or length > MAX_BODY:
            self.record("refused body length")
            self.reply(413, f"the body must be one URL of at most {MAX_BODY} bytes")
            return
        try:
            url = self.rfile.read(length).decode("utf-8").strip()
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            self.record("refused body not UTF-8")
            self.reply(400, "the body must be one UTF-8 URL")
            return
        reason, shown = check_url(url)
        if reason:
            self.record(f"refused {reason}", shown)
            self.reply(403 if shown else 400, f"refused: {reason}")
            return
        command = opener()
        if command is None:
            self.record("failed no opener on PATH", shown)
            self.reply(502, "no `open` or `xdg-open` on PATH")
            return
        result = subprocess.run([command, url], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, capture_output=True, check=False)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            self.record(f"failed opener exit {result.returncode}", shown)
            self.reply(502, f"the opener exited {result.returncode}")
            return
        self.record("opened", shown)
        self.reply(200, "opened")


class LoopbackHTTPServer(http.server.HTTPServer):
    """An HTTPServer that binds without `socket.getfqdn`.

    `HTTPServer.server_bind` resolves the bound host with `socket.getfqdn`, a reverse DNS lookup that takes
    about 35 s on some macOS hosts; nothing here reads `server_name`, so the literal host is kept instead.
    """

    def server_bind(self) -> None:
        socketserver.TCPServer.server_bind(self)
        host, port = self.server_address[:2]
        self.server_name = host
        self.server_port = port


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="regime-url-opener")
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=int(os.environ.get("REGIME_URL_OPENER_PORT", "1456")))
    parser.add_argument("--log", type=Path, default=Path.home() / ".local/state/hcom/url-opener.log")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    Handler.log_path = args.log
    try:
        args.log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
    except OSError as error:
        print(f"regime-url-opener: cannot create the log directory {args.log.parent}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    try:
        server = LoopbackHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", args.port), Handler)
    except OSError as error:
        append_log(args.log, f"failed to bind 127.0.0.1:{args.port}: {error.strerror or error}")
        print(f"regime-url-opener: cannot bind 127.0.0.1:{args.port}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    host, port = server.server_address[:2]
    append_log(args.log, f"listening on {host}:{port}")
    print(f"regime-url-opener: listening on {host}:{port}", flush=True)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
