#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file remove-agent-asset
# @brief Remove one installed agent asset step from its recorded manifest entry.
# @description
#   Defaults to a non-mutating dry run. Actual removal requires `--yes`, and
#   file deletion is limited to normalized paths recorded by the selected step
#   under fixed agent-asset roots. Final symlinks are removed without following
#   their targets.
# @arg $1 string Manifest step name.
# @option --dry-run Print exact inverse operations without executing them.
# @option --yes Execute the guarded inverse operations and remove the step record.

set -Eeuo pipefail

readonly MANIFEST_PATH="${HOME}/.agents/.installed-manifest.json"
readonly CODEX_ASSET_ROOT="${CODEX_HOME:-${HOME}/.codex}"

declare -a RECORDED_PATHS=()
declare -a RECORDED_COMMANDS=()
ENTRY=""
MODE="dry-run"
STEP=""

#
# @description Print command usage.
#
function usage() {
    printf 'Usage: remove-agent-asset <step-name> [--dry-run|--yes]\n' >&2
}

#
# @description Print an error and return failure.
# @arg $@ string Error message words.
#
function fail() {
    printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    return 1
}

#
# @description Return success when a command is available.
# @arg $1 string Command name.
#
function has_command() {
    command -v "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1
}

#
# @description Normalize a path while leaving its final symlink unresolved.
# @arg $1 path Absolute path to normalize.
#
function normalize_action_path() {
    python3 - "$1" << 'PY'
import os
import sys

path = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(sys.argv[1]))
print(os.path.join(os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(path)), os.path.basename(path)))
PY
}

#
# @description Resolve a trusted directory root including its final symlink.
# @arg $1 path Directory root to normalize.
#
function normalize_root_path() {
    python3 - "$1" << 'PY'
import os
import sys

print(os.path.realpath(os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(sys.argv[1]))))
PY
}

#
# @description Return success when a path equals or descends from a prefix, both folded by os.path.normpath first.
# @arg $1 path Candidate path.
# @arg $2 path Prefix path.
# @arg $3 string Optional `strict`, which refuses the prefix itself.
#
function path_has_prefix() {
    python3 -I -c 'import os, sys; p, q = map(os.path.normpath, sys.argv[1:3]); sys.exit(not (p.startswith(q + os.sep) or p == q and sys.argv[3:] != ["strict"]))' "$@"
}

#
# @description Return success when a normalized path is under a fixed removable asset root.
# @arg $1 path Normalized candidate path.
#
function path_is_in_safe_root() {
    local candidate="$1"
    local root

    for root in \
        "${HOME}/.agents" \
        "${HOME}/.claude/plugins/cache" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/plugins/cache" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/.tmp/plugins/plugins" \
        "${HOME}/.local/share/mise/installs" \
        "${HOME}/.local/share/agent-assets"; do
        root="$(normalize_root_path "${root}")" || return 1
        if path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${root}" strict; then
            return 0
        fi
    done

    root="$(normalize_root_path "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/plugins/crit")" || return 1
    if path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${root}"; then
        return 0
    fi

    for root in \
        "${HOME}/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/herdr-agent-state.sh" \
        "${HOME}/.local/bin/hcom"; do
        root="$(normalize_action_path "${root}")" || return 1
        [ "${candidate}" = "${root}" ] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are normalize_action_path forms
    done
    return 1
}

#
# @description Return success when a deletion path stays inside a recorded prefix and a fixed safe root.
# @arg $1 path Candidate deletion path.
# @stdout Prints the normalized deletion path on success.
#
function guard_deletion_path() {
    local candidate recorded normalized_recorded
    candidate="$(normalize_action_path "$1")" || return 1

    if ! path_is_in_safe_root "${candidate}"; then
        fail "refusing path outside allowed asset roots: ${candidate}"
        return 1
    fi
    for recorded in "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"; do
        normalized_recorded="$(normalize_action_path "${recorded}")" || continue
        if path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${normalized_recorded}"; then
            printf '%s\n' "${candidate}"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    fail "refusing path outside recorded manifest prefixes: ${candidate}"
}

#
# @description Print and optionally execute one inverse command.
# @arg $@ string Command and arguments.
#
function run_operation() {
    if [ "${MODE}" = "dry-run" ]; then
        printf 'DRY-RUN:'
    else
        printf 'REMOVE:'
    fi
    printf ' %q' "$@"
    printf '\n'
    [ "${MODE}" = "dry-run" ] || "$@"
}

#
# @description Remove one guarded manifest-recorded filesystem path.
# @arg $1 path Recorded target path.
#
function remove_recorded_path() {
    local target
    target="$(guard_deletion_path "$1")" || return 1
    if [ -L "${target}" ] || [ -f "${target}" ]; then
        run_operation rm -f -- "${target}"
    else
        run_operation rm -rf -- "${target}"
    fi
}

#
# @description Validate every filesystem path before the first destructive operation.
# @arg $@ path Recorded target paths.
#
function preflight_deletion_paths() {
    local path
    for path in "$@"; do
        guard_deletion_path "${path}" > /dev/null
    done
}

#
# @description Remove a preflighted list of manifest-recorded paths.
# @arg $@ path Recorded target paths.
#
function remove_recorded_paths() {
    local path
    preflight_deletion_paths "$@"
    for path in "$@"; do
        remove_recorded_path "${path}"
    done
}

#
# @description Return success when a recorded path is plugin cache or plugin data, not shared config.
# @arg $1 path Recorded path.
#
function is_plugin_data_path() {
    local candidate root
    candidate="$(normalize_action_path "$1")" || return 1
    for root in \
        "${HOME}/.claude/plugins/cache" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/plugins/cache" \
        "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/.tmp/plugins/plugins"; do
        root="$(normalize_root_path "${root}")" || return 1
        if path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${root}" strict; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
    root="$(normalize_root_path "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/plugins/crit")" || return 1
    path_has_prefix "${candidate}" "${root}"
}

#
# @description Return success for shared plugin config files that must never be removed wholesale.
# @arg $1 path Recorded path.
#
function is_plugin_config_path() {
    local candidate settings_path config_path
    candidate="$(normalize_action_path "$1")" || return 1
    settings_path="$(normalize_action_path "${HOME}/.claude/settings.json")" || return 1
    config_path="$(normalize_action_path "${CODEX_ASSET_ROOT}/config.toml")" || return 1
    [ "${candidate}" = "${settings_path}" ] || [ "${candidate}" = "${config_path}" ] # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are normalize_action_path forms
}

#
# @description Remove guarded plugin data when the owning CLI has no usable uninstall.
#
function remove_plugin_data_paths() {
    local path
    local -a data_paths=()
    for path in "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"; do
        if is_plugin_data_path "${path}"; then
            data_paths+=("${path}")
        elif ! is_plugin_config_path "${path}"; then
            fail "plugin entry contains an unrecognized fallback path: ${path}"
            return 1
        fi
    done
    [ "${#data_paths[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
        fail "plugin entry has no guarded cache/data fallback: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    remove_recorded_paths "${data_paths[@]}"
}

#
# @description Execute the inverse for a plugin manifest entry.
#
function remove_plugin() {
    local command owner="" plugin_id="" candidate_owner candidate_id

    for command in "${RECORDED_COMMANDS[@]}"; do
        candidate_owner=""
        candidate_id=""
        case "${command}" in
        "claude plugin install "*)
            candidate_owner="claude"
            candidate_id="${command#claude plugin install }"
            ;;
        "claude plugin update "*)
            candidate_owner="claude"
            candidate_id="${command#claude plugin update }"
            ;;
        "codex plugin add "*)
            candidate_owner="codex"
            candidate_id="${command#codex plugin add }"
            ;;
        "crit install codex-plugin" | "crit install codex-plugin "*)
            candidate_owner="crit"
            candidate_id="codex-plugin"
            ;;
        esac
        [ -n "${candidate_owner}" ] || continue
        if [ -n "${owner}" ] && { [ "${owner}" != "${candidate_owner}" ] || [ "${plugin_id}" != "${candidate_id}" ]; }; then
            fail "ambiguous plugin owner or id for step: ${STEP}"
            return 1
        fi
        owner="${candidate_owner}"
        plugin_id="${candidate_id}"
    done

    [[ "${plugin_id}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.@/+:-]+$ ]] || {
        fail "missing or unsafe plugin id for step: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    case "${owner}" in
    claude)
        if has_command claude; then
            run_operation claude plugin uninstall "${plugin_id}"
        else
            remove_plugin_data_paths
        fi
        ;;
    codex)
        if has_command codex; then
            run_operation codex plugin remove "${plugin_id}"
        else
            remove_plugin_data_paths
        fi
        ;;
    crit)
        # Crit exposes install but no uninstall command; remove only its recorded data root.
        remove_plugin_data_paths
        ;;
    *)
        fail "unknown plugin owner for step: ${STEP}"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
}

#
# @description Execute the inverse for a Brew manifest entry.
#
function remove_brew() {
    local command formula="" candidate
    for command in "${RECORDED_COMMANDS[@]}"; do
        case "${command}" in
        "brew install "*)
            candidate="${command#brew install }"
            if [ -n "${formula}" ] && [ "${formula}" != "${candidate}" ]; then
                fail "ambiguous brew formula for step: ${STEP}"
                return 1
            fi
            formula="${candidate}"
            ;;
        esac
    done
    [[ "${formula}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9@+._-]+$ ]] || {
        fail "missing or unsafe brew formula for step: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    if [ "${MODE}" = "yes" ] && ! has_command brew; then
        fail "brew command not found"
        return 1
    fi
    run_operation brew uninstall "${formula}"
}

#
# @description Execute the inverse for a Herdr integration manifest entry.
#
function remove_integration() {
    local command integration
    local -a integrations=()
    for command in "${RECORDED_COMMANDS[@]}"; do
        case "${command}" in
        "herdr integration install "*)
            integration="${command#herdr integration install }"
            [[ "${integration}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || {
                fail "unsafe Herdr integration name for step: ${STEP}"
                return 1
            }
            integrations+=("${integration}")
            ;;
        esac
    done
    if [ "${#integrations[@]}" -gt 0 ] && has_command herdr && herdr integration uninstall --help > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        for integration in "${integrations[@]}"; do
            run_operation herdr integration uninstall "${integration}"
        done
        return 0
    fi
    [ "${#RECORDED_PATHS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
        fail "integration entry has no guarded fallback paths: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    remove_recorded_paths "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"
}

#
# @description Atomically remove the completed step from the manifest.
#
function remove_manifest_step() {
    if [ "${MODE}" = "dry-run" ]; then
        printf 'DRY-RUN: remove manifest step %s\n' "${STEP}"
        return 0
    fi

    local temporary_path
    temporary_path="$(mktemp "${MANIFEST_PATH}.tmp.XXXXXX")"
    chmod 600 "${temporary_path}"
    if ! jq --arg step "${STEP}" 'del(.steps[$step])' "${MANIFEST_PATH}" > "${temporary_path}"; then
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    fi
    if ! mv "${temporary_path}" "${MANIFEST_PATH}"; then
        rm -f "${temporary_path}"
        return 1
    fi
    printf 'REMOVE: manifest step %s\n' "${STEP}"
}

#
# @description Load and validate the selected manifest entry.
#
function load_entry() {
    [ -f "${MANIFEST_PATH}" ] || {
        fail "installed asset manifest not found: ${MANIFEST_PATH}"
        return 1
    }
    jq -e '.version == 1 and (.steps | type == "object")' "${MANIFEST_PATH}" > /dev/null || {
        fail "invalid installed asset manifest: ${MANIFEST_PATH}"
        return 1
    }
    if ! ENTRY="$(jq -ce --arg step "${STEP}" '.steps[$step] // empty' "${MANIFEST_PATH}")"; then
        ENTRY=""
    fi
    if [ -z "${ENTRY}" ]; then
        printf 'ERROR: unknown manifest step: %s\n' "${STEP}" >&2
        local known_steps
        known_steps="$(jq -r '.steps | keys | join(", ")' "${MANIFEST_PATH}")" || {
            fail "cannot list the steps of ${MANIFEST_PATH}"
            return 1
        }
        printf 'Known steps: %s\n' "${known_steps}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${ENTRY}" | jq -e '
        (.kind | type == "string") and
        (.paths | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string")) and
        (.commands | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string"))
    ' > /dev/null || {
        fail "invalid manifest entry: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }

    local value values
    values="$(jq -r '.paths[]' <<< "${ENTRY}")" || {
        fail "cannot read the recorded paths of manifest entry: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    while IFS= read -r value; do
        [ -z "${value}" ] || RECORDED_PATHS+=("${value}")
    done <<< "${values}"
    values="$(jq -r '.commands[]' <<< "${ENTRY}")" || {
        fail "cannot read the recorded commands of manifest entry: ${STEP}"
        return 1
    }
    while IFS= read -r value; do
        [ -z "${value}" ] || RECORDED_COMMANDS+=("${value}")
    done <<< "${values}"
}

#
# @description Remove hcom: uv uninstalls its tool environment and receipt, then the recorded binary and wheel go.
#
function remove_hcom() {
    local tools=""
    if has_command uv; then
        tools="$(uv tool dir --color never)" || return 1 # herdr panes export FORCE_COLOR and CLICOLOR_FORCE
    elif [ "${MODE}" = "yes" ]; then
        fail "uv command not found, so hcom's uv tool environment and receipt cannot be uninstalled; nothing was removed"
        return 1
    fi
    preflight_deletion_paths "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"
    # An hcom uv no longer has (uninstalled by hand or by an earlier run) must not stop the rest of the removal.
    if [ -z "${tools}" ] || [ -d "${tools}/hcom" ]; then
        run_operation uv tool uninstall hcom
    else
        printf 'SKIP: uv has no hcom tool environment under %s\n' "${tools}"
    fi
    remove_recorded_paths "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"
}

#
# @description Parse arguments and perform the selected inverse operation.
# @arg $@ string Command-line arguments.
#
function main() {
    if [ "$#" -lt 1 ] || [ "$#" -gt 2 ]; then
        usage
        return 2
    fi
    STEP="$1"
    case "${2:---dry-run}" in
    --dry-run) MODE="dry-run" ;;
    --yes) MODE="yes" ;;
    *)
        usage
        return 2
        ;;
    esac

    load_entry
    local kind
    kind="$(printf '%s\n' "${ENTRY}" | jq -r '.kind')"
    case "${kind}" in
    plugin)
        remove_plugin
        ;;
    rsync | installer)
        [ "${#RECORDED_PATHS[@]}" -gt 0 ] || {
            fail "manifest step has no removal paths: ${STEP}"
            return 1
        }
        if [ "${STEP}" = "update_hcom" ]; then
            remove_hcom
        else
            remove_recorded_paths "${RECORDED_PATHS[@]}"
        fi
        ;;
    brew)
        remove_brew
        ;;
    integration)
        remove_integration
        ;;
    *)
        fail "unsupported manifest kind for step ${STEP}: ${kind}"
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
    remove_manifest_step
}

main "$@"

Upstream's deployment guide gives the Router a gh wrapper whose GH_CONFIG_DIR is the agent account's own directory (docs/006-deployment.md "Agent GitHub account", gh-agent), and the Router's GitHub Source names it as its cli (src/sources/github.ts:46-47): the Router acts as the account that wrapper is signed in to, and the Executor calls it as gh. This file is that wrapper for the kit. The login lives in <DSH_HOME>/router-credentials/gh/hosts.yml: the credential root is the one directory the router role of hcom-seat reads beyond the dsh row's grants (allowRead row 7, held like the state root and made 0700 by the launch), every other role denies it for read, and no role writes it (the login is the operator's step, docs/engagement-handout.md: gh auth login --insecure-storage under that GH_CONFIG_DIR; the Keychain stays reachable under srt, and the file-only token source below keeps gh off it). DSH_HOME is the one hcom-seat exports into the Router (its held physical form); unset, ~/.dsh as the kit's default. DSH_HOME, the root, its gh/ and the hosts.yml inside are held as one chain, top-down, each component by its own test before anything is read (U353c, the shape of seat-login-preflight's claude_config_validate; U490f makes DSH_HOME the first component): no link, the three directories this user's, DSH_HOME searchable and read physically (pwd -P), the root read physically inside it and gh/ resolving inside the root, the leaf a regular file of this user; a link, a file in a directory's place, a directory in the file's place, or a directory this user cannot search or resolve refuses (exit 2) before gh runs, and an absent component refuses with exit 3 (U490e, below). No component's absence is claimed before its parent has passed in full: -e is false both for a missing entry and for an entry under a directory this user cannot search, so round 5 called an existing root under a DSH_HOME of mode 000 absent (verdict U490-f6175c44 P1). DSH_HOME itself has no "absent" form: the kit makes it (home/dot_dsh) and every launch holds it, so each failed test on it is exit 2. The chain stands on one text rule, held before any file test (U490g): DSH_HOME's spelling passes the levers' one clean-path grammar, clean_path below, the regular expression of hcom-seat's require_clean_path (absolute; every component of [A-Za-z0-9._@+-]; none empty, . or ..; so no repeated or trailing /), because the shell resolves a trailing / before -L tests the entry, so /path/to/link/ passed round 6's link test and ran gh through the linked root (verdict U490-34bb6fe7 P1 :135); any other spelling is exit 2 naming DSH_HOME and the grammar, and the file tests run on the clean text alone. gh resolves a credential as GH_TOKEN, then the config directory's hosts.yml, then the host-wide Keychain on macOS (gh help environment; verdict U353-8791100f P1 :97): GH_CONFIG_DIR alone let an empty root authenticate as the operator's own Keychain login, since srt permits securityd. So this wrapper is the only credential source gh sees: it reads the oauth_token: of github.com from <root>/gh/hosts.yml itself (a regular file of this user, no link, readable by this user alone as gh auth login writes it; the row at the github.com: block's own depth, exactly one, since gh 2.40 and later repeats each account's row deeper under users:, which is never read (U353c); its value inside [A-Za-z0-9_]; each else refused by name and no gh run, the value never printed) and runs gh with GH_TOKEN set to it and GH_CONFIG_DIR the root's gh/, so the Keychain is never consulted and an absent or empty login is a refusal, never a fallback. The caller's GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN and GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN are replaced or removed first, so the account is the credential root's login and never a value of the caller's environment (the Router's setup removes them too, docs/006-deployment.md "Setup checks"); GH_HOST is removed so the host is github.com. gh is resolved from the caller's PATH (type -P, inside the sandbox the seat's PATH), and an absent gh refuses by name. Every other argument reaches gh verbatim.

#!/bin/bash
# @file router-gh
# @brief The dsh-superagent Router's GitHub CLI: `gh` signed in as the agent account alone, with the token read from the login under the Router's credential root.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U353 (M-26 stage B), U353b and U353c. Upstream's deployment guide gives the Router a `gh` wrapper whose
#   `GH_CONFIG_DIR` is the agent account's own directory (docs/006-deployment.md "Agent GitHub account", `gh-agent`), and
#   the Router's GitHub Source names it as its `cli` (`src/sources/github.ts:46-47`): the Router acts as the account that
#   wrapper is signed in to, and the Executor calls it as `gh`. This file is that wrapper for the kit. The login lives in
#   `<DSH_HOME>/router-credentials/gh/hosts.yml`: the credential root is the one directory the router role of `hcom-seat`
#   reads beyond the dsh row's grants (allowRead row 7, held like the state root and made 0700 by the launch), every
#   other role denies it for read, and no role writes it (the login is the operator's step, docs/engagement-handout.md:
#   `gh auth login --insecure-storage` under that `GH_CONFIG_DIR`; the Keychain stays reachable under srt, and the file-only
#   token source below keeps gh off it). `DSH_HOME` is the one `hcom-seat` exports into the Router (its held physical form); unset,
#   `~/.dsh` as the kit's default. `DSH_HOME`, the root, its `gh/` and the `hosts.yml` inside are held as one chain, top-down,
#   each component by its own test before anything is read (U353c, the shape of seat-login-preflight's
#   claude_config_validate; U490f makes `DSH_HOME` the first component): no link, the three directories this user's,
#   `DSH_HOME` searchable and read physically (`pwd -P`), the root read physically inside it and `gh/` resolving inside
#   the root, the leaf a regular file of this user; a link, a file in a directory's place, a directory in the file's
#   place, or a directory this user cannot search or resolve refuses (exit 2) before `gh` runs, and an absent component
#   refuses with exit 3 (U490e, below). No component's absence is claimed before its parent has passed in full: `-e` is
#   false both for a missing entry and for an entry under a directory this user cannot search, so round 5 called an
#   existing root under a `DSH_HOME` of mode 000 absent (verdict U490-f6175c44 P1). `DSH_HOME` itself has no "absent"
#   form: the kit makes it (home/dot_dsh) and every launch holds it, so each failed test on it is exit 2. The chain
#   stands on one text rule, held before any file test (U490g): `DSH_HOME`'s spelling passes the levers' one clean-path
#   grammar, `clean_path` below, the regular expression of `hcom-seat`'s `require_clean_path` (absolute; every
#   component of `[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]`; none empty, `.` or `..`; so no repeated or trailing `/`), because the shell
#   resolves a trailing `/` before `-L` tests the entry, so `/path/to/link/` passed round 6's link test and ran `gh`
#   through the linked root (verdict U490-34bb6fe7 P1 `:135`); any other spelling is exit 2 naming `DSH_HOME` and the
#   grammar, and the file tests run on the clean text alone.
#   gh resolves a credential as `GH_TOKEN`, then the config directory's `hosts.yml`, then the host-wide Keychain on
#   macOS (`gh help environment`; verdict U353-8791100f P1 `:97`): `GH_CONFIG_DIR` alone let an empty root authenticate
#   as the operator's own Keychain login, since srt permits securityd. So this wrapper is the only credential source gh
#   sees: it reads the `oauth_token:` of `github.com` from `<root>/gh/hosts.yml` itself (a regular file of this user, no
#   link, readable by this user alone as `gh auth login` writes it; the row at the `github.com:` block's own depth,
#   exactly one, since gh 2.40 and later repeats each account's row deeper under `users:`, which is never read (U353c);
#   its value inside [A-Za-z0-9_]; each else refused by name and no `gh` run, the value never printed) and runs `gh` with
#   `GH_TOKEN` set to it and `GH_CONFIG_DIR` the root's `gh/`, so the Keychain is never consulted and an absent or
#   empty login is a refusal, never a fallback. The caller's `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` and
#   `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` are replaced or removed first, so the account is the credential root's login and never a
#   value of the caller's environment (the Router's setup removes them too, docs/006-deployment.md "Setup checks");
#   `GH_HOST` is removed so the host is github.com. `gh` is resolved from the caller's PATH (`type -P`, inside the
#   sandbox the seat's PATH), and an absent `gh` refuses by name. Every other argument reaches `gh` verbatim.
# @description Two refusal codes (regime-cutover U490e). Exit 3 is "not yet": the credential root, its `gh/` or its
#   `hosts.yml` is absent (neither a link nor an entry), or `hosts.yml` names no `oauth_token:` row for github.com at
#   the block's own depth; the agent account's login is the operator's pending step (docs/engagement-handout.md step 2)
#   and nothing is broken. Exit 2 is every other refusal: a broken or unreadable root (a link anywhere in the chain, a
#   wrong owner or mode, a root that cannot be resolved, two rows, a value outside the grammar), a `DSH_HOME` whose
#   spelling is outside the clean-path grammar (U490g), is a link, is not a directory of this user, or cannot be
#   searched or resolved (U490f), an absent `gh`, the self-check. One caller reads the two codes: `check_router_token`
#   in scripts/check-tools.sh (the doctor), an optional warning for 3 and a required failure for 2, with no path test of
#   its own; the Router reads `gh`'s status alone. Both codes print one line on stderr, the same form.
# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @arg $@ string gh's arguments, verbatim.
# @exitcode 2 The self-check, `DSH_HOME`, the credential root, its gh directory, the login file or `gh` refused: broken, not pending.
# @exitcode 3 No login yet: the credential root, its gh directory or the login file is absent, or the login file names no active github.com login; the operator's step.
# @exitcode * gh's own status.
# @example
#   DSH_HOME=~/.dsh router-gh api user --jq .login
set -u

lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''             # producer-status: allow the if below takes an empty home as the checkout layout
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2: a broken or unreadable root, never the pending step.
# @arg $1 string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "router-gh: $1" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the refusal on stderr, the same form, and exit 3: the login is not yet in place, the operator's
#   step (U490e); read by the doctor as an optional warning where exit 2 is a required failure.
# @arg $1 string The reason.
refuse_absent() {
    echo "router-gh: $1" >&2
    exit 3
}

# @description Succeed when `$1` is a clean absolute path, the one grammar every lever holds a path's text to before a
#   file test (regime-cutover U490g; the regular expression of `hcom-seat`'s `clean_path`, copied, not imported, so no
#   other lever is read): `/` followed by components of `[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]` only (no glob metacharacter `*?[]{}`, no
#   whitespace, no quote or backslash), none of them empty, `.` or `..`, and no trailing `/`. The shell resolves a
#   trailing `/` before `[[ -L ]]` tests the entry, so a link spelled `/path/to/link/` is no link to `-L`; on a clean
#   spelling the file tests of the chain judge the entry the text names.
# @arg $1 string The path.
# @exitcode 0 The path is clean.
# @exitcode 1 The path is not clean.
clean_path() {
    [[ $1 =~ ^(/[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]+)+$ ]] || return 1
    [[ /$1/ != */./* && /$1/ != */../* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow a component test on one path, no path compare
}

dsh_home=${DSH_HOME:-${HOME}/.dsh}
# The component chain, each held by its own test before anything is read (regime-cutover U353c, the shape of
# seat-login-preflight's claude_config_validate): `<DSH_HOME>`, `<root>`, `<root>/gh`, `<root>/gh/hosts.yml`, in that
# order, `<DSH_HOME>`'s text first (clean_path, U490g), then no link (`-L` first), the three directories this user's,
# `<DSH_HOME>` searchable and read physically, the root read physically inside it and `gh/` resolving inside the
# physical root, the leaf a regular file of this user readable by this user alone, as `gh auth login --insecure-storage`
# writes it. Round 2 held the root and the leaf alone, so `<root>/gh` as a link to an outside gh directory of this user
# passed and its login reached gh (verdict U353b-9c504ad9 P1 `:106`). Round 5 judged the root before `DSH_HOME`, so `-e`
# on a root under a `DSH_HOME` this user cannot search was false and an existing root was called absent (verdict
# U490-f6175c44 P1): no component's absence is claimed (exit 3) before its parent has passed in full, and `DSH_HOME` has
# no absent form (each else is exit 2). Round 6 tested `-L` on the spelling as given, and the shell resolves a trailing
# `/` before the test, so `/path/to/link/` was no link to it and gh ran through the linked root (verdict U490-34bb6fe7

[[ -d ${dsh_home} ]] || refuse "DSH_HOME ${dsh_home} is not a directory; it must be a real directory of this user"
[[ -O ${dsh_home} ]] || refuse "DSH_HOME ${dsh_home} is not this user's directory"
[[ -x ${dsh_home} ]] || refuse "DSH_HOME ${dsh_home} is not searchable by this user; nothing under it can be judged"
dsh_phys=$(cd "${dsh_home}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve DSH_HOME ${dsh_home}" # cd's own message is dropped: the refusal is the one stderr line (U490e)
root=${dsh_phys}/router-credentials
[[ ! -L ${root} ]] || refuse "the credential root ${root} is a symbolic link; it must be a real directory inside DSH_HOME"
[[ -e ${root} ]] || refuse_absent "the credential root ${root} is absent; hcom-seat router makes it, and the agent account's login inside it is the operator's step"
[[ -d ${root} ]] || refuse "the credential root ${root} is not a directory; it must be a real directory inside DSH_HOME"
[[ -O ${root} ]] || refuse "the credential root ${root} is not this user's directory"
root_phys=$(cd "${root}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the credential root ${root}" # cd's own message is dropped: the refusal is the one stderr line (U490e)
gh_real=$(type -P gh) || refuse "gh not found on PATH"
gh_dir=${root_phys}/gh
[[ ! -L ${gh_dir} ]] || refuse "${gh_dir} is a symbolic link; the login directory must be a real directory inside the credential root"
[[ -e ${gh_dir} ]] || refuse_absent "no gh login under the credential root: ${gh_dir} is absent; the agent account's login inside the root is the operator's step (docs/engagement-handout.md), and gh runs with no other credential"
[[ -d ${gh_dir} ]] || refuse "${gh_dir} is not a directory; the login directory must be a real directory inside the credential root"
[[ -O ${gh_dir} ]] || refuse "${gh_dir} is not this user's directory"
gh_phys=$(cd "${gh_dir}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the login directory ${gh_dir}"
[[ ${gh_phys} == "${root_phys}/gh" ]] || refuse "the login directory ${gh_dir} resolves to ${gh_phys}, outside the credential root" # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms, the hold of the chain
hosts=${gh_dir}/hosts.yml
[[ ! -L ${hosts} ]] || refuse "${hosts} is a symbolic link; the login must be a regular file inside the credential root"
[[ -e ${hosts} ]] || refuse_absent "no gh login under the credential root: ${hosts} is absent; the agent account's login inside the root is the operator's step (docs/engagement-handout.md), and gh runs with no other credential"
[[ -f ${hosts} ]] || refuse "${hosts} is not a regular file; the login must be a regular file inside the credential root"
[[ -O ${hosts} ]] || refuse "${hosts} is not this user's file"
os=$(/usr/bin/uname -s) || refuse 'cannot read the operating system name (uname -s)'
case ${os} in
Darwin) mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -f %Lp "${hosts}") || refuse "cannot read the mode of ${hosts}" ;;
*) mode=$(/usr/bin/stat -c %a "${hosts}") || refuse "cannot read the mode of ${hosts}" ;;
esac
[[ ${mode} =~ ^[0-7]00$ ]] || refuse "${hosts} has mode ${mode}; the login must be readable by this user alone (0600)"
# The value: the `oauth_token:` row of the `github.com:` block at the block's own depth, exactly one, read by the shell
# alone (no external reader sees it) and held to the grammar gh's tokens use; no message prints it. gh 2.40 and later
# writes the active account's rows at the block's depth and every account's `oauth_token:` again under `users:`,
# deeper (verdict U353b-9c504ad9 P1 `:127`: an indentation-blind match counted both and refused one login), so the
# depth is measured from the first row inside the block and a deeper row is never read.
hosts_text=$(< "${hosts}") || refuse "cannot read ${hosts}"
oauth_value='' oauth_rows=0 in_host=0 depth='' rest=${hosts_text}
while [[ -n ${rest} ]]; do
    line=${rest%%$'\n'*}
    if [[ ${rest} == *$'\n'* ]]; then rest=${rest#*$'\n'}; else rest=''; fi
    trimmed=${line%"${line##*[![:space:]]}"}
    case ${trimmed} in
    '') ;;                             # a blank line is no row of the block
    github.com:) in_host=1 depth='' ;; # lint-comparisons: allow the host key of gh's hosts.yml, a YAML mapping key, not a URL
    [![:space:]]*) in_host=0 ;;
    *)
        ((in_host)) || continue
        indent=${trimmed%%[![:space:]]*}
        [[ -n ${depth} ]] || depth=${indent}
        if [[ ${indent} == "${depth}" ]] && [[ ${trimmed} =~ ^[[:space:]]+oauth_token:[[:space:]]*(.*)$ ]]; then
            value=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
            case ${value} in
            \"*\" | \'*\') value=${value:1:${#value}-2} ;;
            esac
            oauth_value=${value} oauth_rows=$((oauth_rows + 1))
        fi
        ;;
    esac
done
if ((oauth_rows == 0)); then
    refuse_absent "${hosts} names no active login for github.com: no oauth_token row at the host block's own depth (the rows under users: are not read); the agent account's login inside the root is the operator's step (docs/engagement-handout.md)"
elif ((oauth_rows != 1)); then
    refuse "${hosts} names ${oauth_rows} oauth_token rows for github.com at the host block's own depth; exactly one is read"
fi
[[ ${oauth_value} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ ]] || refuse "the oauth_token of github.com in ${hosts} is empty or outside [A-Za-z0-9_]"
# The account is the credential root's login alone: no token or host of the caller's environment reaches gh, and with
# GH_TOKEN set gh reads no store (`gh help environment`: the variable takes precedence over stored credentials).
unset GITHUB_TOKEN GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN GH_HOST
GH_TOKEN=${oauth_value} GH_CONFIG_DIR=${root_phys}/gh exec "${gh_real}" "$@"

# @brief The settings writer's entry: resolve the program store by the shell levers' one rule, name the Source rendering beside the manifest, and run the pinned Python body with both as given paths.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U465d (round 4 of U465, the mechanism-change row of 2026-11-11T11:54:59Z, form remove): the Python
#   lever resolved the program store itself (the checkout from the working directory, the derived store by its leaf),

#   origin (verdicts/U465-e6a9a84f.md P1 `:400` and P1 `:457`). From this round the lever is two pinned files, as
#   `acp-broker` and `acp-relay.py` are: this bash entry owns the environment, and `router-settings-apply.py` beside it
#   owns the settings logic and takes its inputs as given paths. Round 5 (U465e, verdicts/U465-9c0244e0.md P1 `:126`
#   and P1 `:203`) closed two channels into that split: the body's argparse expanded `--sto` and let a caller's value
#   after the entry's two win (the body's grammar is exact names, each once), and the entry resolved the checkout under
#   the caller's `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_WORK_TREE` (the environment is scrubbed first). Round 6 (U465f,
#   verdicts/U465-59601417.md P1 `:71` and P1 `:61`) closed two channels into the scrub itself: its here-string failed
#   open when bash could not write the temporary file a here-string is (TMPDIR denied: the redirection failed and
#   `set -e` skipped the loop with no refusal), and the `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang let bash import a caller's exported
#   `compgen`, `set` and `unset` functions before line 1 ran. The interpreter is `/bin/bash -p` (pr-audit.sh's form):
#   privileged mode imports no function and reads no BASH_ENV, SHELLOPTS, BASHOPTS, CDPATH or GLOBIGNORE, and the
#   decision is the shebang's, not a re-exec's, because a re-exec would run in the shell that had already imported the
#   functions (the comment above the guard carries the measurement). The entry
#   0. refuses a run through another shell by name (no `p` in `$-`), then removes every `GIT_*`, `PERL*` and `PYTHON*`
#      variable before any external command runs, by the prefix expansions `${!GIT_@}`, `${!PERL@}` and `${!PYTHON@}`

#      sets only `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, so the git reads below, regime-env's own
#      included, see the working directory alone;

#      stops the entry);

#   3. reads the checkout the working directory is in through `git_isolated` and refuses a linked worktree (the

#      <rendering> "$@"`, so the body's refusals, output and exit status are this command's.

# @option --profile <path> The rendered router cordis.patch.yml (the body's option; default $DSH_HOME/profiles/router/cordis.patch.yml).

fi

export GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):

#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from, beside which the Source rendering lies.
# @set LEVER_DIR The physical directory of this file, where the sourced helpers and the Python body sit.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever=router-settings-apply

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2 (the refusal grammar producer-status-check.sh reads).
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# The one isolated git (U113) and the regime derivation (U33, U215, U216), each sourced from the directory this entry
# runs from and self-checked like a lever, so a rewritten copy stops this entry.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh ]] || refuse "git-isolated.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh"
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh"
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || refuse "regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"

# The two paths are this entry's: a caller naming either would choose the store the body proves or the row it reads.
# The exact flags are refused here; an abbreviation (`--sto`) or a repeat after the entry's two is the body's refusal
# (U465e: its parser takes exact names, each once).
for arg in "$@"; do
    case ${arg} in
    --store | --store=*) refuse "--store is the entry's: the program store is resolved here by regime-env and store_resolve, never given by the caller" ;;
    --source | --source=*) refuse "--source is the entry's: the rendering is router-source.json beside the manifest, never given by the caller" ;;
    esac
done

# @description Choose the program store this lever reads (regime-cutover U216, store move 2 of 5,
#   handoff/07-store-move-design.md; U215 gave regime-env the root): the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>`
#   when that directory exists, the root being the fixed derivation `<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>`
#   the sourced regime-env exports after holding every component of it; else the pre-move form
#   `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`, this main checkout's own store, which stands until U221 moves the
#   live store of this program to the root and removes this form. One rule, two forms: while the derived store exists
#   the checkout form is refused (the caller refuses a path naming it, naming both forms), and while it does not the
#   checkout form is read as before U216. The per-component holds of the chain walk (U71) stay and apply to the form
#   chosen: a symbolic link at `<root>/<program>` is refused by name before anything is read through it, an entry
#   there that is not a directory of this user is refused by name, and only an absent one falls through to the
#   checkout chain, whose three components are each a directory of this user and no symlink. The root's own
#   components are held by regime-env (`regime_store_root`). Nothing is written. The form chosen is printed once on
#   stderr (`store: derived <dir>`, or `store: checkout <dir> (pre-move form, removed by U221)`), the line the
#   coordinator reads after the deploy. The same text stands in pr-merge.sh and pr-close.sh (standing order 36: no
#   helper file); this entry carries it so the settings writer reads the store the shell levers read (U465d).
# @arg $1 string The program name.
# @set store The chosen store, `pwd -P` form (the root and the toplevel are both physical).
# @set store_form `derived` or `checkout`.
# @set store_derived The derived candidate `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>`.
# @set store_checkout The checkout candidate `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # store_form is read by the other levers' callers; the function is one text with theirs
store_resolve() {
    local program=$1 path part
    [[ -n ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT:-} ]] ||
        refuse "regime-env derived no store root for ${toplevel}; the program store is judged under it (U216)"
    store_derived=${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/${program}
    store_checkout=${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
    [[ ! -L ${store_derived} ]] ||
        refuse "${store_derived} is a symlink; the derived program store is a plain directory of this user under the store root ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}, and nothing is read through a link"
    if [[ -e ${store_derived} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${store_derived} && -O ${store_derived} ]] ||
            refuse "${store_derived} exists but is not a directory of this user; the derived program store under ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT} is read only as one"
        store=${store_derived}
        store_form=derived
        echo "${lever}: store: derived ${store}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    path=${toplevel}
    for part in .orchestration orchestrate "${program}"; do
        path=${path}/${part}
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
            refuse "${path} is not a directory of this user (a symlink or a missing store); no derived store ${store_derived} exists, so ${lever} reads only the checkout's own store (the pre-move form, until U221)"
    done
    store=${store_checkout}
    store_form=checkout
    echo "${lever}: store: checkout ${store} (pre-move form, removed by U221)" >&2
}

# @description Hold the Python body beside this file as acp-broker holds acp-relay.py (relay_helper_check): readable,
#   no link, and its sha256 equal to its `claude.levers.sha256.router-settings-apply.py` pin in the manifest this
#   entry's pin came from; the body checks the same pin itself when it starts. Every read is status-checked.
# @set body The body's path.
body_check() {
    local body_pin body_digest
    body=${LEVER_DIR}/router-settings-apply.py
    [[ -r ${body} && ! -L ${body} ]] || refuse "the Python body is unreadable or a link beside this script: ${body}"
    body_pin=$(sed -n -E 's/^      router-settings-apply\.py: ([0-9a-f]{64})$/\1/p' "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || refuse "cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    [[ ${body_pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || refuse "no single sha256 pin for router-settings-apply.py in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        body_digest=$(sha256sum < "${body}") || body_digest=''
    else
        body_digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${body}") || body_digest=''
    fi
    body_digest=${body_digest%% *}
    [[ ${body_digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || refuse "cannot hash ${body}"
    [[ ${body_digest} == "${body_pin}" ]] || refuse "sha256 ${body_digest} of ${body} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
}

python=$(command -v python3) || refuse 'no python3 found (it runs the body, router-settings-apply.py beside this script)'
# The checkout the entry runs in, by its physical path, and it must be the main checkout: a linked worktree (a
# worker's clone) holds a copy of the store that is not the orchestrator's record (U71, bot P1 4370212009; the
# auditor's reproduction of round 3: a forged worktree auto row).
toplevel=$(git_isolated rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'run from the repository checkout that holds the program store'
[[ -n ${toplevel} && -d ${toplevel} ]] || refuse 'run from the repository checkout that holds the program store'
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
git_dir=$(git_isolated -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git_isolated -C "${toplevel}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) ||
    refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "a linked worktree: ${toplevel}; run from the main checkout, where the orchestrator keeps its store"
# U216: regime-env derives `REGIME_STORE_ROOT` for this checkout (its own refusals name this lever). This entry reads
# nothing in the hcom store, so the store's `origin` binding is not asked of it (`--unbound-ok`, as pr-merge.sh: the
# dotfiles program runs on the pre-U33 store pair and its derived hcom store carries no `origin`); the collision
# refusal (an `origin` naming another checkout of the same slug) and every store-root hold stay. The helper's refusal
# (return 1) is this entry's refusal status, exit 2.
regime_env "${lever}" --unbound-ok || exit 2
store_resolve regime-cutover

# The rendering beside the manifest the pin came from (U465c), its directory resolved physically: the body holds every
# component of the path it is given, and `${HOME}` or the checkout's `../..` form is not that.
source_dir=$(cd "${LEVER_MANIFEST%/*}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the manifest directory of ${LEVER_MANIFEST}"
source_json=${source_dir}/router-source.json

body_check
exec "${python}" -I "${body}" --store "${store}" --source "${source_json}" "$@"
