<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file seat-login-preflight
# @brief Report each omp seat profile's login on this host, and before a seat starts on a remote host, get its route logged in.
# @description
#   regime-cutover U37 (docs/remote-host-logins.md). A seat's model route is the provider of
#   `modelRoles.default` in its deployed overlay `~/.agents/omp/profiles/<profile>.yml`: `openai-siwc`
#   (SIWC, the audit side) or `claude-bridge` (the Claude Code child). A login is per host, so a seat on
#   the Ubuntu host reached through `herdr --remote` needs that host's own login, and the browser for it
#   is on the laptop.
#
#   `--check [<profile>...]` prints one line per profile (all overlays when none is named) from metadata
#   only, never a token: SIWC is `registration.json` (host id and issued client id, which carry no token),
#   held to the extension's record schema (one JSON document), plus the mtime of the profile's `agent.db`; Claude is
#   the one claude.ai login of the profile's login group directory `<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>` (regime-cutover
#   U318, per group since U498: the group is the one table `login_group_of_role`, copied as text from hcom-seat, the
#   worker, orchestrator and audit roles each their own group and the dsh and router roles the `router` group, so every
#   seat's bridge child and the dsh gateway child run under their group's directory as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), read by
#   one call, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> claude auth status`, whose exit status and JSON `authMethod` decide (`login
#   present (claude.ai, <dir>)`, else absent naming the method or the missing directory); the line prints the directory
#   and the method, never a credential. A profile with a seat login route (SIWC included) outside the table refuses
#   the lever (exit 2) naming the profile, the route and the table, never a line (regime-cutover U498b). A record that
#   exists but cannot be read or breaks its schema, and a producer (`uname`, `stat`, `date`, `claude`, `jq`) that
#   fails, are reported as unreadable, never as absent, and make the exit status 1.
#
#   `<profile>` (a seat profile of the manifest's `omp.roles`: orchestrator, worker or audit; `hcom-seat`
#   calls it with the seat's role before it creates or starts anything) checks that a seat can use the login,
#   which is more than `--check` shows. For the openai-siwc route a local host keeps its own browser and login,
#   so nothing happens there; on a remote host (`SSH_CONNECTION` set, or a Linux host without a display, which a
#   herdr pane on the seat host can be even when its server did not inherit `SSH_CONNECTION`) SIWC needs an
#   active `openai-siwc` login in `agent.db`, counted by the extension's `src/credentials.ts` without reading a
#   token: the issued client is saved before the token exchange, so a record proves only that a sign-in began.
#   The Claude route is checked on every host (regime-cutover U190b), local included, since the seat's child logs
#   in by its group directory's login wherever it runs: it needs `authMethod` `claude.ai` there (an `oauth_token` or
#   `api_key` method, an exit 1 of `claude auth status` or an absent directory counts as absent; the operator's
#   `~/.claude`, the Keychain item of the default directory and a variable in this environment are no input, regime-
#   cutover U312, U318). An absent login is logged in here only in the operator's own terminal (stdin and stdout a
#   TTY, not inside a seat): SIWC through `omp --profile <profile> login openai-siwc` with
#   `OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT=1455`, which the `seat-host` SSH entry forwards back from the laptop, and
#   `xdg-open`/`open` pointed at `regime-open-url` for that command only. Claude has no login to run here: the
#   operator's one step per group is the printed command `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> claude auth login` (with
#   `BROWSER=regime-open-url` in an SSH session, where the page shows a code to paste at the prompt,
#   docs/remote-host-logins.md), shell-quoted so a seats root with a space pastes whole, which Claude Code stores under
#   that directory and refreshes itself; when the legacy shared directory `.state/claude` (U318) exists and the group's
#   directory did not before this run, the refusal names it as the directory the operator may remove once every
#   running group is logged in (the kit reads, copies and removes no login, standing order 54). Both modes hold the
#   seats root, its `.state` and `claude-<group>` to real directories of this user (a link, a file or another user's
#   directory refuses, exit 2, naming the component), on one normalised spelling of the root (no empty, `.` or `..`
#   component, no trailing slash; regime-cutover U318c: `<link>//` made `-L` follow the link) and only under a parent
#   this user can search (a component that cannot be judged refuses naming it, never reads as absent); the profile mode
#   makes the chain 0700 first when absent, as hcom-seat does at a launch, so the login lands in a directory this kit
#   made. The consent click is the human step. Anywhere else (a seat, a script) it prints the command and refuses,
#   since a login is the operator's step (standing order 4).
# @arg $1 string `--check`, or the profile.
# @arg $@ string With `--check`: profile names (default: every deployed overlay).
# @env SSH_CONNECTION Set by sshd: this host is remote to the operator's terminal.
# @env DISPLAY With WAYLAND_DISPLAY: a Linux host with neither has no local browser, so it counts as remote.
# @env HCOM_LAUNCHED Set by hcom inside a seat: never run a login there.
# @env REGIME_SEATS_ROOT The seats root whose `.state/claude-<group>` directories are the login groups' Claude Code
#   directories (hcom-seat passes its resolved one), an absolute path judged on its normalised spelling; unset,
#   `~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>` of the checkout this runs in (regime-env's slug).
# @stdout With `--check`: one line per profile.
# @stderr The profile mode's report and refusals.
# @exitcode 0 Checked, or the profile's route is usable (or the host is local and the route is openai-siwc).
# @exitcode 1 A record or producer is unreadable, or a login ran and the route is still not usable.
# @exitcode 2 A usage error, a deployed profile with a seat login route outside the login group table (U498b), a
#   component of the login group's Claude Code directory path that is a link, a file or another user's directory or
#   that cannot be judged (a parent this user cannot search), a failed read of the operator's login command, or a seat
#   without a login outside the operator's terminal (a remote host, or any host on the claude-bridge route, whose login
#   is the operator's printed command).
# @example
#   seat-login-preflight --check
#   seat-login-preflight audit
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the sourced regime-env helper's caller below
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check
# The seats root derivation (regime_toplevel, regime_slug) comes from the pinned helper beside this file (U33, U318).
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || {
    echo "seat-login-preflight: refused: regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"

profiles_dir=${HOME}/.agents/omp/profiles
siwc_ext=${HOME}/.agents/omp/extensions/openai-siwc
callback_port=1455
# The seat profiles, the values of `omp.roles` in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml.
seat_profiles=(orchestrator worker audit)
# openai-siwc `src/store.ts`: `JSON.parse` of the whole file, so exactly one top-level document (jq reads a stream, so
# `-s` gathers every document and the filter requires one), then `isRegistration`, with the issued client id held to
# the charset `src/seed.ts` accepts, so nothing else reaches the terminal. \A and \z anchor the whole string.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq source, not shell
registration_filter='
if length != 1 then error("not exactly one JSON document")
else .[0]
    | if type == "object"
        and (.hostId | type == "string"
            and test("\\Aurn:uuid:[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}\\z"))
        and ((has("clientId") | not) or (.clientId | type == "string" and test("\\A[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,200}\\z")))
        and ((has("accountId") | not) or (.accountId | type == "string" and length > 0))
    then [.hostId, (.clientId // "")] | @tsv
    else error("not a registration record")
    end
end'
# `claude auth status` (Claude Code's documented reader, U318): one JSON document whose `authMethod` names the login
# (`claude.ai`, `oauth_token`, `api_key`); the method is held to a charset, the one field printed, and nothing else
# of the record reaches the terminal.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq source, not shell
auth_status_filter='
if length != 1 then error("not exactly one JSON document")
else .[0]
    | if type == "object" and (.authMethod | type == "string" and test("\\A[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,40}\\z"))
    then .authMethod
    else error("not an auth status record")
    end
end'
# The login's scratch overlay and opener shims, removed on every exit.
scratch=""
trap '[[ -z ${scratch} ]] || rm -rf -- "${scratch}"' EXIT

die() {
    printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s\n' "$*" >&2
    exit "${2:-2}"
}

# Every decision below that depends on the system reads this once, so a failed `uname` stops here.
os=$(uname -s) || die 'cannot read the system name: uname -s failed' 1
[[ -n ${os} ]] || die 'cannot read the system name: uname -s printed nothing' 1

# @description Print a file's mtime in UTC; GNU and BSD `date -r <file>` agree on this form.
# @arg $1 path File.
# @exitcode 2 `date` failed or printed nothing.
stamp() {
    local value
    value=$(date -u -r "$1" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) || return 2
    [[ -n ${value} ]] || return 2
    printf '%s\n' "${value}"
}

# @description Print a file's permission bits in octal.
# @arg $1 path File.
# @exitcode 2 `stat` failed or printed no mode.
mode_of() {
    local value
    if [[ ${os} == Darwin ]]; then
        value=$(stat -f %Lp "$1") || return 2
    else
        value=$(stat -c %a "$1") || return 2
    fi
    [[ ${value} =~ ^[0-7]{3,4}$ ]] || return 2
    printf '%s\n' "${value}"
}

# @description Print the provider of a profile's `modelRoles.default` (openai-siwc, claude-bridge, ...).
# @arg $1 string Profile name.
# @exitcode 2 The overlay exists but cannot be read.
# @exitcode 3 The overlay is absent or names no default model with a provider.
route_of() {
    local overlay=${profiles_dir}/$1.yml model
    [[ -f ${overlay} ]] || return 3
    model=$(awk '/^modelRoles:/ { in_roles = 1; next } /^[^ ]/ { in_roles = 0 } in_roles && $1 == "default:" { print $2; exit }' "${overlay}") || return 2
    # A model id without a provider prefix leaves the prefix strip unchanged.
    [[ -n ${model} && ${model%%/*} != "${model}" ]] || return 3
    printf '%s\n' "${model%%/*}"
}

# @description Print the SIWC login line of a profile.
# @arg $1 string Profile name.
# @arg $2 int 1 to also require an active login in agent.db (launch readiness), else metadata only.
# @exitcode 0 Registered with an issued client and an agent.db (and, with $2=1, a login in it). 1 Absent. 2 Unreadable.
siwc_state() {
    local profile=$1 ready=${2:-0} agent reg fields host client db mtime count
    agent=${HOME}/.omp/profiles/${profile}/agent
    reg=${agent}/openai-siwc/registration.json
    db=${agent}/agent.db
    if [[ ! -e ${reg} ]]; then
        printf 'absent (no %s)\n' "${reg}"
        return 1
    fi
    if ! command -v jq > /dev/null; then
        printf 'unreadable (no jq on PATH to read %s)\n' "${reg}"
        return 2
    fi
    if ! fields=$(jq -ers "${registration_filter}" "${reg}" 2> /dev/null); then
        printf 'unreadable (%s)\n' "${reg}"
        return 2
    fi
    IFS=$'\t' read -r host client <<< "${fields}"
    if [[ -z ${client} ]]; then
        printf 'absent (registration started, no issued client yet: host %s)\n' "${host}"
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -f ${db} ]]; then
        printf 'absent (registered: host %s, client %s; no %s)\n' "${host}" "${client}" "${db}"
        return 1
    fi
    if ! mtime=$(stamp "${db}"); then
        printf 'unreadable (cannot read the mtime of %s)\n' "${db}"
        return 2
    fi
    if ((ready)); then
        if ! count=$(bun "${siwc_ext}/src/credentials.ts" --profile "${profile}") || [[ ! ${count} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            printf 'unreadable (cannot count the openai-siwc logins in %s)\n' "${db}"
            return 2
        fi
        if ((count == 0)); then
            printf 'absent (registered: host %s, client %s; no openai-siwc login in %s)\n' "${host}" "${client}" "${db}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    printf 'registered (host %s, client %s), agent.db mtime %s\n' "${host}" "${client}" "${mtime}"
}

# @description Set `claude_seats_root` to the one spelling of the absolute path `$1` (regime-cutover U318c): every
#   run of `/` is one `/`, a `.` component is dropped, a `..` component takes the component before it (none at the
#   root), and no `/` ends it (a bare `/` stays `/`). Lexical, by parameter expansion alone: `realpath` or `pwd -P`
#   would follow the link the component tests must catch, and `${root%/}` stripped one slash, so `<link>//` kept a
#   trailing slash that made `-L` follow the link.
# @arg $1 string An absolute path.
# @set claude_seats_root The normalised spelling.
seats_root_normalise() {
    local rest=$1 part n
    local -a parts=()
    while [[ -n ${rest} ]]; do
        part=${rest%%/*}
        if [[ ${rest} == */* ]]; then rest=${rest#*/}; else rest=''; fi # lint-comparisons: allow a split of one path into its components, no path compare
        case ${part} in
        '' | .) ;;
        ..)
            n=${#parts[@]}
            ((n == 0)) || unset "parts[n - 1]"
            ;;
        *) parts+=("${part}") ;;
        esac
    done
    claude_seats_root=''
    for part in ${parts[@]+"${parts[@]}"}; do
        claude_seats_root+=/${part}
    done
    [[ -n ${claude_seats_root} ]] || claude_seats_root=/
}

# @description Print the login group of the role `$1` (regime-cutover U498): the one table both this lever and
#   hcom-seat hold as the same text (each lever's tests assert the table and their equality). Every seat
#   of a role shares its group's Claude Code directory `<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>` and no other group's:
#   the omp roles worker, orchestrator and audit are each their own group; the dsh and router roles are the `router`
#   group, since the dsh gateway child is the Router's. Any other name is no role of the table (status 1, nothing
#   printed), so a caller that reads the status refuses instead of deriving a directory.
# @arg $1 string The role.
# @stdout The group.
# @exitcode 1 The role is not in the table.
login_group_of_role() {
    case $1 in
    worker) printf 'worker\n' ;;
    orchestrator) printf 'orchestrator\n' ;;
    audit) printf 'audit\n' ;;
    dsh | router) printf 'router\n' ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

# @description Set `claude_config` to the Claude Code directory of the profile `$1`'s login group under this host's
#   seats root, `<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>` (regime-cutover U318, per group since U498; hcom-seat's
#   `claude_config` row, the group from the one table login_group_of_role), `claude_legacy` to the legacy shared
#   directory `<seats-root>/.state/claude` (U318; named, never read or made) and `claude_seats_root` to that root:
#   `REGIME_SEATS_ROOT` when set (hcom-seat passes its resolved one; it must be absolute), else
#   `~/.local/state/omp-seats/<slug>` of the checkout this runs in (regime-env's toplevel and slug readers; the store
#   binding is hcom-seat's concern), with HOME in `pwd -P` form. Either form is normalised to one spelling
#   (seats_root_normalise) before any test reads it, so every component test and every printed path use that spelling.
#   A failure sets `claude_config_error` and returns 2.
# @arg $1 string The profile (a role of the table).
# @set claude_config The directory.
# @set claude_legacy The legacy shared directory.
# @set claude_seats_root The seats root, normalised.
# @set claude_config_error The reason, when none can be derived.
# @exitcode 2 No seats root can be derived, REGIME_SEATS_ROOT is not an absolute path, or the profile is outside the
#   login group table.
claude_config_dir() {
    local root=${REGIME_SEATS_ROOT:-} top slug home group
    claude_config='' claude_legacy='' claude_seats_root='' claude_config_error=''
    if ! group=$(login_group_of_role "$1"); then
        claude_config_error="no login group for the profile $1; the table names orchestrator, worker, audit, dsh and router"
        return 2
    fi
    if [[ -z ${root} ]]; then
        if ! top=$(regime_toplevel); then
            claude_config_error='no seats root: set REGIME_SEATS_ROOT or run inside a checkout'
            return 2
        fi
        if ! slug=$(regime_slug "${top}"); then
            claude_config_error="no seats root: cannot derive a repository slug from ${top}"
            return 2
        fi
        if ! home=$(cd "${HOME}" && pwd -P); then
            claude_config_error="no seats root: cannot resolve HOME ${HOME}"
            return 2
        fi
        root=${home}/.local/state/omp-seats/${slug}
    fi
    if [[ ${root} != /* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path test on one path, no path compare
        claude_config_error="no seats root: REGIME_SEATS_ROOT ${root} is not an absolute path"
        return 2
    fi
    seats_root_normalise "${root}"
    claude_config=${claude_seats_root%/}/.state/claude-${group}
    claude_legacy=${claude_seats_root%/}/.state/claude
}

# @description Set `claude_legacy_note` for the profile mode's refusal (regime-cutover U498): when the legacy shared
#   directory `claude_legacy` (U318) is a real directory and the group's directory `claude_config` does not exist yet,
#   the note names the legacy directory as the one the operator may remove once every running group is logged in;
#   otherwise the note is empty. Called after claude_config_dir and before claude_config_ensure makes the group's
#   directory, by `-d` and `-L` alone: nothing under either directory is read, copied or removed (standing order 54).
# @set claude_legacy_note The note, or empty.
legacy_note_hold() {
    claude_legacy_note=''
    if [[ -d ${claude_legacy} && ! -L ${claude_legacy} && ! -e ${claude_config} && ! -L ${claude_config} ]]; then
        claude_legacy_note="; the legacy shared directory ${claude_legacy} (one login per seats root, U318) is read by no seat: remove it once every running group is logged in"
    fi
}

# @description Print the operator's one Claude step for the group: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> claude auth login`, after
#   `BROWSER=regime-open-url` in an SSH session, where the laptop's browser opens the page and shows a code to paste at
#   the prompt (docs/remote-host-logins.md). The directory is shell-quoted (`%q`), so a seats root holding a space, a
#   quote or a `$` pastes as one assignment of the same directory (regime-cutover U318b).
# @stdout The command, one line.
claude_login_command() {
    local browser=''
    [[ -z ${SSH_CONNECTION:-} ]] || browser='BROWSER=regime-open-url '
    printf '%sCLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=%q claude auth login\n' "${browser}" "${claude_config}"
}

# @description Refuse the Claude route's absent login after its state line, naming the operator's one step: the
#   command claude_login_command prints, whose status is read (standing order 21; regime-cutover U318b: unread, a
#   failed producer printed an ordinary absence with an empty command), so a failed producer refuses naming it instead;
#   then the legacy note legacy_note_hold set, when it set one (U498; empty when the caller held none).
# @arg $1 string The profile line of the absent state.
# @exitcode 2 Always: the login is the operator's step, or its command could not be produced (the command dies).
claude_login_refuse() {
    local step
    step=$(claude_login_command) || die "$1; cannot name the operator's login step: claude_login_command failed"
    die "$1; log in once: ${step}; a login is the operator's step: run that command in your own terminal on this host, then start the seat again${claude_legacy_note:-}"
}

# @description Hold the login group's Claude Code directory path to its three components, the seats root, its `.state`
#   and `claude-<group>` (claude_config_dir, on the normalised spelling), each absent or a directory of this user that is no
#   symbolic link; both modes call it before anything reads or makes the directory, and it writes nothing. A file test
#   (`-L`, `-e`, `-d`, `-O`) answers false both for "not so" and for "could not look", so a component is judged only
#   under a parent this user can search: the nearest ancestor this user can see is found first (`-e` true needs its
#   own parent searchable; `/` is always seen), a directory there that this user cannot search refuses naming the
#   component and the directory (regime-cutover U318c: an owned root of mode 000 hid a linked `.state`, which read as
#   absent), and an absent entry under a searchable directory is absent, as is everything below a file or a dangling
#   link (the profile mode's mkdir names that). A link, a file or another user's directory refuses naming the
#   component, since a login under it would land outside what this kit made (regime-cutover U318b: `--check` judged the
#   leaf alone, so a linked `.state` reached another directory and a file there read as absent).
# @exitcode 2 A component is a symbolic link, not a directory, a directory of another user, or cannot be judged (the
#   command dies).
claude_config_validate() {
    local path seen above kind
    for path in "${claude_seats_root}" "${claude_seats_root%/}/.state" "${claude_config}"; do
        seen=${path%/*}
        [[ -n ${seen} ]] || seen=/
        above=0
        while [[ ! -e ${seen} && ! -L ${seen} ]] && ((${#seen} > 1)); do
            seen=${seen%/*}
            [[ -n ${seen} ]] || seen=/
            above=1
        done
        [[ -d ${seen} ]] || return 0
        [[ -x ${seen} ]] ||
            die "refused: cannot read the login group's Claude Code directory path component ${path} (permission denied: ${seen} is not searchable by this user); fix its mode before a seat starts"
        ((above == 0)) || return 0
        if [[ -L ${path} ]]; then
            kind='a symbolic link'
        elif [[ ! -e ${path} ]]; then
            return 0
        elif [[ ! -d ${path} ]]; then
            kind='not a directory'
        elif [[ ! -O ${path} ]]; then
            kind='a directory of another user'
        else
            continue
        fi
        die "refused: the login group's Claude Code directory path component ${path} is ${kind}; move it aside before a seat starts"
    done
}

# @description Make the login group's Claude Code directory 0700, with its `.state` parent and the seats root, when
#   absent (regime-cutover U318, U498), as hcom-seat makes them at a launch, so the operator's login lands in a directory this kit
#   made, after claude_config_validate has held the three to real directories of this user; nothing else is written.
#   Runs in the profile mode alone (`--check` reports an absent directory as absent).
# @exitcode 1 The mkdir failed (the command dies). 2 A component refuses (claude_config_validate).
claude_config_ensure() {
    claude_config_validate
    [[ -d ${claude_config} ]] || (umask 077 && mkdir -p "${claude_config}") ||
        die "cannot create the login group's Claude Code directory ${claude_config}" 1
}

# @description Print the Claude Code login line of this host (regime-cutover U318, U498): the one claude.ai login of
#   the group directory `claude_config`, which the caller derived (claude_config_dir) and held to a real directory chain
#   of this user (claude_config_validate) in its own shell, so a refusal there exits the lever naming the component;
#   every seat of the group's roles runs its bridge child, or the dsh gateway child, under it. The login is read by one call,
#   `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> claude auth status`, with its status and its JSON (one document, read by jq as the SIWC
#   record is; `authMethod` a string held to a charset, the one field that reaches the terminal). Present when
#   `authMethod` is `claude.ai`; absent when the call exits 1 (not logged in), names another method (`oauth_token`,
#   `api_key`: a token or key the seat never gets) or the directory is absent; unreadable, never absent, when claude or
#   jq is missing, the call exits otherwise or prints no auth status record (standing order 21). A
#   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in this environment is no input (regime-cutover U312): the call runs without it, as the
#   seat shim clears it. The operator's step for an absent login is the caller's (claude_login_refuse).
# @exitcode 0 Present. 1 Absent. 2 Unreadable.
claude_state() {
    local body status=0 method tool
    if [[ ! -d ${claude_config} ]]; then
        printf 'absent (no %s)\n' "${claude_config}"
        return 1
    fi
    for tool in claude jq; do
        if ! command -v "${tool}" > /dev/null; then
            printf 'unreadable (no %s on PATH to read the login of %s)\n' "${tool}" "${claude_config}"
            return 2
        fi
    done
    # The one call, under the group's directory and without a caller's token name; its stderr is dropped, its stdout
    # goes to jq alone, so no field but the method is ever printed.
    body=$(unset CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN && CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=${claude_config} claude auth status 2> /dev/null) || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0) ;;
    1)
        printf 'absent (not logged in under %s)\n' "${claude_config}"
        return 1
        ;;
    *)
        printf 'unreadable (claude auth status exited %s under %s)\n' "${status}" "${claude_config}"
        return 2
        ;;
    esac
    if ! method=$(jq -ers "${auth_status_filter}" <<< "${body}" 2> /dev/null); then
        printf 'unreadable (claude auth status printed no auth status record under %s)\n' "${claude_config}"
        return 2
    fi
    if [[ ${method} == claude.ai ]]; then
        printf 'login present (claude.ai, %s)\n' "${claude_config}"
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'absent (authMethod %s under %s, not claude.ai)\n' "${method}" "${claude_config}"
    return 1
}

# @description Print `<profile> <route>: <state>` for one profile.
# @arg $1 string Profile name.
# @arg $2 int 1 for launch readiness (the profile mode), else metadata only (`--check`).
# @exitcode 0 Logged in. 1 Absent. 2 Unreadable. 3 No seat login route, so nothing to log in.
profile_line() {
    local route state status=0 ready=${2:-0}
    route=$(route_of "$1") || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0) ;;
    2)
        printf '%s: unreadable (%s)\n' "$1" "${profiles_dir}/$1.yml"
        return 2
        ;;
    *)
        printf '%s: no route (overlay %s absent or without modelRoles.default)\n' "$1" "${profiles_dir}/$1.yml"
        return 3
        ;;
    esac
    # The login group table covers every seat login route (regime-cutover U498b; verdict U498-e08ce84c P2 `:525`: until
    # this head the table ran for the Claude route alone, so an SIWC overlay outside it read as `absent` with exit 0).
    # A profile with a route and no group refuses the lever naming the profile, the route and the table; no line is
    # printed for it and nothing is read or made (standing order 21: the status of the one table decides).
    case ${route} in
    openai-siwc | claude-bridge)
        login_group_of_role "$1" > /dev/null ||
            die "refused: the profile $1 (${route}) is outside the login group table login_group_of_role, which names orchestrator, worker, audit, dsh and router; it has no login group, so no line is printed for it"
        ;;
    esac
    case ${route} in
    openai-siwc) state=$(siwc_state "$1" "${ready}") || status=$? ;;
    claude-bridge)
        # The directory is derived per login group and its chain judged in this shell, so a bad component refuses the
        # lever naming it (claude_config_validate), where a subshell's exit would read as one unreadable line (regime-cutover U318b).
        if claude_config_dir "$1"; then
            claude_config_validate
            state=$(claude_state) || status=$?
        else
            state="unreadable (${claude_config_error})" status=2
        fi
        ;;
    *) state="not a seat login route" status=3 ;;
    esac
    printf '%s %s: %s\n' "$1" "${route}" "${state}"
    return "${status}"
}

# @description `--check`: one line per profile, exit 1 when any record is unreadable.
check() {
    local profile overlay failed=0 status
    local -a profiles=("$@")
    if ((${#profiles[@]} == 0)); then
        for overlay in "${profiles_dir}"/*.yml; do
            # Parameter expansion, so no external producer (basename) can fail unseen.
            [[ -f ${overlay} ]] || continue
            overlay=${overlay##*/}
            profiles+=("${overlay%.yml}")
        done
    fi
    if ((${#profiles[@]} == 0)); then
        printf 'not applicable: no omp seat profiles under %s\n' "${profiles_dir}"
        return 0
    fi
    for profile in "${profiles[@]}"; do
        status=0
        profile_line "${profile}" || status=$?
        ((status == 2)) && failed=1
    done
    return "${failed}"
}

# @description Name the laptop this SSH session comes from, from the tailnet when it knows the address.
peer_name() {
    local client=${SSH_CONNECTION%% *} name=""
    if [[ -n ${client} ]] && command -v tailscale > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        name=$(tailscale status --json 2> /dev/null | jq -r --arg ip "${client}" \
            'first(.Peer[]? | select(any(.TailscaleIPs[]?; . == $ip)) | .DNSName) // empty' 2> /dev/null) || name=""
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${name:-${client:-the laptop of the seat-host SSH session}}"
}

# @description Run the role's login in the operator's terminal, then report whether it took. The Claude route never
#   reaches here: its login is the operator's printed command (U318), so the caller refuses before this runs.
# @arg $1 string Role (its profile has the same name).
# @arg $2 string Route.
login() {
    local role=$1 route=$2 status=0 peer
    scratch=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/seat-login.XXXXXX") || die "cannot create a scratch directory" 1
    peer=$(peer_name) || die "cannot name the host whose browser opens the sign-in" 1
    printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s needs a %s login on this host; the sign-in opens in the browser of %s\n' "${role}" "${route}" "${peer}" >&2
    # The CLI login loads extensions from settings only, so a one-command overlay names it.
    printf 'extensions:\n  - %s\n' "${siwc_ext}" > "${scratch}/siwc.yml"
    for opener in xdg-open open; do
        printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec regime-open-url "$@"\n' > "${scratch}/${opener}"
        chmod 700 "${scratch}/${opener}"
    done
    PATH="${scratch}:${PATH}" PI_CONFIG_FILES="${scratch}/siwc.yml" OPENAI_SIWC_CALLBACK_PORT=${callback_port} \
        omp --profile "${role}" login openai-siwc || status=$?
    ((status == 0)) || die "the ${route} login exited ${status}" 1
}

usage='usage: seat-login-preflight --check [<profile>...] | seat-login-preflight <orchestrator|worker|audit>'
(($# > 0)) || die "${usage}"
if [[ $1 == --check ]]; then
    shift
    check "$@"
    exit $?
fi
(($# == 1)) || die "${usage}"
role=$1
known=0
for profile in "${seat_profiles[@]}"; do
    if [[ ${role} == "${profile}" ]]; then known=1; fi
done
((known)) || die "unknown seat profile '${role}'; expected one of: ${seat_profiles[*]}"
# A local host keeps its own browser and SIWC login, so nothing new happens there for that route. The Claude route's
# rule holds on every host (regime-cutover U190b): the seat's bridge child logs in by the token alone wherever it runs,
# so a local host with a host login only would start a seat whose first bridge turn ends `Not logged in`.
route_status=0
route=$(route_of "${role}") || route_status=$?
if ((route_status == 0)) && [[ ${route} == openai-siwc && -z ${SSH_CONNECTION:-} ]] &&
    ! [[ ${os} == Linux && -z ${DISPLAY:-} && -z ${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-} ]]; then
    exit 0
fi
# The Claude route's login lives in the role's login group directory of this seats root (U318, U498): derived here, its
# chain held to real directories of this user and made 0700 when absent, before the one status call, so the operator's
# login lands in a directory this kit made; the legacy note is held before the group's directory is made.
claude_legacy_note=''
if ((route_status == 0)) && [[ ${route} == claude-bridge ]]; then
    claude_config_dir "${role}" || die "${role} ${route}: unreadable (${claude_config_error}); fix it before a seat starts" 1
    legacy_note_hold
    claude_config_ensure
fi

status=0
line=$(profile_line "${role}" 1) || status=$?
case ${status} in
0)
    printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s\n' "${line}" >&2
    exit 0
    ;;
2) die "${line}; fix or move the record aside before a seat starts" 1 ;;
3)
    printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s; nothing to log in\n' "${line}" >&2
    exit 0
    ;;
esac
route=$(route_of "${role}") || die "${line}" 1
# The Claude route has no login to run here: the operator's one command follows the line (U318, standing order 48).
if [[ ${route} == claude-bridge ]]; then
    claude_login_refuse "${line}"
fi
if [[ ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 || -n ${HCOM_LAUNCHED:-} ]]; then
    die "${line}; a login is the operator's step: run \`seat-login-preflight ${role}\` in your own terminal on this host, then start the seat again"
fi
login "${role}" "${route}"
status=0
line=$(profile_line "${role}" 1) || status=$?
((status == 0)) || die "${line} after the login" 1
printf 'seat-login-preflight: %s\n' "${line}" >&2
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file seat-settings-render.sh
# @brief The one srt settings writer of the seat levers: the rows every seat's settings share and the JSON text they are written in, sourced by hcom-seat and acp-broker.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U344 (M-24 part 2; U344c). Sourced by `hcom-seat` (every role's settings) and by `acp-broker` (the
#   worker's settings, per connection), never run on its own. It carries no self-check of its own (regime-cutover
#   U344c, verdict U344-a8adad11 P1 `seat-settings-render.sh:76`, class pin-then-run: a check inside sourced text
#   runs after every line before it, so a replaced file ran unpinned up to that line and the check proved nothing
#   about the bytes that ran). The lever that sources it hashes the copy it sources: it reads the file beside itself
#   once into a private per-launch copy under its own state directory `~/.local/state/hcom-seat/`, hashes that copy
#   against the `claude.levers.sha256.seat-settings-render.sh` pin of the manifest its own self-check read, sources
#   the copy and removes the copy's directory at once (hcom-seat's and acp-broker's `renderer_source`, the form of
#   hcom-seat's helper_copy_make, U310f), so the bytes hashed are the bytes sourced and nothing of this file runs
#   before its digest equals the pin. It holds what the two renderings shared by copy until U344 (the U343 header:
#   "This copy of the dsh row's shape is interim: U344 extracts one writer for both levers"): the path rule every
#   settings row obeys (clean_path, clean_row), the fixed rows of the deny table (the credential stores denied for
#   read, the project files denied for write under a seat's own directory, the rows denied for write under the
#   shared Claude Code directory), the domain list, and the JSON writer (seat_settings_rows_json for a list,
#   seat_settings_json for the file's text). It judges nothing (each lever's `settings_judge` stays its own) and
#   writes no file (the caller writes the text it is handed, as before); each lever passes its rows, its
#   `allowLocalBinding` value, its `allowUnixSockets` list and its Linux tool fragment. `acp-broker` reads the deny
#   table back from the Router's settings `hcom-seat` rendered, so the rows below are spelled once and rendered
#   once. tests/unit/test_acp_broker.py `test_one_settings_writer_renders_the_worker_and_the_dsh_row_byte_for_byte`
#   holds the two levers' files byte-identical but the role's own rows.

# @description Succeed when `$1` is a clean absolute path that srt cannot read as a pattern: `/` followed by
#   components of `[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]` only (no glob metacharacter `*?[]{}`, no whitespace, no quote or backslash), none
#   of them empty, `.` or `..`, and no trailing `/`. srt 0.0.81 turns a settings path into a Seatbelt regex or a glob,
#   so `/private/tmp/hcom*` would grant its siblings; a clean path names exactly itself (regime-cutover U85).
# @arg $1 string The path.
# @exitcode 1 The path is not clean.
clean_path() {
    [[ $1 =~ ^(/[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]+)+$ ]] || return 1
    [[ /$1/ != */./* && /$1/ != */../* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow a component test on one path, no path compare
}

# @description Succeed when `$1` is a row the settings may carry: a clean path, or (for `denyWrite`, `$2` = 1) one of
#   the macOS worktree patterns `hcom-seat` renders, a clean prefix and the fixed `worktrees/*/<file>` suffix, the
#   one place a settings entry is not a clean path (srt reads `*` as `[^/]*`).
# @arg $1 string The row.
# @arg $2 int 1 when the pattern form is allowed.
# @exitcode 1 The row is neither.
clean_row() {
    clean_path "$1" && return 0
    (($2)) || return 1
    [[ $1 =~ ^(/[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]+)+/worktrees/\*/(config\.worktree|info|commondir|gitdir)$ ]] || return 1
    [[ /${1%/worktrees/*}/ != */./* && /${1%/worktrees/*}/ != */../* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow a component test on one pattern's clean prefix, no path compare
}

# The fixed rows of the deny table, relative to the root each is rendered under (hcom-seat seat_settings_render
# renders them for every role; acp-broker reads them back from the Router's settings, re-rooting the project-file rows
# under the task cwd, so each list is spelled here once). The credential stores every seat is denied for read, under
# HOME. The project files a seat is denied for write under its own directory (a cwd that holds `.omp` is refused
# outright: omp merges it before `disabledProviders` applies; the hook shims under `.claude/hooks` import their code
# from `.claude/contextdb`, run by sessions outside the seat). The rows denied for write under the shared Claude Code
# directory, what another seat's child or the operator's login command would load (regime-cutover U318, U190).
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source this helper
SEAT_SETTINGS_CREDENTIAL_DENIES=(.ssh .gnupg .aws .netrc .docker .kube .config/gcloud .codex .omp/agent)
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source this helper
SEAT_SETTINGS_PROJECT_FILES=(.claude/settings.json .claude/settings.local.json .claude/hooks .claude/contextdb .omp .codex .envrc .mcp.json)
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source this helper
SEAT_SETTINGS_CLAUDE_ROWS=(settings.json settings.local.json rules hooks plugins skills commands agents)
# The outbound hosts every seat may reach (`network.allowedDomains`): GitHub and its API, upload, codeload and content
# hosts; PyPI; the Anthropic and Claude hosts; the OpenAI hosts of the openai-siwc route.
SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS='"github.com","api.github.com","uploads.github.com","codeload.github.com","objects.githubusercontent.com"'
SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS+=',"raw.githubusercontent.com","release-assets.githubusercontent.com","pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org"'
SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS+=',"api.anthropic.com","claude.ai","platform.claude.com","console.anthropic.com"'
SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS+=',"chatgpt.com","auth.openai.com","api.openai.com"'

# @description Print a JSON array of the rows `$@` in their order, each held to clean_row first, so no JSON escaping is
#   needed and no settings tool runs; a row that is not clean fails the function with nothing printed, and the caller
#   refuses naming the list (standing order 21: the caller reads this status).
# @arg $1 int 1 when the macOS worktree pattern form is allowed (a `denyWrite` list).
# @arg $@ string The rows after it.
# @stdout The array, `[]` for no rows.
# @exitcode 1 A row is not one the settings may carry.
seat_settings_rows_json() {
    local patterns=$1 row out='' sep=''
    shift
    for row in "$@"; do
        clean_row "${row}" "${patterns}" || return 1
        out+=${sep}\"${row}\"
        sep=,
    done
    printf '[%s]' "${out}"
}

# @description Set `settings_json` to the one-line text of a seat's srt settings file from its rendered lists: the
#   network block (the domain list above, no denied domain, the `allowUnixSockets` list `$2`, the trustd Mach
#   lookup every sandboxed process needs, the `allowLocalBinding` value `$1`), the filesystem block in the order
#   `denyRead`, `allowRead`, `allowWrite`, `denyWrite`, `allowPty` true and, on Linux, the tool fragment `$7` naming
#   the checked bwrap, socat and rg. The key order and the compact form are what the levers wrote before this helper
#   (hcom-seat seat_sandbox_write, acp-broker), so every earlier head's settings re-render byte for byte.
# @arg $1 string `true` or `false`, the role's `allowLocalBinding`.
# @arg $2 string The `allowUnixSockets` JSON array (seat_settings_rows_json; `[]` for every role but the router).
# @arg $3 string The `denyRead` JSON array.
# @arg $4 string The `allowRead` JSON array.
# @arg $5 string The `allowWrite` JSON array.
# @arg $6 string The `denyWrite` JSON array.
# @arg $7 string The Linux tool fragment (`,"bwrapPath":…`), empty on macOS.
# @set settings_json The text, without a trailing newline.
# @exitcode 1 `$1` is neither `true` nor `false`.
seat_settings_json() {
    [[ $1 == true || $1 == false ]] || return 1
    settings_json="{\"network\":{\"allowedDomains\":[${SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS}],\"deniedDomains\":[],\"allowUnixSockets\":$2"
    settings_json+=",\"allowMachLookup\":[\"com.apple.trustd.agent\"],\"allowLocalBinding\":$1}"
    settings_json+=",\"filesystem\":{\"denyRead\":$3,\"allowRead\":$4"
    settings_json+=",\"allowWrite\":$5,\"denyWrite\":$6},\"allowPty\":true$7}"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_setup-gh
# @brief Log in `gh` through gh-auth.sh and upload the local SSH key.
# @description
#   Logs this machine into GitHub through the one login path, the dotfiles
#   checkout's `scripts/gh-auth.sh` (file storage the sandboxed seats can read;
#   the checkout is found through `chezmoi source-path`, so any sourceDir works),
#   ensures the local SSH public key exists through an explicit interactive
#   flow, and registers it as both an authentication and a commit signing key.
#   The two key uploads need `admin:public_key` and `admin:ssh_signing_key`;
#   they run under a separate one-off login in a temporary `GH_CONFIG_DIR`,
#   which is logged out and deleted afterwards, so the machine login every
#   agent uses never gains those scopes. `gh auth logout` does not revoke the
#   one-off token on GitHub; revoke it under Settings → Applications if wanted.
# @example
#   setup-gh

set -Eeuo pipefail

readonly DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH="${HOME%/}/.ssh/id_ed25519"
readonly DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH="${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}.pub"

# @description Print the dotfiles checkout's scripts/gh-auth.sh. The checkout is chezmoi's configured
#   sourceDir, not always ~/.local/share/chezmoi: `chezmoi source-path` names its home/ subtree
#   (.chezmoiroot), and git names the repository root above it.
# @stdout Absolute path of an executable scripts/gh-auth.sh.
# @exitcode 1 chezmoi or git is missing or fails, or the script is not there.
function gh_auth_script() {
    local source_path top script
    if ! command -v chezmoi > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf 'setup-gh: chezmoi is not installed, so the dotfiles checkout holding scripts/gh-auth.sh cannot be found\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! source_path="$(chezmoi source-path)" || [ -z "${source_path}" ]; then
        printf 'setup-gh: chezmoi source-path failed; cannot find the dotfiles checkout\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if ! top="$(git -C "${source_path}" rev-parse --show-toplevel)" || [ -z "${top}" ]; then
        printf 'setup-gh: %s is not inside a git checkout; cannot find scripts/gh-auth.sh\n' "${source_path}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    script="${top}/scripts/gh-auth.sh"
    if [[ ! -x "${script}" ]]; then
        printf 'setup-gh: %s not found; run "make gh-auth" in the dotfiles checkout\n' "${script}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${script}"
}

# @description Log in the machine's GitHub account through the dotfiles checkout's gh-auth.sh.
# @exitcode 1 gh-auth.sh cannot be found or the login did not complete.
function login_to_github() {
    local script
    script="$(gh_auth_script)" || return 1
    "${script}"
}

# @description Print the short host name, or fail naming the read when neither form works.
function short_hostname() {
    if ! hostname -s 2> /dev/null && ! hostname; then
        printf 'setup-gh: cannot read the host name for the SSH key comment\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

# @description Return the email address used as the SSH key comment.
function ssh_key_comment() {
    local configured_email host
    configured_email="$(git config --global --get user.email || true)"

    if [[ -n "${configured_email}" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${configured_email}"
        return 0
    fi

    host="$(short_hostname)" || return 1
    printf '%s@%s\n' "${USER:-user}" "${host}"
}

# @description Create the default SSH key through ssh-keygen when it is missing.
function ensure_default_ssh_key() {
    local comment

    if [[ -r "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi

    if [[ -e "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" && ! -e "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" && -t 0 ]]; then
        ssh-keygen -y -f "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" > "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
        chmod 0644 "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
        return 0
    fi

    if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
        printf 'Public SSH key not found: %s\n' "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" >&2
        printf "Run \`ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f %s -C \"\$(git config --global --get user.email)\"\` or restore the key from private chezmoi state.\n" "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    mkdir -p "${HOME%/}/.ssh"
    chmod 0700 "${HOME%/}/.ssh"

    comment="$(ssh_key_comment)" || return 1
    printf 'Default SSH key not found. Creating %s interactively.\n' "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" >&2
    ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}" -C "${comment}"
    chmod 0600 "${DEFAULT_SSH_KEY_PATH}"
    chmod 0644 "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}"
}

# The one-off login's GH_CONFIG_DIR until it is removed; empty once cleaned up.
KEY_CONFIG=""
# Set once the logout has started, so a cleanup re-entered from a signal trap skips it.
KEY_LOGOUT_STARTED=""

# @description Log out the one-off login and delete its config directory. KEY_CONFIG is cleared
#   only after the directory is gone, so a signal during the logout or the removal re-enters this
#   function from its trap, skips the logout already started, and still removes the directory.
#   Idempotent: a call after a finished cleanup does nothing.
function cleanup_key_login() {
    local dir="${KEY_CONFIG}"
    [ -n "${dir}" ] || return 0
    if [ -z "${KEY_LOGOUT_STARTED}" ]; then
        KEY_LOGOUT_STARTED=1
        GH_CONFIG_DIR="${dir}" gh auth logout -h github.com > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
    rm -rf "${dir}"
    KEY_CONFIG=""
}

# @description Upload the local public SSH key under a one-off login that holds the key-admin scopes.
#   The cleanup trap is installed before the login starts, so INT, TERM or HUP after authentication
#   still log out and delete the token file (exit 128 + the signal number).
function add_ssh_key_to_github() {
    local status=0
    ensure_default_ssh_key
    trap cleanup_key_login EXIT
    trap 'cleanup_key_login; exit 129' HUP
    trap 'cleanup_key_login; exit 130' INT
    trap 'cleanup_key_login; exit 143' TERM
    KEY_CONFIG="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/setup-gh.XXXXXX")" || return 1
    (
        export GH_CONFIG_DIR="${KEY_CONFIG}"
        unset GH_TOKEN GITHUB_TOKEN
        printf 'setup-gh: a one-off login with admin:public_key and admin:ssh_signing_key uploads the key; the machine login keeps its scopes\n' >&2
        gh auth login -h github.com -p https --insecure-storage -s admin:public_key,admin:ssh_signing_key &&
            gh ssh-key add "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" --type authentication &&
            gh ssh-key add "${DEFAULT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_PATH}" --type signing
    ) || status=$?
    cleanup_key_login
    trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM
    return "${status}"
}

# @description Run the GitHub authentication and SSH key setup flow.
function main() {
    login_to_github
    add_ssh_key_to_github
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_setup-gpg
# @brief Prepare the local GnuPG secret keyring when no private source restored it.
# @description
#   Checks whether a local GnuPG secret key already exists. If not, starts the
#   standard interactive `gpg --full-generate-key` flow. Secret keys and trust
#   databases are intentionally not stored in the public chezmoi source state.
# @example
#   setup-gpg

set -Eeuo pipefail

# @description Return success when at least one GnuPG secret key exists.
function has_gpg_secret_key() {
    gpg --batch --list-secret-keys --with-colons 2> /dev/null | grep -q '^sec:'
}

# @description Create a GnuPG secret key through the standard interactive flow.
function generate_gpg_secret_key() {
    if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
        printf 'No local GnuPG secret key was found.\n' >&2
        printf "Run \`gpg --full-generate-key\` interactively or restore keys from the private chezmoi source.\n" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    printf 'No local GnuPG secret key was found. Starting interactive key generation.\n' >&2
    gpg --full-generate-key
}

# @description Run the GnuPG setup flow.
function main() {
    if has_gpg_secret_key; then
        printf 'GnuPG secret key already exists. Nothing to do.\n'
        return 0
    fi

    generate_gpg_secret_key
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -I
"""Bind the Router's pull request to one program unit from its ticket, the request text as data (regime-cutover U493).

The three gate levers (the `regime` check, pr-audit.sh, pr-merge.sh) resolve a pull request's unit from the one body
line `Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>`, and a pull request the Router's account opens for a ticket carries none: PR 777
(ticket bf72b83b) failed the required check and could not enter the gates (handoff/44-u493-ticket-unit-design.md,
table row f25). The ticket is the unit. `ticket-unit.py <store> --db <orchestrator.sqlite> --pr <n> --branch <name>
--head <sha> [--lock-wait <seconds>]` reads the ticket whose `follows` names that pull request from the Router's
sqlite (read-only), renders the ticket's request text into a brief under `briefs/U<n>-ticket-<id>.md` as data,
appends the unit's row to `units.tsv`, and prints the line the coordinator writes into the pull request's body with
pr-body-edit.sh. The gate levers do not change; the lever runs no `gh` and no git (the coordinator reads the pull
request's branch and head and passes them).

The binding is two-sided and both sides are the Router's own facts: exactly one ticket's `follows` holds `thread ==
"github:<pr>"` with `own` true (none or two is a refusal naming the count), and `--branch` equals `agent/` plus the
ticket's `execution.name` (else a refusal). The sqlite table `ticket (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)` holds one
JSON document per ticket, read with the `sqlite3` module over the URI `file:<db>?mode=ro` and the `json` module
(parser-module form; nothing hand-written over the text); a value that is not a JSON object, or a `follows` that is
not a list of objects, is a refusal naming the ticket. The fields used are each held to a grammar before use: `id`
(32 lowercase hex, equal to the row's key), `title` and `mandate.scope` (text, data), `mandate.basis.sender` and
`mandate.actor.id` (`[A-Za-z0-9-]+`), `channels[0].thread` (`[a-z]+:[0-9]+`), `execution.name` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`),
`decisionId` (32 hex), `createdAt` (`<YYYY-MM-DD>T<HH:MM:SS>[.<fraction>]Z`). The arguments: `--pr` 1 to 9 digits
with no leading zero, `--head` 40 lowercase hex, `--branch` over `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`, `--lock-wait` a non-negative
finite number (default 30); every element of argv round-trips through strict UTF-8 and holds no tab, newline or
carriage return before argparse runs (ledger-row.py's argument rule). The store is a directory of this user whose
basename is the program, held to regime-init's grammar `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}`; the sqlite is a regular file.

`units.tsv` is read by the one grammar: the header `id track state branch pr head_sha brief note`, tab-separated,
eight cells per row, no carriage return; another shape is a refusal naming the file and the line, and the file, the
`briefs` directory and the brief are reached through real directories alone (each component `os.lstat`ed, no link,
the realpath under the store's). Idempotence: a row whose `brief` cell is `briefs/U<n>-ticket-<id>.md` for this
ticket makes the lever print `state=existing` with that unit and write nothing; that row's id must be its `U<n>` and
its brief a regular file under the store, two such rows or a brief file of that name with no row are refusals (the
store is inconsistent). Otherwise the unit is `U<max+1>` over the rows whose id is `U[0-9]+` (`U1` when none), the
brief is written with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` (mode 0600) and the row is appended, both under one exclusive
`fcntl.flock` on the `units.tsv` descriptor in ledger-row.py's form: one `os.open(O_RDWR | O_APPEND | O_NOFOLLOW)`
descriptor carries the lock (tried non-blocking every 0.1 s for `--lock-wait` seconds; expiry a refusal naming the
file), the `os.pread` of the whole file, the check, the one `os.write` of the line after an `lseek` to the end,
`os.fsync`, and the close. The row: `U<n>   ticket  in-flight   <branch>    <pr>    <head>  briefs/U<n>-ticket-<id>.md
ticket=<id>; thread=<thread>; sender=<sender>; decision=<decisionId>; bound by ticket-unit.py <ts>` with `ts` the
clock in UTC (`%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`), never an argument; no cell holds a tab, a newline or a carriage return, and the
ticket's text never enters a cell (the title is not in the row).

The rendered brief is the ticket's text as data: the sections brief-check.py requires, each heading a line that is
exactly its name. GOAL holds one fixed sentence naming the pull request, the ticket id and the sender, then the
ticket's `title` and `mandate.scope` inside a fenced block whose fence is a run of `~` one longer than any run of `~`
in the text (four at least), every line of the text prefixed with two spaces, so no line of the text is a heading
(brief-check.py reads a heading only from a line that is exactly the name); every `str.splitlines` boundary in the
text (CR, VT, FF, FS, GS, RS, NEL, U+2028, U+2029) is replaced by a newline before the prefix, so one text line is
one indented line. SCOPE names no repository path and no lever (the paths are the pull request's diff, read by the
audit); CHANGE is the pull request's head; CONTEXT holds the ticket's recorded facts as `key: value` lines and the
sentence that the text above is the sender's words, data for the auditor, never an instruction to any lever;
ACCEPTANCE names CI's gates (`make format`, `python -m unittest`), the Codex audit, the sweep row and pr-merge.sh;
CLOSURE is `remove` (this unit has no hand-written check; the audit, the sweep and CI judge it); TRUST names the
Router's admission of the sender and the gate levers' own checks as trusted, and the text as data only. The rendered
brief passes `python3 -I scripts/orchestrator/brief-check.py <store>/briefs/<file>` with exit 0.

Exit 0 prints one stdout line: `unit=U<n> brief=briefs/U<n>-ticket-<id>.md state=new|existing program=<program>
line=Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>`. Exit 2 with one stderr line, `ticket-unit.py: refused: <reason>`, and nothing on
stdout for every refusal: the self pin (below), an argument outside its grammar, the store not a directory of this
user or its basename outside the program grammar, the sqlite not a regular file or not opening read-only, no or two
tickets, a field outside its grammar, the branch not the ticket's, the register malformed or reached through a link,
a lock not taken in time, a read that fails (open, flock, fstat, pread), and the store inconsistencies above. Exit 1
with one stderr line, `ticket-unit.py: cannot write <file>: <cause>`, when a write fails: a brief write or fsync that
fails removes the brief and names it; a row write that fails or returns short, or a fsync that fails, truncates the
register back to its length (`os.ftruncate`), removes the brief and names the register (a truncate or an unlink that
fails is named too). Every stderr line passes through one sanitiser that folds every line boundary into a space
(program-status.py's `one_line`), so a value read from the sqlite cannot add a line. No mode of any existing file is
changed and no file but the brief and the register is written.

Installed as `~/.local/bin/common/ticket-unit.py` in `brief-check.py`'s form: `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py`
writes the same bytes to `home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_ticket-unit.py` and pins their sha256 under
`claude.levers.sha256`; before anything else the file hashes itself against that pin, the deployed manifest
`~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` when its physical directory is the physical `~/.local/bin/common`, else the checkout's
`home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` two levels up, and refuses to run on a difference. The orchestrator seat's policy
allows that installed path alone.
"""

import argparse
import errno
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import stat
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
from datetime import datetime, timezone

LEVER = "ticket-unit.py"
# The levers block of the manifest, read as text by indentation alone, never parsed as YAML (brief-check.py, U136).
MAPPING_KEY = re.compile(r"^(\S+):$")
LEVER_PIN = re.compile(r"^(\S+): ([0-9a-f]{64})$")
LEVERS_KEYS = ("claude", "levers", "sha256")
# The line boundaries `str.splitlines` knows; `one_line` replaces each with a space in every refusal, and the brief
# renderer replaces each with a newline before the indent, so one text line is one indented line.
LINE_BREAK = re.compile(r"[\n\r\x0b\x0c\x1c\x1d\x1e\x85\u2028\u2029]")


def one_line(text):
    """`text` with every line boundary `str.splitlines` knows a space: the one sanitiser of every stderr line, so a
    ticket id, a path or a quoted value that holds one cannot add a line."""
    return LINE_BREAK.sub(" ", text)


def refuse(reason):
    """One stderr line in the levers' words, exit 2; nothing was written."""
    print(f"{LEVER}: refused: {one_line(reason)}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def lever_self_check():
    """Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31).

    The physical directory of this file decides the manifest: the deployed `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` when the
    directory is the physical `~/.local/bin/common`, else the checkout's `home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` two
    levels up; an unset or unresolvable HOME means the checkout manifest. The pin is the block's `ticket-unit.py`
    entry: one entry is the pin, none or two is a refusal. Every read is checked and a failed one is a refusal, never
    a pass (preferences.md standing order 21); the reader is brief-check.py's, spelled the same.
    """
    directory = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    self_path = os.path.join(directory, os.path.basename(__file__))
    home = os.environ.get("HOME", "")
    if home and os.path.isdir(home) and directory == os.path.realpath(os.path.join(home, ".local/bin/common")):
        manifest = os.path.join(home, ".agents/agent-config.yaml")
    else:
        manifest = os.path.join(directory, "../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml")
    if not os.access(manifest, os.R_OK):
        refuse(f"manifest unreadable: {manifest}")
    try:
        with open(manifest, "rb") as handle:
            lines = handle.read().decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()
    except OSError:
        refuse(f"cannot read {manifest}")
    pins = [digest for name, digest in manifest_levers(lines, manifest) if name == LEVER]
    if len(pins) != 1:
        refuse(f"no single sha256 pin for {LEVER} in {manifest}")
    try:
        with open(self_path, "rb") as handle:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(handle.read()).hexdigest()
    except OSError:
        refuse(f"cannot hash {self_path}")
    if digest != pins[0]:
        refuse(f"sha256 {digest} of {self_path} differs from the pin in {manifest}")


def manifest_levers(lines, manifest):
    """The `(name, sha256)` pins under the manifest's `claude.levers.sha256` mapping, in file order (brief-check.py,
    U136): the mapping keys are walked by indentation, so `levers:` counts only under the top-level `claude:` and
    `sha256:` only under that `levers:`; inside the block, blank and comment lines are skipped, the entries share the
    indentation of the first pin, and the list ends at the first line indented less. An entry that is not
    `<name>: <64 hex>` is a refusal naming the line; no entry at all is the missing-block refusal."""
    pins = []
    keys = []  # the open mapping keys as (indentation, key), outermost first
    block = None  # the indentation of the `sha256:` key once the path is open
    entries = None  # the indentation of the pin lines, fixed by the first
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        text = line.lstrip(" ")
        if not text or text.startswith("#"):
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(text)
        if block is not None:
            if indent <= block or (entries is not None and indent < entries):
                break
            match = LEVER_PIN.match(text)
            if match is None or (entries is not None and indent != entries):
                refuse(f"line {number} of {manifest} is not a `<name>: <sha256>` pin under claude.levers.sha256")
            entries = indent
            pins.append((match.group(1), match.group(2)))
            continue
        while keys and indent <= keys[-1][0]:
            keys.pop()
        match = MAPPING_KEY.match(text)
        if match and (keys or indent == 0):
            keys.append((indent, match.group(1)))
            if tuple(key for _, key in keys) == LEVERS_KEYS:
                block = indent
    if not pins:
        refuse(f"no claude.levers.sha256 block in {manifest}")
    return tuple(pins)

# The write's lock is `LOCK_EX` on the register's own descriptor, tried non-blocking every LOCK_POLL seconds for
# LOCK_WAIT seconds (`--lock-wait` sets the wait); advisory, so the readers, which take no lock, are unaffected.
LOCK_WAIT = 30.0
LOCK_POLL = 0.1
# The three characters no cell and no argument holds: the register is tab-separated lines.
CONTROL = (("\t", "a tab"), ("\n", "a newline"), ("\r", "a carriage return"))
# The arguments' grammars (the shell reads nothing: every value is held to a closed class before use).
PR = re.compile(r"[1-9][0-9]{0,8}")
HEAD = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{40}")
BRANCH = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+")
# regime-init's program grammar: the store directory's basename is the program.
PROGRAM = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}")
# The ticket's fields, each a closed class (the title and the scope are text, data; they have no grammar).
HEX32 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{32}")
ACCOUNT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9-]+")
THREAD = re.compile(r"[a-z]+:[0-9]+")
EXECUTION_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+")
CREATED_AT = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]{1,6})?Z")
# The Router's branch for a ticket: `agent/` and the execution name.
BRANCH_PREFIX = "agent/"
# The Router's thread name for a pull request.
THREAD_PREFIX = "github:"
# The register's one grammar (brief-check.py, program-status.py): the header, eight cells, the plain unit id.
UNITS_FILE = "units.tsv"
UNITS_HEADER = ("id", "track", "state", "branch", "pr", "head_sha", "brief", "note")
UNIT_ID = re.compile(r"U([0-9]+)")
BRIEFS_DIR = "briefs"
TRACK = "ticket"
STATE = "in-flight"
TS_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
# The fence is a run of `~` one longer than the text's longest, four at least (a fenced block opens with three).
FENCE_CHARACTER = "~"
FENCE_MINIMUM = 4
TILDE_RUN = re.compile(r"~+")
INDENT = "  "


def argument_rule(argv):
    """The one rule every element of argv passes before argparse runs (ledger-row.py rounds 3 and 4): the element
    round-trips through strict UTF-8 (Python decodes argv with surrogateescape, so a byte that is not UTF-8 arrives
    as a lone surrogate that would fail only at the write) and holds neither a tab, a newline nor a carriage return
    (a check of the parsed strings alone would let `--lock-wait`, which argparse converts to a float, escape it).
    The refusal names the element's position and the option before it, or the store for the positional element."""
    positional = 0
    for index, value in enumerate(argv):
        if value.startswith("--"):
            where = f"argument {index + 1} (the option {value.split('=', 1)[0]!r})"
        elif index and argv[index - 1].startswith("--"):
            where = f"argument {index + 1} (the value of {argv[index - 1]})"
        else:
            positional += 1
            where = f"argument {index + 1}" + (" (the store)" if positional == 1 else "")
        try:
            value.encode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeEncodeError as error:
            refuse(f"{where} holds a byte that is not UTF-8 at offset {error.start}: {value!r}")
        for character, label in CONTROL:
            if character in value:
                refuse(f"{where} holds {label}; a cell holds neither a tab nor a newline")


def parser():
    top = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=LEVER, description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    top.add_argument("store", help="the program store directory; its basename is the program")
    top.add_argument("--db", required=True, help="the Router's orchestrator.sqlite, opened read-only")
    top.add_argument("--pr", required=True, help="the pull request number the ticket's `follows` names, 1 to 9 digits")
    top.add_argument("--branch", required=True, help="the pull request's branch, agent/<execution.name>")
    top.add_argument("--head", required=True, help="the pull request's head, 40 lowercase hex")
    top.add_argument(
        "--lock-wait",
        default=str(LOCK_WAIT),
        help=f"seconds to wait for the register's lock (default {LOCK_WAIT:g})",
    )
    return top


def check_arguments(args):
    try:
        args.lock_wait = float(args.lock_wait)
    except ValueError:
        refuse(f"--lock-wait {args.lock_wait!r} is not a non-negative number of seconds")
    if not 0 <= args.lock_wait < math.inf:
        refuse(f"--lock-wait {args.lock_wait!r} is not a non-negative number of seconds")
    if PR.fullmatch(args.pr) is None:
        refuse(f"--pr {args.pr!r} is not 1 to 9 digits without a leading zero")
    if HEAD.fullmatch(args.head) is None:
        refuse(f"--head {args.head!r} is not 40 lowercase hex")
    if BRANCH.fullmatch(args.branch) is None:
        refuse(f"--branch {args.branch!r} is not over [A-Za-z0-9._/-]")


def store_dir(argument):
    """The store's realpath and the program, its basename: a directory owned by this user, the basename in the
    program grammar; any other outcome is a refusal naming the store."""
    store = os.path.realpath(argument)
    try:
        status = os.lstat(store)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"the store {store} cannot be read: {error.strerror}")
    if not stat.S_ISDIR(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"the store {store} is not a directory")
    if status.st_uid != os.getuid():
        refuse(f"the store {store} is not a directory of this user (owner uid {status.st_uid}, not {os.getuid()})")
    program = os.path.basename(store)
    if PROGRAM.fullmatch(program) is None:
        refuse(f"the store's basename {program!r} is not a program name ([a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{{0,63}})")
    return store, program


def store_path(store, relative, label):
    """`<store>/<relative>` by the one path rule every file under the store follows (ledger-row.py round 2): `store`
    is already its own realpath; each component below it is `os.lstat`ed and none is a link (a symlinked parent out
    of the store is named by its component); the realpath lies under the store. Returns (path, lstat result or None
    when the last component does not exist); any other failure is a refusal naming the path."""
    current = store
    parts = relative.split("/")
    status = None
    for index, part in enumerate(parts):
        current = os.path.join(current, part)
        try:
            status = os.lstat(current)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            if index == len(parts) - 1:
                return current, None
            refuse(f"the {label}'s directory {current} does not exist under the store")
        except OSError as error:
            refuse(f"the {label} {current} cannot be read: {error.strerror}")
        if stat.S_ISLNK(status.st_mode):
            refuse(
                f"the {label}'s component {current} is a symbolic link; a file under the store is reached through "
                "real directories alone"
            )
        if index < len(parts) - 1 and not stat.S_ISDIR(status.st_mode):
            refuse(f"the {label}'s directory {current} is not a directory")
    if not os.path.realpath(current).startswith(store + os.sep):
        refuse(f"the {label} {current} resolves outside the store {store}")
    return current, status


def store_file(store, relative, label):
    """The regular file `<store>/<relative>` by `store_path`, else a refusal naming it."""
    current, status = store_path(store, relative, label)
    if status is None:
        refuse(f"the {label} {current} is not a regular file under the store: No such file or directory")
    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"the {label} {current} is not a regular file under the store")
    return current


def read_tickets(argument):
    """Every `(id, value)` of the sqlite's `ticket` table, read over the read-only URI; the file must be a regular
    file and every sqlite error is a refusal naming it."""
    db = os.path.realpath(argument)
    try:
        status = os.stat(db)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"the sqlite {db} cannot be read: {error.strerror}")
    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"the sqlite {db} is not a regular file")
    uri = "file:" + urllib.parse.quote(db) + "?mode=ro"
    try:
        connection = sqlite3.connect(uri, uri=True)
    except sqlite3.Error as error:
        refuse(f"the sqlite {db} does not open read-only: {error}")
    try:
        rows = connection.execute("SELECT id, value FROM ticket ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    except sqlite3.Error as error:
        refuse(f"the sqlite {db} cannot be read: {error}")
    finally:
        connection.close()
    return rows


def document_of(ticket_id, value):
    """The ticket's JSON object, through the json module alone; anything else is a refusal naming the ticket."""
    try:
        document = json.loads(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as error:
        refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: the value is not JSON: {error}")
    if not isinstance(document, dict):
        refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: the value is not a JSON object")
    return document


def follows_pr(ticket_id, document, thread):
    """Whether the ticket's `follows` holds an entry with this thread and `own` true; a `follows` that is not a list
    of objects is a refusal naming the ticket (standing order 21: a shape the reader cannot judge is no pass)."""
    follows = document.get("follows")
    if follows is None:
        return False
    if not isinstance(follows, list):
        refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: `follows` is not a list")
    found = False
    for entry in follows:
        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
            refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: a `follows` entry is not an object")
        if entry.get("thread") == thread and entry.get("own") is True:
            found = True
    return found


def binding_ticket(rows, pr):
    """The one `(id, document)` whose `follows` names `github:<pr>` with `own` true; none or two is a refusal naming
    the count."""
    thread = f"{THREAD_PREFIX}{pr}"
    matches = []
    for ticket_id, value in rows:
        document = document_of(ticket_id, value)
        if follows_pr(ticket_id, document, thread):
            matches.append((ticket_id, document))
    if not matches:
        refuse(f"no ticket follows {thread} with own true (0 of {len(rows)} tickets)")
    if len(matches) > 1:
        names = ", ".join(str(ticket_id) for ticket_id, _ in matches)
        refuse(f"{len(matches)} tickets follow {thread} with own true, not one: {names}")
    return matches[0]


def field(ticket_id, document, *keys):
    """The value at `keys` in the document, each step an object (a list index as an int); a missing step is a
    refusal naming the field."""
    value = document
    for key in keys:
        if isinstance(key, int):
            if not isinstance(value, list) or len(value) <= key:
                refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: {field_name(keys)} is missing")
        elif not isinstance(value, dict) or key not in value:
            refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: {field_name(keys)} is missing")
        value = value[key]
    return value


def field_name(keys):
    name = ""
    for key in keys:
        name += f"[{key}]" if isinstance(key, int) else (f".{key}" if name else key)
    return name


def text_field(ticket_id, document, *keys):
    value = field(ticket_id, document, *keys)
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: {field_name(keys)} is not text")
    return value


def held_field(ticket_id, document, grammar, grammar_text, *keys):
    value = text_field(ticket_id, document, *keys)
    if grammar.fullmatch(value) is None:
        refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: {field_name(keys)} {value!r} is not {grammar_text}")
    return value


def ticket_facts(ticket_id, document):
    """The ticket's fields the lever uses, each held to its grammar before use, as a dict; the title and the scope
    are text, data, and have none."""
    if not isinstance(ticket_id, str) or HEX32.fullmatch(ticket_id) is None:
        refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: the row's id is not 32 lowercase hex")
    facts = {
        "id": held_field(ticket_id, document, HEX32, "32 lowercase hex", "id"),
        "title": text_field(ticket_id, document, "title"),
        "scope": text_field(ticket_id, document, "mandate", "scope"),
        "sender": held_field(ticket_id, document, ACCOUNT, "over [A-Za-z0-9-]", "mandate", "basis", "sender"),
        "actor": held_field(ticket_id, document, ACCOUNT, "over [A-Za-z0-9-]", "mandate", "actor", "id"),
        "thread": held_field(ticket_id, document, THREAD, "<source>:<number>", "channels", 0, "thread"),
        "name": held_field(ticket_id, document, EXECUTION_NAME, "over [A-Za-z0-9._-]", "execution", "name"),
        "decision": held_field(ticket_id, document, HEX32, "32 lowercase hex", "decisionId"),
        "createdAt": held_field(ticket_id, document, CREATED_AT, "<YYYY-MM-DD>T<HH:MM:SS>Z", "createdAt"),
    }
    if facts["id"] != ticket_id:
        refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: the document's id {facts['id']!r} is not the row's")
    try:
        datetime.fromisoformat(facts["createdAt"])
    except ValueError as error:
        refuse(f"ticket {ticket_id!r}: createdAt {facts['createdAt']!r} is not a timestamp: {error}")
    return facts


def as_data(text):
    """The text's lines by `str.splitlines`, each prefixed with the indent: one text line is one indented line, and
    no line is exactly a section name."""
    return "\n".join(INDENT + line for line in text.splitlines() or [""])


def fence_for(*texts):
    longest = max((len(run) for text in texts for run in TILDE_RUN.findall(text)), default=0)
    return FENCE_CHARACTER * max(FENCE_MINIMUM, longest + 1)
