def open_register(units_path, wait):
    """The register's own descriptor, `O_RDWR | O_APPEND | O_NOFOLLOW`, locked `LOCK_EX` (ledger-row.py round 4):
    the one descriptor the lock, the read and the write go through, released by its close. The lock is tried
    non-blocking every LOCK_POLL seconds for `wait` seconds; a lock not taken by then is a refusal naming the file."""
    try:
        descriptor = os.open(units_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_APPEND | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot open the register {units_path} for the write: {error.strerror}")
    deadline = time.monotonic() + wait
    while True:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
            return descriptor
        except OSError as error:
            if error.errno not in (errno.EAGAIN, errno.EWOULDBLOCK):
                refuse(f"cannot lock the register {units_path}: {error.strerror}")
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                refuse(
                    f"the register {units_path} is held by another writer after {wait:g} second"
                    f"{'' if wait == 1 else 's'}; nothing is written (--lock-wait sets the wait)"
                )
            time.sleep(LOCK_POLL)


def read_register(descriptor, units_path):
    """The whole text through the locked descriptor: `os.fstat` for the length n0, `os.pread` from offset 0 looped
    until n0 bytes, decoded as strict UTF-8. Every failure is a refusal naming the register. Returns (n0, text)."""
    try:
        status = os.fstat(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot read the register {units_path}: fstat: {error.strerror}")
    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"the register {units_path} is not a regular file")
    length = status.st_size
    chunks = []
    offset = 0
    while offset < length:
        try:
            chunk = os.pread(descriptor, length - offset, offset)
        except OSError as error:
            refuse(f"cannot read the register {units_path}: pread at offset {offset}: {error.strerror}")
        if not chunk:
            refuse(f"the register {units_path} holds {offset} bytes, fewer than its length {length} under the lock")
        chunks.append(chunk)
        offset += len(chunk)
    try:
        return length, b"".join(chunks).decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
        refuse(f"{units_path}: not UTF-8: {error.reason}")


def parse_register(units_path, text):
    """The rows of the register by the one grammar: line 1 the header, every other line eight cells, no carriage
    return; a last line without a newline is a row too. Returns [(line number, cells)]."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    if lines and lines[-1] == "":
        lines.pop()
    if not lines:
        refuse(f"{units_path}:1 is not the header ({' '.join(UNITS_HEADER)}); the file is empty")
    rows = []
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if "\r" in line:
            refuse(f"{units_path}:{number} holds a carriage return")
        if number == 1:
            if line != "\t".join(UNITS_HEADER):
                refuse(f"{units_path}:1 is not the header ({' '.join(UNITS_HEADER)})")
            continue
        cells = line.split("\t")
        if len(cells) != len(UNITS_HEADER):
            refuse(f"{units_path}:{number} has {len(cells)} cells, not {len(UNITS_HEADER)}")
        rows.append((number, cells))
    return rows


def existing_unit(store, units_path, rows, ticket_id):
    """The unit whose row's brief cell is this ticket's brief, after the store's consistency checks, or None."""
    pattern = re.compile(re.escape(f"{BRIEFS_DIR}/U") + r"([0-9]+)" + re.escape(f"-ticket-{ticket_id}.md"))
    found = [(number, cells, match) for number, cells in rows if (match := pattern.fullmatch(cells[6]))]
    if not found:
        return None
    if len(found) > 1:
        lines = ", ".join(str(number) for number, _, _ in found)
        refuse(f"{len(found)} rows of {units_path} (lines {lines}) name {found[0][1][6]}; the store is inconsistent")
    number, cells, match = found[0]
    unit = f"U{match.group(1)}"
    if cells[0] != unit:
        refuse(f"{units_path}:{number} has id {cells[0]!r} but its brief cell {cells[6]} names {unit}; inconsistent")
    store_file(store, cells[6], "brief")
    return unit


def next_unit(rows):
    numbers = [int(match.group(1)) for _, cells in rows if (match := UNIT_ID.fullmatch(cells[0]))]
    return f"U{max(numbers, default=0) + 1}"


def cell_check(name, value):
    """A cell holds neither a tab nor a line break: the register is tab-separated lines."""
    for character, label in CONTROL:
        if character in value:
            refuse(f"the {name} holds {label}; a cell holds neither a tab nor a newline")


def write_brief(brief_path, text):
    """The brief created `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` at mode 0600, written whole and synced. Returns None, or
    the failure text naming the brief after the partial file is removed (exit 1 is the caller's)."""
    try:
        descriptor = os.open(brief_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
    except FileExistsError:
        refuse(f"the brief {brief_path} exists but no row of the register names it; the store is inconsistent")
    except OSError as error:
        return f"cannot write {brief_path}: open: {error.strerror}"
    data = text.encode("utf-8")
    failure = None
    try:
        offset = 0
        while offset < len(data):
            written = os.write(descriptor, data[offset:])
            if written <= 0:
                raise OSError(errno.EIO, "short write")
            offset += written
        os.fsync(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        failure = f"cannot write {brief_path}: {error.strerror}"
    try:
        os.close(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        failure = failure or f"cannot write {brief_path}: close: {error.strerror}"
    if failure is not None:
        return remove_brief(brief_path, failure)
    return None


def remove_brief(brief_path, failure):
    try:
        os.unlink(brief_path)
    except OSError as error:
        return f"{failure}; the brief {brief_path} could not be removed: {error.strerror}"
    return f"{failure}; the brief is removed"


def append_line(descriptor, units_path, length, line):
    """One `os.write` of the line's bytes after an `lseek` to the end (O_APPEND puts it there whatever the offset;
    XNU applies RLIMIT_FSIZE at the descriptor's offset, so the seat makes a size limit cut the write on both
    kernels), its count compared with the line's length, then `os.fsync`. A failure truncates the file back to
    `length`. Returns None, or the failure text naming the register."""
    data = line.encode("utf-8")
    try:
        os.lseek(descriptor, 0, os.SEEK_END)
        written = os.write(descriptor, data)
    except OSError as error:
        return truncate_back(descriptor, units_path, length, f"write: {error.strerror}")
    if written != len(data):
        return truncate_back(descriptor, units_path, length, f"short write, {written} of {len(data)} bytes")
    try:
        os.fsync(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        return truncate_back(descriptor, units_path, length, f"fsync: {error.strerror}")
    return None


def truncate_back(descriptor, units_path, length, cause):
    try:
        os.ftruncate(descriptor, length)
    except OSError as error:
        return (
            f"cannot write {units_path}: {cause}; the register {units_path} may hold a partial last line: "
            f"{error.strerror}"
        )
    return f"cannot write {units_path}: {cause}; truncated back to {length} bytes"


def now():
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime(TS_FORMAT)


def bind(args, store, program, facts, units_path, descriptor):
    """The critical section, under the lock the descriptor holds: the register read and parsed, the existing unit
    answered, else the brief written and the row appended. Returns (0, the stdout line) or (1, the failure text)."""
    length, text = read_register(descriptor, units_path)
    rows = parse_register(units_path, text)
    unit = existing_unit(store, units_path, rows, facts["id"])
    state = "existing"
    if unit is None:
        state = "new"
        unit = next_unit(rows)
        relative = f"{BRIEFS_DIR}/{unit}-ticket-{facts['id']}.md"
        brief_path, status = store_path(store, relative, "brief")
        if status is not None:
            refuse(f"the brief {relative} exists but no row of the register names it; the store is inconsistent")
        cells = (
            unit,
            TRACK,
            STATE,
            args.branch,
            args.pr,
            args.head,
            relative,
            f"ticket={facts['id']}; thread={facts['thread']}; sender={facts['sender']}; decision={facts['decision']}; "
            f"bound by {LEVER} {now()}",
        )
        for name, value in zip(UNITS_HEADER, cells):
            cell_check(f"{name} cell", value)
        line = "\t".join(cells) + "\n"
        lead = "" if text == "" or text.endswith("\n") else "\n"
        failure = write_brief(brief_path, render_brief(unit, facts, args.pr, args.head, program))
        if failure is not None:
            return 1, failure
        failure = append_line(descriptor, units_path, length, lead + line)
        if failure is not None:
            return 1, remove_brief(brief_path, failure)
    else:
        relative = f"{BRIEFS_DIR}/{unit}-ticket-{facts['id']}.md"
    return 0, f"unit={unit} brief={relative} state={state} program={program} line=Program-Unit: {program}/{unit}"


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    argument_rule(argv)
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    check_arguments(args)
    store, program = store_dir(args.store)
    ticket_id, document = binding_ticket(read_tickets(args.db), args.pr)
    facts = ticket_facts(ticket_id, document)
    expected = f"{BRANCH_PREFIX}{facts['name']}"
    if args.branch != expected:
        refuse(f"the branch {args.branch!r} is not the ticket's {expected}")
    units_path = store_file(store, UNITS_FILE, "register")
    descriptor = open_register(units_path, args.lock_wait)
    try:
        code, text = bind(args, store, program, facts, units_path, descriptor)
    except BaseException:  # a refusal (SystemExit) or an unexpected error: the close releases the lock
        try:
            os.close(descriptor)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise
    try:
        os.close(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        if code == 0:
            text = f"the register {units_path} was appended ({text}) but its close failed: {error.strerror}"
        else:
            text = f"{text}; the close failed too: {error.strerror}"
        code = 1
    if code == 0:
        print(text)
    else:
        print(f"{LEVER}: {one_line(text)}", file=sys.stderr)
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
</code></pre>

<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -I
"""Write one `units.tsv` row of the program store by the readers' grammar, in place under its lock (regime-cutover U505).

On 2026-11-13T00:29Z a coordinator cell opened the live register with mode `w` and raised mid-write, leaving a
7203-byte file of 659 rows that only the kernel's memory restored (decisions.tsv lesson row 2026-11-13T00:29:54Z).
This lever is `ledger-row.py`'s form for the other register: the coordinator adds or changes one row through it and
never opens `units.tsv` from a Python cell again.

The register is one table: the header exactly `id track state branch pr head_sha brief note`, tab-separated, eight
cells per row, LF line ends, no carriage return anywhere (the readers: brief-check.py `taken_unit_id`, pr-merge.sh
`unit_row_exists`, program-status.py, ticket-unit.py). A register of another shape is exit 2 naming the file and the
line, and nothing is written. The lever holds every cell it writes to a closed class before the write: `id`
`U<digits>[a-z]*`; `track` and `state` `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*` (a character class, not a word list: the live register
holds 30 tracks and 15 states the coordinator named over a month, and the hcom-orchestration SKILL's state list is
stale, a docs finding this unit records and does not fix); `branch` empty or over `[A-Za-z0-9._/-]`; `pr` empty or
`[1-9][0-9]{0,8}`; `head_sha` empty or 40 lowercase hex; `brief` empty or `briefs/<id>-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+.md` with
`<id>` this row's id; `note` any text without a tab or a line boundary `str.splitlines` knows (the readers split the
file with it, so a U+2028 in a note would split the row). The cells a `set` leaves alone are kept as they are: the
live register holds 8-hex heads and brief cells from before the store move, which the readers accept and this lever
does not re-judge. Every element of argv round-trips through strict UTF-8 and holds no tab, newline or carriage
return before argparse runs (ledger-row.py's argument rule).

`units-row.py <store> add --id U<n>[a-z]* --track <t> --state <s> [--branch <b>] [--pr <n>] [--head <sha>]
[--brief <path>] --note <text> [--lock-wait <seconds>]` appends the row; a row with that id exists is a refusal
naming its line (the U436 class, a duplicated id), unless that row is byte-equal to the one asked for, which prints
`unchanged <id>` and writes nothing. `units-row.py <store> set --id U<n>[a-z]* [--track <t>] [--state <s>]
[--branch <b>] [--pr <n>] [--head <sha>] [--brief <path>] [--note-append <text>] [--lock-wait <seconds>]` replaces
each named cell of the one row with that id (none or two rows is a refusal naming the count and the lines; no option
after `--id` is a refusal, nothing to set); `--note-append` appends `; <text>` to the note, or sets it when the note
is empty. Idempotence: a `set` whose every named value already equals the cell's, `--note-append` counting as equal
when the note is the text or already ends with `; <text>`, prints `unchanged <id>` and writes nothing, so the second
run of one command is a no-op.

The write is ledger-row.py round 4's form with the in-place rewrite `set` needs. One `os.open(units, O_RDWR |
O_NOFOLLOW)` descriptor carries `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`, tried every 0.1 s for `--lock-wait` seconds
(default 30; expiry a refusal naming the file), the `os.fstat` for the length n0 and the owner (this user, a regular
file), the `os.pread` of the whole text from 0 until n0 bytes, the parse by the one grammar, the new text composed
and parsed again before anything is written, then for `add` one `os.pwrite` of the line at n0, for `set` one
`os.pwrite` of the whole new text at 0 followed by `os.ftruncate` to its length when shorter, then `os.fsync`, and
the close, which releases the lock. A write that fails or returns short, or a fsync that fails, restores the old
text (`os.pwrite` of the old bytes at 0 until all are written, `os.ftruncate` to n0, `os.fsync`) and is exit 1
naming the file and the error; a restore that fails is named too (`the register <path> may hold a torn text`). Why
in place and not a temporary file renamed over the register: ticket-unit.py and ledger-row.py lock the register's own
descriptor, and a replaced inode would leave a concurrent appender writing to the old file; the store's own walks
(records-sync.sh, regime-store-move) refuse a name beginning with `.`, and a sync may list the store at any moment.
The lock is advisory and the readers take none; a reader that meets a torn line fails closed (program-status.py
refused a torn last line on 2026-11-12, by design). No file but the register is written and no mode is changed.

Exit 0 prints one stdout line: `added <id> line <n>`, `set <id> line <n> cells=<comma list of the cells changed, in
the header's order>`, or `unchanged <id>`. Exit 2 with one stderr line, `units-row.py: refused: <reason>`, and
nothing on stdout for every refusal: the self pin (below), an argument outside its class, an unknown subcommand or
option (argparse's usage block is folded into the one line), the store not a directory of this user, the register
not a regular file of this user or reached through a symbolic link, the register malformed, a lock not taken in
time, and a read that fails (open, flock, fstat, pread). Exit 1 with one stderr line, `units-row.py: cannot write
<file>: <cause>`, when the write, the fsync or the close fails. Every stderr line passes through one sanitiser that
folds every line boundary `str.splitlines` knows into a space (ticket-unit.py's `one_line`), so a quoted value
cannot add a line.

Installed as `~/.local/bin/common/units-row.py` in `brief-check.py`'s form: `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py`
writes the same bytes to `home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_units-row.py` and pins their sha256 under
`claude.levers.sha256`; before anything else the file hashes itself against that pin, the deployed manifest
`~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` when its physical directory is the physical `~/.local/bin/common`, else the checkout's
`home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` two levels up, and refuses to run on a difference. The orchestrator seat's policy
allows that installed path alone; the worker and audit policies deny the lever by name (standing order 27: the store
has one writer). The lever runs no `gh`, no git and no network.
"""

import argparse
import errno
import fcntl
import hashlib
import math
import os
import re
import stat
import sys
import time

LEVER = "units-row.py"
# The levers block of the manifest, read as text by indentation alone, never parsed as YAML (brief-check.py, U136).
MAPPING_KEY = re.compile(r"^(\S+):$")
LEVER_PIN = re.compile(r"^(\S+): ([0-9a-f]{64})$")
LEVERS_KEYS = ("claude", "levers", "sha256")
# The line boundaries `str.splitlines` knows; `one_line` replaces each with a space in every refusal, and no cell
# holds one (the readers split the register with `splitlines`).
LINE_BREAK = re.compile(r"[\n\r\x0b\x0c\x1c\x1d\x1e\x85\u2028\u2029]")


def one_line(text):
    """`text` with every line boundary `str.splitlines` knows a space: the one sanitiser of every stderr line, so a
    path or a quoted value that holds one cannot add a line."""
    return LINE_BREAK.sub(" ", text)


def refuse(reason):
    """One stderr line in the levers' words, exit 2; nothing was written."""
    print(f"{LEVER}: refused: {one_line(reason)}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def lever_self_check():
    """Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31).

    The physical directory of this file decides the manifest: the deployed `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` when the
    directory is the physical `~/.local/bin/common`, else the checkout's `home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml` two
    levels up; an unset or unresolvable HOME means the checkout manifest. The pin is the block's `units-row.py`
    entry: one entry is the pin, none or two is a refusal. Every read is checked and a failed one is a refusal, never
    a pass (preferences.md standing order 21); the reader is brief-check.py's, spelled the same.
    """
    directory = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    self_path = os.path.join(directory, os.path.basename(__file__))
    home = os.environ.get("HOME", "")
    if home and os.path.isdir(home) and directory == os.path.realpath(os.path.join(home, ".local/bin/common")):
        manifest = os.path.join(home, ".agents/agent-config.yaml")
    else:
        manifest = os.path.join(directory, "../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml")
    if not os.access(manifest, os.R_OK):
        refuse(f"manifest unreadable: {manifest}")
    try:
        with open(manifest, "rb") as handle:
            lines = handle.read().decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines()
    except OSError:
        refuse(f"cannot read {manifest}")
    pins = [digest for name, digest in manifest_levers(lines, manifest) if name == LEVER]
    if len(pins) != 1:
        refuse(f"no single sha256 pin for {LEVER} in {manifest}")
    try:
        with open(self_path, "rb") as handle:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(handle.read()).hexdigest()
    except OSError:
        refuse(f"cannot hash {self_path}")
    if digest != pins[0]:
        refuse(f"sha256 {digest} of {self_path} differs from the pin in {manifest}")


def manifest_levers(lines, manifest):
    """The `(name, sha256)` pins under the manifest's `claude.levers.sha256` mapping, in file order (brief-check.py,
    U136): the mapping keys are walked by indentation, so `levers:` counts only under the top-level `claude:` and
    `sha256:` only under that `levers:`; inside the block, blank and comment lines are skipped, the entries share the
    indentation of the first pin, and the list ends at the first line indented less. An entry that is not
    `<name>: <64 hex>` is a refusal naming the line; no entry at all is the missing-block refusal."""
    pins = []
    keys = []  # the open mapping keys as (indentation, key), outermost first
    block = None  # the indentation of the `sha256:` key once the path is open
    entries = None  # the indentation of the pin lines, fixed by the first
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        text = line.lstrip(" ")
        if not text or text.startswith("#"):
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(text)
        if block is not None:
            if indent <= block or (entries is not None and indent < entries):
                break
            match = LEVER_PIN.match(text)
            if match is None or (entries is not None and indent != entries):
                refuse(f"line {number} of {manifest} is not a `<name>: <sha256>` pin under claude.levers.sha256")
            entries = indent
            pins.append((match.group(1), match.group(2)))
            continue
        while keys and indent <= keys[-1][0]:
            keys.pop()
        match = MAPPING_KEY.match(text)
        if match and (keys or indent == 0):
            keys.append((indent, match.group(1)))
            if tuple(key for _, key in keys) == LEVERS_KEYS:
                block = indent
    if not pins:
        refuse(f"no claude.levers.sha256 block in {manifest}")
    return tuple(pins)


lever_self_check()

# The write's lock is `LOCK_EX` on the register's own descriptor, tried non-blocking every LOCK_POLL seconds for
# LOCK_WAIT seconds (`--lock-wait` sets the wait); advisory, so the readers, which take no lock, are unaffected.
LOCK_WAIT = 30.0
LOCK_POLL = 0.1
# The three characters no argument holds: the register is tab-separated lines (the cells refuse every line boundary).
CONTROL = (("\t", "a tab"), ("\n", "a newline"), ("\r", "a carriage return"))
# The register's one grammar (brief-check.py, pr-merge.sh, program-status.py, ticket-unit.py): the header, eight cells.
UNITS_FILE = "units.tsv"
UNITS_HEADER = ("id", "track", "state", "branch", "pr", "head_sha", "brief", "note")
# The closed class of each cell this lever writes (the module docstring); a `None` class is the note's rule alone.
UNIT_ID = re.compile(r"U[0-9]+[a-z]*")
WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z][a-z0-9-]*")
BRANCH = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+")
PR = re.compile(r"[1-9][0-9]{0,8}")
HEAD = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{40}")
BRIEF = re.compile(r"briefs/(U[0-9]+[a-z]*)-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.md")
CELL_CLASSES = {
    "id": (UNIT_ID, False, "U<digits>[a-z]*"),
    "track": (WORD, False, "[a-z][a-z0-9-]*"),
    "state": (WORD, False, "[a-z][a-z0-9-]*"),
    "branch": (BRANCH, True, "empty or over [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"),
    "pr": (PR, True, "empty or 1 to 9 digits without a leading zero"),
    "head_sha": (HEAD, True, "empty or 40 lowercase hex"),
    "brief": (BRIEF, True, "empty or briefs/<this row's id>-<[A-Za-z0-9._-]+>.md"),
    "note": (None, True, "text without a tab or a line boundary"),
}
# The option of each cell a subcommand may name; `note` is `--note` on add and `--note-append` on set.
CELL_OPTIONS = {
    "track": "--track",
    "state": "--state",
    "branch": "--branch",
    "pr": "--pr",
    "head_sha": "--head",
    "brief": "--brief",
}
NOTE_SEPARATOR = "; "


def argument_rule(argv):
    """The one rule every element of argv passes before argparse runs (ledger-row.py rounds 3 and 4): the element
    round-trips through strict UTF-8 (Python decodes argv with surrogateescape, so a byte that is not UTF-8 arrives
    as a lone surrogate that would fail only at the write) and holds neither a tab, a newline nor a carriage return
    (a check of the parsed strings alone would let `--lock-wait`, which argparse converts to a float, escape it).
    The refusal names the element's position and the option before it, or the store for the positional element."""
    positional = 0
    for index, value in enumerate(argv):
        if value.startswith("--"):
            where = f"argument {index + 1} (the option {value.split('=', 1)[0]!r})"
        elif index and argv[index - 1].startswith("--"):
            where = f"argument {index + 1} (the value of {argv[index - 1]})"
        else:
            positional += 1
            where = f"argument {index + 1}" + (" (the store)" if positional == 1 else "")
        try:
            value.encode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeEncodeError as error:
            refuse(f"{where} holds a byte that is not UTF-8 at offset {error.start}: {value!r}")
        for character, label in CONTROL:
            if character in value:
                refuse(f"{where} holds {label}; a cell holds neither a tab nor a newline")


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """argparse with no option abbreviation (`--note` is not `--note-append`) and its errors as one refusal line:
    no usage block, exit 2 through `refuse`."""

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        kwargs["allow_abbrev"] = False
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

    def error(self, message):
        refuse(f"{message} (the form: {LEVER} <store> add|set --id U<n> ...)")


def parser():
    top = Parser(prog=LEVER, description=__doc__.splitlines()[0], add_help=False)
    top.add_argument("store", help="the program store directory")
    kinds = top.add_subparsers(dest="kind", required=True, parser_class=Parser)
    add = kinds.add_parser("add", help="append one row; the id must be new", add_help=False)
    add.add_argument("--id", required=True)
    add.add_argument("--track", required=True)
    add.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    add.add_argument("--branch", default="")
    add.add_argument("--pr", default="")
    add.add_argument("--head", default="")
    add.add_argument("--brief", default="")
    add.add_argument("--note", required=True)
    setter = kinds.add_parser("set", help="replace the named cells of the one row with the id", add_help=False)
    setter.add_argument("--id", required=True)
    for option in ("--track", "--state", "--branch", "--pr", "--head", "--brief", "--note-append"):
        setter.add_argument(option, default=None)
    for sub in (add, setter):
        sub.add_argument(
            "--lock-wait",
            default=str(LOCK_WAIT),
            help=f"seconds to wait for the register's lock (default {LOCK_WAIT:g})",
        )
    return top


def check_lock_wait(args):
    try:
        args.lock_wait = float(args.lock_wait)
    except ValueError:
        refuse(f"--lock-wait {args.lock_wait!r} is not a non-negative number of seconds")
    if not 0 <= args.lock_wait < math.inf:
        refuse(f"--lock-wait {args.lock_wait!r} is not a non-negative number of seconds")


def cell_rule(name, value, unit):
    """`value` in the closed class of the cell `name` (the brief's id equal to `unit`), else a refusal naming the
    cell, the value and the class. Every cell refuses a tab and every line boundary `str.splitlines` knows."""
    if "\t" in value:
        refuse(f"the {name} {value!r} holds a tab; a cell holds neither a tab nor a line boundary")
    if LINE_BREAK.search(value):
        refuse(f"the {name} {value!r} holds a line boundary; a cell holds neither a tab nor a line boundary")
    pattern, may_be_empty, grammar = CELL_CLASSES[name]
    if value == "":
        if may_be_empty:
            return
        refuse(f"the {name} {value!r} is not {grammar}")
    if pattern is None:
        return
    match = pattern.fullmatch(value)
    if match is None:
        refuse(f"the {name} {value!r} is not {grammar}")
    if name == "brief" and match.group(1) != unit:
        refuse(f"the brief {value!r} names the unit {match.group(1)}, not this row's id {unit}")


def store_dir(argument):
    """The store's realpath: a directory owned by this user; any other outcome is a refusal naming the store."""
    store = os.path.realpath(argument)
    try:
        status = os.lstat(store)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"the store {store} cannot be read: {error.strerror}")
    if not stat.S_ISDIR(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"the store {store} is not a directory")
    if status.st_uid != os.getuid():
        refuse(f"the store {store} is not a directory of this user (owner uid {status.st_uid}, not {os.getuid()})")
    return store


def store_path(store, relative, label):
    """`<store>/<relative>` by the one path rule every file under the store follows (ledger-row.py round 2): `store`
    is already its own realpath; each component below it is `os.lstat`ed and none is a link (a symlinked parent out
    of the store is named by its component); the realpath lies under the store. Returns (path, lstat result or None
    when the last component does not exist); any other failure is a refusal naming the path."""
    current = store
    parts = relative.split("/")
    status = None
    for index, part in enumerate(parts):
        current = os.path.join(current, part)
        try:
            status = os.lstat(current)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            if index == len(parts) - 1:
                return current, None
            refuse(f"the {label}'s directory {current} does not exist under the store")
        except OSError as error:
            refuse(f"the {label} {current} cannot be read: {error.strerror}")
        if stat.S_ISLNK(status.st_mode):
            refuse(
                f"the {label}'s component {current} is a symbolic link; a file under the store is reached through "
                "real directories alone"
            )
        if index < len(parts) - 1 and not stat.S_ISDIR(status.st_mode):
            refuse(f"the {label}'s directory {current} is not a directory")
    if not os.path.realpath(current).startswith(store + os.sep):
        refuse(f"the {label} {current} resolves outside the store {store}")
    return current, status


def store_file(store, relative, label):
    """The regular file `<store>/<relative>` of this user by `store_path`, else a refusal naming it."""
    current, status = store_path(store, relative, label)
    if status is None:
        refuse(f"the {label} {current} is not a regular file under the store: No such file or directory")
    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"the {label} {current} is not a regular file under the store")
    if status.st_uid != os.getuid():
        refuse(f"the {label} {current} is not a regular file of this user (owner uid {status.st_uid})")
    return current


def open_register(units_path, wait):
    """The register's own descriptor, `O_RDWR | O_NOFOLLOW` without the append flag (`set` rewrites at offset 0, and
    Linux puts every write of an append-mode descriptor at the end), locked `LOCK_EX` (ledger-row.py round 4): the
    one descriptor the lock, the read and the write go through, released by its close. The lock is tried every
    LOCK_POLL seconds for `wait` seconds; a lock not taken by then is a refusal naming the file."""
    try:
        descriptor = os.open(units_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot open the register {units_path} for the write: {error.strerror}")
    deadline = time.monotonic() + wait
    while True:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
            return descriptor
        except OSError as error:
            if error.errno not in (errno.EAGAIN, errno.EWOULDBLOCK):
                refuse(f"cannot lock the register {units_path}: {error.strerror}")
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                refuse(
                    f"the register {units_path} is held by another writer after {wait:g} second"
                    f"{'' if wait == 1 else 's'}; nothing is written (--lock-wait sets the wait)"
                )
            time.sleep(LOCK_POLL)


def read_register(descriptor, units_path):
    """The whole text through the locked descriptor: `os.fstat` for the length n0 (a regular file of this user),
    `os.pread` from offset 0 looped until n0 bytes, decoded as strict UTF-8. Every failure is a refusal naming the
    register. Returns (n0, the bytes, the text)."""
    try:
        status = os.fstat(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot read the register {units_path}: fstat: {error.strerror}")
    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
        refuse(f"the register {units_path} is not a regular file")
    if status.st_uid != os.getuid():
        refuse(f"the register {units_path} is not a regular file of this user (owner uid {status.st_uid})")
    length = status.st_size
    chunks = []
    offset = 0
    while offset < length:
        try:
            chunk = os.pread(descriptor, length - offset, offset)
        except OSError as error:
            refuse(f"cannot read the register {units_path}: pread at offset {offset}: {error.strerror}")
        if not chunk:
            refuse(f"the register {units_path} holds {offset} bytes, fewer than its length {length} under the lock")
        chunks.append(chunk)
        offset += len(chunk)
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    try:
        return length, data, data.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
        refuse(f"{units_path}: not UTF-8: {error.reason}")


def parse_register(units_path, text):
    """The rows of the register by the one grammar: line 1 the header, every other line eight cells, no carriage
    return; a last line without a newline is a row too. Returns [(line number, cells)]."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    if lines and lines[-1] == "":
        lines.pop()
    if not lines:
        refuse(f"{units_path}:1 is not the header ({' '.join(UNITS_HEADER)}); the file is empty")
    rows = []
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        if "\r" in line:
            refuse(f"{units_path}:{number} holds a carriage return")
        if number == 1:
            if line != "\t".join(UNITS_HEADER):
                refuse(f"{units_path}:1 is not the header ({' '.join(UNITS_HEADER)})")
            continue
        cells = line.split("\t")
        if len(cells) != len(UNITS_HEADER):
            refuse(f"{units_path}:{number} has {len(cells)} cells, not {len(UNITS_HEADER)}")
        rows.append((number, cells))
    return rows


def rows_with_id(rows, unit):
    return [(number, cells) for number, cells in rows if cells[0] == unit]


def added_text(args, units_path, text, rows):
    """`add`: the new text and the stdout line, or (None, `unchanged <id>`) when the byte-equal row exists."""
    cells = (args.id, args.track, args.state, args.branch, args.pr, args.head, args.brief, args.note)
    for name, value in zip(UNITS_HEADER, cells):
        cell_rule(name, value, args.id)
    existing = rows_with_id(rows, args.id)
    if existing:
        number, old = existing[0]
        if len(existing) == 1 and tuple(old) == cells:
            return None, f"unchanged {args.id}"
        lines = ", ".join(str(number) for number, _ in existing)
        refuse(f"a row with the id {args.id} exists: line{'s' if len(existing) > 1 else ''} {lines} of {units_path}")
    lead = "" if text == "" or text.endswith("\n") else "\n"
    line = "\t".join(cells) + "\n"
    number = text.count("\n") + (0 if lead == "" else 1) + 1
    return (lead + line).encode("utf-8"), f"added {args.id} line {number}"


def set_text(args, units_path, text, rows):
    """`set`: the whole new text and the stdout line, or (None, `unchanged <id>`) when every named value equals."""
    cell_rule("id", args.id, args.id)
    named = {name: getattr(args, option.lstrip("-")) for name, option in CELL_OPTIONS.items()}
    named = {name: value for name, value in named.items() if value is not None}
    if args.note_append is not None:
        named["note"] = args.note_append
    if not named:
        refuse(
            f"nothing to set for {args.id}: name at least one of --track --state --branch --pr --head --brief "
            "--note-append"
        )
    for name, value in named.items():
        cell_rule(name, value, args.id)
    found = rows_with_id(rows, args.id)
    if len(found) != 1:
        lines = ", ".join(str(number) for number, _ in found)
        where = f" (lines {lines})" if found else ""
        refuse(f"{len(found)} rows of {units_path} have the id {args.id}{where}; set needs exactly one")
    number, old = found[0]
    new = list(old)
    changed = []
    for index, name in enumerate(UNITS_HEADER):
        if name not in named:
            continue
        value = named[name]
        if name == "note":
            note = old[index]
            if note == value or note.endswith(NOTE_SEPARATOR + value):
                continue
            value = value if note == "" else note + NOTE_SEPARATOR + value
            cell_rule("note", value, args.id)
        if value == old[index]:
            continue
        new[index] = value
        changed.append(name)
    if not changed:
        return None, f"unchanged {args.id}"
    lines = text.split("\n")
    lines[number - 1] = "\t".join(new)
    new_text = "\n".join(lines)
    if not new_text.endswith("\n"):
        new_text += "\n"
    return new_text.encode("utf-8"), f"set {args.id} line {number} cells={','.join(changed)}"


def restore(descriptor, units_path, old, cause):
    """The recovery of a failed write and its one line: the old bytes written back at 0 until all are written, the
    file truncated to their length and synced, or the restore's own failure named (`may hold a torn text`)."""
    try:
        offset = 0
        while offset < len(old):
            written = os.pwrite(descriptor, old[offset:], offset)
            if written <= 0:
                raise OSError(errno.EIO, "short write")
            offset += written
        os.ftruncate(descriptor, len(old))
        os.fsync(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        return (
            f"cannot write {units_path}: {cause}; the register {units_path} may hold a torn text, the restore of its "
            f"{len(old)} bytes failed: {error.strerror}"
        )
    return f"cannot write {units_path}: {cause}; restored its {len(old)} bytes"


def write_text(descriptor, units_path, old, data, offset):
    """One `os.pwrite` of `data` at `offset` (n0 for an appended line, 0 for a rewritten text), its count compared
    with the length, `os.ftruncate` to the new length when the text shrank, then `os.fsync`. A failure restores the
    old bytes. Returns None, or the failure text naming the register."""
    try:
        written = os.pwrite(descriptor, data, offset)
    except OSError as error:
        return restore(descriptor, units_path, old, f"write: {error.strerror}")
    if written != len(data):
        return restore(descriptor, units_path, old, f"short write, {written} of {len(data)} bytes")
    try:
        if offset + len(data) < len(old):
            os.ftruncate(descriptor, offset + len(data))
        os.fsync(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        return restore(descriptor, units_path, old, f"fsync: {error.strerror}")
    return None


def write_row(args, units_path, descriptor):
    """The critical section, under the lock the descriptor holds: the register read and parsed through it, the new
    text composed and parsed again, the one write. Returns (0, the stdout line) or (1, the failure text)."""
    length, old, text = read_register(descriptor, units_path)
    rows = parse_register(units_path, text)
    if args.kind == "add":
        data, line = added_text(args, units_path, text, rows)
        offset = length
        whole = old + data if data is not None else None
    else:
        data, line = set_text(args, units_path, text, rows)
        offset = 0
        whole = data
    if data is None:
        return 0, line
    parse_register(units_path, whole.decode("utf-8"))
    failure = write_text(descriptor, units_path, old, data, offset)
    if failure is not None:
        return 1, failure
    return 0, line


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else list(argv)
    argument_rule(argv)
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    check_lock_wait(args)
    store = store_dir(args.store)
    units_path = store_file(store, UNITS_FILE, "register")
    descriptor = open_register(units_path, args.lock_wait)
    try:
        code, text = write_row(args, units_path, descriptor)
    except BaseException:  # a refusal (SystemExit) or an unexpected error: the close releases the lock
        try:
            os.close(descriptor)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise
    try:
        os.close(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        if code == 0:
            text = f"the register {units_path} was written ({text}) but its close failed: {error.strerror}"
        else:
            text = f"{text}; the close failed too: {error.strerror}"
        code = 1
    if code == 0:
        print(text)
    else:
        print(f"{LEVER}: {one_line(text)}", file=sys.stderr)
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_uv-format
# @brief Format Python code with Ruff through `uvx`.
# @description
#   Runs Ruff formatting first and then fixes import ordering and selected
#   issues through Ruff's check mode.
# @example
#   uv-format

# @description Run Ruff formatting and autofix passes through `uvx`.
function uv_format() {
    uvx ruff format
    uvx ruff check --fix --extend-select I
}

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    uv_format
fi

docs.text: Regime-cutover U123 (standing order 29: workers never push; the coordinator pushes). The order was text in the first line of every TASK, and on 2026-10-30 six owners pushed anyway; the one stopped was the one whose push route had no key. This lever makes the order a refusal of the tool. Run it from the main checkout: worker-worktree.sh <unit> <branch> <base> makes <root>/<unit> (the root $DOTFILES_WT when set, else ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dotfiles-wt, resolved through its longest existing directory with pwd -P) as a fresh repository, not a linked worktree of the checkout (rounds 1 to 3 hardened git worktree add inside the checkout, and each audit found another channel of the checkout's configuration that runs during creation: post-checkout hooks, hook.<name>.event hooks, a required smudge filter, a locked tree; round 4 removes the linked worktree from the design). The fresh repository shares the checkout's objects alone: - git init -q --template= makes it with no template, under GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, the environment every git this lever runs has (git_run below), so neither the operator's global configuration (a core.hooksPath, a hook.<name>.event, a filter.<name>.smudge, an init.templateDir) nor the checkout's is read while the tree is made; - objects/info/alternates names the checkout's objects directory (git rev-parse --git-path objects there), so the fetch below transfers nothing and a worker's commits are written into the fresh repository's own store; - git fetch <checkout> <base sha>:refs/remotes/origin/main, the sha the checkout's rev-parse --verify <base>^{commit} printed, gives the tree the origin/main the workers' tests read, and git checkout --no-track -b <branch> origin/main makes the branch in the fresh repository: the checkout's own branches are never read or written, so a branch of the same name in the checkout is no conflict; - the fresh repository's own config then holds remote.origin.url (the checkout's, so git fetch origin works and origin/main moves), remote.origin.fetch for refs/heads/*, remote.origin.pushurl = refused://never-push-from-a-worker-worktree (so git push, git push origin <ref> and git push -u origin <branch> fail on a remote helper that does not exist, before any remote is contacted), an empty credential.helper (clears the helper list for an https push that spells the URL), core.hooksPath = <repository>/.git/hooks-lever holding one pre-push hook that prints standing order 29: the coordinator pushes and exits 1 (a push that spells any URL is refused after git has read the remote's refs and before any object is sent), branch.<branch>.remote = origin, branch.<branch>.merge = refs/heads/<branch>, and the three keys a bare git push resolves its remote from, in git's order (git-push(1)): branch.<branch>.pushRemote = origin, then remote.pushDefault = origin, then branch.<branch>.remote, with push.default = current; all are local values, and a local value wins over a global one, so a bare push goes to the refusal URL whatever the worker's global config says (a global branch.<branch>.pushRemote = upstream included). Nothing in the checkout changes at any point: its refs, config, hooks and git worktree list are the same after a failed and after a successful run, and the worker tree is not in that list. The coordinator fetches the worker's head by path and pushes it from the checkout: git -C <checkout> fetch <repository> <branch> && git -C <checkout> push <origin url> FETCH_HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, the line this lever prints. Every input is checked before anything is made (exit 2, nothing created): the unit U<n> or U<n><letter>, a branch git check-ref-format --branch accepts, taken as the normalized name it prints, over [A-Za-z0-9._/-] (the shell reads nothing in the printed push line), a base that names a commit, the working directory a main checkout (not a linked worktree) with an origin remote whose URL is absolute (scheme://, [user@]host: or /-rooted: a relative URL copied into the fresh repository would resolve from there, not from the checkout; the program's origin is https), the root absolute, without a . or .. component, and, resolved through its longest existing directory (cd and pwd -P), outside the checkout's working tree and git directory by identity: the device and inode (stat) of that directory and of each directory above it, up to /, differ from the checkout's and its git directory's, so no spelling of the checkout's path (a case alias on a case-insensitive volume, a symlink, a trailing slash) names it without being it (<checkout>/.git/hooks is no root: a tree made there would write the checkout; round 5 compared the resolved strings, and the audit made the tree through a case alias), and neither the checkout's path nor the root holding a newline, each in its resolved form (a symlink whose name holds none may point at a directory whose name holds one; the alternates file is one path per line); every path read (git rev-parse's and pwd -P's) is captured exactly, a sentinel after the output keeping the trailing newline $(…) would strip, so a directory named trees<LF> is never read as its newline-free sibling trees (round 2 of U123b: the checks ran on the sibling and the tree was made under it). A read that fails before anything is made (git rev-parse, git config, the resolver's cd and pwd -P, the uname -s that chooses stat's format flag, stat itself) is a refusal with exit 2, never an absence (standing order 21). Then mkdir <root>/<unit> (no -p) reserves the target: success means this run owns the directory and may remove it on failure; failure (a directory or symlink there, or mkdir's own error) is a refusal that touched nothing, so two runs for one unit never both proceed and one run's cleanup never removes the other's repository. When a step after the reservation fails, the directory this run reserved is removed again (rm -rf of <root>/<unit>, which this run's mkdir made and only this lever wrote) and the exit is 2 naming the step: no tree without the refusals is ever left, and nothing else is removed. Every git this lever runs has every GIT_* name removed from its environment and the global and system configuration closed (git_run): round 4 listed six names, and the audit found GIT_INDEX_FILE, which writes the fresh repository's index into the checkout, and GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, which names another objects directory for the alternates; the names are subtracted by prefix, so no list of them can be short. Trusted: the worker is a non-adversarial actor whose reflex the refusals stop, not an attacker. A worker that rewrites the fresh repository's config or hooks directory can restore the push path; the tree is the worker's, and the refusal removes the path a push takes by habit, which is the failure that happened.

#   longest existing directory and each directory above it); made when absent, and printed as `pwd -P` resolves it,
#   a resolved form holding a newline refused.
# @stdout `worktree=<path>`, `branch=<branch>`, `head=<sha>` and `push=git -C <checkout> fetch <path> <branch> &&
#   git -C <checkout> push <origin url> FETCH_HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, the line the coordinator runs from the main
#   checkout, one per line; the paths and the URL are quoted for the shell (`printf %q`), the branch's character set
#   needs none.
# @exitcode 0 The repository exists at the base on the branch with the refusals and the upstream set.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, a unit, branch or base outside the grammar, a working directory that is not the main
#   checkout or has no `origin` or a relative origin URL, a root inside the checkout or its git directory by identity,
#   or holding a `.`, `..` or a newline (its resolved form included), a checkout path holding a newline, the target
#   path present (the reservation failed), a read (`git rev-parse`, `git config`, the resolver's `cd` and `pwd -P`,
#   `uname -s`, `stat`) that failed, or the manifest pin differing from this file, each before anything is made; or a
#   step after the reservation that failed, after which the directory this run made is removed again and nothing else.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/worker-worktree.sh U123 feat/refusals-not-sentences origin/main
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest=''
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest=''
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check

lever='worker-worktree.sh'
usage='usage: worker-worktree.sh <unit> <branch> <base>'
pushurl='refused://never-push-from-a-worker-worktree'
hook_message='standing order 29: the coordinator pushes'
path=''

# @description Print a refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was made.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print a failed step on stderr and exit 2; the EXIT trap removes the directory this run reserved.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*; the repository ${path} this run made is removed again" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Run git with every `GIT_*` name removed from its environment and the global and system configuration
#   closed (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`). The names are subtracted by prefix, not listed:
#   round 4 listed `GIT_CONFIG`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE` and
#   `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, and the audit of that round found `GIT_INDEX_FILE` (the fresh repository's index written into
#   the checkout, or the checkout's index reused, so the tree had no README) and `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` (another
#   objects directory named by `rev-parse --git-path objects`, so the alternates pointed elsewhere); every other
#   `GIT_*` name steers a read or a write too. `${!GIT_@}` is the shell's own list of the names, so no producer's
#   status is at stake, and the unset runs in a subshell that execs git, so the caller's environment stays as it was.
#   The closed configuration holds for the reads in the checkout as well: none of them needs the operator's global
#   config, and no `core.hooksPath`, `hook.<name>.event` or `filter.<name>.smudge` of it is read by any git this
#   lever runs.
# @arg $@ string git's arguments.
# @exitcode 2 A name cannot be removed (readonly).
# @exitcode * git's own status.
git_run() {
    (
        for name in "${!GIT_@}"; do
            unset -v "${name}" || {
                echo "${lever}: refused: cannot remove ${name} from git's environment" >&2
                exit 2
            }
        done
        export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
        exec git "$@"
    )
}

# @description Set `exact` to the standard output of the command $@, byte for byte apart from the one newline that
#   ends its line. `$(…)` strips every trailing newline, so `pwd -P` in a directory named `trees<LF>` read as the
#   newline-free sibling `trees`, and the newline check and the identity walk ran on the sibling while the tree was
#   made under it (round 2 of U123b). The command's output is followed by a sentinel `x`, which holds the newlines in
#   place; the sentinel and one newline are removed, and whatever is left of the name, a newline included, reaches the
#   checks. The result is a variable, not output, so no second substitution stands between the read and its reader.
# @arg $@ string The command; its stderr is the caller's.
# @set exact The output.
# @exitcode 1 The command failed.
exact_line() {
    exact=$("$@" && printf x) || return 1
    exact=${exact%x}
    exact=${exact%$'\n'}
}

# @description Print the physical path of the directory $1 (`cd` and `pwd -P`). Run inside `exact_line`'s
#   substitution, so the `cd` is a subshell's and the lever's own directory does not change.
# @arg $1 string A directory.
# @exitcode 1 The directory cannot be entered.
physical_path() {
    cd -- "$1" && pwd -P
}

# @description Resolve $1, an absolute path without `.` or `..` components that may not exist yet, through its longest
#   existing leading directory (`physical_path` through `exact_line`, so a symlink into the checkout is seen for what
#   it is and a trailing newline in the directory's name is kept): `root_prefix`
#   is that directory's physical path and `resolved_root` is it with the rest appended as given, the directories
#   `mkdir -p` would make. The results are variables, not output, so no producer stands between the resolution and its
#   readers, and the prefix is the first directory of the identity walk below.
# @arg $1 string The path.
# @set root_prefix The physical path of the longest existing leading directory.
# @set resolved_root The resolved path.
# @exitcode 1 The existing prefix cannot be entered (`cd` or `pwd -P` failed).
resolve_root() {
    local candidate=$1 rest=''
    while [[ ! -d ${candidate} ]]; do
        rest=${candidate##*/}${rest:+/${rest}}
        candidate=${candidate%/*}
        [[ -n ${candidate} ]] || candidate=/
    done
    exact_line physical_path "${candidate}" || return 1
    root_prefix=${exact}
    resolved_root=${root_prefix%/}${rest:+/${rest}}
    [[ -n ${resolved_root} ]] || resolved_root=/
}

# @description Print the device and inode of $1, one line `<device> <inode>`, as `stat` prints them with the format
#   flag `stat_args` chose for this system; a `stat` that fails or prints another shape is a failed read, never an
#   identity (standing order 21).
# @arg $1 string A path that exists.
# @exitcode 1 The read failed or printed something other than two decimals.
identity_of() {
    local id
    id=$(stat "${stat_args[@]}" -- "$1") || return 1
    [[ ${id} =~ ^[0-9]+' '[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${id}"
}

[[ $# == 3 ]] || refuse "${usage}"
unit=$1
branch=$2
base=$3
[[ ${unit} =~ ^U[0-9]+[a-z]?$ ]] || refuse "the unit ${unit} is not U<n> or U<n><letter>"
[[ -n ${branch} ]] || refuse "the branch is empty"
# check-ref-format --branch prints the name it accepts, normalized (`@{-1}` becomes the branch it denotes), and that
# name is the one made. The character set then excludes what a shell would read in the printed push line (`;`, a
# space, a quote), beyond what git accepts.
normalized=$(git_run check-ref-format --branch "${branch}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "the branch ${branch} is not a name git accepts"
branch=${normalized}
[[ ${branch} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$ ]] || refuse "the branch ${branch} has a character outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
[[ -n ${base} ]] || refuse "the base is empty"

exact_line git_run rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null || refuse 'run from the main checkout'
toplevel=${exact}
exact_line physical_path "${toplevel}" || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
toplevel=${exact}
[[ ${toplevel} != *$'\n'* ]] || refuse "the checkout path ${toplevel//$'\n'/\\n} holds a newline; the alternates file is one path per line" # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test (a newline in the path), no path identity is compared
exact_line git_run rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir 2> /dev/null || refuse "cannot read the git directory of ${toplevel}"
git_dir=${exact}
exact_line git_run rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2> /dev/null || refuse "cannot read the git common directory of ${toplevel}"
common=${exact}
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are git's absolute forms of one checkout
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree (git dir ${git_dir}, common ${common}); run from the main checkout"
exact_line physical_path "${git_dir}" || refuse "cannot resolve the git directory ${git_dir}"
git_dir=${exact}
exact_line git_run rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path objects 2> /dev/null || refuse "cannot read the objects directory of ${toplevel}"
objects=${exact}
[[ -d ${objects} ]] || refuse "${objects} is not a directory"
[[ ${objects} != *$'\n'* ]] || refuse "the objects directory ${objects//$'\n'/\\n} holds a newline; the alternates file is one path per line" # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test (a newline in the path), no path identity is compared
# git config exits 1 for a key that is absent and otherwise for a read that failed (standing order 21): only 1 is absence.
status=0
origin_url=$(git_run config --get remote.origin.url 2>&1) || status=$?
case ${status} in
0) ;;
1) refuse "no origin remote in ${toplevel}" ;;
*) refuse "cannot read remote.origin.url from the checkout's config: ${origin_url}" ;;
esac
# An absolute URL resolves the same from the fresh repository as from the checkout: a scheme (`https://`, `file://`),
# the scp-like `[user@]host:path` (no slash before the first colon, git-clone(1)), or a `/`-rooted path. A relative
# path (`../origin.git`) is relative to the repository git runs in, and copied into the fresh repository it names
# another place.
[[ ${origin_url} =~ ^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|[^/:]+:|/) ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test (absolute or relative), no URL identity is compared
    refuse "the origin URL ${origin_url} of ${toplevel} is not absolute (scheme://, [user@]host: or /-rooted); from the new repository it would name another place"
base_sha=$(git_run rev-parse --verify --quiet "${base}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null) || refuse "the base ${base} names no commit; run git fetch origin"
[[ ${base_sha} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40,64}$ ]] || refuse "the base ${base} resolved to ${base_sha}, not an object name"

root=${DOTFILES_WT:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dotfiles-wt}
[[ ${root} == /* ]] || refuse "DOTFILES_WT ${root} is not an absolute path" # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test (absolute or not), no path identity is compared
# A `.` or `..` component after the last existing directory would make `mkdir -p` land elsewhere than the resolved
# prefix says (`<tmp>/absent/../checkout`), so the root is taken without either.
[[ ${root} != */./* && ${root} != */../* && ${root} != */. && ${root} != */.. ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test (a . or .. component), no path identity is compared
    refuse "DOTFILES_WT ${root} has a . or .. component; give the resolved path"
[[ ${root} != *$'\n'* ]] || refuse "DOTFILES_WT ${root//$'\n'/\\n} holds a newline; the alternates file is one path per line" # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test (a newline in the path), no path identity is compared
resolve_root "${root}" || refuse "cannot resolve DOTFILES_WT ${root}; its longest existing directory cannot be entered"
root=${resolved_root}
# The resolved form is checked again: a symlink whose own name holds no newline may point at a directory whose name
# holds one, and the alternates file and the printed `worktree=` line are one path per line.
[[ ${root} != *$'\n'* ]] || refuse "DOTFILES_WT resolves to ${root//$'\n'/\\n}, which holds a newline; the alternates file is one path per line" # lint-comparisons: allow a shape test (a newline in the path), no path identity is compared
# A root inside the checkout's working tree or git directory (`<checkout>/.git/hooks`) would have the tree made
# write the checkout, which this lever never does. Containment is decided by identity, not by spelling: round 5
# compared the resolved strings, and on a case-insensitive volume a case alias of the checkout path
# (`<CHECKOUT>/.git/hooks`) was no prefix match, so the tree was made in the checkout's hooks directory. The device
# and inode of the root's longest existing directory and of each directory above it, up to `/`, are read with `stat`
# and compared with the checkout's and its git directory's; the components `mkdir -p` would make do not exist yet, so
# none of them is a directory of the checkout. `stat`'s format flag is `-f` on macOS and `-c` on Linux; the system
# name is read once, and a failed read refuses.
os=$(uname -s) || refuse 'cannot read the operating system name (uname -s)'
case ${os} in
Darwin) stat_args=(-f '%d %i') ;;
Linux) stat_args=(-c '%d %i') ;;
*) refuse "no identity read for the system ${os}; stat's format flag is known for Darwin and Linux" ;;
esac
checkout_id=$(identity_of "${toplevel}") || refuse "cannot read the identity (device and inode) of the checkout ${toplevel}"
git_dir_id=$(identity_of "${git_dir}") || refuse "cannot read the identity (device and inode) of the git directory ${git_dir}"
dir=${root_prefix}
while :; do
    dir_id=$(identity_of "${dir}") || refuse "cannot read the identity (device and inode) of ${dir}, which DOTFILES_WT ${root} lies under"
    [[ ${dir_id} != "${checkout_id}" && ${dir_id} != "${git_dir_id}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow compares (device, inode) identities, not paths
        refuse "DOTFILES_WT ${root} lies inside the checkout ${toplevel} or its git directory ${git_dir} (${dir} has the identity ${dir_id} of one of them); a worker tree is never made in the checkout"
    [[ ${dir} != / ]] || break # lint-comparisons: allow the walk ends at the filesystem root, a shape test; no path identity is compared
    dir=${dir%/*}
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
done
path=${root%/}/${unit}

# @description Remove the directory this run reserved when a later step failed, so a tree without the refusals is
#   never left: `<root>/<unit>` is the directory this run's own mkdir made (the reservation) and only this lever wrote
#   under it, and nothing in the checkout was written, so nothing else is removed. Runs on EXIT; a completed run has
#   nothing to remove, and a run whose reservation failed owns nothing.
created=0
completed=0
cleanup() {
    [[ ${completed} == 0 && ${created} == 1 ]] || return 0
    rm -rf -- "${path}" || echo "${lever}: rm -rf ${path} failed; remove it by hand" >&2
}
trap cleanup EXIT

mkdir -p -- "${root}" || refuse "cannot make ${root}"
# The reservation: `mkdir` without `-p` fails when anything is at the path (a directory, a file, a symlink dangling
# or not), so of two runs for one unit exactly one owns the directory, and the other refuses having touched nothing.
if ! reserve_error=$(mkdir -- "${path}" 2>&1); then
    [[ ! -e ${path} && ! -L ${path} ]] || refuse "${path} exists; an existing directory is never touched"
    refuse "cannot reserve ${path}: ${reserve_error}"
fi
created=1
git_run init --quiet --template= "${path}" || fail "git init ${path} exited $?"
fresh_git=$(git_run -C "${path}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir) || fail "cannot read the git directory of ${path}"
[[ -d ${fresh_git}/objects/info ]] || fail "${fresh_git}/objects/info is not a directory"
printf '%s\n' "${objects}" > "${fresh_git}/objects/info/alternates" || fail "cannot write ${fresh_git}/objects/info/alternates"
hooks=${fresh_git}/hooks-lever
mkdir "${hooks}" || fail "cannot make ${hooks}"
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "%s" >&2\nexit 1\n' "${hook_message}" > "${hooks}/pre-push" || fail "cannot write ${hooks}/pre-push"
chmod 755 "${hooks}/pre-push" || fail "cannot make ${hooks}/pre-push executable"
# The refusals and the push shape are written before the fetch and the checkout, so the hooks directory git reads
# while the tree is made is this lever's own, holding `pre-push` alone.
git_run -C "${path}" config core.hooksPath "${hooks}" || fail "cannot set core.hooksPath in ${path}"
git_run -C "${path}" config remote.origin.url "${origin_url}" || fail "cannot set remote.origin.url in ${path}"
git_run -C "${path}" config remote.origin.fetch '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*' || fail "cannot set remote.origin.fetch in ${path}"
git_run -C "${path}" config remote.origin.pushurl "${pushurl}" || fail "cannot set remote.origin.pushurl in ${path}"
git_run -C "${path}" config credential.helper '' || fail "cannot set credential.helper in ${path}"
git_run -C "${path}" config remote.pushDefault origin || fail "cannot set remote.pushDefault in ${path}"
git_run -C "${path}" config push.default current || fail "cannot set push.default in ${path}"
# The base by sha, from the checkout by path: the objects are already present through the alternates, so nothing is
# transferred, and the fresh repository gets the `origin/main` the workers' tests read.
git_run -C "${path}" fetch --quiet "${toplevel}" "${base_sha}:refs/remotes/origin/main" || fail "git fetch ${base_sha} from ${toplevel} exited $?"
git_run -C "${path}" checkout --quiet --no-track -b "${branch}" origin/main || fail "git checkout -b ${branch} origin/main in ${path} exited $?"
git_run -C "${path}" config "branch.${branch}.remote" origin || fail "cannot set branch.${branch}.remote in ${path}"
git_run -C "${path}" config "branch.${branch}.merge" "refs/heads/${branch}" || fail "cannot set branch.${branch}.merge in ${path}"
# The first key git-push(1) resolves a bare push's remote from; a global `branch.<branch>.pushRemote` would otherwise
# stand before the local `remote.pushDefault`.
git_run -C "${path}" config "branch.${branch}.pushRemote" origin || fail "cannot set branch.${branch}.pushRemote in ${path}"
# The refusals are read back from the fresh repository's own config, so a value git wrote elsewhere never reads as set.
set_pushurl=$(git_run -C "${path}" config --get-all remote.origin.pushurl) || fail "remote.origin.pushurl is not set in ${path}"
[[ ${set_pushurl} == "${pushurl}" ]] || fail "remote.origin.pushurl in ${path} is ${set_pushurl//$'\n'/, }, not ${pushurl} alone"
set_hooks=$(git_run -C "${path}" config --get core.hooksPath) || fail "core.hooksPath is not set in ${path}"
[[ ${set_hooks} == "${hooks}" ]] || fail "core.hooksPath in ${path} is ${set_hooks}, not ${hooks}" # lint-comparisons: allow the value written above, read back
set_remote=$(git_run -C "${path}" config --get "branch.${branch}.remote") || fail "branch.${branch}.remote is not set in ${path}"
[[ ${set_remote} == origin ]] || fail "branch.${branch}.remote in ${path} is ${set_remote}, not origin"
set_merge=$(git_run -C "${path}" config --get "branch.${branch}.merge") || fail "branch.${branch}.merge is not set in ${path}"
[[ ${set_merge} == "refs/heads/${branch}" ]] || fail "branch.${branch}.merge in ${path} is ${set_merge}, not refs/heads/${branch}" # lint-comparisons: allow the value written above, read back
set_push_remote=$(git_run -C "${path}" config --get "branch.${branch}.pushRemote") || fail "branch.${branch}.pushRemote is not set in ${path}"
[[ ${set_push_remote} == origin ]] || fail "branch.${branch}.pushRemote in ${path} is ${set_push_remote}, not origin"
head=$(git_run -C "${path}" rev-parse --verify HEAD) || fail "cannot read the head of ${path}"
[[ ${head} == "${base_sha}" ]] || fail "the head of ${path} is ${head}, not the base ${base_sha}"
completed=1

printf 'worktree=%s\nbranch=%s\nhead=%s\n' "${path}" "${branch}" "${head}"
# The paths and the URL are quoted for the shell the coordinator pastes the line into; the branch's character set
# needs no quoting. The fetch by path brings the worker's head into the checkout, and FETCH_HEAD is what is pushed.
printf 'push=git -C %q fetch %q %s && git -C %q push %q FETCH_HEAD:refs/heads/%s\n' "${toplevel}" "${path}" "${branch}" "${toplevel}" "${origin_url}" "${branch}"
</code></pre>

The candidates are the worktrees of this checkout (git worktree list --porcelain -z) under <toplevel>/.claude/worktrees/, except the quarantine <toplevel>/.claude/worktrees/.gc-quarantine/; every other worktree, the main one and the omp seats included, is never listed. A candidate qualifies when its tree is clean (git status --porcelain --ignored=matching --untracked-files=all prints nothing: git worktree remove deletes ignored files without asking, so a tree holding one, an .env say, is kept; and no index entry carries the assume-unchanged or skip-worktree flag, git ls-files -v tag lowercase or S, since an edit to such a file is invisible to git status and to the removal's own check) and its work landed, the first of: its head is reachable from origin/main (git merge-base --is-ancestor); it landed by content (every path git diff --no-renames --name-only -z <merge-base> <head> names holds in origin/main the entry it holds in the head, mode and object, or is absent from both: the case of a squash merge with no later commit; no merge runs, so no configured merge driver or merge= attribute can answer, and a git failure is an error row); or its head is the headRefOid of a merged pull request of this repository (gh pr list --state merged --head <branch> --json number,headRefOid --limit 100, detached --search <sha>). A branch name alone never counts: a commit pushed after a squash merge is not in main, and --head also matches a fork's branch of the same name. A locked or missing worktree is kept. The listing is read field by field on its NUL separators, so a path cannot forge a record; a candidate whose path contains a newline is an error row. Each candidate prints one row <verdict>\t<path>\t<ref>\t<reason> (a newline in the path printed as \n), verdict gc (qualifies), keep or error, then each quarantined worktree a quarantine row with its age, then one summary row.
