#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/ubuntu/server/setup_timezone.sh
# @brief Configure the server timezone.
# @description
#   Points `/etc/localtime` and `/etc/timezone` at `Asia/Tokyo` and installs `tzdata` non-interactively, once.
#   It does nothing on a GitHub runner, because replacing `/etc/localtime` there stalled every server bootstrap
#   leg until the 35-minute cancel (regime-cutover U254, bisected by PRs 681 to 690) and the runner's clock is not
#   the kit's to set. It does nothing when `/etc/localtime` already resolves to the zone, so a second run on a host
#   changes no file.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

#
# @description Print the zone file `/etc/localtime` resolves to.
# @stdout The resolved path, `/usr/share/zoneinfo/Asia/Tokyo` on a configured host.
# @exitcode 1 The link cannot be resolved; the caller reads this as an unknown zone.
#
function current_zone_file() {
    readlink -f /etc/localtime 2> /dev/null
}

#
# @description Apply the repository's preferred timezone configuration, or print why it is left as it is.
# @set TZ string `Asia/Tokyo`, exported for the rest of the bootstrap.
# @stdout One line: `timezone: unchanged on a GitHub runner ...`, `timezone: already <TZ>`, or `timezone: setting
#   <TZ> (was <zone file or unknown>)` followed by the commands' own output.
#
function main() {
    export TZ="Asia/Tokyo"

    if [ -n "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ]; then
        echo "timezone: unchanged on a GitHub runner (GITHUB_ACTIONS is set; replacing /etc/localtime stalls the runner, regime-cutover U254)"
        return 0
    fi

    local current_zone_file
    if ! current_zone_file="$(current_zone_file)"; then
        current_zone_file=""
    fi
    if [[ "${current_zone_file}" == */"${TZ}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow zone-is-the-path-tail (the file was resolved by readlink -f above; tzdata names a zone by its path under zoneinfo, so the tail is the zone, not a path identity)
        echo "timezone: already ${TZ}"
        return 0
    fi

    echo "timezone: setting ${TZ} (was ${current_zone_file:-unknown})"
    sudo ln -snf "/usr/share/zoneinfo/${TZ}" /etc/localtime
    echo "${TZ}" | sudo tee /etc/timezone

    sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y tzdata
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/ubuntu/server/ssh_server.sh
# @brief Install and configure an Ubuntu SSH server.
# @description
#   Installs `openssh-server`, configures it for the repository's Docker test
#   container, and starts the SSH service. The script is container-only: it
#   refuses to run (exit 1) unless `/.dockerenv` exists, so a server-role apply
#   on a real host never reconfigures that host's sshd. Root login keeps the
#   distribution default `prohibit-password` and sshd keeps its default listen
#   addresses.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

declare -r SSH_PORT="${DOTFILES_SERVER_SSH_PORT:-22}"

#
# @description Install the Ubuntu OpenSSH server package and its prerequisites.
#
function install_openssh_server() {
    # install openssh-server and vim
    sudo --preserve-env=http_proxy,https_proxy,no_proxy apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y \
        vim \
        openssh-server
}

#
# @description Merge proxy-related variables into `AcceptEnv` in `sshd_config`.
#
function configure_accept_env() {
    local current add merged

    # Get existing AcceptEnv values (empty if not set)
    current=$(grep '^AcceptEnv' /etc/ssh/sshd_config | sed 's/^AcceptEnv //')

    # Variables to append
    add="HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY NO_PROXY http_proxy https_proxy no_proxy"

    # Merge and remove duplicates
    merged=$(echo "$current $add" | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')

    # Remove existing entries and keep a single AcceptEnv line
    sudo sed -i '/^AcceptEnv/d' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
    echo "AcceptEnv $merged" | sudo tee -a /etc/ssh/sshd_config
}

#
# @description Configure `sshd` for the repository's container-oriented setup.
#
function setup_sshd() {
    sudo mkdir -p /var/run/sshd
    mkdir -p "${HOME}/.ssh"

    sudo sed -i "s/^#\?Port .*/Port ${SSH_PORT}/" /etc/ssh/sshd_config &&
        sudo sed -i 's/^#PubkeyAuthentication yes/PubkeyAuthentication yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config &&
        sudo sed 's@session\s*required\s*pam_loginuid.so@session optional pam_loginuid.so@g' -i /etc/pam.d/sshd

    configure_accept_env

    # check the /etc/ssh/sshd_config
    sudo /usr/sbin/sshd -t

    # create .ssh/authorized_keys if not exists
    touch "${HOME}/.ssh/authorized_keys"
}

#
# @description Start the SSH service after configuration has been validated.
#
function run_sshd() {
    # run sshd
    sudo /usr/sbin/service ssh start
}

#
# @description Install, configure, and start the Ubuntu SSH server.
#
function main() {
    install_openssh_server
    setup_sshd
    run_sshd
}

#
# @description Return success when the script runs inside a Docker container.
#
function in_container() {
    [ -f "/.dockerenv" ]
}

#
# @description Run `main` only inside a container; fail closed anywhere else.
# @exitcode 1 When `/.dockerenv` is absent (not a Docker container).
#
function run_in_container_only() {
    if ! in_container; then
        echo "ssh_server.sh: refusing to configure sshd outside a Docker container (/.dockerenv not found)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    main
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    run_in_container_only
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file install/ubuntu/server/starship.sh
# @brief Install the Starship prompt on Ubuntu servers.
# @description
#   Downloads the pinned Starship release and verifies it against its reviewed
#   sha256 and the .sha256 file published with it. Runs on every chezmoi apply
#   and skips when the pinned release is already installed, so a pin bump
#   applies on the next `make update`.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if [ "${DOTFILES_DEBUG:-}" ]; then
    set -x
fi

readonly BIN_DIR="${HOME}/.local/bin"
readonly STARSHIP_RELEASE_REPO="starship/starship"
# Rendered from assets.starship in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml; change them there.
# starship's releases are mutable and carry only .sha256 sidecars, so the reviewed sha256 is the check.
readonly STARSHIP_PIN_VERSION="v1.27.0"
readonly STARSHIP_X86_64_SHA256="10c8eb4cb3b761d9bf59ea828444c2dab36c900b7d69a69e08814b286969df89"
readonly STARSHIP_AARCH64_SHA256="341f5cbf24699fa0b27ec88965ad25f862ea09e15d35a543fd6ffdff1d2aa00d"

# @description Print the Starship Linux artifact name and its reviewed sha256 for the current architecture.
function starship_artifact() {
    local machine
    machine="$(uname -m)" || {
        printf 'uname -m failed; no Starship artifact was chosen.\n' >&2
        return 1
    }
    case "${machine}" in
    x86_64) printf 'starship-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz %s\n' "${STARSHIP_X86_64_SHA256}" ;;
    aarch64 | arm64) printf 'starship-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz %s\n' "${STARSHIP_AARCH64_SHA256}" ;;
    *)
        printf 'Unsupported Starship architecture: %s\n' "${machine}" >&2
        return 1
        ;;
    esac
}

#
# @description Print the installed Starship version, or nothing when it is absent or cannot report one.
#
function starship_installed_version() {
    local output
    [ -x "${BIN_DIR}/starship" ] || return 0
    # A binary that exits non-zero is broken whatever it printed, so it reports no version.
    output="$("${BIN_DIR}/starship" --version 2> /dev/null)" || return 0
    printf '%s\n' "${output}" | awk '$1 == "starship" { print $2; exit }'
}

#
# @description Download the pinned Starship release, verify it, and install the binary.
# @exitcode 1 The checksum did not match, or the install failed; nothing was installed.
# @exitcode 3 A download failed, so nothing was installed.
#
function install_starship() (
    local actual artifact base_url expected line pinned stage="" tmpdir
    line="$(starship_artifact)" || return
    read -r artifact pinned <<< "${line}"
    base_url="https://github.com/${STARSHIP_RELEASE_REPO}/releases/download/${STARSHIP_PIN_VERSION}"
    tmpdir="$(mktemp -d)" || return
    trap 'rm -rf "${tmpdir}"; [ -z "${stage}" ] || rm -f "${stage}"' EXIT
    mkdir -p "${BIN_DIR}" || return
    stage="$(mktemp "${BIN_DIR}/starship.tmp.XXXXXX")" || return
    # Each curl gets 30 s to connect and fails a transfer under 1 KB/s for 60 s, so a stalled download ends.
    curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 "${base_url}/${artifact}" \
        -o "${tmpdir}/${artifact}" || return 3
    expected="$(curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 60 \
        "${base_url}/${artifact}.sha256")" || return 3
    [ -n "${expected}" ] || {
        printf 'Missing checksum for %s\n' "${artifact}" >&2
        return 1
    }
    actual="$(sha256sum "${tmpdir}/${artifact}" | awk '{ print $1 }')" || return
    # The reviewed sha256 is the check; the release's own .sha256 only re-checks the download.
    if [ "${actual}" != "${pinned}" ] || [ "${actual}" != "${expected}" ]; then
        printf 'Checksum mismatch for %s\n' "${artifact}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    tar -xzf "${tmpdir}/${artifact}" -C "${tmpdir}" || return
    install -m 0755 "${tmpdir}/starship" "${stage}" || return
    mv -f "${stage}" "${BIN_DIR}/starship"
)

#
# @description Remove the locally installed Starship binary.
#
function uninstall_starship() {
    rm -f -- "${BIN_DIR}/starship"
}

#
# @description Install or update Starship to the pinned release.
#
function main() {
    local installed status=0
    installed="$(starship_installed_version)"
    [ "${installed}" != "${STARSHIP_PIN_VERSION#v}" ] || return 0
    install_starship || status=$?
    # A failed download keeps a working Starship; a failed check never does.
    if [ "${status}" -eq 3 ] && [ -n "${installed}" ]; then
        printf 'warning: could not download Starship %s; Starship %s stays.\n' "${STARSHIP_PIN_VERSION}" "${installed}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    return "${status}"
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main
fi

That required job also runs this script, on the runner, for a diff whose home/ paths are all render-only. After chezmoi init, apply and verify it runs the parts of make doctor that judge the applied files and need no installed tool and no login: chezmoi doctor --no-network and scripts/check-agent-runtime.py (its GitHub login line stays a warning). The rest of make doctor stays out: scripts/check-tools.sh and the omp asset checks require mise, uv, gh and omp, which only the skipped installers put on a host, and scripts/check-sleep.sh reads the host's power setting, which no apply changes. #!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file scripts/apply-check.sh
# @brief Apply home/ as a fresh client or server into a scratch HOME, verify it, and run the credential-free doctor checks.
# @description
#   The disposable check `make apply-check` runs inside a container, for client
#   and server. It copies the parts of the working tree
#   that the apply and the checks read (.chezmoiroot, home/, scripts/) into a
#   scratch directory, applies from that copy as setup.sh's chezmoi would from a
#   clone, and points HOME at a scratch home, so the tree, the caller's HOME and
#   the caller's chezmoi config stay untouched.
#   It runs only where scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh's is_ci_runner holds: a GitHub
#   Actions runner, or the container `make apply-check` starts, which declares
#   itself one because it is as disposable and keyless as a runner. There the
#   chezmoi config renders without age encryption (home/.chezmoi.yaml.tmpl), and,
#   as setup.sh does without a tty, the encrypted_* targets leave the copy.
#   Externals are downloads and scripts are installers, so neither is applied;
#   the public-bootstrap CI job runs both. That required job also runs this
#   script, on the runner, for a diff whose home/ paths are all render-only.
#   After `chezmoi init`, `apply` and `verify` it runs the parts of `make doctor`
#   that judge the applied files and need no installed tool and no login:
#   `chezmoi doctor --no-network` and scripts/check-agent-runtime.py (its GitHub
#   login line stays a warning). The rest of `make doctor` stays out:
#   scripts/check-tools.sh and the omp asset checks require mise, uv, gh and omp,
#   which only the skipped installers put on a host, and scripts/check-sleep.sh
#   reads the host's power setting, which no apply changes. Every step's result is
#   printed, then one summary line.
# @arg $1 string `--system`
# @arg $2 string `client` or `server`
# @option --chezmoi <path> The chezmoi binary (default: `chezmoi` on PATH).
# @exitcode 0 Every step passed.
# @exitcode 1 A step failed.
# @exitcode 2 A usage error, or this is not a CI runner.

set -Eeuo pipefail

# dirname is captured on its own line: inside the cd its status would be lost.
script_dir="$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" || {
    echo "apply-check: dirname failed on ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}; the repository root is unknown" >&2
    exit 2
}
repo_root="$(cd "${script_dir}/.." && pwd)" || exit 2
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh
source "${script_dir}/lib/ci-runner.sh"

system=""
chezmoi_bin=chezmoi
while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
    --system)
        system="${2:-}"
        shift 2 || shift
        ;;
    --chezmoi)
        chezmoi_bin="${2:-}"
        shift 2 || shift
        ;;
    *)
        echo "apply-check: unknown argument: $1 (usage: apply-check.sh --system client|server [--chezmoi PATH])" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
    esac
done
case "${system}" in
client | server) ;;
*)
    echo "apply-check: --system must be client or server (got '${system}')" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
if ! is_ci_runner; then
    echo "apply-check: refusing to run outside a CI runner (scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh); run make apply-check, which starts a disposable container" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if ! chezmoi_path="$(command -v "${chezmoi_bin}")"; then
    echo "apply-check: chezmoi not found: ${chezmoi_bin}" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if ! chezmoi_dir="$(dirname -- "${chezmoi_path}")"; then
    echo "apply-check: dirname failed on ${chezmoi_path}" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if ! scratch="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP}/apply-check.XXXXXX")"; then
    echo "apply-check: cannot create a scratch directory under ${RUNNER_TEMP}" >&2
    exit 2
fi
trap 'rm -rf "${scratch}"' EXIT
# The physical path: check-agent-runtime.py resolves its own location, and on macOS /tmp and /var are symlinks, so
# a Codex project trust written for the unresolved path would read as drift.
scratch="$(cd "${scratch}" && pwd -P)" || exit 2

apply_home="${scratch}/home"
# The copy keeps the clone's layout: chezmoi reads .chezmoiroot, so the working tree is apply_tree and the source
# dir apply_tree/home, the paths the Codex config's project trust and check-agent-runtime.py derive from.
apply_tree="${scratch}/tree"
apply_source="${apply_tree}/home"
apply_config="${apply_home}/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.yaml"
mkdir -p "${apply_tree}" "${apply_home}/.config/chezmoi"
cp -R "${repo_root}/.chezmoiroot" "${repo_root}/home" "${repo_root}/scripts" "${apply_tree}/"
rm -f "${apply_source}/.chezmoiexternal.yaml.tmpl"
rm -rf "${apply_source}/.chezmoitemplates/chezmoiexternal.d"
find "${apply_source}" -type f -name 'encrypted_*' -exec rm -f {} +
printf 'sourceDir: "%s"\ndata:\n  email: "ci@example.invalid"\n  system: "%s"\n' \
    "${apply_tree}" "${system}" > "${apply_config}"
printf 'home-sentinel\n' | tee "${scratch}/unmanaged-sentinel" > "${apply_home}/unmanaged-sentinel"

# Everything below reads only the scratch HOME: no inherited XDG or gh directory can point a check at the
# caller's own config, and REPAIR=1 can never turn check-agent-runtime.py into a writer.
unset XDG_CONFIG_HOME XDG_DATA_HOME XDG_STATE_HOME XDG_CACHE_HOME GH_CONFIG_DIR REPAIR
export HOME="${apply_home}"
# check-agent-runtime.py and chezmoi doctor call chezmoi by name.
export PATH="${chezmoi_dir}:${PATH}"
chezmoi=(
    "${chezmoi_path}" --source "${apply_tree}" --destination "${apply_home}"
    --config "${apply_config}" --no-tty
)

results=()
failed=0

#
# @description Run one step from the copied tree, print its result and record it for the summary.
# @arg $1 string The step's name in the summary.
# @arg $@ string The command.
# @exitcode 0 The step passed.
# @exitcode 1 The step failed.
#
function step() {
    local name="$1" status=0
    shift
    printf '\n==> apply-check %s: %s\n' "${system}" "${name}"
    (cd "${apply_tree}" && "$@") || status=$?
    if [ "${status}" -eq 0 ]; then
        results+=("${name}=passed")
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'apply-check %s: %s failed with exit %d\n' "${system}" "${name}" "${status}" >&2
    results+=("${name}=failed")
    failed=1
    return 1
}

# init regenerates the config from home/.chezmoi.yaml.tmpl, as setup.sh's init does. A later step means
# nothing after a failed init or apply, so those two stop the run.
if step init "${chezmoi[@]}" init &&
    step apply "${chezmoi[@]}" --refresh-externals=never apply --exclude=scripts,externals; then
    # verify exits non-zero when any managed target differs from the source after the apply.
    step verify "${chezmoi[@]}" --refresh-externals=never verify --exclude=scripts,externals || true
    # The apply left the unmanaged file alone and wrote the system's shell rc.
    step unmanaged-file cmp "${scratch}/unmanaged-sentinel" "${apply_home}/unmanaged-sentinel" || true
    if [ "${system}" = client ]; then
        step shell-rc test -e "${apply_home}/.zshrc" || true
    else
        step shell-rc test -e "${apply_home}/.bashrc" || true
    fi
    step chezmoi-doctor "${chezmoi[@]}" doctor --no-network || true
    step agent-runtime scripts/check-agent-runtime.py || true
fi

printf '\napply-check summary (%s): %s\n' "${system}" "${results[*]}"
exit "${failed}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file check-sleep.sh
# @brief Fail when this Mac may sleep: `pmset -g` must report `SleepDisabled 1`.
# @description
#   An orchestrator Mac that sleeps overnight stalls every seat, so `make doctor`
#   runs this check after the tools check. On macOS it reads `pmset -g` and
#   requires the `SleepDisabled` line to hold `1`; on any other OS it only says
#   the check is skipped. It runs nothing else and changes no setting: the
#   operator's `sudo pmset -a disablesleep 1` does that.
# @exitcode 0 SleepDisabled is 1, or the OS is not macOS.
# @exitcode 1 SleepDisabled is not 1, its line is missing, pmset -g failed, or uname -s failed.

set -Eeuo pipefail

if ! kernel="$(uname -s)"; then
    echo "sleep check: uname -s failed; cannot tell whether this host is macOS" >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [[ "${kernel}" != Darwin ]]; then
    echo "sleep check: skipped (not macOS)"
    exit 0
fi

if ! output="$(pmset -g 2>&1)"; then
    echo "sleep check: pmset -g failed: ${output}" >&2
    exit 1
fi

value="$(printf '%s\n' "${output}" | awk '$1 == "SleepDisabled" { print $2; exit }')"
if [[ -z ${value} ]]; then
    echo "sleep check: pmset -g reports no SleepDisabled line; run: sudo pmset -a disablesleep 1" >&2
    exit 1
fi
if [[ ${value} != 1 ]]; then
    echo "sleep check: SleepDisabled is ${value}; run: sudo pmset -a disablesleep 1" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "sleep check: SleepDisabled is 1"

<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file scripts/check-tools.sh
# @brief Print a read-only health summary for managed dotfiles tools.
# @description
#   Reports the availability and versions of the commands that participate in
#   the dotfiles lifecycle. This script does not install, upgrade, or modify
#   tools; use `scripts/upgrade-tools.sh` for explicit upgrades.

set -Eeuo pipefail

required_failures=0
optional_warnings=0

#
# @description Print a section heading.
# @arg $1 string Heading text.
#
function section() {
    printf '\n==> %s\n' "$1"
}

#
# @description Require a command and a successful version command.
# @arg $1 string Command name.
# @arg $@ string Optional version command arguments.
#
function check_command() {
    local command_name="$1" command_path
    shift || true

    if ! command_path="$(command -v "${command_name}" 2> /dev/null)"; then
        printf 'required missing: %s\n' "${command_name}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi

    printf 'found:   %s -> %s\n' "${command_name}" "${command_path}"

    local output first_line

    if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
        if ! output="$("${command_name}" "$@" 2>&1)"; then
            printf 'required failed: %s %s\n' "${command_name}" "$*" >&2
            ((required_failures += 1))
            return 0
        fi
    else
        if ! output="$("${command_name}" --version 2>&1)"; then
            printf 'required failed: %s --version\n' "${command_name}" >&2
            ((required_failures += 1))
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    IFS= read -r first_line <<< "${output}"
    printf '%s\n' "${first_line}"
}

#
# @description Run a required read-only doctor command when its tool is available.
# @arg $1 string Command name.
# @arg $@ string Doctor command arguments.
#
function run_required_doctor() {
    local command_name="$1"
    shift || true

    if command -v "${command_name}" > /dev/null 2>&1 && ! "${command_name}" "$@"; then
        printf 'required failed: %s %s\n' "${command_name}" "$*" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
    fi
}

#
# @description Record an optional warning.
# @arg $1 string Warning text.
#
function warn_optional() {
    printf 'optional warning: %s\n' "$1" >&2
    ((optional_warnings += 1))
}

#
# @description Return success when the rendered chezmoi config enables the private layer.
#   Defaults to enabled when chezmoi/jq are unavailable or the config predates the
#   usePrivate key, matching the owner's existing machines' behavior.
#
function private_layer_enabled() {
    local use_private

    if ! command -v chezmoi > /dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v jq > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0
    fi

    use_private="$(chezmoi data 2> /dev/null | jq -r '.usePrivate' 2> /dev/null)"
    [ "${use_private}" != "false" ]
}

#
# @description Print the configured private chezmoi source state.
#
function check_private_chezmoi() {
    local private_source="${HOME%/}/.local/share/chezmoi-private"
    local private_config="${HOME%/}/.config/chezmoi-private/chezmoi.yaml"

    if ! private_layer_enabled; then
        printf 'not applicable: private layer (usePrivate=false)\n'
        return 0
    fi

    if [ -d "${private_source}" ]; then
        printf 'found:   private source -> %s\n' "${private_source}"
        if [ -f "${private_config}" ]; then
            printf 'found:   private config -> %s\n' "${private_config}"
        else
            warn_optional "private config is missing: ${private_config}"
        fi
    else
        warn_optional "private source is missing: ${private_source}"
        if [ ! -f "${private_config}" ]; then
            warn_optional "private config is missing: ${private_config}"
        fi
    fi
}

#
# @description Require Homebrew on macOS and skip it on other platforms.
#
function check_homebrew() {
    local kernel
    if ! kernel="$(uname)"; then
        printf 'required failed: uname; cannot tell whether Homebrew applies\n' >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${kernel}" != "Darwin" ]; then
        printf 'not applicable: Homebrew (non-Darwin)\n'
        return 0
    fi

    check_command brew --version
}

#
# @description Check the key git signs commits with. The managed git config renders
#   commit.gpgsign only when ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub exists at apply time, so signing that is off
#   is an optional notice. With commit.gpgsign=true (now only through a hand edit) a missing
#   user.signingkey file makes every commit fail, so it is a required failure; a git config
#   read that fails (other than "unset") is one too.
#
function check_git_signing_key() {
    local gpgsign key status=0

    gpgsign="$(git config --get --type=bool commit.gpgsign 2> /dev/null)" || status=$?
    if [ "${status}" -eq 1 ]; then
        warn_optional "commit signing is off (no signing key when the git config was applied); run provision-machine-key, register the key, then chezmoi apply"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${status}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${gpgsign}" != "true" ]; then
        printf 'not applicable: commit signing key (commit.gpgsign is false)\n'
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        printf 'required failed: git config --get commit.gpgsign (exit %d)\n' "${status}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi

    status=0
    key="$(git config --get user.signingkey 2> /dev/null)" || status=$?
    if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        printf 'required failed: commit.gpgsign is true but user.signingkey cannot be read (exit %d); run provision-machine-key\n' "${status}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    # A literal key ("key::ssh-ed25519 ...") needs no file.
    if [[ "${key}" == key::* ]]; then
        printf 'found:   commit signing key (literal user.signingkey)\n'
        return 0
    fi
    # git expands a leading ~/ in user.signingkey; do the same.
    key="${key/#\~\//${HOME%/}/}"
    if [ -f "${key}" ]; then
        printf 'found:   commit signing key -> %s\n' "${key}"
    else
        printf 'required missing: commit signing key %s (commit.gpgsign=true, so commits fail); run provision-machine-key and register the key with GitHub\n' "${key}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
    fi
}

#
# @description Report the managed Crit CLI's pinned version and origin, when installed.
#   Installed by ensure_crit_cli in scripts/update-agent-assets.sh from the pinned
#   GitHub release on every OS; not required, so a missing binary is not a failure.
#
function check_crit_cli() {
    local target="${HOME%/}/.local/bin/crit"

    if [ ! -x "${target}" ]; then
        printf 'not applicable: Crit CLI (not installed)\n'
        return 0
    fi

    printf 'found:   crit -> %s (pinned release)\n' "${target}"
    "${target}" --version || warn_optional "crit --version failed; the managed binary may be corrupt (try REPAIR=1 make doctor)"
}

#
# @description Report omp's installed version beside its manifest pin.
#
function check_omp() {
    local target="${HOME%/}/.local/bin/omp"
    if [ ! -x "${target}" ]; then
        warn_optional "omp not installed; run make update"
        return 0
    fi
    local pin
    pin="$(awk -F'"' '/^OMP_PIN_VERSION=/ { print $2; exit }' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/lib/installer-pins.sh" 2> /dev/null || true)"
    printf 'found:   omp -> %s (pin %s)\n' "${target}" "${pin:-unknown}"
    "${target}" --version || warn_optional "omp --version failed; run make update"
}

#
# @description Report hcom's installed version beside its manifest pin.
#
function check_hcom() {
    local target="${HOME%/}/.local/bin/hcom"
    if [ ! -x "${target}" ]; then
        warn_optional "hcom not installed; run make update"
        return 0
    fi
    local pin
    pin="$(awk -F'"' '/^HCOM_PIN_VERSION=/ { print $2; exit }' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/lib/installer-pins.sh" 2> /dev/null || true)"
    printf 'found:   hcom -> %s (pin %s)\n' "${target}" "${pin:-unknown}"
    "${target}" --version || warn_optional "hcom --version failed; run make update"
}

#
# @description Report the installed srt (`@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`, the omp seat boundary, regime-cutover U85)
#   beside its mise pin (U141). srt is resolved as hcom-seat resolves it (`mise which srt`, else PATH). The pin is the
#   exact version of the applied mise config (`~/.config/mise/config.toml`); when that file is absent or still tracks
#   `latest` (the host has not run `make update` since the pin landed), the checkout's `home/dot_mise/config.toml`
#   beside this script is read instead. A pin that cannot be read, a `--version` that fails or prints nothing, and a
#   version whose first token differs from the pin are required failures (a failed read is never a pass); an absent
#   srt is an optional warning.
#
function check_srt() {
    local target pin='' config output first_line version
    if ! target="$(mise which srt 2> /dev/null)" || [ -z "${target}" ]; then
        target="$(command -v srt 2> /dev/null || true)"
    fi
    if [ -z "${target}" ] || [ ! -x "${target}" ]; then
        warn_optional "srt not installed; run make update"
        return 0
    fi
    for config in "${HOME%/}/.config/mise/config.toml" "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/../home/dot_mise/config.toml"; do
        [ -r "${config}" ] || continue
        pin="$(awk -F'"' '/^"npm:@anthropic-ai\/sandbox-runtime" = "/ { print $4; exit }' "${config}")" || pin=''
        if [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+$ ]]; then break; fi
        pin=''
    done
    if [ -z "${pin}" ]; then
        printf 'required failed: srt -> %s; no exact sandbox-runtime pin in ~/.config/mise/config.toml or the checkout\n' "${target}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'found:   srt -> %s (pin %s)\n' "${target}" "${pin}"
    if ! output="$("${target}" --version 2> /dev/null)" || [ -z "${output}" ]; then
        printf 'required failed: srt --version printed no version (pin %s); run make update\n' "${pin}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    IFS= read -r first_line <<< "${output}"
    printf '%s\n' "${first_line}"
    version="${first_line%% *}"
    if [ "${version}" != "${pin}" ]; then
        printf 'required failed: srt %s differs from the pin %s; run make update\n' "${version}" "${pin}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
    fi
}

#
# @description Report Zed on Ubuntu clients. run_after_05-client-install-zed installs it only with an
#   authenticated gh, because a GitHub release attestation is the only verification Zed publishes.
#
function check_zed() {
    local target="${HOME%/}/.local/bin/zed" system kernel
    system="$(chezmoi execute-template '{{ .system }}' 2> /dev/null || true)"
    if ! kernel="$(uname -s)"; then
        printf 'required failed: uname -s; cannot tell whether Zed applies\n' >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${kernel}" != Linux ] || [ "${system}" != client ]; then
        printf 'not applicable: Zed (installed on Ubuntu clients only)\n'
        return 0
    fi
    if [ ! -x "${target}" ]; then
        warn_optional "zed not installed: run make gh-auth, then make update; its release attestation cannot be verified without an authenticated gh"
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'found:   zed -> %s\n' "${target}"
    "${target}" --version || warn_optional "zed --version failed; the install may be corrupt"
}

#
# @description Verify bwrap can create user namespaces when AppArmor restricts them.
#   Sandboxed Codex runs exec /usr/bin/bwrap, which needs the bwrap-userns profile
#   installed by install/ubuntu/common/apparmor_userns.sh. Loaded profiles are
#   root-only to list, so an unprivileged bwrap probe is the effective check.
#
function check_apparmor_userns() {
    local restrict="${APPARMOR_USERNS_SYSCTL:-/proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns}"
    local bwrap="${APPARMOR_USERNS_BWRAP:-/usr/bin/bwrap}"
    local profile="${APPARMOR_USERNS_PROFILE_TARGET:-/etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns}"
    local restricted=""

    # A host without the sysctl has no restriction; one that exists but cannot be read decides nothing.
    if [ -e "${restrict}" ] && ! restricted="$(cat "${restrict}")"; then
        printf 'required failed: cannot read %s; the AppArmor userns restriction is unknown\n' "${restrict}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${restricted}" != "1" ]; then
        printf 'not applicable: AppArmor userns restriction (not enabled)\n'
        return 0
    fi
    if ! command -v codex > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        warn_optional "codex is not installed; skipped the bwrap user-namespace probe"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ ! -x "${bwrap}" ]; then
        printf 'required failed: %s is missing; sandboxed codex runs need it under the AppArmor userns restriction (install the bubblewrap package)\n' "${bwrap}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    if "${bwrap}" --ro-bind / / true > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        printf 'found:   bwrap user namespaces allowed -> %s\n' "${bwrap}"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -f "${profile}" ]; then
        printf 'required failed: bwrap user-namespace probe; %s exists but is not effective (sudo apparmor_parser -r %s)\n' "${profile}" "${profile}" >&2
    else
        printf 'required failed: bwrap user-namespace probe; AppArmor profile %s is missing, so sandboxed codex runs fail (sudo -v && bash install/ubuntu/common/apparmor_userns.sh)\n' "${profile}" >&2
    fi
    ((required_failures += 1))
}

#
# @description Print the current GitHub CLI extension state when gh is installed.
#
function check_gh_extensions() {
    if command -v gh > /dev/null 2>&1 && ! gh extension list; then
        warn_optional "unable to list installed GitHub CLI extensions"
    fi
}

#
# @description Report the Linux prerequisites of the Claude Code Bash sandbox:
#   bwrap and socat on PATH. check_apparmor_userns covers the user-namespace
#   side, so this check has no sysctl or profile logic.
#
function check_claude_sandbox() {
    local command_name command_path kernel

    if ! kernel="$(uname)"; then
        printf 'required failed: uname; cannot tell whether the Claude Code sandbox prerequisites apply\n' >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${kernel}" != "Linux" ]; then
        printf 'not applicable: Claude Code sandbox prerequisites (non-Linux; macOS uses Seatbelt)\n'
        return 0
    fi

    for command_name in bwrap socat; do
        if command_path="$(command -v "${command_name}" 2> /dev/null)"; then
            printf 'found:   %s -> %s\n' "${command_name}" "${command_path}"
        else
            warn_optional "Claude Code sandbox prerequisite is missing: ${command_name} (run make update)"
        fi
    done
}

#
# @description The login group of a seat profile (regime-cutover U498, U498d):
#   the one table `login_group_of_role` of `scripts/orchestrator/hcom-seat` and
#   `scripts/orchestrator/seat-login-preflight`, copied here as the same text
#   (`tests/unit/test_runtime_health.py` holds the copy equal to the lever's),
#   so the doctor names a group's login step from the table and not from a
#   guess: the worker, orchestrator and audit roles are each their own group,
#   the dsh and router roles the `router` group (the dsh gateway child is the
#   Router's). Any other name is no role of the table (status 1, nothing
#   printed).
# @arg $1 string The role (a seat profile's name).
# @stdout The group.
# @exitcode 1 The role is not in the table.
#
function login_group_of_role() {
    case $1 in
    worker) printf 'worker\n' ;;
    orchestrator) printf 'orchestrator\n' ;;
    audit) printf 'audit\n' ;;
    dsh | router) printf 'router\n' ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

#
# @description Set `login_step` to the operator's step for an absent login
#   line of `seat-login-preflight --check` (regime-cutover U498d; verdict
#   U498-8f2cca8c P2 `:413`). The line is `<profile> <route>: <state>`
#   (the pre-flight's `profile_line`), so the profile is its first word and
#   the group the table's (login_group_of_role). The pre-flight's profile
#   mode accepts the seat profiles alone (`seat_profiles` there, the values
#   of `omp.roles`: orchestrator, worker, audit; copied here as the same
#   text), so for those the step is `seat-login-preflight <profile>`, which
#   prints the group's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir> claude auth login` or runs
#   the SIWC login. The dsh profile's group `router` has no profile mode
#   (`seat-login-preflight dsh` and `seat-login-preflight router` exit 2 as
#   unknown profiles), so its step is `claude auth login` under the group's
#   directory, the one this line names and `hcom-seat router --dry-run`
#   prints as CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (every group of the table is a role of
#   hcom-seat). A profile outside the table (a `no route` overlay that is no
#   seat) keeps the general sentence.
# @arg $1 string The `--check` line.
# @set login_step The sentence the warning carries in parentheses.
#
function login_step_of() {
    local profile="${1%% *}" group mode
    local -a seat_profiles=(orchestrator worker audit)
    login_step="log in on this host, once per login group: seat-login-preflight <profile> prints the group's command, docs/remote-host-logins.md"
    group="$(login_group_of_role "${profile}")" || return 0
    for mode in "${seat_profiles[@]}"; do
        if [ "${profile}" = "${mode}" ]; then
            login_step="log in on this host, once per login group: seat-login-preflight ${profile} prints the ${group} group's command, docs/remote-host-logins.md"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    login_step="log in on this host, once per login group: the ${profile} profile is the ${group} group, which has no seat-login-preflight profile mode; run claude auth login with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to the directory this line names (hcom-seat ${group} --dry-run prints it; BROWSER=regime-open-url first on a remote host), docs/remote-host-logins.md"
}

#
# @description Report each omp seat profile's login on this host through
#   `scripts/orchestrator/seat-login-preflight --check` (regime-cutover U37):
#   presence and mtimes only, never a token. The Claude lines name each
#   profile's login group directory `<seats-root>/.state/claude-<group>`
#   (U498: one line per deployed profile, so one per running group). An
#   absent login is an optional warning naming the group's step
#   (login_step_of, U498d), since a login is per host and per group and the
#   operator's step; an unreadable login record is a required failure, never
#   read as absent.
#
function check_seat_logins() {
    local lever="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/orchestrator/seat-login-preflight"
    local output line login_step status=0

    if [ ! -x "${lever}" ]; then
        warn_optional "seat login check skipped: ${lever} is missing"
        return 0
    fi
    output="$("${lever}" --check 2>&1)" || status=$?
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        case "${line}" in
        '') ;;
        'not applicable:'*) printf '%s\n' "${line}" ;;
        # The lever's own refusal or failed producer (pin, uname), never a profile line.
        'seat-login-preflight:'*) printf 'required failed: %s\n' "${line}" >&2 ;;
        *': unreadable'*) printf 'required failed: seat login %s\n' "${line}" >&2 ;;
        *': absent'* | *': no route'* | *': not a seat login route'*)
            login_step_of "${line}"
            warn_optional "seat login ${line} (${login_step})"
            ;;
        *) printf 'found:   seat login %s\n' "${line}" ;;
        esac
    done <<< "${output}"
    if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        printf 'required failed: seat-login-preflight --check exited %d\n' "${status}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
    fi
}

#
# @description Report the class of the Router's GitHub token through the checkout's
#   `scripts/orchestrator/router-gh api -i user` (regime-cutover U490), one call bounded by
#   perl's alarm (`timeout` is not on every host) to `DOCTOR_ROUTER_TIMEOUT` seconds (an
#   integer of 1 to 600; else 30), with the response headers read for `X-Oauth-Scopes` alone.
#   Five cases, decided by router-gh's exit status and, once gh has answered, by the HTTP status
#   line alone (U490e, U490f; the doctor holds no path test of its own: round 4's `[ ! -e ]` read
#   a login directory under an unreadable parent as absent where router-gh refuses `cannot resolve
#   the credential root`, verdict U490-e90feefa P1):
#   (a) router-gh exits 3, its "not yet" code (the credential root, its gh directory or its
#       hosts.yml absent, or hosts.yml naming no active login for github.com): the operator's
#       step (docs/engagement-handout.md step 2), an optional warning quoting router-gh's one
#       stderr line; gh itself is not run;
#   (b) router-gh exits 2, every other refusal (a DSH_HOME that is not a real, searchable
#       directory of this user, a link in the chain, a wrong owner or mode, a root that cannot be
#       resolved, several oauth_token rows, a token outside the grammar): a required failure
#       quoting router-gh's one stderr line (a broken root the operator must repair, never
#       "pending"; rounds 1 to 3 read every refusal as the pending step and exited 0, verdict
#       U490-f441420d P1);
#   (c) any other non-zero exit whose output's first line is an HTTP status line of class 4xx or
#       5xx (`^HTTP/[0-9.]+ [45][0-9][0-9]`; `gh api -i` prints the status line before the body
#       whatever the class and exits 1 on an error answer): GitHub answered and rejected the token
#       (revoked, expired or never valid), a required failure `GitHub answered <status line>` with
#       the remedy (U490f; round 5 read every exit of gh's own as "unreadable", so a revoked token
#       passed the gate as an optional warning, verdict U490-f6175c44 P1);
#   (d) any other non-zero exit with no HTTP status line in front (the alarm included, the
#       transport's own failure text for a host never reached), or an exit 0 without a 2xx status
#       line and a login: an optional warning `unreadable` (an offline or stalled host);
#   (e) a 2xx answer: no `X-Oauth-Scopes` header is a fine-grained token, whose permissions this
#       check cannot read and which cannot write here (GitHub's fine-grained tokens cannot
#       contribute to a repository where the account is a collaborator, and the Router's account
#       is one by the kit's design, M-25), a required failure (U490c); a header is a classic token,
#       found when its list holds `repo` or `public_repo`, else a required failure. Both failures
#       ask for the classic token of the handout's step 2 (`repo` for the writes, `read:org` and
#       `gist` for `gh auth login --with-token`, `notifications` for the poll; U490b), since no
#       other token lets the Router write (measured 2026-11-12: a `notifications` token read the
#       stream and every write failed `HTTP 403`).
#   The decision reads router-gh's exit status and gh's HTTP status line, never router-gh's text
#   and no path; the login is read from the body's `login` key; no token is printed.
#
function check_router_token() {
    local lever="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/orchestrator/router-gh"
    local root="${DSH_HOME:-${HOME%/}/.dsh}/router-credentials/gh"
    local output line status=0 in_headers=1 first_line='' body='' login='' scopes='' scopes_seen=0
    local scope writes=0 remedy bound=30
    local -a scope_list=()
    remedy="place the classic token of docs/engagement-handout.md step 2 (scopes repo, read:org, gist, notifications; a fine-grained token cannot write to a repository where the account is a collaborator) under ${root}"

    if [ ! -x "${lever}" ]; then
        warn_optional "router token check skipped: ${lever} is missing"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "${DOCTOR_ROUTER_TIMEOUT:-}" =~ ^[0-9]{1,3}$ ]] && [ "${DOCTOR_ROUTER_TIMEOUT}" -ge 1 ] && [ "${DOCTOR_ROUTER_TIMEOUT}" -le 600 ]; then
        bound="${DOCTOR_ROUTER_TIMEOUT}"
    fi
    output="$(perl -e 'my $bound = shift; alarm $bound; exec @ARGV or die "exec router-gh: $!\n"' "${bound}" "${lever}" api -i user 2>&1)" || status=$?
    if [ "${status}" -eq 3 ]; then
        IFS= read -r first_line <<< "${output}"
        warn_optional "router token: ${first_line}"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${status}" -eq 2 ]; then
        IFS= read -r first_line <<< "${output}"
        printf 'required failed: router token: %s\n' "${first_line}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        IFS= read -r first_line <<< "${output}"
        first_line="${first_line%$'\r'}"
        if [[ "${first_line}" =~ ^HTTP/[0-9.]+\ [45][0-9][0-9] ]]; then
            printf 'required failed: router token: GitHub answered %s (the token is rejected or expired; %s)\n' \
                "${first_line}" "${remedy}" >&2
            ((required_failures += 1))
            return 0
        fi
        warn_optional "router token: unreadable (router-gh api -i user exited ${status}: ${first_line})"
        return 0
    fi
    # `gh api -i` prints the status line, each header with CRLF, a blank line, then the raw body.
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line="${line%$'\r'}"
        if [ "${in_headers}" -eq 0 ]; then
            body="${body}${line}"
        elif [ -z "${first_line}" ]; then
            first_line="${line}"
        elif [ -z "${line}" ]; then
            in_headers=0
        elif [[ "${line}" =~ ^[Xx]-[Oo][Aa][Uu][Tt][Hh]-[Ss][Cc][Oo][Pp][Ee][Ss]:[[:space:]]*(.*)$ ]]; then
            scopes="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            scopes_seen=1
        fi
    done <<< "${output}"
    if [[ ! "${first_line}" =~ ^HTTP/[0-9.]+\ 2[0-9][0-9] ]] || [[ ! "${body}" =~ \"login\":[[:space:]]*\"([A-Za-z0-9-]+)\" ]]; then
        warn_optional "router token: unreadable (router-gh api -i user answered without a 2xx status line and a login)"
        return 0
    fi
    login="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    if [ "${scopes_seen}" -eq 0 ]; then
        printf "required failed: router token %s: fine-grained (no X-Oauth-Scopes header), which cannot write here (GitHub's fine-grained tokens cannot contribute to a repository where the account is a collaborator, and the Router's account is one by design); %s\n" \
            "${login}" "${remedy}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
        return 0
    fi
    IFS=', ' read -r -a scope_list <<< "${scopes}"
    for scope in ${scope_list[@]+"${scope_list[@]}"}; do
        case "${scope}" in
        repo | public_repo) writes=1 ;;
        esac
    done
    if [ "${writes}" -eq 1 ]; then
        printf 'found:   router token %s: classic, scopes %s\n' "${login}" "${scopes}"
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'required failed: router token %s: classic token with scopes %s, none of which lets the Router write (the acknowledgement, a pushed ref, a pull request); %s\n' \
        "${login}" "${scopes:-<none>}" "${remedy}" >&2
    ((required_failures += 1))
}

#
# @description Run the read-only dotfiles health checks.
#
function main() {
    section "Core commands"
    check_command git --version
    check_command chezmoi --version
    check_command mise --version
    check_command uv --version
    check_command gh --version

    section "Chezmoi"
    run_required_doctor chezmoi doctor
    check_private_chezmoi

    section "Mise"
    run_required_doctor mise doctor
    run_required_doctor mise ls --current

    section "Homebrew"
    check_homebrew

    section "Crit CLI"
    check_crit_cli

    section "Agent tools"
    check_omp
    check_hcom
    check_srt

    section "Seat logins"
    check_seat_logins
    check_router_token

    section "Zed"
    check_zed

    section "SSH"
    check_git_signing_key

    section "AppArmor"
    check_apparmor_userns

    section "Claude Code sandbox"
    check_claude_sandbox

    section "GitHub CLI extensions"
    check_gh_extensions

    printf '\nTool check summary: required failures: %d; optional warnings: %d\n' \
        "${required_failures}" "${optional_warnings}"
    [ "${required_failures}" -eq 0 ]
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main "$@"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file scripts/deploy-kit.sh
# @brief Apply the kit's own chezmoi targets by name, refuse a locally edited one, and do nothing else.
# @description
#   The coordinator's deploy of a merged unit (regime-cutover U276; round 2 U276b, round 3 U276c, round 4 U276d).
#   `make update` is the operator's whole-home step: `chezmoi apply` over every managed target, the tool upgrades,
#   the asset updater and the herdr reload. This script is the chezmoi apply of the managed targets under the kit's
#   own roots and nothing more; the table below is the boundary, and everything else, the pinned asset refreshes
#   included, is left to `make update` and the asset updater under their own contracts:
#
#     root            | reason        | source
#     ~/.local/bin    | levers        | home/dot_local/bin (the orchestrator levers, the seat launcher)
#     ~/.agents       | assets        | home/dot_agents (skills, rules, omp profiles and policies, regime files)
#     ~/.dsh          | profiles      | home/dot_dsh (the DSH profiles and plugins)
#     ~/.omp/profiles | seat profiles | home/dot_omp/private_profiles (the seats' generated claude-bridge.json; U515)
#
#   Each root is read physically before anything else (`cd -P`, `pwd -P`): a root that is missing, is a symbolic
#   link, or whose physical path is not the physical HOME joined with its name (a link on its path) refuses the run
#   with the path, since an apply through a link writes outside the boundary. The roots are read again after the
#   status read, and a root whose physical path changed between the two reads refuses: a root replaced during the
#   run would otherwise be applied through.
#
#   The operator's targets, never touched here: `~/.codex`, `~/.claude`, the shell rc files, `~/.config`,
#   `~/.omp/agent`, `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, `~/.local/share`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.gnupg`, and the run_ scripts of the
#   source, which a named apply does not run.
#
#   Steps, every producer status-checked so a failed read refuses before anything is applied (a failed read is
#   never an empty read; the message names the producer):
#   1. The physical root check above.
#   2. `chezmoi managed --path-style absolute --refresh-externals=never -- <roots>`, filtered to the roots and the
#      roots themselves by the table: the managed kit set. None found is a refusal.
#   3. `chezmoi status --path-style absolute --refresh-externals=never -- <roots>`, filtered the same way, then the
#      root re-read of step 1. A row whose second column is not blank is pending: `chezmoi apply` would change that
#      target. (One status read is the per-target oracle: it compares every target against the source as `chezmoi
#      verify` does, and a verify call per target is one chezmoi start each; verify runs once below, over the
#      applied names.) The listings are split in the shell, not through a here-string: bash backs a here-string with
#      a temporary file, and a redirection that fails there reads as an empty listing.
#   4. A row on a root itself is refused unless it is a plain pending change to the directory entry (first column
#      blank, second not `D`): `MM` on a root is the signature of a root replaced between the reads (chezmoi sees a
#      link where it wrote a directory), and a source that removes a root makes the table stale.
#   5. Every pending name must be a member of the managed kit set of step 2; one that is not (a target that
#      appeared between the two reads, or a row the status read spelled otherwise) is refused by name, since the
#      apply would then act on a name the managed listing never vouched for.
#   6. A pending row whose first column is not blank is refused: the target's content is not what chezmoi last
#      wrote, so an apply would drop an edit the source does not have (`MM` in `chezmoi status`, two-sided drift).
#      The refused rows are printed and nothing is applied.
#   7. `chezmoi apply --verbose --recursive=false` of the pending targets by name. Without `--recursive=false` a
#      pending directory is applied with everything under it, a child added after the status read included, and
#      that child was never in the managed listing; with it, the directory entry alone is applied, and every pending
#      child is in the set as its own row.
#   8. The applied set verified by row kind. A `D` row (the source retired the target) is verified by its absence:
#      `chezmoi verify` on a name the source no longer manages answers `not managed`, which is the retirement
#      succeeding, not a failure. Every other row is verified by one `chezmoi verify --recursive=false` over the
#      names that `chezmoi managed`, read once more after the apply, still lists; a non-`D` name it no longer lists
#      is refused, since its verified state is unknown.
#   9. The applied list. A second run finds nothing pending and exits 0.
#   `--refresh-externals=never`: chezmoi reads its whole source state, every external included, on each of these
#   commands, whatever targets are named; `never` serves a cached external whatever its age (the archives are
#   checksum-pinned, so age changes nothing), and only an external with no cache entry at all is fetched, by
#   chezmoi, as `make update`'s prefetch would.
# @option --dry-run Print the pending rows and the refusals; apply nothing. A refusal still exits 1, so a dry run
#   gives the verdict the real run would.
# @exitcode 0 The pending targets were applied and verified (or none was pending).
# @exitcode 1 A root is missing or a link, a root changed between the reads, a producer failed, no kit target is
#   managed, a row on a root is not a plain pending change, a pending name is not in the managed kit set, a pending
#   target is not what chezmoi last wrote, the apply or the verify failed, a retired target is still present.
# @exitcode 2 Usage.
# @example
#   ./scripts/deploy-kit.sh --dry-run

set -Eeuo pipefail

readonly KIT_ROOTS=("${HOME}/.local/bin" "${HOME}/.agents" "${HOME}/.dsh" "${HOME}/.omp/profiles")

dry_run=false
for argument in "$@"; do
    case ${argument} in
    --dry-run) dry_run=true ;;
    *)
        printf 'usage: %s [--dry-run]\n' "$0" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
    esac
done

#
# @description Whether a chezmoi target is one of the kit roots itself.
# @arg $1 path The target, as `chezmoi status --path-style absolute` prints it.
# @exitcode 0 A root of the table.
# @exitcode 1 Not a root.
#
function is_kit_root() {
    local target=$1 root
    for root in "${KIT_ROOTS[@]}"; do
        [[ ${target} != "${root}" ]] || return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are chezmoi's absolute target spellings (its destination directory joined with the managed path), the boundary table, not filesystem identities; the roots were read physically above
    done
    return 1
}

#
# @description Whether a chezmoi target is one of the kit roots or lies under one.
# @arg $1 path The target, as `chezmoi managed --path-style absolute` prints it.
# @exitcode 0 A root or under one.
# @exitcode 1 Not under one: the operator's.
#
function under_kit_root() {
    local target=$1 root
    for root in "${KIT_ROOTS[@]}"; do
        case ${target} in # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are chezmoi's absolute target spellings (its destination directory joined with the managed path), the boundary table, not filesystem identities; the roots were read physically above
        "${root}" | "${root}"/*) return 0 ;;
        esac
    done
    return 1
}

#
# @description Whether a target is a member of the managed kit set (the filtered `chezmoi managed` listing). A
#   linear scan: bash 3.2, the macOS default, has no associative arrays, and the pending set is small.
# @arg $1 path The target, as `chezmoi status --path-style absolute` prints it.
# @exitcode 0 A member.
# @exitcode 1 Not listed by `chezmoi managed` under the kit roots.
#
function in_kit_set() {
    local target=$1 member
    for member in "${kit_targets[@]}"; do
        [[ ${member} != "${target}" ]] || return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are chezmoi's absolute target spellings from the same destination directory
    done
    return 1
}

#
# @description Split a producer's captured output into ROWS, one line each, with string operations alone. A
#   `while read` over a here-string needs a temporary file, and a failure to make it read as an empty listing.
# @arg $1 string The output, as a command substitution returns it (no trailing newline).
# @set ROWS array The lines, empty ones included.
#
function split_lines() {
    local text=$1
    ROWS=()
    while [[ -n ${text} ]]; do
        ROWS+=("${text%%$'\n'*}")
        [[ ${text} == *$'\n'* ]] || break
        text=${text#*$'\n'}
    done
}

#
# @description Read the managed kit set: `chezmoi managed` over the roots, filtered to the roots by the table.
# @set kit_targets array The managed targets that are a kit root or lie under one.
# @exitcode 0 Read.
# @exitcode 1 `chezmoi managed` failed; kit_targets is unchanged and the caller names the consequence.
#
function read_kit_set() {
    local listing target
    listing="$(chezmoi managed --path-style absolute --refresh-externals=never -- "${KIT_ROOTS[@]}")" || return 1
    split_lines "${listing}"
    kit_targets=()
    for target in ${ROWS[@]+"${ROWS[@]}"}; do
        [[ -n ${target} ]] || continue
        if under_kit_root "${target}"; then
            kit_targets+=("${target}")
        fi
    done
}

#
# @description Print a kit root's physical path, or refuse: a root that is missing, is a symbolic link, cannot be
#   read physically, or whose physical path is not the physical HOME joined with its name (a link on its path) lets
#   an apply write outside the boundary.
# @arg $1 path The root, as the table spells it.
# @stdout The physical path (`cd -P`, `pwd -P`).
# @exitcode 0 A real directory at its own physical place.
# @exitcode 1 Refused; the message names the root and ends with `nothing applied`.
#
function root_physical_path() {
    local root=$1 physical
    if [[ -L ${root} ]]; then
        printf 'deploy-kit: the kit root %s is a symbolic link; an apply through it would write outside the kit roots, nothing applied.\n' "${root}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    if [[ ! -d ${root} ]]; then
        printf 'deploy-kit: the kit root %s is missing; the kit has not been bootstrapped here (make update creates it), nothing applied.\n' "${root}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    physical="$(cd -P -- "${root}" && pwd -P)" || {
        printf 'deploy-kit: the physical path of the kit root %s could not be read (pwd -P), nothing applied.\n' "${root}" >&2
        return 1
    }
    if [[ ${physical} != "${home_physical}/${root#"${HOME}/"}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P physical paths
        printf 'deploy-kit: the kit root %s resolves to %s, not %s; a link on its path would let an apply write outside the kit roots, nothing applied.\n' "${root}" "${physical}" "${home_physical}/${root#"${HOME}/"}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${physical}"
}

home_physical="$(cd -P -- "${HOME}" && pwd -P)" || {
    printf 'deploy-kit: the physical path of HOME %s could not be read (pwd -P); the kit roots are unknown, nothing applied.\n' "${HOME}" >&2
    exit 1
}
root_physicals=()
for root in "${KIT_ROOTS[@]}"; do
    root_physical="$(root_physical_path "${root}")" || exit 1
    root_physicals+=("${root_physical}")
done

read_kit_set || {
    printf 'deploy-kit: chezmoi managed failed; the kit targets are unknown, nothing applied.\n' >&2
    exit 1
}
printf 'deploy-kit: kit roots: %s\n' "${KIT_ROOTS[*]}"
printf 'deploy-kit: managed kit targets: %d\n' "${#kit_targets[@]}"
if ((${#kit_targets[@]} == 0)); then
    printf 'deploy-kit: chezmoi manages no target under the kit roots; the source or the root table is wrong, nothing applied.\n' >&2
    exit 1
fi

if ! status_listing="$(chezmoi status --path-style absolute --refresh-externals=never -- "${KIT_ROOTS[@]}")"; then
    printf 'deploy-kit: chezmoi status failed; the drift of the kit targets is unknown, nothing applied.\n' >&2
    exit 1
fi
for index in "${!KIT_ROOTS[@]}"; do
    root_physical="$(root_physical_path "${KIT_ROOTS[index]}")" || {
        printf 'deploy-kit: the kit root %s changed between the managed read and the status read, nothing applied.\n' "${KIT_ROOTS[index]}" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    if [[ ${root_physical} != "${root_physicals[index]}" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P physical paths of the same root, read before and after the status read
        printf 'deploy-kit: the kit root %s resolved to %s before the managed read and to %s after the status read; the roots changed during the run, nothing applied.\n' "${KIT_ROOTS[index]}" "${root_physicals[index]}" "${root_physical}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

split_lines "${status_listing}"
pending=()
pending_rows=()
retired=()
to_verify=()
root_rows=()
unmanaged_rows=()
refused_rows=()
# Each row is `XY <target>`: X the change since chezmoi last wrote the target, Y the change an apply would make.
for row in ${ROWS[@]+"${ROWS[@]}"}; do
    [[ -n ${row} ]] || continue
    target=${row:3}
    under_kit_root "${target}" || continue
    [[ ${row:1:1} != ' ' ]] || continue
    if is_kit_root "${target}" && [[ ${row:0:1} != ' ' || ${row:1:1} == 'D' ]]; then
        root_rows+=("${row}")
    elif ! in_kit_set "${target}"; then
        unmanaged_rows+=("${row}")
    elif [[ ${row:0:1} != ' ' ]]; then
        refused_rows+=("${row}")
    else
        pending+=("${target}")
        pending_rows+=("${row}")
        if [[ ${row:1:1} == 'D' ]]; then
            retired+=("${target}")
        else
            to_verify+=("${target}")
        fi
    fi
done

printf 'deploy-kit: pending: %d\n' "${#pending[@]}"
for row in ${pending_rows[@]+"${pending_rows[@]}"}; do
    printf '  %s\n' "${row}"
done
if ((${#root_rows[@]} > 0)); then
    printf 'deploy-kit: refused: %d kit roots are not what chezmoi last wrote or are removed by the source (status row on the root itself); the root was replaced between the reads or the root table is stale, nothing applied:\n' "${#root_rows[@]}" >&2
    for row in "${root_rows[@]}"; do
        printf '  %s\n' "${row}" >&2
    done
    exit 1
fi
if ((${#unmanaged_rows[@]} > 0)); then
    printf 'deploy-kit: refused: %d pending names are not in the managed kit set (chezmoi managed did not list them under the kit roots); the source changed between the two reads or the listings disagree, nothing applied:\n' "${#unmanaged_rows[@]}" >&2
    for row in "${unmanaged_rows[@]}"; do
        printf '  %s\n' "${row}" >&2
    done
    exit 1
fi
if ((${#refused_rows[@]} > 0)); then
    printf 'deploy-kit: refused: %d kit targets are not what chezmoi last wrote (status first column); an apply would drop a local edit the source does not have, nothing applied:\n' "${#refused_rows[@]}" >&2
    for row in "${refused_rows[@]}"; do
        printf '  %s\n' "${row}" >&2
    done
    exit 1
fi
if [[ ${dry_run} == true ]]; then
    printf 'deploy-kit: dry run; nothing applied.\n'
    exit 0
fi

if ((${#pending[@]} > 0)); then
    # stdin closed: a target changed between the status read and here would make chezmoi prompt; it fails instead.
    if ! chezmoi apply --verbose --recursive=false --refresh-externals=never "${pending[@]}" < /dev/null; then
        printf 'deploy-kit: chezmoi apply failed; the applied set is unknown, run chezmoi status over the kit roots.\n' >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    present=()
    for target in ${retired[@]+"${retired[@]}"}; do
        # -e follows a link, so a dangling link is present only to -L.
        if [[ -e ${target} || -L ${target} ]]; then
            present+=("${target}")
        fi
    done
    if ((${#present[@]} > 0)); then
        printf 'deploy-kit: %d retired targets are still present after the apply (status D rows); the retirement did not take, run chezmoi status over the kit roots:\n' "${#present[@]}" >&2
        for target in "${present[@]}"; do
            printf '  %s\n' "${target}" >&2
        done
        exit 1
    fi
fi
if ((${#to_verify[@]} > 0)); then
    read_kit_set || {
        printf 'deploy-kit: chezmoi managed failed after the apply; the applied targets are unverified, run chezmoi status over the kit roots.\n' >&2
        exit 1
    }
    unlisted=()
    for target in "${to_verify[@]}"; do
        in_kit_set "${target}" || unlisted+=("${target}")
    done
    if ((${#unlisted[@]} > 0)); then
        printf 'deploy-kit: %d applied targets are no longer in the managed kit set; the source changed during the run and their verified state is unknown, run chezmoi status over the kit roots:\n' "${#unlisted[@]}" >&2
        for target in "${unlisted[@]}"; do
            printf '  %s\n' "${target}" >&2
        done
        exit 1
    fi
    if ! chezmoi verify --recursive=false --refresh-externals=never "${to_verify[@]}"; then
        printf 'deploy-kit: chezmoi verify finds an applied target still differing from the source.\n' >&2
        exit 1
    fi
fi
printf 'deploy-kit: applied: %d\n' "${#pending[@]}"
for target in ${pending[@]+"${pending[@]}"}; do
    printf '  %s\n' "${target}"
done
