        1:update_omp | 1:update_hcom | 1:update_pi_claude_bridge | 1:update_security_audit_skill | 1:update_deepseek_harness | 1:update_dsh_superagent | 1:update_compactiondb | 1:prune_retired_manifest_steps | 1:check_pi_claude_bridge | 1:check_pstack | 1:retire_shared_pstack_copies | 1:retire_marketplace_dev_workflows | 1:retire_understand_anything | 1:retire_agmsg_shim)
            export PATH="${HOME}/.local/share/mise/shims:${PATH}"
            "$1"
            fail_on_pin_failures
            return
            ;;
        esac
        printf 'Usage: scripts/update-agent-assets.sh [update_omp | update_hcom | update_pi_claude_bridge | update_security_audit_skill | update_deepseek_harness | update_dsh_superagent | update_compactiondb | prune_retired_manifest_steps | check_pi_claude_bridge | check_pstack | retire_shared_pstack_copies | retire_marketplace_dev_workflows | retire_understand_anything | retire_agmsg_shim]\n' >&2
        exit 2
    fi

    export PATH="${HOME}/.local/share/mise/shims:${PATH}"
    remove_node_global_agent_cli_shadows
    retire_shared_pstack_copies
    retire_marketplace_dev_workflows
    retire_agmsg_shim
    ensure_mise_npm_agent_cli claude "npm:@anthropic-ai/claude-code"
    # Claude Code plugin convergence comes before any step that may stop the run (set -e), so every pinned
    # plugin is checked; its own failures are counted and fail the run at the end (fail_on_pin_failures).
    update_claude_superpowers
    update_claude_crit
    update_claude_ponytail
    converge_claude_plugins
    retire_understand_anything
    ensure_mise_npm_agent_cli codex "npm:@openai/codex"
    ensure_gh_extensions
    update_codex_superpowers
    update_codex_crit
    update_codex_ponytail
    update_terminal_code
    update_terminal_browser
    update_omp
    update_pi_claude_bridge
    update_security_audit_skill
    update_deepseek_harness
    update_dsh_superagent
    update_hcom
    update_compactiondb
    ensure_herdr_integrations
    prune_retired_manifest_steps
    # After every plugin update above, so the trust hashes follow the plugin content of this run.
    refresh_codex_hook_trust
    # Last, so every other step still ran: a plugin that may stay enabled off its pin fails the whole run.
    fail_on_pin_failures
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main "$@"
fi
</code></pre>

<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file scripts/upgrade-tools.sh
# @brief Update installed tools to the latest safe versions; `make update` runs it after `chezmoi apply`.
# @description
#   Each manager's own safety features decide what the latest safe version is:
#   mise's minimum_release_age and verification settings in the applied
#   ~/.config/mise/config.toml, and a manager's own hold (an exact version in
#   that config, brew pin, uv tool install <pkg>==<version>, apt-mark hold).
#   The default mode updates user-level tooling and Homebrew-managed packages
#   when those managers are available. Pass `--system` to include
#   operating-system package upgrades such as apt. The network-only phases
#   (Homebrew, mise self-update, uv tools, unpinned gh extensions) only warn when they
#   fail, so an offline host still converges; installing the declared mise tools
#   stays required, while a per-tool upgrade that fails only warns. It edits no repository file, and exits 0 without changes
#   on a GitHub Actions runner (is_ci_runner from scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh); an agent shell's CI=true still updates.

set -Eeuo pipefail

# dirname is captured on its own line: inside the cd its status would be lost.
script_dir="$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" || {
    echo "upgrade-tools: dirname failed on ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}; the repository root is unknown" >&2
    exit 1
}
repo_root="$(cd "${script_dir}/.." && pwd)" || exit 1
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/ci-runner.sh
source "${script_dir}/lib/ci-runner.sh"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/npm-release-age.sh
source "${script_dir}/lib/npm-release-age.sh"
# chezmoi applies home/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl to ~/.config/mise whatever XDG_CONFIG_HOME
# says, so mise reads exactly that config: no inherited MISE_CONFIG_DIR, and the isolated Git
# config's XDG_CONFIG_HOME below cannot redirect it.
export MISE_CONFIG_DIR="${HOME}/.config/mise"
# No project config from this checkout upward joins the inventory, so only the host config's tools move.
export MISE_CEILING_PATHS="${repo_root}"

include_system=false
DEFAULT_FORBIDDEN_HOMEBREW_FORMULAE="node node@* python python@* python3 pip npm pnpm yarn claude"
required_failures=0
optional_warnings=0

#
# @description Print a section heading.
# @arg $1 string Heading text.
#
function section() {
    printf '\n==> %s\n' "$1"
}

#
# @description Return success when the current OS is macOS.
# @exitcode 1 Also exits the script when uname fails: a failed read is not "another OS".
#
function is_macos() {
    local kernel
    kernel="$(uname)" || {
        echo "uname failed; cannot tell whether this host is macOS" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    [ "${kernel}" = "Darwin" ]
}

#
# @description Return success when the current OS is Linux.
# @exitcode 1 Also exits the script when uname fails: a failed read is not "another OS".
#
function is_linux() {
    local kernel
    kernel="$(uname)" || {
        echo "uname failed; cannot tell whether this host is Linux" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    [ "${kernel}" = "Linux" ]
}

#
# @description Return success when a command is available.
# @arg $1 string Command name.
#
function has_command() {
    command -v "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1
}

#
# @description Run a required upgrade phase and record failure without stopping later phases.
# @arg $1 string Phase label.
# @arg $2 string Function name.
#
function run_required_phase() {
    local label="$1"
    shift

    if ! "$@"; then
        printf 'required failure: %s\n' "${label}" >&2
        ((required_failures += 1))
    fi
}

#
# @description Run an optional upgrade phase and record warning-only failure.
# @arg $1 string Phase label.
# @arg $2 string Function name.
#
function run_optional_phase() {
    local label="$1"
    shift

    if ! "$@"; then
        printf 'optional warning: %s failed\n' "${label}" >&2
        ((optional_warnings += 1))
    fi
}

#
# @description Return success when the named Homebrew formula is forbidden.
# @arg $1 string Formula name.
#
function is_forbidden_homebrew_formula() {
    local formula="$1"
    local forbidden_formula

    for forbidden_formula in ${DEFAULT_FORBIDDEN_HOMEBREW_FORMULAE} ${HOMEBREW_FORBIDDEN_FORMULAE:-}; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2254 # Forbidden formula entries intentionally support glob patterns.
        case "${formula}" in
        ${forbidden_formula})
            return 0
            ;;
        esac
    done

    return 1
}

#
# @description Upgrade Homebrew packages on macOS when Homebrew is installed.
#
function upgrade_homebrew() {
    if ! is_macos; then
        return 0
    fi
    has_command brew || return 1

    section "Homebrew"
    if has_command gh; then
        # Homebrew verifies bottle build-provenance attestations through gh (HOMEBREW_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS).
        local -x HOMEBREW_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS=1
    else
        printf 'gh not found; Homebrew bottle attestation verification is skipped.\n'
    fi
    brew update || return

    local outdated_formula
    local outdated_formulae_output
    local outdated_formulae=()
    local upgrade_formulae=()
    outdated_formulae_output="$(brew outdated --formula --quiet)" || return
    if [ -n "${outdated_formulae_output}" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r outdated_formula; do
            outdated_formulae+=("${outdated_formula}")
        done <<< "${outdated_formulae_output}"
    fi

    if [ "${#outdated_formulae[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        for outdated_formula in "${outdated_formulae[@]}"; do
            if is_forbidden_homebrew_formula "${outdated_formula}"; then
                printf 'Skipping forbidden Homebrew formula: %s\n' "${outdated_formula}"
                continue
            fi

            upgrade_formulae+=("${outdated_formula}")
        done
    fi

    if [ "${#upgrade_formulae[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        # Homebrew asks for confirmation by default (brew upgrade --help); make update must not wait.
        HOMEBREW_NO_ASK=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALLED_DEPENDENTS_CHECK=1 brew upgrade --formula "${upgrade_formulae[@]}" || return
    else
        printf 'No upgradeable Homebrew formulae after forbidden formula filtering.\n'
    fi

    local outdated_cask
    local outdated_casks_output
    local outdated_casks=()
    outdated_casks_output="$(brew outdated --cask --quiet)" || return
    if [ -n "${outdated_casks_output}" ]; then
        while IFS= read -r outdated_cask; do
            outdated_casks+=("${outdated_cask}")
        done <<< "${outdated_casks_output}"
    fi

    if [ "${#outdated_casks[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        HOMEBREW_NO_ASK=1 HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALLED_DEPENDENTS_CHECK=1 brew upgrade --cask --skip-cask-deps "${outdated_casks[@]}" || return
    else
        printf 'No outdated Homebrew casks.\n'
    fi
}

#
# @description Upgrade standalone mise or skip package-manager-managed installations.
# @stdout Skip message when an official package-manager marker is present.
#
function upgrade_mise_self() {
    local mise_executable
    local mise_dir
    local mise_prefix

    has_command mise || return 1
    mise_executable="$(type -P mise)" || return 1
    mise_dir="$(dirname -- "${mise_executable}")" || return
    mise_prefix="$(cd "${mise_dir}/.." && pwd -P)" || return

    section "mise self-update"
    if [[ -f "${mise_prefix}/lib/mise-self-update-instructions.toml" ||
        -f "${mise_prefix}/lib/mise/mise-self-update-instructions.toml" ]]; then
        printf 'Skipping mise self-update: managed by package manager.\n'
        return 0
    fi

    # Plugin updates are branch moves the release-age cooldown does not cover.
    mise self-update --yes --no-plugins
}

#
# @description Run mise while hiding user-level Git config from package backend operations.
# @arg $@ string Mise command and arguments.
#
function run_mise_with_isolated_git_config() {
    local isolated_xdg_config_home
    local mise_config_dir
    local status

    mise_config_dir="${MISE_CONFIG_DIR}"
    isolated_xdg_config_home="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/mise-git-config.XXXXXX")"
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
        GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null \
        XDG_CONFIG_HOME="${isolated_xdg_config_home}" \
        MISE_CONFIG_DIR="${mise_config_dir}" \
        mise "$@"
    status="$?"
    rm -rf "${isolated_xdg_config_home}" 2> /dev/null || true
    return "${status}"
}

#
# @description Print mise tool names from the current configuration.
# @stdout One tool name per line.
#
function current_mise_tools() {
    local listing

    # Captured first: a failed `mise ls` is a failure of the inventory, never an empty one.
    listing="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config ls --current --no-header)" || return 1
    awk '{print $1}' <<< "${listing}"
}

#
# @description Print the tools the applied mise config holds, one per line: an entry whose comment block
#   directly above it says "Held" (home/dot_mise/config.toml keeps every hold reason there). The config is
#   the one source, so a hold released there leaves no skip behind here. scripts/pin_records.py reads it
#   strictly: the config must be valid TOML and every Held entry a tool.
# @exitcode 2 When the applied config cannot be read or a Held comment names no tool.
#
function held_mise_tools() {
    python3 -I "${repo_root}/scripts/pin_records.py" mise-holds "${MISE_CONFIG_DIR}/config.toml"
}

#
# @description Ask scripts/pin_records.py whether the applied mise config holds one tool.
# @arg $1 string mise tool name.
# @exitcode 0 Held.
# @exitcode 1 Not held.
# @exitcode 2 The config cannot be read or has an unknown shape: never read as "not held".
#
function mise_tool_is_held() {
    python3 -I "${repo_root}/scripts/pin_records.py" is-held "${MISE_CONFIG_DIR}/config.toml" "$1"
}

#
# @description Run a mise lifecycle command for each current tool; only upgrade is per tool.
# @arg $1 string Mise command name: upgrade.
# @exitcode 1 When the current tools cannot be listed.
# @exitcode 2 When the command failed for at least one tool.
#
function run_mise_tool_command() {
    local mise_command="$1"
    local mise_tool
    local mise_tools
    local held
    local failed=0

    if ! mise_tools="$(current_mise_tools)"; then
        printf 'warning: unable to list current mise tools for %s; continuing\n' "${mise_command}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # Read once up front, so an unreadable config stops the phase before any tool moves.
    if ! held_mise_tools > /dev/null; then
        printf 'warning: unable to read the held tools from %s/config.toml; no mise tool was upgraded\n' "${MISE_CONFIG_DIR}" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    while IFS= read -r mise_tool; do
        if [ -z "${mise_tool}" ]; then
            continue
        fi

        if [[ "${mise_tool}" == http:* ]]; then
            printf 'Skipping mise upgrade for pinned HTTP tool: %s.\n' "${mise_tool}"
            continue
        fi
        held=0
        mise_tool_is_held "${mise_tool}" || held=$?
        if [ "${held}" -eq 0 ]; then
            printf 'Skipping mise upgrade for held tool: %s (see its Held comment in the mise config).\n' "${mise_tool}"
            continue
        elif [ "${held}" -ne 1 ]; then
            printf 'warning: cannot tell whether %s is held; no further mise tool was upgraded\n' "${mise_tool}" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        # A plain upgrade keeps the config's "latest" or exact request as written.
        if ! run_mise_with_isolated_git_config upgrade --yes "${mise_tool}"; then
            printf 'warning: mise %s failed for %s; continuing\n' "${mise_command}" "${mise_tool}" >&2
            failed=2
        fi
    done <<< "${mise_tools}"

    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Report that one npm: tool keeps its previous install instead of being rebuilt on the current node.
# @arg $1 string mise npm tool name.
# @arg $2 string The reason.
# @stderr One skip line.
#
function npm_rebuild_skipped() {
    printf 'skip: %s is not rebuilt on the current node (%s); its previous install stays, and the next make update tries again\n' "$1" "$2" >&2
}

#
# @description Rebuild one npm: tool on the current node, keeping its working install until the new one succeeds.
#   mise install --force would delete the install before downloading its
#   replacement, so a rebuild without a network would leave the tool missing.
#   The rebuild reinstalls the exact version already installed, under npm's own min-release-age like every other
#   install: no package is exempt from it. npm refuses a version younger than that window (ETARGET), although the
#   host already runs it, so the rebuild first asks npm for the window and the version's publish time
#   (npm_release_age_verdict) and skips a version that is younger, or whose age it cannot tell, before anything
#   moves. An install npm still refuses (a dependency younger than the window) restores the previous install.
# @arg $1 string mise npm tool name, for example npm:ccusage.
# @stderr A skip line naming the reason when the tool is not rebuilt.
# @exitcode 1 When the tool was not rebuilt.
#
function rebuild_mise_npm_tool() {
    local mise_tool="$1"
    local version install_dir backup min_age times verdict

    version="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config current "${mise_tool}")" || {
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "mise cannot name its current version"
        return 1
    }
    install_dir="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config where "${mise_tool}")" || {
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "mise cannot name its install directory"
        return 1
    }
    # Only an existing absolute install directory is moved or removed.
    [[ -n "${version}" && "${install_dir}" == /* ]] || { # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path prefix test
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "no version or no absolute install directory"
        return 1
    }
    backup="${install_dir}.before-node-rebuild"
    # restore_interrupted_npm_rebuilds put any leftover backup back; never move an install into one.
    [[ -d "${install_dir}" && ! -e "${backup}" ]] || {
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "${install_dir} is missing or a backup of it exists"
        return 1
    }
    # Decided before anything moves, with the npm that mise's npm backend runs (the current node's).
    min_age="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config exec -- npm config get min-release-age)" || {
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "npm config get min-release-age failed"
        return 1
    }
    times="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config exec -- npm view --json "${mise_tool#npm:}" time)" || {
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "npm view cannot read the publish time of ${version}"
        return 1
    }
    local age_status=0
    verdict="$(npm_release_age_verdict "${version}" "${min_age}" <<< "${times}")" || age_status=$?
    if [ "${age_status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "${verdict:-its release age cannot be told}"
        return 1
    fi
    mv "${install_dir}" "${backup}" || {
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "${install_dir} cannot be moved aside"
        return 1
    }
    # Until the new install succeeds, an interruption or exit puts the working install back.
    local restore
    restore="$(printf 'restore_npm_install %q %q' "${install_dir}" "${backup}")"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2064 # Expanded now on purpose: the paths are this function's locals.
    trap "${restore}; exit 130" INT
    # shellcheck disable=SC2064
    trap "${restore}; exit 143" TERM
    # shellcheck disable=SC2064
    trap "${restore}" EXIT
    if run_mise_with_isolated_git_config install --yes "${mise_tool}@${version}"; then
        trap - INT TERM EXIT
        # Renamed before it is deleted, so a backup that cannot be fully deleted is never restored over this
        # install; the dot keeps a leftover out of mise's installed versions.
        local discard="${install_dir%/*}/.${install_dir##*/}.discarded-after-rebuild"
        rm -rf "${discard}"
        mv "${backup}" "${discard}" || {
            printf 'warning: %s was rebuilt, but its previous install %s cannot be set aside\n' "${mise_tool}" "${backup}" >&2
            return 1
        }
        rm -rf "${discard}" || printf 'warning: could not delete %s; nothing uses it\n' "${discard}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    trap - INT TERM EXIT
    restore_npm_install "${install_dir}" "${backup}" &&
        npm_rebuild_skipped "${mise_tool}" "npm refused or could not fetch ${mise_tool#npm:}@${version}, its error is above; a dependency younger than npm's min-release-age is still refused"
    return 1
}

#
# @description Put back every npm: install that a rebuild killed past its traps (SIGKILL, power loss) left
#   moved aside. It runs before any mise command, because mise cannot name an install that is not in place.
#
function restore_interrupted_npm_rebuilds() {
    local backup
    local failed=0
    # mise's own installs directory resolution: MISE_INSTALLS_DIR, then the data directory (MISE_DATA_DIR, then XDG_DATA_HOME).
    local installs="${MISE_INSTALLS_DIR:-${MISE_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/share}/mise}/installs}"
    for backup in "${installs}"/*/*.before-node-rebuild; do
        [ -d "${backup}" ] || continue
        restore_npm_install "${backup%.before-node-rebuild}" "${backup}" || failed=1
    done
    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Put a moved-aside npm: install back, replacing whatever a failed or interrupted install left.
# @arg $1 path The install directory.
# @arg $2 path The moved-aside working install.
#
function restore_npm_install() {
    [ -d "$2" ] || return 0
    # The backup moves only onto a path that is gone, so it is never buried inside a partial install that survives.
    if rm -rf "$1" && [ ! -e "$1" ] && mv "$2" "$1"; then
        return 0
    fi
    printf 'required failure: could not restore %s from %s\n' "$1" "$2" >&2
    ((required_failures += 1))
    return 1
}

#
# @description Rebuild the current npm: tools so they run on the current node; each one not rebuilt says why.
# @exitcode 1 When the tools cannot be listed or at least one was not rebuilt.
#
function reinstall_mise_npm_tools() {
    local mise_tool
    local mise_tools
    local failed=0

    mise_tools="$(current_mise_tools)" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r mise_tool; do
        [[ "${mise_tool}" == npm:* ]] || continue
        rebuild_mise_npm_tool "${mise_tool}" || failed=1
    done <<< "${mise_tools}"

    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Install missing and upgrade outdated mise tools declared in the applied host config.
#
function upgrade_mise_tools() {
    has_command mise || return 1

    section "mise tools"
    local failed=0
    restore_interrupted_npm_rebuilds || failed=1
    mise trust --yes || failed=1
    # minimum_release_age in the config keeps freshly published releases out of both steps.
    # One bare install: it leaves installed tools alone offline, while a per-tool
    # install re-resolves "latest" over the network and fails without one.
    run_mise_with_isolated_git_config install --yes || failed=1
    # Upgrades need the network; an installed tool that cannot move yet is still converged.
    local upgrade_status=0
    run_mise_tool_command upgrade || upgrade_status=$?
    if [ "${upgrade_status}" -eq 2 ]; then
        printf 'optional warning: mise upgrade failed for at least one tool; its installed version stays\n' >&2
        ((optional_warnings += 1))
    elif [ "${upgrade_status}" -ne 0 ]; then
        failed=1
    fi
    # Neither the bare install nor the upgrades rebuild installed npm: tools, and node can also have moved
    # in an earlier run or under the installer, so a marker records the node they were last built on.
    local marker="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-${HOME}/.local/state}/dotfiles/npm-tools-node"
    local node_built="" node_now="" reinstalled=0
    if [ -r "${marker}" ]; then
        node_built="$(cat "${marker}")"
    fi
    node_now="$(run_mise_with_isolated_git_config current node 2> /dev/null)" || node_now=""
    if [ -n "${node_now}" ] && [ "${node_now}" != "${node_built}" ]; then
        if reinstall_mise_npm_tools; then
            reinstalled=1
        else
            printf 'optional warning: npm: tools were not all reinstalled on node %s\n' "${node_now}" >&2
            ((optional_warnings += 1))
        fi
        # A rebuild keeps or restores the previous install, so this final bare install only has to confirm
        # that every declared tool is present; it decides whether the phase converged.
        if ! run_mise_with_isolated_git_config install --yes; then
            failed=1
        elif [ "${reinstalled}" -eq 1 ]; then
            # Only a complete rebuild is recorded, so a failed one is retried by the next run.
            if ! { mkdir -p "$(dirname "${marker}")" && printf '%s\n' "${node_now}" > "${marker}"; }; then
                printf 'required: could not record the npm-tools node in %s\n' "${marker}" >&2
                failed=1
            fi
        fi
    fi
    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Print the manifest pin of an asset installed from a wheel (an assets.<name>.files URL ending in .whl), or nothing.
# @arg $1 string Asset name.
#
function manifest_wheel_pin() {
    # shortcut: reads the unquoted block style of home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml line by line, not as YAML; use a parser if assets: gains quotes or flow style.
    awk -v name="$1" '
        /^[^ #]/ { in_assets = ($0 ~ /^assets:/) }
        in_assets && /^  [^ #]/ { asset = $1; sub(/:$/, "", asset) }
        in_assets && asset == name && /^    pin:/ { pin = $2 }
        in_assets && asset == name && /\.whl$/ { wheel = 1 }
        END { if (wheel) print pin }
    ' "${repo_root}/home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml"
}

#
# @description Upgrade uv tool installations when uv is available, except the ones the manifest pins from a wheel.
#
function upgrade_uv_tools() {
    local tools tool pin failed=0
    has_command uv || return 1

    section "uv tools"
    # Plain text even where FORCE_COLOR or CLICOLOR_FORCE is set: uv colours tool names there.
    tools="$(uv tool list --color never)" || return
    # Tool lines read "<name> v<version>"; their entry points follow as "- <command>".
    for tool in $(printf '%s\n' "${tools}" | awk '/^[^- ]/ { print $1 }'); do
        pin="$(manifest_wheel_pin "${tool}")" || return
        if [ -n "${pin}" ]; then
            # uv's receipt names the local wheel, so an index upgrade has nothing to move; update-agent-assets.sh does.
            printf 'skip: %s (manifest pins %s from a wheel)\n' "${tool}" "${pin}"
        else
            uv tool upgrade "${tool}" || failed=1
        fi
    done
    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Upgrade the GitHub CLI extensions this repository does not pin, one by one, when gh is available.
# @description
#   An extension recorded in scripts/plugin-pins.json (assets.gh-extensions) stays at its reviewed tag:
#   install/common/gh_extensions.sh installs it with --pin, and no blanket `gh extension upgrade --all` runs.
# @exitcode 1 When the pins or the extension list cannot be read (nothing is upgraded), or an upgrade fails.
#
function upgrade_gh_extensions() {
    local listing repository pinned failed=0

    if ! has_command gh; then
        return 0
    fi

    section "GitHub CLI extensions"
    if ! listing="$(gh extension list)"; then
        printf 'warning: gh extension list failed; no extension was upgraded\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r _ repository _; do
        [ -n "${repository}" ] || continue
        # pin_records.py answers exit 0 pinned, 1 not pinned; anything else (unreadable pins, a row that is not
        # <owner>/<name>) is a failure, and the extension is not upgraded.
        pinned=0
        python3 -I "${repo_root}/scripts/pin_records.py" is-pinned-extension "${repo_root}/scripts/plugin-pins.json" "${repository}" || pinned=$?
        if [ "${pinned}" -eq 0 ]; then
            printf 'Skipping gh extension %s: pinned in assets.gh-extensions.\n' "${repository}"
            continue
        elif [ "${pinned}" -ne 1 ]; then
            printf 'warning: cannot tell whether gh extension %s is pinned; it was not upgraded\n' "${repository}" >&2
            failed=1
            continue
        fi
        gh extension upgrade "${repository##*/}" || failed=1
    done <<< "${listing}"
    return "${failed}"
}

#
# @description Upgrade apt packages only when system upgrades are requested.
#
function upgrade_apt_packages() {
    if ! ${include_system} || ! is_linux; then
        return 0
    fi
    has_command apt-get || return 1

    section "apt"
    sudo --preserve-env=http_proxy,https_proxy,no_proxy apt-get update || return
    sudo --preserve-env=http_proxy,https_proxy,no_proxy apt-get upgrade -y
}

#
# @description Parse command-line options.
# @arg $@ string Command-line arguments.
#
function parse_args() {
    while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
        --system)
            include_system=true
            ;;
        -h | --help)
            cat << 'USAGE'
Usage: scripts/upgrade-tools.sh [--system]

Update installed tools to the latest safe versions; make update runs it.

Options:
  --system  Include operating-system package upgrades such as apt.
USAGE
            exit 0
            ;;
        *)
            printf 'Unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
            exit 2
            ;;
        esac
        shift
    done
}

#
# @description Update installed tools through each manager.
# @arg $@ string Command-line arguments.
#
function main() {
    parse_args "$@"
    # A CI runner's tools belong to its image, not to this machine's update.
    if is_ci_runner; then
        printf 'GitHub Actions runner: skipping installed-tool updates.\n'
        return 0
    fi

    # Network-only phases warn and continue, so make update still converges offline.
    run_optional_phase "Homebrew" upgrade_homebrew
    run_optional_phase "mise self-update" upgrade_mise_self
    run_required_phase "mise inventory/install/upgrade" upgrade_mise_tools
    run_optional_phase "uv tool upgrade" upgrade_uv_tools
    run_optional_phase "GitHub CLI extension upgrade" upgrade_gh_extensions
    run_required_phase "apt system upgrade" upgrade_apt_packages

    printf '\nUpgrade summary: required failures: %d; optional warnings: %d\n' \
        "${required_failures}" "${optional_warnings}"
    [ "${required_failures}" -eq 0 ]
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then
    main "$@"
fi
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @file scripts/usage-snapshot.sh
# @brief Capture one daily ccusage snapshot for usage reviews.
# @description
#   Stores weekly and daily ccusage JSON in the repository worklog. Existing
#   snapshots are left unchanged, and unavailable or failing ccusage commands
#   warn without failing scheduled lifecycle runs.

set -Eeuo pipefail

# dirname is captured on its own line: inside the cd its status would be lost.
script_dir="$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" || {
    echo "usage-snapshot: dirname failed on ${BASH_SOURCE[0]}; the repository root is unknown" >&2
    exit 1
}
repo_root="$(cd "${script_dir}/.." && pwd)" || exit 1
usage_dir="${repo_root}/.agents/worklog/claude/usage"
snapshot_date="$(date +%Y%m%d)"
snapshot_path="${usage_dir}/${snapshot_date}.json"

if [[ -e "${snapshot_path}" ]]; then
    printf 'Usage snapshot already exists: %s\n' "${snapshot_path}"
    exit 0
fi

if ! command -v ccusage > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'WARN: ccusage is unavailable; usage snapshot skipped.\n' >&2
    exit 0
fi

if ! weekly_json="$(ccusage weekly --json)"; then
    printf 'WARN: ccusage weekly failed; usage snapshot skipped.\n' >&2
    exit 0
fi
if ! daily_json="$(ccusage daily --json)"; then
    printf 'WARN: ccusage daily failed; usage snapshot skipped.\n' >&2
    exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "${usage_dir}"
captured_at="$(date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')"
temporary_path="${snapshot_path}.tmp.$$"
trap 'rm -f "${temporary_path}"' EXIT
printf '{"captured_at":"%s","weekly":%s,"daily":%s}\n' \
    "${captured_at}" "${weekly_json}" "${daily_json}" > "${temporary_path}"
if ln "${temporary_path}" "${snapshot_path}" 2> /dev/null; then
    rm -f "${temporary_path}"
    trap - EXIT
elif [[ -e "${snapshot_path}" ]]; then
    printf 'Usage snapshot already exists: %s\n' "${snapshot_path}"
    exit 0
else
    printf 'WARN: unable to publish usage snapshot: %s\n' "${snapshot_path}" >&2
    exit 0
fi

printf 'Usage snapshot captured: %s\n' "${snapshot_path}"

docs.text: Regime-cutover U113 (plan P-22). The levers run git through scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh, whose git_isolated carries the one flag set that isolates git from the operator's and the repository's configuration. This check parses each file with shfmt (shfmt -ln bash --to-json) and reports every word that is one plain literal spelling git or a path ending in /git, wherever it stands under a statement: a command word, an argument after command, exec, env, bounded or any other wrapper, an assignment value, an array element, a redirect target, a word inside $(…). The rule is structural, not a command-name match of the first word: the wrappers are open-ended, and a git handed to one runs as surely as a bare one. Two shapes are accepted: a word inside the git_isolated function of the library file itself, and a word whose statement spans a line carrying # git-isolated: allow <reason>; an allow comment without a reason is itself a finding. A quoted 'git' or "git …" is a SglQuoted or DblQuoted part and is not a plain literal (refuse 'git ls-files failed' passes); a heredoc body is one line-shaped literal and is not git; a $(git …) inside an unquoted heredoc body is code and is reported. Before any file is read, scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py proves that the pinned shfmt still produces the node kinds and fields this walk reads, and this walk then visits the contract fixtures itself and is refused if it sees no command and no literal there (regime-cutover U105): "no findings" on the listed files is never "saw nothing". A file shfmt cannot parse is refused, never read as clean. The enforced file set is a test, tests/unit/test_git_invocation_check.py (the library and the five adopted levers); the other scripts under scripts/orchestrator keep their own wrappers until a follow-up unit and are reported, not fixed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file git-invocation-check.sh
# @brief Refuse a `git` word outside `git_isolated` in the levers, found on shfmt's syntax tree.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U113 (plan P-22). The levers run git through scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh, whose
#   `git_isolated` carries the one flag set that isolates git from the operator's and the repository's configuration.
#   This check parses each file with shfmt (`shfmt -ln bash --to-json`) and reports every word that is one plain
#   literal spelling `git` or a path ending in `/git`, wherever it stands under a statement: a command word, an
#   argument after `command`, `exec`, `env`, `bounded` or any other wrapper, an assignment value, an array element,
#   a redirect target, a word inside `$(…)`. The rule is structural, not a command-name match of the first word: the
#   wrappers are open-ended, and a `git` handed to one runs as surely as a bare one. Two shapes are accepted: a word
#   inside the `git_isolated` function of the library file itself, and a word whose statement spans a line carrying
#   `# git-isolated: allow <reason>`; an allow comment without a reason is itself a finding. A quoted `'git'` or
#   `"git …"` is a SglQuoted or DblQuoted part and is not a plain literal (`refuse 'git ls-files failed'` passes); a
#   heredoc body is one line-shaped literal and is not `git`; a `$(git …)` inside an unquoted heredoc body is code and
#   is reported.
#   Before any file is read, scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py proves that the pinned shfmt still produces the node
#   kinds and fields this walk reads, and this walk then visits the contract fixtures itself and is refused if it sees
#   no command and no literal there (regime-cutover U105): "no findings" on the listed files is never "saw nothing".
#   A file shfmt cannot parse is refused, never read as clean. The enforced file set is a test,
#   tests/unit/test_git_invocation_check.py (the library and the five adopted levers); the other scripts under
#   scripts/orchestrator keep their own wrappers until a follow-up unit and are reported, not fixed.
# @arg $@ path The files to check.
# @description The shfmt is PATH's, the one scripts/ci/pinned-tool-version.sh checks ([tools."http:shfmt"], U97); no
#   variable selects another. The library is scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh beside this script's repository,
#   recognised by file identity, so a copy elsewhere that defines its own `git_isolated` is reported.
# @exitcode 0 Every `git` word is inside the library's function or on an allowed statement.
# @exitcode 1 At least one finding, each printed as `file:line: …`.
# @exitcode 2 No file given, a listed file cannot be read or parsed, shfmt or python3 is missing, shfmt's JSON does not
#   match the pinned node table, or this walk visited no command or no literal in the contract fixtures: the list is
#   refused, never read as clean.
# @example
#   scripts/ci/git-invocation-check.sh scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh scripts/orchestrator/records-sync.sh
set -euo pipefail

if (($# == 0)); then
    echo "git-invocation-check: no file to check; an empty list is refused" >&2
    exit 2
fi

for tool in shfmt python3; do
    if ! command -v "${tool}" > /dev/null; then
        echo "git-invocation-check: ${tool} not found; the list is refused" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
done

for file in "$@"; do
    if [[ ! -f ${file} || ! -r ${file} ]]; then
        echo "git-invocation-check: cannot read ${file}; the list is refused" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
done

# The directory of this script, where scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py lives: a parameter expansion, so no
# producer's status is at stake.
case ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} in
*/*) here=${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*} ;;
*) here=. ;;
esac

# Runs the contract, then parses each file with shfmt and walks its typed JSON. argv[1] is the directory of
# shfmt_json_contract.py, the rest are the files. Exits 1 when it prints a finding, 2 when the list is refused.
walk=$(
    cat << 'PY'
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
import shfmt_json_contract as contract  # noqa: E402

MESSAGE = "a git call outside git_isolated; run it through the library, or carry `# git-isolated: allow <reason>`"
REASONLESS = "an allow comment without a reason; `# git-isolated: allow <reason>` names why this git is not isolated"
LIBRARY = os.path.join(sys.argv[1], os.pardir, os.pardir, "scripts", "orchestrator", "git-isolated.sh")
FUNCTION = "git_isolated"
MARKER = ["git-isolated:", "allow"]


def refuse(reason):
    print(f"git-invocation-check: {reason}; the list is refused", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def is_git(word):
    """Whether the word is one plain literal spelling git, or a path ending in /git."""
    parts = word.get("Parts") or []
    if len(parts) != 1 or parts[0].get("Type") != "Lit":
        return False
    value = parts[0].get("Value") or ""
    return value == "git" or value.endswith("/git")


def walk(tree, library):
    """(commands seen, literals seen, [(line, statement lines) per git word], [(line, text) per comment]) of a tree.
    A git word inside the library's git_isolated function is left out; the statement lines are the innermost
    statement's, where an allow comment counts. Iterative: a long && chain nests deeper than Python recurses."""
    calls = lits = 0
    found = []
    comments = []
    todo = [(tree, None, False)]
    while todo:
        node, span, guarded = todo.pop()
        if isinstance(node, list):
            todo.extend((item, span, guarded) for item in node)
            continue
        if not isinstance(node, dict):
            continue
        kind = node.get("Type")
        name = (node.get("Name") or {}).get("Value")
        if kind == "CallExpr":
            calls += 1
        elif kind == "Lit":
            lits += 1
        if "Cmd" in node:
            span = (node["Pos"]["Line"], node["End"]["Line"])
        if "Hash" in node and "Text" in node:
            comments.append((node["Hash"]["Line"], node["Text"]))
        if kind == "FuncDecl" and library and name == FUNCTION:
            guarded = True
        if kind in (None, "Word") and "Parts" in node and is_git(node) and not guarded:
            found.append((node["Pos"]["Line"], span))
        todo.extend((value, span, guarded) for value in node.values())
    return calls, lits, found, comments


try:
    fixtures = contract.verified_trees()
except contract.ContractError as error:
    refuse(f"shfmt's JSON does not match the pinned node table ({error})")

# The contract proved the parser names the kinds; this proves the walk above still visits them, with its own
# traversal and type test, before a listed file is read. The fixtures' own findings are not reported.
seen_calls = seen_lits = 0
for source, tree in fixtures.items():
    try:
        calls, lits, _, _ = walk(tree, False)
    except Exception as error:  # a fixture the walk cannot read is "could not judge" for every listed file
        refuse(f"cannot walk the syntax tree of {source} ({error!r})")
    seen_calls += calls
    seen_lits += lits
if seen_calls == 0 or seen_lits == 0:
    refuse("the walk visited no command or no literal in the contract fixtures, which hold both")

status = 0
for file in sys.argv[2:]:
    try:
        with open(file, "rb") as handle:
            run = subprocess.run(["shfmt", "-ln", "bash", "--to-json"], stdin=handle, capture_output=True, check=False)
        library = os.path.exists(LIBRARY) and os.path.samefile(file, LIBRARY)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot read {file} ({error})")
    sys.stderr.write(run.stderr.decode(errors="replace"))
    if run.returncode != 0:
        refuse(f"shfmt cannot parse {file}")
    try:
        tree = json.loads(run.stdout)
    except ValueError:
        refuse(f"shfmt gave no JSON tree for {file}")
    try:
        _, _, found, comments = walk(tree, library)
    except Exception as error:  # any failure to read the tree is "could not judge", never a clean file
        refuse(f"cannot walk the syntax tree of {file} ({error!r})")
    # An allow comment is the marker's two words then the reason; the comment's text is split on blanks, no pattern.
    allowed = {}
    for line, text in comments:
        words = text.split()
        if words[:2] == MARKER:
            allowed[line] = words[2:]
    findings = set()
    for line, span in found:
        low, high = span or (line, line)
        if not any(allowed.get(at) for at in range(low, high + 1)):
            findings.add((line, MESSAGE))
    findings.update((line, REASONLESS) for line, reason in allowed.items() if not reason)
    for line, message in sorted(findings):
        print(f"{file}:{line}: {message}")
    status = 1 if findings else status
sys.exit(status)
PY
)

python3 -I -c "${walk}" "${here}" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file install-pinned-lint-tools.sh
# @brief Install the pinned ShellCheck, shfmt and Bats from a mise config and put each first on a GitHub Actions PATH.
# @description
#   CI's "Put the pinned `ShellCheck`, `shfmt` and `Bats` on PATH" step (regime-cutover U97; Bats since U127, when the
#   files-test jobs of macos.yaml and ubuntu.yaml began to install Bats alone the same way). `mise install` installs each
#   tool's `http:` pin from the copied home/dot_mise/config.toml, mise checking every download against its sha256.
#   Each binary's location comes from `mise which --tool`, its status checked, and must be an absolute path to an
#   executable regular file; only then is its directory appended to $GITHUB_PATH. Every lookup is checked before
#   anything is appended, so a failed lookup adds nothing (an unchecked `dirname "$(mise which …)"` turned a failed
#   lookup into `.`, round-1 audit of 35739993).
# @arg $1 path The mise project directory that holds the copied config (mise -C).
# @arg $@ string The tools, after the directory: shellcheck, shfmt or bats.
# @env GITHUB_PATH path The file GitHub Actions reads PATH additions from.
# @exitcode 0 Every tool is installed and its directory appended.
# @exitcode 1 An install, a lookup or the append failed, or a lookup named no executable file by absolute path.
# @exitcode 2 No directory or tool, an unknown tool, or GITHUB_PATH unset: nothing was installed.
# @example
#   scripts/ci/install-pinned-lint-tools.sh "${RUNNER_TEMP}/statusline-mise" shellcheck shfmt bats
set -euo pipefail

if (($# < 2)) || [[ -z ${GITHUB_PATH:-} ]]; then
    printf 'install-pinned-lint-tools: usage: GITHUB_PATH=<file> install-pinned-lint-tools.sh <mise dir> <tool>...\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi
dir=$1
shift
keys=()
for tool in "$@"; do
    case ${tool} in
    shellcheck | shfmt | bats) keys+=("http:${tool}") ;;
    *)
        printf 'install-pinned-lint-tools: %s is not a pinned lint tool this step installs (shellcheck, shfmt, bats)\n' "${tool}" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
    esac
done

if ! mise -C "${dir}" install "${keys[@]}"; then
    printf 'install-pinned-lint-tools: mise install %s failed\n' "${keys[*]}" >&2
    exit 1
fi
directories=()
for tool in "$@"; do
    if ! binary=$(mise -C "${dir}" which --tool "http:${tool}" "${tool}"); then
        printf 'install-pinned-lint-tools: mise which --tool http:%s %s failed; PATH is unchanged\n' "${tool}" "${tool}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if ! [[ ${binary} == /* && -f ${binary} && -x ${binary} ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow an absolute-path prefix test
        printf 'install-pinned-lint-tools: mise named %s for %s, not an executable file by absolute path; PATH is unchanged\n' \
            "${binary:-nothing}" "${tool}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    directories+=("${binary%/*}")
done
for directory in "${directories[@]}"; do
    if ! printf '%s\n' "${directory}" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}"; then
        printf 'install-pinned-lint-tools: cannot append %s to %s\n' "${directory}" "${GITHUB_PATH}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    printf '==> %s first on PATH\n' "${directory}"
done

This check parses each file with shfmt (shfmt -ln bash --to-json) and reports every command substitution ($(…) or backquotes) that opens inside another one, as file:line: … at the line where the inner one opens; capture the inner result first, or split a path in the shell (${path%/*}, ${path##*/}). The files are parsed as bash: make shellcheck passes only bash scripts, and bash also parses the repository's POSIX scripts. A file shfmt cannot parse is refused, never read as clean; that includes a heredoc delimiter with ANSI-C escapes (<<$'\x45OF'), which shfmt 3.14.1 and ShellCheck 0.11.0 both fail to terminate (tests/fixtures/shfmt-json/heredoc-ansi-c-delimiter). #   shape, so the linted groups held no nested substitution when the rule was set (regime-cutover
#   U38b). A heredoc body whose delimiter has any quoted or escaped part is literal and skipped, as
#   bash reads it (shfmt expands the body of a partly quoted delimiter such as `<<'E'OF`;
#   tests/fixtures/shfmt-json/heredoc-partly-quoted-delimiter holds that case).
#   The files are parsed as bash: `make shellcheck` passes only bash scripts, and bash also parses
#   the repository's POSIX scripts. A file shfmt cannot parse is refused, never read as clean; that
#   includes a heredoc delimiter with ANSI-C escapes (`<<$'\x45OF'`), which shfmt 3.14.1 and
#   ShellCheck 0.11.0 both fail to terminate (tests/fixtures/shfmt-json/heredoc-ansi-c-delimiter).
#   Before any file is read, scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py proves that the pinned shfmt still
#   produces the node kinds and fields this walk reads, and this walk then visits the contract fixtures
#   itself and is refused if it sees no command substitution there (regime-cutover U105): "no findings"
#   on the listed files is never "saw nothing", and a group whose files hold no substitution is clean.
# @arg $@ path The files to check (the ShellCheck groups of `make shellcheck`).
# @description The shfmt is PATH's, the one scripts/ci/pinned-tool-version.sh checks before `make shellcheck`
#   runs this ([tools."http:shfmt"], U97); no variable selects another.
# @exitcode 0 No command substitution nested inside another.

fi

for tool in shfmt python3; do
    if ! command -v "${tool}" > /dev/null; then
        echo "masked-dirname-check: ${tool} not found; the list is refused" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
done

for file in "$@"; do
    if [[ ! -f ${file} || ! -r ${file} ]]; then
        echo "masked-dirname-check: cannot read ${file}; the list is refused" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
done

# The directory of this script, where scripts/ci/shfmt_json_contract.py lives: a parameter expansion, so no
# producer's status is at stake.
case ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} in
*/*) here=${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*} ;;
*) here=. ;;
esac

# Runs the contract, then parses each file with shfmt and walks its typed JSON. argv[1] is the directory of
# shfmt_json_contract.py, the rest are the files. Exits 1 when it prints a finding, 2 when the list is refused.
walk=$(
    cat << 'PY'
import json
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
import shfmt_json_contract as contract  # noqa: E402

MESSAGE = "a command substitution inside another one loses its status; capture it first, or split a path in the shell"


def refuse(reason):
    print(f"masked-dirname-check: {reason}; the list is refused", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def quoted(word):
    """Whether any part of the word is quoted or escaped."""
    return any(
        part.get("Type") in ("SglQuoted", "DblQuoted") or (part.get("Type") == "Lit" and "\\" in part["Value"])
        for part in word.get("Parts") or []
    )


try:
    fixtures = contract.verified_trees()
except contract.ContractError as error:
    refuse(f"shfmt's JSON does not match the pinned node table ({error})")

findings = set()
substitutions = 0


def walk(node, depth):
    global substitutions
    if isinstance(node, list):
        for item in node:
            walk(item, depth)
        return
    if not isinstance(node, dict):
        return
    if node.get("Type") == "CmdSubst":
        substitutions += 1
        if depth:
            findings.add(node["Pos"]["Line"])
        depth += 1
    elif node.get("Hdoc") and quoted(node["Word"]):
        # shfmt 3.14.1 parses the body of a partly quoted delimiter (`<<'E'OF`, `<<E"O"F`) as expanded text;
        # bash makes the body literal once any part of the delimiter is quoted.
        node = {key: value for key, value in node.items() if key != "Hdoc"}
    for value in node.values():
        walk(value, depth)


# The contract proved the parser names the kinds; this proves the walk above still visits them, with its own
# traversal and type test, before a listed file is read. The fixtures' own findings are not reported.
for source, tree in fixtures.items():
    try:
        walk(tree, 0)
    except Exception as error:  # a fixture the walk cannot read is "could not judge" for every listed file
        refuse(f"cannot walk the syntax tree of {source} ({error!r})")
if substitutions == 0:
    refuse("the walk visited no command substitution in the contract fixtures, which hold some")

status = 0
for file in sys.argv[2:]:
    try:
        with open(file, "rb") as handle:
            run = subprocess.run(["shfmt", "-ln", "bash", "--to-json"], stdin=handle, capture_output=True, check=False)
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(f"cannot read {file} ({error})")
    sys.stderr.write(run.stderr.decode(errors="replace"))
    if run.returncode != 0:
        refuse(f"shfmt cannot parse {file}")
    try:
        tree = json.loads(run.stdout)
    except ValueError:
        refuse(f"shfmt gave no JSON tree for {file}")
    findings.clear()
    try:
        walk(tree, 0)
    except Exception as error:  # any failure to read the tree is "could not judge", never a clean file
        refuse(f"cannot walk the syntax tree of {file} ({error!r})")
    for line in sorted(findings):
        print(f"{file}:{line}: {MESSAGE}")
    status = 1 if findings else status
sys.exit(status)
PY
)

python3 -I -c "${walk}" "${here}" "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file npm-cooldown-skew-check.sh
# @brief Refuse an npm tool whose meta package, or whose platform package for this runner, is younger than mise's release-age window plus 60 s.
# @description
#   A multi-package npm tool publishes its platform binaries as `optionalDependencies`, often minutes after the
#   meta package (ccusage 20.0.38: the meta package at 2026-10-21T10:49:51Z, its linux-x64 package at 10:54:25Z).
#   mise applies `minimum_release_age` to the version it resolves and passes the same cutoff to npm for the
#   dependencies, and npm's rule for an optional dependency it cannot fetch is to proceed without it. A job that
#   starts inside that skew after the cutoff (run 40087404553, 2026-10-24T10:49:49Z) therefore installs the tool
#   without its native binary, and only the smoke test after the install notices. This check runs before the
#   install and refuses the version until every package npm would fetch for this runner clears the window.
#   For each tool it reads, in this order, every answer parsed by Python's json with an exact shape check and
#   never by a regular expression over npm's output:
#   1. the version mise would install: the config's request (`mise tool --json`, `requested_versions`) unless the
#      argument carries one, resolved by `mise latest npm:<name>@<request>` ("Nothing is installed and no config
#      changes") to exactly one SemVer version, read before any registry call: a tag, a range or two lines is exit 2.
#      `mise latest npm:<name>` alone ignores the config's pin (mise 2026.10.19 printed 20.0.44 for a config holding
#      20.0.37 on 2026-10-29), so the request is read first;
#   2. the window: `mise settings get minimum_release_age`, exactly `<N>h` or `<N>d`, passed to
#      npm_release_age_verdict as days (72h is 3; hours round up to the microday, so the window never shrinks);
#   3. the meta package's publish time (`npm view --json <name> time`) through npm_release_age_verdict;
#   4. its `optionalDependencies` (`npm view --json <name>@<version> optionalDependencies`): empty output is "no
#      optional dependencies", otherwise an object of package name to exactly one SemVer version. A tag or a range
#      there (npm would resolve it to a version this check never saw) is exit 2 before any package's `os` and `cpu`
#      are read;
#   5. for each of them, `npm view --json <dep>@<ver> os cpu`, an object whose `os` and `cpu` are lists of strings.
#      The package is this runner's when both lists hold `node -p process.platform` and `process.arch`, each read
#      once before any tool as exactly one word (a malformed answer is exit 2 on every run, with or without optional
#      dependencies to match it against); a `!`-prefixed entry is an unknown shape. Each matching package's publish
#      time goes through npm_release_age_verdict, and no matching package at all is a refusal naming the runner.
#   npm and node are the config's own, `mise -C <dir> exec node -- …`. Naming the tool keeps mise from installing
#   the config's other tools first: an unnamed `mise exec` installed all 35 of them on 2026-10-29.
#   Every refusal is printed, never the first alone, so one run names every package to wait for.
# @option --now <unix seconds> A frozen clock for npm_release_age_verdict (its third argument); nothing else reads the
#   clock. For tests.
# @arg $1 path The mise config directory (`mise -C`), holding the mise.toml whose requests and settings decide.
# @arg $@ string Tools, `npm:<name>` (the config's request) or `npm:<name>@<request>`; at least one.
# @stdout One `refuse: <package>@<version>: <reason>` line per package younger than the window plus 60 s, the reason
#   naming its publish time and the time it clears; `<name>@<version>: no optional dependencies` when there are none;
#   one `pass: <tool>: …` line per tool that passed, naming every package checked with its publish time.
# @stderr The command or field that could not be read, prefixed `npm-cooldown-skew-check:`.
# @exitcode 0 Every package is old enough.
# @exitcode 1 A package is younger than the window plus 60 s, or no optional dependency is built for this runner.
# @exitcode 2 An answer cannot be read: a mise or npm command failed or printed another shape, the window is not
#   `<N>h` or `<N>d`, the version mise resolves or a dependency's is not one SemVer version, the runner's platform or
#   architecture is not one word, or the usage is wrong. Never read as "old enough".
# @example
#   scripts/ci/npm-cooldown-skew-check.sh "${RUNNER_TEMP}/statusline-mise" npm:ccstatusline npm:ccusage
set -euo pipefail

#
# @description Stop with exit 2: an answer cannot be read, so nothing is "old enough".
# @arg $1 string What could not be read, naming the command or the field.
#
function cannot_tell() {
    printf 'npm-cooldown-skew-check: %s; cannot tell whether the tools are old enough\n' "$1" >&2
    exit 2
}

function usage() {
    echo 'usage: npm-cooldown-skew-check.sh [--now <unix seconds>] <mise config dir> <tool>...' >&2
    exit 2
}

now=""
if [[ ${1:-} == --now ]]; then
    (($# >= 2)) || usage
    now=$2
    shift 2
fi
(($# >= 2)) || usage
config_dir=$1
shift
[[ -d ${config_dir} ]] || cannot_tell "${config_dir} is not a directory"

# The directory of this script: a parameter expansion, so no producer's status is at stake.
case ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} in
*/*) here=${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*} ;;
*) here=. ;;
esac
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/npm-release-age.sh
source "${here}/../lib/npm-release-age.sh"

# The one parser of every mise and npm answer: the mode names the shape, stdin carries the answer, and the result is
# printed in the form the shell needs. Exit 0 readable, 1 "not this runner's" (platform only), 2 unreadable with the
# reason on stderr. Read into a variable like npm_release_age_verdict's program, so stdin stays the answer.
parser=""
IFS= read -r -d '' parser << 'PY' || [ -n "${parser}" ] || cannot_tell "the parser program is empty"
import decimal
import json
import re
import sys

mode, *args = sys.argv[1:]
# One word: a platform or architecture as node prints it, or a version request as mise and npm take it.
TOKEN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+-]*", re.ASCII)
# A package name, scoped or not, as the registry lists it.
NAME = re.compile(r"(?:@[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+/)?[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+", re.ASCII)
# One exact SemVer 2.0.0 version, the shape npm_release_age_verdict takes: no build metadata (npm drops it, so
# 1.2.3+build would fetch 1.2.3), and never a tag or a range, which npm would resolve to a version this check never saw.
EXACT = re.compile(
    r"(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)"
    r"(?:-(?:0|[1-9]\d*|\d*[A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*)(?:\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*|\d*[A-Za-z-][0-9A-Za-z-]*))*)?",
    re.ASCII,
)
WINDOW = re.compile(r"(0|[1-9]\d*)([hd])", re.ASCII)


def refuse(reason):
    print(f"npm-cooldown-skew-check: {reason}; cannot tell whether the tools are old enough", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def read_json(source):
    try:
        return json.load(sys.stdin)
    except ValueError:
        refuse(f"{source} printed no JSON")


def strings(value):
    return isinstance(value, list) and all(isinstance(item, str) for item in value)


def requested(tool):
    """`mise tool --json <tool>`: exactly one requested version, the config's."""
    info = read_json(f"mise tool --json {tool}")
    versions = info.get("requested_versions") if isinstance(info, dict) else None
    if not strings(versions) or len(versions) != 1 or not TOKEN.fullmatch(versions[0]):
        refuse(f"mise tool --json {tool} lists {versions!r} as requested_versions, not one version request")
    print(versions[0])


def window():
    """`mise settings get minimum_release_age`: `<N>h` or `<N>d`, printed as the days the verdict takes."""
    text = sys.stdin.read().rstrip("\n")
    match = WINDOW.fullmatch(text)
    if match is None:
        refuse(f"mise settings get minimum_release_age printed {text!r}, not <N>h or <N>d")
    days = decimal.Decimal(match[1])
    if match[2] == "h":
        # Rounded up to the microday the verdict reads, so a window given in hours never shrinks.
        days = (days / 24).quantize(decimal.Decimal("0.000001"), rounding=decimal.ROUND_CEILING)
    print(days.quantize(decimal.Decimal(1)) if days == days.to_integral_value() else days.normalize())


def word(command):
    """`node -p process.platform` or `process.arch`: exactly one word on one line, printed as read."""
    text = sys.stdin.read()
    if text.endswith("\n"):
        text = text[:-1]
    if not TOKEN.fullmatch(text):
        refuse(f"{command} printed {text!r}, not one word")
    print(text)


def version(command):
    """`mise latest npm:<name>@<request>`: exactly one SemVer version on one line, never a tag or a range."""
    text = sys.stdin.read()
    if text.endswith("\n"):
        text = text[:-1]
    if not EXACT.fullmatch(text):
        refuse(f"{command} printed {text!r}, not one exact version")
    print(text)


def optional_dependencies(package):
    """`npm view --json <pkg>@<ver> optionalDependencies`: nothing, or an object of package name to one exact version."""
    text = sys.stdin.read()
    if text.strip() == "":
        return
    try:
        listed = json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        refuse(f"npm view --json {package} optionalDependencies printed no JSON")
    if not isinstance(listed, dict) or not all(
        isinstance(name, str) and NAME.fullmatch(name) and isinstance(version, str) and EXACT.fullmatch(version)
        for name, version in listed.items()
    ):
        refuse(
            f"npm view --json {package} optionalDependencies printed {listed!r},"
            " not an object of package name to one exact version"
        )
    for name in sorted(listed):
        print(name, listed[name])


def platform(system, arch, package):
    """`npm view --json <pkg>@<ver> os cpu`: exit 0 when both lists name this runner, 1 when they do not."""
    shape = read_json(f"npm view --json {package} os cpu")
    lists = [shape.get(field) for field in ("os", "cpu")] if isinstance(shape, dict) else [None, None]
    if not all(strings(entries) for entries in lists):
        refuse(f"npm view --json {package} os cpu printed {shape!r}, not an object whose os and cpu are lists of strings")
    if any(entry.startswith("!") for entries in lists for entry in entries):
        refuse(f"{package} declares a negated os or cpu entry ({shape!r}), a shape this check does not read")
    sys.exit(0 if system in lists[0] and arch in lists[1] else 1)


def published(package, version):
    """`npm view --json <pkg> time`, after the verdict read it: the version's publish time, for the pass line."""
    times = read_json(f"npm view --json {package} time")
    when = times.get(version) if isinstance(times, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(when, str):
        refuse(f"npm view --json {package} time lists no publish time for {version}")
    print(when)


MODES = {
    "requested": requested,
    "window": window,
    "word": word,
    "version": version,
    "optional-dependencies": optional_dependencies,
    "platform": platform,
    "published": published,
}
MODES[mode](*args)
PY

#
# @description Run the parser in one mode on stdin.
# @arg $1 string The mode; the rest are its arguments.
#
function parse() {
    python3 -I -c "${parser}" "$@"
}

#
# @description Print one `npm view --json` answer from the config's npm; exit 2 naming the command when it fails.
# @arg $@ string npm view's arguments after --json.
#
function npm_view() {
    local answer
    answer=$(mise -C "${config_dir}" exec node -- npm view --json "$@") ||
        cannot_tell "mise -C ${config_dir} exec node -- npm view --json $* failed"
    printf '%s' "${answer}"
}

#
# @description Judge one package version against the window through npm_release_age_verdict: a refusal is printed
#   and counted, a pass is recorded with its publish time for the tool's pass line.
# @arg $1 string The package name.
# @arg $2 string The version.
# @arg $3 string `npm view --json <package> time`.
# @set refusals integer Incremented when the package is refused.
# @set checked string The packages that passed so far, for the pass line.
#
function judge() {
    local package=$1 version=$2 times=$3 verdict when status=0
    verdict=$(npm_release_age_verdict "${version}" "${days}" ${now:+"${now}"} <<< "${times}") || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0)
        when=$(parse published "${package}" "${version}" <<< "${times}") || exit 2
        checked="${checked:+${checked}, }${package}@${version} (published ${when})"
        ;;
    1)
        printf 'refuse: %s@%s: %s\n' "${package}" "${version}" "${verdict}"
        refusals=$((refusals + 1))
        ;;
    *) cannot_tell "${package}@${version}: ${verdict:-the release age cannot be told}" ;;
    esac
}

#
# @description Check one tool: the meta package, then every optional dependency built for this runner.
# @arg $1 string `npm:<name>` or `npm:<name>@<request>`.
# @set refused_total integer Incremented by the tool's refusals.
#
function check_tool() {
    local tool=$1 spec name request info version times optional deps dep dep_version shape status matched=0
    case ${tool} in
    npm:?*) ;;
    *) cannot_tell "${tool} is not an npm: tool" ;;
    esac
    spec=${tool#npm:}
    # A scope's leading @ is part of the name; a second @ separates the request.
    case ${spec#@} in
    *@*)
        name=${spec%@*}
        request=${spec##*@}
        ;;
    *)
        name=${spec}
        info=$(mise -C "${config_dir}" tool --json "${tool}") || cannot_tell "mise -C ${config_dir} tool --json ${tool} failed"
        request=$(parse requested "${tool}" <<< "${info}") || exit 2
        ;;
    esac
    version=$(mise -C "${config_dir}" latest "npm:${name}@${request}") ||
        cannot_tell "mise -C ${config_dir} latest npm:${name}@${request} failed"
    version=$(parse version "mise -C ${config_dir} latest npm:${name}@${request}" <<< "${version}") || exit 2
    refusals=0
    checked=""
    times=$(npm_view "${name}" time) || exit 2
    judge "${name}" "${version}" "${times}"
    optional=$(npm_view "${name}@${version}" optionalDependencies) || exit 2
    deps=$(parse optional-dependencies "${name}@${version}" <<< "${optional}") || exit 2
    if [[ -z ${deps} ]]; then
        printf '%s@%s: no optional dependencies\n' "${name}" "${version}"
    else
        while read -r dep dep_version; do
            shape=$(npm_view "${dep}@${dep_version}" os cpu) || exit 2
            status=0
            parse platform "${platform}" "${arch}" "${dep}@${dep_version}" <<< "${shape}" || status=$?
            case ${status} in
            0) ;;
            1) continue ;;
            *) exit 2 ;;
            esac
            matched=1
            times=$(npm_view "${dep}" time) || exit 2
            judge "${dep}" "${dep_version}" "${times}"
        done <<< "${deps}"
        if ((matched == 0)); then
            printf 'refuse: %s@%s: none of its optional dependencies is built for %s/%s\n' "${name}" "${version}" "${platform}" "${arch}"
            refusals=$((refusals + 1))
        fi
    fi
    if ((refusals == 0)); then
        printf 'pass: %s: %s, at least %s and 60 s old\n' "${tool}" "${checked}" "${window}"
    fi
    refused_total=$((refused_total + refusals))
}

window=$(mise -C "${config_dir}" settings get minimum_release_age) ||
    cannot_tell "mise -C ${config_dir} settings get minimum_release_age failed"
days=$(parse window <<< "${window}") || exit 2
platform=$(mise -C "${config_dir}" exec node -- node -p process.platform) ||
    cannot_tell "mise -C ${config_dir} exec node -- node -p process.platform failed"
platform=$(parse word "mise -C ${config_dir} exec node -- node -p process.platform" <<< "${platform}") || exit 2
arch=$(mise -C "${config_dir}" exec node -- node -p process.arch) ||
    cannot_tell "mise -C ${config_dir} exec node -- node -p process.arch failed"
arch=$(parse word "mise -C ${config_dir} exec node -- node -p process.arch" <<< "${arch}") || exit 2

refusals=0
checked=""
refused_total=0
for tool in "$@"; do
    check_tool "${tool}"
done
((refused_total == 0)) || exit 1

# @brief Refuse a lint tool whose version is not the one the mise config pins.
# @description
#   The lint gates run this before they lint (regime-cutover U97): `make shellcheck` for shellcheck and shfmt
#   (scripts/ci/masked-dirname-check.sh parses with shfmt), `make format` for shfmt, ruff and prettier, CI's shfmt
#   and formatting steps for theirs, and run_bats in scripts/run_unit_test.sh for bats before every Bats suite (U127).
#   Each pin is one value in home/dot_mise/config.toml: the `version` of the `[tools."http:shellcheck"]`,
#   `[tools."http:shfmt"]`, `[tools."http:bats"]` or `[tools."http:ruff"]` table, or the exact version of
#   `"npm:prettier"` under `[tools]`. mise installs it on every host, and CI's test jobs install it from a copy of the
#   same file. Releases disagree on findings and formatting (the apt ShellCheck on CI reported SC2015 where the local
#   mise release did not, in U71b and U96), so a run under any other version is refused, naming both, instead of
#   passing locally and failing in CI. The config is read as text, with no TOML library, so the check runs before uv
#   or a recent python3 is on PATH.
# @arg $1 path The mise config that holds the pins (the Makefile and CI pass home/dot_mise/config.toml).
# @arg $@ string The tools to check, after the config: shellcheck, shfmt, bats, ruff or prettier.
# @stdout One line per tool naming the accepted version.
# @exitcode 0 Each tool's `--version` reports its pinned version.
# @exitcode 1 A tool reports another version or none, or fails; or the config cannot be read or pins no version.
# @exitcode 2 No tool is named, or a tool this check does not know.
# @example
#   scripts/ci/pinned-tool-version.sh home/dot_mise/config.toml shfmt ruff prettier
set -euo pipefail

config=${1:-}
if (($# < 2)); then
    printf 'pinned-tool-version: usage: pinned-tool-version.sh <mise config> <tool>...\n' >&2
    exit 2
fi
shift
if [[ ! -r ${config} ]]; then
    printf 'pinned-tool-version: cannot read the mise config %s\n' "${config}" >&2
    exit 1
fi

#
# @description Print the version a config pins for one mise tool: the `version` line of its `[tools."<key>"]` table,
#   or its `"<key>" = "<version>"` line under `[tools]`, indented or not. Every match is printed, so a doubled pin,
#   an indented duplicate included, reads as no pin.
# @arg $1 string The mise tool key, such as http:shfmt or npm:prettier.
# @stdout The matching values, one per line.
# @exitcode 1 When awk cannot read the config.
#
function pinned_version() {
    awk -v key="$1" '
        /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { table = $0; sub(/[[:space:]]*(#.*)?$/, "", table); next }
        table == "[tools.\"" key "\"]" && /^[[:space:]]*version[[:space:]]*=/ {
            value = $0
            sub(/^[[:space:]]*version[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"/, "", value)
            sub(/".*$/, "", value)
            print value
        }
        table == "[tools]" && /^[[:space:]]*"/ {
            entry = $0
            sub(/^[[:space:]]*/, "", entry)
            if (index(entry, "\"" key "\"") != 1) { next }
            value = substr(entry, length(key) + 3)
            if (sub(/^[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"/, "", value)) { sub(/".*$/, "", value) } else { value = "" }
            print value
        }
    ' "${config}"
}

status=0
for tool in "$@"; do
    # The mise key of each tool's pin, and the prefix its `--version` puts before the bare version on one line.
    case ${tool} in
    shellcheck) key=http:shellcheck prefix='version: ' ;;
    shfmt) key=http:shfmt prefix=v ;;
    bats) key=http:bats prefix='Bats ' ;;
    ruff) key=http:ruff prefix='ruff ' ;;
    prettier) key=npm:prettier prefix= ;;
    *)
        printf 'pinned-tool-version: %s is not a pinned lint tool (shellcheck, shfmt, bats, ruff, prettier)\n' "${tool}" >&2
        exit 2
        ;;
    esac
    if ! pin=$(pinned_version "${key}"); then
        printf 'pinned-tool-version: cannot read %s\n' "${config}" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if ! [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+$ ]]; then
        printf 'pinned-tool-version: %s pins no %s version (one exact version for "%s")\n' "${config}" "${tool}" "${key}" >&2
        status=1
        continue
    fi
    if ! banner=$("${tool}" --version 2>&1); then
        printf 'pinned-tool-version: "%s --version" failed; %s pins %s %s\n' "${tool}" "${config}" "${tool}" "${pin}" >&2
        status=1
        continue
    fi
    installed=
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        if [[ ${line} == "${prefix}"* && ${line#"${prefix}"} =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+$ ]]; then
            installed=${line#"${prefix}"}
        fi
    done <<< "${banner}"
    if [[ ${installed} != "${pin}" ]]; then
        printf 'pinned-tool-version: the %s on PATH is version %s, but %s pins %s %s; run "mise install %s" and put it first on PATH\n' \
            "${tool}" "${installed:-unknown}" "${config}" "${tool}" "${pin}" "${key}" >&2
        status=1
        continue
    fi
    printf '==> %s %s, the version %s pins\n' "${tool}" "${pin}" "${config}"
done
exit "${status}"
