# line a 32-bit signed integer, the type editors and the Language Server Protocol address lines with, can name)
# keeps the number far below Python's 4300-digit limit on formatting an int, which an unbounded `1E6000` crossed.
verdict_schema='{
  "title": "pr-audit verdict",
  "description": "The final response of one pr-audit.sh run: the findings, what was reproduced, and the verdict they decide.",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "verdict": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["correct", "incorrect", "blocked"],
      "description": "incorrect when a P0 or P1 finding has weight 10 or more (frequency times severity); correct when none has; blocked when the audit could not be completed."
    },
    "findings": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "priority": { "type": "string", "enum": ["P0", "P1", "P2", "P3"] },
          "confidence": { "type": "string", "enum": ["high", "medium", "low"] },
          "frequency": {
            "type": "integer",
            "minimum": 1,
            "maximum": 10,
            "description": "How often the case arises in the real runs of this repository: 1 never produced by a run, test, incident or user, 10 every run."
          },
          "severity": {
            "type": "integer",
            "minimum": 1,
            "maximum": 10,
            "description": "What it costs when it arises: 1 cosmetic, 10 data loss, a secret leaving the host or a wrong merge."
          },
          "path": {
            "type": "string",
            "pattern": "^[^\\s:]+$",
            "description": "The file, relative to the repository: no colon, no whitespace (the verdict line is read as <path>:<line>: <rationale>, the path its first colon-free token)."
          },
          "line": {
            "type": "integer",
            "minimum": 1,
            "maximum": 2147483647,
            "description": "The exact line of the finding, 1 or more (the first line, for a whole file)."
          },
          "rationale": { "type": "string", "description": "One line." }
        },
        "required": ["priority", "confidence", "frequency", "severity", "path", "line", "rationale"],
        "additionalProperties": false
      }
    },
    "reproduced": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": { "type": "string" },
      "description": "One entry per test or command run, with what it showed."
    },
    "notes": { "type": ["string", "null"] }
  },
  "required": ["verdict", "findings", "reproduced", "notes"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}'

# The reader of the verdict file: `python3 -I -S` with the schema path, the verdict path and the path of the text to
# write. It first refuses the schema itself (naming it) when it uses a keyword or type outside the tables below, since
# the Responses API would then validate the final message by a rule the reader does not know (a bound, for one), and
# the two readings of the schema would differ. It then reads the document as JSON (RFC 8259, through hooks that refuse
# what the json module alone would take: a NaN or Infinity literal, a key written twice, a number outside the exact
# decimal it reads every number as), validates it against the schema (type, enum, bounds, properties, required,
# additionalProperties false, items), applies the decision rule from the findings, writes `verdict.md` whole or not
# at all, and prints the verdict. Any refusal names the file on stderr and exits 3; the lever fails on it (exit 1)
# and prints no verdict. The single quotes keep the Python source for Python, never this shell.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016
verdict_reader='
import decimal
import json
import os
import re
import sys

BLOCKING = ("P0", "P1")
# A weight is a frequency times a severity, each 1 to 10 by the schema. A blocking priority at or above this threshold
# blocks; any priority under it is filed (regime-cutover U125; the number is the one of the AGENTS.md verdict bullet).
WEIGHT_THRESHOLD = 10
# Each verdict and the outcome the findings must derive for it: `incorrect` needs a blocking finding, `correct` and
# `blocked` need none; a filed finding, or a P2 or P3 of any weight, derives nothing (regime-cutover U119, U125). A
# pair outside this table is a contradiction and is refused, never corrected.
ACCEPTED_WITH = {"correct": "correct", "incorrect": "incorrect", "blocked": "correct"}
# The JSON Schema keywords this reader implements: the subset the schema above is written in. Any other keyword in a
# schema is refused before a verdict is read, so a rule can never bind codex and not the lever. `pattern` and
# `minLength` are the path rule (regime-cutover U207 round 2): the verdict line is read by two readers as
# `<path>:<line>: <rationale>` with the path its first colon-free, whitespace-free token, so a path holding a colon or
# whitespace would be written at one location and read at another; it is refused here, where the path is still a
# field, never serialized.
KEYWORDS = frozenset(
    (
        "title",
        "description",
        "type",
        "enum",
        "properties",
        "required",
        "additionalProperties",
        "items",
        "minimum",
        "maximum",
        "minLength",
        "pattern",
    )
)


class Departure(Exception):
    """A text the json module of Python would accept that is not JSON (RFC 8259), or not a number this reader
    represents."""


def number(text):
    """Every JSON number read exactly as its written digits, an integer literal too (the int of Python stops at 4300
    digits with a ValueError, and the bound below must judge the value, not the digit count). A number the decimal
    cannot hold (U106 audit round 4: `1e9999999999999999999` raised InvalidOperation out of the parser) is a refusal."""
    try:
        return decimal.Decimal(text)
    except decimal.DecimalException:
        raise Departure(f"the number {text} is outside what the reader represents") from None


def constant(text):
    """The json module reads `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity`; RFC 8259 section 6 has no such literal (U106 audit
    round 4: `"notes": NaN, "notes": null` was read as a conforming null)."""
    raise Departure(f"{text} is not a JSON value")


def pairs(items):
    """An object whose key appears twice is refused, never read as its last value (RFC 8259 section 4)."""
    seen = set()
    for key, _ in items:
        if key in seen:
            raise Departure(f"the key {json.dumps(key)} appears twice in one object")
        seen.add(key)
    return dict(items)


def is_number(value):
    """A JSON number as the parser below delivers it (an exact Decimal; the bounds of the schema are int literals); a
    bool is never a number."""
    return isinstance(value, (int, decimal.Decimal)) and not isinstance(value, bool)


def is_string(value):
    """A JSON string is a sequence of Unicode scalar values (RFC 8259 section 8.2). The json module decodes an escaped
    lone surrogate (`"\\ud800"`) into a str that UTF-8 cannot encode (U106 audit round 4: it raised in the writing of
    verdict.md and left the file empty), so such a value is not of type string."""
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return False
    try:
        value.encode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeEncodeError:
        return False
    return True


def shown(value):
    return json.dumps(value, default=str)


# Every JSON Schema type (draft 2020-12, section 6.1.1). `integer` is a number with a zero fraction (a JSON number
# without a fractional or exponent part, or whose fractional part is zero), so `1.0` and `1E2` are integers and `1.5`
# is not. The rule is judged on the written digits (U106 audit round 2: the float the json module builds is rounded
# first, so `1.0000000000000001` became 1.0 and `1e-999` became 0.0 and both passed): every number with a fraction or
# exponent is read as an exact Decimal, an integer literal stays int, and the check asks the value, never the type
# the parser chose.
IS_TYPE = {
    "null": lambda value: value is None,
    "boolean": lambda value: isinstance(value, bool),
    "object": lambda value: isinstance(value, dict),
    "array": lambda value: isinstance(value, list),
    "string": is_string,
    "number": is_number,
    "integer": lambda value: is_number(value)
    and (isinstance(value, int) or (value.is_finite() and value == value.to_integral_value())),
}
# The bounds, each with the test a value fails: judged before any formatting of the value (U106 audit round 4: an
# integer of 6001 digits passed the type check and raised in the writing of `path:line`).
BOUNDS = (
    ("minimum", "below", lambda value, bound: value < bound),
    ("maximum", "above", lambda value, bound: value > bound),
)


def refuse(path, reason):
    sys.stderr.write(f"pr-audit.sh: {path} refused: {reason}\n")
    sys.exit(3)


def kinds_of(schema):
    kinds = schema.get("type", [])
    return [kinds] if isinstance(kinds, str) else kinds


def check_schema(schema, where, path):
    """Refuse a schema that steps outside the keyword and type tables, naming the schema file."""
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        refuse(path, f"{where} is not an object")
    for keyword in schema:
        if keyword not in KEYWORDS:
            refuse(path, f"{where} uses the keyword {keyword}, which the verdict reader does not implement")
    for kind in kinds_of(schema):
        if kind not in IS_TYPE:
            refuse(path, f"{where} names the type {json.dumps(kind)}, which the verdict reader does not implement")
    for key, subschema in schema.get("properties", {}).items():
        check_schema(subschema, f"{where}.properties.{key}", path)
    if "items" in schema:
        check_schema(schema["items"], f"{where}.items", path)


def ecma(pattern):
    """A JSON Schema pattern is an ECMA-262 regular expression (draft 2020-12, section 6.4), whose `$` is the end of
    the text alone; the `$` of Python also matches before a final newline, so `^[^\\s:]+$` would pass a path ending
    in a newline and the writer would break the line. A closing `$` is read as `\\Z`, the end of text in Python."""
    return re.sub(r"(?<!\\)\$\Z", r"\\Z", pattern)


def check(value, schema, where, path):
    kinds = kinds_of(schema)
    if kinds and not any(IS_TYPE[kind](value) for kind in kinds):
        allowed = " or ".join(kinds)
        detail = ": it holds a lone surrogate" if "string" in kinds and isinstance(value, str) else ""
        refuse(path, f"{where} is not of type {allowed}{detail}")
    if is_number(value):
        for keyword, side, outside in BOUNDS:
            if keyword in schema and outside(value, schema[keyword]):
                refuse(path, f"{where} is {value}, {side} the {keyword} {schema[keyword]}")
    if "enum" in schema and value not in schema["enum"]:
        allowed = ", ".join(schema["enum"])
        refuse(path, f"{where} is {shown(value)}, not one of {allowed}")
    if isinstance(value, str):
        shortest, pattern = schema.get("minLength"), schema.get("pattern")
        if shortest is not None and len(value) < shortest:
            refuse(path, f"{where} is {shown(value)}, shorter than the minLength {shortest}")
        if pattern is not None and re.search(ecma(pattern), value) is None:
            refuse(path, f"{where} is {shown(value)}, which does not match the pattern {pattern}")
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for key in schema.get("required", []):
            if key not in value:
                refuse(path, f"{where} lacks the required key {key}")
        properties = schema.get("properties", {})
        if schema.get("additionalProperties") is False:
            for key in value:
                if key not in properties:
                    refuse(path, f"{where} has the unknown key {key}")
        for key, subschema in properties.items():
            if key in value:
                check(value[key], subschema, f"{where}.{key}", path)
    if isinstance(value, list) and "items" in schema:
        for index, item in enumerate(value):
            check(item, schema["items"], f"{where}[{index}]", path)


def one_line(text):
    return " ".join(str(text).split())


def write_whole(text_path, text):
    """verdict.md appears whole or not at all: written under a partial name beside it and renamed over the final name.
    A write that fails leaves no verdict.md (U106 audit round 4: a failed write left an empty file at the path the
    lever prints)."""
    partial = f"{text_path}.partial"
    try:
        with open(partial, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(text)
        os.replace(partial, text_path)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        try:
            os.unlink(partial)
        except OSError:
            pass
        refuse(text_path, f"cannot write the verdict text: {error}")


def main():
    schema_path, verdict_path, text_path = sys.argv[1:4]
    try:
        with open(schema_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            schema = json.load(handle)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        refuse(schema_path, f"cannot read the verdict schema: {error}")
    check_schema(schema, "the schema", schema_path)
    try:
        with open(verdict_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            document = json.load(
                handle, parse_float=number, parse_int=number, parse_constant=constant, object_pairs_hook=pairs
            )
    except OSError as error:
        refuse(verdict_path, f"cannot read the verdict file: {error}")
    except ValueError as error:
        refuse(verdict_path, f"not valid JSON: {error}")
    except Departure as error:
        refuse(verdict_path, f"not JSON: {error}")
    check(document, schema, "the verdict", verdict_path)
    verdict = document["verdict"]
    findings = document["findings"]
    blocking = [f for f in findings if f["priority"] in BLOCKING and f["frequency"] * f["severity"] >= WEIGHT_THRESHOLD]
    filed = [f for f in findings if f["frequency"] * f["severity"] < WEIGHT_THRESHOLD]
    derived = "incorrect" if blocking else "correct"
    if ACCEPTED_WITH[verdict] != derived:
        refuse(
            verdict_path,
            f"the verdict.verdict {verdict} contradicts the verdict.findings: {len(blocking)} of priority P0 or P1 "
            f"with weight {WEIGHT_THRESHOLD} or more (weight is frequency times severity; any one means incorrect, "
            "none means correct or blocked; a finding under the threshold is filed and a P2 or P3 changes no verdict)",
        )
    lines = ["## Findings", ""]
    for finding in findings:
        priority, confidence, path, line = (finding[key] for key in ("priority", "confidence", "path", "line"))
        frequency, severity = int(finding["frequency"]), int(finding["severity"])
        # The path passed the pattern of the schema (no colon, no whitespace), so `<path>:<line>` is the location the
        # two readers will read: the first colon-free token. The rationale is free text and is folded to one line.
        rationale = one_line(finding["rationale"])
        lines.append(f"- {priority} ({confidence}) [f{frequency} s{severity}] {path}:{int(line)}: {rationale}")
    if not findings:
        lines.append("- none")
    lines += ["", "## Reproduced", ""]
    lines += [f"- {one_line(entry)}" for entry in document["reproduced"]] or ["- nothing"]
    if document["notes"]:
        lines += ["", "## Notes", "", document["notes"].rstrip()]
    lines += ["", f"Blocking: {len(blocking)}", f"Filed: {len(filed)}", f"Verdict: {verdict}", ""]
    write_whole(text_path, "\n".join(lines))
    print(verdict)


main()
'

schema=${run}/verdict.schema.json
printf '%s\n' "${verdict_schema}" > "${schema}" || fail "cannot write the verdict schema ${schema}"
verdict_json=${run}/verdict.json
verdict=${run}/verdict.md
codex_started=1
status=0
codex_scratch "${audit_timeout}" "${prompt}" "${run}/codex.log" exec --strict-config --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral \
    --ignore-rules "${cyber_program_args[@]}" -C "${work}/cwd" --output-schema "${schema}" -o "${verdict_json}" - ||
    status=$?
((status == 0)) || fail "codex exec exited ${status}; its log is ${run}/codex.log"
[[ -s ${verdict_json} ]] || fail "codex exec wrote no final message to ${verdict_json}; its log is ${run}/codex.log"
# The reader's status decides (standing order 21): a reader that failed or refused yields no verdict, never a default.
value=$("${python}" -I -S -c "${verdict_reader}" "${schema}" "${verdict_json}" "${verdict}") ||
    fail "no verdict was taken from ${verdict_json}; its log is ${run}/codex.log"
[[ ${value} =~ ^(correct|incorrect|blocked)$ ]] || fail "the verdict reader named no verdict for ${verdict_json}: ${value}"
printf '%s\n%s\n' "${verdict}" "Verdict: ${value}"
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-body-edit.sh
# @brief Replace the body of the open pull request of the current branch, the worker seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, the worker seat's lever, allowed only in the form
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-body-edit.sh --body-file *` by `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/worker.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"); the orchestrator's policy denies it. It
#   edits only the pull request of the branch the seat has checked out: `git branch --show-current` must name a
#   branch other than `main`, and `gh pr view --json number,headRefName,state` (the pull request of that branch)
#   must report it as `headRefName` and `OPEN`. The body file is a regular file (not a symlink) of 1 to 65536
#   bytes whose real path is inside `$TMPDIR` or the checkout. The new body must hold exactly one line starting
#   `Program-Unit:`, and it must be `Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>`, the line `regime-ci.py` reads: `<program>` in
#   `regime-init`'s grammar (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) naming a store the checkout holds,
#   `.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/units.tsv` (U71), and a plain unit id (a fix round writes its parent id,
#   `preferences.md` standing order 24); when the current body already carries one such line, the program and the
#   unit must stay the same, so an edit fixes the line or the text but never moves a pull request to another
#   program or unit. Every `## ` heading line and the `Generated with [Claude Code]` footer line of
#   the current body must still be in the new body, so sections are added or rewritten, never dropped. The one
#   write is `gh pr edit <n> --body-file <file>`. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl
#   `alarm`).
# @option --body-file <file> The new body.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `edited pr=<n> branch=<b> program=<program> unit=U<n> sha256=<body sha256>`.
# @exitcode 0 The body was replaced.
# @exitcode 1 A `git` or `gh` read, or the edit, failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, the branch, the pull request's state, the body file, or the body's content.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-body-edit.sh --body-file "$TMPDIR/body.md"
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''             # producer-status: allow the if below takes an empty home as the checkout layout
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check
# The isolated git and the environment scrub come from the library beside this script (U113): the toplevel and the
# current branch are read by a git no caller variable or configuration steers.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh ]] || {
    echo "pr-body-edit.sh: refused: git-isolated.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh"
# shellcheck disable=SC2119 # no name is kept: every GIT_* and transport variable goes
git_env_scrub

[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh ]] || {
    echo "pr-body-edit.sh: refused: read-lib.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/read-lib.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh"

lever='pr-body-edit.sh'
usage='usage: pr-body-edit.sh --body-file <file>'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
unit_line='^Program-Unit: [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}/U[0-9]+$'
footer_re='Generated with \[Claude Code\]\(https://claude\.com/claude-code\)'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Refuse unless $1 is a regular file of 1 to 65536 bytes inside $TMPDIR or the checkout.
# @arg $1 path The body file.
# @set body_path Its real path.
body_file_check() {
    local file=$1 dir root size
    [[ -f ${file} && ! -L ${file} ]] || refuse "the body file is not a regular file: ${file}"
    case ${file} in # lint-comparisons: allow splits the argument at its last slash; the real path is compared below
    */*) dir=${file%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${file}"
    body_path=${dir}/${file##*/}
    size=$(wc -c < "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
    size=${size//[[:space:]]/}
    if ! [[ ${size} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ((size == 0 || size > 65536)); then
        refuse "the body file must hold 1 to 65536 bytes: ${body_path}"
    fi
    for root in "${TMPDIR:-}" "${toplevel}"; do
        [[ -n ${root} && -d ${root} ]] || continue
        root=$(cd "${root}" && pwd -P) || continue    # producer-status: allow a root that cannot be entered holds no body file; the refusal after the loop stands
        [[ ${body_path} == "${root}"/* ]] && return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    done
    refuse "the body file is outside \$TMPDIR and the checkout: ${body_path}"
}

# @description Print the lines of file $2 (CR stripped) that match the ERE $1, one per line. The ERE reaches awk
#   through the environment, since `awk -v` would read its backslashes as escapes.
# @arg $1 string The ERE.
# @arg $2 path The file.
lines_matching() {
    LINES_RE=$1 awk '{ sub(/\r$/, "") } $0 ~ ENVIRON["LINES_RE"]' "$2"
}

[[ $# -eq 2 && $1 == --body-file ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
toplevel=$(git_isolated rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
branch=$(git_isolated branch --show-current) || fail 'git branch --show-current failed'
[[ -n ${branch} ]] || refuse 'HEAD is detached; switch to the branch of your pull request'
[[ ${branch} != main ]] || refuse 'the current branch is main'
body_file_check "$2"
markers=$(lines_matching '^Program-Unit:' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
[[ -n ${markers} && ${markers} != *$'\n'* && ${markers} =~ ${unit_line} ]] ||
    refuse "the body must hold exactly one line 'Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>' (a plain unit id); it holds: ${markers:-none}"
marker=${markers#Program-Unit: }
program=${marker%/*}
unit=${marker##*/}
[[ -f ${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/units.tsv ]] ||
    refuse "the Program-Unit line names ${program}, but the checkout holds no .orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/units.tsv"

view=$(gh_bounded pr view --json number,headRefName,state --jq '[(.number | tostring), .headRefName, .state] | @tsv') ||
    fail "cannot read the pull request of ${branch}"
IFS=$'\t' read -r number head state <<< "${view}"
[[ ${number} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || fail "gh pr view printed no pull request number: ${number}"
[[ ${head} == "${branch}" ]] || refuse "pull request ${number} is the pull request of ${head}, not of the current branch ${branch}"
[[ ${state} == OPEN ]] || refuse "pull request ${number} is ${state}, not OPEN"

current=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pr-body-edit.XXXXXX") || fail 'mktemp failed'
trap 'rm -f "${current}"' EXIT
gh_bounded pr view "${number}" --json body --jq .body > "${current}" || fail "cannot read the body of pull request ${number}"
old_markers=$(lines_matching "${unit_line}" "${current}") || fail "cannot read ${current}"
if [[ -n ${old_markers} && ${old_markers} != *$'\n'* && ${old_markers#Program-Unit: } != "${marker}" ]]; then
    refuse "the current body names ${old_markers#Program-Unit: }; an edit keeps the program and the unit (the new body names ${marker})"
fi
kept=$(lines_matching "^## |${footer_re}" "${current}") || fail "cannot read ${current}"
new_lines=$(lines_matching '' "${body_path}") || refuse "cannot read ${body_path}"
while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ -n ${line} ]] || continue
    grep -Fxq -- "${line}" <<< "${new_lines}" || refuse "the new body drops the line of the current body: ${line}"
done <<< "${kept}"

gh_bounded pr edit "${number}" --body-file "${body_path}" >&2 || fail "gh pr edit ${number} failed"
if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
    digest=$(sha256sum < "${body_path}") || fail "the body was pushed; cannot hash ${body_path} for the report"
else
    digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${body_path}") || fail "the body was pushed; cannot hash ${body_path} for the report"
fi
echo "edited pr=${number} branch=${branch} program=${program} unit=${unit} sha256=${digest%% *}"

# @file pr-close.sh
# @brief Close the pull requests a clean-up table marks `close:`, with the row's text as the comment.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed only in the form
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-close.sh --from-table *` by `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`

#   wrote: a regular file (not a symlink) whose real path is `<store>/handouts/<file>` of one program store, the
#   store chosen by one rule with two forms (regime-cutover U216, store move 2 of 5, handoff/07-store-move-design.md):
#   the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` when that directory exists, the root being the fixed derivation
#   `<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>` the sourced `regime-env` exports (U215); else, until U221 moves
#   the live store of this program there and removes the form, the checkout's own store

}
lever_self_check

# The store root (regime-cutover U216): the program stores lie under `REGIME_STORE_ROOT`, the root the sourced
# regime-env derives from the physical HOME and this checkout's slug (U215) and holds component by component; the
# helper is sourced from the directory this lever runs from and self-checked like a lever (U33), so a rewritten copy
# stops this lever. The call that derives the root comes after this lever's own checkout checks, below.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env ]] || {
    echo "pr-close.sh: refused: regime-env unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/regime-env
. "${LEVER_DIR}/regime-env"

lever='pr-close.sh'
usage='usage: pr-close.sh --from-table <table.md> [--only <pr>]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
header='| PR | branch | opened | files | title | default |'
# The `## Open pull requests` rows as `<pr>\t<branch>\t<default>`; exit 3 for a missing section or header, 4 for a
# row without a `#<n>` PR cell or a backticked branch cell. `\|` inside a cell is text, not a separator.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # awk source, not shell
table_awk='
function trim(s) { sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", s); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", s); return s }
/^## / { if (in_section) { done = 1 } in_section = ($0 == "## Open pull requests"); next }
!in_section || done { next }
/^[ \t]*$/ { if (rows) { done = 1 } next }
!seen_header { if ($0 != header) { exit 3 } seen_header = 1; next }
/^\|( *:?-+:? *\|)+ *$/ { next }
{
    line = $0
    gsub(/\\\|/, "\001", line)
    n = split(line, cell, "|")
    if (n != 8 || trim(cell[1]) != "" || trim(cell[8]) != "") { exit 4 }
    pr = trim(cell[2]); branch = trim(cell[3]); text = trim(cell[7])
    gsub(/\001/, "|", text); gsub(/\t/, " ", text)
    if (pr !~ /^#[1-9][0-9]*$/ || branch !~ /^`[A-Za-z0-9._\/-]+`$/) { exit 4 }
    rows++
    print substr(pr, 2) "\t" substr(branch, 2, length(branch) - 2) "\t" text
}
END { if (!seen_header) { exit 3 } }
'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2; nothing was written to GitHub.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Choose the program store this lever reads (regime-cutover U216, store move 2 of 5,
#   handoff/07-store-move-design.md; U215 gave regime-env the root): the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>`
#   when that directory exists, the root being the fixed derivation `<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>`
#   the sourced regime-env exports after holding every component of it; else the pre-move form
#   `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`, this main checkout's own store, which stands until U221 moves the
#   live store of this program to the root and removes this form. One rule, two forms: while the derived store exists
#   the checkout form is refused (the caller refuses a path naming it, naming both forms), and while it does not the
#   checkout form is read as before U216. The per-component holds of the chain walk (U71) stay and apply to the form
#   chosen: a symbolic link at `<root>/<program>` is refused by name before anything is read through it, an entry
#   there that is not a directory of this user is refused by name, and only an absent one falls through to the
#   checkout chain, whose three components are each a directory of this user and no symlink. The root's own
#   components are held by regime-env (`regime_store_root`). Nothing is written. The form chosen is printed once on
#   stderr (`store: derived <dir>`, or `store: checkout <dir> (pre-move form, removed by U221)`), the line the
#   coordinator reads after the deploy. The same text stands in pr-merge.sh (two levers, standing order 36: no helper
#   file).
# @arg $1 string The program name.
# @set store The chosen store, `pwd -P` form (the root and the toplevel are both physical).
# @set store_form `derived` or `checkout`.
# @set store_derived The derived candidate `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>`.
# @set store_checkout The checkout candidate `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`.
store_resolve() {
    local program=$1 path part
    [[ -n ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT:-} ]] ||
        refuse "regime-env derived no store root for ${toplevel}; the program store is judged under it (U216)"
    store_derived=${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/${program}
    store_checkout=${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}
    [[ ! -L ${store_derived} ]] ||
        refuse "${store_derived} is a symlink; the derived program store is a plain directory of this user under the store root ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}, and nothing is read through a link"
    if [[ -e ${store_derived} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${store_derived} && -O ${store_derived} ]] ||
            refuse "${store_derived} exists but is not a directory of this user; the derived program store under ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT} is read only as one"
        store=${store_derived}
        store_form=derived
        echo "${lever}: store: derived ${store}" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    path=${toplevel}
    for part in .orchestration orchestrate "${program}"; do
        path=${path}/${part}
        [[ -d ${path} && ! -L ${path} && -O ${path} ]] ||
            refuse "${path} is not a directory of this user (a symlink or a missing store); no derived store ${store_derived} exists, so ${lever} reads only the checkout's own store (the pre-move form, until U221)"
    done
    store=${store_checkout}
    store_form=checkout
    echo "${lever}: store: checkout ${store} (pre-move form, removed by U221)" >&2
}

table=''
only=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --from-table)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        table=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    --only)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        only=$2
        shift 2
        ;;
    *) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    esac
done
[[ -n ${table} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
[[ -z ${only} || ${only} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "--only is not a decimal number: ${only}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'

toplevel=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2> /dev/null) || refuse 'not in a git checkout'
toplevel=$(cd "${toplevel}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}"
git_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git directory'
common_dir=$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir) || refuse 'cannot read the git common directory'
git_dir=$(cd "${git_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${git_dir}"
common_dir=$(cd "${common_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${common_dir}"
[[ ${git_dir} == "${common_dir}" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
    refuse "${toplevel} is a linked worktree; run from the main checkout, where the orchestrator writes its tables"
# U216: regime-env derives `REGIME_STORE_ROOT` for this checkout (its own refusals name this lever). This lever reads
# nothing in the hcom store, so the store's `origin` binding is not asked of it (`--unbound-ok`; the dotfiles program
# runs on the pre-U33 store pair and its derived hcom store `~/.local/state/hcom/dotfiles` carries no `origin`, so the
# bound form would stop every run on this host); the collision refusal (an `origin` naming another checkout) and
# every store-root hold stay. The helper's refusal (return 1) is this lever's refusal status, exit 2.
regime_env pr-close.sh --unbound-ok || exit 2
[[ -f ${table} && ! -L ${table} ]] || refuse "the table is not a regular file: ${table}"
case ${table} in
*/*) table_dir=${table%/*} ;;
*) table_dir=. ;;
esac
[[ -n ${table_dir} ]] || table_dir=/
table_dir=$(cd "${table_dir}" && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve the directory of ${table}"
# U216: the table lies in `<store>/handouts/` of one program store, the store store_resolve chooses for the program
# the path names. The directory (`pwd -P` form) is read as `<parent>/<program>/handouts`, the parent one of the two
# roots (the derived store root, or the checkout's `.orchestration/orchestrate`) and the program in the store grammar;
# any other place is refused naming both forms before the store is judged. Then the store chosen for that program must
# be the directory's own `<parent>/<program>`: a table in the checkout form while the derived store exists is refused
# naming both. The root and the toplevel are physical paths, so the comparisons are of `pwd -P` forms throughout.
[[ -n ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT:-} ]] || refuse "regime-env derived no store root for ${toplevel}; the table's store is judged under it (U216)"
program_re='^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$'
store_parent=''
case ${table_dir} in # lint-comparisons: allow the table directory, the root and the toplevel are all pwd -P forms
"${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}"/*/handouts) store_parent=${REGIME_STORE_ROOT} ;;
"${toplevel}"/.orchestration/orchestrate/*/handouts) store_parent=${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate ;;
*) refuse "the table is not under ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>/handouts/ (the derived store, U216) or ${toplevel}/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/handouts/ (the pre-move form, until U221): ${table_dir}" ;;
esac
program=${table_dir#"${store_parent}"/}
program=${program%/handouts}
[[ ${program} =~ ${program_re} ]] || refuse "the program component of ${table_dir} is outside ${program_re}"
store_resolve "${program}"
[[ ${store_parent}/${program} == "${store}" ]] || { # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms (the physical root and toplevel)
    case ${store_form} in
    derived) refuse "the table ${table} lies in the checkout store ${store_checkout}/handouts/, the pre-move form, but the derived store ${store} exists and is the program's store (U216); the checkout form is refused while it exists, until U221 removes it" ;;
    *) refuse "the table ${table} lies in ${store_parent}/${program}/handouts/, which is not the program's store ${store} (no derived store ${store_derived} exists, so the pre-move checkout form stands until U221)" ;;
    esac
}

status=0
rows=$(awk -v header="${header}" "${table_awk}" "${table_dir}/${table##*/}") || status=$?
case ${status} in
0) ;;
3) refuse "no '## Open pull requests' section with the header ${header} in ${table}" ;;
4) refuse "a row of '## Open pull requests' in ${table} has no #<n> PR cell or backticked branch cell" ;;
*) refuse "cannot read ${table} (awk exited ${status})" ;;
esac

selected=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text; do
    [[ -n ${pr} && ${text} == close:* ]] || continue
    [[ -z ${only} || ${pr} == "${only}" ]] || continue
    selected+=("${pr}"$'\t'"${branch}"$'\t'"${text}")
done <<< "${rows}"
if ((${#selected[@]} == 0)); then
    [[ -n ${only} ]] && refuse "the table has no close: row for pull request ${only}"
    refuse "the table has no row whose default starts with close:"
fi

closable=()
refused=0
for row in "${selected[@]}"; do
    IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text <<< "${row}"
    view=$(gh_bounded pr view "${pr}" --json state,headRefName --jq '[.state, .headRefName] | @tsv') ||
        fail "cannot read pull request ${pr}; nothing was closed"
    IFS=$'\t' read -r state head <<< "${view}"
    if [[ ${state} != OPEN ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=state ${state:-unreadable}, not OPEN"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    if [[ ${head} != "${branch}" ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=head branch ${head} is not the table's ${branch}"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    sharing=$(gh_bounded pr list --state open --head "${branch}" --json number --jq '[.[].number | tostring] | join(",")') ||
        fail "cannot list the open pull requests of ${branch}; nothing was closed"
    if [[ ${sharing} != "${pr}" ]]; then
        echo "refused pr=${pr} reason=branch ${branch} is the head of open pull requests ${sharing:-none}"
        refused=$((refused + 1))
        continue
    fi
    closable+=("${row}")
done

closed=0
for row in ${closable[@]+"${closable[@]}"}; do
    IFS=$'\t' read -r pr branch text <<< "${row}"
    gh_bounded pr close "${pr}" --comment "${text}" >&2 || {
        echo "summary closed=${closed} refused=${refused}"
        fail "gh pr close ${pr} failed after ${closed} closed"
    }
    echo "closed pr=${pr} branch=${branch}"
    closed=$((closed + 1))
done
echo "summary closed=${closed} refused=${refused}"
((refused == 0)) || exit 2

docs.text: Regime-cutover U71 (finding F010), the orchestrator seat's only merge path: home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml allows ~/.local/bin/common/pr-merge.sh * and denies the gh pr merge command text (a speed bump: text rows do not stop a glob spelling; a seat running gh itself is the residual unit U88 removes). <pr> is decimal and checked before the first gh call. The lever runs in the main checkout (a linked worktree is refused) and reads one program store, chosen by one rule with two forms (regime-cutover U216, store move 2 of 5, handoff/07-store-move-design.md): the derived store ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program> when that directory exists, the root being the fixed derivation <physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug> the sourced regime-env exports (U215); else, until U221 moves the live store of this program there and removes the form, the checkout's own store <toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program> (the pre-move form; store_resolve, which prints the form chosen on stderr). The store's ledger.tsv (header ts unit pr head_sha verdict verifier evidence), <program> taken from the pull request body's one Program-Unit: <program>/U<n> line, no directory of that chain nor the ledger a symlink, each owned by this user; --records must resolve (pwd -P) to exactly the chosen store (one naming the other form is refused naming both), so a ledger written anywhere else is never read. It reads gh pr view <pr> --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid,isDraft and refuses unless the pull request is OPEN, not a draft and based on main. The verdict is the newest ledger.tsv row whose pr is <pr> and whose head_sha is the full 40-hex sha it judged (a short sha never matches); newest by the row's ts column parsed as a time (the later line at an equal ts), never by its place in the file (U122 round 5). The ledger is read by the checkout's scripts/orchestrator/ledger.py, the one reader of the ledger (U122 round 6: this lever's own awk checked the ts for its shape alone, so a carried row dated hour 25 outranked a valid incorrect row), run as python3 -I -S with its status read, as pr-audit.sh runs the checkout's readers: a store it cannot read as data (a header that is not the store's, a row with another column count or an empty ts, unit, pr, head_sha or verdict cell, a ts strptime does not read as YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ) is refused naming the file and line, and no python3 on PATH or no reader in the checkout is a refusal too. It must start with the word correct, so a later incorrect or blocked row for the same head voids an earlier correct, or with the word carried (regime-cutover U122, standing order 38): then its evidence must hold carried <earlier head> <this head> <sha256>, the line scripts/orchestrator/audit-carry.py printed when this head's diff against its merge base equalled the earlier head's (U180: a note may follow the digest after a space, ;, ,, . or ), and after nothing else), the earlier head is another sha than this one, and the newest row (by ts) for the earlier head must itself be correct (the digest lever carries the earlier head's verdict whatever it says, round 5, so a carry from an incorrect head is a row this gate refuses naming that head); the verdict file and the dispositions the gate then reads are the earlier head's, since its findings are this head's. That sha is always the current head: there is no silent carry-over (U71 audit round 10), so a head that pr-update-branch.sh moved gets a fresh audit or a carried row the coordinator wrote from the digest lever's output. The row alone is not enough (U119 round 2, Codex thread 4419039271): since standing order 35 a correct verdict may carry P2 and P3 findings, and since U125 filed ones of any priority, so the lever also opens the store's verdicts/<unit>-<sha8>.md of the audited head, <unit> the ledger row's unit column (round 2: the body's unit or a U<n>b fix unit of it, standing order 24; a U71b row's verdict is U71b-<sha8>.md, and a row of any other unit is refused) (absent, a symlink or unreadable is a refusal: a merge needs the verdict file, not only the row) and parses its leading ## Findings section, from the first ## Findings line to the next ## heading (a later ## Findings line, in the Notes or a rationale, is text; U119 round 4), the lines pr-audit.sh's reader writes since U125 (- P<n> (<confidence>) [f<n> s<n>] <path>:<line>: <rationale>: the frequency and severity scores, each one of 1 to 10, read by value and never second-guessed, then the path, the first token after ] that holds no colon and no whitespace, the line the digits after it, and the rationale the free text after the following :, or - none; a line without the [f<n> s<n>] token is refused naming it, since this reader always writes it and a verdict of the unscored reader belongs to a merged unit, never to a merge head). That file is the verdict.md of pr-audit.sh, the audit route (hcom-orchestration SKILL step 4, U119 round 3), copied into the store; a verdict of the retired omp-run.sh audit route has no ## Findings heading, is refused by name, and belongs to a merged unit, never to a merge head. A finding's weight is its frequency times its severity, and WEIGHT_THRESHOLD (10, the number of the AGENTS.md verdict bullet and of the reader) decides what the gate asks of each line (U125): a line of any priority with weight under the threshold is filed, reported in the verdict and the code left as it is, so it needs no row; every P2 or P3 line at or above it needs a row of the store's dispositions.tsv (header ts unit head_sha priority path line disposition reference) with the same unit, full head sha, priority, path and line (the finding's whole identity, the key audit-carry.py joins by as well; U122 round 3) whose disposition is residual and whose reference unit=U<n> gate=<clause> names a units.tsv row, or whose disposition is fixed and whose reference starts with the 40-hex sha of the head being merged while that head is carried (U180: a fixed row holds for the head it judges only when the head being merged is the fixing head under a carried row, which can only be a body fix, since a code change would have changed the digest; the sha is the reference's first token, read as 40 hex followed by the end or a character outside hex, and compared whole). A fixed row naming any other head, or any fixed row when the head being merged is the audited head itself, names the later head that fixed the finding and never satisfies the gate for the head it judges. The first finding without such a row is named in the refusal. A P0 or P1 line at or above the threshold under a correct row, a ## Findings line of another shape or without its scores, a score outside 1 to 10, a line whose first token after ] is no <path>:<line>: with a path free of colons and whitespace, a verdict file whose last line is not Verdict: correct, and a dispositions.tsv or units.tsv row whose column count is not its header's or whose required column is empty are refusals naming the line (standing order 21); the rows are split by awk on the tab alone, since bash's read merges adjacent tabs (U119 round 3). Every store path the lever opens (ledger.tsv, verdicts/, the verdict file, dispositions.tsv, units.tsv) must be a regular file or directory of this user and no symlink, and --records must resolve to exactly the store store_resolve chose for the body's program (the derived store, or the checkout's own store while no derived one exists). The lever reads no local git objects or refs; it decides from gh reads and the store alone, and git only names the checkout (rev-parse --show-toplevel, --absolute-git-dir, --git-common-dir). CI is gh pr checks <pr> --json bucket,name between two reads of headRefOid that must both equal the head (and whose second read must still report base main: --match-head-commit pins only the head): at least one check, every bucket pass or skipping, every name of REQUIRED_CHECKS listed with bucket pass, and gh exiting 0; a pending, failed or cancelled check is a refusal naming it, and a required check that is not listed, or is listed with any bucket but pass (skipping satisfies only a check that is not required), is a refusal naming it apart from the red ones (CI has no result for: ...). REQUIRED_CHECKS (regime-cutover U330) is the eight required status contexts of the main ruleset main integration gate (24397953), copied as GitHub names them (measured 2026-11-07T03:34Z, decisions row 2026-11-07T03:35:00Z): a constant in the lever and not a read of the rulesets API at merge time, because that read would be one more gh call in the merge window and a ruleset the operator edits is not the program's record of what a merge needs; tests.unit.test_pr_merge holds the array equal to the contexts recorded from that measurement, so a drift between the lever and the ruleset fails CI, not a merge. Before U330 the gate asked only that every listed check be green, so PR 708's head 792604f9, which conflicted with main and got none of its pull_request workflows (GitHub runs them on the merge ref), would have merged on regime, GitGuardian and CodeRabbit alone with no test leg run (decisions row 2026-11-07T01:45:00Z). The one write is gh pr merge <pr> --squash --match-head-commit <head>, so GitHub refuses the merge if the head moved after these reads; it never passes --admin, --auto or --delete-branch. After the merge, or after a merge error, gh pr view <pr> --json state,mergeCommit,baseRefName,headRefOid decides: MERGED into main at the audited head prints the receipt (the merge happened; never run the merge twice); another state, another base, or another merged head (a merge someone else made after the pinned one failed) is a failure with no receipt that names both shas. The thread check (pr-threads-check.sh) stays a separate step before this lever (hcom-orchestration SKILL step 6). Each gh call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl alarm). Since regime-cutover U147 the lever also requires the unit's security-audit sweep at the audited head, and since U244 of every unit (the AGENTS.md Audit sweep rule: every unit and every program milestone gets one sweep before its pull request merges; U147 read the unit's brief for the trust-boundary mark to tell a trust-boundary unit from the rest, and with one class that reading is gone). After require_verdict_row and before the checks read and the one write, the checkout's ledger.py sweep <unit> <audited head> prints the newest row of the unit or a fix unit of it at the audited head whose verdict starts with the word sweep (pr -, verifier the skill and its pin, evidence the findings file under the store), or none, which is a refusal naming the unit, the head and the rule; an exit-0 answer that is neither none nor one row of four tab-separated fields with a ts is a refusal naming the reader and the answer. The row must be the exact row the rule defines: pr -, verifier the two words security-audit-skill <pin> with the pin word, 8 or more lowercase hex, a prefix of the assets.security-audit-skill.pin of the manifest the self-check read (one probe, sweep_pin_probe, run as python3 -I -S -c over LEVER_MANIFEST), and evidence whose first ;-separated field names a findings file sweeps/<path>.json that is a regular file of this user under the store (never opened); the reader refuses any other sweep row as a malformed store, and a pin that is no prefix or a findings file that is missing, a symlink or another user's is a refusal naming it, so a row written by hand with another verifier admits nothing. The audited head is the one require_verdict_row set, so a head moved under a carried row needs no second sweep. The lever reads no brief, never the findings file a sweep row names, and judges no sweep's content.

#   checked before the first `gh` call. The lever runs in the main checkout (a linked worktree is refused) and reads
#   one program store, chosen by one rule with two forms (regime-cutover U216, store move 2 of 5,
#   handoff/07-store-move-design.md): the derived store `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` when that directory exists,
#   the root being the fixed derivation `<physical HOME>/.local/state/regime-store/<slug>` the sourced `regime-env`
#   exports (U215); else, until U221 moves the live store of this program there and removes the form, the checkout's
#   own store `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>` (the pre-move form; `store_resolve`, which prints the
#   form chosen on stderr). The store's `ledger.tsv` (header
#   `ts unit pr head_sha verdict verifier evidence`), `<program>` taken from the pull request body's one
#   `Program-Unit: <program>/U<n>` line, no directory of that chain nor the ledger a symlink, each owned by this user;
#   `--records` must resolve (`pwd -P`) to exactly the chosen store (one naming the other form is refused naming
#   both), so a ledger written anywhere else is never read. It reads
#   `gh pr view <pr> --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid,isDraft` and refuses unless the pull request is `OPEN`, not a
#   draft and based on `main`. The verdict is the newest `ledger.tsv` row whose `pr` is `<pr>` and whose `head_sha` is

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''             # producer-status: allow the if below takes an empty home as the checkout layout
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
