<pre><code>#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-threads-check.sh
# @brief Refuse a merge while a review thread of the pull request has no disposition, read-only.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28 (ADDENDUM 2), the orchestrator seat's pre-merge check, allowed by the row
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-threads-check.sh *` of `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`; the
#   `hcom-orchestration` SKILL runs it before the merge command (step 6). It lists every review thread of the
#   pull request (GraphQL `reviewThreads`, read-only; more than 100 threads, or more than 100 comments in one,
#   is a refusal, never a partial read) and requires `--head` to be the pull request's current `headRefOid` and
#   a commit in this checkout (`git fetch` first). Every thread, resolved or not (GitHub's `isResolved` alone
#   proves nothing, U28b F1), passes only when the first non-blank line of its newest reply is a disposition of
#   `preferences.md` standing order 22 and that reply's author is a maintainer of the repository: GitHub's
#   `authorAssociation` of the comment is `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR` (`maintainer_associations` below, named
#   once; U124 round 3). A newest reply by anyone else leaves the thread `open (newest reply by <login>, association
#   <value>: not a maintainer)` whatever its text, since the forms are public and the reply is text anyone with a
#   GitHub account wrote. The forms, checked here:
#   `fixed: <sha>` when `<sha>` is `--head` or an ancestor of it and was committed after the thread's first
#   comment (so a thread opened after the head cannot be `fixed`); `refuted: <text>` citing a URL or a
#   `file:line`; `residual: unit=U<n> gate=<clause>` when the finding is P2 or P3 (the `![P<n> Badge]` of its
#   first comment; no badge counts as P1) and `units.tsv` in `--records` has the row `U<n>`; or
#   `residual: operator=<ts>` when `decisions.tsv` in `--records` has a row at `<ts>`, the only residual for a P1;
#   or `filed: f=<n> s=<n> <reason>` (regime-cutover U124, the weighted finding rule of AGENTS.md "Audit") for a
#   thread of any priority when both scores are whole numbers from 1 to 10 and their product, the finding's weight,
#   is under WEIGHT_THRESHOLD below, the one place this file names that number; a weight at or above it is refused
#   naming the product. Each score is accepted by its decimal string (`^(10|[1-9])$`) before any arithmetic, so a
#   decimal past bash's range cannot wrap into one (U124 round 2); a `filed:` of any other shape (a score outside
#   that grammar, a missing score, no reason) is a malformed reply, refused naming what is wrong and quoting the line.
#   The reason is the text after `s=<n>` with the whitespace around it trimmed and must hold a character that is not
#   whitespace (`filed: f=1 s=1  reason`, two spaces, holds; U125 round d), judged on the reply's own text: the
#   listing's `@tsv` writes a tab as the two characters `\t`, and `disposition` decodes the line before it reads it,
#   so a tab-only reason is a missing reason, not a reason of two characters (U124 round 3). A reply whose first line
#   is blank is judged by its first non-blank line, and a reply of blank lines alone is `open` naming its author's
#   login and association as any reply is (U125 round d).
#   A residual without `--records` is a refusal. Any other newest reply, or none, is a refusal: the remedy is a
#   `U<n>b` TASK or a `pr-thread-reply.sh` disposition, never a merge. `<owner>/<repo>` comes from
#   `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`. Each `gh` call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @option --head <sha> The head the orchestrator is about to merge (40 hex).
# @option --records <dir> The program's records directory, holding `units.tsv` and `decisions.tsv`.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One line per thread, `thread comment=<id> severity=<P0-P3> state=<disposition>`, then
#   `summary threads=<n> open=<n>`.
# @exitcode 0 Every thread carries a valid disposition.
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` or `git` read failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, a moved or unknown head, an unread page, or at least one thread without a valid
#   disposition (its line says `state=open`).
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-threads-check.sh 480 --head 907240ec0f2b1f8b0a6a8b1f1c0b3f0d0e2a4b6c --records .orchestration/orchestrate/regime-cutover
set -euo pipefail

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''             # producer-status: allow the if below takes an empty home as the checkout layout
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}
lever_self_check
# The isolated git and the environment scrub come from the library beside this script (U113): the ancestry and the
# commit dates below are read in the checkout by a git no caller variable or configuration steers.
[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh ]] || {
    echo "pr-threads-check.sh: refused: git-isolated.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/git-isolated.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/git-isolated.sh"
# shellcheck disable=SC2119 # no name is kept: every GIT_* and transport variable goes
git_env_scrub

[[ -r ${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh ]] || {
    echo "pr-threads-check.sh: refused: read-lib.sh unreadable beside this script: ${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh" >&2
    exit 2
}
# shellcheck source=scripts/orchestrator/read-lib.sh
. "${LEVER_DIR}/read-lib.sh"

lever='pr-threads-check.sh'
usage='usage: pr-threads-check.sh <pr> --head <sha> [--records <dir>]'
gh_timeout=${PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT:-60}
# The weighted finding rule (AGENTS.md "Audit", regime-cutover U124): a `filed:` reply holds when frequency times
# severity is under this number. AGENTS.md names the same number once in its verdict bullet, and
# tests/unit/test_review_rules.py keeps the two equal.
WEIGHT_THRESHOLD=10
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # GraphQL variables, not shell
threads_query='query($owner: String!, $name: String!, $pr: Int!) {
  repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {
    pullRequest(number: $pr) {
      headRefOid
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        pageInfo { hasNextPage }
        nodes { isResolved comments(first: 100) { totalCount nodes { databaseId createdAt body authorAssociation author { login } } } }
      }
    }
  }
}'
# `head <sha> <hasNextPage>`, then per thread `<first id> <resolved> <created epoch> <P0-P3 or -> <count> <newest
# reply's authorAssociation or -> <its author's login or -> <newest reply's first non-blank line>` (TSV; the reply is
# last because it may be empty, and `@tsv` writes a tab in it as `\t`, which `disposition` decodes; a line is blank
# when it holds no character outside whitespace, so a reply opened by an empty line is read at its text).
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq source, not shell
threads_jq='.data.repository.pullRequest
  | (["head", .headRefOid, (.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage | tostring)] | @tsv),
    (.reviewThreads.nodes[] | .comments as $c | [($c.nodes[0].databaseId | tostring), (.isResolved | tostring),
      ($c.nodes[0].createdAt | fromdateiso8601 | tostring),
      ([($c.nodes[0].body // "") | capture("!\\[P(?<p>[0-3]) Badge\\]") | "P" + .p] | first // "-"),
      ($c.totalCount | tostring),
      (($c.nodes[1:] | last) as $reply | ($reply.authorAssociation // "-"), ($reply.author.login // "-"),
        (($reply.body // "") | split("\n") | map(rtrimstr("\r")) | map(select(test("\\S"))) | (.[0] // "")))] | @tsv)'

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2
    exit 2
}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read failed.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Succeed when the TSV file $1 has a row whose first field is $2.
# @arg $1 path The file.
# @arg $2 string The key.
# @exitcode 0 Found. 1 Not found. 2 Unreadable.
has_row() {
    [[ -r $1 ]] || return 2
    ROW_KEY=$2 awk -F '\t' '$1 == ENVIRON["ROW_KEY"] { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$1" || return 1
}

# @description Print the disposition a thread's newest reply carries, or `open (<why>)`.
# @arg $1 int The created epoch of the thread's first comment.
# @arg $2 string Its severity, P0-P3 or `-`.
# @arg $3 string The `authorAssociation` of the newest reply's author (GitHub's enum), or `-` without a reply.
# @arg $4 string The newest reply's author login, or `-`.
# @arg $5 string The first non-blank line of the newest reply as the listing's `@tsv` escaped it; decoded here before
#   any read.
disposition() {
    local created=$1 severity=$2 association=$3 login=$4 line='' fix fix_time status frequency severity_score weight why
    # The associations GitHub gives a maintainer's comment (U124 round 3); a reply by anyone else closes nothing.
    local maintainer_associations='^(OWNER|MEMBER|COLLABORATOR)$'
    local fixed='^fixed: ([0-9a-f]{40})( |$)'
    local refuted='^refuted: .*(https://[^[:space:]]+|[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)*:[0-9]+)'
    local unit='^residual: unit=(U[0-9]+[a-z]?) gate=[^[:space:]]'
    local operator='^residual: operator=([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z)$'
    local filed='^filed: f=([^[:space:]]+) s=([^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]'
    local filed_scores='^filed: f=[^[:space:]]+ s=[^[:space:]]+[[:space:]]*$'
    local score_re='^(10|[1-9])$'
    # `@tsv` wrote a tab as `\t`, a carriage return as `\r` and a backslash as `\\`, and nothing else starts with a
    # backslash in its output; `%b` reads those three back, so the regexes below see the reply's own characters and
    # a tab-only reason is whitespace, not the two characters `\t` (U124 round 3). An empty reply is left as the
    # empty string above: `printf -v` with nothing to print leaves its variable unset.
    [[ -z $5 ]] || printf -v line '%b' "$5"
    # A reply exists when the listing names its author's association (`-` without one), and its author must be a
    # maintainer whatever the reply says, a reply of blank lines alone included (U125 round d).
    if [[ ${association} != - && ! ${association} =~ ${maintainer_associations} ]]; then
        echo "open (newest reply by ${login}, association ${association}: not a maintainer)"
        return
    fi
    if [[ ${line} =~ ${fixed} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        git_isolated cat-file -e "${fix}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} is not a commit here)"
            return
        }
        status=0
        git_isolated merge-base --is-ancestor "${fix}" "${head}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) ;;
        1)
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} is not in the head)"
            return
            ;;
        *) fail "git merge-base --is-ancestor ${fix} ${head} failed" ;;
        esac
        fix_time=$(git_isolated show -s --format=%ct "${fix}") || fail "git show ${fix} failed"
        if ((fix_time < created)); then
            echo "open (fixed: ${fix} predates the finding)"
            return
        fi
        echo "fixed ${fix}"
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${refuted} ]]; then
        echo refuted
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${unit} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ ${severity} == P2 || ${severity} == P3 ]] || {
            echo "open (residual: unit= is for P2 and P3; this is ${severity/-/P1 (no badge)})"
            return
        }
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check units.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/units.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual ${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no units.tsv row ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/units.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ ${line} =~ ${operator} ]]; then
        fix=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
        [[ -n ${records} ]] || refuse "a residual needs --records to check decisions.tsv"
        status=0
        has_row "${records}/decisions.tsv" "${fix}" || status=$?
        case ${status} in
        0) echo "residual operator=${fix}" ;;
        1) echo "open (residual: no decisions.tsv row at ${fix})" ;;
        *) fail "cannot read ${records}/decisions.tsv" ;;
        esac
    elif [[ ${line} == filed:* ]]; then
        # The shape, then each score by its decimal string (score_re) before any arithmetic: bash evaluates a name or
        # a subscript inside `(( ))` and wraps a decimal past its range (U124 round 2: f=18446744073709551617 read as
        # 1), and the reply is text anyone with a GitHub account wrote. A refusal names the fault and quotes the line.
        why=''
        if [[ ${line} =~ ${filed} ]]; then
            frequency=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
            severity_score=${BASH_REMATCH[2]}
            if ! [[ ${frequency} =~ ${score_re} ]]; then
                why="f=${frequency} is not a whole number from 1 to 10"
            elif ! [[ ${severity_score} =~ ${score_re} ]]; then
                why="s=${severity_score} is not a whole number from 1 to 10"
            fi
        elif [[ ${line} =~ ${filed_scores} ]]; then
            why='the reason is missing'
        else
            why='a score is missing'
        fi
        if [[ -n ${why} ]]; then
            echo "open (filed: reply needs f=<1..10> s=<1..10> <reason>; ${why}; got: ${line})"
            return
        fi
        weight=$((frequency * severity_score))
        ((weight < WEIGHT_THRESHOLD)) || {
            echo "open (filed: f=${frequency} s=${severity_score} weighs ${weight}, not under ${WEIGHT_THRESHOLD}; fix it, or answer refuted: or residual:)"
            return
        }
        echo "filed f=${frequency} s=${severity_score} weight=${weight}"
    elif [[ -z ${line} && ${association} == - ]]; then
        echo 'open (no reply)'
    elif [[ -z ${line} ]]; then
        echo "open (the newest reply by ${login}, association ${association}, holds no text)"
    else
        echo 'open (the newest reply is not a disposition)'
    fi
}

pr=''
head=''
records=''
while (($#)); do
    case $1 in
    --head | --records)
        (($# >= 2)) || refuse "${usage}"
        if [[ $1 == --head ]]; then
            head=$2
        else
            records=$2
        fi
        shift 2
        ;;
    -*) refuse "${usage}" ;;
    *)
        [[ -z ${pr} ]] || refuse "${usage}"
        pr=$1
        shift
        ;;
    esac
done
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr:-none}; ${usage}"
[[ ${head} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || refuse "--head is not a 40-hex sha: ${head:-none}"
[[ -z ${records} || (-f ${records}/units.tsv && -f ${records}/decisions.tsv) ]] ||
    refuse "--records holds no units.tsv and decisions.tsv: ${records}"
[[ ${gh_timeout} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse 'PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT must be a positive integer'
git_isolated cat-file -e "${head}^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || refuse "${head} is not a commit in this checkout; git fetch first"

repo=$(gh_bounded repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner) || fail 'gh repo view failed'
[[ ${repo} =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]] || fail "gh repo view printed no owner/repo: ${repo}"
listing=$(gh_bounded api graphql -f "query=${threads_query}" -f "owner=${repo%%/*}" -f "name=${repo#*/}" \
    -F "pr=${pr}" --jq "${threads_jq}") || fail "cannot list the review threads of pull request ${pr}"

threads=0
open=0
seen_head=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r first resolved created severity count association login reply; do
    if [[ ${first} == head ]]; then
        [[ ${resolved} == "${head}" ]] || refuse "the head of pull request ${pr} is ${resolved}, not ${head}"
        [[ ${created} == false ]] || refuse "pull request ${pr} has more than 100 review threads; check it by hand"
        seen_head=1
        continue
    fi
    ((seen_head)) || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} does not start with its head"
    [[ ${first} =~ ^[0-9]+$ && ${created} =~ ^[0-9]+$ && ${count} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] ||
        fail "unreadable thread row: ${first}"
    ((count <= 100)) || refuse "the thread of comment ${first} has more than 100 comments; check it by hand"
    threads=$((threads + 1))
    # A resolved thread is judged like an open one (U28b F1): GitHub's isResolved says someone clicked, not why.
    state=$(disposition "${created}" "${severity}" "${association}" "${login}" "${reply}") || exit $?
    if [[ ${resolved} == true ]]; then
        case ${state} in
        open*) state="open (resolved without a valid disposition: ${state#open (}" ;;
        *) state="resolved ${state}" ;;
        esac
    fi
    [[ ${state} != open* ]] || open=$((open + 1))
    echo "thread comment=${first} severity=${severity/-/none} state=${state}"
done <<< "${listing}"
((seen_head)) || fail "the listing of pull request ${pr} has no head"
echo "summary threads=${threads} open=${open}"
((open == 0)) || exit 2
</code></pre>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file pr-update-branch.sh
# @brief Merge main into an open pull request's branch (`gh pr update-branch`), the orchestrator seat's lever.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U28, a lever of the omp orchestrator seat, allowed by the row
#   `~/.local/bin/common/pr-update-branch.sh *` of `home/dot_agents/omp/policies/orchestrator.yml`
#   (scripts/orchestrator/README.md, "Seat levers for GitHub writes"). `<pr>` is decimal and checked before the
#   first `gh` call. `gh pr view <pr> --json state,baseRefName,headRefOid` must report `OPEN` and base `main`,
#   else the lever refuses; the one write is `gh pr update-branch <pr>`, GitHub's merge form (never `--rebase`,
#   which rewrites the worker's branch), and the head is read again afterwards. The new head needs its own audit
#   and `correct` ledger row before `pr-merge.sh` merges it (U71: no verdict carries over from the old head). Each
#   `gh` call is bounded
#   by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds (perl `alarm`).
# @arg $1 int The pull request number.
# @env PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT Seconds per `gh` call (default 60).
# @stdout One receipt line: `updated pr=<pr> old=<head before> new=<head after>`.
# @exitcode 0 The branch was updated (`old` equals `new` when it was already up to date).
# @exitcode 1 A `gh` read or the update failed.
# @exitcode 2 Refused: usage, a pull request that is not open, or a base other than main.
# @example
#   ~/.local/bin/common/pr-update-branch.sh 480

usage='usage: pr-update-branch.sh <pr>'

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1: a read or the write failed.

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.

[[ $# -eq 1 ]] || refuse "${usage}"
pr=$1
[[ ${pr} =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,9}$ ]] || refuse "the pull request is not a decimal number: ${pr}"

# @description Read one git configuration key with three outcomes. `git config --get` exits 1 for a key that is
#   unset and with another status when the configuration cannot be read: measured on git 2.56.0 (2026-10-28), 128
#   for an unparsable file, where the manual says 3. Any status other than 0 and 1 is a failure here, so the reader
#   is right under both. Status 1 is also what an unreadable `-f` file returns, with only a warning on stderr
#   (research 01 section 1.2), so git's stderr goes to a file and anything in it is a failed read, whatever the
#   status; 3 is never special-cased. The value is never printed.
# @arg $1 string The git function to read with (`git` reads the user configuration too, `git_isolated` does not).
# @arg $2 string The configuration key.
# @arg $3 string The variable that receives the value.
# @arg $4 path The file that receives git's stderr: truncated first, then required empty.
# @exitcode 0 git exited 0 with a non-empty value and an empty stderr; the variable holds the value.
# @exitcode 1 Absent: git exited 1 with an empty stderr (the key is unset), or 0 with an empty value; the variable is empty.
# @exitcode 2 Failed: any other status, anything on stderr, or a stderr file that cannot be written; one line on
#   stderr names the key and the status.
read_config() {
    local rc_value='' rc_status=0
    printf -v "$3" '%s' ''
    { : > "$4"; } 2> /dev/null || {
        echo "read_config: cannot write ${4} to hold git's stderr for git config ${2}" >&2
        return 2
    }
    rc_value=$("$1" config --get "$2" 2> "$4") || rc_status=$?
    if ((rc_status != 0 && rc_status != 1)); then
        echo "read_config: cannot read git config ${2} (git config exited ${rc_status})" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    if [[ -s $4 ]]; then
        echo "read_config: cannot read git config ${2} (git config exited ${rc_status}); it wrote to its stderr, which a missing key never does" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    ((rc_status == 0)) || return 1
    [[ -n ${rc_value} ]] || return 1
    printf -v "$3" '%s' "${rc_value}"
}

# @description Run a listing producer with its stdout in one file and its stderr in another, with three outcomes.
#   `git ls-files` warns and exits 0 for a directory it cannot open and drops that directory's untracked files, and
#   `find` prints what it could reach before it exits 1 (git 2.56.0 and BSD find, measured for
#   scripts/ci/status-blind-producers.tsv): the status alone cannot clear a listing, so anything on stderr is a
#   failed read as well. Neither file's content is printed (a listed path may hold a redact word). The mid-entry
#   check of a NUL-delimited listing stays at the call site, which reads the file.
# @arg $1 path The file that receives the producer's stdout (truncated first).
# @arg $2 path The file that receives its stderr (truncated first).
# @arg $@ string The producer and its arguments: a command or a function, run as written.
# @exitcode 0 The producer exited 0, wrote nothing to stderr, and the output file is not empty.
# @exitcode 1 Absent: the producer exited 0, wrote nothing to stderr, and the output file is empty.
# @exitcode 2 Failed: a nonzero status (the shell's own when the producer could not be run), anything on stderr, no
#   producer named, or a file that cannot be written; one line on stderr names the producer's first two words and
#   the status.
read_listing() {
    local rl_out=$1 rl_err=$2 rl_status=0 rl_who rl_file
    shift 2
    (($# >= 1)) || {
        echo "read_listing: no producer named for ${rl_out}" >&2
        return 2
    }
    rl_who="$1${2:+ $2}"
    for rl_file in "${rl_out}" "${rl_err}"; do
        { : > "${rl_file}"; } 2> /dev/null || {
            echo "read_listing: cannot write ${rl_file} for ${rl_who}" >&2
            return 2
        }
    done
    "$@" > "${rl_out}" 2> "${rl_err}" || rl_status=$?
    if ((rl_status != 0)); then
        echo "read_listing: ${rl_who} exited ${rl_status}" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    if [[ -s ${rl_err} ]]; then
        echo "read_listing: ${rl_who} exited 0 and wrote to its stderr (kept in ${rl_err})" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    [[ -s ${rl_out} ]] || return 1
}

# @description Read a whole file into a variable, its trailing newlines kept, with three outcomes. The read is one
#   `cat` whose status comes through the substitution (`&& printf .` keeps the final newlines; the dot is removed
#   after), so a read that fails midway is a failure, never the end of the file. cat's own diagnostic is not shown;
#   the line printed here names the path and the status.
# @arg $1 path The file.
# @arg $2 string The variable that receives the content.
# @exitcode 0 The file was read and is not empty; the variable holds every byte.
# @exitcode 1 Absent: the file exists, was read, and is empty; the variable is empty.
# @exitcode 2 Failed: no file at the path, or `cat` exited nonzero (unreadable, a directory, cut short); one line on
#   stderr names the path.
read_file() {
    local rf_text='' rf_status=0
    printf -v "$2" '%s' ''
    [[ -e $1 ]] || {
        echo "read_file: no file at ${1}" >&2
        return 2
    }
    rf_text=$(cat -- "$1" 2> /dev/null && printf .) || rf_status=$?
    if ((rf_status != 0)); then
        echo "read_file: cannot read ${1} (cat exited ${rf_status})" >&2
        return 2
    fi
    rf_text=${rf_text%.}
    [[ -n ${rf_text} ]] || return 1
    printf -v "$2" '%s' "${rf_text}"
}

The store's redact-words.txt (one literal word per line, # comments) is never copied, deleted or published. A deletion candidate (a path of origin/main the store no longer holds as a regular file) gets the name checks only: it is never read, only removed. A file that became a directory, or the reverse, is mirrored as the deletion plus the additions in the one commit. The body lists the units.tsv ids and the decisions.tsv timestamps the sync adds or changes and the line Program-Unit: <program>/<unit>, which the regime check requires (U28c F2). No branch, worktree or file of the checkout is created; the scratch directory is removed on every exit. Each gh call is bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.

# @description Refuse to run unless this file's sha256 equals its pin in the manifest beside it (regime-cutover U31):
#   `~/.agents/agent-config.yaml` for the installed copy under ~/.local/bin/common, which a sandboxed session cannot
#   write, else the checkout's home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml. Every read is checked; a failure exits 2 naming the
#   file. The pin is the `claude.levers.sha256.<name>` line, which `scripts/generate-agent-configs.py` refreshes.
# @set LEVER_MANIFEST The manifest the pin came from.
lever_self_check() {
    local src dir self name pin digest home
    # The directory is split from the path in the shell, so no external producer (dirname) can fail unseen.
    src=${BASH_SOURCE[0]}
    case ${src} in
    */*) dir=${src%/*} ;;
    *) dir=. ;;
    esac
    [[ -n ${dir} ]] || dir=/
    dir=$(cd "${dir}" && pwd -P) || {
        echo "${src##*/}: refused: cannot resolve the script directory of ${src}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    self=${dir}/${BASH_SOURCE[0]##*/}
    # shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source regime-env from this directory
    LEVER_DIR=${dir}
    name=${self##*/}
    home=$(cd "${HOME}" 2> /dev/null && pwd -P) || home=''             # producer-status: allow the if below takes an empty home as the checkout layout
    if [[ -n ${home} && ${dir} == "${home}/.local/bin/common" ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${HOME}/.agents/agent-config.yaml
    else
        LEVER_MANIFEST=${dir}/../../home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml
    fi
    [[ -r ${LEVER_MANIFEST} ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: manifest unreadable: ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    pin=$(sed -n -E "s/^      ${name//./\\.}: ([0-9a-f]{64})\$/\\1/p" "${LEVER_MANIFEST}") || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot read ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${pin} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: no single sha256 pin for ${name} in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null; then
        digest=$(sha256sum < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    else
        digest=$(shasum -a 256 < "${self}") || digest='' # producer-status: allow the regex test below refuses an empty digest
    fi
    digest=${digest%% *}
    [[ ${digest} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: cannot hash ${self}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
    [[ ${digest} == "${pin}" ]] || {
        echo "${name}: refused: sha256 ${digest} of ${self} differs from the pin in ${LEVER_MANIFEST}" >&2
        exit 2
    }
}

# @description Print the refusal on stderr and exit 2.
# @arg $@ string The reason.
refuse() {
    echo "${lever}: refused: $*" >&2

}

# @description Print the failure on stderr and exit 1.

fail() {
    echo "${lever}: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

# @description Run `gh` with its wait bounded by PR_LEVER_GH_TIMEOUT seconds.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_bounded() {
    perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV or die "exec gh: $!\n"' "${gh_timeout}" gh "$@"
}

# @description Remove this run's scratch directory, with the repository the sync was built in.
cleanup() {
    if [[ -n ${scratch:-} && -d ${scratch} ]]; then

# @description Run `gh` as gh_bounded does, with no user or system git config for the `git` it runs.
# @arg $@ string The `gh` arguments.
gh_plain() {
    GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 gh_bounded "$@"
}

# @description Run the isolated git in the sync's own repository (U101): the repository named by `--git-dir`, so no
#   checkout is consulted, and nothing of the user, system or checkout configuration (git-isolated.sh, U113).
# @arg $@ string The `git` arguments.
git_scratch() {

# @description Refuse a path by its name alone: a control character (a newline would end the component split of
#   check_path early and leave the leaf unchecked), a place outside `.orchestration/`, or `..`. A deletion candidate
#   gets only this check (U101): it is never read, only removed from the new tree.
# @arg $1 string The repository-relative path.
check_name() {
    local path=$1
    [[ ${path} != *[[:cntrl:]]* ]] || refuse 'a path of the copy set holds a control character' # lint-comparisons: allow a character test on the raw git path

    case ${path} in # lint-comparisons: allow a repository-relative path as git prints it, refused unless under the store
    .orchestration/*) ;;
    *) refuse "a path of the copy set is outside .orchestration/: ${path}" ;;
    esac
    [[ ${path} != *..* ]] || refuse "a path of the copy set holds '..': ${path}" # lint-comparisons: allow refuses a raw git path that holds ..
}

# @description Refuse a path the store listing names (check_name, then): a published path outside `${records}/`; in
#   the derived form a component beginning with `.` (U220: the checkout form's ignore rules skip such a file today,
#   and a Finder artifact or a repository's own directory is not a record); a symlink at any component below the
#   chosen store (U28b F2: git lists the files below a linked directory too, and the derived walk is held the same
#   way; the store's own chain is held by store_resolve and regime-env); or, when the source `<store>/<rel>` exists,
#   anything but a regular file whose directory resolves (`pwd -P`) inside the store or a directory. A directory
#   stands where the index still has a file of that name (the file became a directory, U101): its own files are
#   listed as entries of their own, and the file it replaced is carried as a deletion.
# @arg $1 string The published path `.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>/<rel>`; its source is `<store>/<rel>`.
check_path() {
    local path=$1 rel prefix part rest source_dir
    check_name "${path}"
    case ${path} in # lint-comparisons: allow a published path, refused unless under the program's prefix
    "${records}"/?*) ;;
    *) refuse "a path of the copy set is outside ${records}/: ${path}" ;;
    esac
    rel=${path#"${records}/"}
    # Split on `/` by parameter expansion (no here-string, so no temporary file can go missing, U101).
    prefix=${store}
    rest=${rel}
    while [[ -n ${rest} ]]; do
        part=${rest%%/*}
        if [[ ${rest} == */* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow splits the path into its components
            rest=${rest#*/}
        else
            rest=''
        fi

            refuse "a name of the derived store begins with '.', which the checkout form's ignore rules skip and no record carries: ${path}"

    done

        [[ ${source_dir} == "${store}" || ${source_dir} == "${store}"/* ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
            refuse "a path of the copy set resolves outside ${store}: ${path}"

    fi

# @description Enter one listed path into the copy set (U220: the one reader of both listings): `redact-words.txt` is
#   skipped, the path is held by check_path, and an existing regular file is kept once (`files`, `present`).
# @arg $1 string The published path.
collect_path() {
    local path=$1
    [[ ${path} != "${words}" ]] || return 0 # lint-comparisons: allow both are published paths of the store
    check_path "${path}"

# @description Choose the program store (regime-cutover U220, store move 4 of 5; the `store_resolve` shape of U216's
#   pr-merge.sh and pr-close.sh, in this lever's own body: no helper file, standing order 36): the derived store
#   `${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}/<program>` when that path exists, which must then be a directory of this user and no symlink
#   (a link is refused by name before anything is read through it; a file or another user's directory is refused by
#   name too), else the checkout subtree `<toplevel>/.orchestration/orchestrate/<program>`, the pre-move form that
#   stands until U221 moves the live store, held as before this unit (U28b F2): `.orchestration` a real directory
#   resolving (`pwd -P`) inside the toplevel, no symlink at `.orchestration/orchestrate` or at the program directory,
#   which must exist. The root's own components are held by regime-env (`regime_store_root`). Nothing is written. The
#   form chosen is printed once on stderr (`store: derived <dir>`, or `store: checkout <dir> (pre-move form, removed
#   by U221)`), the line the coordinator reads after the deploy.

# @set store The chosen store, `pwd -P` form (the root and the toplevel are both physical).
# @set store_form `derived` or `checkout`.
store_resolve() {
    local program=$1 store_derived store_checkout orchestration_real prefix

        refuse "regime-env derived no store root for ${toplevel}; the program store is judged under it (U216, U220)"

    store_checkout=${top_real}/.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}

        refuse "${store_derived} is a symlink; the derived program store is a plain directory of this user under the store root ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT}, and nothing is read through a link"
    if [[ -e ${store_derived} ]]; then
        [[ -d ${store_derived} && -O ${store_derived} ]] ||
            refuse "${store_derived} exists but is not a directory of this user; the derived program store under ${REGIME_STORE_ROOT} is read only as one"
        store=${store_derived}
        store_form=derived
        echo "${lever}: store: derived ${store}" >&2
        return 0
    fi

    [[ -d .orchestration && ! -L .orchestration ]] || refuse ".orchestration is missing or a symlink in ${toplevel}"
    orchestration_real=$(cd .orchestration && pwd -P) || refuse "cannot resolve ${toplevel}/.orchestration"
    [[ ${orchestration_real} == "${top_real}/.orchestration" ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow both sides are pwd -P forms
        refuse ".orchestration resolves outside ${top_real}: ${orchestration_real}"

    for prefix in .orchestration/orchestrate "${records}"; do
        [[ ! -L ${prefix} ]] || refuse "a component of a path of the copy set is a symlink: ${prefix} (in ${records}/)"
    done
    [[ -d ${records} ]] || refuse "no program directory ${records}"
    store=${store_checkout}
    store_form=checkout
    echo "${lever}: store: checkout ${store} (pre-move form, removed by U221)" >&2
}

required_config git user.email author_email # git-isolated: allow the identity is read from the user configuration on purpose

    read_listing "${listing}" "${scratch}/listing.err" find "${store}" ! -type d -print0 || status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0 | 1) ;;
    *) refuse "the walk of ${records}/ failed or warned (its output is withheld); nothing was created" ;;
    esac
    entry=''
    while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
        case ${entry} in # lint-comparisons: allow a path as find prints it, refused unless below the store
        "${store}"/?*) collect_path "${records}/${entry#"${store}/"}" ;;
        *) refuse "the walk of ${records}/ names a path outside the store; nothing was created" ;;
        esac
    done < "${listing}"
    [[ -z ${entry} ]] || refuse "the walk of ${records}/ ends mid-entry; nothing was created"
else
    # Audit of 7b3c2718: the listing is the one index read in the checkout, and a `core.fsmonitor` hook set in any
    # configuration the checkout reads would run inside it (and could write into the store before the copy). The
    # isolated git turns it off, with the hooks path and the user and system files; the repository level has no off
    # switch, so the checkout's own ignore rules and the default ignore file still shape the listing, which the stderr
    # test below bounds.
    status=0
    read_listing "${listing}" "${scratch}/listing.err" \
        git_isolated ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard -- "${records}/" ||
        status=$?
    case ${status} in
    0 | 1) ;;
    *)
        [[ ! -s ${scratch}/listing.err ]] ||
            refuse "git ls-files warned while listing ${records}/ (its output is withheld); nothing was created"
        fail 'git ls-files failed'
        ;;
    esac
    path=''
    while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
        collect_path "${path}"
    done < "${listing}"
    [[ -z ${path} ]] || refuse "the listing of ${records}/ ends mid-entry; nothing was created"
fi
# Full entries (`<mode> blob <oid>` TAB path): the deletions come from them, and the expected change set below
# compares each copy with its entry on main.
git_scratch ls-tree -r -z "${main}" -- "${records}/" > "${listing}" || fail "git ls-tree ${base} failed"
gone=()
base_entries=$'\n'
entry=''
while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
    path=${entry#*$'\t'}
    check_name "${path}"
    base_entries+=${path}$'\t'${entry%%$'\t'*}$'\n'
    [[ ${path} != "${words}" && ${present} != *$'\n'"${path}"$'\n'* ]] || continue # lint-comparisons: allow repository-relative paths as git prints them
    gone+=("${path}")
done < "${listing}"
[[ -z ${entry} ]] || refuse "the listing of ${base}:${records}/ ends mid-entry; nothing was created"
((${#files[@]} + ${#gone[@]} > 0)) || refuse "nothing to sync under ${records}/"

# The masker and the scanner are main's validator, alone in a tools tree whose `home/` holds main's top-level entry
# names (empty), so its home-path pattern skips the repository's own `home/<entry>` paths as in a checkout; a main
# without `home/` gives an empty one.
tools=${scratch}/tools
mkdir -p "${tools}/scripts" "${tools}/home" || fail 'cannot make the tools tree'
git_scratch cat-file blob "${main}:scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" > "${tools}/scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" ||
    fail "cannot read scripts/validate-agent-assets.py of ${base}"
git_scratch ls-tree -z --name-only "${main}" -- home/ > "${scratch}/home-entries" || fail "cannot list home/ of ${base}"
while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
    entry=${entry#home/}
    [[ -n ${entry} && ${entry} != *[/[:cntrl:]]* && ${entry} != . && ${entry} != .. ]] || # lint-comparisons: allow a tree entry name as git prints it
        fail "home/ of ${base} holds an unusable entry name"
    mkdir "${tools}/home/${entry}" || fail 'cannot make the tools tree'
done < "${scratch}/home-entries"
# U101: the copies are masked and scanned in the scratch directory, and these same files are what hash-object
# writes, so the committed bytes are the scanned bytes.
copies=${scratch}/copies
masked=()
for path in ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}; do
    mkdir -p "${copies}/${path%/*}" || fail "mkdir for ${path} failed"
    cp -p "${store}/${path#"${records}/"}" "${copies}/${path}" || fail "cp ${path} failed"
    masked+=("${copies}/${path}")
done
if ((${#masked[@]})); then
    # U101: neither tool's output is shown. The masker prints each copy's path and, on a key collision, the original
    # keys; either may hold a redact word or a secret. Both go to files in the scratch directory (removed on exit),
    # and a failure says only that it happened and the exit status.
    status=0
    uv run --no-project python -I "${tools}/scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" --mask-secrets "${masked[@]}" \
        > "${scratch}/mask.log" 2>&1 || status=$?
    ((status == 0)) || fail "masking the copies failed (exit ${status}); its output is withheld, nothing was published"
    # U101: after masking, no copy may still name a secret, a home path or a redact word, its path included.
    scan=(--scan-identifiers)
    [[ -z ${words_real} ]] || scan+=(--redact-words "${words_real}")
    (cd "${copies}" && uv run --no-project python -I "${tools}/scripts/validate-agent-assets.py" "${scan[@]}" -- "${files[@]}") \
        > "${scratch}/scan.log" 2>&1 || status=$?
    ((status != 1)) ||
        refuse 'the identifier scan found a secret, a home path or a redact word in the masked copies (exit 1); its output is withheld, nothing was published'
    ((status == 0)) || fail "the identifier scan failed (exit ${status}); its output is withheld, nothing was published"
fi

# U101: the new tree is main's tree in a private index, the deletions removed first (a file that became a directory,
# or the reverse, frees its name), then each masked copy hashed with --no-filters and entered by mode and object id.
# The expected change set is computed alongside: every deletion, and every copy whose `<mode> blob <oid>` differs
# from its entry on main.
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=${scratch}/index
git_scratch read-tree "${main}" || fail 'git read-tree failed'
expected=${scratch}/expected
: > "${expected}" || fail 'cannot write the expected change set'
# A bare repository has no work tree, which `update-index --force-remove` asks for; an `--index-info` line of mode 0
# removes the path from the index without one. The zero object id has main's length (SHA-1 or SHA-256).
zero=${main//?/0}
for path in ${gone[@]+"${gone[@]}"}; do
    printf '0 %s\t%s\0' "${zero}" "${path}" | git_scratch update-index -z --index-info ||
        fail "git update-index removing ${path} failed"
    printf '%s\0' "${path}" >> "${expected}" || fail 'cannot write the expected change set'
done
for path in ${files[@]+"${files[@]}"}; do
    blob=$(git_scratch hash-object -w --no-filters -- "${copies}/${path}") || fail "git hash-object ${path} failed"
    mode=100644
    if [[ -x ${copies}/${path} ]]; then
        mode=100755
    fi
    git_scratch update-index --add --cacheinfo "${mode},${blob},${path}" || fail "git update-index ${path} failed"
    if [[ ${base_entries} != *$'\n'"${path}"$'\t'"${mode} blob ${blob}"$'\n'* ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow a repository-relative path and an object id as git prints them
        printf '%s\0' "${path}" >> "${expected}" || fail 'cannot write the expected change set'
    fi
done
new_tree=$(git_scratch write-tree) || fail 'git write-tree failed'
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
# U101: the tree's change against main must be exactly the computed set, as sorted NUL lists.
changed=${scratch}/changed
git_scratch diff-tree -r --no-renames --name-only -z "${main_tree}" "${new_tree}" > "${changed}" ||
    fail 'git diff-tree failed'
LC_ALL=C sort -z "${expected}" > "${expected}.sorted" || fail 'cannot sort the expected change set'
LC_ALL=C sort -z "${changed}" > "${changed}.sorted" || fail 'cannot sort the change set'
cmp -s "${expected}.sorted" "${changed}.sorted" ||
    refuse 'the new tree changes other paths than the copy set; nothing was committed or pushed'
[[ -s ${changed} ]] || refuse 'the copies equal origin/main; nothing to sync'
count=$(tr -cd '\000' < "${changed}" | wc -c) || fail 'cannot count the changed paths'
count=${count//[[:space:]]/}

remote_heads=$(git_scratch -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' \
    ls-remote --heads "${push_url}" 'refs/heads/records/*') || fail 'git ls-remote origin failed'
# U28b F6: a local branch occupies its number too, whatever left it behind.
local_heads=$(git_isolated for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/heads/records/') || fail 'git for-each-ref failed'
pr_heads=$(gh_plain pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName') ||
    fail 'gh pr list failed'
last=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "${remote_heads}" "${local_heads}" "${pr_heads}" |
    PROGRAM=${program} awk '{ ref = $NF; sub(/^refs\/heads\//, "", ref) }
        ref ~ "^records/(sync|program-store|" ENVIRON["PROGRAM"] "-sync)-[0-9]+$" { n = ref; sub(/.*-/, "", n); if (n + 0 > max) max = n + 0 }
        END { print max + 0 }') || fail 'cannot number the sync'
n=$((last + 1))
branch=records/sync-${n}
[[ ${branch} =~ ^records/sync-[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || refuse "the branch is outside records/sync-<n>: ${branch}"

units=$(git_scratch diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -U0 "${main_tree}" "${new_tree}" -- "${records}/units.tsv" |
    sed -n -E 's/^\+(U[0-9]+[a-z]?)\t.*/\1/p' | sort -u | paste -sd ' ' -) || fail 'cannot list the units'
decisions=$(git_scratch diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -U0 "${main_tree}" "${new_tree}" -- "${records}/decisions.tsv" |
    sed -n -E 's/^\+([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]+Z)\t.*/\1/p' | sort -u | paste -sd ' ' -) ||
    fail 'cannot list the decisions'
title="chore(records): ${program} sync ${n}"
message=$(printf '%s\n\n%s\n\n%s\n' "${title}" \
    "Carries ${count} file(s) of ${records}/ from the program store (${store_form} form), compared with origin/main (records-sync.sh)." \
    "${footer}") || fail 'cannot write the commit message'
# U101: author and committer come only from the environment set here, the identity read at the start.
commit=$(printf '%s\n' "${message}" |
    GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=${author_name} GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=${author_email} \
        GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=${author_name} GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=${author_email} \
        git_scratch commit-tree "${new_tree}" -p "${main}" -F -) || fail 'git commit-tree failed'
git_scratch -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' \
    push --quiet "${push_url}" "${commit}:refs/heads/${branch}" || fail "git push ${branch} failed; nothing was opened"
body=${scratch}/body.md
# U220: the contract's first row names the store's form; the derived store's place is a home-directory path, which no
# published text names.
if [[ ${store_form} == derived ]]; then # lint-comparisons: allow the form name store_resolve set, not a path
    listed="the derived program store \`<store root>/${program}/\` (every regular file below it, \`redact-words.txt\` excluded; U220), published at \`.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/\`"
else
    listed="\`.orchestration/orchestrate/${program}/\`, tracked or untracked and not git-ignored, \`redact-words.txt\` excluded"
fi
# U108: the `## Contract` section is what pr-audit.sh judges the pull request against (a body without one is
# refused), so every records sync gets an orchestrator verdict. Only the program name is interpolated.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the backticks are Markdown code spans
contract=(
    "The changed paths are the store's files (${listed}) whose masked copy or executable mode differs from origin/main, plus every path origin/main holds under that directory that the listing does not hold as a regular file; the new tree's change set against origin/main is checked to equal exactly that set."
    'No path lies outside that directory.'
    'Every copy was masked with `validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets` and passed its `--scan-identifiers`, with the program'"'"'s `redact-words.txt` when present.'
    'The commit was built in a repository with no user, system or checkout configuration, and pushed over https with no user configuration.'
    'Left out: the content of the records is not reviewed for truth, only by the identifier scan.'
)
{
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # the backticks are Markdown code spans
    printf '## Summary\n\nRecords sync %s of `%s` (%s file(s)), carried by `records-sync.sh` from the program store (%s form) and compared with origin/main; every copy was masked with `validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets` and passed its `--scan-identifiers`.\n\n' "${n}" "${program}" "${count}" "${store_form}"
    printf -- '- units.tsv rows added or changed: %s\n' "${units:-none}"
    printf -- '- decisions.tsv rows added or changed: %s\n\n' "${decisions:-none}"
    printf '## Contract\n\n'
    printf -- '- %s\n' "${contract[@]}"
    printf '\nProgram-Unit: %s/%s\n\n' "${program}" "${unit}"
    printf '%s\n' "${pr_footer}"
} > "${body}" || fail 'cannot write the body'
url=$(gh_plain pr create --base main --head "${branch}" --title "${title}" --body-file "${body}") ||
    fail "gh pr create failed; the branch ${branch} is pushed"
echo "synced branch=${branch} files=${count} pr=${url}"
</code></pre>

It carries no self-check of its own (regime-cutover U344c, verdict U344-a8adad11 P1 seat-settings-render.sh:76, class pin-then-run: a check inside sourced text runs after every line before it, so a replaced file ran unpinned up to that line and the check proved nothing about the bytes that ran). The lever that sources it hashes the copy it sources: it reads the file beside itself once into a private per-launch copy under its own state directory ~/.local/state/hcom-seat/, hashes that copy against the claude.levers.sha256.seat-settings-render.sh pin of the manifest its own self-check read, sources the copy and removes the copy's directory at once (hcom-seat's and acp-broker's renderer_source, the form of hcom-seat's helper_copy_make, U310f), so the bytes hashed are the bytes sourced and nothing of this file runs before its digest equals the pin. It holds what the two renderings shared by copy until U344 (the U343 header: "This copy of the dsh row's shape is interim: U344 extracts one writer for both levers"): the path rule every settings row obeys (clean_path, clean_row), the fixed rows of the deny table (the credential stores denied for read, the project files denied for write under a seat's own directory, the rows denied for write under the shared Claude Code directory), the domain list, and the JSON writer (seat_settings_rows_json for a list, seat_settings_json for the file's text). It judges nothing (each lever's settings_judge stays its own) and writes no file (the caller writes the text it is handed, as before); each lever passes its rows, its allowLocalBinding value, its allowUnixSockets list and its Linux tool fragment. acp-broker reads the deny table back from the Router's settings hcom-seat rendered, so the rows below are spelled once and rendered once. tests/unit/test_acp_broker.py test_one_settings_writer_renders_the_worker_and_the_dsh_row_byte_for_byte holds the two levers' files byte-identical but the role's own rows.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @file seat-settings-render.sh
# @brief The one srt settings writer of the seat levers: the rows every seat's settings share and the JSON text they are written in, sourced by hcom-seat and acp-broker.
# @description
#   Regime-cutover U344 (M-24 part 2; U344c). Sourced by `hcom-seat` (every role's settings) and by `acp-broker` (the
#   worker's settings, per connection), never run on its own. It carries no self-check of its own (regime-cutover
#   U344c, verdict U344-a8adad11 P1 `seat-settings-render.sh:76`, class pin-then-run: a check inside sourced text
#   runs after every line before it, so a replaced file ran unpinned up to that line and the check proved nothing
#   about the bytes that ran). The lever that sources it hashes the copy it sources: it reads the file beside itself
#   once into a private per-launch copy under its own state directory `~/.local/state/hcom-seat/`, hashes that copy
#   against the `claude.levers.sha256.seat-settings-render.sh` pin of the manifest its own self-check read, sources
#   the copy and removes the copy's directory at once (hcom-seat's and acp-broker's `renderer_source`, the form of
#   hcom-seat's helper_copy_make, U310f), so the bytes hashed are the bytes sourced and nothing of this file runs
#   before its digest equals the pin. It holds what the two renderings shared by copy until U344 (the U343 header:
#   "This copy of the dsh row's shape is interim: U344 extracts one writer for both levers"): the path rule every
#   settings row obeys (clean_path, clean_row), the fixed rows of the deny table (the credential stores denied for
#   read, the project files denied for write under a seat's own directory, the rows denied for write under the
#   shared Claude Code directory), the domain list, and the JSON writer (seat_settings_rows_json for a list,
#   seat_settings_json for the file's text). It judges nothing (each lever's `settings_judge` stays its own) and
#   writes no file (the caller writes the text it is handed, as before); each lever passes its rows, its
#   `allowLocalBinding` value, its `allowUnixSockets` list and its Linux tool fragment. `acp-broker` reads the deny
#   table back from the Router's settings `hcom-seat` rendered, so the rows below are spelled once and rendered
#   once. tests/unit/test_acp_broker.py `test_one_settings_writer_renders_the_worker_and_the_dsh_row_byte_for_byte`
#   holds the two levers' files byte-identical but the role's own rows.

# @description Succeed when `$1` is a clean absolute path that srt cannot read as a pattern: `/` followed by
#   components of `[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]` only (no glob metacharacter `*?[]{}`, no whitespace, no quote or backslash), none
#   of them empty, `.` or `..`, and no trailing `/`. srt 0.0.81 turns a settings path into a Seatbelt regex or a glob,
#   so `/private/tmp/hcom*` would grant its siblings; a clean path names exactly itself (regime-cutover U85).
# @arg $1 string The path.
# @exitcode 1 The path is not clean.
clean_path() {
    [[ $1 =~ ^(/[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]+)+$ ]] || return 1
    [[ /$1/ != */./* && /$1/ != */../* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow a component test on one path, no path compare
}

# @description Succeed when `$1` is a row the settings may carry: a clean path, or (for `denyWrite`, `$2` = 1) one of
#   the macOS worktree patterns `hcom-seat` renders, a clean prefix and the fixed `worktrees/*/<file>` suffix, the
#   one place a settings entry is not a clean path (srt reads `*` as `[^/]*`).
# @arg $1 string The row.
# @arg $2 int 1 when the pattern form is allowed.
# @exitcode 1 The row is neither.
clean_row() {
    clean_path "$1" && return 0
    (($2)) || return 1
    [[ $1 =~ ^(/[A-Za-z0-9._@+-]+)+/worktrees/\*/(config\.worktree|info|commondir|gitdir)$ ]] || return 1
    [[ /${1%/worktrees/*}/ != */./* && /${1%/worktrees/*}/ != */../* ]] # lint-comparisons: allow a component test on one pattern's clean prefix, no path compare
}

# The fixed rows of the deny table, relative to the root each is rendered under (hcom-seat seat_settings_render
# renders them for every role; acp-broker reads them back from the Router's settings, re-rooting the project-file rows
# under the task cwd, so each list is spelled here once). The credential stores every seat is denied for read, under
# HOME. The project files a seat is denied for write under its own directory (a cwd that holds `.omp` is refused
# outright: omp merges it before `disabledProviders` applies; the hook shims under `.claude/hooks` import their code
# from `.claude/contextdb`, run by sessions outside the seat). The rows denied for write under the shared Claude Code
# directory, what another seat's child or the operator's login command would load (regime-cutover U318, U190).
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source this helper
SEAT_SETTINGS_CREDENTIAL_DENIES=(.ssh .gnupg .aws .netrc .docker .kube .config/gcloud .codex .omp/agent)
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source this helper
SEAT_SETTINGS_PROJECT_FILES=(.claude/settings.json .claude/settings.local.json .claude/hooks .claude/contextdb .omp .codex .envrc .mcp.json)
# shellcheck disable=SC2034 # read by the levers that source this helper
SEAT_SETTINGS_CLAUDE_ROWS=(settings.json settings.local.json rules hooks plugins skills commands agents)
# The outbound hosts every seat may reach (`network.allowedDomains`): GitHub and its API, upload, codeload and content
# hosts; PyPI; the Anthropic and Claude hosts; the OpenAI hosts of the openai-siwc route.
SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS='"github.com","api.github.com","uploads.github.com","codeload.github.com","objects.githubusercontent.com"'
SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS+=',"raw.githubusercontent.com","release-assets.githubusercontent.com","pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org"'
SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS+=',"api.anthropic.com","claude.ai","platform.claude.com","console.anthropic.com"'
SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS+=',"chatgpt.com","auth.openai.com","api.openai.com"'

# @description Print a JSON array of the rows `$@` in their order, each held to clean_row first, so no JSON escaping is
#   needed and no settings tool runs; a row that is not clean fails the function with nothing printed, and the caller
#   refuses naming the list (standing order 21: the caller reads this status).
# @arg $1 int 1 when the macOS worktree pattern form is allowed (a `denyWrite` list).
# @arg $@ string The rows after it.
# @stdout The array, `[]` for no rows.
# @exitcode 1 A row is not one the settings may carry.
seat_settings_rows_json() {
    local patterns=$1 row out='' sep=''
    shift
    for row in "$@"; do
        clean_row "${row}" "${patterns}" || return 1
        out+=${sep}\"${row}\"
        sep=,
    done
    printf '[%s]' "${out}"
}

# @description Set `settings_json` to the one-line text of a seat's srt settings file from its rendered lists: the
#   network block (the domain list above, no denied domain, the `allowUnixSockets` list `$2`, the trustd Mach
#   lookup every sandboxed process needs, the `allowLocalBinding` value `$1`), the filesystem block in the order
#   `denyRead`, `allowRead`, `allowWrite`, `denyWrite`, `allowPty` true and, on Linux, the tool fragment `$7` naming
#   the checked bwrap, socat and rg. The key order and the compact form are what the levers wrote before this helper
#   (hcom-seat seat_sandbox_write, acp-broker), so every earlier head's settings re-render byte for byte.
# @arg $1 string `true` or `false`, the role's `allowLocalBinding`.
# @arg $2 string The `allowUnixSockets` JSON array (seat_settings_rows_json; `[]` for every role but the router).
# @arg $3 string The `denyRead` JSON array.
# @arg $4 string The `allowRead` JSON array.
# @arg $5 string The `allowWrite` JSON array.
# @arg $6 string The `denyWrite` JSON array.
# @arg $7 string The Linux tool fragment (`,"bwrapPath":…`), empty on macOS.
# @set settings_json The text, without a trailing newline.
# @exitcode 1 `$1` is neither `true` nor `false`.
seat_settings_json() {
    [[ $1 == true || $1 == false ]] || return 1
    settings_json="{\"network\":{\"allowedDomains\":[${SEAT_SETTINGS_DOMAINS}],\"deniedDomains\":[],\"allowUnixSockets\":$2"
    settings_json+=",\"allowMachLookup\":[\"com.apple.trustd.agent\"],\"allowLocalBinding\":$1}"
    settings_json+=",\"filesystem\":{\"denyRead\":$3,\"allowRead\":$4"
    settings_json+=",\"allowWrite\":$5,\"denyWrite\":$6},\"allowPty\":true$7}"
}

docs.title: scripts/orchestrator/worker-worktree.sh
docs.text: Regime-cutover U123 (standing order 29: workers never push; the coordinator pushes). The order was text in the first line of every TASK, and on 2026-10-30 six owners pushed anyway; the one stopped was the one whose push route had no key. This lever makes the order a refusal of the tool. Run it from the main checkout: worker-worktree.sh <unit> <branch> <base> makes <root>/<unit> (the root $DOTFILES_WT when set, else ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dotfiles-wt, resolved through its longest existing directory with pwd -P) as a fresh repository, not a linked worktree of the checkout (rounds 1 to 3 hardened git worktree add inside the checkout, and each audit found another channel of the checkout's configuration that runs during creation: post-checkout hooks, hook.<name>.event hooks, a required smudge filter, a locked tree; round 4 removes the linked worktree from the design). The fresh repository shares the checkout's objects alone: - git init -q --template= makes it with no template, under GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, the environment every git this lever runs has (git_run below), so neither the operator's global configuration (a core.hooksPath, a hook.<name>.event, a filter.<name>.smudge, an init.templateDir) nor the checkout's is read while the tree is made; - objects/info/alternates names the checkout's objects directory (git rev-parse --git-path objects there), so the fetch below transfers nothing and a worker's commits are written into the fresh repository's own store; - git fetch <checkout> <base sha>:refs/remotes/origin/main, the sha the checkout's rev-parse --verify <base>^{commit} printed, gives the tree the origin/main the workers' tests read, and git checkout --no-track -b <branch> origin/main makes the branch in the fresh repository: the checkout's own branches are never read or written, so a branch of the same name in the checkout is no conflict; - the fresh repository's own config then holds remote.origin.url (the checkout's, so git fetch origin works and origin/main moves), remote.origin.fetch for refs/heads/*, remote.origin.pushurl = refused://never-push-from-a-worker-worktree (so git push, git push origin <ref> and git push -u origin <branch> fail on a remote helper that does not exist, before any remote is contacted), an empty credential.helper (clears the helper list for an https push that spells the URL), core.hooksPath = <repository>/.git/hooks-lever holding one pre-push hook that prints standing order 29: the coordinator pushes and exits 1 (a push that spells any URL is refused after git has read the remote's refs and before any object is sent), branch.<branch>.remote = origin, branch.<branch>.merge = refs/heads/<branch>, and the three keys a bare git push resolves its remote from, in git's order (git-push(1)): branch.<branch>.pushRemote = origin, then remote.pushDefault = origin, then branch.<branch>.remote, with push.default = current; all are local values, and a local value wins over a global one, so a bare push goes to the refusal URL whatever the worker's global config says (a global branch.<branch>.pushRemote = upstream included). Trusted: the worker is a non-adversarial actor whose reflex the refusals stop, not an attacker.
